# Audit log

Every falsification pass, every reopening, every structural change. Append-only.

This file exists because **an unrecorded audit did not happen**. If a claim survived an
attack, the attack has to be visible — otherwise the next reader cannot tell a hardened fact
from an unexamined assumption, and they look identical on the page.

---

## How to record a pass

Append an entry. Never edit or delete an earlier one — a wrong reading that was later
overturned is itself evidence about where the same mistake may be hiding.

```markdown
### YYYY-MM-DD — <pass name>

**Program state:** <snapshot SHA> · <explicit>/<unresolved> · <residual SHA>
**Scope:** which documents were attacked
**Tool run:** audit_crossrefs.py findings before → after

| Document | Claim attacked | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| … | … | … | SURVIVED / OVERTURNED / EXTENDED |

**Overturned:** what changed, what proved it, why the earlier reading was reachable.
**Propagation:** which documents reopened as a consequence.
**Structural changes:** files/folders renamed, moved or created, and why.
```

`SURVIVED` requires naming what you *tried* that failed to break it. "I re-read it and it
still looked right" is not an audit.

### 2026-09-02 — tooling defects found by use

Recorded because tooling defects are claims too, and these were found by running the tools
rather than by reading them.

| Defect | How found | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Wrappers hardcoded `-ProgramName 'FFXII_TZA.exe'` | verification failed exit 1; a `.gzf` imports under the **packed file's** name, which changes every checkpoint | added `ListProjectFiles.java` + `Get-GfzProgramName`; wrappers now auto-discover |
| `Get-GfzProgramName` reported a locked project as "no Program DomainFile found" | headless run while the GUI held the lock | added `Assert-GfzProjectUnlocked` with an accurate diagnostic |
| Headless and GUI contend for one project lock | same | adopted separate project copies for GUI browsing vs headless work |

Both defects were in tooling that had passed a syntax check an hour earlier. **A parse check
is not a proof of correctness** — the same rule the evidence standard applies to claims about
the binary applies to claims about our own tools.

### 2026-09-02 — first mechanical cross-reference audit

**Program state:** snapshot `d2445517c66513976c83a446f87537a3c1d8c21f5bef033779affe98d7e61a20` ·
38,001 explicit / 160 unresolved · call graph 38,161 functions / 90,525 edges
**Scope:** all 25 documents citing addresses.
**Tool run:** `audit_crossrefs.py` — **134 findings** (133 UNACCOUNTED NEIGHBOUR, 1 GHOST ADDRESS).

| Document | Claim attacked | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `15-Input/.../capability-inhibition-policy.md` | `01E0C2C0` is a function with an 88 B body | is it in the current function list? | **OVERTURNED** — it is static data |
| `15-Input/.../capability-inhibition-policy.md` | `00377C20` is "a WorldAreaField field-record policy bit source" | does anything outside WorldAreaField/Input call it? | **OVERTURNED** — 65 callers across 13 subsystems |

**Overturned in detail.**

`00377C20` = `FieldData_GetActiveFieldRecordBit15`, 78 B, WorldAreaField-owned. Verified
against the 90,525-edge call graph: **65 distinct callers** — CombatAction 17, Script/VM 4,
Presentation 4, Movement 4, CombatAI 3, Status/Periodic 3, ActorEntity 2, Items/Equipment 2,
CombatFormula 1, Input 1, Party 1, Rewards 1, WorldAreaField 1, unowned 21.

Nothing in the document was *false*. It was **incomplete in a way that would mislead** — a
reader would take bit 10 for a UI-side concern when it is fed by a predicate 17 CombatAction
functions gate on directly. Incompleteness of that kind is a defect, not a stylistic gap.

This is exactly the failure mode the reopening rule exists for, and no human re-reading would
have caught it: the document was internally consistent and its evidence was correct. Only
joining it against the current call graph exposed the omission.

**Propagation:** none — no other document cited that reading.
**Reopened:** `15-Input/Gameplay-Capability-Policy/capability-inhibition-policy.md`
(`DOCUMENTED` → `REOPENED`, `reopened_count: 1`).
**Opened:** question **C-8** — `00377C20` owes its own document.

**Remaining 131 findings:** undispositioned. Most are category `README.md` files listing
addresses without prose context, which is expected at this stage; each still needs an explicit
disposition before any document reaches `AUDITED`.

**Tool note:** `audit_crossrefs.py` found both defects on its first run against real data.
The GHOST ADDRESS check also proved it distinguishes code from data correctly.

**Correction discipline observed:** the `01E0C2C0` entry was not deleted to silence the tool —
it was moved to §4 with its verified 88-byte size and content hash, because it is real and
load-bearing, just not a function.

### 2026-09-02 — RTTI mapping challenge (loop iteration 1)

**Scope:** the 6,886-method RTTI mapping recovered earlier the same day, attacked before any
attempt to apply it. New tool `analysis-kit/gfz-scripts/rtti_challenge.py`.

| Claim attacked | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Recovered class↔method mapping is trustworthy | do independently-derived GFZ CodeDomains contradict it? | **SURVIVED** — 99.1 % agreement (1,592/1,607) |
| Every method address is a real function entry | addresses landing mid-function | SURVIVED — 3 of 6,886, isolated |
| An address belongs to one class | one address in several unrelated classes | **OVERTURNED for 2,612 addresses** |

**Overturned: 2,612 addresses cannot carry a unique class identity.**

They appear in multiple unrelated classes because MSVC's linker performs identical code
folding. Evidence: `0016D6A0` is `_guard_check_icall` at **3 bytes**; `00314F20` and
`001F2880` are 6 bytes, the latter already classified `NativeLeaf.ConstantReturn`. Shared
addresses have a **median body of 36 B**; unique-class addresses **92 B**. Trivial
destructors and constant-return stubs were folded into single shared copies.

This is a real property of the shipping binary, not a defect in the vtable walk. Consequence:
the applicable subset is the **4,274 unique-class methods**, not 6,609. The headline number
went *down* as a result of the challenge, which is the point.

**Instrument defect found — and it nearly produced a false finding.**

The first agreement test compared the RTTI leaf class name against the GFZ CodeDomain by
substring, and reported **5.9 % agreement**. That looked like the mapping was broken. It was
not: GFZ labels are frequently generic (`Phyre.SceneCamera.NativeQualified`,
`Phyre.Rendering.NativeQualified`), so a leaf-name test fails even when both derivations are
correct and consistent — `Phyre::PCameraPerspective` vs `Phyre.SceneCamera.NativeQualified`
agree on the subject and score as a miss.

Re-run at namespace level over the unique-class subset: **99.1 %**. The 15 residue are the
same artifact (`PClassDescriptorWrapper` vs `PClassDescriptorForType`) or RTTI being *more*
specific than a generic GFZ label. **No genuine contradiction was found anywhere.**

Recorded prominently because this is precisely the failure the protocol exists to prevent:
a broken instrument producing a confident, false, negative result. The 5.9 % figure was never
about the binary — it was about the test. `rtti_challenge.py` still contains the naive leaf
comparison and must be corrected before its output is trusted again.

**Propagation:** none — nothing had been applied or documented from the mapping.
**Structural changes:** new tool `rtti_challenge.py`; outputs `Tools/work/rtti/challenge.md`.

### 2026-09-02 — coverage-drift correction (user-flagged)

**Not a falsification pass — a process failure caught by the user, recorded because process
defects are claims too.**

**What happened.** Across roughly nine consecutive loop blocks the work stayed inside Audio
and post-processing. Measured at the point of correction:

| | |
|---|---:|
| Categories with **zero** documents | **17 of 26** |
| Blocks spent in Audio + Presentation | ~9 consecutive |
| Untouched, >=200 functions | Phyre 6,768 · CRT 5,150 · **Script/VM 1,900** · ThirdParty 1,000 · **Resource 572** · **Movement 485** · **Actor 235** |

**Why it happened.** The string-naming technique kept yielding — 90 audio functions, then 147
post-processing functions, both validating clean. Each block's most obvious next step was
another application of the same method. That is the loop optimising for **what is working**
rather than **what matters**, and nothing in the mission prompt prevented it.

The affected categories are not marginal. Script/VM is the zone scripting system, Spawn is
what XIIOnline's entire roadmap depends on, Movement is 485 functions of locomotion and
navigation. All are more useful to a modder than post-processing internals.

**Correction.** New tool `analysis-kit/gfz-scripts/coverage_balance.py` ranks categories by
`functions / (documents + 1)` and names the next target. Four breadth rules added to both the
mission prompt (as **Phase 0**, run before every block) and the `/goal` skill:

1. never more than 3 consecutive blocks in one category;
2. zero documents + >=200 functions outranks any refinement elsewhere;
3. prefer player-facing categories on ties;
4. closing a question is not a mandate to keep pulling that thread.

**What was not wrong.** The depth itself was correct — the RTTI recovery, the string
cross-validation and the 237 named functions are real results that survived challenge.
Generalising the technique from audio to post-processing was right. Doing it a *third* time
would have been the error, and that is what the rules now prevent.

**No claims retracted.** This changes what gets worked on next, not what is believed.

### 2026-09-02 — ScriptVM dispatch table: fresh derivation disproven by the GFZ

**Scope:** a newly derived verb→handler mapping for the ScriptVM native dispatch table.

| Claim attacked | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `record N = verb N` across the table | a verb whose handler body contradicts its catalog argument count | **OVERTURNED** |

**What was claimed.** A dispatch table at VA `0x01EED720`, stride `0x20`, handler at `+0`,
indexed directly by call ID — yielding 1,224 verb→handler rows. Aggregate validation looked
excellent: **0** handlers outside `.text`, **0** off a function entry, 1,202/1,224 owned by
Script/VM.

**What broke it.** One of three GN-established pairs conflicted: `0x048D
openfullscreenmenu_48d` resolved to `00346DA0` in the table, while GN evidence gave
`003462D0`. Reading both bodies settled it against the catalog's argument counts:

- `003462D0` pops **two** VM operands and drives `002E1A60` → `openfullscreenmenu_48d` (2 args)
- `00346DA0` takes **none** and returns an int → consistent with `getmapgroundtype_48c` (0 args)

**The GFZ was right; the fresh derivation was wrong.** The index mapping is off by one at
`0x048C`/`0x048D` while exact at `0x021A` and `0x040C` — so the table contains a discontinuity
of unknown location. Opened as **I-6**; blocks `DOCUMENTED`.

**Why the aggregate checks could never have caught this.** A systematic off-by-one still lands
on a valid, correctly-owned neighbouring function in the same subsystem. Every summary
statistic stays green. Only a per-row semantic check — argument count against body — exposes
it. **This is the clearest demonstration yet that favourable aggregates do not establish
per-row correctness.**

**A correction to the correction.** This audit was prompted by the observation that *the GFZ
can be wrong* — true, and now recorded in the evidence standard. Testing it here produced the
opposite result: the older claim held and the new one failed. The rule is **settle conflicts
with evidence**, not *distrust the older claim*. Deferring to the fresh derivation would have
been the same error as deferring to the GFZ, in the other direction.

**Documents affected:** `01-Script-VM-Native-Bridge/scriptvm-native-dispatch-table.md`
written as `PARTIAL` with the failure stated in its header rather than buried.
**Propagation:** none — nothing had been built on the mapping.

### 2026-09-02 — provenance-closure campaign, and the first reading of the residual

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26…` · parent `2ed8affb…` · explicit 38003 / unresolved 158
**Scope:** the 13 documents of the AH provenance register, plus `the-unresolved-158.md`
**Tool run:** `check_provenance.py` 29/43 → **43/43** on the current parent ·
`verify_doc_addresses.py --all` 527 entry / 37 interior / **0 ghosts** ·
`check_coverage.py` consistent, 43 documents / 26 categories

The AH register was opened because 14 documents carried stamps naming a **superseded** GZF parent.
The rule adopted then was that a stamp is a claim about work performed, so it may never be
rewritten — only re-earned. `check_provenance.py` was deliberately built **without** a `--fix`.
This campaign closes the register by re-derivation. Two of the thirteen changed as a result.

| Document | Claim attacked | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `native-command-seam.md` | "a *different*, **8-entry** pending action-selection queue" | read the queue bound directly instead of trusting the number | **OVERTURNED** — the `8` is a loop trip count; `& 0x3f` makes the ring **64** entries, drained ≤8 per call |
| `texture-mip-local-memory-budget.md` | "budget reality for texture mods: ~4 MiB" | if `3*w*h` used **PC** dimensions the subtraction would underflow and the budget would be a no-op | **SURVIVED, EXTENDED** — both globals have exactly one writer, `0x200` and `0x1C0`; 512×448 is PS2 NTSC, so the budget is a fixed **1.375 MiB / 176 GS pages** |
| `the-unresolved-158.md` | "~23 index constants shifted by exactly **+2**", "all 1,228 differing bytes accounted for" | re-diff the two twins at byte level against the EXE | **OVERTURNED in part** — 1,228 is right; the classification was not. **42** single-byte `+2` shifts, and **two** of `+59` |
| `two-layer-effect-model.md` | the two-layer merge is the engine-wide convention | look for a subsystem that tests one layer alone | **SURVIVED, EXTENDED** — three further independent sightings, now **ten** |
| `rng-streams.md` | LCG constants and consumer census | already falsified and repaired twice today | **SURVIVED** (§8b previously overturned and rewritten) |
| `mweather-resource-format.md` | 9-bit packed table | re-read the three extractors | SURVIVED — bit offsets 0/3/7 into one shared reader |
| `weather-apply-and-environment-materialization.md` | `0026D910` "is not a setter" | check whether it is a thin writer | SURVIVED — 418 B across MapRef, save payload and Presentation |
| `weather-slot-state-model.md` | `+0x1061` gates `+0x1060` | look for an ungated write | SURVIVED — the policy byte gates the write and is cleared after |
| `ranged-weapon-recipes.md` | "**109** damage recipes" | find the bound in the resolver | SURVIVED — `if (0x6c < bVar1)`, twice, so IDs 0..108 |
| `weather-probability-and-transition-roll.md`, `field-init-weather-to-legacyps2gs-rebuild.md`, `capability-inhibition-policy.md`, `ui-request-router.md` | per register | per register | SURVIVED (see AH-3, AH-5, AH-10, AH-11) |

**Overturned:**

1. **The 8-entry queue.** `BattleUnit_ProcessPendingActionSelectionQueue` sets `lVar4 = 8` as a
   *drain limit*, then advances its read index with `& 0x3f`. The capacity is 64. **Why the error
   was reachable:** in a short queue-draining function the one small integer near the top reads
   like a size, and it is the only number in the body that is *not* about capacity. The correction
   makes the two rings structural twins — same paired byte indices, same 8-byte stride, same
   mod-64 advance — which *strengthens* that document's warning never to merge them.
2. **The twin byte account.** The earlier reading generalised "+2" from a sample. Re-diffing all
   1,228 bytes gives 395 displacement runs (each shifted by exactly −`0x7810`, the inter-function
   distance, with borrow propagation), 42 single bytes at `+2`, and **2 at `+59`**
   (`0x0A → 0x45`). **Why it was reachable:** the sample was real and the pattern was real; it was
   simply not checked to exhaustion. The two outliers are now the most informative bytes in either
   function, because they are the sites that do *not* follow the specialisation.

**Propagation:**
- `two-layer-effect-model.md` reopened — `BattleUnit_IssueCommand`, `FUN_00313DB0` and
  `BattleUnit_ProcessPendingActionSelectionQueue` all compute the engine-wide predicate, taking it
  from seven independent sightings to **ten**.
- `native-command-seam.md` gained a corroboration it previously only claimed as *consistent*:
  `BattleUnit_IssueCommand` is where `qwUnitFlags` bit `0x4000` is **set**, and separate work had
  already established where it is consumed. Producer and consumer were read independently and meet.
- `texture-mip-local-memory-budget.md` §6 rewritten from an approximation to a fixed number, and
  open question **D-5** advanced from OPEN to PARTIAL — the three reserved surfaces are now known
  to be 512×448 at 4 B/pixel, 0.875 MiB each; only their role labels remain inference.

**Structural changes:**
- `Tools/ghidra/scripts/DumpDataXrefs.java` — **new**. Dumps every reference to an address with its
  referencing function and instruction, separating reads from writes. The call-graph dump records
  function→function edges only and cannot answer *"who writes this global?"* — the question that
  settled both the GS dimensions and the command ring's sole producer. It also strips a UTF-8 BOM
  from its input, having lost a target to one on first use.
- `the-unresolved-158.md` restructured: it is no longer a document purely about absence. Five
  functions read, §8b corrected, §9 (the first five) and §10 (structure) added.

**A method error worth recording.** The residual set was recomputed from `graph/functions.tsv`
during this pass and came to **133**, because the derivation treated any `tags` value as a
CodeDomain assignment — but `ContextAuditV108` and `V102_InputCategoryParse` are audit and parse
markers, not the third explicit layer. This is the **second** time a fresh derivation of this set
has disagreed with the ledger and been the party in error. The ledger has been right both times.
The lesson already recorded in §8 — *derive independently, but when the derivation disagrees,
suspect the derivation* — held again.

### 2026-09-02 — falsification backlog, pass 1: third-party inventory

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26…` · parent `2ed8affb…` · explicit 38003 / unresolved 158
**Scope:** `23-Third-Party-Libraries/third-party-middleware-inventory.md`
**Tool run:** full `CodeDomain.ThirdParty.*` census (690 tagged functions, 46 distinct tag strings,
12 libraries) · raw string search of the authorized EXE

| Document | Claim attacked | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `third-party-middleware-inventory.md` | `libvpx VP8 1.6.0` and `zlib 1.2.11`, both **tier 3 — inherited from GFZ tags** | a version string in the binary disagreeing with the tag | **SURVIVED, tier 3 → 2** — each library states its own version in the image |
| same | per-library function counts, balanced by an `(audit-tag residue) 5` line | recount the census grouped by library | **OVERTURNED** — Bullet 120 not 119, libvpx 73 not 70, a zlib adapter omitted; the 5 are attributable, not residue |

**Overturned:** the residue line. Counts had been taken per *exact tag string*, so functions carrying
a longer, more specific tag (`…LibVPX_VP8_1_6_0.Vp8MbPostProcDownC`) fell out of their library's row
into a remainder. **The most precisely identified functions were the ones lost** — a grouping key
finer than the concept being counted drops its best-attributed members first.

**Extended:** a new fact from the banner `WebM Project VP8 Decoder v1.6.0` — only the **decoder** is
linked; no encoder banner exists in the image.

**Method note.** The first census run truncated to the top 40 tag strings and its per-library sums
disagreed with the document. Those sums were not reported and no correction was made from them; the
census was re-run complete first. A disagreement computed from truncated data is not evidence.

**Propagation:** none — no other document cites these counts.

### 2026-09-02 - falsification backlog, pass 2: authored-data table registry

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...` - explicit 38003 / unresolved 158
**Scope:** `02-Resource-And-Asset-Pipeline/authored-data-table-registry.md`
**Tool run:** `DumpDataXrefs.java` over 71 targets spanning the array plus two slots either side -
2,374 references, classified read / write / data

| Document | Claim attacked | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `authored-data-table-registry.md` | "60 of 63 slots referenced; `02EBF178`, `02EBF188`, `02EBF198` have **no** code reference" | one reference to any named slot that is not a load | **OVERTURNED on 2 of 3** - `02EBF178` has 2 writes, `02EBF188` has **93** writes; only `02EBF198` is genuinely dark. 62 of 63, not 60 |
| same | the span is a uniform 63-slot pointer registry | a slot whose reference signature differs | **OVERTURNED in part** - the clean pointer run is `02EBF008`-`02EBF170` (46 slots); above it the signature changes to writes plus `CMP` scalars |

section tabulating all three such failures to date (call-edge census / load scan / uncontrolled
string search) with four binding rules - write-census for globals, positive-control every zero,
never conclude from truncated output, and a negative about a function is not a negative about its

**Extended, and this is the substantive gain:** three of the seven rolls are **roulette-wheel

the authored data would be malformed under any other modulus. This is the numeric core of "keep your
chain up for better drops": rank 0 yields outcome 0 with certainty; the rarest outcomes exist only
at rank 2-3 and only at 5%.

|---|---|---|---|

**The sweep's first casualty was work from this same session.** The cause was **not** the

is **sparse** - six live request ids, not a range of twenty-four - which is the load-bearing fact for
a modder.

| Document | Claim attacked | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| reflection doc | **4,557** reflection functions | a materially different total from an independent census | **SURVIVED exactly** - 4,557, across 4,557 *distinct* functions |
| same | the per-family breakdown | recount each named family | **CORRECTED** - 8 of 10 undercounted; 256 functions misfiled into `(remaining)` |

now disagreed with a recorded figure three times in this database. Twice the record was right - a

sites* differ. The same test isolated the two informative bytes among 1,228 in the residual twins

`edges.tsv` row semantics

| Document | Claim attacked | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| item doc | the **asymmetric** test `record(secondary)[0x11] == record(primary)[0x09]` | an operand mix-up | **SURVIVED exactly** |
| same | §7's own open question - does any caller test the reverse direction? | a call with the operands swapped | **ANSWERED: no** - the one caller has two call sites and **both** put slot 0 in the secondary position |
| same | the `0xFFFF` guard | what it actually returns | **EXTENDED** - returns **true**; an empty slot is compatible with everything |

**The asymmetry is real and consistently oriented.** `+0x11` is always read from slot 0, `+0x09`
always from the item being fitted against it. P-2 (what the bytes mean) stays open, but the
direction is now fixed - which is the part a modder editing them needs.

**A tooling defect found, affecting more than this document.** `002F9F20 -> 002F7EC0` shows **1
edge** but the body has **2 call sites**. `edges.tsv` holds exactly one row per caller-callee pair
(90,525 rows, 90,525 distinct pairs, zero duplicates), so an edge count is a **distinct-caller**
count and never a call-site count.

**Self-retraction.** Pass 9 (accessor hubs) reported that the hub tables "survive a check they did
not claim - edges equal distinct callers, so no function calls any of these hubs twice." **That
inference is vacuous**: the identity holds by construction for every function in the binary. It is
retracted in place; the row counts it accompanied are unaffected. Added as rule 6 in the evidence
standard: never phrase an edge count as "called N times", and never infer anything from
`edges == distinct callers`.

Prompted by pass 11, which found that `edges.tsv` holds one row per caller-callee pair, so an edge
count is a **distinct-caller** count and never a call-site count. A newly found failure mode is

| Claim | Source | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `capability-inhibition-policy.md` - "29 direct call sites across 25 functions" | instruction-level | **EXACT** - measured 29 sites / 25 functions |
| `heading-speed-to-position-delta.md` - "Movement... 10 call sites, against Combat AI's 5" | edge census | **MISLABELLED** - those are caller counts; the true call-site figures are **11** and **7** |
| `the-unresolved-158.md` - "`002AE610` called **twice** by `002AC5F0`" | body read | **CORRECT** - both calls visible in the decompiled body |
| `party-roster-and-control-suppression.md` - "appears twice in that gate" | body read | **CORRECT** |

**Only one document was wrong, and its conclusion survives.** Movement leads every owned subsystem
on *both* measures - 11 call sites to Combat AI's 7, 10 distinct callers to 5 - so the finding
"Movement is the single largest owned consumer of the combat slot pool" stands. Only the labels were

census **cannot** produce, so it must have been measured at instruction level. It got the
distinction right before the rule existed, and a verification note now records that.

**Pattern across sweeps.** This is the third database-wide sweep triggered by a defect found in one
document (after the switch-label sweep and the counted-table sweep). All three found the same shape
of result: **one or two real errors, and a control case that had already got it right.** The control
cases are what make the corrections diagnosable rather than merely fixable.

### 2026-09-02 - O-4 chased: the battle runtime mode ladder, read in full

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Scope:** open question **O-4**, opened one pass earlier
**Tool run:** full decompile of `0030D9A0`, `00303D90`, `00303EE0`, `002EF3C0`, `0030DA10`;
byte-pattern scan of `.text` for the displacement `0x00005B04`

**Not a backlog pass - a question chased instead.** Pass 14 found that seven sites across four
subsystems gate on "mode == 2" without anything in the database saying what the mode was. A
predicate that many places depend on was worth more than the next unaudited document.

**Answered.** `BattleRuntime_GetMode0To5FromFlagsAndFieldBit15` is a **strict priority ladder** over
one flags word at `state+0x5B04`: bit 3 -> 5, bit 2 -> 4, **field-record bit 15 -> 3**, bit 1 -> 2,
bit 0 -> 1, else 0. Only four bits are consulted and the first match wins.

**The result that matters.** **Mode 3 is tested before mode 2.** Setting an area's authored
field-record bit 15 forces the mode to 3, so every `== 2` test silently stops matching. The
"per-area waivable" behaviour recorded in the party document is therefore **priority pre-emption
inside this ladder**, not a parallel exemption check - a sharper statement than the "two independent
routes" phrasing used one pass earlier, which is corrected in place.

**Found alongside:**
- `00303EE0` / `00303D90` are the getter and setter for flags bit 1. Enabling writes the float
  `0x43340000` = **180.0f** to `+0x5AE4`; disabling reaches into **party roster slot 3**, the guest
  slot identified in the party document.
- **36 sites across 18 functions** touch `+0x5B04`, including Save/Load, UI, World/Area/Field and
  Combat Action.
- The block is **captured into a transition record and restored** - the mode is persisted state, not
  transient. Directly relevant to XIIOnline: two clients can disagree about it across a transition.
- `DAT_02EBF190` is the runtime state block that `authored-data-table-registry.md` §8b identified as
  the single non-table slot; `0x5B04` = 23,300 is consistent with its recorded ">= 23 KB" size. Third
  independent confirmation of that finding.

**Structural change:** new document
`00-Engine-Core-Runtime/Battle-Runtime-Mode/battle-runtime-mode-ladder.md` (PARTIAL). The ladder,
its inputs and its persistence are tier 1; **what the six modes mean is explicitly not claimed**, and
O-4 stays open on that half.

### 2026-09-02 - O-4 continued: two of the six modes are dead code

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Scope:** `00-Engine-Core-Runtime/Battle-Runtime-Mode/battle-runtime-mode-ladder.md`
**Tool run:** decompile of `00307200`, `00307240`, `003072A0`, `003072E0`, `00304140`, `00313550`,
`00313840`, `003135E0`, `00313650`, `00306760`; caller census of every bit accessor

**Finding: modes 4 and 5 cannot occur.** Flags bits 1, 2 and 3 each have a getter/setter pair of
identical shape. The bit-2 and bit-3 pairs have **zero callers**, in either direction. That alone
would not settle it, so **all 36 sites touching `+0x5B04` were read for what they write**: every
write is `| 1`, `& ~1`, `| 2` or `& ~2`, plus three whole-word save/restore copies and one
whole-word zero. **Nothing sets bit 2 or bit 3.**

The effective ladder is therefore three tests deep, with four reachable modes (0, 1, 2, 3) - and
**mode 3, the authored per-area bit, outranks every mode the engine can actually produce.**

**Self-correction.** The document written one pass earlier said the authored bit *"outranks two of
the six modes"*. That was wrong twice over: by priority it outranks **three** (2, 1, 0), and since
4 and 5 are unreachable it outranks **all** of them. Corrected in the headline and in §2.

**Also mapped.** Bit 0 is driven by a **UI**-side family (`00313550`, `00313840`, `00313650`,
getter `003135E0`); bit 1 from Combat Action, Audio and two adapters.
`BattleAction_UpdateSpecialPresentationSequence` is the **only** function that manipulates both,
consistent with being the heaviest user of the word at six sites.

**Caveat recorded, not assumed away.** The save/transition path copies the whole word, so a
hand-edited save could carry bits 2 or 3 and reach modes 4 or 5 - behaviour no shipped code path
produces or tests.

### 2026-09-02 - thunk sweep, and a self-refutation one tick old

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Scope:** every address the database cites, checked for thunked reach
**Tool run:** decoded every function of <=16 bytes beginning `E9` (`JMP rel32`) and resolved its
target; joined against the 537 addresses cited by the database

Prompted by pass 15, where a 5-byte thunk carried 47 callers a documented count of 65 had missed.

**The image contains 835 bare `JMP rel32` thunks forwarding to 750 distinct targets.** A caller
census of a *target* does not see them.

| Cited function | Direct | Via thunk | Union | Consequence |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `00682D20` Lua push routine | 7 | **834** | **841** | nearly all 1,219 bindings funnel through it |
| `00377C20` field-record bit 15 | 65 | 47 | 110 | corrected in pass 15 |
| `00303EC0` mode-2 predicate | 6 | **15** | **21** | my own document said "six callers" |
| `00263750` `PartyRoster_GetActorBySlot` | 43 | 12 | 55 | |
| `003072x0` mode 4/5 accessors | **0** | **1 each** | 1 each | **refutes a finding two ticks old** |

**Self-refutation.** Two ticks ago this log recorded that *"modes 4 and 5 are dead in the shipping
binary"*, because their accessors had zero callers and no other site wrote bits 2 or 3. **The first
leg was wrong.** All four accessors are reached through thunks, and **every caller is
`Script_VM_Native_Bridge`**:

```
00307200 (set bit 3 -> mode 5)  <- 0037D110 <- 00351E50
00307240 (set bit 2 -> mode 4)  <- 0037D120 <- 00351B40
003072A0 (get bit 3)            <- 0037C890 <- 003573A0
003072E0 (get bit 2)            <- 0037C8B0 <- 00356DF0
```

**Modes 4 and 5 are script-set modes**, not dead code - which is a far better result than the
claim it replaces, and it completes the ladder into an authority hierarchy: **script VM (5, 4) >
authored area data (3) > combat/audio (2) > UI (1) > nothing (0)**. A running cutscene outranks the
zone's data, which outranks combat, which outranks the interface.

**The timing is the lesson.** The thunk blind spot was documented in pass 15 for *another*
document's caller count, and then committed in my own work **one tick later**. Knowing a failure
mode is not the same as having a check for it. Added as rule 6 of the evidence standard: **before
claiming a function is uncalled, resolve the thunks that point at it** - with the sweep script to
make it mechanical rather than remembered.

**Documents corrected:** the battle-runtime-mode ladder (headline, section 2b rewritten, caller
count 6 -> 21, evidence row, modding note, open questions) and the Lua bindings document (push
routine reach 7 -> 841).

### 2026-09-02 - O-4 largely answered: modes 4 and 5 are named by the game's own script verbs

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Tool run:** decompile of `00351B40`, `00351E50`, `003573A0`, `00356DF0`; lookup in
`Tools/work/rtti/scriptvm_dispatch.tsv`

The thunk sweep established that modes 4 and 5 are set by the script VM. Reading the four natives
and looking them up in the dispatch map names them:

```
0x050F  seteventpartymode      1 arg   -> 00351B40 -> bit 2 -> MODE 4
0x0510  geteventpartymode      0 args  -> 00355FE0
0x0513  geteventpartymodebit   0 args  -> 00356DF0 -> reads bit 2
0x0514  seteventparty2mode     1 arg   -> 00351E50 -> bit 3 -> MODE 5
0x0515  geteventparty2mode     0 args  -> 00356370
0x0516  geteventparty2modebit  0 args  -> 003573A0 -> reads bit 3
```

**The names are verified, not merely looked up.** `scriptvm-native-dispatch-table.md` warns its
index mapping is wrong in at least one region and that a row is *"a lead, not fact"* until the
handler's argument count is checked against the catalog. **That check passes on all four**: the
`set` verbs take 1 argument and their handlers contain exactly one
`VMValueStack_PopInt32CoerceFloat32`; the `…bit` verbs take 0 arguments and their handlers contain
exactly one `VMResult_WriteInt32`. This is the first time that document's prescribed check has been
applied and passed, and a note recording it was added there.

**Complementary evidence:** bits 0 and 1 have **no script verbs at all**, confirming they are
engine-internal - UI and combat respectively.

**What it reframes.** The ladder is not a generic "battle runtime mode" - it is a **party-control
authority order**:

```
5, 4   event script   (seteventparty2mode / seteventpartymode)
3      authored area data
2      combat / audio
1      UI
0      nothing
```

That is why its consumers are `PartyControl_RecomputeSuppressionFromLeaderBattleState` and
`InputGameplay_ArbitrateDigitalInputAndModalState` rather than anything about damage, and why the
bit-1 setter reaches into party roster slot 3. **During a cutscene the script asserts an event party
mode and overrides the zone's data, combat and the interface at once** - which is why normal control
and gambit behaviour stops during events: not because each system tests for "in a cutscene", but
because one number changed underneath all of them.

**O-4 goes from PARTIALLY to LARGELY ANSWERED.** Modes 0-2 are still unnamed in their own terms.

**Two process failures in this tick, both caught and both worth recording.**

1. **A staged batch was never committed.** The patch that rewrote section 2b built a `dbpatch.Batch`
   with four replacements - including the document's headline - then performed the 2b rewrite by a
   *direct file write*, then built a **second** batch and committed only that. `b.commit()` was
   never called. The result was a document whose section 2b said modes 4 and 5 are script-set while
   its headline still said they were unreachable - **self-contradictory, and neither the link check
   nor the address check can see that.** Fixed by re-applying the missing edits.
   *Lesson: `dbpatch` prevents partial application within a batch; it cannot prevent a batch that is
   never committed. Mixing a direct write into a batched patch is what hid it.*

2. **The audit-log entry was written by a separate interpreter invocation**, so when the document
   patch aborted the log still landed - the exact failure `dbpatch` was built to stop, reintroduced
   by splitting the work across two `python` calls instead of one. The log described naming work
   that was not yet applied, for the length of one command.
   *Lesson: the log write must be in the same process, after the commit - not merely later in the
   shell script.*

Both were repaired within the tick, and the document now reads consistently.

### 2026-09-02 - new check: cross-document fact consistency

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Tool run:** `analysis-kit/gfz-scripts/check_consistency.py`, new

**Why.** A document was left self-contradictory earlier the same day - a headline saying two modes
were unreachable above a section saying the script VM sets them. **Neither `check_links.py` nor
`verify_doc_addresses.py` can see that**, because both check form (do links resolve, do addresses
exist) rather than content. Four checks ran at every commit and none of them read what the documents
actually claim.

**What it checks.** For every address the database cites, it collects each stated **size**, **name**
and **caller count**, then flags any address described two incompatible ways - within a document or
across the set.

**Two instrument failures caught while building it, both by its own output.**

1. The first version extracted **6 names from 45 documents**, because its pattern matched only the
   inline form ```ADDR` `Name``` and the database overwhelmingly uses table cells
   (`| ADDR | Name | size |`). It reported "consistent" while seeing almost nothing. The final
   version extracts **189**. The summary counts are printed precisely so that this failure mode is
   visible rather than silent - positive-control every zero, including a checker's own.
2. The fixed version then reported **4** disagreements, of which **3 were false positives**: the
   PPFX tables have a *class* column beside a *method* column, and `Phyre::checkPhyreObject` differs
   from `checkPhyreObject` only by namespace. A compatibility rule now treats names as agreeing when
   one qualifies or extends the other. **A checker that cries wolf gets ignored**, which matters more
   here than recall.

**The one real finding.** `0026D910` carries two names: `WorldField_InitializeCurrentFieldRuntimeParameters`
(the GFZ's) and `WorldField_ApplyWeatherSlotAndDerivedEnvironmentState` (this database's, adopted
deliberately because the body is a multi-subsystem apply owner rather than a setter). **Both appear
in one document with nothing saying they are the same 418-byte function.** Fixed by recording the
equivalence in both weather documents rather than by dropping either name - the GFZ name is needed to
trace back to the annotation set, the database name carries a justified reading.

**Result: 45 documents, 122 sizes, 189 names, 7 caller counts - one disagreement, now resolved.**

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Scope:** `24-Compiler-And-CRT-Runtime/Binary-Hardening-And-Hooking/image-hardening-cfg-aslr-dep-and-stack-cookies.md`

**Chosen because the document calls itself the most useful page here for anyone hooking FFXII**, and
every claim in it is a header field - so every claim is exactly checkable in one pass.

| Claim | Result |
|---|---|
| `ImageBase 0x00120000`, no ASLR, DEP on, CFG off, `SecurityCookie 0x01F44830`, `__guard_check_icall_fptr 0x008C31C0`, `0016D6A0` = `ret 0` | **ALL SURVIVED exactly** |
| CFG "compiled in, shipped off" | **STRENGTHENED** - load-config `GuardFlags = 0x100` = `CF_INSTRUMENTED` with `CF_FUNCTION_TABLE_PRESENT` **absent**; the binary says so itself |

short, inside `.pdata`. **On the page that presents itself as the hooking reference, an address off
by the image base is the worst error to ship** - and section 4 of the same document states the very
rule it broke: Ghidra VA equals runtime VA because the base is already included.

shipped.

virtual size `0x7A0800`; the true value is `0x7A0635` (the former is aligned). The percentage is
unchanged at two decimals, so that document stands, with the discrepancy recorded here.

### 2026-09-02 - the address checker had never looked at data addresses

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Tool run:** `verify_doc_addresses.py`, widened

Pass 16 corrected two section addresses that were RVAs written as VAs. Sweeping for more of the
same exposed something larger about the **checker** rather than the documents.

**The gap.** `verify_doc_addresses.py` matched `00[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}` - only the `.text` range. Every
`.data` and `.rdata` citation was therefore **invisible to it**, including load-config and registry
globals the database leans on: `01F44830` (SecurityCookie), `02EBF190` (the runtime state block),
`0209C4D0` (the actor registry), `02EBF0C0` (loot profiles). **51 cited addresses had never been
checked by any tool**, across five checks run at every commit.

**Result of widening.** All 49 in-image citations resolve to real sections - **no ghosts**. Coverage
went from 683 to **757** verified addresses, adding **73 data citations**.

| Bucket | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| entry | 636 | 636 |
| interior | 38 | 38 |
| `.text` non-function | 2 | 2 |
| **data (`.rdata`/`.data`)** | **5** | **78** |
| **`.pdata`/`.xdata` (banned as evidence)** | — | **1** |
| literal | 2 | 2 |

**New bucket: `unwind-BANNED`.** The evidence standard bans `.pdata`/`.xdata` as proof, so a
citation landing there is now called out by name. There is exactly one, in
`the-unresolved-158.md`, and it is **deliberate** - that document cites a `.pdata` entry precisely
to say it is inadmissible. The bucket exists so a future one cannot slip in unnoticed.

**Two non-addresses correctly rejected.** `0EE477C3` and `0966B7B4` are **body-hash prefixes**, not
addresses. Widening the pattern made them visible, and a context rule excludes them.

**That exclusion rule then produced a false positive of its own.** Written as "hex followed by
optional whitespace and an ellipsis", it wrongly dropped `002AF340 …` - a real address at the end of
a truncated list. The discriminator is the whitespace: a truncated **hash** elides its own tail
(`0ee477c3...`), a truncated **list** elides further items (`… `). Fixed, and all three cases are
positive-controlled in the tool's docstring: `002AF340` kept, both hash prefixes excluded.

**No database error was found by this sweep** - the documents' data addresses were right all along.
What was wrong was that nothing had ever checked them.

### 2026-09-02 - falsification backlog, pass 17: static initialization and injection timing

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Scope:** `24-Compiler-And-CRT-Runtime/Static-Initialization-And-Lifetime/static-initialization-order-and-injection-timing.md`
**Tool run:** direct parse of the PE TLS data directory; full read of the 1,172-entry CRT
initializer table against `functions.tsv`

| Claim | Result |
|---|---|
| **1,172** eager CRT initializers at `008C31D8`-`008C5678` | **SURVIVED, and strengthened** - all 1,172 entries point into `.text` and **all 1,172 are known function entries**; zero nulls, zero strays |
| TLS `AddressOfIndex`, `AddressOfCallBacks`, empty callback array, 8-byte raw data | **ALL SURVIVED** |
| TLS directory at `0x01BCBED8` | **OVERTURNED** - that is the **RVA**; the VA is **`0x01CEBED8`** |

**Third RVA-as-VA error, all three in category 24.** With `.reloc` and `.gfids` from pass 16, the
cause is now identifiable: **PE data directories and the section table hold RVAs**, while **every
Ghidra address already includes the base**. Every Ghidra-sourced address in these documents is
correct; every hand-read PE structure address was short by `0x120000`. Mixing the two sources inside
one table is the mechanism.

**A guard for it was written and then deleted.** The obvious mechanical test - *outside the image,
inside it once the base is added* - **misses all three real cases**, because the image spans
`0x121000`-`0x3095400` and an RVA that large is itself a valid VA (`0x01BCBED8` resolves cleanly
into `.rdata`). Its only hits were **quoted float bytes**, `0000803F` (1.0f) and `0000F041` (30.0f),
which land in `.text` once the base is added purely by coincidence. **Two false positives, zero true
ones.** Removed, with the reasoning recorded in `verify_doc_addresses.py` so it is not retried.
Catching this class needs a citation's *semantics* checked against the real PE structure - which is
what a falsification pass does by hand.

**Injection-relevant finding worth flagging:** the TLS callback array is **empty**, confirmed at the
structure level. No TLS callback runs in this binary, so that pre-`main` hook point does not exist.

### 2026-09-02 - falsification backlog, pass 18: resource section addressing

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Scope:** `02-Resource-And-Asset-Pipeline/resource-section-addressing.md`
**Tool run:** full decompile of `00409C30`, `004096C0`, `00409600`, `00409780`, `00409A30`,
`00409210`

**A PE-structure sweep that found nothing, and a backlog pass that found plenty.** This document was
first checked for the RVA-as-VA class that broke two documents in category 24 - it is immune, because
its "sections" are **resource-file** sections, not PE sections. The PE sweep is therefore complete:
only category 24 was ever affected.

| Claim | Result |
|---|---|
| both tag wildcards (`0`, `@ALL`), NULL name wildcard, eight-dword 32-byte compare, `-1` sentinel, two storage modes, `DAT_02B62E10` re-resolve flag, fail-closed default | **ALL SURVIVED** - §2 needed no change |
| header is `0x30` bytes | **CONFIRMED by stride** - the finder walks `section_header + 1` on the `0x30` type, so the size no longer rests on a Ghidra type name containing a number |
| name padding | **REFINED** - the query is normalised, so the caller passes a plain C string |

**New: the container magic and a naming convention.** The finder validates the first header against
`0x50524640` = **`@FRP`**, requires `+0x04 == 0`, and reads the **section count from `+0x0C`**. Real
sections start at `+0x30`. With the `@ALL` wildcard this reveals a convention the document did not
state: **a tag beginning `@` is reserved** - `@FRP` for the container, `@ALL` for "any section" - so
authored tags should avoid `@`.

**Refined, with three consequences for a modder.** `FUN_00409210` zero-fills 32 bytes, `strncpy`s at
most 32, then forces a NUL at byte `0x1F`. Therefore: the caller supplies an ordinary C string and
the engine pads it; **section names are capped at 31 characters**, because byte 31 is destroyed in
every query; and a stored name must be **zero-padded** to be findable by name at all. The scratch
buffer is a single fixed global (`0x02B62E20`), so by-name lookup is **not re-entrant** - worth
knowing before calling it from a hook on another thread.

### 2026-09-02 - falsification backlog, pass 19: sound variant selection

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Scope:** `18-Audio/Sound-Selection/sound-variant-selection.md`
**Tool run:** callee census and full decompile of `007E5160`, `007E58D0`, `007E6360`, `007CF9C0`,
`007CF830`; inlined-constant search, positive-controlled against two known RNG consumers

**A document that refused to claim something, tested on exactly that refusal.** This one reads the
shape of `RandomSound` / `OrderSound` / `CycleSound` and then states *"No claim is made about
randomness or ordering."* The attack was to settle the question it declined.

| Claim | Result |
|---|---|
| the versioned accessor `(v >= 3) ? rec[0x10] : rec[4]` | **SURVIVED exactly** - `(1 < v) && (v != 2)` is `v >= 3`, in both the byte and boolean accessors |
| (withheld) does `RandomSound` use an RNG? | **ANSWERED: not either documented stream** |

**The finding.** `RandomSound::Select` has **no RNG callee** and **no inlined RNG constants** - no
`0x41C64E6D`/`0x3039`, no MT19937 constants. The second test is the one that counts, because
`rng-streams.md` §8b already recorded a call-edge census missing seven functions that inlined the
LCG. **The zero was positive-controlled**: the identical search finds the LCG recurrence in
`Loot_RollAdditionalItemChance` and the MT19937 thunk in the weather draw, and nothing in
`007E5160`.

**Bounded exactly:** not the shared LCG, not MT19937. A driver-local generator, a counter or a hash
would be invisible to both tests, so no claim of determinism is made either.

**The document's restraint is vindicated, and that is the point.** The obvious sentence -
*"RandomSound picks a random entry"* - would have implied a link to the gameplay RNG that does not
exist, sending anyone chasing determinism to the wrong stream. Withholding was the correct call, and
it can now be stated positively as what the function is **not**.

**Lead recorded:** `CycleSound::Select` calls `007E5E80`, which the other two do not - the most
promising place to find what actually separates Cycle from Random, given they share an accessor and
a second-pass shape.

### 2026-09-02 - a third random source, and a same-hour self-correction

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Scope:** `18-Audio/Sound-Selection/sound-variant-selection.md`, `21-RNG-And-Determinism/rng-streams.md`
**Tool run:** decompile of `007E5E80`; `rand()` search across the three `Select` bodies and the
whole call graph

**Self-correction.** Pass 19 (one tick earlier) tested `RandomSound::Select` for the two documented
RNG streams, found neither, and framed the source document's refusal to claim randomness as
vindicated. **The bounded sentence was true and remains true** - it uses neither the shared LCG nor
MT19937 - but the search never looked for the **CRT `rand()`**, which it does call. §9 of that
document is struck through and superseded by a new §10 rather than deleted.

**The rule, now read.** `RandomSound::Select` draws `rand()` **once**, takes `% 0x65` (101), and
walks the entries accumulating a per-entry weight until the running total reaches the draw. The same
pattern appears in `007E5E80`, reached from `CycleSound::Select`, which additionally stores the
chosen index as cycle position at record `+0x01` (`0xFF` when nothing qualifies). **`OrderSound::Select`
draws nothing at all** - the cleanest evidence the other two really are random, since all three
share the same container walk.

**A claim in that document is corrected as a consequence.** §2 called `FUN_007CF9C0` / `FUN_007CF830`
*"the differing per-entry predicate"*. They are not predicates: **`007CF9C0` returns a 0-100
selection weight** - the addend in the cumulative sum - and `007CF830` is the same byte as a boolean.

**A third RNG source is now on record.** `rng-streams.md` gains §8g: the engine has three sources,
not two - shared LCG (loot, chain, rewards), MT19937 (weather), and **CRT `rand()` (sound driver)**.
`rand()` is seeded and stepped independently, so **sound variant choice is not reproducible from a
gameplay seed and costs no gameplay draw**. For XIIOnline that means audio selection can diverge
between clients without any gameplay desync.

**The methodology lesson, which is the durable part.** Pass 19 **did** positive-control its zero -
and still reached a misleading conclusion, because the control proved only that the instrument could
find *the constants it was given*. **A positive control validates an instrument, not the completeness
of the question.** Recorded in the document rather than only here.

**Recorded as read, not resolved:** `% 101` with `<=` covers 101 outcomes for weights summing to
100, one more than the loot system's `% 100` with `<`. Off-by-one or deliberate headroom is not
established.

### 2026-09-02 - the third RNG source is not peripheral: 48 sites across 30 functions

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Tool run:** byte-level resolution of the `rand()` calls in `007E5160` / `007E5E80`; PE import-table
lookup of IAT slot `0x008C3098`; `.text` scan for every `FF 15` resolving to that slot

**Two corrections to work published earlier the same day, one of them substantive.**

**1. The evidence basis was the decompiler's label, and it needed to be the bytes.** The previous
entry claimed `RandomSound::Select` "calls the CRT `rand()`" because the decompiler printed
`rand()`. **Neither function contains a direct call to `rand`.** Both reach it through an `FF 15`
indirect call on IAT slot `0x008C3098` - which the import table resolves to **`rand` in
`api-ms-win-crt-utility-l1-1-0.dll`**. The claim survives; its footing was wrong until now.

**2. `rand()` is not the sound driver's private generator.** A `.text` census of that import slot
finds **48 call sites across 30 functions**: **Movement** 7 (`BattleLocomotion_TryStartRandomizedAvoidanceManeuver`,
`PartyFollow_SolveFormation`, ...), **Audio** 7, **Combat Action** 3 (including
**`BattleAction_ComputeChargeLimitTicks`**), **Presentation** 2, **Combat Formula** 1, **UI** 1,
**Lua** 2 (**`LuaMath_Random`, `LuaMath_RandomSeed`**), and 7 unowned.

So the third source **decides gameplay** - charge timing, locomotion, party formation - and **backs
Lua's `math.random`**, meaning `math.randomseed` reseeds it process-wide.

**A withdrawal.** The earlier entry stated that sound selection "costs no gameplay draw", so audio
could diverge between clients without gameplay desync. **That is withdrawn**: the same generator
serves both. Whether an audio draw actually perturbs a combat draw depends on whether they share a
thread - UCRT `rand()` state is per-thread - and **that is not established**, so no claim is made
either way.

**Why it was nearly missed twice.** There are **two** `rand` entry points: the import (48 sites) and
a statically linked `rand` at `0x00861F38` (1 site, from `00149610`). A census counting only direct
`E8` calls to the static one reports a single caller and misses every real user.

**Standing lesson, now demonstrated three times in a row.** A positive control validates an
instrument, not the completeness of the question - and a decompiler's symbol is a *claim* about the
bytes, to be checked against them like any other.

### 2026-09-02 - the import-table blind spot, measured and tooled

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Tool run:** new `analysis-kit/gfz-scripts/iat_xrefs.py` - resolves every IAT slot to `dll!symbol`
and counts `FF 15` call sites per slot across `.text`

**The scale of what the call graph cannot see.** An imported function is called through a pointer
slot, so it produces **no function-to-function edge**:

```
import slots referenced by an FF 15 call : 417 of 538
total indirect call sites through the IAT: 3,543
```

**None of those 3,543 sites appear in `edges.tsv`.** Any "who calls X" claim is understated whenever
X is imported. `rand` sat at 48 sites / 30 functions while the graph showed one caller - which is
exactly how it came to be recorded as a sound-driver detail rather than a gameplay RNG.

**Steam callback count confirmed by a second instrument.** `SteamAPI_RegisterCallback` has **8 call
sites**, `SteamAPI_UnregisterCallback` **8** - matching the **8 RTTI `CCallback<>` classes** found in
pass 12 (3 achievements, 1 overlay, 4 connection lifecycle). Two independent instruments, the same
number, and still **no registration for matchmaking or P2P**. A ninth registration would have to
exist for those interfaces to be in use, and there is none. Added to the Steam document, which
previously rested on RTTI names alone.

**Busiest imports, for orientation:** `_invalid_parameter` 434, `LeaveCriticalSection` 310,
`EnterCriticalSection` 286, `memmove` 244, `OutputDebugStringA` 150 - the last worth noting, since a
retail build still calls it from 93 functions.

**Two rules added to the evidence standard**, numbered 6 and 7:
- a direct-caller census misses imported callees entirely - use `iat_xrefs.py` for any import;
- **a decompiler's symbol is a claim about the bytes, not the bytes** - Ghidra printed `rand()` in
  two functions that contain no call to `rand`. Where a name carries a finding, resolve it.

### 2026-09-02 - falsification backlog, pass 20: EXP and LP award, formula completed

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Scope:** `13-Rewards-Progression-Economy/experience-and-license-point-award.md`
**Tool run:** full decompile of `Reward_ComputeExperienceForRecipient` (`002F8BB0`) and
`Reward_ComputeLicensePointsForRecipient` (`002F90C0`)

**A document that declared itself incomplete, finished.** It said *"Do not treat the formula as
complete"* and carried `<term>` placeholders. Nothing in it was contradicted; the placeholders are
now filled.

**EXP.** `base = (foe.bLevel - foe.bGrowthBaseLevel) * (int)S8[0x34] + (int)S7[0x34]`, then
**`base / count`** on the shared path and `base` on the solo path. The `<term>` was not a different
expression - **both paths compute the same base**, and sharing divides it by the number of eligible
recipients. So per-character EXP falls as more characters qualify while the total stays constant.

**LP.** `(foe.bLevel - foe.bGrowthBaseLevel) * (byte)S8[0x2F] + (byte)S7[0x2F]` - **different
offsets, byte-width rather than int, and never divided among recipients.** Both LP fields are
therefore capped at 255 where EXP's are 32-bit.

**Three modifier bits, in a two-layer pair.** `0x08` doubles EXP, `0x10` doubles LP, `0x20` zeroes
EXP - each tested in **both** `recipient[0x6B]` and `recipient[0x7B]`. In play these are the
machinery behind the game's EXP-doubling, LP-doubling and no-EXP effects; that correspondence is
inference, the arithmetic is read.

**Eleventh sighting of the two-layer convention, and the most informative one.** Every previous
sighting used the status masks at `+0x3C`/`+0x64`. This pair is `+0x6B`/`+0x7B`, so the two-layer
test is **a convention applied at several field pairs**, not a property of one pair of fields.
Propagated to `two-layer-effect-model.md`.

### 2026-09-02 - falsification backlog, pass 29: numeric formatting (headline RETRACTED)

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Scope:** `16-UI/Text-And-Number-Rendering/numeric-formatting-and-glyph-advance-layout.md`
**Tool run:** capstone disassembly of `002AE610` (302 instructions); `.rdata` read at `00916520`

**The document's headline claim is wrong and has been retracted.** It said digits are laid out at
the fixed width of the character `'0'`, which is why counting numbers do not jitter - a causal story
about something a player can see. It rested on a single decompiler line assigning a `ushort` into a
**3-byte** field, which is not the shape of an advance width. Disassembly settles it:

```
002AE931  movzx ecx, word ptr [r9+rax*2]   ; code = TABLE[ch-0x20]
002AE95F  mov   byte ptr [rsp+0x30], cl    ; stored as CHARACTER data, 1 byte
002AE96D  mov   word ptr [rsp+0x30], cx    ; ... or 2, chosen by cmp ax,0xDF
002AE9FC  call  0x2a9f00                   ; buffer address passed on
```

**The table holds character codes, not advance widths.** The value is written back out as text and
handed to `002A9F00`; the one-byte/two-byte choice is a multi-byte encoding decision. The real
advance is `xmm8`, accumulated **after** that call - so per-character advance comes from `002A9F00`
(2,304 B, unread), and `002AE610` computes no widths at all.

**The `'0'` read is neither hoisted nor a width.** `002AEA96 jl 0x2ae920` is a backward jump to the
loop head, so the read at `002AE984` is **inside** the loop; and it **overwrites the emitted
character** under a decrementing counter against a threshold. It is **padding** - emitting `'0'` -
which fits the minimum-width clamp and says nothing about spacing.

**Survived:** the power-of-ten table, re-read from `.rdata` - `1 ... 100000000`, next word `12047`,
so exactly nine entries.

**Root cause, and it is a rule already in the standard.** The decompiler named a register
`glyphTable` and the document **inherited that name as a fact**. Advance widths, hoisting,
anti-jitter and the modding advice about replacing a font all descend from an unchecked variable
name. *A decompiler's symbol is a claim about the bytes* - applied here to the one symbol nobody
checked.

**Lesson recorded in the document:** the player-facing sentence was the **least** evidenced part of
it. A story that neatly explains something familiar is the first thing to attack, not the last.
Section 1 now states what is known and explicitly states what is not; three new open questions
(**AC-8/9/10**) replace the withdrawn claim, including that nobody has actually measured whether
digit columns are even.

`0x02EBF138` as `base + id * stride`, and reads `rec[0x0C] bit 0x80000` / `rec[0x1E] == 1` to widen

```

```

with `1/256` read as the literal `0.00390625` at `009088D8`. The attack roll is **upward-only**:
`ATK + (rand() % (int)(ATK*12.5))/100`, so attack power lands in `[ATK, ATK*1.125)` and never below
the weapon's own Attack.

**Seven variants, differing in exactly the ways that matter.** Six measure against target `+0x2F`;
**`PrepareStrengthAttackVsMagickResist` measures against `+0x30` instead** - one changed offset is
the whole of "this weapon ignores Defence". `Speed` divides by **218**, not 256. `Vitality` is the
only one with **no `+1.0` floor**. `Scaled150` adds a `x1.5`.

**The stat block was cross-validated, not assumed.** The four `Reduce*` functions each name a stat
and read an offset: Strength `+0x2A`, Magick Power `+0x2B`, Defence `+0x2F`, Magick Resist `+0x30` -

with a floor of **1** when the stat byte is zero. Every attribute is a **single byte**, so all cap
at 255.

**`+0x2C` / `+0x2D` deliberately left unconfirmed** - Vitality and Speed rest on GFZ function names
only, unlike the five the `Reduce*` family pins. Recorded as **AJ-5** rather than asserted.

assert a final damage equation - the three scratch floats feed **45** unread CombatFormula functions
(380 sites on the multiplier slot alone). Seven open questions **AJ-1..AJ-7**.

### 2026-09-02 - falsification backlog, pass 32: AJ-2 answered, the damage equation

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Scope:** `08-Combat-Formula/Attack-Vs-Defense/attack-defense-preparation-and-stat-scaling.md`
**Tool run:** capstone disassembly of `BattleFormula_FinalizeTargetHpMagnitude` (`0038D280`, 180 B)
with **machine-resolved** RIP operands

**The document shipped refusing to state a damage equation.** That refusal was correct, and the
right attack on it was to go find the consumer. Found:

```
movss  xmm1, [02AEE058]   ATTACK
subss  xmm1, [02AEE05C]   DEFENCE
comiss 0.0, xmm1 / jbe    -> if negative: write 0 and RETURN
mulss  xmm1, [02AEE054]   MULTIPLIER
cvttss2si eax, xmm1       truncate toward zero
```

**`damage = trunc((ATK + variance - DEF) * (1 + (Level + Stat) * Stat / 256))`, floored at 0.**

**Three consequences read straight off the instruction order:**
1. **Subtraction precedes multiplication** - the multiplier scales the post-defence remainder. A
   weapon whose Attack does not exceed Defence deals **exactly zero** no matter the Strength or
   Level. Strength cannot rescue a weak weapon; only Attack can.
2. **The zero floor is hard and early** - `0` is written and the function returns *before* the
   multiplier is loaded. No minimum-damage-of-1 on this path.
3. **Truncation, not rounding** - `cvttss2si` rounds toward zero, so fractions are always lost in
   the target's favour.

**Every RIP operand was machine-resolved rather than computed by hand**, deliberately: this session
had already published one hex slip (`0x200` reported as `0x2000`), and the headline equation should
not rest on mental arithmetic.

**The honest boundary, stated in the document.** Between preparation and this finalizer sit element
affinity, combo, knockback, guard/parry and HP post-multipliers - **45** functions touch the scratch
record and most rewrite the very slots the equation reads. So the equation is exact **for the values
present when the finalizer runs**, not for those the preparation stage wrote. Registered as
**AJ-8**; the two result slots and their selector as **AJ-9**.

Document promoted **PARTIAL -> DOCUMENTED** for the arithmetic core.

### 2026-09-02 - falsification backlog, pass 34: AK-7 answered - the recipe interpreter

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Scope:** `08-Combat-Formula/Step-Table/combat-formula-step-table.md`
**Tool run:** capstone disassembly of `BattleFormula_ResolveTargetResult` (`00385F60`, 2,302 B)

**Pass 33 left an anomaly: recipes are lists of slot ids, yet a full scan found zero indexed
accesses to the table.** Either the recipe model was wrong or the scan was blind. **The scan was
blind.**

**The interpreter, read:**

```
lea    rbx, [rip-0x2663b7]                ; rbx = 00120000 = IMAGE BASE
movsxd rax, dword ptr [r13 + rbp*4]       ; slotId = list[i], SIGNED
call   qword ptr [rbx + rax*8 + 0x1dda5c0]; stepTable[slotId](rcx, rdx, r8)
cmp    dword ptr [02AEDFB8], 1 / je done  ; a step can abort the recipe
inc rbp / cmp rbp, r12 / jl loop
...
call   00390F20                           ; ApplyTargetStatusActionPostModifiers, unconditional
```

**Five facts fall out:** every step has the same three-argument signature (`rcx`,`rdx`,`r8`); ids are
**signed**, consistent with the `-1` terminator; **a step can abort the pipeline** by setting
`02AEDFB8` to 1, so a miss or immunity ends the recipe rather than running and discarding; one step
(`ApplyTargetStatusActionPostModifiers`) runs **outside** the loop and the abort check; and the
compiled fixed sequences from pass 33 use the same abort protocol.

**The base is now over-determined:** `00120000 + 0x01DDA5C0 = 01EFA5C0`, computed from the
dispatcher's own arithmetic. Third derivation, and the first genuinely exact one - derivation 1 was
the numerology retracted in pass 33; derivation 2 was the eleven-slot Bow recipe.

**Third instrument blind spot recorded.** The address is **image base (register) + RVA
(displacement)**. Pass 33 searched RIP-relative targets and `[reg*8 + VA]`; this form is neither.
Joining the other two - an edge list that sees `E8` but not `E9`, and a caller census blind to
address-taken refs - all three share a shape: *a census answering a narrower question than the one
asked*. **Standing rule: when reporting a zero, state which encodings were searched.**

**AK-7 closed; document promoted to DOCUMENTED.** The mechanism is fully read; what remains is the
meaning of the 125 unnamed steps (**AK-3**).

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Scope:** `04-Actor-Entity/Battle-Record-Kind/battle-record-kind-byte.md`
**Tool run:** full-image write census for byte writes to `[reg+5]` under the `+0x698` dataflow

**When the readers cannot settle a field, the writers usually can.** The new document refused every
reader-side reading of `record[5]`; this pass ran the writer census it had listed as never run.

**AL-5 answered: nothing writes the byte through the record pointer.** Strict census returns **0**
sites. The widened form returns exactly one function, whose write is not to the record. **The byte
is set when the record is installed and never touched again.**

**Who installs it:** of 17 eight-byte writes to `[reg+0x698]`, only two are on the battle-unit path -
`BattleUnit_ApplyUnitDefinition` (`0023ABFA`) and `BattleUnit_ResetStateForReuse` (`00236AB4`). The
other 15 are Audio-owned or unowned functions writing that offset on **a different structure** - the
same contamination that made the unfiltered `[reg+5]` scan useless.

**The byte is authored definition data.** `ApplyUnitDefinition` unpacks a cluster of small fields
from the record it installs - `[r15+4]`, **`[r15+5]`**, `[r15+6]`, `[r15+0x22]`, `[r15+0x23]`,
`[r15+0x27]`.

**This reframes AL-1 rather than answering it.** A *definition kind* can be shared by units that
behave differently in play - which is exactly why the party/foe reading failed. The contradiction
was never in the evidence; it was in assuming the field described a **side** rather than a **kind of
definition**. A reader-side census could never have separated them.

**New structure: `+4` and `+5` are one 16-bit field.** `ApplyUnitDefinition` reads
`movzx ebx, word ptr [rax+4]` - a word spanning both bytes - while `FUN_002F8E90` reads `+4` as a
type id (`0x1B..0x27`) and `+5` as the kind. **The kind is the high byte of a 16-bit identifier whose
low byte is a type**, consistent with the classifier consulting the low byte only for kind 0.
**AL-6.**

**A caveat on this document's own headline figure.** The record is stored at **both** `unit+0x698`
and `unit+0xE68` (`0023A91C`). The 104-site census keyed only on `+0x698`, so it **under-counts by
construction** - a second such limitation after the taint-drop-at-calls one already recorded.
**AL-7.**

### 2026-09-02 - falsification backlog, pass 38: the record is a window into an authored definition

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Scope:** `04-Actor-Entity/Battle-Record-Kind/battle-record-kind-byte.md`
**Tool run:** trace of the record's provenance through `BattleUnit_ApplyUnitDefinition`; full read of
`SpawnKeep_ResolvePrimaryEntry` (`00236100`, 56 B); machine-resolved RIP operand for the table
pointer

**The provenance chain, read end to end:**

```
movsx edx, byte ptr [rdi + 0x57]   ; index
mov   rcx, qword ptr [rdi + 0x40]  ; spawn keep
call  SpawnKeep_ResolvePrimaryEntry
sub   rax, -0x80                   ; record = definition + 0x80
```

**`SpawnKeep_ResolvePrimaryEntry` in full:** `keep[0]` is an entry count, `keep[1+index]` a
one-byte definition id, `0xFF` marks an empty slot, and the result is
`*(void**)0x0208E690 + id * 0x250`.

**What it settles:** the unit definition table pointer is **`0x0208E690`** (`.data`, null in the file
image so runtime-loaded), records are **`0x250` = 592 bytes**, ids are a **single byte**, and
`unit+0x6A0` is the record base while **`unit+0x698` is that same record + 0x80**.

**So the "battle record" is not a separate object** - it is a **window into the authored unit
definition**. Therefore `record[5]` is **byte `+0x85` of a 592-byte definition record**, and
`record[4..5]` is the definition word at `+0x84`.

**AL-1 is re-posed in its final form and simultaneously bounded:** the question is what definition
field `+0x85` enumerates - a question about a **data table**, not about code - and since the table is
runtime-loaded, it is **unanswerable from the executable alone**. Recording that boundary is worth
more than continuing to hunt it in the binary.

**A second document sharpened.** `battle-command-availability-and-reason-codes.md` asks what
`unit->[0x6A0][0]` masks `0x30`/`0x48` are (**AI-6**). `unit+0x6A0` is now identified as the
definition base, so that test reads **byte 0 of authored data**.

**A naming imprecision recorded rather than fixed.** "Battle record" was named from the access path
before its origin was known; it is really the tail of a definition record. The term stays because 82
readers reach it through `+0x698`, but the document now gives the true frame of reference.

New **AL-8**: what the 592-byte unit definition record contains.

### 2026-09-02 - falsification backlog, pass 41: AM-1 - the turn limiter is a hysteresis loop

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Scope:** `06-Movement-And-Navigation/Battle-Locomotion/battle-locomotion-steering-and-recovery.md`
**Tool run:** full capstone disassembly of `ApplyHeadingTurnLimiter` (`003364D0`, 564 B) with
machine-resolved RIP constants; identification of `Angle_NormalizeRadiansPi`

**The document published three angular constants and explicitly refused to say which did what. That
refusal was the thing to test - and one disassembly settles it.**

**The three angles are one mechanism:**

| angle | role |
|---|---|
| **45 deg** | deadband - at or below it **no turn starts** and the current heading is returned unchanged |
| **120 deg** | gates latching the **fast** turn rate (also requires `st[0x170] & 0x1C == 0x1C`) |
| **20 deg** | releases the latch; the turn finishes at the **slow** rate |

Entry at 45, escalate past 120, ease off inside 20, stop on arrival - **hysteresis with two rates**
(`st[0xEC]` slow, `st[0xF0]` fast), not three unrelated clamps. Turn direction is recorded in
`fl[0x21]` bits 1/2, and the "turning" flag `fl[0x38] & 8` is cleared only when the heading matches -
so **the deadband governs starting a turn, not finishing one**.

**Player-visible consequences now explained:** big reversals snap round then visibly slow as they
line up (120 latch, 20 release); and **course corrections under 45 deg produce no turn at all**,
which is why battle units so often walk slightly off-axis rather than aiming exactly where they go.

**A correction to my own document from the previous tick.** It grouped `ApplyStopAndTurn` and
`ApplySimpleHeadingLimit` with the limiter as "the mechanism behind the stop-and-pivot". **Neither is
called by the limiter, and neither is called from anywhere inside the family** - their only caller is
`00339F00`. The stop-and-pivot comes from the limiter's own deadband. Association by name proximity
again; corrected and registered as **AM-7**.

**Shared utility identified:** `Angle_NormalizeRadiansPi` (`0033CB70`, 128 B) normalises to
(-pi, pi] and has **25 call edges** image-wide - an engine helper, not a locomotion detail.

New **AM-8**: what `st[0x170] & 0x1C == 0x1C` tests.

### 2026-09-02 - falsification backlog, pass 42: AM-2 - the arrival curve

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Scope:** `06-Movement-And-Navigation/Battle-Locomotion/battle-locomotion-steering-and-recovery.md`
**Tool run:** full disassembly of `ComputeStepDistance` (`00339BF0`, 503 B) with machine-resolved
constants; identification of `Vector3_ComputeXZDistance`, `ActorRuntime_GetClass3FloatPair` and
`thunk_FUN_00253b90`

**The document had listed seven constants and said they were "not read".** Numbers on record without
their branches is exactly the state that produced a false elemental-affinity reading earlier today.
Read.

**They are not seven speed regimes - they are ONE quadratic arrival curve.** The step is
`rem^2 * speedB`, where `rem` is the distance still to cover **beyond the stop radius** `st[0xD0]`,
divided by a per-situation factor (`/7`, `/5`, `/3`, `/1.5` or `x0.25`). Units decelerate smoothly
into their stopping point rather than running flat out and halting.

**`x0.99` is an overshoot guard.** If the computed step exceeds the remaining distance the unit moves
`dist * 0.99` instead - **landing 1 % short every frame**. Approach is asymptotic and a unit never
steps past its target, which is the visible creep at the end of a closing move.

**Distance is horizontal only** - `Vector3_ComputeXZDistance` ignores Y, so a target directly above
or below counts as distance zero to this solver.

**`00253B90` now appears in a THIRD documented system.** It selects both divisor pairs here, and is
already recorded as the capability-inhibition policy's bit-1 predicate and as a gate in the action
availability cascade. Capability, action availability and movement speed all branch on it.

**And it is reached through a `jmp` thunk** (`thunk_FUN_00253b90`, `0030C0D0`), so an edge-list
caller census of `00253B90` does not show this consumer - the `E8`-versus-`E9` blind spot recorded

### 2026-09-02 - falsification backlog, pass 44: the ScriptVM dispatch table is one column of three

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Scope:** `01-Script-VM-Native-Bridge/scriptvm-native-dispatch-table.md`
**Tool run:** full reads of `VMNativeCommandDispatch_InitializeFamilyTables` (`003DC2D0`),
`GetBeginCallback`, `GetPollCallback`, `GetResultCallback`; direct reads of the three callback
columns for every id this document names

**Found while reading the Script/VM category for an unrelated target** - the breadth check had just
identified Script/VM as the largest player-facing debt.

**The table is a three-callback native command table.** `InitializeFamilyTables` fills **16 family
tables**; twelve share a default, and families 0, 3, 5, 7 get their own. **Family 0's table is
`0x01EED700`, and its count field is 1496** - exactly the record count this document has reported
since it was written. The accessors fix the layout: `begin = tbl+8+32N`, `poll = tbl+16+32N`,
`result = tbl+32+32N`.

**This document has been reading the `result` column.** `0x01EED720 = tbl + 32`, so its "record N,
field +0" is `result(N)`. Verified against every id it names - `setweatherslot`, `getweatherslot`,
`getmapgroundtype_48c`, `openfullscreenmenu_48d` - all four match the result column exactly.

**Two long-running puzzles dissolve at once.**

*The GFZ "contradiction" was never one.* GN attributed `003462D0` to `openfullscreenmenu_48d`; the
table gave `00346DA0`. **Both are correct**: `003462D0` is that command's **begin** callback,
`00346DA0` its **result**. The arity argument in section 2 was sound and identified the two
callbacks, not two commands - a begin pops the operands (2), a result writes the return value (0).

*I-2 is answered.* The extra fields are the **next command's** callbacks, because the frames differ
by 24 bytes: `+0`=`result(N)`, `+8`=`begin(N+1)`, `+16`=`poll(N+1)`. That is why pass 33 found
`003462D0` at "record 0x048C field +8" - it is `begin(0x048D)`. It also explains the field-count
histogram: most commands are instantaneous and carry only a `result`, hence **1,155 records with
exactly one non-null field** and only **one** with four.

**Nothing extracted was wrong; the frame of reference was one column off.** Base, stride, extent, the
1,224 rows, 0 outside `.text`, 0 off a function entry, 1,166 distinct handlers, 58 shared and the
owner split all stand. Document promoted **PARTIAL -> DOCUMENTED**.

**Method note.** Three passes attacked this document's *numbers* and found them sound; the defect was
in what the numbers were numbers **of**. A correct measurement of the wrong column survives every
consistency check - which is why naming the structure, not re-verifying the values, is what finally
resolved it.

### 2026-09-02 - NEW SYSTEM: native command lifecycle (answers I-3)

**Program state:** snapshot `46f02e26...` - parent `2ed8affb...`
**Scope:** new `01-Script-VM-Native-Bridge/Native-Command-Lifecycle/native-command-lifecycle.md`
