**Three details only a read produces, and the third is the point of the whole exercise:**

- **An unchanged name is a no-op** — lengths, then `memcmp`, then a jump straight to cleanup. Setting
  the same name again re-classifies nothing and clears no flag.
- **Two flags, two different update rules, in one function.** Both zeroed on entry, but B is written
  with `cmovne` **against its own current value** — sticky — while A is written only on the positive
  path. *"I would not have believed that from a summary."*
- **`01DFE40C` is `-1` at rest.** It holds the slot index only during the call and is reset on **every**
  exit path, including the early ones. **Anything reading it from outside sees `-1`** — a
  *currently-being-set* indicator, not a record of the last slot used.

> **That last distinction is exactly what a five-document chain of entry-only citations gets wrong**,
> and it is the clearest demonstration yet of what the "leaned on and never opened" cut is measuring.

**What was not guessed:** what `sum_`, `spc_` and `0001` abbreviate. *"The evidence is that the strings
are matched, not what they stand for — and the obvious expansions are inviting enough that I have left
them out."*

### The tail-call hazard, checked rather than assumed

All three functions taken from the cut were disassembled to their last instruction **before a line of
any of them was read**: `002F7380` ends `ret` at `002F7652`, `002AAE40` at `002AB7C7`, `0020AC30` at
`0020AE6B`, **and no `jmp` leaves any of their extents.** The hazard did not apply — *measured, not
assumed.*

> **"Working from capstone rather than a decompiler makes me immune to that particular rendering, but
> not to the underlying mistake, so it was worth the one check."**

**A warning that turns out not to apply, checked in one step, is a warning that worked.**

### "Sixteen callees, each called once" — a static fact stated as a behavioural one

**Retracted by its own author within the hour.** `002AAE40` was reported as *"505 instructions,
sixteen distinct callees each called exactly once, almost no comparisons — a linear builder or
registrar"*, and the coordinator accepted it and said a document describing a registrar was worth
writing. **Then:**

```
002AB67A  jmp -> 002AAFD2      a backward jump spanning almost the whole body
```

**Nearly the whole function is one loop, and all sixteen call sites are inside it.**

> **A count of call sites is not a count of calls.**

**This is the same error shape as `001A9930`/`00193D50` being published as "45 and 33 arms" when they
were 45 and 33 *call sites* — arrived at independently, by a different session, on a different
function, from a different instrument.** Twice now, a static census has been read as a dynamic one.

**And the evidence that would have caught it was already in the histogram that produced the mistake:**
**`movups` 78, `movss` 50, `movaps` 34 — 162 of 505 instructions are SSE moves**, against 10 `cmp`.
The low comparison count is not *"no branching logic"*; it is **float work**. Per iteration the body
writes `1.0f` into two pairs of slots and computed pairs into four consecutive floats — **the corners
of a textured quad** — and preserves `xmm9`/`xmm13`/`xmm14`/`xmm15`, a register budget no integer
formatter needs. **It is a per-item quad emitter.**

**Caught by looking for backward jumps rather than trusting an instruction histogram.** The histogram
was not wrong; **the question asked of it was.**

### One field, two meanings, separated only by which pass is running

In `002F7380`:

> **`word +0x0E` on a record is a reference counter in pass 2 and is overwritten with a slot index in
> pass 3.** A reader arriving at pass 3 and calling it *"the count"* would be wrong, and **nothing but
> the pass separates them.**

`word +0x0C` marks a continuation, so a reference counts against a whole **run** of records rather
than a single one — which means even the counter is not counting what its name would suggest.

**Same family as the displacement trap** (`[rbx+0x24]` an accumulator, `[rsi+0x24]` a stats field) and
the width trap (an 8-byte store over two 4-byte fields): **complete, plausible, well-formed, and about
the wrong thing.** This is the third mechanism in that family found tonight, and the first where the
two meanings share **both** the base and the displacement — only *time* separates them.

### A rule that produced the wrong outcome while being followed correctly

**Rule 3 was followed exactly and the result was still bad:** findings staged in an inbox for someone
who had not read the function.

> **A rule that produces the wrong outcome when followed correctly is worse than one that is broken,
> because nothing flags it.**

And the amendment fixes what asking could not have: *"I would have kept asking permission each time."*
**The failure was not a session's judgement; it was the rule's, and only a session acting on it could
surface that.**

### An instrument's shape decides what can be absent

**Two gaps found hours apart turn out to be one hazard at two layers.**

- **The function list.** A caller census reported nothing writes a value; the only writer was a
  27-byte function **absent from `functions.tsv`**. The list covers **92.91 %** of its own span.
- **The encoding.** A census keyed on `mov reg, [reg+4]` missed `cmp byte ptr [reg+4], imm` —
  **precisely how the motivating site is written.** First run found **1** site; corrected, **7**.

> **An instrument's shape decides what can be absent from its output.** A list decides which functions
> can be missing; an encoding decides which instructions can be. **Neither absence looks like an
> absence — both look like a result.**

**And the honest half of the second one is the better half.** The 13-value band's count of **28** was
unaffected by the correction, because every band site happens to use the register form. *"That is
luck, not validation"* — and the document says so, rather than presenting 28 as robust.

### `record[+0x04]` is a partitioned number line, and the partition is stated in one place

```
0 … 6   |   7 … 25   |   26   |   27 … 39   |   40 +
```

**`Reward_ComputeLicensePointsForRecipient` tests `<= 6`, `== 0x1A`, `< 0x28` in sequence** — one site
naming the whole partition — and a Script-VM bridge classifies a record into **five** outcomes using
every boundary.

**The band `0x1B … 0x27` is one predicate inlined 27 times.** A census of every constant tested
against that byte found 28 sites using `0x1B`, and **27 are byte-for-byte `(type − 0x1B) <= 0xC`,
never once a different bound** — across ActorEntity, CombatAction, CombatFormula, CombatAI, Status,
Rewards and the Script VM.

> **A category consulted that widely, with no function of its own, is why it never acquired a name.**

**`0x1A`'s divergence is now located**, answering why two adjacent tests were written separately:

| | band `0x1B–0x27` | `0x1A` |
|---|---|---|
| experience recipient count | excluded | **excluded** |
| License Points | rejected | **accepted** |

**Had `0x1A` belonged to the band, `(type − 0x1A) <= 0xD` would have been smaller code and a silent
behaviour change.** *"Two tests where one would do is usually two different reasons"* — the reasons
coincide in one consequence and diverge in the other.

**The 28th site indexes rather than tests**: for one action id, `type − 0x1B` indexes a 13-entry table
that is an exact arithmetic progression, **`code = 42 + 3 × (type − 0x1B)`**.

> **The progression is the finding.** A hand-authored lookup would not be arithmetic — **the table
> exists because the codes are laid out three-per-type somewhere else**, and this is the cheapest way
> to reach the first of each block.

### The name that was not written

A thirteen-value category in this game has an obvious name. **Nothing in the corpus ties any span to a
player-facing concept** — no string, no table name, no label — so the spans are listed unnamed.

> **The measurement was easy and the temptation was the whole test. Naming it would have cost nothing
> today and been unfalsifiable forever.**

**And a correspondence held as a correspondence:** the Script-VM ladder tests `(type − 7) <= 0x12`,
**character-for-character the guest predicate from the party layer**, applied to a different field.
**No site has been read that copies one field into the other**, and the document says so instead of
merging them.

### "Check the target, not the mnemonic" — a warning that was nearly a new defect

The tail-call warning went out as *"disassemble the tail; a trailing `jmp` is a tail call."* Applied to
`002AC5F0`, whose **last instruction is a `jmp` at `002AE32C` targeting `002ACFE7` — inside its own
body**, that rule would have **truncated a 1,658-instruction function at its own loop back edge.**

> **A trailing `jmp` is a tail call only when its target lies outside the function's extent.**

**Caught by the session applying it**, on the first function it was applied to. A warning issued to
prevent one mis-binding was one step from causing another.

### The seeded generator, and a thunk that is not in the function list

`0022A0B0` seeds the engine's Mersenne Twister with **`0x11B9` = 4537, an immediate**, through
`00863D30`, whose first-use path seeds with **`0x1571` = 5489 — `std::mt19937::default_seed`.**

> **The Mersenne stream is identical on every launch. What varies between playthroughs is how many
> draws have been taken by the time a roll happens, not the numbers themselves.**

**And the call reaches it through `00379CF0`, a 5-byte thunk (`jmp 00863D30`) absent from
`functions.tsv`.** A caller census of the seeding function that did not follow thunks would report this
site as absent — **the second time in one night that the function list's shape decided what could be
absent from an answer.**

### The band, recounted by encoding rather than by call graph

Scanning `.text` for the exact bytes `2C 1B 3C 0C`:

```
26 occurrences · 22 distinct functions
23 of 26 test `byte ptr [reg + 4]`, on nine different base registers
21 of 26 are preceded by a [+5] test within six instructions
```

> **It is a two-byte discriminator, not a lone range check:**
> `rec[5] == 0 && (uint8)(rec[4] − 0x1B) <= 0x0C` — **and eight subsystems consult it without any of
> them saying what it is.**

**Two cautions that make the census usable rather than merely large:** the **polarity differs by call
site** — in the periodic tick the branch skips the guarded block — so a reader must check the branch
at each site; and it counts a **different quantity** from the existing `+5` census (104 sites, 82
functions), so it was placed beside that one rather than merged into it.

### Key the census on the OS boundary, where the engine cannot rename anything

Told to expect thunks in the asset pipeline, a session went one level lower and **keyed its census on
the IAT slot address**, mapping every slot to `dll!name` through the import descriptors first.

> **Keying on the slot is immune to both of tonight's hazards.** A thunk cannot hide a call that goes
> through the slot, and **no naming convention is required — the OS boundary is the one place the
> engine cannot rename anything.**

That turned the byte-delivery surface into a **measurement rather than a search**: three `ReadFile`
sites, all owned by `Resource`; 17 `fread`; **and no memory-mapped path at all** — neither
`CreateFileMapping` nor `MapViewOfFile` appears among the imports, **a directory-level negative that
needs no call-site search to be complete.**

**The residual gap is stated rather than papered over:** a pointer copied out of a slot into a register
or structure would evade it.

### The archive names itself, and the modding rule falls out of where the hash is taken

`fopen("rb")` — **CRT stdio, not Win32** — magic `SRYK`, an index-size dword, **the last sixteen bytes
of a 31 GB file** read via `_fseeki64(-16, SEEK_END)`, the whole index in **one** `fread`, `fclose`,
then six CryptoAPI calls hashing that buffer with **`CALG_MD5`**. The failure branch prints
**`"BigFile head wrong!"`** — *BigFile* is the developers' term; `SRYK` is only the magic.

> **The digest covers the index and nothing else.** Replacing an entry's payload in place — same
> offset, same length — **leaves the digest valid**; changing the index in any way breaks it, and the
> failure is **at open, not at use.**

**And `fclose` runs inside the opener, before verification — the integrity test is on the in-memory
copy**, so what is cached is the index, not the file.

**The restraint is the part worth copying:** the six CryptoAPI calls are decoded, but the comparison
consuming `HP_HASHVAL` was not chased to its branch, so the document says *"the check is present; its
consequence is assumed, not read"* rather than asserting the game refuses to boot.

> **That is the claim a reader would most want and the one its author had least right to make.**

### One structure, three windows — and consolidating three true observations paid out a status id

This coordinator reported three sightings of *"a two-layer status arrangement at a stride of `0x10`"*
— `+0x68`/`+0x78`, `+0x6B`/`+0x7B`, `+0x6E`/`+0x7E` — across three subsystems, and read the repetition
as a pattern.

**It is not a pattern. Each layer is 16 bytes, so every byte inside them is `0x10` apart by
construction.**

| offsets | byte of each layer | status ids |
|---|---:|---|
| `+0x68` / `+0x78` | 0 | 0–7 |
| `+0x6B` / `+0x7B` | 3 | 24–31 |
| `+0x6E` / `+0x7E` | 6 | 48–55 |

> **Three true observations that were cheaper and sharper as one.** Nothing was wrong; the reading was
> **three structures sharing a stride** where the fact is **one structure seen through three windows.**

**And the consolidation produced something none of the three could:** the elemental-affinity function's
nested condition tests bit `0x10` of byte 6, which under the layer document's own
`byteIndex = n >> 3` / `bit = 1 << (n & 7)` rule is **status id 52**. The condition reads *does the
target have status 52 in either layer* — **a specific claim recovered by merging observations, not by
reading more code.**

### A fourth shape of cut entry: read for one purpose, rest of the body unexamined

`0030E130` was cited as *"complete body … tier 1"* and its bit arithmetic **is** exactly right. But the
function is named `…AndProcessSideEffects`, and

> **553 bytes for `byteIndex = n >> 3` is a great deal of code.**

**None of the side effects were in the document.** Reading them gave the mechanical join between two
systems that had only ever been related by argument:

**Status ids 104–113 — ten consecutive — each adjust a unit's usable gambit-slot count by one**, up on
set and down on clear (`sub r14b, 0x68` / `cmp r14b, 9` / `lea edx, [rbx*2 - 1]`), and **nothing else
in the id space touches that counter.**

**Two behavioural facts the bit arithmetic cannot give:**

- **Re-applying a status a unit already has is a complete no-op** — every mode aborts before the
  auxiliary update, the transition result and all side effects.
- **The layers gate side effects by their union.** Setting an id in layer 0 while layer 1 already
  carries it **stores the bit and fires nothing.**

**Seventh instance of the computed-operand hazard, and the first on a call *target*:** the result
builder is selected **by function pointer via `cmovne`**, so **a scan for `call <literal>` finds
neither builder at that site.**

### A function nothing calls is still a function something references

Every code-side route into the glyph cluster was closed, **by the session that closed them**: no
imports, no direct strings, no named caller anywhere. So it stopped looking at code.

> `002AAE40` has **zero callers** and **exactly one pointer in the image**. Immediately after that
> address sit `1, 10, 100, … 100000000` — **the powers of ten.** Immediately before it: **six function
> pointers.**

**The way in was a pointer table, not the call graph.** **Two kinds × three operations**, selected by
**one signed byte at `obj[0xA3]`**, dispatched by three small functions that index the table and
tail-jump. **Column 0 is numeric** — its handler takes the address of the powers-of-ten table.
**Column 1 is text** — its handler directly calls the 7,489-byte drawer.

**Column 2 is the only kind-specific operation, and no dispatcher references it** — a zero produced by
**an instrument demonstrably reporting non-zero for its siblings** (one reference to column 0, two to
column 1), which is what makes the zero a measurement.

**The selector is read with `movsx` and never bounds-checked**; the only protection is a null test on
the loaded pointer, **which will not catch a garbage one.**

### An instrument that computes an address should be made to read it back

**A different failure from the seven encoding hazards, and no key would have caught it.** A pointer
scan reported a **decimal** offset; converting it to hex went wrong **twice**, and two wrong `.rdata`
neighbourhoods were dumped before the value at the address failed to match the value the scan claimed.

> **Not a wrong key — wrong address arithmetic.** The scan now **verifies every hit by reading back
> the VA it reports**: one line, and a silent arithmetic error becomes an assertion.

**Standing rule, added beside the encoding family:** *an instrument that computes an address must read
that address back before reporting it.*

### Reading a table to its last non-null entry is not reading the table

A document reported the glyph dispatch table as **two rows**. It has **four** — the read stopped at the
last non-null entry before a gap.

```
009164C0   002A9980   002A8C50   002A9F00     kind 0
009164D8   002A9980   002A8C50   002AA800     kind 1
009164F0   (null)     (null)     (null)       kind 2
00916508   (null)     (null)     002AAE40     kind 3
```

**The null rows are part of the table — they are why every dispatcher null-tests the loaded pointer** —
and the orphan function the earlier section opened with sits **inside the rows that had not been read.**
Four rows of three, 96 bytes, ending exactly where the powers-of-ten table begins. Corrected in place
with the original claim quoted.

### 4,038 bytes whose only reference in the image is a table slot nothing indexes

Nothing indexes column 2, so a column-2 handler is reachable only by a direct call. Tested with
**unbounded** scans — every `E8` and `E9` displacement in `.text`, plus every verified 8-byte pointer
in every non-`.text` section:

| handler | `E8` | `E9` | pointers |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `002A9F00` (kind 0) — **control** | **8** | 0 | its table slot only |
| `002AA800` (kind 1) | **0** | **0** | its table slot only |
| `002AAE40` (kind 3) | **0** | **0** | its table slot only |

> **A zero from an instrument reporting eight for a sibling in the identical position is evidence.**
> The control sits in the *same column of the same table* and survives because it is **also** called
> directly — its table slot is redundant rather than load-bearing.

**And the kinds were not named.** Ten byte-writes to the selector exist image-wide; four are in this
cluster and write 0, 0, 2 and 3 — **and the writer of 1 is in `Audio`**, which may be a different
structure at the same offset. *"Not resolved, and not assumed"* — the same trap the `[reg+4]` census
taught.

### The game's text is variable-width, and one instruction is the whole rule

```asm
002A8D8C  lea    rax, [rdi + 1]
002A8D90  add    rdi, 2
002A8D94  cmp    cl, 0x20
002A8D97  cmovae rdi, rax        ; >= 0x20 -> one byte;  < 0x20 -> two
```

> **Any tool measuring FFXII text length by counting bytes over-counts every tag.**

**`0x0F` introduces a tag and the tag character selects which render-state field is written** — seven
handled tags, **seven distinct destinations** (`-` `#` `"` `;` `/` `p` `=`). A 64-bit lookahead mask
`0x4100400000000000` **was decoded by evaluating it rather than reading it off by eye**, giving bits
46, 56, 62 — `.` `8` `>` — **three characters recognised here and handled elsewhere.**

**And a bound kept rather than a guess taken:** the `/` tag does a magic divide, and it was **not**
claimed to be the documented `0x88888889` family — **the shift was not read, and the multiplier alone
does not fix the divisor.**

**A shape worth a second ranking column:** **208 `movups` against exactly one backward jump.** That
combination is never a processing pass — it is a large structure snapshotted to the stack, modified and
written back. **SSE-moves-per-loop would have flagged this function and two others as one family before
anyone opened any of them.**

### Pre-screening tells you what you are walking into; re-running tells you what you left behind

A session **created the read-but-uncited false positive itself, two blocks after characterising it, in
a document about it.** After writing the section it re-ran the check and **the pair was still on the
cut** — entries cited, the finaliser's interior cited, and **no interior address of either function it
had just read.**

> **The only reason it was caught is that the check was re-run *after* writing rather than before.**
> **They are different checks**, and only the first was being done.

Fixed with an anchor table — tail-jmp sites, first and last `_Init_thread_header`, first and last field
call, named `lea` sites. **Both cleared.**

### 315 functions share one epilogue, and the tail-call hazard finally applied

**`00639450` is the shared finaliser of class registration**: 315 functions have `jmp 0x639450` as
their **final instruction**. Not a helper called from many places — **a common epilogue**, marking the
descriptor with `0x40000000` at `+0xFC` and self-linking an empty list at `+8`.

> **This is the first time in the run that the tail-call hazard actually applied.** Every previous
> check found a loop back edge; here both functions genuinely leave their extent. **The rule earned its
> keep on roughly the twentieth check** — about the right rate for a hazard worth carrying.

**Two related populations, deliberately not merged:**

```
tail-calling 00639450                      315
   of those, containing a field call       173
field-call sites inside them               593
field-call sites outside any registrar      89
image-wide                                 682   <- independently reproduces a published figure
```

**142 of the 315 register no named field, and 89 registrations happen outside any registrar** — so
*"315 classes"* and a published *"246 named classes"* are **answers to different questions.** The 682
was reproduced **without reading the document that contains it**, which is what makes the rest
trustworthy.

**A counting trap from the same anchors:** one function makes **18** registrations across 20 `m_*`
strings; the other **4** across 5, because most of its 29 strings are **method** names.
**Counting name strings and counting registrations measure different things**, and both are in the
table rather than one standing in for the other.

**And the recovered animation schema is an API rather than a field table** — `playOnce`, `playLooping`,
`stop`, `setSpeed`, plus per-slot variants with explicit weight control. **That is the animation
surface a mod can drive, recovered by name from a function nobody had opened.**

### Choosing the next block by measurement rather than estimate

Asked for judgement on which open item was tractable, a session **probed in two commands** instead:

| open item | verdict |
|---|---|
| *why column 2 exists* | a **"why"** — not answerable from a binary; would have produced a story |
| the kind identities | leads into unnamed residuals; the setter of kind 1 is in `Audio` and may be a different struct at the same offset |
| **what the context object is** | **one writer against 121 readers** — tractable, and it was |

**A static 4,360-byte struct, zeroed once by a 69-byte initialiser that then publishes the pointer**;
never reallocated, **no vtable written** — consistent with the cluster dispatching through a hand-rolled
table rather than virtual calls. **25 offsets are touched and they are the last sixty bytes.**

**And the negative it refused to make is the entry worth keeping:**

> **The measured statement is "not accessed here". The unmeasured one would have been "not
> accessed".** The scanner tracks a register inside one function and cannot cross a call — **and the
> pointer is placed in `rcx` at nine call sites to seven functions.**

> **CORRECTED 2026-09-03: those nine call sites did not exist.** The tracker walked instructions
> **linearly, ignoring control flow**, so at a jump target it carried a value every real path had
> killed. Made block-aware, the same census returns **zero**. **The refusal still stands — but the
> reason given for it has been withdrawn**, and it survives because the corrected tracker
> under-reports by construction.

**Both absences are recorded at different strengths**: zero indexed accesses is a counter that would
have reported non-zero, so it is a measurement; the untouched 4 KB is scoped, **with the nine sites
given so a reader can size the gap.**

### An instrument that does not model control flow does not under-report — it invents

**The most dangerous instrument failure of the run, and the first that *creates* evidence rather than
missing it.**

A register tracker reported *"the context pointer is passed as argument 1 at nine sites to seven
functions."* It walked instructions **linearly, ignoring control flow**, so **at a jump target it
carried a value that every real path had killed.** Made block-aware, the same census returns **zero**.

> **A register-tracking instrument that does not model control flow is not conservative; it is
> wrong.** It does not under-report — **it invents** — and **all nine inventions looked like ordinary
> call sites at real addresses.**

**Every hazard catalogued before this one was an absence**: a key that missed an encoding, a list that
omitted a function, a control that certified the wrong axis. **This one is a fabrication**, and
nothing in the gate suite can see the difference between a real call site and an invented one.

**What caught it was reading the output rather than tabulating it.** At one site the three
instructions before the call set `r9`, `r8` and `rdx` and are reached by a branch — **`rcx` is never
set on that path.** And the seven "callees", read in full, are **three-byte sequence decoders**: they
read `[rcx+1]` and `[rcx+2]` and return the constant `3`.

> **The callees made no sense as callees.** That check is cheaper than any tool and available to
> anyone who reads what an instrument hands them.

### Two conclusions that survived the correction of their own evidence

- **The field map was rebuilt with the fix and its shape did not move** — same three pointer slots,
  same tail block, one spurious offset removed. **A conclusion that survives the correction of its own
  evidence was resting on the structure, not on the counts.**
- **The refusal survived too, for a different reason than it was made for.** The front 4 KB was left
  unclaimed *because callees might use it*; that reason is withdrawn, and the refusal stands because
  **the corrected tracker under-reports by construction.**

> **The reason to refuse a claim changed; the refusal did not. A negative that only holds while one
> particular support holds was never worth making.**

### A clean check is not evidence that the instrument asked the right question

**Three of one session's four instruments were corrected after publishing** — an argument scanner, a
context mapper and a pointer scan.

> **In every case the defect was found by reading output rather than by running a check.**

**All three passed every gate this project has**, before and after. The gates compare documents against
the binary and against each other; **none of them can ask whether the question an instrument answered
was the question that was asked.**

### One function turns the class magic numbers into a map, without overriding the caution that kept them unlabelled

`00322C50` is a **32-way jump-table dispatch on the class argument**, every case landing on one shared
tail:

```asm
00323030  jl  fail            ; id < 0
00323036  lea eax, [rcx - 1]  ; rcx = the slot's count
0032303B  jg  fail            ; id >= count
```

> **`valid ⇔ 0 ≤ id < count`, where count is the dword at `slot + 4`** — the header field the registry
> document already describes. **A null slot yields 0**, so an unloaded table makes every id *invalid*
> rather than faulting.

**Sharing is asymmetric** — one slot serves classes 22–24, another 15/30/31, another 19/20 — **class 13
is composite** (three slots plus a constant), and **class 1 re-dispatches**, the function's only loop.

**The registry's caution was sharpened rather than overturned, and the distinction is the entry.** That
document says a slot whose only consumer is this function is *"an id-indexed table and nothing more"*
and **deliberately leaves those slots unlabelled.** That stands.

**What changed is that three rows now have two independent sources:**

| class | second source | conclusion |
|---:|---|---|
| 20 | an availability document reading its caller pass an **action id** | indexed by action id |
| 23 | a spawn document reading its caller pass a **definition selector** | indexed by definition selector |
| 29 | a status document reading it gate **status side effects** | indexed by status id |

> **A class number from this function, and an argument name from a document that read the caller.**
> That is a different thing from labelling a slot by a consumer that touches everything — **which is
> exactly what the caution warns against. The caution is what made these three worth stating and the
> other 26 not.**

**And the fan-in fits without being offered as proof:** the action-id slot is the registry's named
heavyweight at 128 referencing functions. **Stated as a fit.**

**Not claimed:** the other 26 slots — *a class number is an identity, not a description* — and what
distinguishes classes 22, 23 and 24, which **this function treats identically**, so the distinction
lives in their callers.

### The placement rule earning its keep in the quiet case

The class map went into the **registry** document rather than the availability document that cites the
function most, **because the subject is the registry's slots.**

> **Under the old rule this would have gone wherever the citation count pointed, and the class map
> would have been an appendix to a combat document instead of the key to a data-pipeline one.**

**A rule change is easiest to judge on the case where nothing went wrong.**

### Two documents at opposite ends of the engine, meeting on one call site

The level-up function ends with:

```asm
0030C831  mov  ecx, 7           ; sound bank 7
0030C836  call 003A1180
0030C840  mov  edx, 0x40        ; pan
0030C847  lea  r8d, [rdx+0x3f]  ; = 0x7F, volume
0030C84B  call 002DF220
```

**`003A1180` and `002DF220` are the two functions read for the audio-boundary block hours earlier**, and
`0x40` / `0x7F` are **exactly the literals that document decodes** — centre pan, because the formula is
`pan − 0x40`, and full volume, because it is `clamp(v, 0, 127) / 127`.

> **The audio document derived what those constants mean from the mixer; this one is a caller passing
> precisely them, for a level-up. Neither read informed the other, and nobody was looking.**

**It is also the argument for opening things rather than citing them: that join could not exist while
the function was a name on a door.**

### Levelling: stored, capped, and one-way

- **`stats + 0x1C2` is the level, one byte, and this function is its writer** (`0030C7BB`) — **the same
  byte the foe-stat formula reads** as the left half of `growth × (level − base) + base`. **The byte
  this function writes is the byte that decides how strong a foe is.**
- **It cannot go down.** An entry guard returns when the target is at or below the current level, and
  the loop only increments — **a lower target is a no-op, not an error and not a decrease.** The 99 cap
  is applied **twice**, to the target and to every increment. **Control on the absence:** the same
  reading positively finds the guard and the increment, and finds **no `dec` or subtracting store** to
  that byte anywhere in the decoded body.
- **Stats are grown per level, not recomputed** — six fields per iteration, **four of the six sharing
  one growth function** and differing only by which byte of a **stride-3 packed growth record** they
  read. **The derived-state rebuild runs once, on the final level only**: a four-level gain rebuilds it
  once, not four times.
- **The growth record is indexed out of `02EBF130`**, which the class map assigns to classes 1 and 2 —
  **so that slot is the per-character growth table**, identified the same **two-source** way as the
  other three: a class number from the validator, an argument name from a caller read independently.
- **The third argument is a silence flag**, `NOT(bit 1)`, gating the notification together with *is this
  the final iteration*. **Both known callers pass `0`, so both notify** — but the result applier's byte
  can be `-1`, and **`-1` has bit 1 set, so that path is silent.** It suppresses the fanfare; the stats
  are untouched.

### A value only ever tested for exact equality is a magic, whatever its digits spell

The save header's two "version" dwords, `0x20050223` and `0x05071901`, each come from a six-byte getter
with **exactly one caller**. An immediate sweep found **every** occurrence in the image — three and one
— and **the only comparison is `cmp` followed by `je`. No `jb`, no `ja`, no subtraction against either
value anywhere.**

**They do spell dates in packed decimal**, and that reading was **kept out of the mechanism**: the
document states the comparison first and the digits second, **because the conclusion does not depend on
the reading and would have survived the digits meaning nothing at all.**

> **The modding consequence follows from the comparison rather than from the name: an edited save whose
> stamp differs is not migrated and not partially accepted.**

**And the stamp is load-bearing.** It guards a **29,712-byte runtime state block** that is zeroed and
re-stamped on mismatch — **and that block is where the party roster and reserve live**, at the same
base and offsets mapped independently in the party work. **A one-dword mismatch discards all of it.**

### Loading is not restoring

Nine steps in the load sequence, five named: restore the active field id, **import the persistent flag
bank**, restore transition metadata, touch achievements, and **reseed the RNG from `_time64`**.

> **The named steps *import*, *restore* and *reseed* rather than copy** — which is why reloading
> rerolls combat outcomes, closing the loop with the determinism finding from the boot side.

### A name that diverges from its behaviour, reported as divergence

`EventMemory_*`, carrying the `Story_Event_Quest_Hunt` owner, turns out to be **buffer lifetime
management**: free-if-held, then allocate **1 MiB** and **100 KiB** from pool 5, with both pointers
touched only by `ActorEntity` code.

> **So the two "event memory" lookups gate memory, not story state.** The engine asks whether a
> definition id is already known and, if not, **makes room for it.**

**The document reports the behaviour and states the divergence** rather than choosing between them —
and it makes the *"there is no hunt system"* negative **stronger**, not weaker: there is even less
native story machinery than the first pass claimed.

### "Am I looking at all of it" — a hazard with no instrument-side tell

Generalising the `+0x10E4` resolution:

> **Every hazard catalogued before it asks *"is this instrument lying to me about what I am looking
> at"*. This one asks *"am I looking at all of it"* — and it has no instrument-side tell at all,
> because each reader's evidence was complete and correct for the function in front of them.**

**The only defence is cheap and was found by accident:** take the displacement and **scan the whole
cluster for every site before deciding what the field is.** *"I would not have done it if we had not
disagreed."*

### The area-music handoff, and a latch that changes what a caller is

`00261F90` was cited by four documents as *"the Audio callee"* and nothing more.

```asm
00261FA3  test byte ptr [rcx + 0x10], 0x40
00261FA7  jne  return                       ; already done
002620D5  or   byte ptr [rcx + 0x10], 0x40  ; latched on the only completing path
```

**Nothing in the function clears that latch**, and the per-frame field pass calls it every frame.

> **The latch is the entire difference between a transition handler and a per-frame one** — the caller
> looked like it was doing this work continuously and is not.

**And the save file can pin the music.** One bit at `+0x1063` of the save payload makes the track come
from `+0x1534` and **skips the field-to-track mapping entirely** — *saved audio state, not a setting.*
Four sources in priority order, with a per-track flag table deciding whether a mapped track is usable
at all, and **failure is explicit**: if nothing is chosen and nothing is playing, a bit is cleared and
music is abandoned for that transition rather than retried.

**`0x7F` for the third unrelated time this session.** Derived from the mixer, then confirmed by a
level-up fanfare, now by an area-music crossfade — **none of the three knowing about the others.**

**And `0x78` was not called frames.** Two seconds at 60 Hz is the obvious reading; **recorded as an
inference because that function does not establish what the fader counts.**

**A fourth sighting for the runtime-installed-tunables note, and it runs the other way:** these fade
constants are **immediates**, not globals — **which is precisely why they would survive a static patch
when the spacing globals would not.**

### `0x80000003` is the floor of a family of nested masks

**Eight sightings across seven subsystems, and it turns out to be the smallest member of a set ordered
by inclusion.**

```asm
0023B166  and eax, 0x8800403B
0023B173  and edx, 0x8800003B
```

**Both are strict supersets** of the predicate this database has tracked all night, and **they differ
from each other by exactly bit 14.**

| mask | extra bits over `0x80000003` |
|---|---|
| `0x8800403B` | 3, 4, 5, **14**, 27 |
| `0x8800003B` | 3, 4, 5, 27 |

> **The statuses that stop you *controlling* a character are a superset of those that stop it
> *acting*.** A unit can be eligible to act on its own and still refuse player input — **the
> mechanical shape of "I can't move but my gambits still run".**

**This answers the reworded question.** `PROPOSED-repos46-5` was changed from *what state does this
mask mean* to *what set is this* — and the answer is **a family of sets ordered by inclusion, with
`0x80000003` as its floor.** Anyone treating it as *the* status-suppression mask is using the narrowest
member of three.

### One mask, three consumers, one of them inverted

| bit | consumer |
|---:|---|
| 0 | movement suppression |
| 1 | a ten-byte function, **negated** |
| 2 | suppression mask 1 |

> **A set bit means *permit* on one path and *suppress* on the other two.** A reader assuming one
> polarity across the mask gets one of three backwards — **same species as the mode/flags dword: the
> field is uniform, its interpretation is not.**

**And the `0x40` bit is not one input among many — it is the mask's initial value**, materialised by
`and al,0x40` / `sbb esi,esi`: **set means "start fully suppressed", clear means "start from nothing"**,
and the rest of the function refines that seed. **Two further bits of the same global** are read later,
so it carries at least three control-policy bits where the citing document knew one.

**The tail-call hazard fired for the second time tonight** — last instruction `jmp` to a distinct
ten-byte function.

### An off-by-one that would have been a silent under-report in play

```asm
007E651F  mov  rcx, [rbp - 0x21]
007E6523  dec  ebx                 ; step back before breaking
```

**Without that `dec`, the first entry of every run after the first would be skipped.**

> **It is invisible in a summary and produces no error — just a sound that never fires.** *"I would not
> have seen it from anything but the instruction stream."*

**A defect whose only symptom is an absence in play is the strongest argument in this database for
reading bodies rather than citing them.**

### A constant that reaches four subsystems is not a constant, it is an interface

`01DFE0B8` came out of the frame-limit settings work as the **frame-rate base**; it set the enmity
decay interval; it decides a boot-time global by integer division; and it now converts an **authored
second-count into ticks** in spawn persistence — **`× 30.0` giving 30 or 60 ticks per second at either
frame rate.**

> **Four documents, four subsystems, one dword.** Anything that changes it changes all four, and only
> the chain of reads makes that visible.

### Noting that a mechanism is over-determined is a finding

**A two-slot spawn-persistence buffer needs no timer to be correct, and there is one.**

> **The extra machinery exists for a reason outside the function** — which is a far more useful open
> question than *"what does this timer do"*, and the same shape as declining to call a fade constant
> "frames" when the function does not establish what the fader counts.

### The mirror of the incomplete-population hazard: reading the wrong site first

Two consumers of the same global:

```asm
0030CB06  test dword ptr [02089340], 0x400   ; + a slot flag -> suppress entirely
0030CBAD  test dword ptr [02089340], 0x200   ; -> clear the out-parameter
```

**tested separately, with different effects** — while a second function tests them **together as
`0x600`.**

> **Two consumers, one global, and the pairing is the caller's choice rather than the field's
> structure.**

**This is the mirror of the `+0x10E4` entry rather than another instance of it.** There, **two sites
disagreed and both were right**, because the field had two roles. **Here the two sites agree and one is
simply coarser** — nothing contradicts, **but a reader who saw only the `0x600` test would describe a
two-bit policy as one bit and never know.**

> **The first is a hazard of reading too few sites; this is a hazard of reading the wrong one first.**

**Whether `0x200` and `0x400` are one policy or two genuinely depends on which function you open**, and
neither reading was corrected, **because both are correct for their own site.**

### A slot can be ready and still not play

`BattleAction_CheckPresentationSlotReady` **answers two questions on two channels, and they can
disagree:**

- **the return value** is *is the slot ready* — three separate dwords at `+0x10`, `+0x14`, `+0x18` must
  **each equal 3**; **not a bitmask, not a counter, three parallel sub-states reaching one value**;
- **the out-parameter** is *should it play* — vetoed by the caller's flags, then restorable by a chain
  of tests on the action record.

> **A caller that checks only the return value gets a `true` that does not mean what it looks like.**

**Thirty-two slots of 48 bytes**, and **an out-of-range index yields a null base rather than a fault**,
so **a caller cannot distinguish that from a legitimately empty slot.**

**And the registry slot `02EBF138` is confirmed a third time** — the slot's `word +0x1C` indexes it as
an action id, **from a consumer neither the availability document nor the class map touched.** Three
independent identifications of one table.

### The combat chain has no unread link

**Commit → presentation check → apply**, all three read from their bodies, with the formula and the
auto-status rebuild either side. **The leaned-on cut went from 23 to 4 in the course of one run.**

### The third value is what stopped it being a claim

Three authored thresholds: `810627072`, `1075331072`, `-1071661038`.

> **As floats, two are plausible — `2.379` and `-2.496` — and one is not, at `7.6e-10`.**

The field was **almost** called a float on the strength of the first two. **The code compares it with a
signed-integer `cmp`**, which is order-preserving over float bit patterns **only while both operands
are non-negative — and one of the three has its sign bit set.** Type not established, no reading
asserted.

> **Two out of three fitting is exactly how the `0.00555556`-is-`1/180` mistake would have gone.**
> **The outlier is the control**, and it only works if you look at all three before deciding.

### An open question that closes as a negative and reopens better

**The eleven counter achievements have no threshold in their table.** The accumulate path **never reads
the threshold field**, and every numeric-type entry's value is `0` — except one whose `16` is a **bit
index for a bitfield mode**, not a target.

> **So whatever decides a counter has reached its goal is not in this function.** The question closes
> as posed and reopens as *"who compares a counter against a target"* — **a better question than the
> one it replaces.**

**And achievements keep their own memory:** a dedicated **30-bit "already fired" bitmap**, indexed by
the same 0–29 index, separate from whatever else they read.

### Two runs of the same length and shape is not an identification

Eleven entries carry a numeric type; a catalogue elsewhere lists **eleven** `ACH_COUNT_*`. Ten entries
share one mode with thresholds **0–9**; the same catalogue lists **ten** `ACH_SPECIAL_MONSTER01..10`,
*"a flat, zero-padded run of ten"*.

> **No string in the table ties an index to a name.** The correspondence is **recorded and explicitly
> not called a mapping** — it narrows the open question to *"the ten differ only by a 0–9 parameter
> into one shared mode"* **without claiming which name is which index.**

### The three input profiles are three regions of one flat space

Three device classes with **16, 8 and 4** slots at base offsets **0, `0x10`, `0x18`** — end to end, no
gap, no overlap. **16 + 8 + 4 = 28 = `0x1C`**, and the profile stride is **`0x70` = 28 dwords.**
**Every number agrees with every other**, which is rare enough to say out loud.

**And the geometry produces the finding:** the conflict scan's bound is **`0x54` = 84 = 3 × 28**,
walking from the class-0 base.

> **A key already bound in a *different profile* is a conflict.** The search does not stop at a profile
> boundary — **the three profiles are not independent keymaps; they are three regions of one.**

**Both remapping policies exist and the caller chooses**: a flag clear **refuses** the assignment with
its own return code, set **trades the two bindings**. Four distinct return codes let a caller tell
*reserved* from *already bound* from *bad slot*, and **assigning code `0` clears the slot with no scan
at all.**

**Thirty-five codes cannot be bound**, from a table consulted before anything else — **twenty-two of
them the contiguous run `0x83`–`0x98`.** What they mean is not established; **the list is worth having
as a list**, because *"which inputs the game will not let you rebind"* becomes answerable the moment
that code space is named.

### "The count and the data agree" is the two-source discipline, cheaply

The unbindable table's bound of 35 is confirmed twice independently — **by the loop counter
(`cmp edx, 0x23`) and by the data (the dword after the table is `0`).**

> **It is the same two-source rule as the class-map rows, just cheap enough that it is easy not to
> notice one is doing it.**

**Worth naming precisely because it is invisible when it works:** a count taken only from a loop bound
is one source; a terminator that agrees with it is a second, and **the pair is what makes the number a
measurement rather than a reading.**

### A fifth way the decompiled output misdescribes itself, and the first about a null path

```asm
00864F8E  je   0x864F96
00864F90  lea  rdx, [rax + 8]     ; non-null
00864F96  xor  edx, edx           ; NULL
00864F98  movups xmm0, xmmword ptr [rdx]     ; both paths converge
```

> **An `if`/`else` that assigns a pointer, followed by a merge, reads as a conditional *expression* —
> which invites rendering the dependent reads as though they were guarded.** They are not: the `+8`
> adjustment is conditional and **the use is not.**

**Four earlier misdescriptions were about return types, an extent, and locals behind a stack probe.
This one is about control flow itself**, and it was avoided only by declining to read a branch
structure out of a decompiler and asking for the image instead.

### Two functions on one ranking, opposite conventions

- **`0018A120`** loads four constant rows **before** its null test — **a missing source is a defined
  default.**
- **`00864F30`** sets its pointer to zero on the null path and **dereferences it fourteen instructions
  later.**

> **One treats a missing source as a value; the other treats it as impossible.** Neither is called a
> crash — *"the resolver never returns null in practice"* is a claim about callers — **but the path
> exists, it is unguarded, and nothing between the `xor` and the first read touches the register.**

### Double-buffering proved by geometry, with nothing naming it

`CharacterRenderObject` slot 13: two transform banks at `+0x4C4` and `+0x584`, and
**`0x584 − 0x4C4 = 0xC0` = exactly three 64-byte matrices** — contiguous, equal, adjacent, with the
scalar pair likewise four bytes apart.

> **The geometry proves the double-buffering; no flag or name says it.** The bank is chosen by one byte
> behind a shared accessor, so **which copy is "current" is not this object's decision.**

**Two smaller facts with player consequences:** the enable gate **preserves rather than clears** — with
one flag clear, nothing is written and **both banks keep their previous contents**; and **a NaN takes
the non-zero branch** of the two-float zero test, because the parity guards send unordered comparisons
down that path. **The flag means "definitely both zero", not "not non-zero".**

**And that entry is the argument for the SSE column in one line:** 48 `movups` in 105 instructions with
zero loops, **found by neither the citation graph nor bytes-per-line — because the row existed and only
its description cell was empty.**

### For a negative, use the instrument that cannot invent; for a search, the one that cannot miss

**A refinement of the fabrication finding rather than a new species**, and it inverts the fix.

The register-tracking scan that **invents** call sites when run linearly was made **block-aware**, which
is the correct cure. Run block-aware on a *search*, it returned **zero accesses — including one its own
operator had already read with their own eyes**, because the base register is loop-invariant and
survives a branch the conservative version resets at.

**Run permissively, it found the real accesses — and every hit was read before being counted.**

> **The conservative version omits as badly as the linear one invents.** **Block-awareness is the right
> fix for *inventing* and the wrong default for *searching*** — and **not saying which mode is in use
> is how a zero becomes a claim.**

### A negative that survived three different questions

**The first in this run to do so.** *Do maps 1–4 ever diverge from map 0 after the copy?*

| instrument | question | result |
|---|---|---|
| displacement census | what writes offset N? | initialiser only |
| base-keyed scan with `lea` | does a pointer into the range escape? | **0** |
| register-held-offset scan | is a base loaded as an **immediate** and indexed? | 8 reads, **0 writes** |

**And the second gap was not the one predicted.** The published caveat named `lea` as the escape
hatch; **the actual escape was bare immediates** — `mov esi, 0x5A5A` then `[rsi + ptr]` — **which
neither a displacement census nor a `lea` scan can see.** Seven such sites for one map alone.

> **A negative is only as strong as the variety of questions that failed to overturn it.**

**And the framing both sides had used — *"four views allowed to drift"* — is withdrawn on both sides,
because it asserted a freedom nothing supports.**

### A call site only shows the number going in

**A document recorded class 1 as "the equipment class", from four call sites that all pass 1.**
**Class 1 names no class at all** — its arm **derives a class from the id** and re-enters the switch.

> ***"Equipment passes class 1"* is true. *"Class 1 is the equipment class"* is false. And the
> difference is invisible from every caller.**

**Four call sites agreed, and agreement among call sites cannot distinguish the two readings.** Only
the callee's own dispatch can, and **the mapping existed nowhere but in a jump table.**

### Four documents, each holding one row of a table nobody had extracted

**The pair-ranking shape one level up.** Not two documents failing to cite each other — **four
documents each carrying a single class number, with the mapping that relates them living only in a
32-entry jump table.**

Extracting it settled all four at once, and **two rows were confirmed from the opposite direction to
the documents they confirm**, the validator sharing no code with either consumer:

- **class 20 → `02EBF138`**, the action table a licence document reads from the consumer side;
- **class 23 → a literal bound of 9**, matching nine configuration slots found independently in the
  party work.

### Three arms consult no table, and the extractor is why anyone noticed

**Of thirty-two arms, three read no descriptor at all:** the dynamic one, a **range** check
(`0xE000`–`0xEFFF`, *ids that are not indices*), and a **literal bound of 9**.

> **The extractor reported those as "no global read" rather than picking up whatever rip-relative
> operand came next** — which is the only reason they were seen.
>
> ***"The class picks a table" is the rule and not the definition.*** An extractor that assumed a
> descriptor per class **would have been wrong three times and looked complete.**

**And classes 30, 31 and 32 alias other arms** — three pairs sharing a table, **not three more tables.**

### A wrong address does not fail; it returns something

**One tick after the image-base RVA class was reported, this coordinator walked straight into it.** A
console table was addressed as `[rsi + id*16 + 0x1CD6E68]` with **`rsi` holding the image base**, and
the raw displacement was dumped as an address.

> **The dump returned plausible 16-byte records and nothing in it announced that it was the wrong
> memory.** The only reason the error surfaced is that the *"pointers"* in it **did not look like
> pointers.**

**The real table is at `01DF6E68`** — sixteen bytes per id, a qword pointer into a packed run of
**seven-character, NUL-terminated authored codes** (`ous0101`, `nal0101`, `rwr0101`), most entries
null.

**A warning received and understood does not protect against the thing it warns about**, which is the
same lesson as the taxonomy entry that did not protect its own author. **What caught it was reading the
bytes and finding them implausible — the third time tonight that reading output rather than tabulating
it produced the correction.**

### Naming a table by its consumers is a different act from reading it

**14 of 25 anonymous registry descriptors named, and eleven left unnamed** because every function
touching them is `FUN_xxxxxxxx`.

> **The names are inferences from referrer names; the referrer *sets* are tier-1 measurements.** A row
> with one named referrer is weaker than one with 128, **so the count is a column rather than a
> footnote** — *a registry that did not say which act it had performed would be read as the stronger
> one.*

**And a fourth numeric coincidence declined:** three classes are read by functions named for item
classes `0x9`, `0xA` and `0xD`, so the encoded-id class space and the item-category nibble **meet** —
**recorded as a correspondence across two numbering schemes, not an identity**, because no code was
read that converts one into the other.

### The fix generalises even where the detection does not

For the shape *"four documents each holding one row of a relation whose other rows are unreachable"*:

> **When a document cites a bare number from a shared helper, that number is a key into a table that
> exists somewhere.** Four documents cited a class and none asked where the mapping lived.

**A convention of "cite the registry, not the number" would have made the gap visible with no new
tool** — which is worth more than an instrument, because it costs nothing and works at writing time.

### Which object a byte hangs off decides what it means

**A document read a branch correctly and attributed the byte to the wrong object.** `+0x6B7` was called
*"the source's record byte"*; **it is on the unit.** The two are built separately in the same function —
one from an owner lookup, the other from a `base + kind*0x40` record — **and the gate reads the unit
while the stored nibble lives in the record.**

**The consequence inverts the reading.** An authored record byte is **a per-action knob a modder could
set**; **a runtime counter with two writers — one incrementing, one clearing on action reset — is
memoisation, and is not patchable the same way.**

> **The skipped roll is not a designer override. The count was decided on hit 1 and kept.**

**And the open answer is why it was correctable.** The falsification row read *"nothing here says who
writes `+0x6B7`"*.

> **Leaving the writer open is what kept the error from becoming load-bearing.** A plausible story in
> that cell would have been quoted forward.

### A combo is a re-commit, and it blocks two other systems

`0030FA00` **re-commits the same action** — reading three fields and calling the commit function with
all three unchanged — and **only a successful commit advances the counter.** Two consequences from one
byte, neither previously written down:

- **You cannot move while your combo is running** — a non-zero counter is an unconditional refusal in
  the navigation check;
- **a combo in progress overrides the leader's party-control suppression wholesale**, **discarding the
  flags accumulated above it rather than adding one.**

### A function that proves its own return type by construction

`BattleStats_FindOwningBattleUnit` **walks the slot pool and matches on `+0x698`** — so its result is a
BattleUnit **because it came from the slot-index getter, not because of its name.**

> **It also identifies `+0x698` as the unit's stats pointer, from the opposite direction to the gambit
> cascade** — a second reading of a field that had only one.

### Four reachable values, no meaning claimed

`+0x6B4` is now constrained by three documents' reads **and by none of their claims**: **`0` from the
action reset, `2` from all 25 dispatcher arms, `5` from the combo continue path, compared against `9`
in party control.** **Recorded as an observation only** — four values with no reading attached is a
better artefact than one value with a story.

### A blank produced by a method is a fact about the method

**Eleven registry descriptors had no named referrer** and looked like a dead end under the naming method
that had worked for fourteen. **Following the anonymous referrers rather than accepting the blank turned
it into a positive claim.**

All eleven are referenced by **the same two functions and nothing else**: an **authored-table loader**
that binds 36 descriptors at area load, and a **generic per-class query** reaching 26.

> ***"No named referrer" was a statement about this database's naming. The engine's answer is "generic
> access only."***

**The fourteen nameable classes have those same two referrers as well** — *what makes them nameable is
the specialised consumers they have in addition.* **So the eleven are live data**, bound at load,
reachable by the generic query, and touched by nothing that would give them a name.

**And one class has neither.** Class 12's descriptor is referenced by **the validator alone** — the
loader does not bind it and the generic query does not reach it. **One of thirty-two classes has no
consumer of any kind.**

> **Both times this move has worked** — here, and in the residual cluster where the evidence was one
> call below where the scan was looking — **asking what the anonymous thing *was* converted "cannot
> name" into a structural finding.**

**It also closed a pair nobody had connected:** the loader is the same function a resource document
already records as populating the slots at area load. **That document reached it from the resource
side; the class work reached it from the class side; neither cited the other** — and *"cite the
registry, not the number"* would have caught this one too, because **the resource document cites the
binder and the class documents cite a number.**

### Print the discriminator you intend to claim

**A census summary printed `{'(none)': 93}` — an aggregate of the *owner* column — and it was read as
a count of *functions*, because the eight rows displayed happened all to sit in one function.**

**The claim "all 93 references come from one function" was false.** The split is **84 / 9** across two
functions.

> **A summary line that aggregates one column will be read as aggregating the column you had in mind.**
> **Print the discriminator you intend to claim, and read more rows than the ones that agree with
> you.**

**93 rows existed and 8 were looked at — all eight agreeing.** That is the same shape as the four call
sites that all passed the same class number, and as the two of three thresholds that read plausibly as
floats: **agreement among the sample you looked at is not evidence about the sample you did not.**

**And the two claims in that message ended differently:**

> ***The claim that was checkable survived; the claim I had not checked did not — and both were in the
> same message. Only one of them was a measurement.***

**What survived:** 93 references, **all on a string start, none mid-string, no pointer array anywhere**
— which settles that the region **cannot be indexed** and is reached only by individual `lea`s.

**And the corrected number was more informative than the wrong one**, because it exposed what the
wrong one hid: **one parameter name has three references across both loaders.** ***A census of a name
counts lookups, not settings.***

## EBP container round — falsification passes, 2026-09-03

**Merged by `repos-55` from five parallel sessions.** Thirteen of fourteen EBP units landed in one
round. Every sheet below was written to `FORMAT.md`, declares its own `ebp_units`, and carries
**interior** address anchors per claim rather than one per function.

**Nothing here is a falsification pass by an independent party.** Each session records the
adversarial work done *while authoring*, which is a weaker thing and is labelled as such: the sheets
carry `audit.passes: 0` and still owe an outside attack.

### Attacks that changed a reading — the ones worth reading

| session | attacked | outcome |
|---|---|---|

### A correction kept rather than rewritten

`section-002-text.md` §6 records permanently that its **first reading treated the entry as a plain
`u32`, concluded `section_002` was structurally broken at 38.8 %, and was wrong** — and *why* that
was reachable, because that is where the same mistake hides elsewhere.

> **Any format whose flag bits are always clear in the simpler of two variants will do this again.**

### Method notes

- **`repos-3f` re-read a whole loader contract from raw instruction bytes via capstone**, against
  the authorized EXE, independent of Ghidra's decompiler. Both agree — the decompiler-invention
  attack executed rather than ticked.
- **`repos-3f` settled the offset origin at the instruction** (`add rax, r8`, `0x00264D8A` /
  `0x00264DBA` — the section), not by inference. File, container and section are three origins.
- **`ff12-script` was deliberately not consulted** by `repos-c7` for either of its sections, before
  or after. **The oracle stays available to falsify the sheets**, which is worth more than a
  confirmation obtained by looking first.
- **A peer check landed a better explanation than the author's.** `repos-4b` established from
  `katanotelload.c` (string `0xd10958`, dispatcher `0x003306E0`) that the four camera/shake sections
  are two **DAT/CTL pairs** — `CAMDAT`/`CAMCTL`, `SHKDAT`/`SHKCTL` — which explains *why* `CML1`
  occupies two slots. `repos-1e` adopted it over its own "shared track container" phrasing.

### Gates

All sessions re-ran `check_ebp`, `check_links`, `check_source_hygiene`, `check_named_not_cited` and
`check_located_not_read` **after** writing, not only before. No unit collisions. Link breaks
observed during the round were **forward references between sheets not yet written** and cleared as
their targets landed — the concurrency case, not a defect.

### Audit debt created

**Thirteen new sheets, all `audit.passes: 0`.** `audit_coverage` fell from 83.73 % to 82.68 % across
the round — the denominator grew faster than attacks were performed. **That is the metric behaving
correctly**, and the debt is real: every one of these owes an independent falsification pass.

## Enemy-record round — merged 2026-09-07 by `xiionline-61` (coordinator)

**Five sessions, one target, and it is the first round in this campaign that hit a success condition
stated in advance.** The board asked for *"a modder can find a specific enemy and change what it
is"* and recorded that **nobody could name one byte of a Marlboro's stats.** They can now.

Program state throughout: **GN160** `fa0db2933c988211ed4f3c76a7dbe3454fc95866745af4605c35177943d2f708`.
Re-verified by the coordinator on 2026-09-07 before the merge — ledger `internal=38161 owner=9409
finalNo=585 codeDomain=28028 explicit=38022 unresolved=139 pct=99.63575`, snapshot
`b57264ba73231665bf226da6d5761feee72df36c5999fc68ae14adfdd18fea34`, residual
`b5008f9d42c7cd6c8f4737528cb9c821cd2b4da419e5523fc7bf67dcdc5e3274`, embedded EXE
`73461d0896204b1c259c52f61aef4efbc95a2ffc388cadb36493d5d1d89721f8`. **All four reproduce**, so every
address below is anchored to a program state that still exists.

### The finding that would not have survived a friendlier round

**`repos-1e` audited the work board's own "already established" block and broke it.** The block read:

```
definition record +0x004   the row index (one byte)
  -> a row in one of the four .ard st2e tables (84 / 88 / 56 / 56)
```

`BattleStats_RebuildEffectiveStatsAndAffinityState` performs that lookup **twice, against two
different registry slots, and only one is an `.ard` slot** — `0x002FF119` resolves `0x02EBF120`
(`.ard` directory slot 2) and `0x002FF065` resolves `0x02EBF130`, *character/unit growth
definitions*, which the `.ard` loader never fills (that loader binds exactly `02EBF150 / 02EBF168 /
02EBF120 / 02EBF148 / 02EBF140`). The function reads **seven** registry slots, not four.

> **Two authors were building on the wrong half at the time it was caught.**

**And the attribution of the error is the part worth keeping.** `authored-data-table-registry.md`
states the lookup **generically** — *"read slot pointer, count at `+0x04`, stride at `+0x08`, RVA at
`+0x0C`, row = base + index × stride"* — and **never says `.ard`.** The document was not at fault.
The `.ard` clause was introduced **by the coordinator's own summary of it**, which is the same
failure the 2026-09-06 10:40 board rewrite was written to fix: *a summary that reads as settled and
is one clause stronger than its source.* **Second instance of that exact shape in three days.**

`repos-c7` reached the same defect independently and **before** reading `repos-1e`'s note, which is
what makes it a finding rather than a report.

### Attacks that changed a reading

The row was written against a gap that had closed. **Independent re-derivation then agreed with all four.** |

`repos-c7` read `0x002FEF30` as a **consumer**; `repos-c9` tracked the same fields across the
**corpus**. They land on the same three edges from opposite ends

`repos-3f`'s opening `ListAgents` returned **`repos-4b`**; a later call returned **`repos-3f`**, with
`repos-4b` live as a separate peer. **Everything that session produced for hours went into another
session's inbox, another session's board row, another session's scratch directory, and audit stamps
reading `last_pass_by: repos-4b`.** The session did not re-check the name after the first call, and
reported the error itself.

**One consequence is substantive rather than cosmetic:** under the name it now holds, that session
**audited and stamped two sheets it had written**, which breaks *an author never audits their own
sheet*. The audit is independent in substance — read cold, and it found the unmasked-count defect at

session's word.** Logged as audit debt against `section-002-text.md` and `section-003-text.md`.

> **The rule this earns: a session's own name is an observation, not a constant.** Re-check it before

## Crossref pass 2026-09-07 — the database's only BODY DRIFT, closed from the image

`xiionline-61`, against a freshly regenerated `ADDRESS-INDEX.md` (**6,975 addresses from 233
documents**, up from 6,940/222) and the GN160 call graph.

**374 findings: 373 `UNACCOUNTED NEIGHBOUR`, 1 `BODY DRIFT`, 0 `GHOST ADDRESS`, 0 `CLASSIFICATION`.**
Zero ghosts and zero classification conflicts across 233 documents is the load-bearing half of that
result — **every address this database cites is still a function, and no document calls something
unresolved that has since been classified.**

**The one drift, settled and closed.** `what-the-console-tunes.md` stated `00200BE0` at 8 B; it is
**7**. Read from the authorized EXE at file offset `0xE01E0`, not from the annotation that raised the
finding:

```
83 39 06   cmp   dword ptr [rcx], 6      3 B
0F 94 C0   sete  al                      3 B
C3         ret                           1 B
```

**The one-byte error is a missing `disp8`.** `cmp dword [rcx], 6` is `83 39 06`; `cmp dword [rcx+8],
6` is `83 79 08 06`. Hand-encoding it with the displacement gives 4+3+1 = 8. **Every sibling accessor
in the family does take a displacement** — `Variant_ReadFloat` and `Variant_ReadInt` both read the
tag off a field — so the expectation was the natural one. `Variant_IsAbsent` reads the tag at offset
**0**, which is a fact about the structure and not only about the encoding: **the tag is the first
member.**

**What was attacked and held:** the semantic reading. The function tests `tag == 6` and returns the
boolean; only the size and the operand form were wrong. The document's own §8 method — *"their raw
bytes, decoded"* — is correct and was applied correctly to `00200B50` and `00200B80`.

**Re-run after the fix: `BODY DRIFT` 0.** `check_links` 10,129/10,129.

**Remaining, and it is the real backlog:** **373 `UNACCOUNTED NEIGHBOUR` across 192 documents.**
Silence is not disposition — each one must be answered, including *"this neighbour is genuinely
irrelevant, and here is why."* Report at `Tools/work/crossref_20260907b.txt`.

## ScriptVM dispatch index mapping — exhaustive pass, 2026-09-07

`xiionline-61`, GN160 `fa0db2933c988211ed4f3c76a7dbe3454fc95866745af4605c35177943d2f708`, table read
directly from the authorized EXE at file offset `0x1DCBD00`.

**Four open questions closed (`I-4`, `I-5`, `I-6`, `I-7`), three opened (`CE-1..3`), and the method
that closed `I-6` five days ago was found to be circular even though its answer was right.**

### The attack

`I-6` had been marked **WITHDRAWN 2026-09-02** in the document and left **OPEN** in the register —
correctly, because the withdrawal rested on **two sample points**. *"No discontinuity was detected
where anyone looked"* is not *"no discontinuity exists."* This pass tested all 1,496 records.

### The circular filter, caught before publication — mine, this session

My first test selected rows where `arity_status == CONFIRMED` and `pops_int + pops_float == arity`,
then asked whether `arity == cat_args`. It reported **567 of 567 agreeing, zero disagreements** —
a suspiciously perfect result on a question that had been open for days.

**`arity` is a reconciled column.** When the catalog and the measurement agree it equals both; when
they disagree it takes **the catalog's** value. So `pops == arity` selects exactly the rows where
they already agreed, and the subsequent `arity == cat_args` test cannot fail. **The filter was the
conclusion.**

The tell was the perfection. Re-running without `arity` — comparing `pops_int + pops_float` to
`cat_args` directly — gives **645 anchors, 575 agreeing, 70 disagreeing.**

> **The 2026-09-02 withdrawal used the same shape** — *"arity over all 1,224 rows shows no shift in
> any band"*, over a population selected by the reconciled column. **It reached the right answer by
> a route that could not have reached a wrong one.** The document now says so.

### What replaced it, and why it is not circular

The catalog's argument count comes from the ff12-script toolchain. The VM operand count comes from
counting `VMValueStack_Pop*` calls in the handler body in this image. **Neither is derived from the
other**, and `arity`/`arity_status` are not used at all.

| | |
|---|---:|
| independent anchors | **645** |
| agreement under `record N = verb N` | **575 / 645 = 89.1 %** |
| agreement under a one-record shift | **55.7 %** |
| span | `0x0000`-`0x05D7`, the entire table |
| mean anchor spacing | 2.32 records |

**Per-bucket agreement is flat at 77.6-100 % with no step.** A slip at record K produces ~89 % below
K and ~56 % above it; no such boundary exists. **The two lowest buckets are the first two**, which is
the opposite of a discontinuity signature.

### What failed to break it

- **An orthogonal cross-check nobody set up.** The callback pattern (`begin`/`poll`/`result`
  presence, read from `.data` here) predicts the catalog's `shape` classification (produced by the
  ff12-script toolchain) on **1,485 of 1,487** records. That agreement is built from no arity
  information whatsoever, and a shifted mapping would break it too.
- **The TSV reproduces from the image**: 1,496 rows × 3 columns, **0 mismatches**. The prior
  session's extraction is independently confirmed.
- **The record count 1,496 is a value the accessors read**, not a shape inferred from contents.

### The residual, stated rather than rounded away

A **compensating pair** of shifts — one skip and one re-add — falling entirely inside a single
anchor-free window cannot be seen by this test. **The largest such window is 25 records.** Every
single shift, and every persistent shift of any size, is excluded.

### The 70 disagreements are a catalog gap

Delta `measured − cat_args` is **+1 in 40 of 70**. That cluster is one family — `camerasync`,
`motionsync`, `fadesync`, `effectsync`, `effectreadsync`: catalog arity **0**, measured **1**, every
one **durative**. They pop the handle of the thing being waited on: **implicit in the authored
syntax, explicit on the VM stack.** A statement about what ff12-script prints, not about which record
the engine reaches. **The remaining 30 are not explained and are now `CE-3`** — a modder hand-writing
one of those verbs will get the operand count wrong.

### The oldest puzzle in the document, dissolved

`0x048D` `openfullscreenmenu_48d` is **the only durative command in its neighbourhood**, and all
three handlers attributed to `0x048C` are its own. **It is what the verb means:** opening a fullscreen
menu is not instantaneous, so `begin` opens it, `poll` asks each frame whether the player is still
inside, and `result` delivers what they chose. Its neighbours — `getmapid`, `getmapgroundtype`,
`npc_to_gimmick` — are one-shot queries needing only a `result`.

**`I-5`'s premise was wrong in the same way.** 262 records lack a *result*; only **3** lack any
callback at all, and **259 are durative commands with `begin` and `poll`.** *"Null handler"* was an
artefact of reading one column of a three-column table — the same frame error, one layer down.

**Document moved to `audit.passes: 4`, `last_pass_state: GN160-xiionline-61-index-mapping-exhaustive`,
`verified_against` re-stamped from GN158 to GN160.**
