## ScriptVM `*sync` verbs — a claim from this morning, attacked and killed, 2026-09-07

`xiionline-61`, GN160. **The claim under attack was my own, published four hours earlier in the same
day's falsification pass.**

### The claim, and why it was worth attacking rather than banking

Section 15 of `scriptvm-native-dispatch-table.md` explained the `+1` arity cluster as *"popping the
handle of the thing being waited on — implicit in the authored syntax, explicit on the VM stack."*
It was reached from a **delta histogram and five verb names**. No body had been read.

**It was written into three places** — the document, the register and this log — with the confidence
of a measurement, and it was an inference.

### The killer observation, and it cost six seconds

Decompiled 29 addresses: the begin/poll/result of every `cat_args = 0, measured = 1` verb plus a
control group of durative verbs where catalog and measurement agree.

`0x0034C290` — the `begin` shared by `camerasync`, `effectsync` **and** `effectreadsync`:

```c
VMValueStack_PushInt32(vs, 0);
iVar1 = VMValueStack_PopInt32CoerceFloat32(vs);
*slot = iVar1;
```

**The handler pushes its own operand and pops it back.** No handle, nothing from the script. The
control group behaves as predicted — `wait`'s begin (`0x0034CF90`) pops **without** a preceding push,
because `wait` really does take an argument.

> **The catalog was right and the instrument was wrong.** The pop existed; it just wasn't an
> argument.

### The instrument finding underneath it

Three metrics were in play and **all three are unsound**: raw pops over-counts (self-supplied
operands), `net = pops − pushes` under-counts (`ames` nets −1, `messync` −2, because they push a
return value), and the reconciled `arity` column is circular for `cat_known` rows. **Arity is a
dataflow property being answered with a histogram.** Raised as `CE-4`.

### What this did to the conclusion it was supporting: made it stronger

`I-6` was re-run under the second metric.

| metric | anchors | identity mapping | one-record shift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `pops` (over-counts) | 645 | 89.1 % | 56.0 % |
| `net` (under-counts) | 612 | **97.2 %** | 59.0 % |

**Two instruments biased in opposite directions both place `record N = verb N` 33–38 points above
its own shifted baseline**, and the disagreement count falls from 70 to 17.

> **The lesson is about test design, not about arity.** The mapping result survived a broken
> instrument because it was posed as a *comparison under a fixed metric* rather than as a
> measurement. Had it been *"the arities match, therefore the mapping is right"*, the refutation of
> the metric would have taken the conclusion with it.

### A third, unused corroboration found afterwards

The GFZ's own per-function evidence record on `0033F4C0` reads
`DISPATCH_PROVENANCE=family0[185].BEGIN`, and `fadesync` is call id `0x00B9` = **185**. It was sitting
in the decompile header the whole time and played no part in reaching the conclusion — which is what
makes it corroboration.

### And a second over-general claim, caught by census before it was published

Reading three polls that all call `FUN_00267310(actorState + 0x15)`, where a non-zero result ends the
wait early and `effectsync` additionally cancels the effect, the natural write-up was *"every durative
poll checks for a skip."*

**Censused first: `00267310` has 65 callers, and only 19 of the 127 distinct family-0 poll callbacks
are among them — 15.0 %.** It is a property of a subset. Published as `CE-5` with the guess (cutscene
skip) named as a guess and the killer observation stated: find the writer of `actorState + 0x15`.

**Two over-generalisations in one block, one caught by reading and one by counting.** The pattern in
both is the same — **five agreeing examples were treated as a family.**

### New engine behaviour recorded

`Native-Command-Lifecycle/native-command-lifecycle.md` section 13: the `begin` callback's third
argument is the command's **private scratch word**, written once by `begin` and read every frame by
`poll`. `wait` stores a frame count and its poll decrements it to below zero; the `*sync` verbs store
a hardcoded selector — `camerasync` waits on camera channel **0**, `eventsync` on slot **1** — which
is exactly why their authored syntax takes no argument. **230 poll slots are served by 127 distinct
functions and 277 begin slots by 191**, so editing one handler edits every verb pointing at it.

Both Script/VM documents restamped GN158 → GN160, `audit.passes` 3 → 4.

## Crossref disposition and the CFG closure — 2026-09-07, `xiionline-61` with `xiionline-8d`

### The largest crossref finding in the database, dispositioned by measuring it

`audit_crossrefs.py` reported **117 edges to/from Presentation never mentioned** by
`resource-section-addressing.md` — the biggest of 384 findings and **8 % of every implicated edge**.

**Censused rather than judged.** `ResourceTable_ResolveEntryByIndex` (`002ED570`) has **87 direct
callers: Presentation 59 (67.8 %), unresolved 16, Boundary 6, and Resource itself 6 (6.9 %).**

> **A Resource-owned document whose subject is called two-thirds by the renderer.** Its §1 already
> said *"every loaded thing in the game arrives this way"* — true, unquantified, and an unquantified
> universal is exactly what hides a 68 % concentration.

Dispositioned as a **real omission of emphasis, not of fact**, and closed with the number.
**Explicitly not licensed:** 59 Presentation callers do not make this a Presentation function.
`002ED570` is a registered hub in `cross-subsystem-accessor-hubs.md`, which already records it as
*"owner Resource — not middleware."* **General rule established for the remaining 383 findings:**
where a finding is driven by a registered hub, disposition by reference to the hub document plus a
caller census — never by asserting the neighbour is irrelevant, and never by moving the document.

### `B-2/a` closed in the negative, and that is a definite answer

*"Which empty destructor did the linker fold onto `0016D6A0`?"* presumes one recoverable identity.
**There is none.** The population is everything in the program whose body is `ret 0`; `/OPT:ICF`
destroyed the distinction at link time and no further reading recovers it.

**Two members survive, and neither is named by the body** — both are named by something outside
`.text` that still points at them:

1. **The CFG check function**, named by the PE load-config directory.
2. **At least one genuine array-element destructor**, named by `Unwind@0089dd0e` passing
   `0016D6A0` in a role a CFG check cannot occupy.

**Derived independently twice**, by `xiionline-61` and `xiionline-8d`, in separate project imports,
both parsing the PE from the authorized EXE rather than trusting Ghidra. Every figure agreed.

**Byte-level correction propagated:** the body is `C2 00 00` — **`ret 0`, not a bare `ret` (`C3`)**.
Three documents said the latter; corrected in `gi-render-command-family.md` and
`why-the-unowned-code-has-no-owner.md`, and by `xiionline-8d` in its own two.

**The naming argument, settled on a principle worth reusing.** `_guard_check_icall` beats
`ICF_FoldedRetStub` because **the load config is the only source that gives those three bytes an
identity the binary itself asserts**; `ICF_FoldedRetStub` describes a shape every empty function in
the program shares. **Prefer the structure that *defines* a name over the structure that merely
*contains* it.**

### What that closure exposed — new question `B-2/f`

`GuardCFFunctionTable = 0`, `GuardCFFunctionCount = 0`, `GuardFlags = 0x00000100`
(`CF_INSTRUMENTED`, **no** `CF_FUNCTION_TABLE_PRESENT`), check function `ret 0`, dispatch pointer
reaching `FF E0` = `jmp rax`. **The compiler emitted `_guard_check_icall` before indirect calls
throughout the image and nothing validates the target at runtime.** Indirect calls can be hooked
without CFG rejecting them. Whether ASLR, DEP and stack cookies are similarly nominal is now open
rather than assumed.

### A peer's self-correction worth recording as a method

`xiionline-8d` had written `set_name` for `0016D6A0` because the address occupies the sixth qword of
both EASTL allocator vtables. **A folded `ret 0` in a vtable slot proves the slot's function is
empty — never which function it is.** Retracted and kept in §8 as a superseded reading rather than
quietly fixed. **Same failure shape as naming a field from its position, one level up: naming a
body from its slot.**

### Instrument defects recorded this pass

- **`iat_xrefs.py` undercounts every import reached through a jump thunk** — `sqrtf` 0 → **566**,
  `memset` 0 → **830**, `memcpy` 0 → **632**, `free` 37 → **860**; headline 3,543 → **7,707 sites**.
  A near-published conclusion (*"the game ships its own maths library because it never calls
  `sinf`"*) rested on a zero. **`memset` scoring zero is what exposed it.** Found by `xiionline-8d`.
- **`check_consistency.py` cross-pairs every address with every name in one table row**, so a
  legitimate `A / B` pairing manufactures a disagreement. `00902FD0` is a `.rdata` vtable named
  correctly twice in its own document. **Writing rule: one address, one name, one row.**

## Third-party inventory attacked, and two peers' findings routed — 2026-09-07

`xiionline-61`, GN160. Block chosen by rebalancing out of Script/VM after two consecutive blocks;
23-Third-Party-Libraries was the highest-debt category not delegated to a peer.

### The attack, and why the document deserved it

`third-party-middleware-inventory.md` sourced its census from **GFZ tag names**. The mission is
explicit that those are claims, not sources. Three claims went to the image and came back
differently.

**CONFIRMED, by a property the tags cannot encode.** Tremor is integer-only Vorbis; libvorbis is
floating-point. Counting float SSE opcodes over exact bodies: **`Audio.Tremor` 4 functions / 5,791 B
/ 0 ops; `Audio.LibVorbis` 11 functions / 7,498 B / 121 ops.** Different link regions too
(`007Fxxxx` versus `0088`-`0089xxxx`). **Both decoders genuinely ship.**

**NOT SUPPORTED.** libxml2 — six markers, zero hits. `002B39A0`, *named* `xmlStrchr`, is a **generic
`strchr`**, and the string `xmlStrchr` appears **0** times in the binary, so the name is a prior
session's identification of a body carrying no library-specific evidence. `002A3730` is a state
machine with nothing XML in it. **Reopened as `CF-1`.**

**X-8 advanced.** Exact versions recovered from the image's own banners: **zlib 1.2.11**,
**Lua 5.2.1**, **libvpx VP8 decoder v1.6.0**. Bullet, JsonBox, Dear ImGui and YEBIS carry **no
version banner at all** — recorded as an honest negative (`CF-3`), possibly unanswerable from this
binary.

### The two lessons, which point in opposite directions

**String absence is not absence** — a decoder is tables and arithmetic, and stopping at the string
scan would have refuted a true claim. **A body every C library shares identifies nothing** — which
is why `xmlStrchr` cannot be confirmed from its body, and why the Vorbis test worked: it used a
property the tag does not encode.

### Routed from `xiionline-13`, whose block contradicted its own brief

**PhyreEngine does not draw this game.** They followed the frame from Phyre's slot 4 to pixels
without passing through a single `Phyre::` symbol. The scene is drawn by a **PlayStation 2 Graphics
Synthesizer GIF command stream** — 16-byte (data, register) records, double-buffered at 512 each,
published to a graphics thread the game thread spin-waits on. GIFtag `0x1000000000008000` decodes to
EOP=1, NREG=1, FLG=PACKED, REGS=0xE (A+D). **The Legacy-PS2-GS texture document reached the same
fossil from the opposite end of the engine** — two independent arrivals at one conclusion.

Also corrected against their own brief: **`SQEX::` is not a rendering layer.** All 353 methods are
`SQEX::Sd::*`, the sound driver, which is 18-Audio's row rather than 22's.

New questions filed from their block: **`CF-4`** (`gi-render-command-family.md` reopen — 36
three-slot command classes in a vtable block it never mentions), **`CF-5`** (the developer console
tunes the renderer; two documents hold half each and neither cites the other), **`CF-6`** (below).

### The most consequential instrument finding yet, and it is not about a script

**Ghidra's decompiler deletes this engine's lock-free settle-spins.** `0036F2C0`'s real 43-byte body
spins until two successive reads of one global agree, then clears bits. **The decompiler emits only
the clear** — it CSEs the two loads and proves the loop unreachable. The idiom is inlined at
**eleven sites, including inside `MainLoop_Draw` and `MainLoop_UpdateAndRenderFrame`.**

> **Read from decompilation alone, this engine's frame contains no synchronisation at all.**

Every threading claim in this database sourced from decompiled output is now suspect and owes a
re-derivation from disassembly. Filed as `CF-6`.

### `0016D6A0` gained a third role, and it changes how the ledger's name must be read

The engine's frame-phase markers compile to `lea rcx,[string]; call 0016D6A0`, so the fold also
carries a **retail-stubbed debug marker**, recovering `PAD CONTROL`, `DRAW`, `CAMERA`, `FAST MODE`,
`VFX`, `UI VFX`, `ATEL CONTROL`, `SOUND`, `CLOSE FULLMENU`, `SCREEN CAPTURE`, `CAPTURE DRAW` and a
`[PS2]*` family.

**Three proven roles, one body, and no name is right at all three.** `_guard_check_icall` is the
**GFZ ledger's own name** — it appears in decompiler output, so this is not a naming choice the
database can simply reverse — and it is **false at two of the three role sites**. Ghidra renders the
engine naming its own frame phases as `_guard_check_icall("PAD CONTROL")`. **This is `/OPT:ICF`
damage beyond a missing name: it attributes one library function's identity to unrelated engine call
sites.** Recorded at `B-2/a` and in `COVERAGE.md` with the reading rule.

### Method note on my own block

The string scan came first and pointed at *two* refutations — libxml2 and Vorbis. **Only one
survived contact with the bodies.** Had the pass been written after the scan and before the reads,
it would have deleted a true library from the inventory. **A scan proposes; a body disposes.**

## `CF-6` worked: the settle-spin census, by disassembly — 2026-09-07

`xiionline-61`, GN160. Block chosen over a fresh category because `CF-6` is a **systemic** risk: if
the decompiler deletes this engine's synchronisation, threading claims across several categories are
wrong. It spans categories, so it does not concentrate the loop.

### The result

**`0x02EBA3F8` is the entire handshake between the game thread and the graphics backend**, and it is
one 32-bit word. New document:
`17-Presentation-Rendering/Graphics-Thread-Handshake/the-shared-command-state-word.md`.

```asm
0036F2D0  mov  ecx, dword ptr [02EBA3F8]
0036F2D6  mov  eax, dword ptr [02EBA3F8]        ; the SAME address, read twice
0036F2DC  cmp  ecx, eax
0036F2DE  jne  0036F2D0                         ; spin until two reads agree
0036F2E0  and  dword ptr [02EBA3F8], 0xFFFFFEF3 ; clears bits 2, 3, 8
```

**Bit 8 is the published-batch flag and the ledger's own names say so.** Three publishers write the
literal `0x100` into the word — `mov`, not `or` — and all three are named `…PublishState100`.
*"State100" is the value `0x100`.* Effect capture layers bit 16 on top and retires **bits 8 and 16
together** with one `AND 0xFFFEFEFF`.

### Census, and it exceeds the reported count

**Twelve settle-spin loops in `.text`; eleven on `0x02EBA3F8`**, including inside **`MainLoop_Draw`**
and **`MainLoop_UpdateAndRenderFrame`**. The twelfth, in `AddMotion_LoadHighModelReplace`, runs the
same shape on a **different global** (`0x02ADD940`) over 11 instructions — so the idiom is a **house
style, not one function's quirk**, which is a stronger statement than the original finding supports
and could only be made by censusing.

`xiionline-13` reported eleven; the difference is exactly that twelfth site on another global.
**Independent derivation, agreeing figure, plus one.**

### Why it is invisible, stated precisely

Two loads of the same address with no `volatile`: CSE folds them, `cmp x, x` is constant-true, the
`jne` is proven unreachable, the loop is deleted. **Correct under the C memory model, wrong about the
machine.**

> **Read from decompiled output alone, this engine's frame contains no synchronisation whatsoever.**

### My own instrument failed first, and the control caught it

The census scan returned **0 sites** — including on `0036F2D0`, which had already been disassembled
by hand in the same block. The loop-start was computed as `jne_offset + 2 + displacement` where the
displacement is already relative to the instruction end: **a double count of two bytes.**

> **A census that returns zero on its own positive control is a broken census.** It was rerun, not
> reported. Had the known site not been in the corpus, "there are no settle-spins" would have looked
> like a clean negative result — and it would have *contradicted a peer's finding*, which is exactly
> the shape of a false refutation.

**This is the third instrument failure in three blocks** — the circular arity filter, the byte scan
matching the REX.W prefix (a peer's), and now this. **All three were caught by a control, none by
inspection.** The pattern worth keeping: *run the thing you already know the answer to, first.*

### New questions

`CG-1` bits 2 and 3 have no located writer · `CG-2` the `0x7FFF0` literal written then partly
retired · `CG-3` the two-thread topology is inferred (tier 8), not read — **the weakest claim in the
new document, and labelled as such in its own evidence table** · `CG-4` whether `0x02EAF6D8` is the
same protocol on a second word, which would make this a family · `CG-5` why nine sites spin inline
*and then* call a function that spins again — **a redundant spin in the main loop is a frame-pacing
cost.**

## Registry census, and a correction to a document I published the same day — 2026-09-07

`xiionline-61`, GN160. Block chosen by rebalancing to `registry_explained`, the lowest-scoring
enumerable metric (9 of 63).

### The census

`.text` disassembled function by function, every RIP-relative operand resolved, every reference into
`02EBF008`-`02EBF1F8` attributed to its owning function. **62 of 63 slots referenced** — slot 50
`02EBF198` by nothing, independently reproducing `AG-4`. **40 of the 62 have a reader the ledger has
already named**, against **9** slots this database explains.

**Published as tier-4 leads and labelled as such before the table, not after.** A reader's name is a
prior session's claim; the census establishes *"a function called X reads this slot"*, which is a
call-graph fact, and nothing about what the slot holds. **`AG-2` moves from an open-ended search to a
ranked worklist with a named entry point per slot.**

**Slot 23 `02EBF0C0` is the loot table** — read by `Loot_RollDropEntries`, `Loot_RollNormalSlotChance`
and `Loot_RollNormalSlotQuantityBucket`, and by nothing else. *What a monster drops.* The surrounding
fifteen-function `Loot_*` family is a complete bounded system with no document.

**A structural find in the tail:** slots 52-62 carry **exactly 2 references each** and 53-62 have no
named reader. Eleven consecutive slots with an identical minimal count is the signature of the
generated per-slot setter family — setter writes, one generic consumer reads. Same shape as the
eleven anonymous class descriptors.

### The correction, and it is against a document published four hours earlier

**`the-shared-command-state-word.md` §1 asserted a two-thread model as fact.** `xiionline-13`
enumerated every thread the image creates — 5 `CreateThread` + 4 `_beginthreadex`, each disassembled
for the `lea` supplying its start routine, largest procedure 555 B — and **none can be a consumer of
the graphics command stream**; imports name no graphics module beyond stock `d3d11`/`dxgi`/
`D3DCOMPILER_47`.

**Verified here by disassembly before accepting it.** `0036F2F0` loads `[02EAF6D8]` at the top, and
its `jne` at `0036F302` targets the `test` at `0036F300` — **the load is outside the loop and nothing
inside can change `eax`.** Inert regardless of who writes the word.

Document reopened (`reopened_count: 1`), §10 added, §1 rewritten to claim only the publish-and-account
protocol, and the two-thread row in its evidence table marked **WITHDRAWN**.

> **The eleven sites in that census survive**, because the scan required **two or more RIP loads of
> one address inside the loop body** — which a hoisted spin cannot satisfy. **Recorded as luck as
> much as design:** the filter was written to find the idiom, not to exclude its inert twin.

### `CF-6` upgraded — two failure modes, not one

> **A spin loop cannot be verified from decompiled output at all.** Only the branch target separates
> a working spin from a dead one, and that is exactly what decompilation discards.

`0036F2C0` and `0036F2F0` are **thirty bytes apart and are opposites** — one re-reads and is genuine,
one is hoisted and is dead — and **decompiled, both render as ordinary spins.** The decompiler
*deletes* genuine spins and *preserves* inert ones.

### Routed from `xiionline-8d`

**`CH-1` — a `.pdata` trap that manufactures a false refutation of `B-2`.** `UNW_FLAG_CHAININFO`
traversal yields **3,828 "gameplay parents"** (Movement 127, ActorEntity 54, CombatAction 49 …).
Killed by two measurements: **zero** of 11,353 entries chain to a parent registering
`__CxxFrameHandler3`, and **all 11,339 resolvable ones chain to the function they are already
inside**. Recorded both in the register and inline under the B-2/e checkbox, because that is the
document whose reader would run it.

**`B-2/e` closed**, and its own count called wrong rather than quietly replaced: **4,314 parents,
3,930 unowned**, not 250. The identifiable unowned ones are Phyre script-binding and reflection, an
octree, and an authored-event path parser — **no battle or field logic**, so `B-2`'s core survived
the attack.

**`CH-2` — a live developer debug menu ships in the retail binary.** `001D0390`, 4,812 B, **301
developer strings** (`100% Spawn Rare Monster :`, `60fps input : `, `Advanced panorama: `).
Undocumented. **Among the highest modding-value findings in the project**, and flagged not to be
conflated with the separate 282-command Developer-Tuning-Console.

### Three sessions, three self-refutations, one day

`xiionline-13` broke a claim it had already reported as surviving its killer observation.
`xiionline-8d` believed a standard traversal's output before checking self-identity. This session
published a two-thread model it had inferred rather than read. **All three were caught by a peer or a
control, none by the author re-reading their own work** — which is the argument for the whole
adversarial structure, stated in one day's evidence.

## Two novelty overclaims, one hour apart, from two sessions — 2026-09-07

`xiionline-61` and `xiionline-8d`. **Neither was an instrument failure.** Both instruments were
correct; both conclusions were about the database and neither session searched the database.

### Mine

The registry census (previous block) reported **40 slots with "a named consumer sitting there
unused."** Grepping each slot address across the database: **39 of the 40 are already cited.**
Exactly **one** — slot 14, `02EBF078` — has a named reader and no citation anywhere.

Worse, the census singled out **slot 23 as "the one worth taking first"** and called the fifteen
`Loot_*` functions *"a system nobody has documented."* `13-Rewards-Progression-Economy/loot-drops-and-enemy-chain.md`
had named `02EBF0C0` the **loot chance-profile table** on 2026-09-02, listed it in its own
frontmatter, and read `Loot_RollAdditionalItemChance` completely. **The claim was false when
written.**

Corrected in place with the withdrawal visible, and the census restated as what it actually
establishes: 62 of 63 slots referenced, **46 cited, 9 explained, 1 genuinely uncited** — plus two
real structural findings (slot 50 referenced by nothing, reproducing `AG-4`; slots 52-62 with exactly
two references each, the generated setter-family signature).

### `xiionline-8d`'s

`CH-2`, filed by me from their report: *"301 developer debug-menu strings shipped in retail,
documented nowhere."* It is the **label-table installer of the Developer-Tuning-Console**, tier 1 in
`arm-catalogue-slice-E-ids-140-171.md` §4 since 2026-09-03; the strings are its **293 command
labels**.

**And it is the exact system the filing warned against conflating it with.** My question text said
*"the Developer-Tuning-Console describes a different 282-command console, do not assume they are the
same system"*, and they report reading that as licence to treat them as different rather than as an
instruction to check. **A warning that names the right document and is phrased as a caution can send
a reader away from it.**

`CH-2` **struck as filed in error, not closed as answered** — at their request and it is the right
call. Recording it as answered would put a discovery in the register that never happened.

### The retraction produced a real result, which is why it is here and not only in `COVERAGE.md`

**`xiionline-8d` re-derived the label table independently before withdrawing**, decoding
`001D0390`'s instruction stream rather than scanning it: **293 conforming label stores, ids 1-294, 0
non-conforming** — identical to slice E, reached by a different method (instruction decode vs that
document's `lea`+`mov` pair walk), and **without reading slice E's numbers until after theirs came
out.**

> **`arm-catalogue-slice-E-ids-140-171.md`'s label extraction now carries an independent
> confirmation.** A survived challenge, obtained accidentally, by a session trying to establish the
> opposite.

### The rule both sessions were missing

> **An absence claim about the database needs a search of the database, exactly as an absence claim
> about the binary needs a positive control.**

Both had been rigorous about positive controls all day. Neither applied the same standard to *"this
is not documented."*

**The mechanism is worth stating precisely: a discovery does not prompt its own verification.** A
measurement invites *"is my instrument right?"* A discovery invites *"what does this mean?"* — never
*"is this already known?"* Both sessions ran controls on their scanners; neither ran a grep on the
answer.

### Instrument tally for the session, now five

`FF 15`-only import census: `sqrtf` 0 → **566**. `0F 51/52/53` byte pattern: 18 `sqrtps` / 4 `rcpps`
→ **13** and **0**. Displacement string scan: 301 "debug strings" → **293** documented label stores.
Plus the circular arity filter and the double-counted branch displacement from earlier blocks.
**Every one caught by a control or a peer; none by the author re-reading their own work.**

### Independent corroboration of the sync-word census, by a different method

`xiionline-13`'s **displacement scan** found **62** references to `0x02EBA3F8`. This session's
**per-function instruction decode** found **24 write-form + 38 read-form = 62**. **Two methods, same
number, neither derived from the other.**

They also kept the right framing on the census filter: requiring two in-loop loads excludes the
hoisted twin **because of a property it happens to encode, which nobody chose**. A future filter
written to the same spec by someone reasoning about *idioms* rather than *branch targets* would lose
that property silently. Recorded as luck, not design, in both documents.

### A session stopped deliberately, and it was the right call

`xiionline-13` declined a scoped, ready fourth target (`Phyre::PSerialization::PStream` `00D26C60`,
`PStreamReaderFile` `00D26C90`, `PStreamWriterFile` `00D26CD0`, `PAssetReference`) on the grounds that
**a third consecutive deep dive in one category is the drift the breadth rules exist to stop**, and
that two corrected, cross-linked, gate-clean documents plus a bounded open question is a better
handoff than a half-read fourth thread.

> **Banking and rebalancing is the rule working, not a session underdelivering.** The entry points
> are recorded so the next block starts warm.

## First independent falsification pass on the maths library — 2026-09-07

`xiionline-61` against `24-Compiler-And-CRT-Runtime/Maths-Library/the-maths-the-game-runs-on.md`
(`xiionline-8d`, same day, `passes: 0`). **The auditor had not read the document before the pass and
did not read the author's inbox notes on it.** Chosen because it is the most falsifiable document in
the owing set: every claim is a constant or a count.

### Method

Every function in the ledger's list decoded linearly from its entry across its exact body extent,
SSE mnemonics counted from the **decoder**, and a per-function byte-count check
(`decoded == body size`) so a desynced stream could not contribute phantom instructions.

### Survived

**`sqrtss` = 4 exactly**, and all four sites match — `0016A270`, `007D0FB7`, `007D119B`, `007E9184`.
That is the document's headline and the basis of its `/fp:precise` conclusion, which stands.
`rsqrtps` = 10. `rcpss` / `sqrtsd` / `rsqrtss` / `sqrtpd` = 0.

**Every cited constant read at its cited address and matched to the digit** — `+4pi` `00D10B0C`,
`-4pi` `00D10B20`, `pi` `01CEBC50`, `-pi` `00915620`, `2pi` negated `00915624`, `2pi` `01CEBC78`.
`02EADEF0` **could not be read as a float because it lies past `.data`'s raw backing**, which is
itself confirmation of the claim that `0.225` is computed at boot rather than stored.

### Refuted

**`rcpps` = 2, not 0.** Both in `FUN_0080A270`, decoded 1,191 of 1,191 bytes with no desync:

```asm
0080A333  psrlq     xmm11, 0x14     ; 20-bit exponent extraction
0080A339  rcpps     xmm8, xmm5
0080A33D  rcpps     xmm10, xmm9
0080A341  cvtps2pd  xmm4, xmm8      ; reciprocal seed widened to double
```

The function is tagged **`Runtime.Math.VectorPowf4`** — a 4-wide vectorised `powf`, exactly where a
reciprocal seed belongs. **This does not overturn `/fp:precise`**: two reciprocals inside a
hand-vectorised `powf` are a library routine choosing its own approximation, not compiler fast-math.
The table said zero; the number is two.

### Corrected, and it changes how the document reads

**`sqrtps` = 14, not 13 — and all fourteen sit in `Audio`-owned functions** (`FUN_007F0320`,
`FUN_007F25E0` and neighbours, `GFZ.V120.PrimaryOwner.Audio`). **The 4-wide square roots in this
image are not geometry.** The geometry path is the `rsqrtps` + Newton-Raphson normalise the document
already documents at `007EF257`. A reader who assumes 4-wide square roots mean vector maths would be
looking in the wrong subsystem, so the attribution was added above the fold.

### The lesson, and it is about corrections rather than scans

The document carries an admirably explicit instrument note: a byte scan reported 18/14/4, a
disassembly pass cut it to 13/10/**0**, a 28 % false-positive rate. **The disassembly pass removed
two true positives along with the false ones.**

> **The scan was checked against a decoder; the decoder was checked against nothing.** Fixing a
> false-positive problem introduced false negatives — harder to notice, because the number moved in
> the direction the author already expected. **When a fix moves a count toward the answer you
> predicted, re-measure rather than stop.**

`status` unchanged at **DOCUMENTED**; the corrections are two counts in one table, not the argument.
`audit.passes: 0 -> 1`. **`audit_coverage` 81.41 % -> 81.91 %, the first rise of the day.**

### `CF-4` corrected — filed by me with a peer's wrong number

`xiionline-13` applied the absence-claim rule to their own earlier report and found that
`gi-render-command-family.md` **does** mention the two classes it owns, and that the uncovered count
is **34, not 36**. **The framing was the worse error:** *"never mentions"* implies an omission, when
that document's census is correct within its own stated scope and the 34 are a gap in a neighbouring
vtable block. Row rewritten.

**Their diagnosis is the sharpest version of the rule yet:** *the failure survives partial reading.*
They had opened the document, quoted its shapes and cited its slots — **having read some of it is
what made them confident enough not to search it.** Three instances in two hours, three different
mechanisms: never opened it, never checked the database at all, read part and generalised.
**Familiarity is the risk factor, not ignorance.**

## `BP-2` closed — the reserved control codes, from both readers — 2026-09-07

`xiionline-61`, GN160. Block chosen by rebalancing back to writing after two audit-flavoured blocks;
**15-Input** was the highest-debt category no peer holds.

### The answer

**The 35 ids at `01DF13E0` are a bind-blacklist**, and they are in the **game's own control-code
space**, not Windows virtual-key codes.

### How the encoding was settled, and why it did not need a new derivation

`BP-2` recorded that the value `2` and the run `131`-`152` fit either reading. **The adjacent table
decides it without touching the 35 at all.** Four dwords at `01DF1470`, read with a single `movups` by
`InputManager_MaterializeRuntimeBindingProfiles`, hold `{65, 66, 67, 118}` — which under this
database's own `PInputKeySemantic − 1` mapping is **F1, F2, F3, Left Shift**, *exactly* the
`Speed1/2/3/WalkMode` defaults `BP-6` had recovered independently from `keymap.ini`. Under Windows VK
they would be `A, B, C, F7`.

> **The neighbouring table was the evidence, not the table under question.** Nothing in the 35 values
> themselves could distinguish the two encodings; four values sitting eight bytes past them could.

### What the list does, from both of its readers

`InputManager_ValidateBindingUniqueness` (`00196550`, 135 B) rejects a set if any code is **duplicated
across all 84 slots** or **appears in the 35-entry list**. `01DF146C − 01DF13E0 = 0x8C = 35 dwords`, so
**the count is the loop bound itself** rather than a run length someone eyeballed — and
`InputManager_AssignBindingWithConflictPolicy` (`00198A00`, 349 B) confirms it a second time with a
literal `0x23` loop bound.

That second function is the whole single-assignment path: kinds 0/1/2 with slot limits 16/8/4,
reserved-check first, `0` unbinds and always succeeds, then either **refuse (`1`)** or **swap** — the
swap hands the conflicting slot this slot's old code, which is what a player sees in the remapping
screen.

**A reserved code and an out-of-range slot return the same error (`2`)**, which is why a hand-edited
`keymap.ini` line using a reserved code fails without saying why.

### A layout confirmation nobody was looking for

The three `kind` cases bound slots at **16 / 8 / 4**, and the three name tables hold exactly **16 / 8
/ 4** entries — `Select…Square`, `RX_P…LY_N`, `Speed1…WalkMode`. **16 + 8 + 4 = 28**, the profile
stride, and 3 × 28 = **84**, the validator's `0x54`.

**`BP-6` derived 28 from the file format; this derives it from the assignment code.** Two independent
routes to the same layout, neither citing the other.

Also worth recording as an instrument note: **the name tables are UTF-16**, so an 8-bit string read
returns only first letters — `S`, `L`, `R`, `S`… which looks like a plausible table of abbreviations
and is not one. Index 13/14 read correctly as `Circle`/`Cross`, the pair `BP-1` proved the platform
swap exchanges.

### Left open honestly

**Why each code is reserved is not established.** The contiguous `131`-`152` tail reads as enum values
with no keyboard behind them and the punctuation exclusions (`83`, `86`, `87` remain *bindable*) read
as layout-dependent keys, but the two functions say only that these are refused, never why. Recorded
in the document as not established rather than as a plausible story.

## The maths document's real error, found by a peer verifying my audit — 2026-09-07

**My pass corrected two counts and passed the document. The larger error was in the half I
confirmed rather than the half I corrected**, and `xiionline-8d` found it while reproducing my
corrections.

### What I got right, and the note that turned out to be the thread

I recorded, as an aside to the `sqrtps` count correction, that **all fourteen sites are
`Audio`-owned**. `xiionline-8d` pulled that thread across the whole instruction set:

| instruction | sites | `Audio`-owned |
|---|---:|---|
| `sqrtps` | 14 | **14 / 14** |
| `rsqrtps` | 10 | **10 / 10** |
| `sqrtss` | 4 | **3 / 4** — the exception is `0016A270`, the boot-time constant |

> **Every SIMD square-root site in the image belongs to the sound engine.**

### Why that is a correction and not a footnote

The document's §2 and §4 were built around the `rsqrtps` group — *"the vector maths that **is** in the
game"* — with the Newton-Raphson normalise at `007EF257` as its centrepiece, presented as **geometry**.
**It is the sound engine's DSP.** The body reading was correct throughout; 3-D positional audio needs
exactly cross products and normalises. **The attribution was wrong, and it would have sent a modder
hunting geometry code into the audio subsystem.**

**The corrected claim is stronger than the original.** The geometry path contains **no SIMD at all**
and takes every square root through the 566 scalar `sqrtf` calls — *which is precisely what
`/fp:precise` predicts*. The document's two headline findings now corroborate each other instead of
sitting next to each other.

### What my audit did wrong, precisely

I checked **ownership for the count I corrected** (`sqrtps`) and **not for the counts I confirmed**
(`rsqrtps`, `sqrtss`). Confirming a number felt like finishing with it.

> **A confirmed count is not a checked claim.** The number was right and the sentence built on it was
> wrong, and nothing in "14 is really 14" prompts you to ask what the fourteen *are*. **An audit that
> verifies figures and not attributions will pass a document whose figures are all correct and whose
> reading is inverted.**

### The instrument bug, now precisely named

`xiionline-8d` re-derived the counts by **disassembling all 38,161 functions linearly from their own
entries** — no scanner, no false-positive correction, seconds to run — and reproduced 14 / 10 / 4 / 2
exactly.

The original scan excluded any `0F 5x` whose preceding byte was `0x40`-`0x4F`, an exclusion added **to
fix an earlier REX undercount in the prefixed forms**. It then discarded the REX-prefixed **NP-forms**:
`44 0F 51` at `007F0A17`, `44 0F 53` at `0080A339`, `45 0F 53` at `0080A33D`.

> **The fix for one REX blind spot created another, in the same instruction family, on the same
> line.** And because the corrected count moved *toward* the expected answer, it read as confirmation
> rather than as an untested new result.

### Boot order — the prologue, and why it is an injection-timing fact

`xiionline-8d` grepped first this time and reports **no large gap**: the 1,172-entry table, the C/C++
split, TLS, teardown and `T-1`/`T-2`/`T-3` were already covered. What was missing is the *prologue*
— the document began at `_initterm`, and two things run before it:

```
AddressOfEntryPoint RVA 006E8EE4 -> entry (00808EE4, 18 B)
   call __security_init_cookie (00809B8C)      <- the FIRST call in the process
   jmp  00808D78  (CRT startup, 330 B)
        _initterm_e (00862022) -> C table,   __xi,     3 entries
        _initterm   (0086201C) -> C++ table, __xc, 1,172 entries
        _get_narrow_winmain_command_line -> call 007A3770 (45 B)
```

**True order: cookie, 3 C initialisers, 1,172 C++ initialisers, game.**

**The modding consequence is real and belongs to this repository.** The stack-cookie global ships
holding the MSVC default and is randomised by **the first call in the process** — so **anything
injected before `entry` reads a stale cookie and anything after reads the live one.** That document's
own *"TLS: storage yes, callbacks no"* finding proves there is no earlier hook, so `entry` really is
first, and the **earliest engine-neutral hook point is `00808D78`.**

`007A3770` sits in the slot MSVC reserves for `WinMain`, and 45 bytes is a thunk rather than an
application. **Recorded as positional — tier 1 for the call sequence, tier 6 for the CRT-source
shape — and deliberately not traced.** The obvious next pull for whoever wants the game's real main.

### A generalisation of the `B-2/b` deletion worth keeping

`xiionline-8d` on my row-splice error: **every other mistake traded this session left a wrong value
someone could read and doubt. That one left nothing.** It was caught only because a *different* file
still pointed at the hole.

> **A deletion is invisible in the file it happened to.** The defence is that a programmatic anchor
> must be **unique**, not merely correct at the point you looked — and only a cross-file checker can
> see the damage when it is not.

## `CB-5` advanced — the two stat paths, and a decompiler struct that names one record twice — 2026-09-07

`xiionline-61`, GN160. Block chosen by rebalancing to a named open question in the enemy-record
thread, which is where the mission's own success condition sits.

### What was learned

**`rec[+0x05]` selects two disjoint stat sources inside one function.** When it is `0`, growth comes
from the character/growth definitions at registry slot `0x02EBF130` and the record's contributions are
read as **`float`**. Otherwise it comes from the four **`.ard`** tables as
`growth[col] × (bLevel − bGrowthBaseLevel) + base[col] +` an integer record modifier. **Both paths
converge on the same output slots and the same clamps** — which is exactly what makes the columns
nameable.

**The `.ard` growth/base column map**, derived by pairing each computed value with the clamp it lands
on and using output names this database proved *from readers*:

`+0x20` int **HP** (`0x7FFF`) · `+0x24` s16 **MP** (999) · **`+0x26`-`+0x29` = Strength, Magick Power,
Vitality, Speed** (99, four consecutive bytes in on-screen order) · `+0x2B` **Defence**, `+0x2C`
**Magick Resist**, `+0x2D` **Attack** (255, *not* contiguous with the core four and *not* in screen
order) · `+0x2A`, `+0x2E`, `+0x02`, `+0x03` the four rate fields (100), the last three reached only
through the `[spine+0x15]` flag-gated blocks.

> **An enemy's Strength growth is one byte** — `.ard` column `+0x26` of the growth table at slot
> `0x02EBF140`, with its flat base at the same column of `0x02EBF148`.

### The finding that outranks it

**The decompiler's typed struct names the same record inconsistently, and the function proves it.**
Four output slots are fed by `(float)nAttackPowerModifier`, `(float)nMagickResistModifier`,
`(float)nWeaponGuardRateModifier` and `(float)nSpecialGuardRateModifier` on the `rec[+0x05] == 0`
path, and by `nStrengthModifier`, `nMagickPowerModifier`, `nVitalityModifier` and `nSpeedModifier` on
the `.ard` path — **and all four clamp at 99**, the cap proved from readers to belong to the four core
attributes.

Either the struct named those offsets after one branch, or **the same bytes mean different things
depending on the selector.** The function cannot distinguish the two, and the document does not
choose. Filed as `CB-12` with the killer observation named.

**Why this is a `COVERAGE` rule and not just a note:** a decompiler struct arrives *rendered into the
C* as though the binary asserted it. Nothing in the output marks it as an annotation, it reads with
the typography of a fact, and **the inconsistency is invisible unless you read both branches** — a
reader who opens the function at the branch they care about finds perfectly plausible names.
**Where a struct name and a clamp class disagree, the clamp is a machine fact and the name is not.**

### Method note

The naming was done **entirely from clamp classes and computation order**, never from the struct
names — which is the only reason the inconsistency was visible at all. Had the struct been trusted,
the four core attributes would have been recorded as Attack, Magick Resist and two guard rates on the
character path, and the contradiction would have been written into the database as a finding.

### `CB-5` is advanced, not closed

It asked what the **eleven `s16` record fields at `+0x08`-`+0x1C`** are called. This pass mapped the
**`.ard` columns**, which are the *other* term in the same sum. **Naming the eleven requires settling
`CB-12` first**, and that dependency is now explicit in the register instead of latent.

## `§3b` of the Phyre schema-join document refuted, and the two wrong answers had one cause — 2026-09-07

`xiionline-8d` auditing `22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Reflection-And-Class-Metadata/the-file-schema-against-the-runtime-schema.md`.
⚠ **Attribution corrected 2026-09-07:** this log first recorded the document as `xiionline-13`'s. **It is
not theirs** — it is dated **2026-09-05**, two days before that session began, and was already in the
category listing before their first edit. It sits in their *row*, so applying the REOPEN was their job
and they did it, but **the author is someone else and the trail must say so.** `xiionline-13` raised
the correction themselves, on the grounds this database already holds: *who wrote a claim is evidence
about where the same mistake hides*, and the unstated-method failure below is now a lead about that
author's other work rather than about a session that merely inherited the file. **Audited read-only** — category 22 had a file modified minutes earlier, and they
would not write into a moving lane. Disposition routed to the owner rather than applied.

### What survives

The class-level join, the `Base` trap (**all eight pairs** re-checked against an independent string
scan), the unattributed-member honesty, and the corpus-skew statement. **The refutation touches none
of it.**

### What breaks

§3b builds a negative on *"`PClusterHeaderBase` has eighteen recovered field records and not one name
string in the image."* **False, and not narrowly** — all 22 candidate gaps are present, three
independent ways:

| test | result |
|---|---:|
| bare name string in `.rdata` | **22 / 22** |
| `PClassDescriptor*<T>` RTTI descriptor naming the class as a **template argument** | **21 / 22** |
| `PObjectAccessor<class …>::Get` script-accessor string | **21 / 22** |

Only `PContextSwitch` lacks the latter two. The decisive artefact is the third line of this triple,
which is not a name in a string table but **the reflection system's own class-descriptor template,
instantiated for that class and compiled into this build**:

```
.rdata  "PShaderVertexProgram"
.rdata  "…PObjectAccessor<class Phyre::PRendering::PShaderVertexProgram *>::Get"
.data   ".?AV?$PClassDescriptorAbstract@VPShaderVertexProgram@PRendering@Phyre@@@Phyre@@"
```

So §3b's reading 2 — *"the PC binary may simply never register it"* — **is refuted for 21 of 22**, and
its conclusion *"the question is not statically answerable"* is false: it is answerable on **Route 1,
the document's own first route**, done correctly.

### The cause, and it is the same cause twice

**`xiionline-8d`'s first attempt failed the same way the document did.** They searched direct RTTI —
`.?AVPShaderVertexProgram@Phyre@@` — found **2 of 22**, and were about to file a narrow partial
correction.

**The control refused it.** Of 18 classes the document says *are* recovered, only **one** has a direct
RTTI descriptor, and the whole image holds just **40** `@Phyre@@` descriptors against **246** class
names. **A "no" from that search carries no information.**

What broke it open: Phyre does not emit RTTI for the class, it emits RTTI for
`PClassDescriptor*<TheClass>` — so the class name appears **as a template argument**. Searching for it
directly finds almost nothing; searching for it as an argument finds everything.

> **Both wrong answers came from searching for a name in the form we expected it to be written, and
> then reading absence as evidence.** The escape was running a positive control *before* writing.

### The methodological finding, which outlasts the correction

§5 of that document specifies its corpus scanner reproducibly. **The image-side string search in §3b
states no method at all** — no sections, no length bounds, no tool.

> **Every other claim in the document is reproducible from what it writes down, and the one claim
> whose procedure is unstated is the one that is wrong.** A falsified measurement with no recorded
> procedure cannot be debugged, only replaced.

That is a sharper argument for recording method than any rule in the evidence standard, because it is
an observed correlation inside a single document rather than a principle asserted about documents in
general.

### Disposition

**REOPEN is mandatory** under the standing rule (a claim overturned by stronger evidence), and it is
the owner's edit to make. Recommended and routed, not applied: close §7's leading question as
*recovery gaps, 21 of 22, `PContextSwitch` open*; **keep §3b rewritten rather than deleted**, since
Routes 2 and 3 remain sound and the section is stronger as *"three routes failed and the fourth, done
correctly, succeeded"*; and `evidence_tier` should improve off 9 now that the central question no
longer rests on the corpus.

New question for the neighbouring document (`CL-1`): **why does the 682-call-site census miss 21
classes that carry descriptor RTTI and script accessors?** §11's *142 registrars with no named field*
is exactly where that document guessed to look — **it was right about the place and tested the wrong
names against it.**

## World loot pickups documented — 2026-09-07

`xiionline-61`, GN160. New document:
`13-Rewards-Progression-Economy/world-loot-pickups-the-ten-slot-pool-and-the-despawn.md`.

**Chosen because a grep for `WorldPickup` across the whole database returned zero** — the drop *roll*
was documented since 2026-09-02, and what happens to loot once it is on the ground was not covered
anywhere. **That check was run before the block, not after**, which is the habit three sessions spent
today's failures learning.

### What was learned

**The world holds exactly ten loot pickups.** Both bounds are literal in `Loot_CreateWorldPickup` —
`iVar4 < 10` and a `0x18`-dword (`0x60`-byte) node step. **An eleventh drop is never refused and never
queued: the engine evicts the list head, the oldest pickup still on the ground**, sends it
presentation op **5**, clears its presence slot and reuses the node. In a long fight in a crowded
room, uncollected loot is being deleted behind the player, oldest first, with no signal.

**The lifetime ladder, exactly.** With `DAT_01CEBCAC = -30.0f` and `DAT_01DFE0B8 = 1.0f` both read
from the image, `step = -30`, and states 2-6 advance on
`stamp + 30 × (60 − (7 − state)) ≤ now` — thresholds **1650, 1680, 1710, 1740, 1770** — with expiry at
`stamp + 30 × 60 = 1800`. **Total 1800 clock units, the blink occupying the last 150 in five equal
steps**, and the presentation argument is `7 − state`, counting **5, 4, 3, 2, 1**.

**The unit of the clock is deliberately not claimed.** 30 Hz would make it sixty seconds with
one-second blinks, which matches play — recorded as an unproven reading in §5 and `CM-1`, and marked
in the evidence table as **not evidence**.

**A pickup carries seven item stacks**, bounds confirmed independently in the grant loop and the tier
scan, with `0xFFFF` the empty sentinel. **The three presentation tiers are computed before the pickup
exists** and short-circuit: one class-1 entry whose runtime category is 1-5 returns tier 0 at once, so
the shine advertises a pickup's *best* contents rather than an average. The encoded item id carries
its own row — `stride × (id − 0x1000) + base` into registry slot `02EBF0F8`.

### The cheapest modding lever found today

**`01DFE0B8` is one float in `.data`, default `1.0`, multiplying the entire ladder.** Because the
blink and the expiry share the term, changing it scales both coherently — `0.5` doubles how long loot
survives. No code change.

### Method note

The GFZ's own annotations on these functions were unusually rich — *"fixed ten-node 0x60-stride local
pickup pool"* was already written into the comment block. **Every figure in this document was
re-derived from the body anyway**, and the two agree. That is worth recording as a case where the GFZ
was *right*: the standing rule is not that its annotations are wrong, it is that they are claims, and
this one survived being treated as one.

Where the GFZ's typed struct was used (`FFXII_WorldLootPickupNode_0x60_Partial`), **the field offsets
were cross-checked against the raw dword indices in the other three functions** — `pNext` at `+0x18`,
`pPrev` at `+0x10`, handle at `+0x58` — and are self-consistent, unlike the `target_bkbi` struct
whose names this session refuted an hour earlier.

### The REOPEN, and a regex that would have quietly closed a question

`xiionline-13` **re-derived the refutation from the image before applying it** — an audit is a claim
like any other. It held decisively: §3b reported `ClusterHeader` → 0 strings and the image has **18**;
`PClusterHeaderBase` **6**, including three mangled descriptors in `.data`; `ShaderVertexProgram`,
also reported 0, has **10**. Independent census over all 22: **bare name 22/22, `PClassDescriptor*<T>`
21/22, absent by all three 0/22** — matching `xiionline-8d`.

**One disagreement, and the looser instrument lost.** `xiionline-13` initially got **22/22** on object
accessors where `xiionline-8d` had **21/22**. Their regex matched the class name *anywhere inside the
angle brackets*, so it counted

```
PArray<class Phyre::PRendering::PContextSwitch const *,8>::Get
```

— an accessor for **an array of** the class, not for the class. They adopted the stricter 21/22.

> **A looser regex would have quietly closed `CL-2`.** The question *"is `PContextSwitch` genuinely
> unregistered?"* only exists because one search was strict enough to leave it open. **A permissive
> matcher does not usually announce itself by being wrong; it announces itself by making a residual
> disappear.**

Applied by the owner of the row: `status` → **REOPENED**, `reopened_count` → 1, `evidence_tier`
**9 → 3** (the load-bearing evidence is now `@Phyre@@` qualified symbols rather than the corpus). §3b
rewritten as **four routes, three failing and the fourth settling it**, keeping Routes 2 and 3 intact.
Two §6 falsification rows overturned **in place rather than deleted** — including one that had claimed
the string search was already falsified, now marked as that document's worst error.

**The methodological finding was given its own section rather than a line**, with the recall argument
in reusable form — ***a search that finds 1 of 18 known positives cannot support a negative*** — plus
the note that a control passing on *one* positive licenses nothing. `xiionline-8d`'s near-miss is
recorded there too: **an audit that almost filed the wrong correction, and the control that refused
it, is worth more than a clean catch.**

## The frame-rate scalar triple, and a modding note that was wrong in the way that matters — 2026-09-07

`xiionline-61`, GN160. Block chosen by rebalancing into **06-Movement-And-Navigation**, the one
player-facing category this session had never touched — and the register answered the question before
the work started.

### `K-8` already held the answer to a question filed one block earlier

`CM-2` asked what `01DFE0B8` is, offering the `Speed1/2/3` toggles as a lead. **`K-8`, closed on
2026-09-02 from the Movement side, had already censused the triple** and reported all three writes
inside `001EDDC0` with the 60 fps setting running at 2.0 / 0.5.

> **The answer was in the register under a different category, filed five days earlier.** The register
> is searched by id and by owner document; **nothing in the workflow searches it by *address*.**

### Verified rather than adopted, and the branch is now read

```asm
001EDDC4  test  ecx, ecx
001EDDC6  je    0x1EDE1F            ; zero -> block skipped, .data defaults stand
001EDDC8  movss xmm0, 2.0
001EDDD0  movss xmm1, 0.5
001EDDD8  movss [01DFE0B8], xmm0
001EDDE0  movss [01DFE0BC], xmm1
001EDDF2  mov   dword [01DFE0B4], 2
```

**Defaults `(1, 1.0, 1.0)`; enabled `(2, 2.0, 0.5)`** — an integer sub-step count, a scale-up and its
reciprocal. Independent read census: **211 / 45 / 182**, against `K-8`'s 211 / **46** / 182. **A
one-count difference on the middle term, recorded and not adjudicated** — neither write-up states its
method finely enough to settle it, and the agreement on structure is the finding.

### What it settles downstream

**`CM-1` closes: the field clock counts frames.** The pickup step is `(int)(scalar × −30.0)` = 30 or
60 frames, so a pickup's life is **1800 frames at 30 fps and 3600 at 60 fps — sixty seconds either
way**, five one-second blink steps. **The scalar exists precisely to hold wall-clock duration constant
across frame rates**, which turns the seconds reading from an assumption I refused to publish into a
consequence I can. **The caution was right and the evidence arrived one block later.**

**`CM-2` closes and its lead was wrong** — nothing to do with the game-speed toggles.

### The correction that matters most, and it is to my own modding advice

The pickup document named `01DFE0B8` **"the single cheapest lever on this system — one float, no code
change."** The arithmetic was correct. **The consequence was not:** the float is read **438 times
across the triple**, and moving it rescales every timed system in the game.

> **A modding note is a claim about *consequence*, not about arithmetic — and it is the one kind of
> claim in these documents a reader acts on directly.** *"This float multiplies the term"* is a
> measurement. *"This is the cheapest lever"* asserts something about **everything else that reads
> it**, and that requires a read census which had not been run.

**Rule added: before naming any address as a lever, count its readers.** The census that settles what
a global *is* also settles whether it can be moved.

Corrected in place with the original wording visible, because *"true about the arithmetic, wrong about
the consequence"* is a failure shape worth being able to recognise again.

## `K-6` closed, and the frame audit returns — 2026-09-07

### `K-6`: `movementState + 0xA8` is the facing angle

`xiionline-61`, GN160. **A dataflow scan finds exactly two writers image-wide** — a register *proven
loaded from* `[actor + 0xB8]` and then stored through at `+0xA8`. One writes a qword and cannot be
this float field. The other, `FUN_002E5E10` (374 B, Movement), stores

```
bias  = (angle >= 0) ? +pi : -pi
[state+0xA8] = ((angle + bias) - (int)((angle + bias)/2pi) * 2pi) - bias
```

— **a normalisation into `[-pi, pi]`, open-coded rather than calling `Angle_NormalizeRadiansPi`.**
Since there is one writer, **no path can leave the field out of range.**

Setting a facing also pushes three or four sub-objects through `FUN_003DA850` (transform
invalidation), with **actor `+0x0D` bit 5 suppressing two of them** — `K-12`. `FUN_002E5F90`
re-applies the field's own value: *"re-commit the facing I already have."*

**The question was malformed and saying so is the answer.** `K-6` asked which of the two GFZ names
(`flCurrent_heading` `+0xA0`, `flDesired_heading` `+0xA4`) is wrong. **The pair was never a complete
account of the group** — `K-1` proved those two drive *motion*, and the unnamed `+0xA8` is what the
engine reports as *facing* to the canonical accessor's 33 callers. **No renaming proposed.** The
facing-versus-motion relationship is an inference from combining two results and continues as `K-11`.

### The instrument, and why the first version was worthless

The first scan used **co-occurrence** — a function that stores to `[reg + 0xA8]` and *somewhere else*
loads `[reg + 0xB8]` — and returned **283 of 450 sites**. That is no signal: `0xA8` and `0xB8` are
ordinary struct offsets and almost any large function touches both.

> **The positive control is what made the replacement trustworthy.** The dataflow version was run
> first against `FUN_00265200`, whose read of `+0xA8` is already known, and found it. **A scan that
> cannot find its own control is not evidence about anything else** — the fourth time today that rule
> separated a result from a number.

### `xiionline-8d`'s frame audit — both named claims survive, and one should be *strengthened*

**`REGS = 0xE` is A+D: survives three independent ways**, none needing the PS2 hardware reference the
document apologises for leaning on.

1. **The record layout is the A+D layout** — `*p = data; p[1] = regId; p += 2` is the definition of
   the packed A+D record, and the document's own struct says so without joining it to the `0xE`.
2. **Eleven consecutive valid register ids** in `0036D400` — `4C 4E 18 40 1A 46 45 47 00 01 47` =
   FRAME_1, ZBUF_1, XYOFFSET_1, SCISSOR_1, PRMODECONT, COLCLAMP, DTHE, TEST_1, PRIM, RGBAQ, TEST_1 —
   which a wrong REGS reading would have to produce by chance, in initialisation order.
3. **The data words match the register field layouts.** `SCISSOR_1` is written
   `((base-1) << 32 | (extent-1)) << 16`, placing the maxima in SCAX1/SCAY1 with the minima zero — a
   full-screen scissor, nonsense under any other field reading — and `RGBAQ` is written as a dword
   **the function immediately above splits on exactly the R/G/B/A byte boundaries**.

Also consistent: `TEST_1 = 0x50000` is ZTE=1 / ZTST=GEQUAL, `PRIM = 6` is *sprite* (the full-screen
quad), and XYOFFSET uses the standard 2048-origin bias.

> **The recommendation is to make §4.1 *less* tentative** — the rarer failure direction, and worth
> correcting for the same reason as over-confidence. The PS2 reference should drop from *"the
> corroboration this rests on"* to *"a name for something already proven."*

**Frame modes: survive**, re-derived over **every** mode value 0-7 rather than at the values named.
`(mode-4) & 0xFFFFFFFD == 0` holds for exactly 4 and 6; `(mode-2) & 0xFFFFFFFC == 0` for 2-5; the net
*"input pumped in 2, 3, 5 only"* holds, including that mode 6 never reaches the inner test. **The
author's own hedge — strong for what a mode does, weaker for what a player calls it — is correct and
should stay.**

### New and undocumented: a second, outer back-patched length

`0036D400` reserves a 16-byte record **ahead of** the GIFtag and patches it after finalising:

```c
region = *cursor;  *cursor = region + 0x10;
... 11 A+D records ...
n = ((pWrite - region) >> 4) - 1;
*(u64 *)region       = n | 0x10000000;
*(u64 *)(region + 8) = n ? (n << 32 | 0x5000000011000000) : 0;
```

**Two nested back-patched lengths** — the GIFtag `NLOOP` the document covers thoroughly, and this
outer one it never mentions. The same `0x10000000` constant *is* discussed elsewhere in that document,
at a site where it is written bare with a zero second qword and reasonably called a **terminator**;
here it carries a count, **so "terminator" is not a general reading of that constant.** Structure
stated as the finding, DMA-chain-tag shape as corroboration only. **Modding consequence: rewrite the
register batch and *both* counts need fixing.**

### The audit states its own scope, which is the part to copy

§2.4, §2.6, §4.3, §4.4, §5 and the companion document's order-key/sort-site gap were **not
examined** — *"a partial audit that gets logged as a full one is its own failure mode."* Recorded
here as partial, and **the frame document does not gain a `passes` increment for sections nobody
read.**

## The spatial audio object model, and a claim I passed confirmed by a test it never ran — 2026-09-07

`xiionline-61`, GN160. New document: `18-Audio/the-spatial-audio-object-model.md`. Entry point was
this session's own maths audit, which found **every `sqrtps` and `rsqrtps` in the image is
Audio-owned** and left that as a one-line attribution note.

### The finding

**FFXII has five shapes of sound source, and the amount of vector maths per class tracks the
geometric complexity of the shape.**

| class | slot 34 | SIMD |
|---|---|---|
| `PointSound` | yes, `007F1A50` | `sqrtps` x1 |
| `PolygonSound` | yes, `007F25E0` | **`sqrtps` x7** |
| `DynamicSound` | yes, `007F1340` | `sqrtps` x1 |
| `DirectionSound` | **no** — heavy method at slot 7 | `rsqrtps` x1 |
| `AmbientSound` | **no override at all** | **none** |

> **A sound that is everywhere needs no geometry, and the class that models it has none.**
> `AmbientSound` contributes three methods and not one SIMD instruction; `PolygonSound` needs seven
> square roots because distance to an *edge* is not distance to a *point*.

Nine `SQEX::Sd::Lay::*` classes, **39 recovered virtual methods**, each class's overrides occupying
**one contiguous address range** — compile order, hence declaration order in one translation unit.

### The methodological point: owner tags are a classification, not a reading

The maths document concluded *"the geometry path contains no SIMD at all"* from the fact that every
SIMD site is **owner = Audio**. **That is a GFZ classification and therefore a claim.** If the cluster
were a general vector library mis-tagged, the conclusion would be wrong.

**Censused the callers rather than the functions: 12 direct callers, 12 Audio-owned, none from
Movement, Presentation or anywhere else.** The cluster's own callees are Audio functions plus
`__security_check_cookie`.

> **A claim resting on an owner tag can be upgraded by censusing the *callers*, which the tag does
> not determine.** The conclusion I passed in audit this morning now rests on a test the original
> never ran — and it survived.

### Why this family was invisible

**Five of the twelve SIMD functions have zero direct callers**, including a 2,115-byte method holding
seven of the fourteen `sqrtps` in the executable. They are **virtual methods**: a call-graph search
returns nothing, and every prior pass over Audio walked call graphs.

**The recovered RTTI vtable map is what made them findable** — `B-3`'s 4,275 address-to-class-and-slot
rows, applied for the first time here to a *system* rather than to naming. That was the stated value
of the RTTI work when it was banked on 2026-09-02, and this is the first block to collect it.

### The honesty note that matters most in this document

**Section 1 is the weakest part and is marked so in the evidence table at tier 8.** *"A river is a
polygon source"* is a reading of a class name and an instruction count — **no audio was heard and
exactly one body was read.** The writing standard asks for the player-facing opening in a confident
register; the evidence table is where the real tier belongs, and the two must not be allowed to
agree by default.

`PolygonSound`'s actual distance-to-edge formula is **not extracted** and is filed as `CO-3` — it is
the thing that would turn §1 from plausible into proven.

### Residue

`CO-1` the `+0xE4` gate · `CO-2` slot 34's return value · `CO-3` the polygon algorithm · `CO-4` why
`DirectionSound` uses slot 7 · `CO-5` the listener object behind `FUN_007BB610` (position at `+0x30`,
a sixteen-float transform at `+0x60`) · `CO-6` proving `AmbientSound` has no spatial path at all.

## `CO-3` extracted — the polygon distance algorithm, and a constant that nearly became a story — 2026-09-07

`xiionline-61`, GN160. Complete decompilation of `PolygonSound::slot34` (`007F25E0`, 2,115 B), taken
deliberately as **new evidence rather than self-audit** on a document written an hour earlier whose
§1 was marked tier 8.

### The algorithm

**Two modes, on a byte at `+0x104`.** Mode `0` scans `+0x108` vertices for the nearest. Non-zero runs
the plane path: normal from three vertices (`FUN_007F74E0`, normalised with `rsqrtps`), signed plane
distance `t = dot3(n, v0 − P)`, project the listener to `P + t·n`, point-in-triangle test
(`FUN_007F7570`) — **inside gives the perpendicular `|t|`; outside gives the minimum of three
closest-point-on-segment distances** (`FUN_007F7440`), the edges indexed by a compiler-expanded
`i % 3`.

**That is the textbook point-to-triangle distance**, and it accounts for the seven `sqrtps`.

### The near-miss, and it is the useful part

Every distance is `sqrt(Σ (P−Q)² · w)` where the decompiler renders `w` as **four separate symbols** —
`_DAT_00D11570`, `_UNK_00D11574`, `_UNK_00D11578`, `_UNK_00D1157C` — multiplied into four separate
lanes.

**That reads exactly like per-axis weighting**, and per-axis weighting would have been a genuine
finding worth writing up: a designer could make a sound fall off faster vertically than horizontally.
The sentence was drafted.

**The sixteen bytes say `(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0)`.** It is the **W-lane kill mask**, and it is the *same
constant at the same address* that the maths library document already records for the masked
3-component dot product. **It is an ordinary 3-D Euclidean distance computed 4-wide.**

> **Four adjacent `_UNK_` symbols are one constant the decompiler could not name.** The rendering
> multiplies a vector constant lane by lane and gives each lane its own symbol, which manufactures
> the appearance of four independent parameters. **Reading the bytes settled it in one step; the
> story would have survived every gate in the kit.**

This is the second time today a decompiler *rendering* — not a decompiler error — nearly produced a
false finding: the first was the `target_bkbi` struct naming one record two ways. **Both were
invisible to every checker and visible immediately in the raw bytes.**

### What it does to the document it was aimed at

**§1's polygon claim moves from tier 8 to tier 1.** *"A polygon source is measured to a surface, not
to a point"* was written from a class name and an instruction count; the plane projection, the inside
test and the three edge distances are now read. **The evidence table records the split** — polygon
tier 1, the other four classes still tier 8, because their bodies remain unread.

**And it corrected §1 as well as confirming it:** there are **two** modes, and a `PolygonSound` in
nearest-vertex mode behaves much more like a point source than the section implies. A confirmation
that changes nothing is usually a confirmation that did not look hard enough.

### Residue

`CO-7` which mode the shipped data uses · `CO-8` `+0x218`, written `0xFFFFFFFF` **only when an edge
wins** and never when the perpendicular or a vertex does, so it records *which feature* was closest ·
`CO-9` whether the vertex array is one triangle or a fan.

### Audit debt handed out

`the-spatial-audio-object-model.md` and
`world-loot-pickups-the-ten-slot-pool-and-the-despawn.md` were both authored by this session today
and both carry `passes: 0`. **Handed to `xiionline-8d` for cold falsification passes**, with the
weakest claim in each named explicitly: for the audio document, §1's tier-8 shape descriptions and
the 12-of-12 caller census that props up the maths document's SIMD conclusion; for the pickup
document, that *"non-zero `ecx` means 60 fps"* is **an inference from the constants — the caller that
passes `ecx` was never found**, and if it is wrong the entire timing section is out by a factor of
two.

## Two cold audits of this session's own documents — 2026-09-07

`xiionline-8d` auditing `18-Audio/the-spatial-audio-object-model.md` and
`13-Rewards-Progression-Economy/world-loot-pickups-the-ten-slot-pool-and-the-despawn.md`, both
authored by `xiionline-61` earlier the same day. **Scope declared on both, and both partial by

sentinel and the seven-granted claim **remain unaudited**.

**The auditor also declared an interest before starting**: the audio census is cited as support for
their own maths document, and they checked whether their claim depends on it first. **It does not** —
theirs is about the *functions'* owner tags from their own decode, mine about *callers*. Recorded
either way, which is the right handling.

### Audio — the conclusion survives, the number was inflated fourfold and partly circular

*"The twelve functions have 12 direct callers"* — **there are nine distinct callers.** Twelve is the
number of call **edges**, and *the coincidence that the edge count equalled the function count is
exactly what hid it.* The document's own neighbouring line — *"the five heavy methods have no direct
callers"* — was in tension with it and nobody noticed.

**Worse, four of the nine are members of the twelve** (`007EF630`, `007EF790`, `007F1670`,
`007F25E0`): **the cluster vouching for itself.**

> **Honest figure: five callers from outside the cluster, all Audio-owned.** The conclusion holds —
> zero non-Audio callers, internal or external — **but on five independent supports rather than
> twelve.**

**Second finding, unflagged by the author:** the `Sd::Lay::*` class table accounts for **4 of the 12**
SIMD-bearing functions. The other eight carry SIMD and no class attribution, two of them two `sqrtps`
each. **The table reads as a complete partition and is not one.** Now `CO-10`, and a warning block
sits above the table.

### Loot — the caller I could not find exists, and it upgrades the claim it corrects

This document recorded *"non-zero `ecx`"* as **an inference from the constants**, with the caller
never located. It exists, there is exactly one, **and it was in the call graph the whole time**:

```c
0022BDF0 (146 B, CoreRuntimeScheduling):
    iVar1 = FUN_0017D8F0();            /* 11 B: *(u32 *)(*(void **)0x01F82D20 + 0x48) */
    FUN_001EDDC0(iVar1 == 1);
```

**`0x01F82D20` is the `GameSetting.ini` singleton and `+0x48` is `FrameLimit`, settings index 18** —
**already documented in this database.** The scalar is chosen by a named user setting read from the
ini, so the claim moves from *inference from constants* to a read chain ending at an authored
configuration field.

**Two corrections.** The gate is **`FrameLimit == 1`, not "non-zero"** — every other value takes the
other branch and leaves the defaults, so the original phrasing was wrong for any state above 1.
**That is precisely the factor-of-two worry the author flagged when handing the document over,
surviving in the phrasing after the substance was fixed.** And the other branch is **not inert**: it
raises the Windows multimedia timer via `timeBeginPeriod`, released by `timeEndPeriod` on the `== 1`
path — **a lower-rate mode needing finer OS timer granularity is independent corroboration that these
are two frame-pacing modes.**

**Still not established, and now recorded as `CM-7`:** that `FrameLimit == 1` means **60** rather than
30. The scalars are unambiguously *twice the base rate*; the base is not read. Every wall-clock figure
in that document rests on the base being 30.

### The pattern the auditor named, and it deserves the standing they suggest

> **The missing caller was a search failure, not an absence.**

Same shape as their own `001D0390` retraction, from the other side — and the third instance this
session of *the thing was already there and findable*: the registry census (39 of 40 slots already
cited), the debug menu (documented since 2026-09-03), and now this caller (in the call graph, and the
field it reads already documented in another category).

**All three were absence claims about work that existed.** The scanner rule — *a zero from an
instrument is a claim about the instrument* — has an exact twin for the database, and it has now cost
three blocks: **an absence claim about the database needs a search of the database, and "I could not
find the caller" is such a claim.**

**And the habit paid out rather than merely preventing an error:** the auditor found `+0x48` by
grepping the database **before** calling it unknown, which is what turned a dead end into a closed
chain.

`xiionline-61` and `xiionline-8d`, both cold, both partial, both scoped explicitly. **They reached

### The finding, twice

§1: *"Nothing in the executable holds those numbers at rest."* **The executable holds all three** —
`39.0`, `42.0`, `43.0` at `009146EC`/`F0`/`F4`, read by `FUN_0023A520` (66 B), which installs the
whole default set: three floats, `0xB4` (180, the forward half-circle) and `1`.

**And this is not a research gap — the document already has every fact.** Line 276 calls
`FUN_0023A520` *"the only writer of the whole default set"*; lines 280-287 give the disassembly
*including* `movss xmm0, [009146EC] ; 39.0`; lines 466-468 tabulate all three floats by address.
**§1 asserts the negative of what §3 tabulates, four hundred lines apart.**

> **Worse than the audio case earlier today, not better.** That contradiction was a paragraph apart
> between two technical statements. **This one crosses the §1/§3 boundary — and §1 is the section
> written for the reader who will never reach §3.**

**`xiionline-8d` added the noise floor**, which an absence claim and its refutation both need: each of
`39.0`, `42.0`, `43.0` occurs **exactly once** in the whole 32 MB image, 4-byte aligned, and the three
are consecutive.

**And the corpus comparison, which makes the consequence concrete.** The sentence tells a modder the
default ring is not patchable in the binary. **It is: 12 bytes at `009146EC`** changes the ring and
retire range for every zone that does not override — **368 of 406 by the document's own §2f** — plus
one immediate at `0023A550` for the arc. The alternative it implies is editing zone scripts, of which
§2f counts **828**. *The document's own corpus numbers show the binary patch is two orders of
magnitude cheaper.*

### What survived, verified independently by `xiionline-61`

Every measurable claim attacked reproduced exactly: the three `.rdata` constants; the complete 66-byte
installer body instruction for instruction; **all five tunable globals past `.data`'s raw backing, so
zero at image load** — which is what makes §1's *intended* reading correct; Correction 1's
decomposition of `0x0002200000000000` into bits **45 and 49**; and Correction 2's stride.

**Correction 2 deserves specific credit for what it does not rest on.** `0x9400` partitions exactly
**both** ways — `64 x 592` and `296 x 128` — so the arithmetic alone could never settle it. It rests
on **sixteen `imul r, r, 0x250` sites**, and a census run with a positive control (the document names
`0023588B`; the scan found it first) confirms **exactly sixteen Spawn-owned functions**, every one it
names among them. Image-wide the immediate appears in 18 functions / 27 sites, the extras being
unrelated UI and Presentation uses — so the claim is correct as scoped and the scope should be stated.

### The error this pass made, and it is the more useful half

**`xiionline-61` filed the GN158 `verified_against` stamp as a defect and updated it to GN160.**
`xiionline-8d` caught it. **The stamp records what the document was verified against**, and it was
last reviewed when GN158 was current — the frontmatter working as designed. The standing rule is
explicit: *never edit a provenance stamp to make a check pass.* **What was stale is the review, not
the stamp.** And a **partial** pass cannot update a whole-document stamp regardless: four claim groups
were examined and six sections were not.

Reverted, and the pass section now carries the withdrawal in place of the false finding.

> **The failure is dangerous because it does not feel like a claim.** *"Bring the stamp to current"*
> looks like housekeeping, passes every gate, and erases which program state the evidence was
> gathered against — **and it was done by the session that had just flagged the stamp as
> suspicious.** Noticing a field is out of date and *correcting the field* is the natural next
> motion, and it is exactly backwards.

The document carries **`audit.passes: 0`** and **`falsification_passes: 1`** at once. It was handed to
the auditor as *"never falsified"* when `repos-9e` had run a full pass on 2026-09-03. **`progress.py`
