## 2026-09-08 — A gate that checks a claim, not a document

**The §38 integrity item said the gates "check document hygiene, not knowledge integrity".** The
contradiction ledger, one block old, said which claims this database gets wrong: `no-reader-found`
and `E8-only-reachability`, **6 of 33 corrections between them**. `check_absence_claims.py` tests
that class and only that class. New page: [`ABSENCE-CLAIM-GATE.md`](ABSENCE-CLAIM-GATE.md).

```
absence phrasings found                     372
  no address on the line - unverifiable     298   (80 %)
  address-anchored and tested                74
    call claims      35   |  reference claims  39
  naming instrument NEGATIVE - claim stands  46
  naming instrument POSITIVE - flagged       28
    of those, the SAME LINE already refutes   7
```

**Reading the remaining 21 line by line: no unhedged false absence claim.** The corpus hedges in its
own words — *"was read in this pass"*, *"was found"*, *"Not established, and deliberately not
claimed"* — and several are narrative *about* a past correction rather than a new one.

> **A null result with a denominator.** Before this there was no instrument; now 74 claims are tested
> on every run, and the gate will catch the next unhedged one the day after it is written.

### The tool's own output corrected the tool, twice

**1. A phrase names which instrument can refute it.** The first version ran all four against every
phrasing and returned **55** candidates. Most were the documents agreeing with themselves: *"`0081D790`
has zero callers"* flagged because a `lea` materialises the address — while the next clause of the
same line reads *"it is address-taken once, at `0081DF7C`"*.

> **A function with no caller can perfectly well be address-taken.** "Zero callers" is a claim about
> `E8`/`E9`; an operand hit does not contradict it. Binding phrases to instruments took 55 → **28**.

**2. The `qword` instrument is a poor absence-refuter.** Scanning every section at 4-byte stride
collected **98,285** plausible VAs; narrowed to 8-aligned data sections it still holds **92,162**.
Against a corpus that size a coincidental match is likely for any address, and it produced 19 of the
original 55. **It is excellent for confirming a pointer sits in a vtable — the use it was introduced
for — and weak as a general "is this referenced" test.** After the phrase mapping: 3 of 28.

> The mission prompt's four-instrument rule says each has produced the only correct answer at least
> once. **That remains true and is not the same as saying each is equally precise**, and this run
> measured the difference for one of them in one role.

### A heuristic removed rather than shipped

A filter to skip lines that negate the phrase — *"**not** unreferenced"* — **never fired once across
the corpus**, while the identical regex matched the identical line correctly in isolation. The cause
was not found.

> **A filter that reports zero while possibly being broken is worse than no filter**, because every
> later run inherits a silent exemption. Deleted. Its job is now done by the phrase→instrument
> mapping, which is a rule rather than a guess.

### Deliberately not claimed

That the database makes no false absence claims. **298 of 372 phrasings name no address** and cannot
be tested by anything; the 74 that can were read at **line level only**, not in the context of their
sections; and proximity-matching an address to a phrase is a heuristic that can pick the wrong
subject.

## 2026-09-08 — Which way a character turns, and a mode that depends on the frame rate

Three blocks of tooling; this one is game knowledge. `coverage_balance.py` ranks
`06-Movement-And-Navigation` the second-highest **player-facing** debt (485 functions, 5 documents),
and the index named its most-called undocumented function: **`0026C120`, 354 B, 26 callers**. New
document:
[setting the movement mode](../06-Movement-And-Navigation/Movement-Mode-Selection/setting-the-movement-mode-and-which-way-a-character-turns.md).

### The finding, in the game's own terms

**A character turns the short way round because the heading difference is wrapped into (−π, π] before
its sign is taken**, and that sign is stored as **one bit** — `steer->+0x62 & 0x40` — decided once
when the mode is set and spent over the following frames.

```asm
movss  xmm0, [steer + 0x34]      ; target heading
subss  xmm0, [body  + 0xA8]      ; minus current heading
call   0x3A1C50                  ; wrap
comiss xmm0, 0  /  jb            ; negative -> set bit 0x40, else clear it
```

`003A1C50` is an angle normaliser and its four constants prove it rather than suggest it:
`00915620 = -π`, `01CEBC78 = +2π`, `01CEBC50 = +π`, `00915624 = -2π`.

Modes 2 and 3 also write the rate: **`+0x58 = 0x3E20D97C` = π/20 = 9 degrees**, and
**`+0x5C = 0x40490FDB` = π = a half-turn.**

### Gated to one actor kind, which is why 26 callers can be unconditional

```asm
movzx eax, byte ptr [rcx + 3] / and al, 0xE0 / cmp al, 0x60 / jne -> return
```

`+0x03` is the packed `(kind << 5) | sequence` discriminator, so this is **`kind == 3`**, the
steerable kind. Every other actor falls straight out.

### A player's Frame Rate setting changes when mode 4 ends

```asm
movsx eax, word ptr [steer + 0x68]
cmp   eax, dword ptr [01DFE0B4]        ; the FrameLimit time base, 1 or 2
ja    -> leave the mode running
      -> set the facing, then RESET the mode to 0
```

**`01DFE0B4` is the `FrameLimit` time base** documented earlier in this session from the settings
config — 1 or 2, chosen by the player's Frame Rate option. **Mode 4 is a one-shot that ends a frame
earlier at one setting than the other.**

> That is a menu option reaching into movement timing. **The comparison is real and is stated as what
> the code does; whether a player can see it is not established** and is filed as `DP-2` rather than
> asserted.

### Two documents met in the middle

`how-a-character-turns.md` already documents `0026B620` (`Actor_SetFacingHeading_Variant1`) and names
`+0xF0` as *"pointer to the steering record"* — **and nothing else about that record.** `0026C120` is
the layer above it: it writes `+0x28`, `+0x34`, `+0x58`, `+0x5C`, `+0x62` and reads `+0x65`, `+0x68`,
and calls `0026B620` as one of five outcomes. **Six new fields on a record another document had only
a pointer to.**

### Deliberately not claimed

That `+0x58` is "9 degrees per frame" — π/20 and π are unmistakable as a step and a half-turn, but
**the consumer was not read**, so the units are `DP-1`, not a statement. That the mode numbers mean
*walk* or *run*: the switch is the evidence, the vocabulary is not, and no caller was traced to
supply one. And `002EBE50`, `002E8EE0`, `002E6300` are named as the mode-0 chain and left unread.

## 2026-09-08 — How a sound fades: six curves, written out with their constants

`18-Audio` is the **largest single owner in the ledger** — 2,064 functions, more than any other
category — with 12 documents. The index named its most-called undocumented function with a real
formula in it: **`007A9E50`, 204 B, 63 callers.** New document:
[how a sound fades](../18-Audio/Audio-Boundary/how-a-sound-fades-the-ramp-and-its-six-curves.md).

### The six curves, complete and closed

A six-arm jump table at `007A9F1C`, using exactly two constants — `01CEBBA8` = **1.0f**,
`01CEBC08` = **2.0f** — and `powf`:

```
id 0        0                    (silence; also where every id > 5 lands)
id 1        1 - (1 - t^2)^3
id 2        1 - (1 - t)^2
id 3        t^2
id 4        2^t - 1
id 5        2 - 2^(1-t)
```

**All five real curves map 0 -> 0 and 1 -> 1.** Ease-in: 3 and 4. Ease-out: 1, 2 and 5. Reproducible
by hand at the midpoint — 0.578, 0.75, 0.25, 0.414, 0.586 — which is the writing standard's test for
whether a formula is documented or merely mentioned.

### The ramp, proven twice over

```
ramp +0x08 start   +0x0C target   +0x10 elapsed   +0x14 duration   +0x1C curve id
stride 0x30
```

> **Two independent functions read those same five offsets**, which is why the layout is `PROVEN`
> rather than read once and believed: `007A9E00` evaluates a single ramp, `007A9D30` walks an array
> of them, and they agree field for field.

`duration == 0.0f` is tested with an **equality** compare and means *snap to target, no
interpolation* — a very small non-zero duration does not take that path.

**A voice's parameter is a PRODUCT**: every ramp's current value multiplied together, times a master
at `voice->+0x4C`, with the accumulator starting at 1.0. So a track fading in while the mix ducks
does both at once and the result is the product, not the sum.

### Nothing clamps `t`

Neither caller clamps `elapsed / duration`, and `007A9E50` guards only the curve **id**
(`cmp edx, 5 / ja`). At `t = 1.5`, curve 3 returns 2.25 and curve 4 returns 1.83. **Whether that can
happen depends on whoever advances `elapsed`, which was not read** — `DQ-1`, filed rather than
assumed away in either direction.

### Deliberately not claimed

**Which parameter these ramps drive.** A normalised interpolation multiplied into a product with a
master level is the shape of a volume chain, and saying so would have been easy and probably right.
**No caller was traced to a mixer field**, and the same machinery would serve pitch or a filter
cutoff identically. `DQ-2`. Nor that the curve ids have authored names: they are `0…5` as the jump
table decides them, and the shapes are the evidence, not a label.

## 2026-09-08 — The reconstruction roadmap, and a metric that counts denials

**Two charter §38 first-actions close together**: *identify subsystems near reconstruction readiness*
and *build a prioritized roadmap*. Both were open for one reason — `DJ-1`, the readiness ladder is
stated in **6 of 221** documents — so `readiness_rank.py` ranks the **preconditions** instead. New
page: [the reconstruction roadmap](RECONSTRUCTION-ROADMAP.md).

### The answer

**`19-Save-Load-Settings` is the only category with a contract, a type and coverage all non-zero**
(1 contract, 1 type / 40 fields, 34.5 % of its owner's functions cited). `16-UI` and `18-Audio` each
have a contract and **zero types** — their §3 is a header table, not a `_types/` entry, and that is
the next step for both.

Cheapest completions: `14-Story-Event-Quest-Hunt` at **100 % owner coverage** over 15 functions,
`10-Status-Periodic-Terminal` 91.7 %, `13-Rewards` 78.9 %, `21-RNG` 77.8 %.
Thinnest: `17-Presentation-Rendering` **5.9 %** over 1,564 functions, `01-Script` 6.8 % over 1,900.

### A ratio whose halves came from different populations

The first version divided *"functions this category's documents cite"* by *"functions this owner
owns"* and reported **313 % for `14-Story-Event-Quest-Hunt`**. A category's documents freely cite
functions another category owns.

> **A ratio whose numerator and denominator are drawn from different populations is not a ratio.**
> `cov%` is now the intersection and cannot exceed 100 %. The bad version was caught by its own
> output being impossible, which is the cheapest kind of catch and the reason to print the number
> rather than a grade.

### The metric that counts denials

`program_coverage.py` reports *"documents citing any runtime/live-process evidence"* by searching the
body for markers — `live process`, `debugger`, `tier 10`, `breakpoint`, …

**Those markers match negations.** Of 17 documents containing one, **at least 3 have every occurrence
inside an explicit denial** — including two contracts written this session whose sentence is,
verbatim, *"Nothing in this contract has been observed in a live process."*

> **A document is counted as runtime-evidenced for saying it has no runtime evidence** — and the
> documents doing it are the ones I wrote to be careful about exactly that claim.
>
> **The over-count is a floor, not a total.** A 110-character negation window catches that sentence
> and misses a marker sitting under a *"What this document does not claim"* heading, which is how
> several others are phrased. The true figure is at most 14 and `DR-1` does not guess where below.

### Two indexing fixes on the way there

- **`runtime_markers` is now a column** on `documents`, so the index and the coverage report answer
  the same question. The existing `high-confidence-no-runtime` query had been looking in
  **frontmatter**, where no such key exists, and would have returned every PROVEN document — right
  answer, wrong reason.
- **The marker list is imported, not copied.** A copy dropped four of eleven markers and reported 11
  where the owning tool reported 14. Same drift as the question ledger, same fix: one definition,
  one caller. The two now agree at **14 and 14**, and the `13` in `PROGRAM-STATE` was simply stale.

### Not claimed

That any subsystem has reached the charter's runtime gate. Correcting for the defect above, **no
category has a document that positively asserts live-process observation of the system it
documents.** The roadmap says which subsystem is closest to the gate, not that one has passed it.

## 2026-09-08 — Acting on the roadmap: the two contracts that had no type now have one

The roadmap written one block ago named the next step in one sentence: **`16-UI` and `18-Audio` each
have a contract and zero types — that is their next step.** This block took it.

```
GAME types in the _types/ store        2 -> 4
fields on a GAME type                 81 -> 109
categories with contract + type       1 -> 3   (of 3 that have a contract at all)
```

**Both are game types, not engine types** — the number the charter's L2 gap is actually about.

### `AudioParameterRamp`, and why it is not `TYPE RESOLVED`

Six fields, stride `0x30`, from
[how a sound fades](../18-Audio/Audio-Boundary/how-a-sound-fades-the-ramp-and-its-six-curves.md).
The stride is **proven** — `add rbx, 0x30` in the array walk — and the five live fields are read at
identical offsets by two independent functions.

> **24 of those 48 bytes have no reader in either function** (`0x000`–`0x008`, `0x020`–`0x030`), so
> the type is **`SIGNATURE RESOLVED`**. Calling a half-read record `TYPE RESOLVED` because its
> extent is known would be exactly the rounding-up the ladder exists to prevent.

### That exposed a real flaw in the validator's own rule

`types_index.py` suppressed gap warnings for any type below `TYPE RESOLVED`, on the reasoning that a
sample-derived type has gaps by construction. **That rule conflated two different situations**:

| | |
|---|---|
| *"we only sampled this type"* | a Phyre reflection class: extent unknown, gaps meaningless |
| *"we know the exact extent and half of it is unread"* | `AudioParameterRamp`: gaps are **findings** |

Labelling the ramp honestly would have **hidden its two real gaps**. The rule now keys on
**whether the type declares a numeric size**, not on its readiness label: a declared size means a
known extent, and its gaps are reported whatever the label says. Both `AudioParameterRamp` gaps are
back in the report, and the 179 sample-derived Phyre types still produce none.

> **The honest label and the visible gap were in tension, and the fix was to stop deciding by label
> and start deciding by evidence.**

### `Widget`

15 header fields from [the contract](../16-UI/Widget-Object-Model/CONTRACT-widget-object.md), which
were already differential-tested — 320 cases, 192 bytes compared, 0 mismatches. **`size` is
`UNRESOLVED` on purpose:** it is an *argument*, 26 distinct values from `0xC0` to `0xBC08`, so there
is no `sizeof(Widget)` to record. `+0x10 parent` is `PROBABLE` where `+0x18`/`+0x20` are `PROVEN` —
the child and sibling links are proven by the broadcast recursion, the parent link only by a flag
write.

### The roadmap keeps its original figures

Its table now reads `~~0~~ **1**` rather than `1`. **A roadmap that silently rewrites itself cannot
be checked against what it recommended**, and the point of the page is that a recommendation was made
and then acted on.

## 2026-09-08 — the database, measured against the charter's own quality standard

**Block:** charter §38's oldest open first action — *audit the database against the
reconstruction-grade requirements (§3)*. New tool: `charter_grade_audit.py`. New index:
[`RECONSTRUCTION-GRADE-AUDIT.md`](RECONSTRUCTION-GRADE-AUDIT.md) + `.tsv`.

### The finding that changes how every other metric here reads

**Documents name 5,812 of the 7,376 function entries they cite — 78.8 %. `functions.tsv` carries
a name for 677 — 9.2 %.** 5,383 names exist only in Markdown; 248 only in the ledger; 1,316
nowhere. Every tool in this kit that has asked *“is this function identified?”* asked the ledger,
and **understated §3's first dimension roughly eight to one.** `DU-1`.

### One dimension of seven cannot be asked at all

§3 wants preconditions, postconditions, invariants, state read and written, side effects,
allocations, branches, state transitions, failure paths, edge conditions. **The schema has nowhere
to put any of it** outside contract prose, and there are three contracts. **No keyword proxy was
invented for it** — that is exactly how `DR-1` happened, where a marker list counted documents
denying runtime evidence. `Behaviour` is reported UNMEASURABLE and the record type it would need
is named.

### Ladder monotonicity is now checkable, and 10 of 15 labelled documents owe a rung

Six of the thirteen rungs have a mechanical criterion; the other seven are reported
`not-evaluable`, never as passing. Two distinct shapes of debt:

- **4 documents at or above `RUNTIME VALIDATED` owe exactly that rung.** Nothing in the database
  has reached it. One blocked experiment — `EXP-001`.
- **6 at `BEHAVIORALLY UNDERSTOOD` over a category with no `_types/` entry and no contract** owe
  `SIGNATURE RESOLVED` and `TYPE RESOLVED`, both **below** them. Undone work, and cheaper.

> **Nobody was demoted.** Rung debt is a fact about a label and the evidence under it; whether to
> relabel four documents or to declare the ladder non-ordinal is a decision, and a decision is not
> a measurement. What is plain: **the ladder cannot express “everything except runtime”**, which
> is exactly what this database's four best documents are, and each says so in its own words.
> `DV-1`.

### §27 scored by hand: 20 of 21

No mechanical proxy for *“can a researcher answer what its invariants are”* is honest, so the
completion gate was scored by reading, on one named subsystem — the `GameSetting.ini`
configuration object. **20 of 21 answered; the miss is destruction, and the contract states it
rather than omitting it.** §26's readiness gate then fails on one question only: runtime
validation. **The category around it does not follow** — save image layout, version stamps,
locale and file locations have no contract.

### The tool corrected itself twice before shipping

Its first Identity row read **7,376 / 7,376 named** — that every cited function has a semantic
name. `NOT LIKE 'FUN[_]%' ESCAPE '['` asks for a literal `]` and matched every row. **An
implausible 100 % is what exposed it.** Its first summary line then claimed all 10 debtors owed
the same rung, while its own table showed six owing two different ones. Both are fixed, and the
first is recorded in a comment beside the query so it cannot come back.

## 2026-09-08 — the steering record, found by following a pointer instead of a displacement

**Block:** the cheaper half of the rung debt the reconstruction-grade audit measured — six
documents at `BEHAVIORALLY UNDERSTOOD` over categories with no type and no contract. Two are
`06-Movement-And-Navigation`.

| | |
|---|---|
| new tool | `record_field_scan.py` — follows a pointer CHAIN, register by register, per function |
| new document | [the two steering slots](../06-Movement-And-Navigation/Facing-And-Steering/the-two-steering-slots-and-what-a-character-resumes.md) |
| new side file | `steering-record-fields-observed.tsv` — 32 offsets, every site |
| new type | **`SteeringRecord`**, `0x80`, 32 fields (13 named, 19 `UNRESOLVED`) |
| questions | **`DW-1`**, **`DW-2`** filed |
| type store | 183 → **184** types, 722 → **754** fields, **0 errors** |

### What the binary said that no document had

`Movement_SelectSteeringSlot` (`00269F90`, 36 B) is four instructions of arithmetic and it
settles the record's identity outright:

```
movzx eax, byte [rcx+0xDC] ; cmp al,1 ; ja ret ; movsx rax,al ; shl rax,7 ;
add rax,0x120 ; add rax,rcx ; mov [rcx+0xF0], rax
```

**`shl rax, 7` is the size.** The record is `0x80` bytes, it is **not allocated**, and there are
**two of them inline** in the movement context at `+0x120` and `+0x1A0`. `+0xF0` is a cursor, not
an owning pointer. The 32 observed fields span `+0x00`–`+0x7C` — **exactly filling `0x80`**, an
independent corroboration of the stride.

Its only two callers are a **depth-one push/pop pair** whose guards are symmetric and both fail
closed: push refuses when the selector is already 1, pop refuses when it is already 0. The pop
replays three saved dwords, dispatching on `flags & 7`.

### An ambiguity between two documents, settled from the binary

`how-a-character-turns.md` called `+0x29` *“the stored steering mode”*;
`setting-the-movement-mode…md` called `+0x28` *“MODE”*. **Both setters reach the same record by
the same chain, so these are two adjacent fields, not one described twice.** Neither document was
wrong; between them they had given two different bytes the same name, and no gate could see it —
`check_consistency` compares names per ADDRESS, and these are two different offsets on a record
that has no address of its own.

### The control caught a real defect before anything was published

`record_field_scan.py` requires hand-derived controls and **refuses to report if one fails**. The
second control demanded `+0x58`, `+0x5C`, `+0x65` from `0026C120` and the first run produced none
of them: the scan is **linear, not control-flow aware**, and that function restores
`mov rbx,[rsp+0x30]` in its mode-4 epilogue, killing register tracking for the mode-2/3 block
that follows and is only reachable with the register live. Epilogue restores no longer
invalidate. **Without the control the record would have shipped with 29 fields and no sign three
were missing.**

### Gates

`check_links` · `check_consistency` · `check_questions` · `verify_doc_addresses` ·
`types_index.py --validate` (0 errors) · `ADDRESS-INDEX.md` regenerated.

## 2026-09-08 — the fourth contract, and a latent write-before-the-bank found while writing it

**Block:** charter §4 over `14-Story-Event-Quest-Hunt`, chosen because the reconstruction-grade
audit named **Interface** (3 of 224 documents) the weakest §3 dimension that is measurable at all,
and this is the only category at **disposition A for its entire owned population**.

| | |
|---|---|
| new contract | [the persistent-flag-bank contract](../14-Story-Event-Quest-Hunt/CONTRACT-persistent-flag-banks.md) — 17 entries, 16 sections |
| new type | **`PersistentFlagPayload`**, `0x1538`, 9 fields (6 named, 3 `UNRESOLVED`) |
| Interface | 3 → **4** of 226 documents |
| GAME types | 5 → **6**; store 184 → 185 types, 754 → 763 fields, **0 errors** |
| rung debt | `14-Story-Event-Quest-Hunt`'s two labelled documents **leave the list** |
| questions | **`DX-1`** filed |

### The finding §10 forced out

A contract's *failure paths and edge conditions* section makes you census every bound test rather
than quote the one you already read. Doing that across all eleven bank accessors:

```
QueryBank2048, QueryBank512Low/High   cmp / jl  PLUS  test ecx,ecx / js    negative REJECTED
SetPrimary, SetBank2048, SetBank512x  cmp / ja  (unsigned)                 negative REJECTED
QueryBank64A/B, SetBank64A/B          cmp / jl or jge, and nothing else    negative ACCEPTED
```

**Seven reject, four do not.** In the two `Bank64` setters `movsxd rcx, edi` sign-extends the
byte offset and `or byte [rax + rcx + 0x1384], bl` **writes before the bank** — `id = -16` lands
on payload `+0x1382`, `id = -1024` on `+0x1304`, both inside save state.

> **Latent, not demonstrated, and recorded as latent.** No caller passing a negative was found;
> the ids in both shipped lists are `u16` and reach the setter zero-extended. The source document
> had already noted the sign-correction idiom and stopped there — **the census is what turned an
> observation into a consequence.** `DX-1`.
>
> It also has a goal-2 consequence worth stating once: **a reimplementation that adds the missing
> guard is more defensive than the original.** That is a parity difference and must be declared,
> not silently fixed.

### The type reports that nine tenths of the payload is unmapped

`PersistentFlagPayload` declares 441 of 5,432 bytes — **8.1 %** — and `types_index.py` reports
three gaps totalling 4,991, which sums back to `0x1538` exactly. **The six banks are what is
understood; they are not what the payload mostly is.**

### A summary line that had already gone stale, fixed

`charter_grade_audit.py` summarised the sub-`RUNTIME VALIDATED` debtors as *“over a category with
no `_types/` entry and no contract”*. **That went stale the moment a category gained a type** —
three rows then owed one rung while the sentence still claimed two. It now prints the unmet sets
and their counts and asserts no cause.
### And the consistency gate caught the contract's own first draft

§15 originally read *“every caller of `002EF2B0` censused (70) plus the raw-buffer route (28
callers, 36 displacements)”*, and `check_consistency` immediately reported a **caller-count
disagreement on `002EF2B0`**: 28 here against 70 in the weather document. Both figures came from
an older census, and the *28* belonged to the other function on the line — the parser attached it
to the nearest address, which is what it is for.

Rather than reword around it, both routes were **re-counted from the binary**: **`002EF2B0` has
121 `E8` call sites and 0 `E9`; `002EF640` has 40 and 0**, controls positive for each instrument.
Neither matches 70 or 28, because those were **census populations, not call-site counts** — a
different unit, which is precisely the *“counts are only comparable to counts of the same kind”*
rule the gate already encodes. The contract now states its own numbers with the instrument named,
and does not restate another document's census figure as a caller count.

### Gates

## 2026-09-08 — goal 2: the fifth reconstruction, and the first test written to settle a prediction

**Block:** charter §18–§20 over the contract written in the previous block. `§16` of that contract
listed `CALCULATION` and `STRUCTURAL` as testable statically; this is that test.

| | |
|---|---:|
| reconstruction | `Reconstruction/Game/Story/flag_banks.{h,c}` — 4 accessors |
| harness | `Tests/Differential/diff_flag_banks.py` |
| ids | 153, of which **67 negative** |
| payloads | 3 — all-zero, all-ones, pseudo-random |
| **comparisons** | **2,754** |
| **mismatches** | **0** |
| reconstructions / harnesses | 4 → **5** / 4 → **5**; parity-certified **still 0** |

### Two firsts

**No stub anywhere.** Every other harness in the tree replaces at least one callee with
`mov eax, imm32 ; ret`. This one maps `SaveImage_GetPersistentPayloadBase` (`002EF2B0`),
`SaveImage_GetActiveBuffer` (`002EF640`) **and** the accessor, all as shipped, and puts its payload
at the address the second returns. **The reference side runs three real functions.**

**It tested a PREDICTION rather than an assertion.** The contract's §10 claimed four of eleven
accessors accept a negative id and worked out by hand where the write lands. Execution confirmed
it exactly — `-16` → payload `+0x1382`, `-1024` → `+0x1304`, `-4096` → `+0x1184` — and over the
test's id set **12 distinct offsets below the bank base**, down to `0x0FE0`.

> ### And it sharpened the prediction the contract had left blunt
>
> `SetBank64A` **accepts 77 of 153 ids including all 67 negatives, and only 22 write anything.**
> `shl bl, cl` on an 8-bit register masks the shift count to five bits, so a bit index outside
> `0..7` yields a zero mask and the `or` is a no-op. Working it through: for a negative id
> `bit = ((id + 7) & 7) - 7`, in range **only when `id` is a multiple of 8**.
>
> **A negative id writes only when it is a multiple of 8.** The contract said where a write lands
> and was silent on how few ids produce one. Both the contract and `DX-1` now carry the
> correction.

### One payload hid half the behaviour

The first run used a single random payload and reported *“no byte changed”* for cases that had
plainly written. **An `or` that sets an already-set bit changes nothing**, and a comparison of
resulting memory cannot see a write that was a no-op. Every case now runs three times.

**39 effective writes per value, identical between the zero and ones passes — and that symmetry is
the check, not a coincidence to wave through.** Each id appears once with each value, so equality
is what a correct harness must produce; it was verified against the accept/mask breakdown rather
than assumed (`SetPrimary` 17 of 153 accepted, 17 effective; `SetBank64A` 77 accepted, 22
effective; 17 + 22 = 39).

### The divergence that was deliberately NOT made

The reconstruction **reproduces the missing guard**. A reimplementation that added it would be
more defensive than the original, which is a parity difference; this tree measures parity rather
than improving on the game, and the non-fix is recorded in `Reconstruction/README.md` under known
intentional divergences so it cannot be mistaken for an oversight.

### An operator note, and a mistake

`vcvars64.bat` under `cmd.exe` from git-bash produced **no output and never returned** across two
attempts; the same command through the PowerShell tool built in seconds. Recorded because the next
session will otherwise lose the same ten minutes.

**And the root `.gitignore` was overwritten by mistake** while adding a rule that turned out to be
already present. It was tracked, so `git checkout --` restored it exactly, and no rule was lost.
Recorded rather than quietly repaired.

`ADDRESS-INDEX.md` regenerated (unchanged at 7,382 addresses).

## 2026-09-08 — the fifth contract, and two questions answered by writing it

**Block:** charter §4 over `06-Movement-And-Navigation`, chosen as the largest single
debt-clearing move available: three labelled documents each owing exactly `SIGNATURE
RESOLVED`, over a category that already had its type.

| | |
|---|---|
| new contract | [the facing-and-steering contract](../06-Movement-And-Navigation/CONTRACT-facing-and-steering.md) — 10 entries, 16 sections |
| Interface | 4 → **5** of 227 documents |
| rung debt | all **three** `06-` documents leave the list; sub-runtime debt **5 → 2** |
| questions | **`ED-2` and `ED-3` ANSWERED**; **`DY-1`** filed |
| claim withdrawn | a modding note in `how-a-character-turns.md` |

### `check_already_answered.py` earned its rule again

Two questions were about to be filed as new. The pre-filing check returned **`ED-2` and
`ED-3`, both already open and both asking exactly what this block had just answered.** They
were closed instead of duplicated. **The non-negotiable says run it before *filing*, not only
before assigning, and this is the second time in the session that has mattered.**

### `ED-2` answered: the flag selects nothing

The two facing variants normalise to **29 instructions each, differing in exactly one** —
`xor r8d, r8d` against `mov r8d, 0x1` — with RIP targets resolved and internal branch targets
ignored. **And `0026B6A0` never touches `r8` in any of its 120 bytes**, by operand analysis
over every instruction rather than by eye.

> **So the two variants are behaviourally identical**, and `ED-2`'s own framing — *“it is the
> entire reason both exist”* — is wrong as well. `how-a-character-turns.md`'s modding note,
> *“hooking one and not the other will produce an asymmetry”*, is **withdrawn**: there is no
> asymmetry to produce. The mechanism it described was right; the consequence it drew was not.

**A byte-level diff would have said the opposite.** Comparing the two bodies byte for byte
gives **71 of 117 differing**, because `xor r8d,r8d` is three bytes and `mov r8d,1` is six, so
everything after shifts and every RIP displacement changes. **That number is an artifact and is
recorded here so it is not mistaken for evidence later.** The instruction-level comparison with
targets resolved is the instrument that answers the question.

### `ED-3` answered: `0026C090` dispatches on the actor kind

It **wraps the heading again** — idempotent, so the double wrap is harmless and the function is
safe to call directly — then branches on `packed_03 >> 5`: **kind 3** writes
`record->target_heading_34`; **kind 1** calls `0026B6A0(a, t, 1)`, which writes context `+0x38`
and `+0x48`; **every other kind does nothing.** The same two-kind dispatch appears in both
functions, which is the shape of the subsystem.

### Two angle normalisers, filed as `DY-1`

The facing path wraps with a truncating `fmod`; `0026C120` calls `003A1C50`, a loop. **Same
three constants** — `01CEBC50` = +π, `00915620` = −π, `01CEBC78` = 2π, all resolved by tool —
**different arithmetic.** The loop is exact; the `fmod` does one pass and inherits `float`
rounding at large magnitudes. Whether they can disagree on a real input is not established, and
§16 names the wrap as the honest next differential pilot for exactly that reason.

## 2026-09-08 — the sixth contract, and three findings that turned out to be already known

**Block:** charter §4 over `01-Script-VM-Native-Bridge`, the seam §29 names first. It owed
**both** remaining rungs and it is the bridge of a script-driven game.

| | |
|---|---|
| new contract | [the script-to-native bridge contract](../01-Script-VM-Native-Bridge/CONTRACT-script-to-native-bridge.md) — 13 entries, 16 sections |
| new types | **`VmValueStack`** `0x284`, **`VmResultEntry`** `0x28` |
| Interface / GAME types | 5 → **6** of 228 / 6 → **8** |
| type store | 185 → 187 types, 763 → 770 fields, **0 errors** |
| rung debt | `01-` leaves the list; sub-runtime debt **2 → 1** |
| questions | **`EF-1` PARTIALLY ANSWERED** |

### Three of four candidate findings were already in the database

`check_already_answered.py` returned all three before anything was filed:

- **`BQ-8`** — `00267DB0` is misnamed `VMValueStack_PopNumericDiscard` and discards nothing.
  Closed 2026-09-02 and filed in `NAME-EQUIVALENCES.tsv` **rather than renamed**, because the
  sanctioned pipeline has no rename script.
- **`AO-2`** — the 63-entry stack shape, already established from the executor side.
- **`EF-1`** — the result tag question itself.

> **The block re-derived all three independently from the binary and said so.** That is
> corroboration and it is worth having; presenting it as discovery would not have been. **This
> is the third time this session the pre-filing check has stopped a duplicate**, and the rule
> that it runs before *filing* rather than before *assigning* is why.

### One sharpening of `AO-2`, from the push side

`AO-2` records *“value words at `+0x84+i*4` and `+0x184+i*4`”*. **Only `+0x184` is a value.**
Both pushes write a literal `0` to `+0x84` and the payload to `+0x184`. The type store records
`+0x84` as `UNRESOLVED` with that evidence rather than as a second value word.

### `EF-1` partially answered, and the trap it exposes

```
STACK   tag at +0x04 + slot      1 = int32     2 = float32
RESULT  tag at entry +0x15       2 = int32     3 = float32
```

**The two spaces share a range and mean different things in it.** `VMResult_WriteFloat32`
(`0026B4C0`) writes the payload at the **same `+0x0C`** the int writer uses and tag `3` at
`+0x15`, so the entry discriminates purely by the tag. Whether tags above 3 exist is still
open — `0026B500` onward is unread, which is the remainder of `EF-1`.

> **For a reimplementation this is the sharpest trap in the subsystem**: one shared enum for
> both records compiles, runs, and silently returns a float where an int was meant.

### And the two pops disagree about an unknown tag

`PopInt32` treats any tag but 1 or 2 as an error and calls `008620C0(1)`. **`PopFloat32` falls
through to returning `0.0f` without calling it.** One branch apart, and only one of them
reports. Recorded in §10 and §14 rather than smoothed over.

## 2026-09-08 — the seventh contract, and the sub-runtime rung-debt list empties

**Block:** charter §4 over `05-Spawn-Encounter-Lifecycle`, the **last** document owing a rung
below `RUNTIME VALIDATED`. It owed both, and both are paid.

| | |
|---|---|
| new contract | [the group-completion contract](../05-Spawn-Encounter-Lifecycle/CONTRACT-group-completion-and-respawn.md) — 9 entries, 16 sections |
| new types | **`SpawnRecord`** `0x250`, **`SpawnGroupLedger`** `0x18` |
| Interface / GAME types | 6 → **7** of 229 / 8 → **10** |
| type store | 187 → 189 types, 770 → 776 fields, **0 errors** |
| rung debt | **sub-runtime debt 1 → 0** |
| questions | **`EE-1` SHARPENED** |

### The milestone, stated with its denominator

The reconstruction-grade audit opened this thread with **10 of 15 labelled documents carrying
rung debt in two shapes**. **The shape that represented undone desk work is now empty.** Every
labelled document owes exactly one rung and it is the same one: `RUNTIME VALIDATED`, blocked on
`EXP-001`.

> **It is a narrow milestone and the page says so.** **15 of 229 documents carry a readiness
> label at all** (`DJ-1`). This says the labelled subset is consistent with the ladder; it does
> not say the database is finished, and the ladder still cannot express *“everything except
> runtime”*, which is what seven documents now are.

### `EE-1` sharpened: the question is real and this instrument cannot answer it

`EE-1` asked whether the respawn cooldown at spawn-record `+0x10` is in seconds. **Four
instruments over each of the three record accessors, controls positive for each:**

```
00235F50 GetDeathCount              E8 1  E9 0  operand 0   -> 0050F660  VM verb
00235FB0 elapsed SECONDS            E8 1  E9 0  operand 0   -> 0050FAB0  VM verb
002366E0 GetRespawnCooldownTicks    E8 1  E9 0  operand 0   -> 005101F0  VM verb
```

**No native function reads more than one of them**, so nothing native relates the cooldown to
the elapsed time. **The unit is a script-side convention**, and only the authored script or a
runtime observation can settle it. That moves `EE-1` from *not yet checked* to **not answerable
by a static instrument, and here is the one that could** — which is a more useful state for a
question to be in.

### What the game does, for the record

**Killing a group is a checklist, not a counter.** `(memberMask & deadMask) == memberMask` over
64 groups × 64-bit masks. Order does not matter, overkill does not count, and **a group whose
`memberMask` is zero completes on the first death** — which matters because the ledger is BSS
and starts at zero, so whatever writes `memberMask` must run first. That writer is still
unidentified: `EE-2`, and §13 names the one read that would settle it.

**A respawn wait is the same wall-clock length at either frame rate**, because the elapsed
reader divides by `(int)(scale × 30.0f)` — 30 or 60. Both constants resolved by tool.

### An unreachable check, kept in the contract rather than tidied away

The prologue nine accessors share runs `movzx eax, dl` then `test eax, eax / js`. **A byte
zero-extended into a 32-bit register is never negative**, so that arm cannot execute — in all
nine. The contract records it and tells a reimplementation which of the two sign checks is real.

## 2026-09-08 — Behaviour becomes askable, and the fix was to stop looking for a new record type

**Block:** charter §7, closing the gap the reconstruction-grade audit named as the one §3
dimension that could not be asked at all.

| | |
|---|---|
| new tables | `contract_sections` **115 rows**, `contract_claims` **63** |
| new queries | `behaviour`, `contract-claims`, `unresolved-claims` |
| §7 supported queries | 23 → **26** |
| §3 dimensions askable | 6 of 7 → **7 of 7** |

### The gap was an index, not a record type

The audit's wording was *“the schema has nowhere to put preconditions, postconditions,
invariants, state transitions or failure paths outside contract prose”*. **The escape was in
the sentence.** The seven contracts share an **exact 16-section skeleton** — every numbered
heading from 2 to 16 appears in all seven — and §§4, 5, 7, 10 and 12 are precisely those five
things. The structure was already there; only the index was missing.

> **Three contracts could not have supported this. Seven can.** The same block written a week
> ago would have produced a parser fitted to three documents and called it a schema.

### Columns mapped by header, which mattered immediately

Six contracts write `| claim | evidence | tier | confidence |`. **`CONTRACT-widget-object.md`
writes three columns and has no confidence at all.** Reading column four positionally would
have **invented a confidence for six documents and lost it for one** — a silent corruption of
exactly the field the charter's Validation dimension depends on. The parser reads the header.

### What the first run found

**63 claims: 44 `PROVEN`, 11 `UNKNOWN`, 2 `VERY HIGH`, 6 with no confidence column.**

> **Five of the eleven unknowns are the same claim** — *“any runtime observation — none
> exists”* — written independently by five different contracts. **That is `EXP-001` measured
> from a direction the readiness ladder cannot see.** The ladder says seven documents stand
> above a rung nothing has reached; the contracts' own evidence tables say the same absence in
> their own words, five times. **Two independent instruments, one blocked experiment.**

And it surfaces thin sections without anyone reading for them: **`CONTRACT-field-music-selection.md` §7 is 29 characters.** Whether *“no state transitions”* is correct or merely
unwritten is now a visible question.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**The dimension is askable, not covered** — 7 of 229 documents, and the audit page now says so
in the same row that reports the closure. **`chars` measures presence and size, not quality**;
a long failure-paths section is not thereby a good one. And **no keyword proxy was invented at
any point**: the index reads structure the documents already have, never words they happen to
contain, which is the distinction `DR-1` was filed for.

## 2026-09-08 — a differential test that measures the game rather than the reimplementation

**Block:** charter §18–§20 over the pilot the facing-and-steering contract's §16 named as
*“the honest pilot”*, chosen because `DY-1` was a question a float sweep could answer outright.

| | |
|---|---:|
| reconstruction | `Reconstruction/Game/Math/angle_wrap.{h,c}` — both forms |
| harness | [`diff_angle_wrap.py`](../../../Reconstruction/Tests/Differential/diff_angle_wrap.py) |
| inputs | **4,140** distinct float bit patterns |
| **comparisons vs the shipped bytes** | **8,280** |
| **mismatches** | **0** |
| reconstructions / harnesses | 5 → **6** / 5 → **6**; parity-certified **still 0** |
| questions | **`DY-1` ANSWERED** |

### `DY-1`: yes, on 88.8 % of the sweep

```
in   -0.0        loop  -0.0          fmod  +0.0        the sign of zero
in    1.0        loop   1.0          fmod   1.0000002  ALREADY IN RANGE, still perturbed
in   +pi         loop  +pi           fmod  -pi         opposite sign at the boundary
in    2pi        loop   0.0          fmod  -2.384e-07
```

**The `fmod` form is not the identity on its own output range.** It adds `±pi`, takes a
truncating `fmod` through a 32-bit int, and subtracts `±pi` again; the round trip costs a
couple of ulp even when the input needed no wrapping. The loop form leaves an in-range value
exactly alone, because both `while` conditions are simply false.

> **These are two different functions and the call site decides which.** Substituting one for
> the other changes the stored heading on almost nine inputs in ten — which is exactly the
> kind of thing a reimplementation does by accident when a helper looks generic.

### The loop form does not always terminate

Once `ulp(x) > 2 × 2pi` — `|x| >= 2**27`, about `1.34e8` — adding `2pi` is absorbed and the
loop cannot progress. **6 of 4,140 inputs are in that state, verified by evaluating
`x + 2pi == x` in float32 rather than inferred from a timeout**, and they include both
infinities. A NaN is safe: `comiss` is unordered, both `jbe`s are taken, and it falls through.

### The harness was wrong and the reconstruction was right

The first version ran the emulator with a flat **2,000,000-instruction cap** and reported every
unfinished run as non-terminating. **It was wrong on `1e7` and `-1e7`** — about 1.6 million
iterations, roughly 6 million instructions: slow, not infinite. The driver said so and the
reference contradicted it.

> **A cap is not a proof of non-termination**, and treating it as one would have published a
> false hazard threshold two orders of magnitude too low. The harness now makes a **per-input
> prognosis** — *absorbed* (verified), *too slow to emulate* (counted and named), or *runs*
> (with a cap sized from that input's own estimate) — and reports the three separately rather
> than summing them.

### No stub on either side

`003A1C50` is pure. `0026C090` runs with a real actor, movement context and steering record in
emulated memory, kind byte set to 3, and the harness reads the wrapped heading back **out of
`record->target_heading_34`** — a real store through the real kind dispatch, not a value lifted
from a register.
### And `build.bat` had been broken since 2026-09-08, committed that way

Adding the sixth driver revealed that the fifth's line was already corrupt:
`..\..\Game\Story\flag_banks.c` had been committed as
`..\..\Game\Story<FF>lag_banks.c`. **A shell heredoc consumed the backslash as a formfeed**, and
the same thing happened again to the new `angle_wrap` line, and a third time to the script
written to repair them.

> **It went unnoticed because the flag-banks driver was built by hand through PowerShell when
> `cmd` would not run `vcvars64`, so the build script itself was never exercised.** A green
> differential test says nothing about the script that is supposed to produce it.
>
> Both paths are repaired — through a **file**, not a heredoc — and `build.bat` was then **run
> end to end**: *built all six differential drivers*. **Verified by running it, not by reading
> it.**

### Gates

`check_links` · `check_consistency` · `check_questions` · `verify_doc_addresses` ·
`ADDRESS-INDEX.md` regenerated.

## 2026-09-08 — reading `DT-1`'s largest entry found a central update gate above it

**Block:** charter §29 high-leverage knowledge, taking the head of `DT-1` — the 112 functions
the residual worklist names that **no document has ever cited**, and which an earlier block
showed will not shrink on their own.

| | |
|---|---|
| new document | [one word decides which fifteen subsystems tick](../00-Engine-Core-Runtime/Per-Frame-Update-Gate/one-word-decides-which-fifteen-subsystems-tick.md) |
| read | `0028BB50` (2,387 B), `0028C4C0` (42 B), `0028E290`'s fan-out |
| new to the database | `01E0C464`, `0028E290`, `002507C0`, `0028C4C0`, `0028BB50` |
| questions | **`DZ-1`**, **`DZ-2`** filed |
| `DT-1` | 112 → **111** |

### The finding is above the function, not in it

`0028BB50` is 2,387 bytes of angle arithmetic. Walking up its one caller twice reached
`0028E290`, and that function is **sixteen `test byte [01E0C464], imm` sites against one
global**, each gating one group of per-frame updates.

> **One 16-bit word decides which fifteen subsystems tick.** Never a different global, never a
> computed index, and **a clear bit stops a whole group outright** — there is no degraded mode
> in this fan-out. Six of the fifteen groups are `UI`-owned; the actor, battle and script
> systems are not in the list at all.

**Bit `0x0010` is absent.** Fourteen consecutive bits are used from `0x0001` to `0x8000` and
that one appears nowhere. Recorded as an observation, not explained.

### What was deliberately not named

The node type. The arithmetic is inviting — degrees to radians by **two units a thousand apart**
(`pi/180` and `pi/180000`), `±pi/2` clamps, `atan2f` twice, and the `FrameLimit` time base — and
the list is walked under a `UI` bit. **Consistent with a minimap, a compass, a reticle or a
3D-positioned UI element, and consistent-with is not evidence.**

> **The size refuses the best guess.** `Phyre::PCameraPerspective` is recovered at `0xBB8`
> (`BE-6`); a node here is **at least `0xD78`**, because the list link sits at `+0xD70`. The
> camera reading is not merely unproven, it is **excluded**. `DZ-1`.

### And a modding hazard worth stating

`0028C4C0` walks `n = n->next_D70` until null, with **no cycle guard**. A list made circular by
a mod hangs the frame.

## 2026-09-08 — two questions given a method, neither given an answer

A `FrameLimit=30` / `=60` table said *never written* in its 30 fps cells while the same document

inside `001EDDC0`, the *apply frame limit* function — **the 60 fps arm**.

**And the first repair was not one.** Rewriting the cells to *“not written on this path”*
swapped one absence phrasing for another and the next run flagged the same line. The cells now

**Block:** finishing the sweep the previous block named. Both remaining gates were read.

It flagged `how-a-sound-request-becomes-a-voice.md` for

covering `+0x14`–`+0x1B`, with the next write a dword at `+0x1C`.

> The gate's own docstring already said deliberately overlapping views are legitimate; **it
> just could not see one being declared.** It now honours a `(covers +0xA and +0xB)`
> annotation, and **its self-test still fires on the deliberately broken block** — a clean run
> from a broken parser is worthless, which that gate says on every run.

`section-016.md` (*the POSENT position-entry table*) linked `section-012.md` and labelled it

> is left unresolved rather than reassigned** — the corpus cannot settle it, and moving a tag

| gate | kind | state |
|---|---|---|
| `check_links` | correctness | **green** — 11,4xx relative links resolve |
| `check_consistency` | correctness | **green** — no address described two ways |
| `check_questions` | correctness | **green** — table and checklists agree |

## 2026-09-08 — the block that set out to rediscover something, and found one address wrong

**Block:** `DT-1`, taking the second-largest function no document had ever cited — `00565E00`,
1,914 bytes. `DT-1`: 111 → **110**.

### Reached by no call at all

| instrument | result | control |
|---|---:|---|
| `E8 call` | **0** | `001DE4F0` → 1 |
| `E9 jmp` | **0** | `001D1660` → 1 |
| code memory-operand | **1** | `02ADD0A8` → 3 |
| raw data-section qword | **0** | `005C5230` → **2,527 slots** |

Its only reference is a `lea` inside a 38-byte registrar that hands it to the widget factory as
a **512-byte** construction. **A call-only query would have called it unreachable and a vtable
scan would have agreed.**

### The first draft was a rediscovery and was deleted

The registrar calls `00244F50`, which the draft re-derived in full and presented as *“an
undocumented 247-call-site pool allocator that no document in this database had cited”*.

> **`check_already_answered.py` returned three documents and a type-store row.** The
> unowned-code census §6 has it *read in full* — 112 records, stride `0x120`, both free-slot
> conditions, the heap fall-through — and `_types/types.tsv` records it as `Widget`'s allocation
> site with `002465F0` as constructor and the note that **the size is an argument, 26 distinct
> values across 49 construction sites**. The draft's open question *“is this argument a size or
> a type id?”* was answered before it was asked.
>
> **The draft was deleted rather than trimmed**, and the document that replaced it cites the
> factory instead of explaining it. **Fourth time this session the pre-filing check has stopped
> a duplicate**, and the first time it stopped a whole block.

### The re-derivation was not wasted

The census records the table pointer as **`0x02093958`**. It is **`0x0208EA58`**:

```
00244F7F   48 8b 1d d2 9a e4 01     mov rbx, qword ptr [rip + 0x1E49AD2]
           next instruction 0x00244F86  +  0x1E49AD2  =  0x0208EA58
```

**`0x02093958` appears nowhere in the function's 175 bytes** — every RIP-relative operand was
re-resolved with a tool and there is exactly one. The difference is `0x4F00`, not a
transposition. **Everything else in that section reproduces exactly**, and the correction is
written there, not only in the new document.

> **That is the case for re-deriving a documented reading rather than citing it blind** — and
> equally the case for the pre-filing check. Between them a wasted block became a one-address
> correction plus a function nobody had read.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**What the widget is.** 1,914 bytes, four message arms, and **only the kind-1 arm read** — the
one that writes `0x0209AC30->+0x168`, the field its own registrar tests, closing a one-shot
latch. The name would come from the other three arms or from a string; **the call graph has
nothing to offer here**, which is the point. `EJ-1`.

## 2026-09-08 — the query chose the function, and the function chose the unit

**Block:** charter §29 *high-connectivity callgraph nodes*. The target was picked by a query
rather than by judgement — *the highest-connectivity callee with a real body that no document
cites* — which returned `00246AD0`: **321 bytes, 148 call sites** (142 `E8` + 6 `E9`, controls
positive for both).

### Milliseconds become frames, at a hard-coded sixty

```asm
00246BDF  imul ecx, eax, 0x3C                   ; x 60
00246BE2  mov  eax, 0x10624DD3 ; mul ecx ; shr edx, 6    ; / 1000
00246BEC  mov  [rbx+0x70], edx                  ; the duration IN FRAMES
```

`0x10624DD3` with a 32×32→64 multiply and `shr edx, 6` is the compiler's unsigned divide by
1000, so the stored value is `(ms * 60) / 1000`. **The 60 is an immediate and there is no
frame-rate variable anywhere in the function** — an authored millisecond becomes a frame count
at a fixed sixty, once, when the motion starts.

### It corroborates a reading another document deliberately declined to assert

[The blinking icon](../99-Unresolved-Residual/the-blinking-icon-and-its-atlas.md) uses
`0208F570` in `sinf(DAT_0208F570 * pi / 30)` and says plainly: *“that it counts frames is the
reading, not a measurement.”*

> **Here it is a start timestamp** — stored to `+0x74` when a motion begins, and reflected as
> `2*now - span - start` on the state-4 arm — **immediately beside a duration this same function
> computes in frames.** A value stamped as *now* next to a frame count, reflected about the
> present, is a frame counter being used as one. **Two unrelated functions, one reading.**
> Recorded as `PROBABLE` corroboration, not promoted to proven, and the other document's caution
> stands unchanged.

### And it constrains `DL-1` from a new direction

The widget message protocol records id **14** — **48 handlers, 22.7 %** — as *“teardown-ish”*,
and `DL-1` lists it among the **23 of 32 ids** whose meaning is unrecovered.

> **Here id 14 is the last thing a START does**, dispatched after the rate is reset, the
> duration converted and the state nibble set to `2`. **That is the opposite end of a lifetime
> from teardown.** It does not name the id — **one sender is not a census** — but it is a
> constraint, and it points the other way.

### Smaller things worth having

**The object arrives in `rdx`, not `rcx`**, and is null-checked in the first instruction — a hook
written for the usual convention reads the wrong register. The state is **a signed four-bit
field** (`shl 28 / sar 28`) with arms for only `0`, `1` and `4`. The duration has an **inline
override**: bit 10 of `+0x7C` redirects it to bits 12–21 of the same dword and **clears itself**,
so the override fires once.

### Not claimed

**What “mode 2” is.** The rate is `1.0f` unless `00229DF0()` is non-zero *and* `00229EA0()`
returns exactly 2, in which case it becomes `1.0f / 00229E70()`. All three are unread; the shape
is proven and the meaning is not. `EK-1`.

### Gates

`check_links` · `check_consistency` · `check_questions` · `check_denominators` ·
`verify_doc_addresses` · `ADDRESS-INDEX.md` regenerated.

## 2026-09-08 — the query that hunts undocumented functions was blind to how they are spelled

**Block:** charter §29 again, by query — *the highest-connectivity callee with a real body that
no document cites*. It returned **`002F9860`**: 180 bytes, **160 callers**, apparently untouched.

### It had been read line by line

[The VBF / st2e tables document](../02-Resource-And-Asset-Pipeline/VBF-Archive-And-Authored-Tables/vbf-archive-and-st2e-tables.md)
§9 quotes ten of its instructions, names both group tables at `0x02EC3D80` / `0x02F973C0`,
derives the `0x10624DD3` reciprocal divide, states the 28-group bound, and builds `AY-10` on the
result. **A fresh read of the function reproduced that document exactly** — including the part
an isolated reading would get wrong: the high pool's domain is `100,000–379,999`, not
`0–279,999`, because the **caller** subtracts 100,000 before dividing by 10,000.

> **The document is right and was invisible.** It spells the function `FUN_002F9860`, and the
> extractor anchors a backtick on each side of the eight digits — so the address, sitting inside
> a token, matched nothing. **`FUN_<addr>` is the GFZ ledger's spelling for every UNNAMED
> function**, which makes the missing form the form used for exactly the population a
> *“what is undocumented?”* query searches. **The blind spot was aligned with the search space.**

### Four extractors, four different rules, no one had compared them

| tool | what it saw before |
|---|---|
| `knowledge_db.py` | backtick only |
| `gen_address_index.py` | backtick for `.md`, bare for `.tsv` |
| `program_coverage.py` | bare with word boundaries — so **not** `FUN_002f9860` |
| `check_located_not_read.py` | backtick + bare-inside-a-fence, since 2026-09-03 |

All four now count the same three forms — **backtick, `FUN_` symbol, bare inside a fence** — and
all four strip long hex runs first, because a sha256 opens with eight hex digits and **every**
document states the exe hash. [citation forms](CITATION-FORMS.md).

### What moved, and what deliberately did not

| instrument | before | after | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `knowledge_db.py` distinct function entries cited | 7,420 | **7,780** | **+360** |
| `ADDRESS-INDEX.md` addresses cited by a document | 7,421 | **7,783** | **+362** |
| authored functions cited | 5,969 | **6,186** | **+217** |
| `script-verbs-undocumented` | 1,158 / 1,224 | 1,153 / 1,224 | −5 |
| `check_located_not_read` | 55, 14 vendor | 55, 14 vendor | **0** |
| `check_named_not_cited` | 414 / 96 docs | 414 / 96 docs | **0** |
| GM160 residual worklist, uncited members | 106 / 160 | 106 / 160 | **0** |

> **The published figure moved for two different reasons and they are kept apart.** The file on
> disk said 5,922; a fresh run of the **unfixed** tool gives 5,969; the fixed tool gives 6,186.
> **+47 was staleness, +217 was the defect.** Reporting 264 as one number would have hidden
> which was which.
>
> **And `DT-1` did not move.** Not one of the 160 GM160 residuals was hidden by the blind spot,
> so that backlog is a real frontier and not an artefact of a broken instrument. A correction
> that fails to move a suspicious number is worth as much as one that moves it.

### The form that is still not counted, and the number that justifies it

A bare address in an ordinary sentence is **not** counted, because it cannot be told from a
constant of the same width. That is measured rather than asserted: the form contributes **12
function entries no other form reaches**, and **two of the twelve are values** —
`+0x118 = 0x003C0000`, an actor-record field default landing inside `FUN_003bfff0`, and
`0x00555556`, the compiler's divide-by-3 reciprocal, landing inside `00555400`.

**Ten of the twelve are genuine**, so the rows are kept and the form is excluded:
`knowledge_db.py` now exposes `citations` with a `form` column and a `cited` view that drops
`prose`. **`form = 'backtick'` reproduces the pre-correction number exactly**, which is what
makes the correction auditable rather than a silent widening.

### The instrument that was right

**`check_already_answered.py` found the document immediately**, because it does a literal
case-insensitive substring search and never tries to parse. It is the tool the non-negotiables
require before *filing* a question — **second block in a week where it stopped a rediscovery**,
and the first where it exposed a defect in the tool that chose the block.

> **Third time this project has found an instrument that could not see evidence in the form the
> evidence is usually written in.** `check_located_not_read.py`'s own docstring already says it
> about fenced listings. **The pattern is the finding:** when a query returns a suspiciously
> clean answer about what the database does *not* have, suspect the extractor before believing
> the gap.

### Not claimed

**That the three counted forms are exhaustive.** A document can name a function and cite no
address at all — a different gate, `check_named_not_cited`, **414 mentions across 96
documents**. And citation still does not mean understanding; this block made the weakest signal
in the coverage report *correct*, not stronger. `EL-1` records the survivors of the corrected
query.

## 2026-09-08 — six green harnesses, zero certified, and now a reason instead of a silence

**Block:** charter §38's last-but-one undone first action — *define the reconstruction
architecture and parity framework*. It outranks another prose document by the skill's own
ordering, and it had been open while fourteen blocks did §29 knowledge.

### The suite was re-run, not quoted

| harness | cases | comparisons | mismatches |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `angle_wrap` | 4,140 | **8,280** | 0 |
| `flag_banks` | 918 | **2,754** | 0 |
| `quality_preset` | 600 | — | 0 |
| `field_music` | 396 | — | 0 |
| `widget_construct` | 320 | — | 0 |
| `name_registry` | 154 | — | 0 |

> **`field_music` runs 396 cases over 12 tables by default**, where the README's table quotes
> **1,200 over 20** — the documented figure comes from an invocation with explicit flags. Both
> are true and the page now says which is which. *“Re-run suites; never quote a count from a
> document”* is a project rule and this is why.

### The gate

```text
PARITY CERTIFIED  requires  every APPLICABLE dimension COVERED
                  and       every N/A carrying a stated reason
                  and       INTEGRATION covered AGAINST THE RUNNING GAME
```

**The third clause is the whole cost.** Charter §19 opens *“the original **running** game is
the reference behaviour”*, and Unicorn executes the same static artifact the reconstruction was
derived from. A differential test proves the arithmetic; **it cannot prove the function is
called when we think, with the inputs we assume, in the state we assume** — and those are the
assumptions that break a reimplementation.

### What the scoring found

**Two dimensions are `NOT COVERED` by every pilot without exception — `INTEGRATION` and
`FULL-SUBSYSTEM`.** Every other dimension is covered somewhere or genuinely `n/a`. **0 of 6
certified, for a short stated reason rather than a scattering of gaps.**

> **Three of the eleven dimensions had never been scored at all.** `CONTRACT` and
> `FULL-SUBSYSTEM` were absent from the tree's old table, and **an omitted dimension does not
> score zero — it reads as covered.** Scoring them found that **`name_registry` has no
> behavioural contract**, and that no pilot covers a whole subsystem: each reimplements between
> one and four entry points of a subsystem whose entry points have never been enumerated.

**And one existing claim did not survive its own criterion.** `field_music` was listed
`STRUCTURAL: covered`; it returns a value and writes no memory, so the dimension is `n/a`.
**Reading a structure correctly is `CALCULATION`.** The reclassification is recorded in the
README rather than quietly applied.

### Two defects in the reporter, both caught by its own output

**It printed `cases` under the label `comparisons`.** `flag_banks` runs 918 cases against three
payloads for **2,754** comparisons and `angle_wrap` 4,140 bit patterns through two forms for
**8,280**; taking whichever pattern matched first published the smaller number under the larger
one's name. **A wrong denominator** — the error class this project exists to stop making. Both
are now collected and printed and neither stands in for the other.

**And it called a dimension universally unmet when it was merely never asked.** `SERIALIZATION`
scores 0 covered / 1 not covered / **5 `n/a`**, and the first version reported it as failing for
every pilot without exception. **`N/A` is not a failure**; universal now means
`not_covered == pilots`, which leaves exactly `INTEGRATION` and `FULL-SUBSYSTEM`.

### What is deliberately not claimed

**That a `COVERED` declaration is a measurement.** It is the harness author's claim that the
criterion is met, and nothing checks it; the tool's measured column says only that the harness
still runs and still reports zero mismatches, and the page says so. **A harness whose output
cannot be parsed is reported `UNPARSED`, never as zero** — a reporter that silently matches
nothing produces a page of confident zeroes, which is exactly what a citation extractor did
here earlier the same day. `EM-1` filed for contract-claim mapping.

## 2026-09-08 — completing a family of eleven, and what the seventh member said about the first

**Block:** the parity status page named `flag_banks` as the pilot closest to the gate. Its
`FULL-SUBSYSTEM` gap was structural — **4 of the contract's 11 bank accessors reimplemented** —
so the block completed the family.

### Eleven of eleven

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| bank accessors | 4 | **11** (5 queries, 6 setters) |
| cases | 918 | **2,601** |
| comparisons | 2,754 | **7,803** |
| mismatches | 0 | **0** |

**Every bound test was re-read from the shipped bytes**, not copied from §10's table — and the
table reproduced exactly: `QueryBank64B` `cmp ecx,0x40 / jl` with no `js` in its 93 bytes;
`SetBank2048` a single unsigned `cmp ecx,0x7FF / ja`; `SetBank512Low/High` unsigned against
`0xFF`; both `Bank512High` accessors carrying their own `lea eax,[rcx+0x100]`.

> **One idiom difference worth keeping:** `QueryBank2048` spends **two** tests rejecting
> negatives (`jl` plus an explicit `js`) where `SetBank2048` spends **one** (an unsigned `ja`).
> Same bank, same bound, two spellings — which is why the four `Bank64` accessors' missing
> guard is a *shape* to check per accessor and not a property of the bank.

### And then the seventh member disproved a line about the first

§10 says a negative id writes *“into the unmapped payload stretch between `+0x1164` and
`+0x1384`”*. **That is `SetBank64A`'s landing zone generalised to a pair** — and `Bank64B`'s
base is eight bytes higher, so some of its negative writes must land in `Bank64A`.

**Measured rather than argued:** every id in `-1024..-1` executed under emulation against a
zero payload, the changed byte read back.

```
SetBank64A   128 of 1024 negative ids write   +0x1383 down to +0x1304   none in a named bank
SetBank64B   128 of 1024 negative ids write   +0x138B down to +0x130C   EIGHT inside Bank64A

  SetBank64B(-64) -> Bank64A flag 0      SetBank64B(-32) -> Bank64A flag 32
  SetBank64B(-56) -> Bank64A flag 8      SetBank64B(-24) -> Bank64A flag 40
  SetBank64B(-48) -> Bank64A flag 16     SetBank64B(-16) -> Bank64A flag 48
  SetBank64B(-40) -> Bank64A flag 24     SetBank64B(-8)  -> Bank64A flag 56
```

> **128 of 1,024 — exactly the multiples of 8** — confirms the earlier mask finding with a
> denominator instead of a worked example. **The two accessors are not equivalent hazards:**
> one writes into payload nobody has claimed, the other can flip a flag another accessor reads.
>
> **It could not have been found without running the second member of the pair.** That is the
> argument for completing a family rather than sampling it, and it is the second time in three
> blocks that extending an instrument's reach corrected something already written down.

`DX-1` is unchanged: **nothing here shows an authored path can produce a negative id.** The
hazard is a property of the accessor, not a demonstrated bug.

### The criterion was not bent to fit the work

**`FULL-SUBSYSTEM` is still `NOT COVERED`** — the standard written one block earlier asks for
**every entry point of the subsystem**, and the bank accessors are a family inside it. The
verdict now carries its denominator: **11 of the 17 entry points the contract enumerates**, the
six outstanding named individually (the authored gate — partially reconstructed, its schedule
arm needs authored data — the threshold schedule, the new-game list, the reset, the
event-memory predicate, and the payload-base helper, which the reference side executes as
shipped rather than reimplementing).

> **Meeting a criterion one block after writing it would have been the wrong kind of progress.**

## 2026-09-08 — “nothing restores it” was a property of most users, stated as a property of the area

**Block:** `EL-1`'s largest survivor — `0026EE00`, **1,560 bytes, 104 callers**, uncited by any
document under the corrected citation instrument.

### The correction

[The shared transform workbench](../00-Engine-Core-Runtime/Shared-Transform-Workbench/the-shared-transform-workbench.md)
§6 — a document with a falsification pass already recorded — tells a modder:
*“Anything you write there is visible to the next user and **nothing restores it**.”*

> **`0036D930` and `0036D8E0` are an explicit save/restore pair.** `Save` is variadic over the
> register home area: for each of `count` pointers it stores the pointer at `02EC0A00[i]` and
> the 16 bytes it points at into `02EC0800[i]`, then writes `count` to **`022D8F08` — inside
> the workbench itself**. `Restore` walks the same arrays, writes each value back through its
> pointer, and zeroes the count.

**Nine functions call `Save` and the same nine call `Restore`** — no function saves without
restoring, none restores without saving. **9 of the 249 that write the area, 3.6 %.**

| instrument | `Save` | `Restore` | control |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `E8 call` | **9** | **5** | `001DE4F0` → 1 |
| `E9 jmp` | 0 | **4** | `001D1660` → 1 |

> **Four of the nine restores are tail-jumps** — `0026F413`, `003AFFAB`, `00431F0A`,
> `0046242E`. **An `E8`-only scan finds five of nine and reports a leak that is not there.**
> The four-instrument rule is usually invoked for *“is this reachable”*; here it decided a
> question that looked like bookkeeping.

**Only two rows are ever protected:** `022D8F30` (5 callers) and `022D8F90` (3), with
`0042FDB0` saving both. Decoded from the argument setup at all nine `Save` sites, RIP
displacements resolved with a tool.

**The conclusion of §6's advice survives and its reason did not.** 240 of the 249 writers
restore nothing, so *“assume the area is clobbered”* is still right — but the corrected text
says why, and names the two rows where it is false.

### Emulation as a research tool, not a test oracle

`0026EE00` is 1,560 bytes of unrolled byte-scatter and packed 16-bit multiplies: a readable
shape with no readable meaning. **Charter §18 — implementation is also a research tool** — so
the shipped bytes were executed under emulation with controlled inputs, both callees mapped and
running as shipped.

```
out_byte[i]  =  min(255,  2 x ((row[i] x arg_byte[i]) mod 256))       for i = 0, 2, 3
```

**168 combinations, 0 disagreements** — 3 byte positions x 8 row values x 7 argument values.

> **The two narrowing steps behave differently, and one input proves it.** `row = 127, arg = 3`
> returns `0xFA`: the inner product `381` is **truncated** to `125`, and the outer doubling
> `250` needed no saturation. A model that saturated at both stages predicts `0xFF` and is
> wrong on that one input — which is why the grid was run rather than the rule assumed.

**And the restore was verified by execution, not only by reading the pair.** A 16-byte marker
at `022D8F30` survives the call intact and the depth counter returns to zero.

### The memory calling convention, caught in the act

Of every RIP-relative global `0026EE00` touches, **exactly one is read and never written:
`022D8F10`, 16 bytes wide, once.** Every other workbench address it reads, it wrote first.

> **A fourth argument arriving through memory.** A reader tracing arguments through registers
> sees three pointers and would call the function pure in its inputs. It is not.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**Ownership.** 102 of the 104 callers are owned by Presentation and **a caller is not evidence
of ownership** — the document says `owner_layer: none` and is filed with the workbench it
corrects, not with the layer that calls it.

**What the computation is for.** The mapping is measured; the purpose is not established.
**How the two integer arguments combine** is `EN-1`: each alone fits the rule exactly and
together **6 of 80 combinations deviate**, by `+1`, `+2` and once `+12`. **`row[1] >= 0x80`
forces all four output bytes to `0xFF` with both arguments zero**, while `row[3] = 0x80` obeys
the positional rule — so it is that byte specifically and not a lane's sign bit, and what it
selects is unknown.
