## 2026-09-08 — the first autonomous runtime experiment, and the false falsification it nearly published

**Block:** an instructed extension of the operating model — the running game becomes an
experimental evidence source the project drives itself, with manual gameplay as the fallback.
**Every existing standard stays binding**; automation raises the cost of sloppiness rather than
lowering the bar.

### Capability audit first, building second

Already present: `runtime_probe.py` (attach, base control at `ImageBase`, read control on
`LUAC_TAIL`, typed dump from `_types/`, declarative `--check` lists), the Cheat Engine and
Ghidra-debugger MCP servers, `Reset-LiveLogs.ps1`, and charter §15's experiment record format.

> **The gap was never *how do we read the game* — it was *how do we get a trustworthy one
> running*.** `EXP-001` had been designed and left unrun for exactly that reason.

`ffxii_runtime.py` fills it: `env` / `status` / `launch` / `close` / `run`, driving
`runtime_probe.py` for every read rather than reimplementing it — **one definition of the
controls, not two.**

### A matching hash is not a clean environment

| install | build | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `D:\SteamLibrary\…\FINAL FANTASY XII THE ZODIAC AGE\x64` | authority match | **CLEAN** — loaders renamed `.modbak`, no `modules\`, no `hook.ini` |
| `FFXII_TestClient1\x64` | authority match | rejected — 4 loaders, 11-file `modules\`, `hook.ini` |
| `FFXII_TestClient2\x64` | authority match | rejected — 4 loaders, 10-file `modules\`, `hook.ini` |
| `FFXII_TestClient3\x64` | authority match | rejected — `xinput1_3.dll`, 1-file `modules\` |

**All four hash to the authority SHA-256 and three are invalid references**, because
`XIIOnlineNet.dll` writes engine state — which `EXP-001`'s own control variables forbid. The
live module list is re-checked after launch, since a file absent from disk can still be
injected. The operator independently confirmed the Steam copy is the unmodded one; the
structural check had already nominated it.

### The run

Launch → wait for the harness's own controls → wait for the singleton → settle → observe →
capture → close. **No human touched the game.**

**Both controls passed live.** The module loaded at `0x00120000`, matching the PE `ImageBase` —
so **a database VA is a runtime address, verified rather than assumed** for the first time in
this project. `LUAC_TAIL` read back exactly.

**The `FrameLimit` biconditional holds.** At 30 s: `setting[18] == 1`, `0x01DFE0B4 == 2`,
`0x01DFE0B8 == 2.0`, `0x01DFE0BC == 0.5`, `0x01F82E38 == 1` — every element of the contract's
predicted `FrameLimit=60` column, present simultaneously.

### The result that matters most is the one that was nearly wrong

> **Run 1 observed at the first instant the controls passed and the singleton was non-null.**
> `E1` was already `1` while `E2`/`E3`/`E4`/`E5` still read `1` / `1.0` / `1.0` / `0` — the
> *other* column. **Taken alone that is a live falsification of a claim the contract labels
> `PROVEN`**, and it would have been published as one.
>
> It was a timing artefact. **“The object exists” is not “the writer has run.”** `--settle` and
> `--repeat` were added, and the answer changed the moment the question was asked properly.
> **A single observation cannot distinguish “the claim is wrong” from “we looked too early”**,
> and the very first autonomous experiment this project ran proved it the hard way.

**The artefact is itself a finding.** There is a real window in which `setting[18] == 1` and the
time base is still `1`: **applying `FrameLimit` is not atomic with constructing the settings.**
The engine starts on the 30 fps base and moves to the 60 fps one later in startup. Static
analysis had the chain; only the running process had the **order**. `PROBABLE` — two runs show
the window exists, not how long it is.

### One expectation failed, and the database was not what was wrong

The TSV asserted `[0x01F82D20]+0x448 == 81` unconditionally. **The contract does not say that** —
it says the field is *“unset until `001DF240`”* and is `81` *“whenever the tables are
initialised”*. Live: **0** early, **`0x69705F70`** (ASCII `p_pi`) at 30 s.

> **The expectation was written stronger than the claim it tested.** The correct disposition is
> to fix the expectation and leave what `+0x448` holds **unresolved** — two non-81 readings
> prove it is not a count then and prove nothing about whether it is ever 81. `EO-1`.

### What is deliberately not claimed

**That any pilot is now parity-certifiable.** The harness observes startup state; `INTEGRATION`
requires the game exercising a subsystem **through its real caller**, and remains `NOT COVERED`
for all six.

**That the reference session is stable.** In run 2 the game **exited on its own between 30 s and
60 s after readiness**, with Steam running; passes 2 and 3 found no process and the tool refused
to report rather than inventing values — failing closed, as designed. Cause unknown, window
short, every future experiment must design around it. `EO-2`.

**That a clean directory guarantees a clean process.** It does not, which is why the live module
list is a separate check — and **that check has never fired**, so it is unproven in the
direction that matters.

### Gates

`check_links` · `check_consistency` · `check_questions` · `check_denominators` ·
`verify_doc_addresses` · two live runs · `ADDRESS-INDEX.md` regenerated.

## 2026-09-08 — the controlled arm: one edited line, five values, four controls that held

**Continuation of the same block.** The first two runs observed the machine's existing
configuration and could only establish **co-occurrence**. The directive's §7 asks for causality,
so the input was varied.

### Method

```
hash GameSetting.ini  ->  36A6BE8D...0EEB
FrameLimit=60 -> FrameLimit=30
ffxii_runtime.py run ... --settle 30       (settings are read once at startup: restart required)
restore from the hashed copy
re-hash                ->  36A6BE8D...0EEB   VERIFIED
```

### Result

| row | `FrameLimit=60` | `FrameLimit=30` | predicted |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `setting[18]` `+0x48` | **1** | **0** | 1 / 0 |
| `0x01DFE0B4` time base | **2** | **1** | 2 / 1 |
| `0x01DFE0B8` scale | **2.0** | **1.0** | 2.0 / 1.0 |
| `0x01DFE0BC` inverse | **0.5** | **1.0** | 0.5 / 1.0 |
| `0x01F82E38` gate | **1** | **0** | 1 / 0 |
| Language / Quality / Shadow / Decide | 1 / 3 / 2 / 1 | 1 / 3 / 2 / 1 | *not varied* |

> **Five outputs moved in the predicted direction; four control fields did not move at all.**
> The unchanged four are what make this an experiment rather than a coincidence — had they
> drifted too, the run would have proved only that restarting the game changes things.

**`GameSettingConfig` advances `CONTRACT READY` → `RUNTIME VALIDATED`** — the first subsystem in
this database to clear that rung.

### `DH-6` advanced, and the caveat is the interesting half

This machine holds **three** `GameSetting.ini` files. The game reads the **Steam-ID-scoped** one:

| file says | field | live | contract's encoding |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `FrameLimit=60` | `+0x48` | 1 | boolean-reduced; only exactly `1` counts |
| `Quality=VQ_CUSTOM` | `+0x0C` | 3 | *“`001DE4F0` with `quality == 3` (`VQ_CUSTOM`)”* |
| `Shadow=High` | `+0x1C` | 2 | LOW `0`, MEDIUM `1`, HIGH `2` |
| `DecideButton=Cross` | `+0x64` | 1 | `0` Circle, `1` Cross |

**The unscoped file matches none of them** — it says `30`, `VQ_MEDIUM`, `Medium`, `Circle`.

> **`DH-6` asked what a SHIPPED installation writes, and that is still open.** The file the game
> reads is one **the game itself rewrote** — its mtime moved during these runs — so it is not
> installer output and cannot answer the question as asked. Advanced, not closed.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**That the reference environment was left untouched.** It was modified on purpose, and the
modification is recorded, isolated to one file, restored, and **verified by re-hashing to the
pre-change value**. A run that silently left `FrameLimit=30` in place would have poisoned every
later experiment on this machine.

**That `+0x448` is understood.** Three runs, three different non-81 values — `0`,
`0x69705F70`, `0x41505F50`, the latter two ASCII text. `EO-1` stays open.

## 2026-09-08 — chasing the crash found a hole in the instrument first

**Block:** `EO-2`, the reference session dying on its own. A short session bounds every runtime
experiment, so it outranked any single question.

### What was actually contaminating the reference

FFXII's **Steam launch options** for app `595520` were set to

```
"...\DynamoRIO-Windows-11.91.20692\bin64\drrun.exe" -c "...\dr_client\build\RelWithDebInfo\dr_spawn_trace.dll" -- %command%
```

Both binaries present, the client DLL built the previous day. **Every Steam launch of FFXII ran
under dynamic instrumentation**, and the operator was seeing a fatal-error dialog. Nothing in
the game directory records it and **a reinstall does not clear it** — it lives in Steam's user
config. Found by grep after the operator surfaced a tooltip naming `drrun.exe`.

### The check that was supposed to catch this

> **A blocklist has two failure modes and both fired within a day of shipping it.**
>
> **False negative:** it enumerated loader DLL *names next to the exe*. DynamoRIO puts no file
> there — it wraps the **launch**. A file check cannot detect a contaminant that is not a file.
>
> **False positive:** it listed `xinput1_3.dll`. The reinstall restored **that file and none of
> the others**, and Steam restores only what it ships — so it is the game's own XInput
> redistributable, and the check had been one rename away from rejecting a clean install.

**Rebuilt as an allowlist** (13 shipped names, established by the reinstall acting as an
unplanned control), plus a Steam launch-options reader, plus the **complete live module list**
recorded as evidence instead of hits against a name list.

### The new check shipped broken, and its own control caught it

The launch-options reader used a regex over VDF and **returned empty for a fixture that plainly
contained the wrapper**. On a real machine that empty string is indistinguishable from *“no
wrapper set”* — the exact shape of failure this project keeps finding in its own instruments.
Replaced with brace matching, and `ffxii_runtime.py self-test` now proves it fires:

```
wrapper present, nested block after it     expect True  got True  PASS
no LaunchOptions key                       expect False got False PASS
wrapper on a different app only            expect False got False PASS
LaunchOptions present but empty            expect False got False PASS
```

**Two more of the same shape were found and fixed in the same block:** the process check
aborted a whole run on a **transient** `CreateToolhelp32Snapshot` failure (now retried, and an
empty module list is treated as failure rather than as *clean*), and the dump triage flagged
**System32's** `dinput8.dll` and the game's **own** `xinput1_3.dll` as injected because it
matched basenames without paths.

### `EP-1` — a question the evidence cannot answer

Were the three `EXP-001` runs instrumented? **Unanswerable.** They recorded *blocklist misses*
against names the harness knew, and DynamoRIO was not among them. They were launched
**directly**, and launch options apply only to Steam-initiated launches — which argues they
were clean, **but that is an argument, not a record.** Every run from now on stores the
complete module list, which is the only reason the question is answerable next time.

### The crash, localised — and it is not the wrapper

`minidump_triage.py` (new) parses the dumps the game writes beside itself. It **seeks**: these
are 2 GB full-memory dumps and the first version's slurp exceeded its own timeout. It also read
`ModuleNameRva` at the wrong offset and printed pages of mojibake — **a parser that prints
garbage instead of failing is worse than one that refuses**, so it now rejects an implausible
name length.

| when | code | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| before the reinstall | `0xE06D7363` | MSVC C++ throw; `param[0] = 0x19930520` is the EH magic and the **exception object is NULL** — a rethrow |
| after a clean reinstall, wrapper removed | `0xC0000005` | **read** access violation |

```
003845F0  sub  rsp, 0x38          AreaData_BindAndRebaseSectionDescriptor (252 B, WorldAreaField)
003845F4  mov  [rcx], rdx         ; store the descriptor
003845F7  test rdx, rdx / je      ; a NULL descriptor IS handled
00384600  mov  eax, [rdx + 0xC]   ; <-- FAULTS.  rdx = 0xFFFFFFFF82AD88C0
0038460C  add  eax, edx           ; ...the rebase the function is named for
```

> **`0xFFFFFFFF82AD88C0` is `0x82AD88C0` sign-extended into 64 bits** — a 32-bit offset being
> used as a pointer, inside the function whose job is to rebase 32-bit offsets. Non-null, so it
> passes the guard, then faults on the very next read.

**Both launch routes crash** — direct and `steam://rungameid/595520` — on a freshly reinstalled
game with no wrapper. **So `EO-2` is not the wrapper.** The two were found together and are
separate; closing `EO-2` on the wrapper's removal would have been closing it on a coincidence.

### What is deliberately not claimed

**What supplies the un-rebased offset.** The faulting instruction, the bad pointer and its
sign-extension are measured; the caller that passed it is not identified, and no claim is made
about why a fresh install reaches that state.

**That the earlier `EXP-001` results are void.** Nothing suggests they are — the controls
passed, the values were internally coherent, and they matched the installed ini field by field.
**But `EP-1` says plainly that the environment record for those runs is insufficient**, and the
`RUNTIME VALIDATED` label carries that caveat rather than being quietly withdrawn or quietly
kept.

`ffxii_runtime self-test` (4/4) · `verify_doc_addresses` · `ADDRESS-INDEX.md` regenerated.

## 2026-09-08 — measuring the crash six ways, and finding one signature under two sites

**Block:** `EO-2`. A session that crashes bounds every runtime experiment, so it outranks any
single question about the game.

### What was varied, and what happened

| launch route | wrapper | lifetime | outcome |
|---|---|---:|---|
| direct exe | set | **14.9 s** | `0xE06D7363` — MSVC rethrow, EH magic present, exception object NULL |
| `steam://rungameid` | set | **6.1 s** | crash + dump |
| direct exe | removed, after reinstall | ~30 s+ | reached readiness, then crashed |
| direct exe, cwd `x64` | removed | **1 s** | `0xC0000005` read AV at `001D6E20` |
| direct exe, cwd install root | removed | **1 s** | `0xC0000005` read AV at `001D6E20` |
| `steam://rungameid` | removed | **52 s** | crash + dump |

**Two routes, two machine states, two working directories — six launches, six crashes.**

### The signature

```
001D6E20       movzx ecx, byte [rbx]     rbx = 0xFFFFFFFF8BC13000
001D6E20       movzx ecx, byte [rbx]     rbx = 0xFFFFFFFF8BC1F000   (a second run, 48 KB apart)
003845F0+0x10  mov   eax, [rdx+0xC]      rdx = 0xFFFFFFFF82AD88C0
```

> **`0x8BC13000`, `0x8BC1F000`, `0x82AD88C0` all have bit 31 set**, so each is a 32-bit value
> sign-extended into `0xFFFFFFFF8…`. **Two unrelated functions — one owned by `Resource`, one
> by `WorldAreaField` — fail the same way.** The 48 KB gap between two runs of the same site
> says these are real allocation addresses, not a constant written into data.

### Identifying `001D6E20` changed what the crash means

```asm
001D6DFD  sub  rax, rbx                 ; dst - src: one counter drives both sides
001D6E20  movzx ecx, byte [rbx]         ; <-- FAULTS. the SOURCE string
001D6E23  mov  [rax + rbx + 0x20], cl   ; into the object under construction, at +0x20
001D6E27  lea  rbx, [rbx + 1]
001D6E2B  test cl, cl / jne 001D6E20    ; until NUL
```

**That is a `strcpy`.** `FUN_001d6d90` (225 B, owner `Resource`) is building an object and
copying a **name** into `+0x20`. So the failure is not a corrupted heap — **it is a pointer
that was never 64 bits.**

### Two environment facts, from the reinstall as an unplanned control

- **`steam_appid.txt` was a modding artifact.** It was present before and the reinstall did not
  restore it; Steam restores only what it ships. That file is what lets the exe run without
  Steam launching it, which is why it was there.
- **The install is complete**: `appmanifest_595520.acf` reads `StateFlags 4`,
  `BytesToDownload 0`, `SizeOnDisk 31,246,606,698`. Not a partial download.

### What is deliberately not claimed

**That the game is broken.** The operator reports it launches normally for them. **Six harness
launches crashed and zero operator launches did**, so the difference lives in the launch
context, and that difference — not the pointer — is what remains unknown. Publishing *“FFXII
sign-extends a 32-bit pointer”* as an engine defect would be reading a machine-state artefact
as a property of the game.

**That the two faulting sites share a cause.** They share a *shape*. Nothing here connects them
beyond that, and the earlier `0xE06D7363` rethrow is a third signature again.

**Per the directive's fallback rule**, the operator is asked exactly one thing — whether a
launch they start now reaches the title screen — because that single answer splits the space
and everything around it is already instrumented.

### Gates

`check_links` · `check_consistency` · `check_questions` · `check_denominators` ·
`ffxii_runtime self-test` · `verify_doc_addresses` · `ADDRESS-INDEX.md` regenerated.

## 2026-09-08 — `EO-2` answered, and the reference process has two hooks nobody had recorded

**Block:** `EO-3` was taken statically — the hypothesis is about how a pointer is *stored*, and
that is in the binary. The operator then asked for a launch they could watch, and the
observation answered `EO-2` outright.

### The answer

**FFXII restarts itself through Steam.** `launch` reported **pid 2392** reaching readiness; the
game that reached the **title screen** and stayed there was **pid 39424**.

> **Six recorded “crashes” were the harness watching the first process do exactly what it is
> supposed to do.** The readiness gate was satisfied by a process that was about to hand over.
> `settle_restart()` now waits after readiness and adopts the replacement.

**This does not explain the `.dmp` files**, which are real and stay with `EO-3`. What it settles
is that a short-lived first process is **normal Steam behaviour**, not evidence of a broken
game — and that every conclusion drawn from watching it was drawn from the wrong process.

### The third blocklist-shaped defect in one day

The process control reported the healthy game as **`contaminated: dinput8.dll`**. That is
**System32's DirectInput**, which the game loads legitimately — and it shares a filename with
the DLL the FFXII mod stack proxies. **Same name, opposite meaning; only the path separates
them.**

`live_modules()` recorded `szModule` (the base name) and not `szExePath`, so the information
needed to tell them apart **was never captured**. Now it records full paths and classifies by
path, the same fix `minidump_triage.py` had already needed.

> Blocklist by name, in one day: **could not see DynamoRIO** · **rejected `xinput1_3.dll`** ·
> **rejected System32's `dinput8.dll`**. Three failures, one root cause.

### The clean run

`EXP-001` against the live title screen, attaching rather than launching:
**`E1=1`, `E2=2`, `E3=2.0`, `E4=0.5`, `E5=1`** — the `FrameLimit=60` column, from a process
that was demonstrably healthy and observed by the operator.

**`EO-1` advanced:** `+0x448` read **`0`** on both passes. The earlier `0x69705F70` /
`0x41505F50` (ASCII `p_pi`, `P_PA`) came from **dying** processes. `0` is exactly what the
contract's *“unset until `001DF240`”* predicts, so what remains open is only **when** it
becomes `81` — and the experiment's unconditional `expect 81` is still the thing that was wrong.

### What the full module list showed, which a blocklist never would

**99 modules**: 89 Windows, 4 in the game directory, and **six that are neither**:

```
gameoverlayrenderer64.dll     Steam's overlay -- an in-process graphics hook
steamclient64.dll  tier0_s64.dll  vstdlib_s64.dll     the Steam client runtime
mpoav.dll                     Windows Defender
discordhook64.dll             Discord's overlay hook
```

> **Two third-party in-process hooks are in the reference environment.** A blocklist would have
> called this process clean — correctly, but **by luck**, since neither is on any list this
> project maintains. They are irrelevant to reading static configuration and **not** irrelevant
> to any future experiment about presentation or timing. Recording the whole list is what makes
> that judgement possible at all.

### What is deliberately not claimed

**That the crashes are explained.** `EO-3` stands: three page-aligned, sign-extended pointer
values clustered in 64 KB. Answering `EO-2` removes the *bogus* crashes from the record; it
does not account for the dumps.

**That Steam's and Discord's hooks are harmless.** Nothing here tests that. They are recorded
because an experiment that later disagrees with expectation needs to know they were present.

## 2026-09-08 — the first question this database answered because it could run the game

**Block:** with a healthy reference session up and standing authorisation to launch and close
the game, the target chose itself: **the question the database had already marked as
unanswerable without a live process.** `AY-10`, open since 2026-09-02, blocked on the st2e
group tables at `0x02EC3D80` / `0x02F973C0` — *“null in the file and populated at load”*.

### Controls, before any number

Beyond the harness's standing two (module at `ImageBase`, `LUAC_TAIL`), this read needed two of
its own:

- **an offset read** — `table + 8` returns the window shifted by exactly one qword, so reads are
  position-accurate and not cached;
- **the arena base at `[0x01F83530]` reads `0`** at the title screen. That matters:
  `ImageAddress_ResolveRuntimePointer` adds it, so with a zero base **the stored values are the
  addresses**, and dereferencing them directly is legitimate rather than a guess.

### The result

**16 of 28 slots populated · every one magic `st2e` · 3,969 entries · slot `n` holds ids
beginning at exactly `n × 10,000`, 16 of 16.**

`[rax+4]` reads **428** for slot 1 and **71** for slot 23 — the entry count, which is exactly
the bound `002F9860` tests before indexing. The header's shape was predicted by the code and
confirmed by the data.

### It contradicts a published conclusion

> [The VBF / st2e document](../02-Resource-And-Asset-Pipeline/VBF-Archive-And-Authored-Tables/vbf-archive-and-st2e-tables.md)
> §9: *“`40,000–41,243` falls in the gap between the two pools … **this resolver can never
> return text for a `help_action` id.**”*
>
> **Slot 4 is populated and its first ids are `40000, 40100, 40101, 40102`** — precisely the
> `40000 + category*100 + slot` shape the question was about. **The gap does not exist.**

**What survived and what did not is the useful part.** Every *mechanical* reading in that
section held: the `0x10624DD3` and `0x68DB8BAD` reciprocal divides, the 28-group bound, the
fixed empty string, both table addresses, the resolution through
`ImageAddress_ResolveRuntimePointer`. **What failed was the inference stacked on top of them** —
and it failed for a reason no amount of re-reading the code would have fixed: **the table's
indexing is not in the code.** It is in the data, and the data only exists at runtime.

### The tension it opens, left open

Both resolvers read **the same two tables** — identical displacements in both bodies,
tool-resolved. The table is ÷ 10,000-indexed. So:

```
002F9920  id / 10000  ->  slot 4 for id 40000     consistent with the table
002F9860  id /  1000  ->  slot 40 for id 40000    out of range
                      ->  slot 10 for id 10000    whose ids start at 100000
```

> **At most one divisor can be indexing this table correctly and the data says which.** What
> `FUN_002F9860`'s ÷ 1,000 path is *for* is **not established** — a domain below 10,000, or
> legacy. **Recorded as a tension, not resolved by preference.**

### What was deliberately not claimed

**Any string.** Only headers and the leading id runs were read; **nothing here says what id
40000 actually says.** The claim is about the table's shape and membership.

**That the 12 empty slots are unused.** They are empty *at the title screen*. A read taken in a
field area would separate *“never used”* from *“not loaded yet”* — `EQ-1`, and now a cheap
experiment rather than an operator request.

> **This is the static → runtime → static loop closing once.** A static reading reached its
> limit; the limit was honestly recorded as a live-only question and left open for six days;
> the harness made the read cheap; the answer went back into the static document as a
> correction. **The question was answerable all along and the project could not ask it.**

## 2026-09-08 — the treasure verb was not about treasure

**Block:** `coverage_balance.py` ranks **`01-Script-VM-Native-Bridge` highest for player-facing
debt** — 190, over 1,900 functions and 9 documents. Took `setuptreasure` (verb `0x2BE`,
`00355210`, 240 B), the largest script-verb handler no document cited.

### What it actually found

`002E97C0` (68 B) is **the script VM's entity resolver**, and it was uncited. **Eleven callers,
five of them named verbs** — `setuptreasure`, `puppetbind`, `bindp`, `bindh`, `bindc`: the
whole *bind* family. The treasure verb was one worked example of a general mechanism.

```
id  ==  ( u16[rec + 0x24] << 16 ) | ( u16[rec + 0x1A] | 0x8000 )
slot =  id & 0x7FFF,  and the slot must be < 128
records are 64 bytes at 0x0215FDA0  ->  128 x 64 = 8,192 bytes
```

> **The id is the record's own identity, read back and compared.** `bts edx, 0xF` sets bit 15
> before the comparison, so **bit 15 is always set in a valid id**; `cmovne rax, r9` returns
> NULL on mismatch. **A stale id addresses a live slot and still fails** — which is the whole
> point of a generation check, and it means a wrong id is safe while a lucky guess is not.

**One instruction is dead and is reproduced anyway.** `002E97E6 je` tests the flags from
`add rax, rcx` where `rcx` is a fixed non-zero table base — the sum is never zero. Compiler
output. **A reimplementation that omits it is still correct; one that acts on it is not**, so
it is recorded rather than tidied away.

### Five bytes decide where a chest stands

`002FAF60` (104 B) has **exactly one caller**, so the decoder belongs to this verb and the
claim is bounded to it.

```
x       = (int16)rec[+0x04] / 10.0
y       = 0.0                                  always -- written, never read from the record
z       = (int16)rec[+0x06] / 10.0
w       = 1.0
heading = -( rec[+0x08] & 0x3F ) / 60.0 * 2*pi
```

**Every constant resolved with a tool**, never by hand: `008F8180` = `10.0` (used for both
axes), `008F6D54` = `60.0`, `01CEBC78` = `6.2831855` = 2π.

> **The position is in tenths and the facing is one of sixty.** `x`/`z` are signed 16-bit
> tenths — ±3276.7 at 0.1 resolution. **`y` is not authored at all.**
>
> And the facing is **six bits divided by sixty**. Codes `0..59` step the circle in exactly
> **6°**; codes `60..63` are representable and divide **past a whole turn**. The field width and
> the divisor disagree, the engine does not clamp, and that is what the bytes say rather than
> what a tidy reading would prefer.

**The facing is set twice**, through `Actor_SetFacingHeading_Variant1` and
`Actor_SetDesiredMovementHeading`, **with the same value** — a chest is placed already pointing
where it will stay, with no turn to play out.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**That the other four `bind*` verbs decode a placement.** They share the **resolver** and not
the **decoder** — `002FAF60` has one caller, and assuming otherwise would be exactly the
family-generalisation that `SetBank64B` punished earlier today.

**What the 128 records are.** Four fields are read on this path; the other 56 bytes of each
record are unread. The table is **past the end of `.data`'s file image**, so it is empty in the
executable and built at load — `ER-1`, and **now a cheap live read** rather than an operator
request, which is what the runtime harness changed.

**What `002E28E0` (2,026 B) does with the record**, what `002EC5B0(actor, 0x10)` sets, or what
the `-1.0f` at `0026DAC0` means. All named, all unread.

## 2026-09-08 — the live read's first result was that my own document was wrong

**Block:** `ER-1`, filed one block earlier with its method already stated — *a live read would
answer it*. It did.

### The correction, first

The placement formula had been published as `rec[+0x04]`, `rec[+0x06]`, `rec[+0x08]`. Reading
the table live shows **`+0x00` and `+0x08` are `prev`/`next` pointers**.

> **The decoder does not operate on the entity record.** `setuptreasure` calls `002FAF60` with
> the result of `002650B0` — a different object. The C sketch in the document had that right;
> **the formula block did not**, because it reused the name `rec`. The offsets collide and the
> structures do not, so **a reimplementer following the formula would have decoded a `prev`
> pointer as an X coordinate.**

Re-reading the entry sequence to check that found a second error: the selector is **`args[2]`**
— `mov r8d, dword ptr [rbx + 8]` where `rbx` is the argument pointer — not `args[1]`, which is
**not read on this path at all**. Both corrected at the source with the reason recorded.

### What the table is

**128 records of 64 bytes, every one pre-initialised.** Applying the resolver's own validity
rule to the live bytes: **128 of 128 pass.**

**Only nine byte offsets differ across the entire table** — `0..3`, `8..11`, and `26`:

```
slot 0    +0x00  00 00 00 00     +0x08  e0 fd 15 02  -> 0x0215FDE0 = slot 1
slot 1    +0x00  a0 fd 15 02     +0x08  20 fe 15 02  -> slot 0, slot 2
slot 127  +0x00  20 1d 16 02     +0x08  00 00 00 00  -> slot 126, and NULL
```

> **A doubly-linked free list spanning the whole pool** — head at slot 0 with a null `prev`,
> tail at slot 127 with a null `next`. Exactly what a slot pool looks like with no map loaded,
> and it is the **baseline** a later field-area read gets diffed against.

**The pool is fixed at 128**, so **a map can name at most 128 entities** — a hard limit rather
than a soft one, and a real constraint on what a mod can add.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**That `+0x24` is a generation counter.** It is `0` in all 128 records — **one observation, one
value.** The resolver's compare-before-use is proven from the code; that the stamp ever
*changes* is not observed, so the label is `HYPOTHESIS`. It also means **the check currently
protects nothing**: every slot's naive id `0x8000 | slot` resolves.

**Anything about a loaded map.** 46 bytes of every record are zero throughout at the title
screen and stay unread.

### The capability the block ended on

**`ER-1` and `EQ-1` now want the same thing and neither can have it: a field area.** The harness
launches to the title screen and no further. **Nine saves exist** (`FFXII_000`–`FFXII_008`), so
the state is reachable — the route is what is missing. **`ES-1`** filed as the capability, which
is charter-directive §4's automated state establishment, and §3 permits narrowly scoped input
automation for exactly this.

**The launch also confirmed `EO-2`'s fix in practice** — the harness printed *“the launched
process exited; adopting pid 35280 (the game restarts itself through Steam)”* and went on to
read successfully.

**Block:** `ES-1` — reach a field area, the capability `ER-1` and `EQ-1` both wait on.

### The detector first, deliberately

**Input automation without state detection is a guess with a keyboard attached.**
`ffxii_runtime.py state` reads the observables `EXP-002` and `EXP-003` baselined, keyed on the
sharpest: **all 128 script-entity records are chained on the free list with no map loaded**, and
**a map cannot place anything without taking slots off that list.**

The verdict is deliberately weaker than it could be: `title` or **`changed`**, never *“in a
field area”*. **Naming the new state would need a second baseline taken somewhere known**, and
that does not exist yet.

### It earned itself on the first run

```
first reading after the readiness gate    st2e groups  0 of 28    area id  -1
ten seconds later                         st2e groups 16 of 28    area id  12
then stable for a minute
```

> **The readiness gate fires before the game has finished loading.** That is exactly the trap
> `EXP-001` fell into — observing at the first readable instant and nearly publishing a false
> falsification — and it is now **measured on a second, independent observable** rather than
> remembered as an anecdote.

**And `EXP-002` reproduced across sessions**: the same 16 groups, the same set, the same area
id 12. A live reading taken twice on different process instances agreeing is the cheapest
reproducibility evidence available, and it had never been collected before.

### The input attempt, bounded and negative

**The window is found and focused** — `SetForegroundWindow` succeeds and `GetForegroundWindow`
returns the game's own handle, so that half works. **`SendInput` with `KEYEVENTF_SCANCODE`**
(not `SendKeys`, which DirectInput never sees) was tried over five candidate confirm keys:
`0x1C` Enter, `0x39` Space, `0x2C` Z, `0x9C` numpad Enter, `0x2A` Shift.

**No state change whatsoever.** 128 of 128 entity slots still free after every attempt.

> **The attempt is not diagnosable, and naming that is the block's real result.** The only
> observable distinguishes *title* from *a map is loaded*, and **a menu cursor moves between
> them invisibly**. So three different failures — *the key was wrong*, *the input never
> arrived*, *the menu moved and nothing else did* — are **indistinguishable with the

**Guessing more keys would have been motion, not progress**, so the attempt was stopped at five
and the missing instrument was filed instead. `ET-1`: charter-directive §6's **state snapshot +

## 2026-09-08 — built the instrument that could say no, and it did

**Block:** `ET-1`, filed last block as the **prerequisite** for `ES-1` rather than a nicety.
Directive §17 says to prioritise a capability that unlocks many questions; this one gates every
field-dependent question the project has.

### What was built

`ffxii_runtime.py snapshot` / `diff` / `churn`, on a new `runtime_probe --dump` that writes raw
bytes to a file instead of hex to stdout — hex is fine for 200 bytes and hopeless for 8 MB.

**8,454,144 bytes in 0.66 s** across `.data` and three BSS spans. **Page-chunked**, because a
single `ReadProcessMemory` over a multi-megabyte span fails completely if one page inside it is
uncommitted — which for a BSS sweep is the normal case. **Unreadable pages are counted**, since
a snapshot silently full of zeros would diff clean against anything.

> **One reporting bug, caught by an implausible number.** The first run printed `-1 bytes` for
> every region: the parser split the whole of stdout and picked a word out of
> `CONTROL 1 base match`. The dumps had been written correctly all along — **8.4 MB on disk
> while the summary said zero.** Fixed to read the last line.

### Two controls, because a diff of a running game is not evidence

**The game rewrites thousands of bytes a second.** With no input and three seconds between
captures: **7,818 bytes across 407 runs.** A raw diff across *“press a key”* would have shown
thousands of changes and meant nothing.

**And the subtraction needs its own floor**: how much does a no-input window differ from
*another* no-input window, under the same subtraction? **242 bytes.**

### The result

| comparison | NEW bytes |
|---|---:|
| baseline no-input, test no-input | **242** — the noise floor |
| baseline no-input, test **keypress** | 319 |
| baseline `B→C`, test **keypress** | 251 |
| **baseline keypress, test no-input** — reversed | **311** |

> **The reversal is the whole result.** A keypress window scores 319 against a no-input
> baseline; a **no-input** window scores **311** against the keypress baseline. **The measure is
> symmetric.**
>
> **A real effect appears in one direction. Noise appears in both.** 319 against a floor of 242
> with a reversal of 311 is two arbitrary windows of a running game failing to touch identical
> byte sets — **not a signal.**

**The symmetry check is now in the tool**, so the next input attempt is graded automatically
rather than by eye.

### What this changes about `ES-1`

Last block's honest *“not diagnosable”* becomes **a controlled negative**: the keypress produced
**no detectable change anywhere in 8.4 MB** of the game's own writable memory, with the window
verifiably focused. **So the next thing to try is a different input PATH, not a different key** —
virtual-key `SendInput` rather than scan codes, a virtual gamepad, raw HID. **None tested.**

### What was deliberately not claimed

**That the input never reached the process.** *“Reached and was discarded”* produces the same
reading. The claim is **no detectable effect**, labelled `PROBABLE` for the stronger version.

**That there was no change anywhere.** The snapshot covers `.data` and three BSS spans —
**8.4 MB, not the address space**. A change confined to the heap or to another module's data
would not be seen, which is why the conclusion is *“no detectable change”* and not *“no
change”*.

## 2026-09-08 — bypassing the OS was the right idea, and the answer is still no

**Block:** `ES-1`'s redirect — *try a different input path*. Virtual-key `SendInput` was tried
first and is **also negative**: **293 forward against a 425 reversal**, i.e. the no-input window
differed from the keypress window *more* than the reverse. Conclusively noise.

**Then the operator proposed the better route**: stop feeding the operating system, find the
input state the game reads, and write it.

### The chain was already ours, statically

`check_already_answered` returned
[binding profiles](../15-Input/Binding-Profiles/binding-profiles-remapping-and-control-state.md),
which already records `0079E6A0`, the `(code - 0x1C)` bias and the backend at
`FUN_00796E20() + 0xDF8`. **Not a rediscovery — a runtime validation**, and every link held:

```
[0x02EA5368]                  ->  0x01F7E350   the input manager
manager + 0xDF8               ->  0x01F7F150   the backend
backend + device*8 + 0x118    ->  a HEAP block; device 0 is the only non-null of seven
block + 0x30 + (code - 0x1C)  ->  256 bytes, one per input, ALL ZERO when idle
```

> **The codes are the `GameSetting.ini` `[Keyboard1]` numbers.** Their minimum is **28**, which
> is exactly the `0x1C` the query subtracts — so `index = keymap_value - 28`. **`HIGH`, not
> proven**: nobody watched a real press set a specific byte, and that distinction is kept.

### The tool is separate on purpose

`runtime_probe.py` opens the process `PROCESS_VM_READ` only and its docstring says why: **a
validation instrument that can perturb its subject is not a validation instrument.** That
guarantee underwrites every live number this project has published, so it was **not weakened**.
`runtime_poke.py` is a different tool with a louder contract: it resolves the chain fresh every
run (the block is heap and moves), **refuses to write when anything is already held**, restores
what it wrote and **verifies the restore**, and prints that the state it produces is
**INSTRUMENTATION-INDUCED** and must never be reported as naturally reached.

### The result

`Start`, `Cross` and `Circle` each written to `1`, held 12 frames, released, restore verified.
**No state change** — 128 of 128 slots still free, `st2e` still 16 of 28, area id still 12.

> **The decisive follow-up.** Written to `1` and polled for 400 ms *without* being cleared:
> `[1,1,1,1,...]`, twenty readings. **The byte persists.**
>
> So it is **not** the case that a device poll overwrites the write each frame — the value sits
> there untouched and **nothing consumes it**. That rules out the most obvious explanation and
> leaves three, none of them tested.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**Why nothing consumes it.** `EU-1`. Candidates: input is not processed while the window is
unfocused (which would also explain both `EXP-004` negatives); the title screen reads a
different path; the held-array is downstream of an edge buffer that is what actually gets
polled. **The measurement does not choose between them.**

**That the code mapping is right.** `keymap_value - 28` fits the bias exactly and is still an
inference. **The cheapest confirmation is one irreducible manual step** — hold a key while the
harness polls the array — which would settle the mapping *and* whether the array is written by
real input at all. That is a genuinely small ask and it is the kind §16 of the directive
reserves for the operator.

## 2026-09-08 — back to the database, and a format recovered whole

**Block:** the guard is *max three consecutive blocks in one category* and runtime tooling had
run to five. Switched back and took the largest survivor on `EL-1`'s corrected list:
**`002432B0`, 609 bytes, 108 call sites** — 36 owned by `UI`, 72 unowned — and uncited by any
document. Charter §29's *high-connectivity callgraph nodes*, top of the list.

### It is an authored-format decoder

```
[obj + 0x20]  ->  ImageAddress_ResolveRuntimePointer  ->  a table of 20-byte records
record.dword0 & 0x3FF   =  the ITEM COUNT      ten bits, so at most 1,023
record.dword4           ->  the item bytes, through the same arena

item[0] = its own byte length      item[1] = its type, 1..9
```

> **Two bytes carry the whole format.** The walk reads the type to decide a cost and the length
> to advance, so items are **variable-length and self-describing** — an unrecognised type costs
> zero space and the list still steps correctly past it. That is a real robustness property and
> it falls straight out of the two-byte header.

### The tables, resolved with a tool

Both are image-base-relative: sizes at `00243514`, constructors at `00243538`.

| type | node size | constructor |
|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | `0x20` | `0029ECB0` |
| 2 | `0x40` | `0029F4C0` |
| **3** | **0** | **none** |
| 4 | `0x20` | `0029ED40` (9 B) |
| 5 | `0x30` | `0029FEB0` |
| **6** | **0** | **none** |
| 7 | `0xA0` | `0029F130` (841 B) |
| 8 | `0x20` | `0029F930` |
| 9 | `0x40` | `0029F4C0` |

> **Types 3 and 6 cost nothing and build nothing.** They take the same `xor eax, eax` arm the
> out-of-range default takes — so *“unknown”* and *“deliberately empty”* are the same code path,
> which is why the format tolerates both.
>
> **Types 2 and 9 are aliases** — identical size, identical constructor. **Nothing here says
> why there are two codes for one thing**, and inventing a reason would be exactly the kind of
> tidy story the evidence does not support.

### One allocation, sized by the first pass

The running total **starts at `count * 8`** — the pointer array — and then accumulates each
item's size, so a single block holds the pointers **and** the nodes:

```
total = count * 8  +  sum over items of size[type]
if total == 0   ->  out->list = NULL, nothing built
```

**A list of nothing but types 3 and 6 still allocates `count * 8`** — the pointer array exists
even when there is nothing for it to point at. That is a checkable prediction about the
allocator's behaviour and it comes free from reading the arithmetic.

### The node, field by field

Four `u16`s are copied straight across from item `+0x04`/`+0x06`/`+0x08`/`+0x0A` into node
`+0x0C`/`+0x0E`/`+0x10`/`+0x12`. The `+0x08` dword is a **packed flags word** assembled with
the `x ^ ((x ^ v) & mask)` bitfield-insert idiom and then masked with `0xFFFF003F` — **bits
6–15 are deliberately cleared whatever the authored bytes said.**

### What was deliberately not claimed

**What the list is a list of.** The types are numbered, sized and constructed; **nothing here
names them.** `EV-1` — and the constructor that would say the most is `0029F130`, 841 bytes,
the one behind the 160-byte type 7.

**Ownership.** 36 of 108 callers are `UI`-owned and the function carries **no ledger owner**.
The document is filed under the resource pipeline **for what it does**, and says so — a caller
is not evidence of ownership.

### Gates

## 2026-09-08 — reading the constructors gave the format its vocabulary

**Block:** `EV-1`. Last block recovered the format's **structure** — counts, lengths, type
codes, sizes, one allocation — and could not say what any of it **meant**. That is precisely
the *“understand”* versus *“could reimplement”* gap the charter puts at the centre.

### The reading was cheap because the constructors are private

**All six have exactly one caller**, `002432B0`. Nothing else in the image reaches them, so
they are the decoder's own vocabulary rather than shared helpers whose meaning would have to be
generalised.

| type | size | constructor | what it builds |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| **1** | `0x20` | `0029ECB0` | **a 192-byte Widget**, through the factory `00244F50` with proc `0029E7D0`, stored at node `+0x18` |
| 2 | `0x40` | `0029F4C0` | calls `002A0060` — **not identified** |
| **3** | 0 | none | nothing at all |
| **4** | `0x20` | `0029ED40` | **9 bytes: `node[+0x18] = 0`** — occupies a node and builds nothing |
| **5** | `0x30` | `0029FEB0` | **TEXT** — see below |
| **6** | 0 | none | nothing at all |
| 7 | `0xA0` | `0029F130` | arena data + two `Resource` helpers — **not identified** |
| **8** | `0x20` | `0029F930` | **A NESTED LIST** — recurses into the decoder |
| 9 | `0x40` | `0029F4C0` | same constructor as type 2 |

### Type 5 is where the static format meets the live table

```asm
0029FF42  mov  ecx, [rdi + 0x14]     ; the STRING ID
0029FF45  cmp  ecx, -1 / je          ; -1 means no string
0029FF4A  call 0x2f9920              ; the st2e HIGH-pool resolver
0029FF4F  mov  [rbx + 0x18], rax
```

> **`002F9920` is the resolver `EXP-002` enumerated in a running process** — 16 populated slots,
> magic `st2e`, slot `n` holding ids from `n × 10,000`. **An authored UI item carries a string
> id and looks it up in the table that experiment mapped.** A static read and a live read,
> taken days apart for different reasons, meeting at one `call`.

```
opacity = (item[+0x10] == 0) ? 1.0 : item[+0x10] / 100.0     008F3134 = 100.0, 01CEBBA8 = 1.0
string  = (item.dword[+0x14] == -1) ? none : st2e_high(...)
```

**An opacity expressed as a percentage in one byte**, with `0` meaning *use the default* rather
than *fully transparent* — a distinction a reimplementation would get wrong by writing the
obvious thing.

### Type 8 makes the format recursive

```asm
0029F950  mov  ecx, [rdx + 0x20]     ; THE SAME table offset the outer decoder used
0029F959  movzx ebx, word [rsi + 0xc]; an INDEX, u16 at item +0x0C
0029F96A  lea  r10, [rbx + rbx*4]    ; the SAME index * 5 stride
          ... then calls 002432B0
```

> **A type-8 item names another record in the same table and decodes it.** Lists compose out of
> lists — which explains the context argument the decoder carries, and why types 1 and 8 are
> the only ones handed it.

### A loose end from the previous block, closed

§7 recorded that the decoder **clears bits 6–15** of every node's `+0x08`
(`and dword [rbx+8], 0xFFFF003F`) and left that as a curiosity. **The constructors fill them
back in.** Type 5:

```asm
0029FF08  movzx eax, word [rdi + 0x12] / shl eax, 6
0029FF0F  xor eax, [rbx+8] / and eax, 0xffc0 / xor [rbx+8], eax
```

**`0xFFC0` is exactly the complement of the `0x3F` the decoder keeps.** So it is a **division of
labour** — the decoder owns the low six bits, the per-type constructor owns the next ten — and
not, as the previous block's wording allowed, a value being thrown away.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**Types 2/9 and 7.** `0029F4C0` (through `002A0060`) and `0029F130` (841 bytes, the 160-byte
type) are **still unidentified — two of the nine**, and `EV-1` stays open on exactly those.
Naming them from their call graphs alone would be the guess this block avoided everywhere else.

**That type 1's widget proc `0029E7D0` does anything in particular.** It is a proc address
passed to the factory; **it was not read.**

`verify_doc_addresses` · `ADDRESS-INDEX.md` regenerated.

## 2026-09-08 — the contract dimension, and what measuring it cost

**Block:** `EM-1`. Two consecutive blocks in the resource pipeline, and `CONTRACT` was the
only one of charter §21's eleven dimensions not already `NOT COVERED` for every pilot — so it
was the one place the parity table could still move.

### The verdict is now derived, not written

```text
harness CONTRACT_MAP  ->  claim strings checked against the contract's section 15 table
                      ->  verdict DERIVED:  COVERED iff every testable claim is EXERCISED
                      ->  declared != derived  ->  a reported declaration problem
```

Four statuses, and the distinction that matters is between the last two:

| status | meaning |
|---|---|
| `EXERCISED` | a case reaches it, **and breaking the claim breaks the test** |
| `PARTIAL` | touched, but not over the range the claim states |
| `NOT EXERCISED` | no case reaches it — with what would |
| `OPEN QUESTION` | the row records an `UNKNOWN`; there is no behaviour to exercise |

> **Only `OPEN QUESTION` leaves the denominator, and every excluded row is printed.** A claim
> no differential *can* reach — an image-wide census, a startup-ordering fact — **stays in**
> and counts as unexercised. Excusing it would have been the easy move and would have made the
> number meaningless.

### What the measurement found

| subsystem | §15 rows | exercised | of testable | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `field_music` | 8 | 6 | **6 of 7** | NOT COVERED |
| `flag_banks` | 12 | 5 | 5 of 10 | NOT COVERED |
| `quality_preset` | 9 | 2 | 2 of 7 | NOT COVERED |
| `angle_wrap` | 9 | 1 | 1 of 7 | NOT COVERED |
| `widget_construct` | 6 | 1 | 1 of 6 | NOT COVERED |
| `name_registry` | — | — | — | **no contract exists** |

**15 of 37 testable claims, across 44 rows in five contracts.**

> #### The one pilot that claimed the dimension was claiming it wrongly
>
> `flag_banks` declared `CONTRACT: COVERED`, reasoning that *“12 of its 12 section-15 claims
> concern these four accessors”*. Reading the twelve rows against the harness, **four concern
> other functions entirely**: the encoded-id decoder `0032A8A0` (not one of the eleven ops),
> the threshold schedule `00377970`, the new-game list reached from `002EF2D0`, and the two
> shipped `.fst` files. A fifth — *“the two routes, re-counted here”* — is `PARTIAL`: both
> routes are **executed as shipped**, but their call-site census (121 and 40) is a static count
> no differential can run.
>
> **The declaration was not dishonest; it was unchecked.** That is the whole argument for
> deriving it.

### Positive control — three planted defects, three reports

A checker that reports nothing is indistinguishable from a checker that cannot see. Three
defects were planted in a copy of the harness tree and the tool run against it:

| planted | reported |
|---|---|
| a mapped claim reworded (`Writes no state` → `Writes no state at all`) | **yes** — as one missing claim *and* one unmatched row |
| five `widget_construct` statuses flipped to `EXERCISED` | **yes** — `declared NOT COVERED but the map derives COVERED` |
| `angle_wrap`'s map renamed away | **yes** — `no CONTRACT_MAP -- the verdict is asserted, not derived` |

Exit code 1, four problems, and the unmodified tree reports **zero**. The clean run is
therefore a real negative.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**That an `EXERCISED` mark is verified.** It asserts that breaking the claim breaks the test;
**nothing mutates the reconstruction to confirm that it would.** The claim *strings* are
checked mechanically, the *mapping* is a human judgement, and [the parity standard](../../../Reconstruction/PARITY-STANDARD.md) §7 now says so as an
open item beside mutation testing.

**That anything got better.** `CONTRACT` was `COVERED` for one pilot and is now `COVERED` for
none — it has joined `INTEGRATION` and `FULL-SUBSYSTEM` as a dimension no pilot meets. The
page reads worse because it is now measuring something.

**No question was filed.** Every unexercised claim is a harness that does not reach far enough,
not an unknown about the game — filing one would have been padding. The two cheapest are
recorded in `PROGRAM-STATE.md` §4af instead.

## 2026-09-08 — four negatives, one confound, and a mechanism

**Block:** `EU-1`, chosen because **`INTEGRATION` is `NOT COVERED` for all six parity pilots**
and cannot move until the game reaches a real state. `EU-1` gates `ES-1`, which gates
`EXP-001`. One question sits under the whole parity table. [`EXP-006`](../_experiments/EXP-006-the-array-is-written-on-transition.md).

### The route not taken, and why

`EXP-005` left three explanations and proposed testing them. Charter §7 says trace causality,
not correlation — so the first attempt was to **watch the address and see who reads it**
rather than to test guesses. That failed, informatively:

| step | result |
|---|---|
| hardware watchpoint on the heap array | refused — the tool watches module-mapped addresses only |
| trace `0079E6A0` (the query) | `Module 'FFXII_TZA' not in address map` |
| populate the map by `POST /debugger/sync_modules` | **worked** — `DYNAMIC_BASE` is clear, so the Ghidra base *is* the runtime base |
| trace target **and a control**, then continue | both **0 hits** |

> **Zero on the control is what saved this.** A negative on the target alone would have read
> as *“nothing calls the input query”*. Measuring CPU time instead — with a positive control
> that burned 1.984 s — showed the game had used **0.000 CPU seconds over 2.0 s wall**.
>
> **The game was frozen.** The engine reported `running`; only **detach** resumed it (0.391 s
> over 2.0 s). The traces measured nothing because nothing was executing. Filed as `EW-2`.

### The operator step that was not irreducible

`EXP-005` recorded that settling this needed *“one irreducible manual step — the operator
holds a key while the harness polls.”* **The operating system can hold the key and the harness
can hold the foreground.** Charter §16 makes manual testing the fallback; it had been reached
for while an automated route was available.

`window_focus.py` takes the foreground **and verifies it with `GetForegroundWindow`**, because
`SetForegroundWindow` fails silently for a process that does not own the foreground — a probe
that does not check is measuring its own terminal. `runtime_input_probe.py` presses 18 keys,
polls the array every 10 ms, and re-checks focus on **every** poll.

### What was measured

**18 of 18 keys moved exactly one index. Control clean. 0 of ~630 polls lost focus.** Five
named bindings land on their own `GameSetting.ini` codes, so `index = code - 28` moves from
`HIGH` to `PROVEN` — it had been *inferred* from the minimum code being 28.

> **And the array is indexed by PHYSICAL KEY, not by game action.** Thirteen of the eighteen
> land on codes no binding names — `A`→28, `Z`→53, `Up`→108. The `[Keyboard1]` section is a
> binding **out of** this space, and most of the space is unbound. Nothing had said so.

### The mechanism

```text
A.  hold Escape for real -> the game sets index 36 to 1
    WRITE 0 over it, keep holding
    -> 000000000000000      fifteen polls, 300 ms, the game NEVER restores the 1

B.  WRITE 1 with no key down
    real press   -> still 1
    real release -> 0       the RELEASE wrote
```

**A is decisive.** A per-frame snapshot of keyboard state would have restored the `1` on the
next frame, with the key still down. It did not, fifteen times. **The game writes this byte
when the key's state changes and at no other time**, which explains both halves of `EXP-005`
at once: a written level persists because nothing rewrites levels, and nothing responds
because what is consumed is the change.

### The confound, quantified

| | NEW bytes | the REVERSAL |
|---|---:|---:|
| `EXP-004`, **unfocused** | 319 | 311 |
| `EXP-006`, **focused** | **17,584** | **31** |

Same instrument, same game, same keys. Area id `12` → `306`; the save buffer went from
all-zero to populated.

> **`EXP-004`'s symmetry check was right both times.** 319 against 311 is noise measuring
> itself — the instrument said so and the instrument was believed. **The error was in the
> variable list**, not the measurement: foreground was never in it, across two experiments and
> four negatives.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**What screen the game reached.** Area id `306` and a populated save buffer say it left the
title. **Nothing here says what it is showing.** `EW-1`.

**That the harness's own verdict is trustworthy.** `ffxii_runtime.py state` still printed
`TITLE` after the game had plainly moved, because the verdict keys on the entity free list and
a menu spawns no entities. **The indicator is too coarse and is now recorded as such** rather
than quietly relied on.

**Which `SendInput` form works.** Virtual-key and scan-code were sent together on purpose:
`EXP-004` tested them separately and got two negatives, and which one works is a later
question than whether either does.

**Bookkeeping:** `F-2a` was still labelled *now highest leverage* on the frontier while
`globals_index.py` had already shipped — `global_refs` holds **164,489 rows over 35,879
globals** and cited coverage is **1,397 of 35,879 = 3.89 %**, not the 3.16 % the entry quoted.
Marked done with the real numbers.

### Reference environment

Launched by the harness, closed by the harness, exit verified. The debugger was detached and
the game resumed before any further measurement. **No file in the install was touched**; the
only writes were to process memory, each restored and verified, and each announced as
instrumentation-induced.

## 2026-09-08 — the harness could change the screen and not know which screen

**Block:** `EW-1`. `INTEGRATION` is `NOT COVERED` for all six pilots; `ES-1` is the only route
to it; and `ES-1` could not navigate deliberately while `state` reported `TITLE` after
`EXP-006` had plainly moved the game. **The missing capability was not input — it was sight.**
[`EXP-007`](../_experiments/EXP-007-navigating-the-front-end.md).

### The instrument, and the two traps it hit

| | result |
|---|---|
| `PrintWindow` + `PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT` | **93.8 % one colour, black** — a Direct3D swap chain does not draw itself through GDI |
| screen `BitBlt` of the window rect | a real image |

**The tool reports which path produced the image and how flat the result is**, so *“the screen
is black”* and *“the capture failed”* are distinguishable. The blank was rejected rather than
written out as a photograph.

> **The first capture photographed a neighbouring window.** The process was DPI-unaware, so
> `GetWindowRect` returned **logical** coordinates while the screen DC is in **physical**
> pixels. The window is **1938 × 1089**, not the 1292 × 726 every earlier tool had recorded.
> **Every number the tool printed was self-consistent; only the image caught it.**

### `ES-1` — done

Cold launch, nobody at the keyboard: main menu photographed → one `Down` moved the cursor
**Load Game → Trial Mode** → `Up` → `Circle` → *“Checking save data…”* → **six save files**
→ `Circle` → **Vaan, Dalmasca Estersand, HP 103/103**. [the loaded save](../_experiments/evidence/EXP-007-03-loaded-estersand.png).

### The audit finding: the harness's verdict was wrong, not coarse

`state` said `TITLE` with a party member rendered. **Two independent errors:**

1. **`0215FDA0` is the SCRIPT VM's entity-name table**, not a general entity table — nothing
   puts a slot on it because the world has bodies in it. **A script-VM fact was being read as
   a world fact**, which is the ownership-by-convenience mistake the charter forbids, made by
   a tool rather than a document.
2. **“on the free list” and “has content” are independent.** With a map loaded, all 128 records
   are still linked **and** all 128 carry a populated body. The free list was never evidence
   about the world at all.

```text
just launched   area id  -1   save buffer empty       -> UNKNOWN   (no baseline; it says so)
front-end       area id  12   save buffer empty       -> MENU
save loaded     area id 227   save buffer populated   -> IN-WORLD
```

**Controlled in both directions**: closed, relaunched, back through an honest `UNKNOWN` while
the front-end initialised, then `MENU`. A verdict that could only say `IN-WORLD` would have
been as wrong as the one it replaced. The verdict now **refuses to name a screen** and says
which tool can.

### Two questions moved without being chased

**`ER-1`, open half answered.** The script-entity table is populated **at map load** — 0 of 128
bodies at the menu, **128 of 128** in-world — not lazily when a script first names something.
`+0x1A` holds the slot index, `+0x16` a constant `0x006D` across the three records read.
**Naming the rest from three records was refused.**

**`EQ-1` narrowed.** st2e groups: **0** just after launch, **16** at the front-end, **still
16** with a map loaded. Loading a map filled none. One map and one save — narrowed, not
closed, and *“merely unloaded at the title”* is now the weaker reading.

### A contradiction inside a row this project already wrote

`ER-1` records *“`+0x00` = `prev`, `+0x08` = `next`, head at slot 0”*. The live read:

```text
slot 0   +0x00 = 0215FDE0 (slot 1)   +0x08 = 0
slot 1   +0x00 = 0215FE20 (slot 2)   +0x08 = 0215FDA0 (slot 0)
```

**`+0x00` points at the next-higher slot and `+0x08` at the next-lower; slot 0's `+0x08` is
null.** With the head at slot 0 those labels are backwards. **The naming was not flipped** —
which end the allocator pops was not read, and that is what decides it. The address-ordered
fact is recorded label-free and the naming is filed as `EW-3`.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**What area id 227 means.** It is the id present when this save is loaded. **One sample is not
a mapping**, and no attempt was made to name ids to places.

**Anything about the save files.** They were listed by the game and one was loaded. **No save
file was opened, parsed or modified by any tool here.**

**That the navigation route is robust.** It worked once, with fixed delays, from a known
cursor position. A reusable route needs the screen **recognised** rather than assumed — now
possible, not done.

### Reference environment

Launched, driven and closed by the harness; closed again after the control relaunch, exit
verified both times. **No process memory was written in this block at all** — every tool used
was read-only on the game, and the only writes anywhere were pixels on the desktop.

## 2026-09-08 — the game was asked what fills its own table, and it answered in four bytes

**Block:** three of the five pilot contracts carry an explicit *“any runtime observation —
none exists”* row, and those rows are what block `CONTRACT`. With `ES-1` done they became
cheap. `field_music` was taken first: **6 of 7 on `CONTRACT`, the closest pilot to the gate**,
and its only open question (`DG-1`) answerable by a memory read. [`EXP-008`](../_experiments/EXP-008-the-real-music-table.md).

### `DG-1`, answered

```text
[0x02B5E0D0]  ->  0x653B0FC0
  +0x00   4D 55 53 30      "MUS0"
  +0x04   1F 05 00 00      max field id = 1311
  +0x08   11 absolute page addresses
```

**A four-character format tag the static reading never mentioned** — because the function
does not check it, so no amount of reading `003EAA70` would ever have produced it. The header
is self-consistent in a way that is not coincidence: `⌈1312/128⌉ = 11`, and there are exactly
11 page pointers.

> The prior `DG-1` note traced the buffer to an allocator and named `0032E620` as the filler,
> unread. **That is neither confirmed nor needed now** — the content is read directly, and the
> row says so rather than quietly inheriting an unverified attribution.

### A prediction from a crash, confirmed in the real data

**The format has no chain terminator.** `diff_field_music.py` learned this by generating
synthetic tables that produced **access violations rather than test failures**, and wrote down
the consequence: the shipped data must end every page with a run whose start is above every
field id that can reach it.

**All 11 pages do.** 316 runs, 263 naming a track, no empty pages, and the whole table parses
cleanly under the documented format. **A property inferred from a bug in invented data,
observed in the real thing.**

### The differential, over the game's own data

```text
cases            : 400 over THE GAME'S OWN TABLE
  resolved a track: 112      resolved -1: 288      distinct tracks: 35
mismatches       : 0
no-state check   : 80 of 400 cases re-read the whole table image and the table
                   pointer afterwards; 0 showed ANY byte changed
```

**`CONTRACT` is `COVERED` for `field_music` — 8 of 8.** The first pilot to cover a dimension
that was `NOT COVERED` for all six one block ago. Both changed rows were measured, not
argued: *“what fills the table”* is now the run's **input**, and *“writes no state”* is checked
by re-reading every page the function can address.

### A driver bug only real data could find

```text
asked VirtualAlloc for 653B0FC0  ->  got 653B0000  ->  refused
```

**`VirtualAlloc` rounds a reservation down to the 64 KB allocation granularity.** Every
synthetic table had been placed at `0x30000000` — a round address — so the driver's check had
never been tested against an unaligned base. **The refusal was right and its reasoning was too
narrow:** the requirement is that the *image bytes* land at the base, not that the
*allocation* start there. It now reserves the containing granule, copies at the offset, and
asserts the bytes are where they must be.

> **It failed loudly**, which is why this cost one rebuild rather than a debugging session. A
> driver that had silently mapped elsewhere would have compared the reconstruction against
> garbage and reported mismatches that meant nothing.

### A failed search that produced a better instrument

The block began by hunting the **menu cursor index** in memory, to make front-end navigation
deterministic. Method: three snapshots one row apart, keep bytes that stepped `n, n+1, n+2`.

| stage | result |
|---|---|
| naive diff | 28 candidates |
| **control: same intervals, no key pressed** | 5 of them still stepped — clocks, excluded |
| **reversal: press `Up` instead of `Down`** | **every survivor still incremented** |

**A cursor decrements on `Up`. None did.** So the menu cursor is **not in the four scanned
static regions** — unsurprising for a heap-allocated UI object, and an honest negative.

**The survivors were something better:** five bytes that advance by **exactly** the number of
presses delivered — `01FD36B4`, `02EAD4C4`, `02EAD5A4`, `02EAD638`, `02EAD6C4`. Validated
against press counts of **1, 4, 2 and 7**, with **two zero-press controls that moved 0**. That
is a numeric input-arrival check, far cheaper than a screenshot, and it exists because the
reversal test was run rather than assumed.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**`INTEGRATION`.** [The parity standard](../../../Reconstruction/PARITY-STANDARD.md) §3 asks for the game's **caller** *and* its **inputs**.
This has the inputs. The caller is a test driver, and the declaration now says exactly that
instead of the old reason (*“tables here are synthetic”*), which is no longer true.

**That the right music plays.** 35 distinct track ids were resolved from real data. **No track
id was mapped to a piece of music and no audio was observed.**

**That “writes no state” means the body has no stores.** What is proven is that nothing was
written to the pages the function can address; a store outside them would have faulted and
been reported as an emulation error.

**What the five counters count.** They advance one per press and not with time. Whether they
are an input-event counter or something downstream of one is **not established**.

### Reference environment

Launched and closed by the harness, exit verified. **Read-only throughout** — no process
memory was written in this block.

### Gates

`check_links` · `check_consistency` · `check_questions` · `check_denominators` ·
`verify_doc_addresses` · `ADDRESS-INDEX.md` regenerated · `parity_status.py` 0 problems.

## 2026-09-08 — writing the missing contract disproved the page it was written from

**Block:** category switch, after three consecutive runtime blocks. Charter §4 asks for
behavioural contracts for subsystems already close to readiness, and **`name_registry` was
the only pilot of six with no contract at all** — so its `CONTRACT` dimension could not be
scored, only excused, while being the most ready subsystem in the tree (`IMPLEMENTED`,
`DIFFERENTIAL TESTED`). [the input name registry contract](../15-Input/Input-Name-Registry/CONTRACT-input-name-registry.md).

### The audit finding

The system document opens: *“Two **byte-identical** 132-byte functions — `00879570` and
`00876C80`”*. **Four of the 132 bytes differ**, in two adjacent pairs. Resolved with capstone,
never by hand:

```text
00879570  +29   mov rbx, [rip + 0x26407EC]   -> 02EB9D80
          +106  mov [rip + 0x264079F], r11   -> 02EB9D80
00876C80  +29   mov rbx, [rip + 0x2641714]   -> 02EB83B8
          +106  mov [rip + 0x26416C7], r11   -> 02EB83B8
```

**Each names its own list head, once to read and once to write.** Two independent instruments
agree: `globals_index.py` reports **exactly one writer** for each head — `02EB9D80` 1 writer /
148 readers, `02EB83B8` 1 writer / 102 readers — and the single write it finds is the store at
`+106`.

> **The claim was re-derived from the binary, not softened.** And the corrected version is
> *stronger* than the wrong one: *identical apart from the two displacements that select the
> registry* explains how one routine serves two lists, which **byte-identical could not** —
> byte-identical functions cannot address different globals.

### The subsystem turned out to be five functions, not one

| channel | key | size | differing bytes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `008794F0` | `00876C00` | 122 | 8 |
| **`00879570`** | **`00876C80`** | **132** | **4** |
| `00879600` | `00876D10` | 103 | 2 |
| `00879670` | `00876D80` | 222 | 8 |
| `00879760` | `00876E60` | 87 | 2 |

**Every difference is a pair of adjacent bytes** — displacement low halves, the same shape as
the insert's. *(Enumeration method, which `FULL-SUBSYSTEM` requires to be stated: the readers
of each head from `globals_index.py`, intersected with the functions inside the two address
runs.)*

`FULL-SUBSYSTEM` for this pilot is therefore **1 of 5 entry points**, a measured gap rather
than the vague *“lookup and teardown are not covered”* it carried before. **What the other

statically — **the same walk settles the registration order and the completeness question at

97 would be a runtime registration. `EW-5`.

> **It was deliberately not done in this block.** The guard is max three consecutive blocks in

## 2026-09-08 — the format's vocabulary was in BSS, and the rule about `SizeOfRawData` earned its keep

**Block:** charter §29, the highest-ranked item once the §38 first-actions are done. `002432B0` has **108 call sites** and its nine item types were sized, constructed and
**unnamed** — `EV-1`. [a typed list, measured once and built in one allocation](../02-Resource-And-Asset-Pipeline/a-typed-list-measured-once-and-built-in-one-allocation.md) §5c.

### Types 2 and 9: a sprite out of a named UI atlas

```text
item +0x0C (u16)  ->  002A0060
  [ctx+8] -> arena -> 16-BYTE name records, record = base + id*16
      +0x00..+0x0D  the atlas NAME, inline
      +0x0E         1 once resolved
      +0x0F         the registry slot it resolved to
  cached?  ->  RE-COMPARE the slot's name against the record's, and only
               re-look-up when it no longer matches
```

> **The cache is checked, not trusted** — and it is checked with the *same inlined `movzx`/`movzx`
> comparison the input name registry uses*, two subsystems apart. That idiom is now the
> project's most reliable fingerprint for a string compare that no xref will find.

### The registry, and the trap that was avoided

```text
0024A5F0(i)     ->  0208F580 + i * 0x48
0024A610(name)  ->  linear scan, 64 slots, stride 0x48
                    +0x00  name, inline    +0x20  the atlas object
                    +0x38  bit 0x20 = OCCUPIED
```

**`0208F580` is past `.data`'s raw content.** Reading it from the shipped file returns the
*following section's bytes* — which would have produced a table of confident, invented names.
The tool checked `SizeOfRawData` rather than the virtual range, reported
**“NOT BACKED BY RAW DATA — the table is BSS and is filled at runtime”**, and the answer had
to come from a running game.

> **That standing rule exists because this project got it wrong once.** This is the first
> block where following it changed the answer from a fabrication to a question.

**21 of 64 slots occupied at the front-end:** `buttonicon` `bt_win_0_c` `cm_win_c`
`cursol_4_p` `keyboard` `battle_4_c` `targetline_p` `s_font_c` `battle_4_p` `mini_face_c`
`partytop_4_c` `partytop_8_c` `party_grd_2` `icons_c` `extra_c` `lic_4_c` `Loca_8_c`
`LocaBack_c` `w_line01` `title_logo` `shape`.

### The sub-image lookup — read from code, then validated live

```text
page  = u16[T + 0x14 + (code >> 8) * 2]
entry = u16[T + 0x14 + (page + (code & 0xFF)) * 2]
rec   = T + u16[T + 0x10] + entry * 8            T = atlas[+0x20] + 0x30
```

Walked against `buttonicon`, `s_font_c` and `title_logo` in a live process and it resolves in
all three. **Byte 7 of the record is a default the authored data can decline**: item `+0x12`
of `0xFF` takes `rec[7]`, otherwise the authored byte wins.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**The 8-byte record's fields.** The first two `u16`s differ per atlas — `7A 00 64 00` for
`buttonicon` code 0 — and **nothing read says what they are.** Calling them a UV rect would be
a guess dressed as a finding.

**Type 7.** It begins exactly as types 2/9 do, then repeats the whole name resolution on a
second `u16` guarded by `cmp ebp, 0xFFFF` (**`0xFFFF` = no second atlas**), and sets bit
`0x2000000` in the node. **Its remaining ~700 bytes are unread**, so it is recorded as
**PARTIAL** rather than named from two atlas references.

**The ledger's tag on `0029F130`** reads `Presentation.Rendering.ShaderMaterial`. **It was not
used.** A ledger tag is a claim, not a mechanism, and nothing read here supports or refutes
it.

**Whether `_c` and `_p` mean anything.** Twelve of the 21 names carry one suffix or the other.
**No reading was attempted**, because a plausible expansion is not evidence.

### `EW-6` — a lookup that cannot report failure

`0024A610` ends `xor eax, eax / ret` when the scan exhausts, and `mov eax, r10d / ret` on a
match — with `r10d` starting at 0. **“Not found” and “matched slot 0” are the same answer**,
and the caller stores it as the cached handle and dereferences it, so **an absent name
resolves to whatever occupies slot 0** rather than failing. Read from the code; **whether any
authored name is ever absent is not established**, so it is filed as a latent property, not a
bug.

### New tool

`disasm_fn.py` — disassembles a function and **resolves every RIP-relative target with the
tool**, annotating string and possible-vtable destinations and reading only within
`SizeOfRawData`. Every previous block wrote that arithmetic inline; it exists once now.

### Reference environment

Launched and closed by the harness, exit verified. **Read-only** — no process memory written.

## 2026-09-08 — the game became the oracle, and it agreed node for node

**Block:** `EW-5`. `INTEGRATION` is `NOT COVERED` for all six pilots and is the universal
blocker on certification; `name_registry`'s contract had named the exact experiment that would
move it, one block earlier, and deliberately not run it. [the input name registry contract](../15-Input/Input-Name-Registry/CONTRACT-input-name-registry.md) §13.

### One walk, two unresolved items

```text
PInputChannelSemantic   143 nodes   Empty=0 first, then STRICTLY DESCENDING by value
                                    only ties: values 11..26 -- the 16 alias groups
                                    113 distinct values across 143 entries
PInputKeySemantic        97 nodes   Empty=0 first, then strictly descending, no ties
```

The list is **push-front**, so the chain preserves the order it was built in and reversing it
recovers the CRT static-initialiser order — which no static read can reach.

**Completeness:** against the 240 names recovered statically, **0 live-only and 0 static-only**,
both registries. Nothing is registered at runtime in the observed state, and the static recovery
was complete. Both §14 items resolved.

> **The live order reproduced the alias grouping independently.** The document derived 16 alias
> groups from the *names*; the live chain shows the only places consecutive registrations share
> a value are **exactly 11..26**. Two derivations from different evidence, agreeing.

### The reconstruction against the running game

```text
inputs  the game's own nodes, read live, at their own addresses
order   the game's own registration order, recovered by reversing the live chain
oracle  THE GAME'S OWN LIST, walked from the head in the same process

PInputChannelSemantic   OK x143   0 of 143 nodes differ
PInputKeySemantic       OK x97    0 of  97 nodes differ
```

Every earlier differential in this tree compared the reconstruction against **the shipped bytes
under emulation** — the same static artifact the reconstruction came from, executed rather than
read. **This compares it against a data structure the running game built.**

It also retired an inherited claim: §16 had recorded `00876C80` as *“inherited, not tested”*
because only `00879570` is emulated. The **key** registry's live 97-node list is now rebuilt node
for node, so the two instances agree on a result as well as on their bytes.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**`INTEGRATION` coverage.** §3 asks for the game's **caller** *and* the game's **inputs**. The
inputs and the oracle are the game's; **the caller is not** — the initialiser sequence is never
executed, only its order recovered and its result compared. **A reconstruction that inserted
correctly but was never invoked would look identical here**, and the declaration says so.

**That 143 and 97 are complete in every state.** They are complete **at the front-end**, which is
where the walk was taken. A registration during a later load would not have been seen.

**Why the order descends.** It is CRT link order and the observation is that it descends by
value; **nothing here explains why the linker emitted it that way**, and a plausible story would
be a story.

`PARITY-STATUS.md` read *“across the **five** pilots that have a contract”* — one block after the
sixth contract was written. The sentence was a literal in `parity_status.py`. **It is now
