## 2026-09-08 — the blocker under everything, and what removing it cost

**Block:** `EW-2`. `INTEGRATION` is `NOT COVERED` for all six pilots; its missing half is always
*“the game's caller”*; and knowing whether a function is called at all needs a breakpoint. The
dbgeng-based MCP server **froze the game**, so every causality experiment was blocked behind one
broken instrument. [`RUNTIME-RESEARCH.md`](RUNTIME-RESEARCH.md) §8d.

### The fix was to stop debugging someone else's engine

`hwbp.py` drives the Win32 debug API directly — `DebugActiveProcess`, a
`WaitForDebugEvent`/`ContinueDebugEvent` loop, `DebugActiveProcessStop` — and sets **hardware**
breakpoints in the **DR registers of every thread**.

> **No code byte is modified.** An `INT3` patch would be a write into the reference environment;
> a debug register is not, and it also survives any code the game checksums. §13 of the runtime
> directive asks for exactly this discipline.

```text
target CPU while attached : 5.062 s over 6.0 s wall   IT KEPT RUNNING
threads armed             : 105
control 0020E600          : 133,679 hits, with arguments
```

**Two guards are built in, both earned from earlier failures in this session.** It samples the
target's **CPU time** before, during and after, so a frozen target is reported as *frozen*
rather than as *quiet* — which is precisely what `EW-2` was and what cost a block to notice. And
`--control` is not optional in spirit: **without a control that fires, the run declares the
instrument unproven and refuses to let a zero stand as a negative.**

### The cost, and it is a real one

```text
BEFORE attach        3 of 3 presses counted
DURING the session   0 of 3
AFTER detach         0 of 3
```

**Attaching permanently disables the game's input**, and it is the **attach** that does it, not
the detach. The game runs normally throughout — 6.7 CPU seconds over 8.1 s wall, control firing
127,578 times. **Alive, rendering, and deaf.**

> This was found the honest way: a navigation that had worked twice suddenly did nothing, and
> **the keypress counter discovered two blocks ago said input was not arriving at all** rather
> than arriving and being ignored. The before/during/after control was then run deliberately.
> **A tool built for one purpose diagnosed a different instrument's side effect.**

**Operating rule, now in the tool's own banner:** *establish the state first, attach second, and
accept that the state cannot be changed afterwards.*

### What it measured on its first day

| target | state | hits in 8 s | control |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `003EAA70` `FieldMusic_Select` | front-end | **0** | 133,679 |
| `003EAA70` `FieldMusic_Select` | **in-world, save loaded** | **0** | 127,578 |
| `00265270` `FieldData_GetVariable0` | in-world | **114,204** | 127,578 |

**Field music is not selected per frame.** Eight seconds standing in Dalmasca Estersand, with a
control firing 127,578 times beside it, and `FieldMusic_Select` is **never called**. It is
**event-driven** — a behavioural fact no amount of reading `003EAA70` produces, and a *real*
negative because the instrument was proven positive in the same run.

**And the function `diff_field_music.py` stubs as its progress source is one of the hottest in
the game** — `FieldData_GetVariable0`, 114,204 calls in eight seconds. The harness treats it as a
field-music detail; it is plainly general.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**Why attaching kills input.** Alive-but-deaf fits an anti-tamper response and an
operating-system input-queue effect equally well, and **nothing here separates them**. `EW-7`.

**That `FieldMusic_Select` is called on a field change.** What is measured is that it is **not**
called while standing still. *“Presumably on a field change”* is the obvious reading and it was
**not tested** — testing it needs a field change, a field change needs input, and input dies on
attach. The experiment is **defined and blocked**, which is where it is recorded.

**`INTEGRATION` coverage for anything.** Nothing moved on that dimension this block. What moved
is that its blocking experiment now has an instrument and a named obstacle instead of no
instrument at all.

### Reference environment

Launched and closed by the harness four times, exit verified each time. **No process memory was
written**; the only target state changed was the debug registers, cleared on every exit path,
and `DebugSetProcessKillOnExit(FALSE)` was set first so that losing the tool could not kill the
game. **The input side effect is a change to the reference environment and is recorded as one** —
the remedy is a relaunch, and it is stated in the tool.

**CORRECTED 2026-09-10 (ASTRA):** the pre-attach protection assertion above is withdrawn.
EXP-016 records that call failing with error 6. [EXP-017](../_experiments/EXP-017-debugger-exit-policy.md)
reproduces target death under the old ordering on a disposable process and survival
after checked post-attach setup. Shared hwbp now checks the supported order. This
does not certify armed-game liveness or protect the attach-to-policy interval.

## 2026-09-08 — a positive control proves the instrument can see, not that it left the program alone

**Block:** `EW-7`, filed one block earlier as *“why does attaching any debugger permanently
disable the game's input”*. **The premise was wrong, and disproving it retracted a published
finding with it.** [`RUNTIME-RESEARCH.md`](RUNTIME-RESEARCH.md) §8d.

### The discriminator that should have been run first

The original test conflated two things: the **debug attach** and **writing debug registers on
105 threads**. Separating them needs one control — attach, service every debug event, program
nothing:

| run | breakpoints armed | input | `003EAA70` hits |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `--no-arm` | none (event loop only) | **3 of 3** | — |
| cold | `003EAA70` alone, at the front-end | **3 of 3** | 0 |
| hot | `0020E600` alone (255,944 hits / 12 s) | **0 of 3** | — |
| three at once, in-world | `003EAA70` + `00265270` + `0020E600` | not measured | **0** |
| **alone, in-world** | **`003EAA70` only** | worked during navigation | **1,130,002** |

**Attaching does nothing.** It is the **hit rate**: a breakpoint firing ~21,000 times a second
starves the game; one that never fires costs nothing measurable.

### The retraction

The previous block recorded, as a headline finding: *“Field music is not selected per frame — 0
hits in eight seconds in-world, beside a control firing 127,578 times.”* **Two of the three
armed breakpoints in that run were hot.** Armed **alone**, in the same state, `003EAA70` fires
**1,130,002 times in 75 seconds** — roughly 15,000 a second. It is one of the hottest functions
in the game once a map is loaded.

> **The rule this adds.** The project already required a positive control before any negative.
> That control **did** fire — 127,578 times — and the negative was still false. **A positive
> control proves the instrument can SEE. It does not prove the instrument left the program
> ALONE.** A perturbing instrument satisfies every existing guard and still lies.
>
> **Arm the target alone. Take the control in its own run.** Both are now in the tool's banner
> and its docstring.

### What replaced the retracted claim

`003EAA70` is called continuously while a map is loaded, and **every printed sample carried
`rcx = 0xE3 = 227`** — exactly the area id observed for that save. That is `INTEGRATION`'s
missing half coming into view: **the caller the game actually uses, and the input it actually
supplies.**

**Confidence: HIGH, not PROVEN.** Only five samples were printed; the run captured 40 and the
tool shows five. **No claim is made that `rcx` is the field id in general**, only that these
samples carried the area id, and that the contract independently says the first argument is the
field id.

### The reference environment was lost once, and it was my doing

A bare `DebugActiveProcess` with **no event loop** freezes the target — which is precisely what
the dbgeng server had been doing — and the experiment hung against a frozen game. Killing the
stuck debugger **took the game process with it**, despite `DebugSetProcessKillOnExit(FALSE)`.

**Follow-up 2026-09-10 (ASTRA):** the call's presence did not establish success.
[EXP-017](../_experiments/EXP-017-debugger-exit-policy.md) demonstrates a failing
pre-attach call and debugger-loss termination in a disposable control. The historical
incident has no policy API receipt, so its precise cause remains unproven.

**The install was verified immediately afterwards: `CLEAN`, hash matching authority.** Only the
process died; no file was touched. **Never attach without an event loop** — recorded here and in
the tool.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**That `rcx` is always the field id.** Five samples in one area. The area id and the field id
agreeing at 227 is a strong coincidence and **not a demonstration**; a second area would settle
it and was not visited.

**`INTEGRATION` coverage.** Still `NOT COVERED` for all six pilots. What changed is that
`field_music`'s caller has now been **seen**, with an argument, which is the first time any
pilot's real caller has been observed at all.

**Why a hot breakpoint stops other code running.** The obvious reading is starvation — the
process spends its time round-tripping through the debugger — but **nothing here measures
that**, and 60.9 CPU seconds over 75 s wall says the process was busy, not idle.

## 2026-09-08 — amending the rule that failed, then reading the four functions nobody had

**Block:** category switch after three runtime blocks. Two things belonged in it.

### 1. The evidence standard was wrong and is amended

The standing rule — *“any claim of the form ‘X is not present’ must be accompanied by a positive
control”* — was **fully satisfied** by the finding retracted last block. The control fired
**127,578 times**. The negative was still false, because two other breakpoints in the same run
were firing tens of thousands of times a second and **the program stopped executing the path
being measured**.

> **A positive control proves the instrument can SEE. It does not prove the instrument left the
> program ALONE.**

[`EVIDENCE-STANDARD.md`](EVIDENCE-STANDARD.md) now requires, of any instrument that can change behaviour — a breakpoint, hook,
patch, write or injected DLL — three further things: **run it with the measured target alone**,
**report its own load**, and **re-take any negative at a lower load** before writing it down. A
row was added to the failure-mode table beside the other twelve.

**Nothing already in that document would have caught this.** A perturbing instrument satisfies
every other guard there and still lies — which is the argument for a new rule rather than a
footnote on an old one.

### 2. `EW-4` — the other four functions per registry

| channel | key | size | what it is |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `008794F0` | `00876C00` | 122 | **scalar deleting destructor** — installs the vtable, unlinks the node by patching the predecessor's link, then `operator delete(this, 0x20)` when the low bit of arg 2 is set |
| `00879570` | `00876C80` | 132 | the insert |
| `00879600` | `00876D10` | 103 | **find by name, out-parameter** — writes the node or `NULL`, returns **`0x13`** when absent |
| `00879670` | `00876D80` | 222 | **enumerate into a flat array** — counts the list, reallocates `count * 8` only when the count differs, then writes each node pointer in order |
| `00879760` | `00876E60` | 87 | **find by name, pointer-returning** — no status code |

**Two facts the insert could never have shown, and neither was guessed.**

**The return-code family has a fourth member.** `0x00` OK, `0x11` NULL_KEY, `0x12` DUPLICATE,
**`0x13` NOT_FOUND** — and the insert has no path that returns `0x13`. A contract written from
one function of five recorded three of the four codes and had no way to know it.

**The enumerator's count field carries an ownership bit.** Before freeing the previous array it
tests **bit 31 of the stored count** (`shr eax,0x1F / not al / test al,1`) and frees only when
that bit is clear — so a caller can hand in a **borrowed** array by setting the high bit and it
is refilled rather than freed. That is a real API contract hiding in a sign bit.

### The pairing is verified, not inherited

Each key-side function was checked with the tool to reference **its own** head `02EB83B8`, and
`00876C00` installs vtable `01CD89D8` — the `PInputKeySemantic` descriptor, matching
`008794F0`'s `01CD9908` for the channel side. The earlier claim rested on a byte-difference
pattern; it now rests on resolved targets.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**That any of the four is reconstructed.** None is. `FULL-SUBSYSTEM` moves from *“1 of 5
reconstructed, the other four unread”* to *“**5 of 5 identified, 1 of 5 reconstructed**”* — an
understanding gap became a reimplementation gap, and the dimension is still `NOT COVERED`.

**Who calls the four.** The destructor's caller is the `atexit` registration already documented;
**the callers of the two finds and the enumerator were not censused**, and a lookup with no
callers would change what this subsystem means.

**What the enumerator is for.** It flattens the registry into an indexable array. **Nothing read
says who wants one**, and the obvious guess — a settings UI listing bindable names — is a guess.

## 2026-09-08 — a recording stub caught my own reading of the disassembly

**Block:** the parity table now measures `CONTRACT`, and most pilots score low because their
harnesses **declare** claims they never exercise. `widget_construct` was 1 of 6 and
`quality_preset` 2 of 7, each with one specific, cheap, offline gap. Both are closed.

### `widget_construct` — and the finding that was not planned

The harness stubbed every proc as a bare `ret` and said so: *“The construct message is NOT
compared.”* It is now a **recording stub** — `mov [scratch], rcx` / `mov [scratch+8], rdx` /
`inc dword [scratch+16]` / `ret` — so the harness sees what the original hands its proc.

**The reconstruction had to be extended to state what it would send**, because a differential
test has no proc to call. Writing that required knowing the message, so I read it out of
`0024660A`:

```text
0024660A  mov dword [rsp+0x20], 1        the id
00246615  xorps xmm0, xmm0
00246620  movdqu [rsp+0x28], xmm0        <- read as “zero +0x08..+0x17”
00246730  mov eax, [rsi+0x10]            <- read as “ZERO-EXTENDED dword”
00246733  mov [rsp+0x30], rax
00246748  call rax                       rcx = the object, rdx = &msg
```

**The first run reported 320 message mismatches out of 320.**

```text
original        00000001 00000000 1122334455667788 99AABBCCDDEEFF00
reconstruction  00000001 00000000 0000000000000000 00000000DDEEFF00
```

> **Both halves are full 64-bit copies of the caller's argument qwords.** The `movdqu` reading
> was wrong and so was the zero-extension. **The reconstruction was corrected from the recorded
> bytes, not from a better re-reading of the disassembly** — which is precisely the argument for
> comparing a message instead of describing one.

**And the payload is now randomised per case**, so a reconstruction that hardcoded
`1122334455667788` and `99AABBCCDDEEFF00` — the constants the harness used to write — would
fail. Final run: **320 of 320, 0 message mismatches, exactly one proc call per construction.**

### `quality_preset` — the bytes that must not move

The compared window stopped at `0x7C`, the 31 settings. The contract claims **`+0x554` is
unwritten by config code** and rated it `VERY HIGH` on a displacement scan. Both sides now get
the whole **`0x65C`** object, **poisoned byte by byte** before the call, compared by hash:

```text
bytes compared                                            : 0x65C per case
bytes changed beyond the settings, summed over 600 cases  : 0
full-object mismatches                                    : 0
```

`STRUCTURAL` for this pilot now compares the **1,504 bytes that must stay unchanged**, not just
the 124 that move — which is what §3 of the parity standard actually asks for.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**That `+0x554` is unwritten by ALL config code.** The claim's wording covers the subsystem; the
measurement covers **`001DE4F0`**. One differential on one entry point cannot reach the rest, and
the map row says so rather than quietly taking credit for the broader claim.

**That the reconstruction SENDS the message.** It states what it would send. There is no proc to
call in a test, and pretending otherwise would be a fiction the harness then compares against
itself.

**That the message's two payload qwords are `args[+0x08]` and `args[+0x10]` for reasons the
code explains.** They are copied verbatim; **what they mean is not read**.

### Movement

**27 of 49**. Both harnesses re-run green: widget 320 cases 0 mismatches, quality_preset 600
cases 0 mismatches.

## 2026-09-08 — auditing the weakest pilot's assertions, and reading a dispatch whole

**Block:** `angle_wrap` scored **1 of 7** testable contract claims, the worst of the six. Three
of the unexercised ones were mechanically checkable, and **two are static assertions about
function bodies** — the exact shape of claim that turned out wrong for the input name registry
two blocks ago, where *byte-identical* meant four differing bytes. So this was an audit first.

### The instrument

`fn_audit.py`, new:

| mode | what it does |
|---|---|
| `--compare A:LEN B:LEN` | **normalised** instruction diff — RIP operands replaced by their **resolved absolute target**, branch targets made **relative to the entry**, and nothing else touched, so two bodies referencing *different* globals still differ |
| `--fn A:LEN --touches REG` | capstone's **`regs_access`**, which reports **implicit** reads and writes — `push r8`, `xor r8d,r8d`, a `div`'s implicit `rdx` |

> **Reading operand text with a regular expression would miss every implicit touch**, and a
> claim of the form *“never touches this register”* is exactly where that matters. The tool
> exists because the cheap version of it would produce a confident false negative.

### Both claims hold

```text
the two facing variants  : 29 and 29 instructions, 1 differing
    [12]  xor r8d, r8d              |  mov r8d, 1
0026B6A0 touching r8     : 0 of 30 instructions
CONTROL, touching rcx    : 6 instructions
```

**The control is not decoration.** Last block established that a positive control proves only
that the instrument can see; here it is the whole defence against a register-family bug making
*“never touched”* free. **Both checks now run inside the harness on every invocation**, so the
claims are exercised rather than inherited from a reading done once.

### The kind dispatch, read whole

The harness pinned kind 3 and the map called the claim `PARTIAL`. Running the other arms first
**faulted** — which was itself the finding: they are not equivalent code paths.

```text
ecx = (actor[+3] >> 5) - 1
  kind 1  ->  mov r8d,1 ; JMP 0026B6A0        the r8 the callee never reads
  kind 2  ->  ret                             nothing at all
  kind 3  ->  [[actor+0xB8]+0xF0]+0x34 = the wrapped angle
```

**Kind 2 is a no-op.** **Kind 1 leaves through a tail jump** carrying the very argument
`0026B6A0` never reads — which ties the two claims together: the dispatch bothers to set `r8`
for a callee that ignores it. Only kind 3 writes the record, and the run reports exactly that:
kinds 1 and 2 match kind 3's observable on **none** of the cases.

Kind 1 could only be run by mapping `0026B6A0`. **It is the real callee at its real address,
executed** — not a stub — so nothing about the arm is faked.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**That the dispatch claim is fully exercised.** It names **both** `0026B6A0` and `0026C090`.
`0026C090`'s three arms all run; `0026B6A0`'s own dispatch is **executed but not separately
driven**. That is **3 of the 6 function-by-kind combinations**, and the row stays `PARTIAL`
rather than being promoted on the strength of the half that improved.

**What kind 1 and kind 2 are for.** The code says one tail-jumps and the other returns.
**Nothing read says which actors are which kind**, or why a kind would want the no-op.

**That the r8 result generalises.** It is `0026B6A0`'s 120 bytes. A callee it reaches could
read `r8`; the claim, and the check, are about this body.

### Movement

`angle_wrap` **1 → 3 of 7**. Tree-wide contract coverage **29 of 50**. The harness re-runs
green: both shipped forms agree with the reconstruction over 4,140 float bit patterns.

`check_links` · `check_consistency` · `check_questions` · `check_denominators` ·
`verify_doc_addresses` · `ADDRESS-INDEX.md` regenerated · `parity_status.py` 0 problems.

## 2026-09-08 — `EN-1`: stop fitting the outputs, read the arithmetic, keep the apparatus

**Block:** `EN-1` was the sharpest unknown in the ledger — a formula that fitted **168
combinations with zero disagreements** on one argument and failed on **6 of 80** with two, the
deviations already quantified as `+1`, `+2` and once `+12`. **A model known to be wrong is worth
more than an unexamined one**, and it names its own next experiment. [the workbench has a save and a restore](../00-Engine-Core-Runtime/Shared-Transform-Workbench/the-workbench-has-a-save-and-restore-and-nine-functions-use-it.md) §6.

### The apparatus had been thrown away

The earlier measurement was recorded as made *“by running it”* and **the script was not kept**.
A measurement whose apparatus is gone cannot be re-run, extended, or checked when a later
reading contradicts it. That is a process defect, not a knowledge one, and it is fixed:
`workbench_probe.py` is the apparatus.

> **It was validated before it was trusted.** The probe reproduces every documented worked
> example — `row=127` with argument 1, 2, 3 giving `0xFE`, `0xFF`, `0xFA`, and `16×16` giving
> `0x00`. Only then was a novel result believed. Building it also required mapping the
> save/restore pair's **own** storage at `02EC0800`/`02EC0A00`, which is nowhere near the
> workbench; mapping only the workbench faults inside the save, which reads as a fault in the
> function under test.

### Reading the arithmetic beat fitting the outputs

The body is 1,560 bytes, but the instruction census shows only **8 `imul`** — everything else is
byte scatter through `movd` and `psrldq`. That is what made the derivation tractable at all.

```text
out_byte[i] = min(255, ( 2*((row[i]*(a_byte[i] + b_byte[i])) mod 256)
                         + ((a_byte[i]*b_byte[i]) >> 7) ) mod 512)     i = 0, 2, 3
```

**1,331 of 1,331** exhaustive combinations — 11 row values × 11 × 11 arguments — and **120 of
120** hold-out on each of byte positions 0, 2 and 3, on values the model never saw.

**The two arguments multiply.** With the row zero, either alone gives `0` and the pair gives
`min(255, (a·b) >> 7)` — 9 of 9, including `a = 300` behaving exactly as `a = 44`, which is how
the mod-256 reduction of the arguments announced itself.

**Nothing earlier is contradicted.** With `b = 0` the cross term vanishes and
`2·((row·a) mod 256)` never exceeds 510, so `mod 512` is the identity: the old formula **is**
the `b = 0` case. It was right about what it measured.

### The part that was nearly curve-fitting, and how it was avoided

Four placements of the saturation — per-term saturated, per-term wrapped, sum-first saturated,
sum-first wrapped — **all plateaued at exactly 1,256 of 1,331**. Adding more variants was the
moment to stop guessing and look at the residual: every one of the 75 failures had the same
shape, `634 -> 122`, `600 -> 88`, `556 -> 44`, `553 -> 41`. **Those are the sum mod 512.** A
**nine-bit intermediate**, saturated to eight afterwards, fits all 1,331.

> **The plateau was the signal.** Four models scoring identically means the axis being varied is
> not the one that is wrong.

### A hypothesis killed by its own test

Every one of the eight `imul`s is fed by **`movsx`** — sign-extended 16-bit — and the four
results are stored back as **16-bit words** at `022D8F30`…`3C`. That reading predicts the row is
four signed 16-bit lanes, and therefore that `row[1] >= 0x80` forces `0xFF` because byte 1 is
lane 0's **high** byte. It is a clean mechanism and it explains a documented anomaly.

**It is wrong.** Setting the high byte of each lane in turn, **only byte 1 does anything**;
bytes 3, 5 and 7 at `0x80` change nothing, and all four at `0x7F` change nothing. A lane sign
bit would have fired four times.

> **The test was built to check the prediction and it killed it in the same run.** That is the
> right order, and the hypothesis is recorded as `CONTRADICTED` in the document's evidence table
> rather than quietly dropped.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**Byte position 1.** The rule fits positions 0, 2 and 3 at 120 of 120 each and **56 of 120 at
position 1**. It is genuinely different, the lane explanation is dead, and **nothing here
replaces it**.

**What the computation is FOR.** The mapping is now exact; its purpose is not established. Nine
functions share this workbench and none carries a ledger owner.

**That the formula holds outside the sampled ranges.** Rows and arguments were sampled to 255
and the arguments are reduced mod 256 anyway; **the row was not tested above 255**, and a row
byte is a byte.

`check_links` · `check_consistency` · `check_questions` · `check_denominators` ·
`verify_doc_addresses` · `ADDRESS-INDEX.md` regenerated.

## 2026-09-08 — the instrument was counting itself, and a retraction is retracted

**Block:** `INTEGRATION` is `NOT COVERED` for all six pilots and `field_music` is one dimension
short. The plan was to capture the game's **own** inputs and its **own** answer — breakpoints at
`003EAA7D` (field id in `ebx`, progress in `eax`) and at both `ret` sites — and compare against
the reconstruction over the real table. [`RUNTIME-RESEARCH.md`](RUNTIME-RESEARCH.md) §8e.

### The discrepancy that stopped it

Three breakpoints inside `003EAA70` reported **0 hits** in-world. So did the entry armed alone.
**Last block reported 1,130,002 hits on that entry, 13 bytes away, in the same state.** Both
could not be true, and a zero and a million disagree too loudly to average.

### A hardware breakpoint re-fires unless you tell it not to

`hwbp.py` set `EFLAGS.RF` on no thread and cleared `DR6` on none. The CPU re-trapped on the
instruction it had just reported, so the tool looped on one address at the speed of the
debug-event round trip. **The test is one line of arithmetic on data the tool already had:**

```text
60 consecutive recorded hits on 0020E600  ->  1 distinct (thread, rcx, rdx) triple
after the fix, 300 recorded hits          ->  161 distinct triples
```

**Every count this tool has produced is retracted as a count of anything:** 133,679, 127,578,
255,944, 114,204, 1,130,002.

### The retraction of the retraction

The previous block withdrew *“field music is not selected per frame in-world”* — a finding taken
two blocks before that — on the grounds that 1.13M hits proved it false, and blamed the original
zero on perturbation from two hot breakpoints sharing the run.

**That reasoning is void and the original finding stands.**

| run | breakpoints | state | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 3, two of them hot | in-world | 0 hits |
| B | `003EAA70` alone | armed at the front-end, **spanned a map load** | 1,130,002 (storm) |
| C | `003EAA70` alone | in-world, armed after the load | **0 hits** |
| D | 3, all inside the function | in-world | **0 hits** |

**A storming instrument cannot re-report an event that never happened**, so the zeroes were
never affected by the bug — only the counts were. The real difference between B and the rest is
that **B spanned a map load**. Field music is selected at map load and not while standing still,
which is what run A said.

> **I was right, then wrong about why, and only the second correction had a control.** The
> retraction was made with the same reasoning it was criticising: a number believed because the
> instrument produced it.

### The guard that was missing

Every rule already in force **passed**. The instrument had a positive control that fired. It was
run with the target alone. It reported its own CPU load. [`EVIDENCE-STANDARD.md`](EVIDENCE-STANDARD.md) now carries a second
amendment:

> **A hit count is not an event count.** Record enough state per event — thread, arguments, a
> timestamp — to tell *one thing happening many times* from *one thing reported many times*, and
> **print the distinct count beside the raw one**.

### Two more bugs, found while fixing the first

| bug | how it showed | fix |
|---|---|---|
| a full thread-context write on **every** debug event, not just the trapping thread's trap | the target's CPU fell to **0.062 s over 8.1 s wall** and it stopped responding | restricted to `EXCEPTION_SINGLE_STEP` on `ev.dwThreadId` |
| the CPU liveness check used an **absolute** threshold | a `--stop-after` run finishing in 0.1 s wall was reported **FROZEN** | it is a **rate** now, and only applied to runs over a second |

**The first of those cost a game process** — wedged, then relaunched. The install was unaffected.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**The in-world re-measurement with the fixed tool.** It was not taken: navigation could not be
re-established after the tool runs, and the two zeroes on record were measured with the buggy
version. **They are still valid** for the reason given above, and that reason is stated rather
than assumed — but a clean confirmation is owed.

**Any `INTEGRATION` movement.** None. The capture the block set out to make did not happen, and
the dimension is where it was.

**That the fixed counts are now correct.** 300 hits over 161 distinct triples says the storm is
gone; it does not say the remaining duplicates are all real repeat calls. **Distinctness is a
lower bound on the event count, not the event count.**

### Gates

`check_links` · `check_consistency` · `check_questions` · `check_denominators` ·
`verify_doc_addresses` · `ADDRESS-INDEX.md` regenerated · install verified `CLEAN` after the wedged process.

## 2026-09-08 — the running game as the oracle, and two debts discharged

**Block:** the capture the previous block set out to make and could not, now that `hwbp.py` no
longer re-reports itself. [`EXP-009`](../_experiments/EXP-009-the-games-own-answer.md).

### One call, both inputs and the answer

```text
003EAA7D   just after the progress getter returns
             rbx = the field id     (set by `mov ebx, ecx` at the entry)
             rax = the progress     (what 00265270 just returned)
003EAAFE   the first  ret           rax = the track id
003EAB54   the second ret           rax = the track id
```

Entry and exit paired **within a thread, in order**; the game's own `MUS0` table read out of the
same process; the same inputs then put through the emulated shipped bytes and the reconstruction
at that table's real address.

| field | progress | the game | shipped bytes, emulated | the reconstruction |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 227 | 68 | **100** | 100 | 100 |
| 253 | 1,580 | **20** | 20 | 20 |

**126 entry→exit pairs per run, 0 unpairable rows**, from two areas reached by loading two
different saves while armed.

> **Every differential in this tree before now compared the reconstruction against the same
> static artifact it was derived from**, executed rather than read. This compares it against the
> answer the running game produced.

### Two debts discharged

**The in-world zero.** The previous block recorded that a clean confirmation was owed. It is
discharged by argument rather than by another zero: **126 calls across a 70-second run** that
spanned one map load and roughly fifty seconds of standing still, with a **400-hit cap that was
never reached**. Per-frame at 60 fps would be about 3,000 calls. The per-frame reading is
excluded **without needing timestamps the trace does not carry**.

**The operating rule is withdrawn.** *“Establish the state first, attach second”* was written
when the storm made every armed breakpoint fire thousands of times a second. The game was
navigated **through two menus and a save load while three breakpoints were armed**, and its own
keypress counter moved `0 -> 6`. The starvation was the storm, entirely.

### An observation nobody asked for

**Every one of the 252 pairs left through the SECOND `ret`.** `003EAAFE` recorded **0 hits** in
both runs. The function has two exits and the game, on these inputs, never took the first.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**`INTEGRATION` coverage.** §3 asks for the reconstruction to be exercised *through the game's
caller*. **It is still invoked by a test driver.** Everything else changed — the inputs, the
table and the oracle are the game's own — so **the remaining gap is substitution, not
evidence**, and the declaration says exactly that instead of claiming the dimension.

**A population of two.** Each save loads one area and the field id does not change while
standing still, so two saves gave two inputs. **Widening it is cheap and was not done.**

**What the progress value counts.** `68` and `1,580` were read from the getter's return.
Nothing here says what they measure.

**That the two `ret`s mean different things.** `003EAAFE` was never taken. Whether it is an
error path, an early-out, or merely unreached on these inputs is **not read**.

### Reference environment

Launched, navigated and closed by the harness three times, exit verified. **No process memory
was written**; the only target state changed was the debug registers, cleared on every exit
path. [`RUNTIME-RESEARCH.md`](RUNTIME-RESEARCH.md) §8e records why these counts are trustworthy where the earlier ones were not.

## 2026-09-08 — a reconstruction that was written and never run

**Block:** category switch after two runtime blocks. `flag_banks` held the biggest remaining
contract gap at **5 of 10**, and its most player-facing unexercised claim is the **authored
gate** — the decoder that turns a script's encoded id into which story flag gets read. [the persistent flag banks contract](../14-Story-Event-Quest-Hunt/CONTRACT-persistent-flag-banks.md).

### What `0032A8A0` does

```text
id = encoded & 0x3FFF
bit 14 set   ->  tail-jump to the threshold schedule at 00377970
bit 14 clear ->  id >= 0x200 : 0        fails closed
                 id == 0     : 1        hardwired, touches no storage
                 id == 1     : 0        hardwired
                 otherwise   : bit (id & 7) of payload[0x14F4 + (id >> 3)]
```

The contract already claimed *“bit 14 selects, 0/1 hardwired”*. Reading the body adds the
`>= 0x200` bound and names the bank the fall-through reads — **Primary, at `0x14F4`**.

### The finding: it was already reconstructed, and never tested

`PersistentFlag_Gate` existed in `flag_banks.c`, with `FLAG_GATE_SCHEDULE_BIT` and
`FLAG_GATE_INDEX_MASK` in the header. **No case had ever called it.**

> **A written-but-unrun function is a claim, not a reconstruction.** It looks like progress in a
> source tree and contributes nothing to parity. The `CONTRACT_MAP` discipline is what surfaced
> it — the row read `NOT EXERCISED` while the code sat a directory away, compiled.

**Checked against the binary line by line, one difference, and it is not a bug.** The original
tests `id >= 0x200` **before** the two hardwired ids; the reconstruction tests it **after**.
Both hardwired ids are below the bound, so no input can distinguish the orders. Recorded rather
than “fixed”, because changing correct code to match an irrelevant ordering is noise.

### Exercised as op 11

**87 encoded ids × 3 payloads = 261 comparisons, 0 mismatches.** **42 of the 87 carry bit 14**,
so both arms of the selection are taken rather than only the one the shipped data happens to
use. Ids were **chosen, not sampled**: `0`, `1`, `2`, `3`, `7`, `8`, `9`, `0x1FE`, `0x1FF`,
`0x200`, `0x201`, `0x3FF`, `0x3FFE`, `0x3FFF`, each with and without bit 14, plus 60 random.

**The schedule is stubbed with a sentinel both sides answer with.** `00377970` reads a runtime
table through `[02ADD0C8]` and calls the same progress getter field music uses; it is **not
reimplemented**. What the claim asserts is the *selection*, and a stub makes the selection
testable without pretending to model the delegate.

Whole harness: **8,064 comparisons, 0 mismatches**, all eleven prior accessors still green.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**That the schedule arm is tested.** It is stubbed. *“The schedule is a parity”* remains
`NOT EXERCISED`, and reaching it needs `00377970` reimplemented along with the table it reads.

**That `0x200` is a bank size.** The bound is what the code tests. The Primary bank's extent is
a separate claim and this block did not re-derive it.

**That any caller passes a bit-14 id.** The decoder handles it; **nothing here shows a script
ever sets that bit**, which is the same shape as the still-open question about negative ids.

### Movement

`flag_banks` **5 → 6 of 10**; tree-wide contract coverage **30 of 50**.

## 2026-09-08 — a differential test that compared against its own copy

**Block:** last block found `PersistentFlag_Gate` written, compiled and never called, by hand.
**That is a systemic question**, and charter §38 asks for integrity automation, so it was made
mechanical: `recon_coverage.py` checks every public function the reconstruction declares against
every differential driver.

### The finding

`angle_wrap_driver.c` defines `wrap_loop_capped()` — a copy of `Angle_WrapLoop` with an
iteration cap — and printed **that copy's** result. So this line, which the harness has printed
for as long as it has existed:

```text
  1. loop form  003A1C50   vs reconstruction : OK
```

compared the emulated original against **a copy of the reconstruction living inside the test**.
`Angle_WrapLoop` had **never been executed by anything**.

> **This is worse than an unused function.** An unused function claims nothing. A test that
> prints *“vs reconstruction: OK”* while comparing against its own copy makes a claim that is
> false about the artifact it names, and it is the kind of false claim that gets more
> convincing the longer it passes.

**The cap exists for a real reason** — six inputs genuinely cannot terminate, which the harness
itself reports — so the fix does not remove it. The capped walk is now a **predicate** deciding
whether the real loop can be entered, and the compared value comes from `Angle_WrapLoop`.

**It still passes.** The reconstruction was correct; it had simply never been proven, and the
passing test was not evidence that it was.

### One false alarm, and why the tool now classifies

`PersistentFlag_BitAddress` is named by no driver **and runs on all 8,064 flag-bank
comparisons**, because `query()` and `set()` call it. Reporting that as a gap would be a false
alarm, and **a tool that cries wolf gets ignored**, so the sweep distinguishes:

| header | declared | direct | indirect | unreached |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `Game/Audio/field_music.h` | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| `Game/Config/quality_preset.h` | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| `Game/Input/name_registry.h` | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| `Game/Math/angle_wrap.h` | 2 | **2** | 0 | 0 |
| `Game/Story/flag_banks.h` | 13 | 12 | 1 | 0 |
| `Game/UI/widget_construct.h` | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| **total** | **20** | **19** | **1** | **0** |

### What was deliberately not claimed

**That 20 of 20 reached means 20 of 20 tested.** The sweep counts a **mention**, not a call. A
driver naming a function in a comment or behind `#if 0` would count. **Its failures are exact
and its passes are weak**, and the tool prints that sentence itself.

**That no other test has the same defect.** The sweep finds functions nothing names; it does
**not** find a driver that names the right function and then compares the wrong value. Catching
that needs mutation testing — already an open item in [the parity standard](../../../Reconstruction/PARITY-STANDARD.md) §7.

**That the loop form's result changed.** It did not. Both before and after the fix the
comparison reports `OK`; what changed is **which artifact produced the compared value**.

## 2026-09-08 — mutation testing, and a suite that scores 52 %

**Block:** the last two blocks each found a test that proved nothing — `PersistentFlag_Gate`
never called, and `angle_wrap_driver.c` comparing against its own copy of the reconstruction —
and **both were found by other means while the harness stayed green**. [The parity standard](../../../Reconstruction/PARITY-STANDARD.md) §7 has named
the remedy since it was written.

### The manifest is generated, because the charter says so and the charter is right

A hand-picked mutation list is **a list of things the author already believed were covered**.
`mutation_test.py` produces it from the source text by five stated rules — integer literal + 1,
`>=`/`>`, `<=`/`<`, `==`/`!=`, shift direction — with **every** matching site becoming a
mutation and nothing filtered for looking interesting. The `.h` is in the surface too: several
pilots keep their constants as macros, and a tool reading only the `.c` would report a
suspiciously small manifest and never touch the numbers that matter.

Each mutation is applied, rebuilt, run, and **the sources are restored byte for byte in a
`finally`**, verified before exit. A mutation left on disk is a corrupted reconstruction, which
is worse than no measurement.

| pilot | generated | tested | killed | survived | score |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `angle_wrap` | 5 | 5 | 4 | 1 | 80 % |
| `quality_preset` | 10 | 10 | 9 | 1 | 90 % |
| `name_registry` | 30 | 23 | 12 | **11** | **52 %** |

`name_registry` generated 30, of which **6 did not compile** (not a test result, reported apart)
and 1 timed out.

### A survivor is not a gap until it is adjudicated

**Both single survivors are equivalent mutants, and neither was assumed to be.**

**`angle_wrap` line 20**, `(x >= 0.0f)` → `(x > 0.0f)`. The only inputs that can distinguish the
two are `±0.0`. **Both variants were built and run** on `±0.0` and `±1.0`: byte-identical
output. Equivalent, demonstrated.

**`quality_preset` line 17**, the loop start `0` → `1`, skipping setting index 0. The shipped
mask table at `00900CC0` begins `00 00 00 00 00 00` — **indices 0 through 5 are all zero** — so
`if (mask[i] == 0) continue;` skips index 0 regardless.

> **It is equivalent under the shipped table and only under it.** The harness deliberately feeds
> the REAL tables, and that choice is exactly what makes this mutant unkillable. **Real data
> buys meaning and costs sensitivity**, and a mutation score is the place that shows up.

> **A fact that fell out of checking it:** only **10 of the 31** settings have a non-zero mask.
> Twenty-one are never touched by a quality preset at all.

### `name_registry`'s eleven are not equivalent

| what survived | how many | reading |
|---|---:|---|
| `v = 0 -> 1` and `i = 7 -> 8` in `load_q` | 2 | **equivalent** — the value is shifted out of the qword before it is returned |
| the `!p` early return, and the both-null arm of `names_equal` | 2 | **defensive paths no case reaches** — every address the test uses lies inside a supplied region, and the `NULL_KEY` guard returns before any comparison |
| every `need` argument (`8`, `8`, `1`, `1`), both operators of the bounds check, and the store loop's `i < 8` | 7 | **boundary insensitivity — a real gap** |

**The regions the harness supplies are strictly larger than the addresses it uses**, so no case
ever sits on a region boundary and the bounds check is never tested at the only place it can be
wrong. And the suite compares the **resulting list**, so a store loop writing **one byte past
the qword** changes nothing it looks at.

> That last one is the same shape as `quality_preset`'s old window stopping at `0x7C`: **a test
> that compares the thing that moved and not the bytes that must not.**

### What was deliberately not claimed

**A mutation score for the tree.** Three of six pilots are measured; `field_music` (49),
`flag_banks` (68) and `widget_construct` (98) generate **215 further mutations that were not
run**. Averaging three suites into a headline number would invent a figure.

**That a killed mutation means the behaviour is well tested.** It means **one** case
distinguished it. Mutation testing bounds coverage from below, not above.

**That the eleven survivors are bugs.** They are **gaps in the test**, not defects in the
reconstruction — the reconstruction is unchanged and still passes. Closing them means adding
cases, and **no case was added in this block**.

## 2026-09-08 — the measurement was measured, and it was wrong

§4aw scored `name_registry` at 52 % and named **seven boundary-insensitivity survivors**. All seven
are closed, the score is **21 of 23 (91 %)** — and **the 52 % itself was wrong**, not merely
conservative, in a way that looked like a legitimate category.

### The 52 % was measured through a leaked process

§4aw reported *"did not compile: 7"*. **Those seven compiled.** A mutation that stops the dedup walk
terminating (`n != 0` -> `n != 1`) hangs the driver; `subprocess.run(timeout=)` killed the harness
but **not the driver the harness had spawned**; the orphan held `name_registry_mut.exe` open, and
every later `cl /Fe:` failed to overwrite a running executable. **A locked output file was recorded
as a source-code category.** One such orphan was still running 24 minutes later with **1440 s of
CPU**, competing for the machine with the measurement that replaced it.

Three of the seven lost mutations were `.h` constants that had therefore never been tested at all.
Timeouts now take the whole tree down with `taskkill /F /T`, and the per-mutation timeout is **6x the
measured baseline run** instead of a fixed ten minutes — the baseline here is 0.1 s, so ten minutes
was never the right order of magnitude.

**The hang is legitimate and the reconstruction is right to allow it.** There is no cycle guard in
`NameRegistry_Register` because **there is none in the original**: `008795C7`/`008795CE` is a bare
`mov r9,[r9+0x10]` / `test r9,r9` / `jne`. Adding one to make the suite cheaper would be changing the
reconstruction to suit the test. A hang is neither a kill nor a survivor — the harness never returned
a verdict — so it stays out of the ratio and is named individually, because *"2 timed out"* hides
**which** behaviours went unmeasured.

### Proving equivalence instead of arguing it

Adjudicating survivors by hand is where a mutation score goes soft: *"that one is equivalent"* is
exactly the sentence a tired author writes about a real gap. One class can now be settled
mechanically. Builds run with **`/Brepro`** on compiler and linker, making MSVC output
byte-for-byte reproducible (verified: two builds of identical source, identical SHA-256). **A mutant
whose executable hashes the same as the baseline emitted the same machine code, so no test could ever
kill it.**

It proved **5** at once — including `line 20: 0 -> 1` and `line 24: 7 -> 8`, the two `load_q`
shift-out mutants that §4aw adjudicated **by hand**. The tool now proves what a human asserted. The
other three are `name_registry.h`'s `NAME_NODE_TYPE`, `_VALUE` and `_SIZE`: the header documents all
five node fields, the registration function reads **two**, and mutating a declaration nothing
compiles against had been sitting in the survivor list looking like a test gap.

The implication runs one way only — identical code proves equivalence, **different code proves
nothing** — and those mutants still go to the harness.

### An address on the boundary is not a boundary test

The first attempt at closing the seven added a name at a region's **first** byte and a node whose
`next` read ends on its **last** byte. Both sat exactly where they should. **Both killed nothing.**

- `va >= r->va`: the boundary name belonged to a node that was **unique**, so failing to resolve it
  merely failed to match — and the node registered `OK`, which is what it returned anyway.
- `va - r->va + need <= r->size`: the boundary node was registered **last**, so it was the head and
  nothing ever walked *through* it. `load_q(node5 + NEXT)` was never called.

**A boundary case must be built so that resolving the boundary and failing to resolve it give
different verdicts.** Rebuilt that way, all four die:

| case | returns | what it makes observable |
|---|---|---|
| `01F500C0` DUPLICATE keyed at a region's **first** byte | `DUPLICATE` | resolve `va == r->va` and it is DUPLICATE; fail and it is OK |
| `01F50180` duplicate reachable only **through** the boundary node | `DUPLICATE` | forces the `next` qword ending on the region's last byte to be read |
| `01F501C0` empty name **on** a region's last byte | `OK` | joins the chain |
| `01F50240` DUPLICATE compared at a region's **last** byte | `DUPLICATE` | puts that address on **both** sides of `names_equal`, so either `need` -> 2 flips the verdict |

The last needed a **fourth region**, 0x40 bytes, existing only to hold a name whose first byte is the
region's last byte — the only address where `names_equal`'s `need` of 1 can be wrong.

### The digest failed first, and the fixture was wrong, not the reconstruction

An FNV-1a digest over **every region byte** now runs beside the chain comparison — the half the suite
never had, since it compared what moved and never what must **not** move (the lesson
`quality_preset` learned when its window stopped at `0x7C`).

It failed on its first run. `scratch[a:a + 12] = b"NotAName_1\0"` is **eleven bytes into a
twelve-byte slice**, and a bytearray slice assignment of a different length **resizes the array**.
Two such writes had quietly shortened the scratch region to `0xFFE` while every offset in the file
was computed against `0x1000`; the boundary node therefore sat two bytes past the region it was meant
to touch exactly, and `NameImage_At` **correctly refused** the out-of-region write.

**The reconstruction was right and the fixture was lying about its own size.** A chain-only
comparison would have stayed green against a region two bytes smaller than it claimed. Writes now go
through a helper that cannot resize, and `build_regions` asserts every region length before
returning. The pattern appears in **no other harness** — checked across all six.

### Two survivors cannot be killed by any differential, and the binary proves it

`00879570`, 132 bytes, has **no bounds check and no null tolerance anywhere**:

```text
00879574  mov   r10, qword ptr [rcx + 8]          ; the key, straight out of the node
0087957B  test  r10, r10 / jne                    ; the ONLY validation in the function
008795A0  mov   rax, qword ptr [r9 + 8]           ; the other node's name...
008795B0  movzx edx, byte ptr [rax]               ; ...dereferenced unchecked
008795D0  mov   qword ptr [r11 + 0x10], rbx       ; next = old head
008795DA  mov   qword ptr [rip + 0x264079F], r11  ; head = node   (02EB9D80)
```

`load_q`'s `!p` early return (`line 23`) and `names_equal`'s both-null arm (`line 58`) have **no
counterpart in the shipped code**. They exist only because the reconstruction addresses memory
through an explicit region image instead of raw pointers. The original would **fault** where they
return a value, so a case that distinguishes them is a case that cannot be run.

They are **interface artifacts, not test gaps** — §4aw's "defensive paths no case reaches" was too
weak a claim. They are the entire remaining survivor list.

### The score

| pilot | generated | equivalent | timed out | tested | killed | survived | score |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `angle_wrap` | 5 | — | — | 5 | 4 | 1 | 80 % |
| `quality_preset` | 10 | — | — | 10 | 9 | 1 | 90 % |
| `name_registry` **(§4aw)** | 30 | — | — | 23 | 12 | 11 | 52 % — *invalid, see above* |
| `name_registry` **(now)** | 30 | 5 | 2 | 23 | **21** | **2** | **91 %** |
| *not run* | `field_music` 49, `flag_banks` 68, `widget_construct` 98 | | | | | | |

Remaining survivors, both proven unkillable: `name_registry.c line 23: 0 -> 1`, `name_registry.c line 58: == -> !=`

### What was deliberately not claimed

**A mutation score for the tree.** Three of six pilots are measured; `field_music` (49),
`flag_banks` (68) and `widget_construct` (98) are **215 mutations that have not been run**.

**That 91 % means the reconstruction is 91 % correct.** It means the suite distinguishes 21 of 23
mutants that emit different code. Mutation testing bounds coverage **from below**.

**That the equivalence prover is complete.** It settles one direction only. A mutant that emits
different code and survives is still adjudicated by hand, or by adding a case.

**That `name_registry` gained parity evidence.** The reconstruction is **unchanged** by this block —
every line of it. What changed is the harness, and what it can now see.

## 2026-09-08 — an answered question the roadmap still called open

`EC-1` was answered by hand earlier today. This block **re-derived that answer independently, with a
tool**, and the tool led to four factual errors in a document that the hand pass had no reason to
look for.

### The roadmap disagreed with the ledger, and no gate noticed

`OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` recorded `EC-1` as **ANSWERED**. `PROGRAM-STATE.md` §4 still read *"**Not yet
done:** a sweep of existing documents"* and §5 still listed `F-5` as frontier work. **`check_questions`
passes on both**, because it compares the question table to the documents' checklists — never the
roadmap to the ledger. A block chosen off the frontier therefore starts work that is already closed.
Filed as **`EC-4`**; both stale statements are corrected.

### The sweep is now an instrument, not an episode

`sweep_funclet_claims.py` recomputes every population from `functions.tsv` and `edges.tsv` on each
run — 3,895 EH functions, 3,834 EH-sourced edges of 90,525 (4.24 %), 838 callees touched, **278
authored functions with no non-EH caller** — using the same `authored = all − generated − thunks`
definition as `program_coverage.py`, so the two cannot drift apart silently. It then finds
reachability language within one line of a contaminated address. It searches **both** address
spellings, because `ANY_HEX8` needs a non-word character before the digits and so misses the GFZ's
own `FUN_002f9860` form — the spelling that once hid 226 authored functions.

**It carries a positive control, because the expected result is a negative.** A clean sweep and a
broken sweep print the same thing. `--control` plants a document citing a real contaminable address
in both spellings beside real reachability language; if that is not found, the run **aborts** rather
than reporting a reassuring zero. Control: **FOUND**.

| measure | count | denominator |
|---|---:|---:|
| documents scanned | 331 | — |
| contaminable functions cited anywhere in the database | 5 | 278 (**1.8 %**) |
| EH-touched functions cited anywhere | 27 | 838 (**3.2 %**) |
| reachability claims beside a contaminated address, system docs | **2** | — |

Both were adjudicated against a fresh derivation and **both are correct**: `0080926C`
(`_Init_thread_abort`) is 1,545 EH sites and **zero** non-EH, exactly as written, and `006DA980` is
99 and zero. `EC-1`'s answer stands, now on two independent derivations.

### Four corrections, every one re-derived from the binary

| where | was | is |
|---|---|---|
| `00896280` "first funclet" | `lea rcx,[rip+guard] ; jmp _Init_thread_abort` | `lea rcx,[rip] -> 01F7E350 ; jmp 00793250` — a 353 B Phyre function, **not** `_Init_thread_abort` |
| `008A6960` "last funclet" | "same family" | `mov rcx,[rdx+0x58] ; jmp 00199D30` — loads an object field, not a static guard |
| `00861ECC` `_CxxThrowException` | "used by **8** catch funclets" | **64** sites in **64** distinct `Catch_All@` bodies, plus 5 ordinary call sites |
| `0016D6A0` `_guard_check_icall` | "tail target of 172 funclets" | 172 funclets **and 2,422 ordinary call sites in 2,308 functions**, which the funclet figure alone does not suggest |

The *block boundary* `00896280`–`008A6960` is **right** — all 1,545 guard funclets lie inside it —
but the guard-family body had been attributed to the block's two endpoints, which do not have it.
The true endpoints of that family are `008964A0` and `008A6950`, now listed. The document's worked
example, `Unwind@008964A0` with guard `01F7F5C8`, disassembles **exactly** as written.

### What the four-instrument rule bought, again

`edges.tsv` said `00861EAE` had **1** EH caller; the document said **86**. The PE-derived instrument,
with its own passing control, says **86** — **the document was right and my first instrument was
wrong.** Had I filed on that reading I would have "corrected" a correct number into a false one. The

## 2026-09-08 — auditing the instruction that chooses the audits

Last block began work that was already finished, because `PROGRAM-STATE.md` still listed it as
frontier work. **This block began the same way**, on `F-2`: the roadmap said *"Schema migration
toward machine-queryable knowledge"* and `knowledge_db.py` already answers **26 of charter §7's 30
queries**, naming the other 4 and the source each would need.

Twice is a pattern, so the block became the pattern rather than the item.

### The block-selection prompt is the stale surface that matters

The prompt that chooses every block puts, at priority 1: *"The program has not yet produced
multidimensional coverage metrics, a machine-queryable schema, integrity automation, or a
reconstruction/parity skeleton."*

**All four exist.** `check_frontier.py` checks that sentence against the filesystem:

| charter §38 first-action | artifacts | status |
|---|---|---|
| multidimensional coverage metrics | `program_coverage.py`, `COVERAGE-DIMENSIONS.md` | **SATISFIED** |
| a machine-queryable schema | `knowledge_db.py`, `knowledge.sqlite` | **SATISFIED** |
| integrity automation | the five gates, `check_caller_claims.py`, `sweep_funclet_claims.py` | **SATISFIED** |
| a reconstruction/parity skeleton | `mutation_test.py`, six differential pilots | **SATISFIED** |

**4 of 4 satisfied; the sentence is true of none of them.** It is the single highest-leverage claim
in the program — it directs every block choice — and it has been directing them toward work that is
done. That is a bigger finding than either individual stale item, and neither of the two mechanical
checks below would ever have caught it, because it names no question and no file.

> **This sits in the skill prompt, not in this database, so this block did not edit it.** Changing
> the instructions that govern block selection is the operator's call, not a side effect of a block.
> It is recorded here so the finding survives.

### `check_frontier.py` — three checks and a control

    STALE-QUESTION  an open frontier item cites a question the ledger marks ANSWERED
    CLAIMED-ABSENT  a sentence asserting absence names a file that exists on disk
    MAYBE-DONE      an open item names an artifact that exists (advisory: an item can be
                    honestly open with every artifact present)
    FIRST-ACTIONS   charter §38's four, each mapped to concrete artifacts

**It carries a positive control, because a clean roadmap and a broken parser print the same
thing.** `--control` plants an open frontier item citing a genuinely ANSWERED question; if that is
not flagged the run aborts instead of reporting a reassuring zero. Control: **FOUND**.

Its first run produced a **false positive**, and fixing it was the point: it flagged §4's own
correction note, which *quotes* the wording it corrects. A claim of absence inside a quotation is a
report of what was said, not an assertion — and a checker that cannot tell those apart teaches its
reader to ignore it. It is now quotation-aware.

### `F-2` is done, and its residue is now precise

`knowledge_db.py` builds ten sources into `knowledge.sqlite`: 249 documents, 16,786 citations,
38,161 functions, 90,525 edges **with `caller_is_eh` as a column**, 164,489 global references, 189
types, 776 fields, 864 questions, 1,224 script verbs, 33 contradictions.

Materialising the EH flag as a column is the part worth naming: it turns *"remember to filter the
banned edges"* into *"write a `WHERE` clause you can see."*

`F-2`'s rationale named two example queries. One — *"all high-confidence functions lacking runtime
validation"* — is now `high-confidence-no-runtime`. The other, *"every writer of this field"*, is
**still unsupported**, and the tool says exactly why: `global_refs` is address-keyed, so it names
every writer of a **global**, but `obj->field` is `[reg+disp]` with the object identified only by
dataflow. That is carried forward as `F-6` rather than left as a vague open `F-2`.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**That the schema is complete.** 26 of 30 §7 queries are answerable; the 4 that are not are listed
by the tool with the missing source named for each. A schema that answers 26 and says so is worth
more than one that answers 30 by inventing data.

**That `check_frontier.py` makes the roadmap trustworthy.** It compares prose to the ledger and to
the filesystem. It cannot tell whether an item is *substantively* finished — only whether the
document contradicts something checkable sitting right next to it. Both stale items that motivated
it were caught by the FIRST-ACTIONS table, not by the two general checks.

**That anything was learned about FFXII this block.** Nothing was. This block bought back the
reliability of block selection, which had misdirected the two before it.

## 2026-09-08 — a verb family read from the binary

Two blocks in a row learned nothing about FFXII. This one chose on evidence rather than on the
roadmap's prose: `knowledge_db.py` reports **1,152 of 1,224 script verbs have a handler no document
cites (94 %)**, and script dispatch is a §29 high-leverage subject that is also directly
player-facing.

### What a player sees

Followers that flatten, lose their shadows, or stop flinching when something clips them, the moment
a scene starts. **The engine is not deciding that — a zone script asked for it**, one setting at a
time, for the whole party at once. None of these verbs can target a single character.

### A family, proven rather than asserted

Seven verbs sit at consecutive call ids `040D`-`0413`. **Four of them are the same 187-byte function
with one call swapped** — `partyusecharhit` (`040E`), `partysetlod` (`040F`), `partyshowshadow`
(`0410`), `setpartyprojectionshadow` (`0413`). All four call the same argument reader
(`VMValueStack_PopInt32CoerceFloat32`), the same two collectors and the same cookie check, and
differ **only** in the per-member setter. *(Enumeration: all 49 verbs whose name contains `party`
were taken from the dispatch table; the four with a body of exactly 187 bytes were compared
instruction by instruction.)* Disposition **B** — proven member of an understood family, with the
method and count stated.

### The exact writes, which is what makes it reconstructable

| verb | setter | what it writes |
|---|---|---|
| `partysetlod` | `002EC680` | `pres[+0x13] = value` — a **whole byte**, unclamped, then a refresh |
| `partyshowshadow` | `002ECD80` | `pres[+0x151]` bit 3 `= value & 1`, behind two gates |
| `setpartyprojectionshadow` | `002E8730` | record `[+0x304]` bits `0x1000`/`0x2000` as a **two-bit field** |
| `partyusecharhit` | `0026A430` | **one boolean into two bytes**: `a[+0x08]` bit 3 and `a[+0x09]` bit 6 |

Two details a reimplementation would get wrong by guessing. The projection shadow's off-path clears
`0x3000` — **both** bits — so `10` and `11` are states the verb cannot reach; and `[+0x290] |=
0x400000` is set on both paths, the signature of a dirty bit rather than part of the setting.

### The collector, and a cross-subsystem correction to my own first reading

`0031B670`/`0031B680` are 8- and 11-byte adapters onto one collector at `0031B5A0`, called with
selector **0** and **1**. It walks **four slots**, and the split is a range test:
`(uint8_t)(rec[+0x04] - 7) <= 0x12`, i.e. **`rec[+0x04]` in 7..25**.

The table it reads is `[02EBF190] + 0x5A5A`, and **the database already knew what that is.**
`11-Party` had established five parallel maps `0x12` apart, nine two-byte slots each, and named map
**1** (`0x5A5A`) *the combat-processing set*. So:

- **These verbs read map 1, not map 3** — and map 3 is the one that document names *the script-VM
  bridge* as passing. The party-presentation family is an exception inside its own subsystem: it
  dresses the characters **combat** is servicing.
- **The collector reads four of the nine slots**, a deliberate subset — the class-`0x17` bound is 9,
  per the encoded-id class registry.
- **It never calls `BattleSlotMap_ResolveMappedBattleSlot`**; it computes the displacement inline.
  That is why `11-Party` §2b's census of 31 resolver call sites could not see it. **A consumer that
  reads a displacement directly cannot be found by asking who called the accessor** — which is the
  transferable lesson, and the reason this consumer went unnamed until a verb-side sweep reached it.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**That three of the seven verbs were read.** `partyusemapid` (312 B), `partyshowshadow_411` (82 B)
and `partyhideshadow` (79 B) were not disassembled; `0411` demonstrably differs, reading its argument
through `00267F90` rather than `00267E10`.

**L2.** The document is **L1**. The verb layer is reproducible byte for byte, but the presentation
*consequence* is not: the LOD refresh `002E8CE0` (309 B) is unread and
`Actor_RefreshPresentationVisibility` (793 B) is identified by name only. Stating L2 here would be
implying a level rather than stating one.

**Any runtime observation.** Every claim is static disassembly at the certified hash. Nothing was
watched running, and no value was seen to change.

**That map 1 is the same membership the player sees following them.** Filed alongside `SP-1`.

## 2026-09-08 — a verb whose name says `id` and whose bytes write two bits

§4ba read four of the seven verbs at `040D`-`0413` and said so three times. The remaining three are
now read, and the block is complete.

### Two of them implement nothing

`partyshowshadow_411` (`0411`, 82 B) and `partyhideshadow` (`0412`, 79 B) each push a constant with
`VMValueStack_PushInt32` and **tail-jump into `partyshowshadow`**, which pops it as its argument:

```text
00342360  mov edx, 1  ...  call 00267F90  ...  jmp 00341B90     ; show
00342830  xor edx, edx ... call 00267F90  ...  jmp 00341B90     ; hide
```

**Three verbs, one behaviour.** `partyshowshadow 1` is byte-for-byte `partyshowshadow_411`. Both
wrappers preserve `rcx`/`rdx`/`r8`/`r9` across the push, so the tail-jump receives the original
arguments untouched. §4ba had noted `0411` "reads its argument through `00267F90`, a different
reader" — it does not read an argument at all; `00267F90` is the **push**, not a read, and the
correction is now in the document.

### `partyusemapid` does not set an id

`040D` is the family shape with three calls per member instead of one: a flag write, then
`Actor_GetWorldPosition`, then a write of **the same three floats, unmodified** — a re-place at the
current position, which is what a caller does when a flag change means the actor must be re-resolved
against the world rather than moved.

The flag write, in full (`0026AD60`, 34 B):

```c
uint8_t b = (value != 0);
m[+0x08] &= 0xF9;                          /* clear bits 1 and 2 */
m[+0x08] |= (b << 1) | ((!b) << 2);
```

**Bits 1 and 2 of `m[+0x08]` are a mutually-exclusive pair** — exactly one is set, chosen by the
argument. Not a flag, not an identifier, despite the verb's name.

And the byte is shared: `partyusecharhit` writes **bit 3** of that same `m[+0x08]`. **This verb
family alone drives at least three of that byte's eight bits**, which is the kind of overlap a
reimplementation that gave each verb its own field would get silently wrong.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**What the bit pair selects.** The write is exact; the meaning is not. `partyusemapid` *suggests*
"use the map's own placement versus something else", but that is the name's suggestion, and the name
already proved unreliable here — it says `id` and writes two bits. Carried into `SP-1`.

**That the re-place is a position write.** `002E5DF0` is a 22-byte adapter that appends a zero fifth
argument and calls `002E5C90` (340 B, **unread**). That the round trip re-places is inferred from the
floats passing through unmodified, not from reading the callee.

**Any movement on the document's level.** It stays **L1**. Closing three verbs does not make the
presentation consequence reproducible: `002E8CE0` and `002E5C90` are both still unread.

## 2026-09-08 — a finding that came from joining two documented things

The `partystdmotion*` verbs (`053E`-`0541`) are read. They are a clean **2x2**, and reading them beside
§4ba/§4bb produced something neither family shows alone.

### What a player sees

In a cutscene the whole party reacts at once — everybody nods, everybody drops into the same stance.
And the motion **does not restart when it is already running**: that is not animation smoothing, it
is a **different script command**, and the author chose it.

### The 2x2

| verb | pops an extra argument first | third pushed value |
|---|---|---:|
| `053E` `partystdmotionplay` | no | **1** |
| `053F` `…withoutsame` | no | **0** |
| `0540` `…_540` | **yes** | **1** |
| `0541` `…withoutsame_541` | **yes** | **0** |

Two independent bits, each one instruction. *"withoutsame"* is `mov edx, 1` versus `xor edx, edx`
before the third `VMValueStack_PushInt32` — the names corroborate the constants, but the constants
are the evidence. And `0540`/`0541` **read an argument and throw it away**
(`VMValueStack_PopNumericDiscard`) before touching a single slot.

### The per-actor call goes through the VM value stack

The verb pushes three values — `motion`, the `.rdata` constant `-1.0f` (`01CEBC9C`, `0xBF800000`,
loop-invariant), and the same/without-same flag — then calls `003580C0(actor, stack)`, which performs
**three pops of its own**. The shared routine is written the way a *verb* is written: it reads its
arguments off the script stack, and the party verbs reuse it by **synthesising a call frame per
actor**.

### The finding: "the party" is two different things in one subsystem

| family | how it finds the party | what that is |
|---|---|---|
| appearance `040D`-`0413` | `[02EBF190] + 0x5A5A`, class `0x17`, `BattleUnit_FindByDefinitionSelector`, three gates, a 7..25 split | an **authored id table** — slot map 1 |
| motion `053E`-`0541` | `PartyRoster_GetActorBySlot` | the **live four-pointer array at `0209A1F0`** |

Both halves were already in the database — `11-Party` had read the roster array and named slot map 1
in separate blocks. **What was not written down is that two verb families in the same subsystem
iterate different ones.** Nothing in either function reconciles them and nothing requires them to
agree, so an actor in the roster array that fails the appearance gates gets its motion changed and
its shadow left alone. Filed as `SP-2`.

This is the shape §29 predicts: the value came from **joining two documented things**, not from
finding a third.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**Which pushed value is which argument of `003580C0`.** Three go on (`int`, `float bits`, `int`);
three pops come off (`Int32Coerce`, `Int32Coerce`, `NumericDiscard`). **The pairing was not traced**,
so which pop consumes the `-1.0f` is unproven. Stating an order would be inference dressed as a
formula.

**What `-1.0f` means.** A "use the default" sentinel is the pattern, and a pattern is not evidence
from this function.

**That the two rosters actually diverge in shipped content.** The *mechanism* permits it; no case was
demonstrated. That is exactly what `SP-2` asks.

**L2.** Still **L1**: `003580C0` was read only for its call targets, and `00233F50`/`002ED020` not at
all.

## 2026-09-08 — a page that carried its own contradiction in plain sight

Category switch after three script-verb blocks. Chosen on evidence: `knowledge_db.py` reports the
per-frame update gate as `PROVEN` but only `SEMANTICALLY IDENTIFIED`, and §29 names **central update
loops** as top-tier leverage. The document also contradicted itself, which settled it.

### The document counted fifteen and tabulated fourteen

`one-word-decides-which-fifteen-subsystems-tick.md` said *"Sixteen `test` sites, fifteen distinct
masks"* — and listed **fourteen** rows. Nothing reconciled the two, and `check_consistency` passes,
because it compares addresses across documents, not a count to the table beneath it.

The missing group is **`0x0800`**, tested at `0028E54E`. **It is the one group reached by `jmp`
rather than `call`:**

```text
0028E54E  test dword ptr [01E0C464], 0x800
0028E558  je   0028E56F                      ; skip the group
0028E55A  lea  rcx, [rbx + 0x7EA0]           ; rbx = [0209BE80]
0028E56A  jmp  0028C870                      ; the group's update, 197 B
```

**A census that looks for `call` after a `test` finds fourteen and reports fifteen.** This is the
mission prompt's own four-instrument rule failing inside this database's pages: `E8 call` alone was
the instrument, the single `E9 jmp` group fell out of the table, and the count above it stayed
right — so the page carried its own contradiction in plain sight.

### Three more corrections, all tool-derived

**The sites are not all `test byte`.** The document said *"every one is `test byte [01E0C464],
imm`"*. Re-derived by resolving every RIP-relative operand with a tool: **8 are `test byte`
(`0x0001`-`0x0080`) and 8 are `test dword` (`0x0100`-`0x8000`)**, exactly half and half. A byte test
cannot reach past bit 7, so **a reimplementation that took that sentence literally and made the
enable a `uint8_t` would silently lose eight of the fifteen groups.**

**Fifteen bits are used, not "fourteen consecutive".** Every bit of the low 16 except `0x0010` —
a set with a hole, not a run. The old wording undercounted by one *and* described a contiguity that
does not exist.

**The duplicated mask is `0x0002`**, tested at `0028E2B7` and again at `0028E3AE`, gating different
calls at two points in the frame. That is what makes sixteen sites out of fifteen masks; the document
stated the arithmetic without naming which mask repeated.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**That the gate is now understood.** The *bitfield* is completely enumerated and tool-verified; what
the fifteen groups **do** is not. Readiness stays `SEMANTICALLY IDENTIFIED` — knowing every switch
in a panel is not knowing what the machine does.

**That `0028C870` was analysed.** 197 bytes, unnamed, `BoundedLoop.DirectCallOnly`, **not read**.
Its argument is `[0209BE80] + 0x7EA0`; `0209BE80` has 296 reads and 2 writes and is cited by exactly
one document.

**That no other table in the database has this defect.** One instance was found and fixed. Filed as
`EC-5`, because the check is mechanical: *a stated count that disagrees with the table beneath it*.

## 2026-09-08 — the first run measured the tool, not the database

§4bd found the update gate's missing group **by eye**: a table of fourteen rows under prose saying
fifteen. `EC-5` observed that the check is mechanical. This built it and swept all 332 documents and
**2,431 tables**.

### Calibration is the story, because the first run measured the tool

| version | findings | what changed |
|---|---:|---|
| naive "a number near a table" | **1,114** of 2,431 (46 %) | — |
| minus section labels, dates, grouped numbers | 591 | `## 3. The registry` contributed a "3"; `33,346` contributed a "33" |
| a count must be followed by what it counts | 327 | *"fifteen distinct masks"* counts; *"an 8-byte getter"* and *"modes 4 and 5"* do not |
| multi-item rows reconciled | 148 (headings) | `vtable-method-index.md` heads each section *"N methods"* and lays them out **two per row** — 47 -> 24, 3067 -> 1534, `ceil(N/2)` every time. A formatting choice, not a miscount |
| a left boundary on numbers | **134** (headings), 259 (all) | *"3067 methods"* was being read as **67** |

**Every step was justified by an observed pattern, not by a wish for a smaller number.** The
positive control earned its keep twice: it aborted the run when the plural-noun rule went in, because
the control's own count is written in bold and **emphasis sits between a count and its noun** —
a regression that would have silently broken on the database, where bold counts are the norm.

### What it found, stated without inflation

Three heading-sourced candidates were adjudicated in full:

| candidate | verdict |
|---|---|
| `battle-runtime-mode-ladder.md` — *"Four authorities"* over 5 rows | **clean.** The fifth row is the authored field-record override, with `—` for getter and setter: not an authority |
| `force-fight-mode.md` — *"Fifteen consumers"* over 7 rows | **clean.** The text states the arithmetic itself: 7 direct sites + 8 through a thunk = 15, and the table lists the *named* ones |
| `arm-catalogue-slice-D` — *"Twelve float fields"* over 14 rows | **clean, and it pointed at a real one two lines away** |

The third is the interesting one. Fourteen rows are fourteen consecutive dword offsets
`+0x2D0`-`+0x304`, but **only twelve carry an arm id** — `+0x2E4` and `+0x2F8` are un-armed. So the
heading correctly counts arm-driven fields. **But the paragraph above says "Thirteen arms", and the
table maps twelve ids** (114-118, 127-133). That is a genuine internal inconsistency, and it is
flagged in the document rather than repaired: resolving it needs the arm bodies re-read, not a number
edited until the page agrees with itself.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**That the sweep found a second instance of the update-gate defect.** It did not. Three candidates
were adjudicated and all three headings were correct. One led to an adjacent discrepancy — which is
what an advisory instrument is *for* — but the specific failure §4bd exposed, a census losing a row
to a call-only instrument, has **one** known instance.

**That 134 findings are 134 defects.** They are 134 pairs worth a human's eye, and the sample says
most will be clean. The tool prints the sentence beside every hit so adjudication is cheap, and it
labels itself advisory rather than a gate. **It is not wired into the block-ending gate run**, because
a check with this precision would train its reader to skip it — the failure mode `recon_coverage.py`
already names.

**That the remaining 131 were looked at.** They were not.
