## 2026-09-08 — a checker at 0/5 precision, and seven findings that were all the instrument

§4cb was the eighth time in this program that a document outlived its own facts, and the second in
two blocks where **I** was the one misled. The pattern is stable enough to automate: the database
gates links, addresses, questions, denominators, cross-document consistency and global writer
claims, and **nothing compares a document against its own structure.**

### What already existed, and what it could not see

`check_self_contradiction.py` covers one shape — an absence-of-write claim refuted elsewhere in the
same file. **It was reporting 5 findings, and all five were false**, in two ways this session had
already solved elsewhere:

- **scope.** *"`022D9138` is read and never written **by this function**"* sat two lines from a
  table naming its two image-wide writers.
- **attribution.** The claim was charged to **every** address on the line. *"`A` is never written …
  its writers are `B` and `C`"* indicted B and C.

Both filters were ported from `check_global_claims.py`, where each had already cost a false
positive. **The sweep is now 0, and its self-test still fires on a planted contradiction** — the
recall was not traded away for the precision.

### Two new classes, in `check_doc_self.py`

| class | what it catches |
|---|---|
| **EMPTY-SECTION** | a document saying *"§13 is empty"* while §13 has content |
| **FRONTMATTER** | frontmatter `readiness:` disagreeing with the body's *"Readiness is X"* |

**Regression-tested against the case that motivated it.** Run against the `GameSettingConfig`
contract at `HEAD~1` — before §4cb's correction — **both classes fire**: EMPTY-SECTION reports
"§13 is empty" against a §13 of **26 non-blank lines**, and FRONTMATTER reports `RUNTIME VALIDATED`
against a body asserting `CONTRACT READY`. **A checker that cannot catch the error that prompted it
is decoration.**

### It found seven things and every one was wrong — which is why they are not in the database

The first sweep reported 7 EMPTY-SECTION hits across 6 contracts. **All false**, and both causes
were mine:

1. **A section that declares itself empty is empty.** *"**None. Empty deliberately, and this is the
   gate the subsystem fails.**"* followed by the cheapest confirmation to run is **good writing**,
   and my line-count threshold punished it. Fixed: a section whose opening line declares emptiness
   counts as empty however much it then says about what would fill it.
2. **`## 13b.` was counting toward `13`.** The section-head pattern stripped the letter suffix, so a
   contract whose §13 says `EMPTY` and whose §13b holds a differential test was reported as
   contradicting itself. **A lettered subsection is a different section.**

**No document was edited to satisfy the checker.** The checker was wrong and the documents were
right, which is the only correct resolution when a gate disagrees with careful prose — the same call
made in §4bx when `check_global_claims` fired on a correct sentence.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**That the database is free of self-contradiction.** It is free of *these three shapes*, over 324
documents, with four controls passing. `check_self_contradiction.py`'s own docstring already records
its blind spot: a contradiction not expressed through an address is invisible to it.

**That a clean sweep means the corpus improved.** It means the instrument stopped being wrong. The
one real instance was fixed in §4cb, before this gate existed.

**Any judgement about which side of a disagreement is right.** The tool reports the disagreement and
says so; the fix may belong to the frontmatter, the body, or the section.

## 2026-09-08 — three mutants that were undefined behaviour the tests could not see

The gap I have recorded three times now: **ten contracts, one implemented differential-tested
operation.** The charter's goal 2 is *"reconstruct the game's systems in maintainable source"*, and
the two workbench primitives were the best available candidates — pure leaves, **156 call sites**,
and laws already established by **350 predictions** rather than by reading shuffles.

### Result

`Reconstruction/Game/Math/transform.c`, compared against the shipped bytes:

| | |
|---|---|
| point cases | **123**, each comparing **five buffers** — `out` plus all four deposits |
| compose cases | **123**, across **3 aliasing modes** |
| mismatches | **0** |
| mutation score | **19 of 20 (95 %)** |

### The deposits are the reason this is worth doing

On the documented consumer path the installed matrix is the **identity**, so the multiply is a
no-op and `00398F90` is called **only for what it writes into shared scratch**. A reconstruction
filling just `out` would pass a naive test and starve every consumer that reads the workbench.

**And one detail the comparison settled:** the accumulator at `022D91A0` holds the sum **without**
the translation row — the result is that value plus `M[3][c]`. Depositing the finished value there
fails all 123 point cases on that buffer and no other.

### The tests were changed by the mutation score; the source was not

First run: **17 of 20**, three survivors, all `< 4` → `< 5`. Each writes one element past a `Vec4`
or `Mat4` — **UB the comparison could not see**, because the harness reads back only `sizeof` bytes.
**Canaries after every output buffer in the driver** killed two of the three → 19 of 20.

**The last one is left alive deliberately.** It overruns *locals inside the reconstruction*, and the
16-byte copy out means the extra lane never reaches the interface — benign in this build's stack
layout rather than genuinely equivalent. **Killing it would require canaries in production code to
satisfy a test.** The instrument was strengthened where that was legitimate and the source was left
alone where it was not.

### What was deliberately not claimed

**That the subsystem is `RECONSTRUCTION READY`.** Two leaf primitives are implemented; the **156
call sites** around them are not, and none was read.

**That the reconstruction models the workbench globals.** It takes them as parameters and names the
physical addresses in its header. **The mapping is the caller's**, and no caller is reconstructed.

**That the surviving mutant is equivalent.** It is UB whose effect this build discards; a different
stack layout would have killed it, and the page says so.

## 2026-09-10 — the `memberMask` writer was four functions away, and a reset claim was its own arithmetic misread (FABLE)

First package under the three-agent protocol: `FABLE-EE2`, the queued lead. `EE-2` asked what
writes a spawn group's `memberMask`, because a BSS ledger with a zero mask completes on the first
death and the 2026-09-08 read of six bodies found no writer.

### The cheapest route was the index that already existed

`global_refs` — RIP-relative only, so a negative from it is worthless, but its positives are
trustworthy — listed **six** functions taking the ledger's address, and four were unread:
`00306E60`, `00307030`, `003070E0`, `00307110`. Before believing "six", the range was re-scanned
from every function entry with both addressing forms (`data_xref_scan.py --range`, control
`02089340` = 126): six. The four bodies, their callers, and the two that write the unit's group byte
were then read from the shipped EXE.

### What FF12 does

- `00306E60(unit, add)` sets (`add != 0`) or clears one unit's slot bit in its group's `memberMask`
  and **clears the unit's dead bit either way**, behind the death handler's own gates and slot
  resolution, with the same sign-extended 32-bit shift.
- Its `add` caller `00239710` has one caller, the wrapper for **script verb `0x3030`
  `btlAtelSetEventFlagGroup`**. `00239710` is also the **only byte writer** of `+0xE98` (group) and
  `+0xE99` (mode bits: bit 0 = `mode == 1`, bit 1 = `mode == 2`) — a from-entry displacement sweep
  with a positive control on the `00239746` write found no other; the one other `+0xE98` writer is
  a qword store inside a long zeroing run over a different object.
- Its `remove` caller is range retirement, `002350C0` at `002352BB` with `edx = 0`.
- **The reset zeroes `memberMask`.** The contract's §7 said it did not. The 2026-09-08 reading had
  tabulated the eight qword stores *and* recorded the `+0x10` bias, then read `rax-0x10` as if `rax`
  were the entry base. Re-tabulating each store against the bias puts two stores in every entry —
  one per mask. Corrected in the contract with the old text struck through.
- The two completion arms are two routes to one ledger flag: mode 1 raises it at once with event
  `0x2005`; otherwise unit bit 47 is set with event `0x2008`, and the reaction handler's jump table
  (decoded from the image: `0x2007/0x2008/0x200C/0x200E` → case `00325185`) clears bit 47 and raises
  the flag. `00307030` consumes every raised flag once per field frame and posts the group number
  to `u16` slot 3 of the table at `*(02098E68)`. Bit 47 is touched at **four** sites in the whole
  image (immediate-operand sweep, controls the two arm sites).
- The three prologue calls are an event lock: capability row 12 bits, party suppression,
  `02089340` bits `0x20`/`0x80`. **No one-shot, no rewards** on the path; a repeat completion needs a
  respawned member to re-register.

So the answer to *"when, relative to the first death"* is **whenever the member's own script says
so** — the engine has no populator, and the ledger is rebuilt by script after every area init.

### The int pop is silent on empty — a contract corrected against itself

A review lead said the two value-stack pops fail differently on an empty stack. The bytes agree:
`00267E10` returns `0` with no `008620C0` call and no depth change (`00267E18`→`00267E3B`);
`00267DB0` reports and returns `0.0f`. The bridge contract (§4, §10, §12) said both report; the
verb-dispatch page said the opposite, correctly, since 2026-09-08. **Two documents disagreed for two
days and no checker fired**, because the contradiction is not expressed through an address —
`check_self_contradiction.py`'s own docstring names that blind spot. Corrected in the contract,
`EF-6` answered, the calling-convention pseudocode's `<failure path>` filled in. Nothing downstream
implements the pops.

### Instruments

- `data_xref_scan.py --range` with control — the negative "six and only six".
- `field_disp_scan.py`, new in the kit: from every function entry, memory operands with a given
  displacement, read/write classified, **refuses to answer without its control**. One bounded slice
  of frontier item `F-6`, not the index.
- an immediate-operand sweep for the bit-47/bit-33 masks and `bt*` counts (kept in
  `Tools/work/FABLE/bit47_scan.py`; its eight rows are in the system page).
- the `003250F0` jump table, decoded from the index-byte and offset-dword tables in the image
  rather than from a decompiler's switch.

### What was deliberately not claimed

The script-side argument order of the verb (`(group, mode)` by the pop-order law; no decompiled
script — the `.ebp` files on hand are containers the decompiler rejects unpacked, `EE-11`); what
the row-12 bits, the `0x30B` message and slot 3's reader mean (`EE-7`–`EE-9`); any runtime
observation (request `FABLE-REQ-ASTRA-LEDGER`). `EE-6` is closed only by reference: the gate is the
authored kind byte, and its meaning is that page's question.

### Handoffs

`FABLE.md`: the unit-field table for OPUS (`FABLE-REQ-OPUS-UNITGROUP`), the two predicted runtime
reads for ASTRA, and the exact callback sequence ASTRA's `ASTRA-GROUP-REQUEST` asked for — three
callees in order with `ecx = 1`, then one dispatch `(unit, 0x2005 | 0x2008, 0)`, identical on any
repeat.

## 2026-09-10 — the deferred arm's consumer has no static route, found four hours after publishing it (FABLE)

Starting the next package (the frame chain) meant asking how `00233F70` and `003250F0` are reached,
since neither has a caller. `00233F70` is simple: `ActorSystem_BindBattleUnitsForEligibleRecords`
takes its address (`00265A4F lea r13`) and stores it into the actor record at `+0x38`
(`00265AA8`) — a per-actor callback, exactly the mechanism the evidence standard's *"a function's
address need not be stored anywhere"* section describes.

`003250F0` is not simple. Every route the standard lists was run **boundary-free over all of
`.text`** with positive controls — `E8`, `E9`, both `LEA` encodings — plus whole-file searches for
64-bit pointers and for 32-bit VA/RVA words: **nothing targets it**, nor its neighbours `00325090`
and `00325260` (`BattleUnit_HandleActionTimelineEvent`, 1,215 B), while the functions on either side
are reached by ordinary calls. And the event those handlers would consume goes somewhere else:
`003299B0` stores it at actor-work `+0xF0` and hands it to the animation layer
(`002EB030` → `002EB0D0` → `00427320`).

**So the morning's EE-3/EE-4 answer described what `003250F0` does if it runs, and nothing shows it
runs.** As read, a mode ≠ 1 completion sets bit 47, plays `0x2008` and never raises the ledger flag.
The system page, the contract and the two rows now carry that caveat; `EE-12` is filed, and the
discriminating runtime observation — one hardware breakpoint on `00325260` in any fight, with the
stack on the first hit — is `FABLE-REQ-ASTRA-HANDLERS` at P1, because a hit would mean a dispatch
route invisible to every static instrument this database has.

**What was wrong in the first version:** not the bytes read, but treating a jump-table case inside a
function as a live route without first asking whether the function is entered. The standard's
route-enumeration rule was applied to the *target* of the route, not to its *source*.
## 2026-09-10 — the world tick, the field frame, and how the per-unit frame is reached (FABLE-FRAME1)

Chosen because the two orchestrators the group-completion family hangs off — `World_UpdateSimulationTick`
and `BattleSystem_RunFieldFrameOrchestrator` — were cited by three pages each, all at their entry,
and no page owned the ordering. Update ordering is a charter §26 criterion.

### What FF12 does

- **Three frame modes tick the world with different arguments.** The field frame (mode 2) passes
  `0`; the full-menu and capture frames (modes 3, 5) pass `1` under their `ATEL CONTROL` label.
  Mode 0 runs **sixteen sub-steps over five actor-manager slots**, sub-steps 1–15 only for slots
  whose `+0x201` byte is set — the per-manager bitmask the cutscene-slots page traced to two
  script commands. Mode 1 ticks slots 3–4 once. **The field frame is slot-0-only, so nothing on
  the battle layer advances behind the menu.**
- **The field frame is 23 ordered steps**, every one cited: clock advance and the "did not move"
  bit, the `0x0B` / `0x18` / `0x17` UI-request latches with their party-state predicates read, the
  capability reconciliation, a per-unit reset loop that runs every second frame by a bit-3 parity,
  eleven subsystem steps including the group-completion dispatch, and the party-follow solve.
- **The per-unit lifecycle frame is a callback.** Its address is materialised at exactly one `lea`
  in the image (`00265A4F`, boundary-free sweep with controls), stored at actor record `+0x38` when
  a unit is bound, and called at `0025E222` inside the actor drive loop under four record-bit
  gates. Inside it, unit flag bit 4 is "simulated", bit 1 a no-op, bit 3 required, bit 16 must be
  clear; the active path ends in range retirement, the idle path in teardown on bit 33.

### Instruments

The same boundary-free `.text` sweep that found the deferred completion arm's consumer
unreachable found the unit frame's single `lea` — the two results were produced by one instrument
in one run, which is the control the negative needed. `check_caller_claims --addr` on every caller
count the page states (control `memcpy` 632).

### What was deliberately not claimed

What the fifteen extra sub-steps are for, what the three UI requests are, what the tail's three
large callees do, and what the four unnamed unit flag bits mean — `EX-1`–`EX-7`. Nothing here was
observed at runtime.
## 2026-09-10 — the HP write, read end to end (FABLE-HP1)

`BattleStats_ModifyHPAndProcessLethalState` (`00300530`, 880 B) was named by four pages and decoded
by none — the applier page says so in its own words. It is the one function every damage and heal
ends in, and the page that now owns it reads it to every `ret`.

### What FF12 does

- **Eight flag bits** select the side effects; the applier builds them from the result record's
  `+0x2C` (bits 19 → 8, 10 → 5, `!18` → 6, `!6` → 4) and picks the absolute writer on bit 3; the
  reconcile writer passes `0x217`; the deferred-HP queue committers pass `0`.
- **Two eligibility gates** — the low and high halves of the packed mask the periodic tick already
  named — one before everything, one that skips only the store.
- **Damage to KO / Stone / Vanished is refused** by the writer itself unless field bit 15.
- **The clamp**: floor = battle unit `+0x48` (a scripted "cannot be killed" shape, writers unread),
  cap = max HP, doubled by status bit 28, frozen at `max(old, 1)` by bit 16 (Disease). The
  reconcile writer computes the same cap.
- **Healing from zero clears KO; reaching the floor sets KO** — both through
  `BattleStats_ChangeStatusAndProcessSideEffects` with the mode in the seventh argument (0 / 3).
- **The lethal path** then writes the killer's handle to the victim's `+0x30`, bumps the spawn
  record's death count and second-stamp, calls the group ledger, and plays `0x2007`/`0x2008`
  (or `0x200E`) unless the group completed — the variant chosen by bit 8 of the source's
  target-buffer entry for this target.
- The `sethp` script verbs do not come here; they tail-jump `004738D0`.

### What was deliberately not claimed

Bit 28's name (its help text is in an `st2e` container not decoded here), the floor's writers,
`00469BB0`'s effect and the identity of the pass-through pointer, the reaction table at `01EED300`,
and `004738D0` — `EY-1`–`EY-6`. Nothing observed at runtime.

## 2026-09-10 — the result applier, decoded in execution order (FABLE-APPLY1)

`BattleFormula_ApplyTargetResult` (`003112F0`, 2,040 B) had a shape survey that said, in its own
words, that it did not decode the callees or the order. It now carries a twenty-step decode with
every step cited, and three of the survey's claims corrected:

- **`+0x58` is the remove mask**, not a second apply mask — the seventh argument to `0030E360` is
  mode `3` (set) for `+0x54` and mode `0` (clear) for `+0x58`.
- **`+0x3C`–`+0x41` go to `0030E130`**, the status-*layer* function, in modes 2 and 0 — not to
  `0030E360`; "statuses to remove" withdrawn, the calls recorded.
- **`r14d` — the "anything applied" flag that gates the final recompute — is not set by HP, MP,
  gil, item or timer writes**, only by status and stat changes. A pure damage result never runs
  `0030FED0`.

New in the decode: three per-unit **steal slots** (record `+0x32`–`+0x34` → an item id from the
unit's `+0xE60` object → inventory, and one consumed bit in the spawn record's `+0x14`, matching the
imported name `bStealAvailabilityFlags`), a direct item add at `+0x38`, a **gil deduction** at
`+0x08`, the source's own HP/MP numbers with their flag mapping, the level-advance calls at
`+0x11C`/`+0x11D`, the `0x34` sound on `+0x140` bit 14, and the two transient "being applied" bits on
the unit. `EZ-1`–`EZ-6` filed. Status raised to DOCUMENTED; the page's earlier falsification pass
stands.

## 2026-09-10 — the status write, read end to end (FABLE-STATUS1)

`BattleStats_ChangeStatusAndProcessSideEffects` (`0030E360`, 1,323 B) had its mode table and its
three terminal cases read by two pages and nothing else. The rest is now read and the whole function
is in execution order in its own page:

- **the party-side shortcut** — a kind-0, type `0x1B..0x27` unit given KO / Stone / Vanished goes
  straight to defeat cleanup with no mask write, no event and no rewards;
- **two per-status arrays nobody had seen**: `+0xBC[32]` (u32) and `+0x13C[32]` (u16) on the BKBI
  record, initialised on the `+0x64` modes from the caller or from the authored defaults
  (`status_data +9 × timer scale × 30` for the word), and exactly the slots the applier's
  copy-through lands on;
- **presence is the OR of two words** and nothing fires unless it changed;
- **a status builds its own result record, and in the shipped builders only one transition applies
  it: removing status 28 halves current HP, rounded up** — the second Bubble-shaped mechanic on
  that bit, still unnamed;
- **the cascade**: the definition's `+0x0C` mask — which the field-record page had used only to check
  help-text alignment — clears statuses at runtime, in mode 0 with the recompute deferred;
- **the per-status terminal table** decoded from the image: besides 0 / 1 / 31, statuses 2 and 8
  record a party-side source, 4 fires `0x2001`, 5 and 27 reset action control;
- **the defeat cleanup** raises the party-state requests `0x0B` / `0x18` / `0x17` at once and sets
  `02089340` bits `0x100` / `0x200` / `0x400` / `0x800` — three of them the capability policy page
  lists as unexplained.

`EZ-1` closed by reference to the two-layer page; the applier page's step 14 reworded. `FA-1`–`FA-5`
filed. The page was committed at `612f9c4` while ASTRA held the index files; this entry and the FA

## 2026-09-10 — BattleUnit +0x698 is one type with two homes, keyed by the definition id's class byte (OPUS-CONTRA-BU698)

OPUS's ticket set an equality test against a `BattleSystemState` element (`0031B7B1`) against the
kind-byte page's "spawn record + 0x80". Reading the one installer of the field settles it:
`BattleUnit_ApplyUnitDefinition` splits on the definition id's high byte (`0023A626`, `0023A62E`) —
**1** stores the spawn record's `+0x80` page at `+0x698` and the spawn record at `+0x6A0`; **0**
stores `*(02EBF190) + 8 + index × 0x1C8` at `+0x698` and NULL at `+0x6A0` (`0023AA49`–`0023AC01`).
Both are the same `0x1C8`-byte stats record: `BattleStats_InitializeDefinitionRecord` opens with
`memset(page, 0, 0x1C8)` and writes the whole id into the page's `+4` word (`0023AD8E`), so **the kind
byte at `+5` is the id's class byte** — which closes the kind-byte page's `AL-1`. The same read
located the authored source of the steal slots (`EZ-2`: the enemy row's words `+0x32`–`+0x36`).
Corrections carried into the kind-byte page (a CORRECTED block in §2), the group page and contract,
and the HP page; the type rows are OPUS's.

**Instrument:** the ticket's own counter-evidence was right; the page's reading had followed one of
two paths through the installer without noticing the branch on the class byte.

## 2026-09-10 — how a battle unit is built from its definition (FABLE-UNITDEF1)

The read that resolved the ticket became a page: `BattleUnit_ApplyUnitDefinition` (1,808 B) and
`BattleStats_InitializeDefinitionRecord` (717 B) in execution order. The enemy path resolves the
row in the area's `.ard` enemy table, bounds-checks its four sibling-table selectors, takes the spawn
record from the lane map, initialises the `+0x80` stats page on a fresh record, sets the three
**steal bits** from the row's item words, and bumps a **per-area spawn-history counter** the record
keeps a copy of. The party path takes the row from the party table and the stats record from the
battle-state array; the initialiser gives a character its **five equipment words, its licence nodes
(a 7-bit per-character ownership mask on each licence entry), its level and its gambit preset**.
Both paths zero the HP floor at `+0x48`. `FB-1`–`FB-5` filed.

## 2026-09-10 — a foe's innate augments and starting statuses are script-written; the spawn counters are two banks (FABLE-FOEMASK1)

The recompute's foe sources `unit + 0xE80` / `+0xE90` had no known writer. A from-entry displacement
sweep (control: the recompute's own reads) finds exactly three on battle units — the reset and the
tails of two script verbs:

- **`btlAtelSetAbility` (`0x3000` → `002390B0`)** writes the 128-bit innate source from two popped
  words, **each bit-reversed into its 32-id half** (the authored word's bit 0 is id 31 / id 63);

## 2026-09-10 — CORRECTION: the typed field scanner dropped tracked registers at early-return epilogues (FABLE-SCANFIX1)

`hop_scan.py` treated `mov rbx, [rsp+X]` and `pop rbx` as kills of a tracked register; on a linear
scan those are an early-return epilogue, and the blocks after it still hold the record on the path
that reaches them. Found by tracing the release function (`00234200`), which had no rows. Fixed
(callee-saved restores are no longer kills) and the three maps rerun with controls found:
`BattleUnit` 1,463 → **1,777** rows (144 → 163 offsets, 310 → 328 functions); `BattleStatsRecord`
1,268 → **1,281** (85 offsets, 283 → 285 functions); `SpawnRecord` hop route 118 → **358** (the rows
above `+0x80` being the stats page). **No untouched-range claim changed** on any page. The two
generated pages and their tables are rebuilt; the spawn page carries a CORRECTED note; the contract's
item-6 note is updated; `--only ADDR` tracing stays in the script.

**Instrument:** a linear-disassembly scan is path-insensitive; a kill rule that is right for a
straight-line program is wrong across an early `ret`. The control found at the first run did not
catch it because the control function had no early-return block before its access.

## 2026-09-11 — no load-side checksum: a controlled negative (FABLE-PUB56); SAVENEST answered

The executable never recomputes or compares a loaded save image's CRC-32: the helper has two
callers (both write-side), its polynomial appears as an immediate only inside it, the one CRC
table belongs to zlib's `crc32_little` and is reached only from hashing helpers, and the census
shows the checksum field written once and read never. Each method's positive hit is stated
beside the negative; the function-list gap and a non-standard table are the stated limits.
OPUS-CONTRA-SAVENEST answered in the inbox: migrate (A) — the payload map is a census, the store
describes each byte once, element accesses inside declared arrays stay census rows.

## 2026-09-12 — the runtime-evidence layer is half-invisible to its own instruments (OPUS-RUNTIME-CLAIM-AUDIT)

**Scope:** every contract's §13 against every experiment record, in both directions, past what
`check_contract_runtime.py`'s implementation tests. **Tool run:** that checker reports
`UNDERSTATED 0 · OVERSTATED 0 · UNLINKED 2 · PROSE 0`, exit 1 — a board that reads clean.

**It is clean over a corpus missing half its records, and this is the finding.**

| measurement | value |
|---|---:|
| experiment records under `_experiments/` | **76** |
| records with **no YAML frontmatter at all** | **38** |
| the frontmatter-less run | **`EXP-037` … `EXP-074`, consecutive** |
| records outside that run without frontmatter | **0** — `EXP-001`…`036` and `075`/`076` all have it |
| records naming a contract by path (what the checker can link) | **9** |
| contracts citing any experiment | **6 of 37** |
| contracts citing any of `EXP-037`…`074` | **0 of 37** |
| records in `EXP-037`…`074` naming a contract anywhere, frontmatter or body | **0 of 38** |

**The link is absent in both directions for exactly the frontmatter-less run.** Not one contract
cites one of those 38, and not one of those 38 names a contract — so this is not a stale key the
checker refuses to resolve. It is a convention that stopped at `EXP-037` and resumed at `EXP-075`,
and while it was stopped the records could not be indexed, given a machine-readable `status:`, or
linked to the systems they are about.

**They are not trivial records.** Their own titles: *original target-buffer append boundaries*,
*attacker registration ends at a reset boundary*, *original action MP-cost calculation*,
*scratch-to-result-to-native-MP composition*, *save checksum recurrence, covered bytes and source
buffer*, *original facing writer boundary and callback controls*, *procedural RNG steps, scratch
writes and exact rounding*, *original UI router dispatch and policy gates*. That is isolated
original-code evidence about subsystems that have contracts — `battle-target-buffer`,
`commit-action`, `save-image-buffers`, `facing-and-steering`, `gameplay-generators` — and none of it
reaches them.

**Two instruments are therefore narrower than they read:**

- **`check_contract_runtime.py`** links by the record's own `contract:` key. Its clean board is over
  the 38 records that have frontmatter. **Its control passes** — `CONTRACT-field-music-selection` is
  linked by two records, and the run exits 2 if it is not — so the matcher works and the corpus is
  what is missing. A checker cannot report a record it cannot parse, and this one does not claim to.
- **`check_gate26.py`**'s *"5 of 37 live"* has the same denominator problem from the other side. It
  classifies each contract's §13 **prose**, so it is not blind to a contract that carries live
  evidence without an experiment record — `CONTRACT-input-name-registry` is exactly that, classed
  live on `walk_name_registry.py` and `integration_name_registry.py` against the running game, with
  no `EXP` record at all. But nothing checks a §13's live claim **against** a record, so the 5 is
  neither a floor nor a ceiling: it is a reading of prose.

**Live evidence lives in three places and only one of them is indexed:** experiment records, tool
scripts cited in a §13 and nowhere else, and §13 prose. `OPUS-NOTICE-EXPERIMENT-FRONTMATTER` routes
the first to ASTRA, who own `_experiments/`.

**Overstatement: none found, and the search is stated so the negative is readable.** Every contract
citing an experiment cites one that exists (`001`, `005`/`006`, `008`/`009`, `011`/`014`/`019`,
`013`), and the two `UNLINKED` rows are the record's key being stale rather than the contract
inventing evidence. **No contract claims a live observation this audit could not find support for.**
That is a real negative over the 6 contracts that cite anything; it is **not** a statement about the
31 that cite nothing, which this audit cannot distinguish from having no runtime evidence at all.

**Propagation:** no contract corrected — nothing was found overstated. The two `UNLINKED` rows and
the 38-record run are routed, not fixed here, because `_experiments/` is ASTRA's.
**Structural changes:** none.

## 2026-09-12 — the GHOST ADDRESS class was 100% noise, so a real ghost would have been invisible (OPUS-GHOST-ADDRESS-AUDIT)

`audit_crossrefs.py` is what the evidence standard tells you to run before every falsification pass,
and it reported **22 GHOST ADDRESS findings** — *"cited with a body size but is not a function in the
current program"*, which reads as a physical-integrity failure in twelve documents. **None of the 22
was a document defect.**

**What produced them.** `BODYSIZE` matches a table row shaped `ADDR | description | N B`. A document
that lists a **data block with its size** matches it exactly — the transform primitives' four 16-byte
deposit slots, the log gate's globals, the position-to-scalar deposits, the FST table. **A body size
is a FUNCTION body's size**, so a data address cannot have one and those findings could not have been
defects however the documents were written. Classified against the PE section table: **20 of 22 lie
in `.data` or `.rdata`.**

**The other two were checked by hand, and both documents are right:**

| address | what it is | how it was checked |
|---|---|---|
| `002FE7D0` | a real **106-byte function** — `mov r8,[rcx+0x708]` through `002FE839 ret`, then `int3` padding to `002FE840`, giving an extent of exactly `0x6A` | disassembled. It is absent from the **census**, not from the binary, and `battle-action-handler-table.md` says so in the very row the tool flagged (`AT-3`, FABLE, same day) |
| `00431410` | a **jump table inside `.text`** | its six dwords are `00311401`, `00311390`, `003113A4`, `003113BA`, `003113D2`, `003113FD`, which resolve against the image base to exactly the six addresses the document lists |

**The fix, and why it is not a narrowing.** The check now skips any cited address outside the code
range, which is derived from the census itself and needs no new input. The class falls **22 → 2**,
and both survivors are real observations worth surfacing — one of them a **function the census does
not contain**, which is a fact about the instrument the whole database rests on. Nothing was made to
pass by softening a claim; what changed is a heuristic that was asking data whether it was a function.

> **What this actually attacked, and what it did not.** It attacked the instrument the standard tells
> you to trust *before* you attack a document. A finding class where every member is structurally
> incapable of being a defect does not merely waste attention — **it hides the ones that are**, and it
> had been reporting a clean-looking twelve-document spread the whole time.

**Not touched:** `UNACCOUNTED NEIGHBOUR`, the other 789 findings in the same report, which have not
been sampled and may be sound, noisy, or both. No document was edited by this pass, and no document
gained a falsification pass from it — `audit_crossrefs.py` performs steps 3 and 7 of a pass, not a
pass.
**Structural changes:** `audit_crossrefs.py` only.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the render-record pool: SURVIVED, and it was missing its own termination argument (OPUS-RENDER-POOL-PASS-1)

The first falsification pass this database has recorded on a **contract**. Every contract sat at
`passes: 0`; this one is now at 1. Peer-authored, `L1`, five operations over a 160-slot pool with
four indices, a free cursor and a live count — the invariants live *between* the functions, which is
what makes it worth attacking.

**All five invariants were attacked by naming the killer and going looking for it, and all five
hold**, each at the exact instruction the document cites:

| # | the killer | what the binary says |
|--:|---|---|
| 1 | the two emptiness tests read the same field | `00427A18` is `headPending` (`+0x48810`), `0042882A` is `headActive` (`+0x48800`) — two lists, and the offsets are tail-relative as §3 says |
| 2 | the ceiling is `>`, another constant, or after the increment | `004279E9 cmp dword [rbx+0x4880C], 0xA0 / jge` returning 0, with the `inc` at `00427A7F` — after |
| 3 | one release path stores something other than zero | `00429140` is literal; `00427C90` stores `ebp`, and `00427CBA xor ebp, ebp` is the only write to it before the use |
| 4 | promotion touches `liveCount` | no access to `+0x4880C` anywhere in `00428710` |
| 5 | the scan tests another offset, or a release leaves `+0x284` set | `00427AD2` compares `[record+0x284]` against a zeroed `eax`; `0042049A` sets `0x2010F9`; both releases reach `0041F730`'s whole-record `memset` |

**What the pass added.** The free-cursor advance at `00427AB0`–`00427ADA` has **no iteration bound**,
and the document had every piece of why it terminates without ever joining them: invariant 2
guarantees a free slot exists, and `0041F730` opens with `memset(record, 0, 0x740)`. The hardest
attack was to look for **a release that decrements `liveCount` without resetting the record** — the
one thing that would make that loop spin forever. It failed, but not trivially: `00427C90` **does not
call `0041F730` at all**. It calls `004200A0 CharacterRenderRecord_TeardownAndReset`, which calls it
in turn, and §7's wording reads as though the release path calls the reset itself.

**What was tried and did not break it, recorded because an unrecorded audit did not happen:** the
pool arithmetic recomputed (`160 × 0x740 + 0x130 = 0x48930`, the stated allocation); every stated
body size re-checked against the current census (**no drift**); a banned-evidence sweep for `.pdata`,
`.xdata`, unwind, EH-map and IP-to-state (**nothing**); and `audit_crossrefs.py`, which reports **no
findings** for this document — so `crossref_clean` is now true rather than assumed.

> **One pass is one pass, and `AUDITED` is not `true`.** The five operations are still **unexecuted**
> — this contract's §13 pilot does not exist — so everything above rests on reading instructions, and
> reading is what two pilots refuted within the hour earlier the same day.
**Structural changes:** none.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the movement body pool: SURVIVED, and it had a fifth consumer it never named (OPUS-BODY-POOL-PASS-1)

The central claim is a **universal** — *every* consumer in the creation sequence re-loads the chain
and guards each hop, which is why the 129th actor loses collision instead of crashing. Universals are
the most attackable thing a document can say, so that is what was attacked: the sequence at
`002E3500` was walked and every callee's first dereference read.

**It holds, and the guards are explicit.** `00269EC0` tests `+0xC0` then `+0x138`; `002682D0` tests
`rcx`, `+0xC0`, `+0x138` *and* `+0x30`; `002685F0` tests both and substitutes `xorps xmm0, xmm0` on
the miss; `00268380` tests both at `002683AD`/`002683BD`. The allocator's silence holds exactly:
`003DA8B5 cmp dx, r9w` against `0xFFFF` reaches `003DA9DF mov rax, rsi` with `rsi` zeroed at
`003DA8AD`, then `ret` — **no flag, no global, no other write** — and `int3` padding at `003DA9E8`
confirms the 328-byte extent. The layout argument recomputes: `0x02B4E4C0 + 128 × 0x130 = 0x02B57CC0`
with the free head four bytes past it.

**TWO ADDITIONS.**

**There are five consumers, not four.** `002E3558 call 002681D0` sits between `00269EC0` and
`002682D0`, and `002681D0` was **absent from `entries` and unmentioned anywhere in the document**. It
is ten bytes — `test rcx, rcx / jne / ret` — tail-jumping to a body that re-loads `+0xC0` and tests
it. **The omission hid evidence FOR the contract's central claim**, which is the easiest kind of gap
to leave and the least likely to be noticed by a reader who already agrees with the conclusion.

**"Guards each hop" is exact for the first dereference and generous for the rest.** `00268380`
re-loads `+0xC0` and `+0x138` three further times — `002684BB`/`002684C5`, `002684D1`/`002684DB`,
`002684E7` — **without re-testing**. That is safe by domination, not by guarding: every path into
those loads passes the earlier `je 0x26851E`, and the only branch from before it lands *on* the
guard.

> **Still unexecuted.** No pilot drives any of these eight functions. The pass establishes that the
> document says what the instructions say, not that the instructions do what anyone expects.
> `crossref_clean` stays **false** — this pass did not run that tool clean against this document.
**Structural changes:** none.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the transform workbench: the exact count reproduces, and "nesting cannot happen" is true for a better reason (OPUS-WORKBENCH-PASS-1)

**Two claims here are the most falsifiable kind** — an exact image-wide count, and a negative about
nesting. Both hold.

**The count.** §15 says *"the depth counter is touched by exactly four instructions image-wide"*.
Re-derived by disassembling **every function in the census from its own entry** — 38,161 functions,
**1,787,590 instructions, none skipped** — every RIP-relative operand landing in the region's first
sixteen bytes: **`022D8F08` has exactly four** (`0036D8E6` and `0036D912` read, `0036D91A` zeroes,
`0036D982` writes), and `022D8F0C` four bytes later has **nine**, seven in `FUN_00501820` and two in
`FUN_00502280` — which is §15's *other* claim, now with its functions named. **The document's care in
separating `+0x08` from `+0x0C` is why both are true**: a sweep of "the region" returns 13.

**The nesting negative holds for a stronger reason than it states.** *"Nesting cannot happen on the
direct call graph"* reads as though the nine users do not reach one another. **They do** —
`0044BAC0` transitively reaches six of the other eight. Nesting needs a user called **while the
workbench is held**, so each user's Save-to-Restore window was measured: **four calls inside all nine
windows combined, none to a user, none to anything that reaches one, and NOT ONE INDIRECT CALL in
any window.** `0044BAC0`'s single inside-call is `sqrtf`. That guarantee does not depend on the call
graph being complete, which the original phrasing does.

**A new structural fact: four of the nine restore by TAIL JUMP** — `0026EE00` at `0026F413`,
`003AFDD0` at `003AFFAB`, `00431D30` at `00431F0A`, `00462260` at `0046242E`, each `jmp 0036D8E0` as
its last act. The other five use `call`.

**Two instrument failures of my own, recorded so they are not repeated.** A **linear** sweep of
`.text` returned **zero** references to the depth counter — a spectacular refutation that was
entirely my bug, because capstone's `disasm` stops at the first undecodable byte and an 8 MB linear
pass ends in the first padding it meets. **A sweep that returns zero should be suspected before the
document is.** And counting only `call` sites dropped four of the nine users as unmatched pairs,
which is how the tail-jump fact surfaced.

> **Still unexecuted for the negatives.** §15's first five claims carry isolated original-code
> evidence; the rest are static, and this pass read instructions rather than running them.
**Structural changes:** none.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the HP write: the cross-subsystem claim is exact, and about a hundred and fifty times bigger than it says (OPUS-HP-WRITE-PASS-1)

§15 claims *"the same `0x80000003` mask with the same bit-15 override guards the gambit condition
evaluation"* — a **cross-subsystem** claim, which is where contradictions hide. Read at both ends,
it is not merely true, it understates itself:

```asm
00300621  mov eax,[rsi+0x64] / or eax,[rsi+0x3c] / test eax,0x80000003 / je / call 0x377c20 / test / je
0030152B  mov eax,[rcx+0x64] / or eax,[rcx+0x3c] / test eax,0x80000003 / je / call 0x377c20 / test / je
```

**The same five instructions, the same two status words, the same callee, the same branch shape** —
one composed predicate, not one shared constant. And the override has a name: `00377C20`
**`FieldData_GetActiveFieldRecordBit15`**, so *the active field record's bit 15* decides whether a
downed combatant is still actionable and still harmable.

**What the pass adds is the scale.** `0x80000003` appears at **173 instructions image-wide**, about
150 of them in battle, AI, menu, enmity, reward, perception and party code —
`BattleMenu_BuildCommandEntryList`, `BattleEnmity_WriteForCombatantId`,
`Reward_ComputeExperienceForRecipient`, `BattleUnit_RunPeriodicCombatMaintenance` among them. **It is
not a rule with two ends; it is the engine's universal downed-combatant predicate.** For anyone
changing what "downed" means, that is the number that matters.

**Verified at the exact cited instructions:** gate 3 skips only the store (`00300740 call 0x30B8E0`
→ `00300747 jne 0x30074D`, landing past the store and nowhere else); the store is
`00300749 mov dword ptr [rsi+0x48], r14d`; and damage landing exactly on the floor is death, because
`0030078E` is **`jg`** — equal falls through to the death path.

**Mechanical:** no body-size drift against the current census; banned-evidence sweep clean; every
cited entry resolves and the 79 further citations are instruction sites inside them.

> **This pass read instructions.** The contract's executed claims were executed by its own pilot and
> were not re-run here, and claim 14 stays static **by the contract's own words** — *"in a different
> function, which this contract's pilot does not execute."* The 173-site census is static too.
**Structural changes:** none.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the manager slot entry tables: the A/B asymmetry is in the mechanism, not the value (OPUS-SLOT-TABLES-PASS-1)

Every claim checked at the instruction it cites, and every one holds — the unsigned `ja` at
`003DA41D` and `003DA4D3` (a signed `jg` would accept `0xFFFFFFFF`), the `jae` bound at `003DA434`,
the null test at `003DA423`, the ordering (`003DD265` **above** the checks at `003DD26C`–`003DD282`,
`003DA46E` **below** its own), and the unbounded subscript at `003DA4B1`→`003DA4B9` with nothing
between them.

**The tiling is corroborated from the addressing rather than the arithmetic:**
`003DA446 lea rdi, [rsi + rsi*2]` then `003DA471 mov dword ptr [rbx + rdi*8 + 0x110], edx` is a
**24-byte stride from `0x110`**, and the reverse lookup reads `+0x114` — the entry's own `+0x04`.

**The finding.** *"Side A clamps a negative fifth argument and side B resolves it"* reads as though
the sides do different things to the value. **They do not:**

```asm
003DA45A  xor    ecx, ecx      / 003DA460 test eax, eax / 003DA46E cmovns ecx, eax
003DD261  test   ecx, ecx      / 003DD263 jns … / 003DD265 call 0x5c5230 / 003DD26A mov ecx, eax
```

**`005C5230` is a three-byte retail stub — `xor eax, eax / ret`.** Both sides compute
`(x >= 0) ? x : 0`; A branchlessly and after validation, B through a conditional call to a no-op and
before it. **What a reimplementation must preserve is the call, not the value** — and the call is
observable only in a trace, which is what this contract's pilot already compares on refused inputs.

> **A stub in the ORIGINAL deserves the same care as a stub in a fixture.** The standing rule is
> *"a stub is not proof of its native effects"*; the mirror is that **a shipped no-op is not proof
> of an absent mechanism** either. `005C5230` may have resolved something in a debug build. What can
> be said is what it does in *this* image: nothing, returning zero.

**A second asymmetry, smaller but real:** the two sides validate the record index differently — A
with one unsigned compare that rejects negatives by itself, B with an explicit `js` **plus** a `jae`.
Same rejections, different instructions, and no observable separates them.

**Mechanical:** no body-size drift; banned-evidence sweep clean; all eight entries resolve, every one
reached from `Script_VM_Native_Bridge`.
**Structural changes:** none.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on commit-action: the literal census reproduces to the digit, and "immediate" is the word that makes it true (OPUS-COMMIT-ACTION-PASS-1)

**Every claim checked holds at the instruction it cites**, and two are sharper than written.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the inventory class storage: a PROVEN claim is REFUTED — seven NULL handlers, not four (OPUS-INVENTORY-PASS-1)

**The first claim this sweep has actually broken.** §15 said, at `PROVEN`, *"dispatch is per class
through the handler pointer at `+0x50`, and **four** of the fifteen rows carry NULL"*. The descriptor
table was re-read out of `.data` at the base and stride the contract itself derives —
`00309F67 lea rax, [rip → 01EEBCC0]`, `00309F63 imul rdx, rax, 0x58` — and **seven rows carry a NULL
handler: 5, 7, 9, 10, 11, 13 and 14.**

**The four is a real set, and it is the interesting one**, which is almost certainly what was meant:

| rows | `+0x50` | `+0x3C` | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0, 1, 2 | `002FD8D0` | 64, 420, 512 | the packed-count handler |
| 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 | `002FD970` | 81, 24, 256, 512, 32 | the bitset handler |
| **9, 10, 13, 14** | **NULL** | **512, 256, 128, 4095** | **declare items and answer the default for every id** |
| 5, 7, 11 | NULL | 0 | reject on the bound before the handler is reached |

Corrected **from the binary, not softened**: the row now states seven, and a second row states the
four that matter and why — `00309F96 mov rax, [rdx+0x50]` / `test rax, rax` / `je 0x309FA9` returns
the default, so four declared classes always answer it.

**Claim 9 raised from `HIGH` to `PROVEN`**, because the mechanism reads whole:
`00309F75 and ecx, 0xfff` / `00309F7B mov eax, [rdx+0x3c]` / `00309F7E **dec eax**` /
`00309F80 cmp ecx, eax` / `00309F82 **jg**`. **The `dec` is what makes the claim true** — at
`itemCount 0` the bound is `-1`, and the index is masked non-negative, so every id is rejected. The
signed compare matters because the *bound* can go negative, not because the index can.

**Also checked and holding:** the class nibble refused above `0x0E` (`and ax, 0xF000` / `cmp ax,
0xE000` / `ja`), id `0xFFFF` refused first, **all forty-five storage pointers NULL in the image**
(`+0x08`, `+0x20`, `+0x30` across fifteen rows), and `+0x10 == ceil(+0x3C / 16)` on every bitset row —
81→6, 24→2, 256→16, 512→32, 32→2.

> **`003008A0` has 25 callers across four subsystems.** A miscounted row in this table is not a local
> matter, which is the reason to read the bytes rather than the prose.
**Structural changes:** none.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on party slot assignment: slot −1 is a clean removal, and every other bad slot is corruption (OPUS-PARTY-SLOT-PASS-1)

**A thorough contract. Every claim held at the instruction it cites**, including the two a pass
usually catches: `(slot > 3) + 2` is `00269CE5 movsx eax, bl` / `cmp eax, 3` / `00269CEE **seta** al`
/ `add al, 2` — **unsigned `seta` over a sign-extended operand**, so a negative slot lands on `3`;
and the reader disagreement is **a one-instruction difference**, `00263753 **ja**` bounding unsigned
so `-1` returns NULL against `00263776 **js**` sending `-1` to `00263797 call 0x3590D0` / `jmp
0x3588B0`, **the current focus**.

**Cross-contract:** both readers and the assigner resolve the same roster at `0209A1F0` — the
address [the field runtime pass](../04-Actor-Entity/CONTRACT-field-runtime-pass.md) names for its
four-iteration party walk. Three contracts, one table, no disagreement.

### The refinement

§10 said an out-of-range slot leaves the record *"believing it holds a slot that does not exist"*.
**True of `100`, false of `-1`.** `00269CEB mov byte ptr [rdi+0x12], bl` writes `bl`, and `bl` of
`-1` is **`0xFF`** — the very sentinel §2 defines as **"none"**. With `+0x0F = 3` from the `seta`,
the record ends **byte-for-byte in the state the vacate path writes** at `00269CD5`/`00269CD9`.

**So assigning slot `-1` removes an actor from the party cleanly, and every other out-of-range slot
corrupts it.** All three facts — the skipped install at `00269CDD`, the `bl` store, the `seta` — were
already in the document, each in a different place. **Nothing had put them together**, and the
composition is the fact a reimplementation needs.

**Mechanical:** no body-size drift; banned-evidence sweep clean; all nine entries resolve, and
`00263750` carries **43 callers across five subsystems**.
**Structural changes:** none.

**Two exact image-wide counts, both reproduced with an independently written instrument, and the
contract's own stated control with them.**

| claim | reproduced |
|---|---|
| exactly six functions address the ledger | **six**, one `lea` each, and **zero** image-base-register references — the table is reached only RIP-relatively |
| its control `02089340` | **126** — the number §15 chose in advance |

> strongest thing a census claim can offer, and this contract had already built it in.

**The unreachable arm is not trivial, and that is the point.** `00235F83 movzx eax, dl` /

where the operand came from.**

eax**` / `cmp ebx, eax` / `**jg**` is the *same* bound idiom as `00309F7B`–`00309F82` in the
inventory class storage — **count minus one, compared signed** — and in both, the `dec` is what makes

## 2026-09-12 — the claim ledger recounted: the census was wrong about its population, and the finding it produced was an artefact (OPUS-CLAIM-CENSUS-RECOUNT)

**A tool I published this morning was measuring the wrong rows, and §5 of the audit has been
rewritten from it.** The ledger now reads **634 claims — 3 live, 282 executed, 227 static, 5 corpus,
51 none, 66 unclassified** — replacing **644 / 4 / 251 / 248 / 85**.

**Three population defects, none of them arithmetic** — the fourth time this sweep a count has gone
wrong about *what it was counting*:

| defect | effect |
|---|---|
| the row pattern ran over the **whole of §15** instead of the claim table | **41 non-claim rows counted** — per-slot function maps, and the `§15a` falsification-pass records *this sweep has been adding*, which are themselves `\| claim \| …` tables. **My own new work was corrupting the measurement.** |
| the row pattern hard-coded **four columns** | **9 real claims invisible** — `CONTRACT-widget-object.md`'s claim table has three |
| cells were split on every `\|` | a markdown-**escaped** pipe inside a claim — ``presence is `+0x3C \| +0x64` `` — shifted every column to its right |

625 correctly-counted rows + 9 invisible = **634**, now checked row-for-row against the tables rather
than taken from a total: **634 body rows selected, 634 counted, zero dropped.**

### The retraction matters more than the recount

**§5 previously reported THREE §15 schemas and named eight contracts to normalise. There is one
schema.** All 42 claim tables carry `\| claim \| evidence \| tier \| confidence \|`; the "schemas"
were rows lifted out of *other* tables in §15. Before the recount I had inspected those same eight
and concluded their third column held a *richer* compound class — that conclusion was drawn from
mis-attributed rows and is withdrawn.

**The real defect is inside the one schema, and it is worse.** The column named `tier` holds two
different vocabularies: **330 rows put an evidence CLASS in it, 272 put a number**, and **8 contracts
use both in a single table**. These grade different things — [`EVIDENCE-STANDARD.md`](EVIDENCE-STANDARD.md)'s
tiers 1–11 grade the **kind of source**, the class grades **how the claim was established** — so a
row states one axis and leaves the other unrecorded.

> **266 of the 272 numeric rows are tier 1 — 48 of them citing an executed pilot, 218 not.** A claim
> proved by *running the original code* and a claim *read off the instructions* are the **same
> tier**. So the tier column cannot answer [COMPLETION-PLAN.md](COMPLETION-PLAN.md) §1 even in
> principle, and that is where **all 66 unclassified claims** come from.

**The prescription inverts.** §5 told a reader to normalise eight documents; normalising them would
**delete the stronger statement 330 rows are making**. What the tables need is an added `class`
column beside `tier`. That is a schema change across **42 peer-owned contracts**, so it is registered
as **`SC-1`** in [OPEN-QUESTIONS.md](OPEN-QUESTIONS.md) and **not made unilaterally** — it needs an
owner's decision and one mechanical pass, not 42 incidental edits.

**Structural changes:** `claim_census.py` rewritten (table selected by header and taken **first**, not
last; columns located **by name**; escaped pipes respected; a `schema_overload` report added so the
tool states the finding that produced it). §5 of `RECONSTRUCTION-GRADE-AUDIT.md` rewritten by hand —
the generator emits 35 lines and would discard it. The retracted paragraph in `PROGRAM-STATE.md` is

**Not claimed:** nothing here judges whether a claim *earns* the class it states. That is final-audit
pass 8, and §4 of the plan says of the thirty: **"Do not start."** The live figure moved 4 → 3
because of the recount, **not** because live evidence was gained or lost; the pause still holds.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the authored-table row lookup: two numbers reproduced exactly, and that is what makes the third worth correcting (OPUS-PASS-AUTHORED-TABLE-ROW-LOOKUP)

**`audit_coverage` 182 → 183 of 317. OVERALL 44.09 %.** The largest contract still at `passes: 0`.

**The suspicion was the population** — `movzx r, word [reg+8]` and `mov r32, [reg+0xC]` are among the
commonest addressing patterns in any C++ image, so a census of them is evidence about *this* record
only if it is confined to the shape. **Refuted:** image-wide the patterns give **1377 reads in 694
functions** and **4898 in 2028**, far above the document's 566/264 and 1100/227. The census is not
image-wide.

**So I implemented the document's own criterion instead** — a register tainted by
`mov R64, [rip → slot]`, taint carried through 64-bit moves and killed by any other write; the
reference half is `mov ecx, [taintedR + 0x0C]` *reaching* `call 0020E600`; the stride half is a u16
at `[taintedR + 8]`; a slot qualifies when **one** function shows both — and ran it over the whole
band `02EBEF70`–`02EBF3FC`, 146 qword slots, disassembling **per function** (38,161 functions,
1,787,590 instructions, **0 skipped**).

| the document says | this pass measures | |
|---|---|---|
| 40 registry slots are headers of this shape | **40** | exact |
| 226 functions perform the lookup | **226** | exact |
| the reference is read in 227 functions | **227** — the 226 that resolve plus one that reads the stride and does not | exact, **and it dissolves the 226/227 gap I was about to report as an inconsistency** |

**Control:** `02EBF118`, the worked instance's slot, shows `+0x0C` ×43 and `+0x08` ×42 and reaches the
resolver 42 times. The instrument sees halves where they exist.

### Corrected: no slot shows a single half

§15 said *"exactly one slot in the band shows a single half"*. **Zero do.** Every slot shows **both**
halves or **none**. The four in dispute — `02EBF078`, `02EBF0D0`, `02EBF160`, `02EBF170` — show **no
read at all** through a register tainted by them: `02EBF170` is referenced 58 times and every one is
a null test or a pass to a binder (`movsxd rdx, [rax+0xF8]` then `call 003846F0`), never a field read.
**The model's limit is stated in the document**: register taint does not follow a header spilled to
the stack or passed through a call — but the same model reproduces the document's own 40 and 226
exactly, which is the control that makes the disagreement mean something.

### Corrected: §7's map is not the roster behind the 40

35 mapped rows + 4 bespoke-binder slots = **39**, and the two sets are not nested. **Three mapped
slots never qualify** (`02EBF078`, `02EBF160`, `02EBF170`); **four qualifying slots appear nowhere in
§7** (`02EBF120`, `02EBF140`, `02EBF148`, `02EBF150`). Overlap **36**. The count is right and the
enumeration is a different set — consistent with §7's own "the map is the direct part", but a reader
counting its rows to check the 40 will not get it. §7 now says so.

### Left open rather than closed: the stride census's 264

Only **227** functions read the stride of a registry header at all, and 226 of those resolve. **264 is
wider than the shape and narrower than image-wide (694), and five stated populations** — 694, 301,
252, 233, 227 — **give none of them.** It is plausibly the shape plus functions receiving the header
as a *parameter*, which would be legitimate, but the document does not record which population it is,
so it cannot be reproduced from what is written. **The claim does not rest on it**: the stride is
established by `00387707` and by the executing suite, so the row stays `PROVEN` with its evidence
qualified rather than being demoted on a count nobody can check.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the sound request: there are five resolvers, not four (OPUS-PASS-SOUND-REQUEST)

**A bolded `PROVEN` claim refuted, and the reason it was wrong is worth more than the number.**

### Reproduced exactly, by a third instrument

Capstone over `functions.tsv`, **per function** (38,161 functions, 1,787,590 instructions, **0
skipped**), classifying each rip-relative reference as READ / WRITE / LEA from the operand rather
than from a pattern — deliberately different from the source page's §10 and from `data_xref_scan.py`,
because **two instruments agreeing is worth less when they may share an assumption**.

| the document says | measured |
|---|---|
| the gate `02091098` has exactly four references, one a write | **4** — `00249C64`, `00249CA4`, `0024A1A6` read, `00249FC0` writes |
| handle A `02AEF3FC` 5 refs · handle B `02AEF400` 4 refs | **5** and **4** |
| the table `lea` resolves to `02AEEDC0` in all four resolvers | it does |

### Refuted: `003A1240` is a fifth resolver

66 bytes, the same arithmetic on the same table: `movzx r8d, cx` / `lea rax, [r8+r8*2]` /
`lea r8, [rip → 02AEEDC0]` / `movzx r9d, word [r8+rax*8+8]` / `or` with `+0xA` / `cmp` against the
argument with bit 31 cleared / **`shl r9d, 9`** (×512) / `lea eax, [rdx+r9]` — and it carries the
same provably dead sign test the contract already documents in the other four.

> **Why it was missed.** Every known resolver names one of the three handle **globals**, so a census
> anchored on those globals returns exactly four *and its control passes*. `003A1240` takes its
> handle **as a parameter** and touches no handle global. **A census keyed on the data cannot find a
> function that never names the data.** That is the same failure mode as every other miscount in
> this sweep: wrong about the population, right about the arithmetic.

**The suite does not cover it.** §13 runs six bodies and this is not one of them; the contract now
says so rather than implying coverage. §13's own "four resolvers" wording was **left alone** — it
describes what the suite runs, and inflating it to five would have manufactured coverage.

### Qualified: "the table is exactly 64 entries" is not established by its evidence

Every claim in this contract names an address and an instruction, so each was checked **where it
stands**: `0059A3C6 mov ebp, 0x54` (84 bytes read); `0059A3E2 lea eax, [rbp - 0x4b]` — `0x54 − 0x4B =

**0 occurrences across `.text`'s 7,997,440 raw bytes**, so the zero is real and not a wrong-section
artefact. But **`RYHP` occurs 7 times**: the compared constant is `0x50485952`, which in little-endian
memory *is* the bytes `R Y H P`.

> A reader who greps for `PHYR`, finds nothing and concludes the engine never names the marker would
> be wrong twice — it names it seven times, spelled the other way round. **A negative is only as good
> as the spelling it was tested in.** The row now carries both numbers.

[rsi+0x50]`. The substance ("not a dword loop") is right and the instruction count was half the real
one. The useful part is the arithmetic it exposes: **5 × 16 + 4 = 84**, so the copy **re-derives the
header size** independently of the reflection registrations and of `mov ebp, 0x54`.

`0059A4E6`, a dataflow argument this pass did not repeat. The branch's existence and target are
confirmed; its unreachability is left as the document has it — recorded so the distinction is not

### The "family is 0..15 by construction" argument, completed

§15 cited `0025E5AF movzx ebx, byte [r14+2]`. **That instruction alone loads a byte, which could not
produce `id >> 12` at all.** The construction is four:

```asm
0025E5AF  movzx ebx, byte [r14+2]   ; high byte, zero-extended
0025E5B4  movzx eax, byte [r14+1]   ; low  byte, zero-extended
0025E5B9  shl   bx, 8
0025E5BD  or    bx, ax              ; a 16-bit id in ebx, upper half zero
```

Both halves are zero-extended and the result is 16 bits, **so bit 31 is guaranteed clear** — which is
exactly why `00262205 sar r12d, 0xc` is safe: on this value an arithmetic and a logical shift cannot
differ. The row cited one instruction; the guarantee needs all four, and it holds.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the script-to-native bridge: each pop reports one failure, and they report opposite ones (OPUS-PASS-SCRIPT-BRIDGE)

**`audit_coverage` 194 → 195 of 318.** Every claim names a body or an instruction, and every one
reproduced where it stands: `00267F63`/`00267F93` both `cmp eax, 0x3f / jge` (**63 slots**); both
pushes `mov dword [rcx+rax*4+0x84], 0`; `lea r8, [rax+rax*4]` then `*8` = **stride 40** with the value
at `+0x0C`; `0026B4F0` writes tag **2** in `VMResult_WriteInt32` and `0026B4D6` writes **3** in
`VMResult_WriteFloat32`; both pops take `sub edx, 1 / je` to the int arm and `cmp edx, 1 / je` to the
float arm; and `005103F0` calls `00267E10` twice, the first result becoming `edx` and the second
`r8d`.

> **Tag `2` means FLOAT on the way in and INT on the way out.** The contract has this right, and it
> is worth repeating: the stack vocabulary and the result vocabulary are different and overlap on one
> value — the kind of inversion a reconstruction gets silently wrong.

### Extended: the two pops cover their failure modes in mirror image

§15 records the empty-stack halves. Read whole, each body has **two** failure modes:

| | empty stack | unknown tag |
|---|---|---|
| `00267E10 VMValueStack_PopInt32CoerceFloat32` | `jle 0267E3B` → `xor eax, eax` — **silent** | `0267E31 mov ecx, 1 / call 008620C0` — **reports** |
| `00267DB0 VMValueStack_PopNumericDiscard` | `jle 0267DF2` → `mov ecx, 1 / call 008620C0` — **reports** | `jne 0267DFC` → `xorps` — **silent** |

**Neither reports both; neither is silent about both.** The int pop complains about a tag it cannot
read and says nothing about an empty stack; the float pop does exactly the reverse. On all four paths
the depth word at `[rcx]` is untouched — **a refusal is not a pop**.

That the *empty* halves differ was documented. **That the difference reverses on the other failure
mode was not**, and a reconstruction making either function report both — or neither — would match
the documented behaviour and still be wrong half the time.

### A defect I introduced and caught in the same pass

My first draft wrote the two functions as `PopInt32CoerceFloat32` and `PopNumericDiscard`.
`check_consistency.py` failed immediately: **an abbreviated name is a competing name for that
address**, and the checker counts distinct names per address rather than matching prefixes. Full
names restored, 0 disagreements. Worth recording because it is a cheap mistake to repeat in prose.

`contract_map_sync.py` clean. `check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency` pass.

**Not claimed:** whether tags above 3 exist is still `UNKNOWN`; nothing here is a runtime observation.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the packed namespace: counting `bswap` to audit "nine words" returns five (OPUS-PASS-PHYRE-NAMESPACE)

### The reader, read whole

`0059A6F0` is **116 bytes**, exactly as claimed, and every clause of §15 is visible in it: the only
validation is `test r9d, r9d` and `test r8, r8`; **one** read through the stream vtable at
`0059A723 call qword [rax+0x28]`; `0059A726 add [rbx+0x18], eax` advances `bytesConsumed` **before**
`0059A72B cmp eax, esi`; and `mov ebx, 9` / `cmove ebx, ecx` returns `0` on a full read and `9`
otherwise.

**The swap really does fire on a short read.** `0059A73B`/`0059A740` gate the `call 0059C180` on the
**buffer and the flag only** — `ebx` was decided at `0059A732` and is never consulted again.

### The trap

`0059A780` strides `lea rax, [rax + 0x24]` (**36 bytes**) and swaps **nine** consecutive dwords per
iteration, `[rax-0x2c]` … `[rax-0xc]`. **Only five use the `bswap` instruction.** The other four —
`-0x2c`, `-0x1c`, `-0x18`, `-0x14` — are open-coded as
`shl 0x10` / `and 0xff00` / `or` / `shl 8` / `sar 8` / `sar 0x18` / `movzx`.

> **A reader or tool auditing "nine words" by counting `bswap` finds 5 and reports a defect that is
> not there.** Same family as a constant hoisted into a register, or a sentinel compared through
> `r12w`: **the operation is present; its canonical spelling is not.** That is now three traps of
> this shape in this sweep, and they all punish a detector keyed on one mnemonic.

### Confirmed

Member records stride `[rax + 0x18]` with 14 `bswap` in `0059C180`. The type table's swap **is**
vectorised — `0059A8BE cmp ecx, 8`, then `movdqu`/`pand`/`pslld`/`psrld`/`por`, byte-swapping by
shift-and-mask in SSE with one scalar `bswap` for the tail. And the swap order is not the layout
order: `0059C1D5 call 0059A780` for classes, members inline, and the type table **last and by tail
`jmp`** at `0059C245`.

**Suite re-run:** serialization, structural, calculation and edge-case parity over all three
routines, every byte compared, nothing scripted. `contract_map_sync.py` in step at 18 claims.
`check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency` pass.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the coast-down latch: an UNKNOWN row whose answer was already in this database (OPUS-PASS-COAST-DOWN)

Every cited instruction read at its address, and both float constants **dereferenced** rather than
trusted: `004240D8 mulss xmm0, [rip → 00D12434]` holds `3F547AE1` = **0.82999998**, and `004240EE
movss xmm0, [rip → 008F30E8]` holds `3D4CCCCD` = **0.05000000**. The record arithmetic
(`0042408A movsx rax, cx`, `00424091 imul rbx, rax, 0x740`), the 16-byte mirror
(`00424182`/`00424185` with `rdi = rbx + 0x610`), the live-flags clear (`0042419B and word [rdi+0xc],
ax`) and the unchecked dereference (`004241AB call`, one unrelated `mov`, then `004241B6 mov rcx,
[rax+0xda8]` — **no `test`**) all hold as written.

**The two float-comparison claims are exactly right and worth spelling out.** `0042413F ucomiss xmm1,
xmm0` is followed by **both** `jp` and `jne` to the cache path: unordered (NaN) takes the `jp`, while
`−0.0` against `+0.0` is equal *and* ordered, so neither branch is taken and the latch **arms**. And
`0042414D movsx ecx, byte [rbx+0x457]` sign-extends a **byte**, then `00424154 cmp ecx, eax` /
`00424156 **jb**` compares it **unsigned** — a negative stop-frame count becomes a very large
unsigned value, fails the `jb`, and **arms rather than caching**. The extension's signedness and the
comparison's disagree, and the boundary follows the comparison. That is the fourth contract this
sweep whose behaviour turns on exactly that mismatch.

### The `0020E600` row was stale, and the answer was already here

§15 listed `0020E600` as *"not established — supplied as oracles, bodies not read"*. It **is**
established, by [`CONTRACT-authored-table-row-lookup`](../02-Resource-And-Asset-Pipeline/CONTRACT-authored-table-row-lookup.md),
which names it `ImageAddress_ResolveRuntimePointer`, reads it whole and executes it —
`mov eax, ecx` / `add rax, [01F83530]` / `ret`.

> **This sharpens the unchecked dereference rather than softening it.** That contract also
> establishes the global at `01F83530` is **zero for the whole life of the shipped process** (no
> writer exists in the image), so `resolve(x) = (uint32)x`. A zero or small reference therefore makes
> `004241B6` read **`[0 + 0xDA8]`** — a near-null dereference with no test in front of it, not merely
> an unvalidated pointer.

Row corrected to **PARTLY ESTABLISHED**. **`0051B9E0` remains genuinely unread** and is left open —
an answer found is not a licence to close its neighbour.

**Suite re-run: 75 comparisons, 0 mismatches.** `contract_map_sync.py` in step at 12 claims — the
claim wording is unchanged, only its evidence and confidence. `check_links`, `check_counts`,

bytes; the buffer is only ever handed over whole.

which is also why the earlier `+0x554` row was right to be withdrawn: there is no field there to be

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the battle runtime mode: six is the number of modes, not of tests (OPUS-PASS-BATTLE-MODE)

**`audit_coverage` 203 → 204 of 319.**

### Corrected

`0030D9A0` is 105 bytes and reads whole as a **priority cascade with five decision points**:
`0030D9B1 test cl, 8` → 5; `0030D9C0 test cl, 4` → 4; `0030D9CF call 00377C20` / `test eax, eax` →
3; `0030D9EF test cl, 2` → 2; and `0030D9FE movzx eax, cl` / `0030DA01 **and eax, 1**` → 1 or 0.

**Four `test` instructions — the fifth decision is an `and`.** Six is the count of *outcomes*, modes
0–5, and §2's "6 tests" reads the result column as though it were the test column. **A reconstruction
implementing "six tests" adds a branch the engine does not have.** Likewise "two early returns" is
**four**, unless it means *two that return before the `call`* — which is true, is the useful
distinction (modes 5 and 4 never consult the field bit), and is now what the row says.

### Confirmed, and a trap I backed out of

The flags word is `*(02EBF190) + 0x5B04`, loaded at `0030D9A4`/`0030D9AB` **and again, identically,
at `0030D9E2`/`0030D9E9`** — re-read after the call rather than cached. The table-absent path is
`00377C5F mov edx, 0xfff` / `shr edx, 0xf`. The bound is `00377C39 jae` (**unsigned**), the stride
arithmetic `00377C3E lea rax, [r8 + rcx*2]`.

> **My first detector flagged `0030D9D4 test eax, eax` as a null check**, which made *"the ladder does
> not null-check the state pointer"* look false. It is not a pointer test at all — it tests **the
> return value of `call 00377C20`**. The claim concerns the pointer loaded from `02EBF190`, and that
> is dereferenced immediately on both loads with nothing in between. **A register name is not a
> value's identity** — the same lesson as `r8` ceasing to be the third argument two contracts ago,
> and the third time this sweep a loose detector nearly refuted a correct claim.

The `0xFFF >> 15` here is the same failure value the field-record-accessors pass established as
*"permission denied"*, so **with no field table this ladder can never return 3** and falls through to
the chocobo and summon bits.

`contract_map_sync.py` clean; `check_counts`, `check_consistency` pass, and `check_links` is now
clean — the peer-owned broken link reported in the previous package has been fixed by its owner.
