## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the achievement counters: a 0x20-byte block the table implies and the document never states (OPUS-PASS-ACHIEVEMENTS)

**`audit_coverage` 205 → 206 of 319.** The descriptor table at `00D10460` is in **`.rdata`**, **30
entries of 8 bytes**, and the two entries after it are visibly a different structure — the boundary
is in the data, not merely asserted. Every cited instruction is where the document puts it:
`00316B8B mov eax, 0x7fff`, `00316BA9 mov eax, 0x7fffffff`, `00316B9F jns 00316BBD` whose target is
**past** the fall-through `00316BBB add ebx, edi`, and `00316B73 lea eax, [rdi - 0xe2]`.

### The population the "no counter" claim is about

Reading all 30 width bytes: **`2` → 7 ids, `4` → 4 ids, `0` → 19 ids.** So **11 of 30 ids carry a
counter and 19 do not** — the number the *"when the id has no counter"* claim needs and never gives.

### The counter block is `0x20` bytes, with a gap that is alignment and not a field

The second descriptor byte is the counter's offset, and across the eleven it falls out as:

```
+0x00 +0x02 +0x04 +0x06 +0x08 +0x0A +0x0C    seven int16
+0x0E                                         two bytes, unused — alignment
+0x10 +0x14 +0x18 +0x1C                       four int32
```

The words end at `+0x0D` and the dwords begin at the next 4-byte boundary, not at `+0x0E`.

> **A reconstruction that packed the dwords at `+0x0E` would place all four 32-bit counters wrong
> while every individual claim in §15 still held** — because no claim states the block's shape; it is
> only derivable by reading all thirty descriptors together. That is the difference between a
> document that lists fields and one that gives a layout.

`contract_map_sync.py` clean; `check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency` pass.

**Not claimed:** no runtime observation.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the bazaar: the purchase IS an authored-table row lookup, on one of the forty slots (OPUS-PASS-BAZAAR)

**`audit_coverage` 206 → 207 of 319.** Every cited instruction reads as written: `0030B1F4 lea ecx,
[rdi - 0xd000]`; `0030B203 and byte [rsi + 0x59c8], 0xfd` (and `0xFD` **is** `~0x02`); `0030B461 or
byte [rdi + 0x59c8], 3` at the same displacement; `0030B1B8`–`0030B1C1` deriving `[02EBF190] + (id &
0xFFF)` from `bx` rather than taking it as an argument; and `0030B198 call 00322C50` before anything
else.

**The class bound is signed, and the mechanism is on the page now**: `0030B3B1 mov eax, [rdx+0x3c]` /
`0030B3B4 dec eax` / `cmp ecx, eax` / **`jg`** — with a count of zero the comparand is `−1`, so every
non-negative index is *greater* and is **rejected**. (The flag-bank family's `Bank64` accessors fail
the other way on the same shape; the difference is whether a `js` or an unsigned compare stands
beside it.)

### The cross-contract join

`0030B1AC`–`0030B1FD` is the [authored-table row
lookup](../02-Resource-And-Asset-Pipeline/CONTRACT-authored-table-row-lookup.md) instruction for
instruction: `mov rax, [rip → 02EBF058]` / `test` / `mov ecx, [rax+0x0C]` / `call 0020E600` / `test` /
`movzx ebx, word [rcx+8]` / `imul` / `add`. **`02EBF058` is one of the forty slots** that pass that
contract's own criterion — so the bazaar's goods table is a member of the family and inherits
everything established there.

> **And the family's known weakness is visible right here.** Both `je`s land on `0030B201 xor ebx,
> ebx`, and execution **falls through** into `0030B203` and then `0030B20C movzx ecx, word [rbx +
> 0x16]` — with `ebx = 0`, a read of address **`0x16`**. §15's *"a failed row resolution does not
> abort the purchase"* and *"none tests it"* turn out to be one fact seen from two sides, and its
> consequence is a **near-null read**, not merely an unvalidated pointer.

`contract_map_sync.py` clean; `check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency` pass.

**Not claimed:** the three scripted callees still run as oracles; nothing observed at runtime; §13's
untested containment assumption stands.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the character transform publish: the two banks abut, which a subtraction could not show (OPUS-PASS-TRANSFORM-PUBLISH)

**`audit_coverage` 207 → 208 of 319.** Counting the 16-byte stores in each branch and printing their
displacements turns the `0xC0` subtraction from an inference into a demonstration.

**Branch A** (taken at `001FB1BA je 001FB260`): **12** stores at `+0x4C4, 0x4D4 … 0x574`.
**Branch B** (the fall-through): **12** at `+0x584, 0x594 … 0x634`. Stride **exactly 16**,
`12 × 16 = 192 = 3 × 64` — three 64-byte matrices per bank.

> **And the runs are contiguous.** A's last store covers `+0x574`–`+0x583`; B's first begins at
> **`+0x584`**. `0x584 − 0x4C4 = 0xC0` is the distance between two labels; **that the banks abut with
> no gap and no overlap** is a different statement, and only enumerating the stores shows it.

`001FB14A imul rdi, rax, 0x318`, `001FB185 test r8d, r8d` and `001FB1B1 cmp byte [rax+0x1c], 0` all
read as written.

### The motion flag guards **both** floats against NaN, and short-circuits

`001FB162 ucomiss xmm7, xmm0` / `jp` / `jne`, then — only when the first compared an ordered equal —
`001FB170 ucomiss xmm6, xmm0` / `jp` / `je`. **Each float has its own `ucomiss`, and each has a `jp`
in front of its equality test**, so a NaN in *either* component reports motion. The second test is
reached only if the first was an ordered zero: a short-circuit, not two independent tests.

`contract_map_sync.py` clean; `check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency` pass.

**Not claimed:** nothing observed live.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the field music selection: a `nop` is not a write, and one stub serves three subsystems (OPUS-PASS-FIELD-MUSIC)

**`audit_coverage` 208 → 209 of 319.**

### "Writes no state", exhaustively

`003EAA70` is 229 bytes / **73 instructions**: **0** stack writes, **0** real stores anywhere else,
and **2** instructions my detector flagged before I read them — `nop dword ptr [rax]` and
`nop dword ptr [rax + rax]`, the multi-byte alignment NOPs, **which write nothing**.

> **The fourth trap of this shape in the sweep**, after `test` counted as a store, `r8` ceasing to be
> the third argument, and a `bswap` open-coded as shift-and-mask. **An instruction is not its operand
> shape** — a detector keyed on "first operand is memory" calls a padding NOP a write every time.

### The arithmetic, and a value widened twice in opposite senses

`003EAA96 sar eax, 7` (page stride 128); `003EAAB8 shr edx, 0xb` / `003EAABB and ecx, 0x7ff` (the
11/5 split, and the identical pair again at `003EAAE9`/`003EAAEC`); `003EAB48 cmove r9d, eax` (track
`0` folds to `−1`).

**Progress is widened twice, in opposite senses**: `003EAA84 movzx r11d, ax` loads it
**zero**-extended, and `003EAB10 movsx r11d, r11w` re-extends it **signed** before the comparison. A
reconstruction that kept the first widening and skipped the second agrees on every non-negative
progress value and diverges on exactly the ones the ladder exists to order.

### One writer image-wide, and a stub in its third subsystem

A whole-image scan of `02B5E0D0`: **1 writer**, `003EAB78 mov qword [rip → 02B5E0D0], rax` inside the
load path §15 names, and **2 reading functions**.

§14.4's site table gives `00473D20`'s rebase callback as **`0016D6A0`** — the same three-byte `ret 0`
this sweep found standing in for an absent verb-dispatch callback and for the save-image clear's tail
jump. **Three unrelated subsystems share one no-op stub**; a reconstruction giving each its own would
triple a function the engine has once.

`contract_map_sync.py` clean; `check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency` pass.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the Lua chunk loader, and the last of forty-two (OPUS-PASS-LUA-LOADER)

**`audit_coverage` 209 → 210 of 319.** With this pass **every one of the 42 contracts has survived a
falsification pass** — `passes: 0` is now **0 of 42**, from 28 at the start of this sweep. That is a
floor, not a finish: one pass each is the entry condition the `COMPLETION-PLAN` sets, and the L1 gate
and the thirty final audits are untouched by it.

### The header, rebuilt from the immediates that build it

`0082E4C7 mov esi, 0x61754C1B` → `1B 4C 75 61`; `0082E4D6 … 0x04010052` → `52 00 01 04`;
`0082E4DE … 0x00040408` → `08 04 04 00`; then `0082E4E6 mov [rsp+0x2C], eax` → `19 93 0D 0A` and
`0082E4B9 movzx edi, word […]` → `1A 0A`. Three immediates and a six-byte tail, reassembling to the
stated header byte for byte. **Byte 10 is `04`, byte 11 `00`** — `sizeof(lua_Number)` is **4**.

### Eighteen built, seventeen read — and the length is an immediate

§15 cites the planted `0082E4EA mov byte [rsp+0x38], 0x1B` and the `lea rdx, [rsp+0x39]`. **The other
half of the proof sits beside them**: `0082E4CC mov r8d, 0x11` — **17**, the read length, stated by
the call's own argument rather than inferred from a displacement.

### All eighteen compared — including the byte that was never read

`cmp rcx, rdx` over 0–7, `cmp rax, [rsp+0x40]` over 8–15, `cmp di, word [rsp+0x48]` over 16–17:
`8 + 8 + 2 = 18`, nothing skipped. **But byte 0 is inside the first comparison and was planted by the
loader**, so a file whose first byte is not `0x1B` still passes that byte. **The signature check on
byte 0 is vacuous** — which is what "planted, not read" means, said in the terms a reconstruction
needs.

The five rejections are `0082E521`, `0082E52D`, `0082E536`, `0082E544`/`0082E546` — progressively
narrower slices of the same eighteen bytes, as §15 describes.

`contract_map_sync.py` clean; `check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency` pass.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the battle-unit field map: 577 citations checked, and the check was wrong three times before the map was (OPUS-PASS-BATTLE-UNIT-MAP)

**`audit_coverage` 210 → 211 of 319.** The sweep moves off contracts onto the 108 remaining
documents, starting with the largest — a 117 KB field map whose rows each cite the instruction that
touches the field. That makes the whole document mechanically checkable: **577 sites across 194
rows**, every one disassembled and its displacement compared with its row's offset.

| outcome | sites |
|---|---:|
| displacement **is** the row's offset | **432** |
| resolved through an embedded sub-object base | **132** |
| cites the **source object** of a cross-object copy | 2 |
| not an access site — a data address or control flow | 7 |
| indexed, indeterminate by displacement alone | 4 |

**No site contradicts its row.** Saying so took three corrections to the check.

**First**, comparing an absolute offset against a raw displacement called 134 sites wrong. The base
register is already offset into the unit; subtracting gives **34 distinct sub-object bases** —
`+0x80` (41 sites), `+0x730` (18), `+0x6B0` (16), `+0xBC0` (7) — which §2.1 says exist but never
enumerates. **Those three commonest account for 75 of the 132.**

**Second**, two sites under `+0x060` have displacements *larger* than the row's offset, which no base
can explain: they write the **render record's** `+0xCC`/`+0xCE`, and that row documents a copy *from*
the render record. A row describing a cross-object chain cites addresses in the other object.

**Third**, four "sites" are not code — `02EBF140`/`02EBF148` in `.data`, `008FCC90`/`009002BC` in
`.rdata` — and three are instructions touching no memory (`test`, `je`, `call`), cited for the
control flow around a field.

> **An address in a citation is not automatically an instruction, and an instruction is not
> automatically the access.** Fifth trap of this shape in the sweep and the largest: at face value it
> reported a 23 % error rate in a document that has none.

### The three-way join the `.data` citations turn out to be

`+0xE70` cites **`02EBF148`** and `+0xE78` cites **`02EBF140`** — **both registry slots in the
forty** that `CONTRACT-authored-table-row-lookup` §15a enumerates. Those two fields are the
reward-row pointers that
[the experience and licence award](../13-Rewards-Progression-Economy/CONTRACT-experience-and-licence-award.md)
dereferences **with no null check**, and the rows behind them are supplied by a lookup whose resolve
can fail and return zero.

> **The award's unchecked dereference and the lookup's one-sided guard are the same hazard seen from
> the two ends of one pointer** — and this field map is the document that names the slot in the
> middle. None of the three said so before today.

`check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency` pass.

**Not claimed:** the census's own coverage limits are untouched — §2.1's warning about

## 2026-09-12 — the sound-request page catches up with its contract, two more maps clear, and my own targeting was wrong (OPUS-PASS-SOUND-PAGE)

### A correction that had not propagated

`how-a-sound-request-becomes-a-voice.md` §9 still read **"four resolvers over three handles"** — the
count this sweep corrected in `CONTRACT-sound-request` earlier today. **`003A1240` is a fifth**, and
the reason it was missed is the reason it stayed missed here too: every other resolver names one of
the three handle globals, and this one takes its handle as a **parameter**. Corrected in place.

### `02AEEDC8` has no references, and now it has a cause

A controlled scan (`02AEEDC0` as the positive control, which passes) finds **0 references to
`02AEEDC8` image-wide**. §10.3 attributes the checker's old complaint to a `BODYSIZE` regex artefact,
which is true but is not why the address is unreferenced. **The page and the instructions use
different origins for one table**: the resolvers' `lea` computes `02AEEDC0` and reads the handle at
`+8`/`+0xA`; §3 and §7 take the entry origin as `02AEEDC8` and read `+0`/`+2`.

`02AEEDC0 + 24N + 8` **is** `02AEEDC8 + 24N` — the same bytes, two origins, neither wrong about the
data. But **only `02AEEDC0` is an address the image ever forms**, which is exactly why nothing cites
the other. Recorded as §10.3a so the ghost has a cause rather than a dismissal.

### Two more field maps, and what the direct rate measures

| map | sites | direct | bases |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| result record | 151 | 89.4 % | `+0x5C`, `+0xDC` |
| **actor storage record** | 218 | **98.6 %** | `+0x120`, `+0x350` |

**Eight maps, 2,239 cited sites, nothing undecodable.** And the spread is structural: 98.6 % here
against **15.7 %** for the save payload. **A field map's direct-citation rate measures how much of its
record is addressed as itself** rather than through embedded sub-blocks — a property of the record,
not of the writing.

### My own targeting was wrong, by the same kind of error I keep finding

I reported "104 documents short" from a list of **114** built on the wrong rule. `audit_coverage`
accepts **two** routes — a stamped `passes`/`last_pass_state`, **or** `falsification_passes > 0` plus
a falsification-pass section — and my scan honoured only the first, so documents already counted
appeared unaudited. Stamping the sound-request page moved the metric by **nothing**, which is how I
found it. My scan also walked the whole database where the metric counts only `NN-` directories.

> **Reproducing the metric's own rule gives 319 documents, 215 audited, 104 remaining** — the figure
> I had been quoting, arrived at correctly for the first time. A population error in my targeting is
> the same defect as one in a document, and it earned the same correction.

`check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency` pass.

| `0035C8E0` ignores `0x18` | `sub ecx, 0xb` / `je` / `cmp ecx, 0xc` / `jne` — only `id − 0x0B == 0x0C` acts |
| the callback under **four** record-bit gates | four, with `test rax, rax` on `+0x38` being the callback-pointer null check rather than a fifth |

The cited range holds **39 calls to 35 distinct targets**. Counting calls and calling the 23 wrong
would have been the sixth such mistake in this sweep — a *step* is a numbered row that may issue
several calls, and counted as steps it is exactly 23 across exactly the cited range.

### The rule is now in the standard

Six correct counts this sweep were unreproducible until their unit was identified:

| written | the unit that gives it | units that do not |
|---|---|---|
| "the fifteen functions that reference `01EEBCC0`" | 15 functions | 19 instructions |
| "the 21 `02EBF170` sites" | 21 name-lookup sites | 42 / 58 references, 9 functions |
| "eleven read-modify-write masks" | 11 distinct constants | 16 instructions, 12 offsets |
| "251 handlers" | a union of two sets | 239 + 13 = 252 |
| "121 sites in 70 functions" | both, named separately | either alone |
| "the 23 steps" | 23 numbered steps | 39 calls, 35 targets |

**In every case the document was right and my checker was wrong** — and in every case the checker had
no way to know, because "sites", "handlers", "steps" and "masks" each admit readings that differ by a
factor of two or more.

Added to [`EVIDENCE-STANDARD.md`](EVIDENCE-STANDARD.md) as **AMENDMENT 2026-09-12**, beside the
event-count amendment it complements: that one asks whether repeated events are *distinct*; this one
asks what a thing *is* before it is counted. **Unlike the event rule, this one bites on zeroes too** —
"no writer" means nothing until *writer* is defined as an instruction, a function, or a path.

The rule has two halves: **name the unit in the same sentence as the count**, and, as a reader,
**change the unit before doubting the value** — six times out of six, the value was right.

`check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency` pass.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the status write: a branchless `cmov` is why the stub exists (OPUS-PASS-STATUS-WRITE-PAGE)

**`audit_coverage` 225 → 226 of 321.** Nine claims re-derived from the shipping bytes; **all nine
hold**, and two are now stated more precisely than the page stated them.

| claim | measured |
|---|---|
| thirty-three stated function sizes | **33 of 33** |
| `0030E360` — 14 call sites in 10 functions | **14 in 10**, and **zero tail jumps** |
| the jump table at `0030E8A4` has eight targets | **8 distinct**; byte table max index **7**; **8 statuses named, 24 on the default** |
| clear mask `0xFFFFFFFDFFE7FFFD` → bits 1, 19, 20, 33 | **[1, 19, 20, 33]** |
| presence is `+0x3C` OR `+0x64` | exact |
| the case-4 filter | exact, **including the conjunction** |
| `0046A800` fires only for statuses 1 → `0x12`, 31 → `0x11` | exact |
| `003876D0` = definition `+9` × `[01DFE0B4]` × 30 | exact |

### `0030E816` is the tail, not a do-nothing body

§2.6 row 7 calls `0030E816` **the recompute gate**; §2.7's default row calls the same address
**"nothing"**. A reader reconciling them could conclude the 24 default statuses skip the recompute.
**They do not** — the image shows three ways that this is the tail every case converges on: **case 7
*is* `0030E816`**, **six cases `jmp` to it**, and **case 0 falls through into it**. What actually
skips the recompute is the **early-out at `0030E5CB`**, which jumps to `0030E82D`, past the gate —
which is what makes §1's rule 3 literally true: re-adding a status a unit already has is a no-op
**including derived state**.

### The negative claim, with controls, and the mechanism behind it

*"`0046A800` … reached only by `call rax`"* was checked over **38,161 disassembled bodies**: **zero**
direct sites, against four controls that must be non-zero — `00300140` **5**, `0030FED0` **25**,
`003284D0` **1**, `0046AB10` **48**. The address is spelled out **nowhere** in the image but its own
`.pdata` entry. The positive half is **one instruction**:

```asm
0030E710  lea    rcx, [rip+0x15C0E9]   ; -> 0046A800   the real handler
0030E719  lea    rax, [rip-0x1A1080]   ; -> 0016D6A0   the 3-byte stub, C2 00 00
0030E720  cmovne rax, rcx              ; adding ? handler : stub
0030E727  call   rax
```

> **The call happens either way.** The selection is a branchless `cmovne`, so "removing → the stub,
> i.e. nothing" is right about the effect and wrong about the control flow: removing does not skip
> the call, it calls `ret 0`. **And that is why a `ret 0` stub exists at all** — you cannot `cmov` a
> null and then call it, so a branchless two-way call needs a *callable* no-op. It is the same
> `0016D6A0` this sweep found serving four unrelated subsystems after the linker folded their
> identical 3-byte bodies; this is the shape that creates one.

`[01DFE0B4]` is an **integer, not a float**, and the image initialises it to **1**. *(Corrected
later the same day: it is the **frame base**, not "a tuning slot set to unity" — see the
frame-base entry below.)*

`check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency` pass.

**Not claimed:** nothing executed or observed live; `FA-3` and `EY-1` remain open.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the formula scratch block: 87 of 88 numbers exact, and the 88th is the only accumulator in the block (OPUS-PASS-SCRATCH-BLOCK)

**`audit_coverage` 226 → 227 of 321.** §2.2 carries **eighty-eight numbers** — a write count and a
read count for each of 44 words. All of them were recomputed from every rip-relative reference into
`02AEDFB8`–`02AEE05F` across every body in `functions.tsv`, with the table **parsed out of the page
rather than retyped**.

| claim | measured |
|---|---|
| **912** referencing instructions | **912** |
| **44** words and no others | **44 distinct addresses touched**, none outside the table, no row unreferenced |
| the 88 per-word counts | **44/44 writes exact, 43/44 reads exact** |
| `003849B0`: **340 B, 42 stores, 43 of the 44** | **340 B, 42 stores, 43 covered** |
| `02AEDFD4` untouched by the reset | confirmed, and it is the only one |
| `02AEDFF0` has **20** writers | **20**, once two `cmp dword ptr [rip], …` are excluded |

### Three counts in one document, three different units

**44 words over 168 bytes** — which is only **42 dwords**. The count is right because **three entries
are single bytes** (`02AEE04C/4D/4E`, the steal tiers): 41 dwords + 3 bytes = 44. `02AEE04F` is
referenced by nothing in the image.

**42 stores covering 43 entries** — only 42 distinct addresses are stored, and the extra entry comes
from one instruction being wider than its neighbours: `00384A1C mov word ptr [rip+0x276962a], ax` is
a **2-byte** store spanning `02AEE04D` *and* `02AEE04E`. That is exactly why §2.2 records `4E`'s
reset as "(with 4D)". The page was already right; this is the instruction that makes it right.

**Eight reads that are also eight writes** — the single disagreement in 88 numbers. The page's
convention is that a **read-modify-write counts as a write only**, which §2.2's "counts instructions,
not functions" note does not say. It matters in exactly one row:

> **`02AEDFF0` is the only word of the 44 that is ever read-modify-written.** Every other one of the
> 912 references is a pure load or a pure store. This word takes **eight `add dword ptr [rip], eax`**
> — four in `BattleFormula_RollSpecialGuardOutcome` and four in `00389370`. So "**rewrites it seven
> times**" is **exact as a count** (3 `mov` + 4 `add`) **and misleading as a verb**: four of the seven
> do not rewrite the threshold, they **accumulate into it**. The avoid threshold is a running total
> built across the function, and `00389370` has the identical 3-plus-4 shape. A modder who reads
> "rewrites" and substitutes a `mov` for one of those `add`s changes the outcome of the roll.

`check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency` pass.

**Not claimed:** nothing executed or observed live; §2.3–§2.7's semantic readings were not
re-derived, and `FT-4` remains open.

## 2026-09-12 — the frame base has one writer and 212 readers, and I called it a unity tunable twice (OPUS-NOTICE-FRAME-BASE)

Two passes I published earlier today — the status write and the post-result events — each found
`01DFE0B4` behind a duration and each described it as **"a tuning slot currently set to unity"**.
That is wrong in implication, and the periodic-tick page already said so: `01DFE0B4` is **the frame
base**, 1 at 30 fps and 2 at 60 (§5, corrected 2026-09-12 by FABLE).

Measured across every body in `functions.tsv`:

| | |
|---|---|
| references to `01DFE0B4` | **212** |
| writers | **1** — `001EDDF2 mov dword ptr [rip], 2`, in `001EDDC0`, on its `ecx != 0` branch |
| value in the image | **1**, initialised in `.data` (not BSS: the RVA is inside `SizeOfRawData`) |

**One writer and 212 readers** is the sharpest statement of what this word is: a single global,
written once by the frame-rate path, read everywhere. "Set to unity" describes the *image*, not the
*program* — and a reader who took my wording at face value would conclude a 60 fps session keeps the
30 fps tick counts.

What the correction changes, concretely:

- the status beat timer is definition `+9` × 30 at 30 fps and **× 60 at 60** — a constant wall-clock
  duration, not a constant tick count;
- the battle-message dedup window is `0x1C2 × base` — **450 frames at 30 fps, 900 at 60**, the same
  wall-clock wait either way;
- and the drain beat is `base × 10` ticks, which §5 of the periodic-tick page already states.

Both pass sections and both log entries are corrected in place, with the correction left visible
rather than the original wording erased. **This is a third subsystem for the same word**, which the
periodic-tick page's "the same word scales every status duration and beat" did not yet cover: the
message rate limit.

**Not claimed:** `001EDDC0`'s caller and what selects its `ecx` were not read, so *which* setting
turns the frame base to 2 is taken from the periodic-tick and boot pages, not re-derived here.

## 2026-09-12 — falsification pass 1 on the periodic tick: the control that earns the sentence is +50, not 101 (OPUS-PASS-PERIODIC-TICK)

**`audit_coverage` 228 → 229 of 322.** The page has been reopened once and corrected twice, so this
pass targeted what those rounds did not.

| claim | measured |
|---|---|
| six stated sizes | **6 of 6 exact** |
| "its first ninety instructions refusing to run" | the body is **296 instructions**; the last gate call is inside the first 90 and the `0x148` `memset` is **instruction 95** |
| `unit+0xDD0` deadline clears `0x40000000` | `cmp` / `jae` / `and dword ptr [rsi], 0xbfffffff` — bit **30** |
| `00385DF0`: five calls, last a tail call | five targets in that order, last a `jmp`, and **no `ret` anywhere in the body** |
| the beat is base × 10 | `imul … 0x1e`, `0xaaaaaaab`/`shr 1` = ÷ 3, `div`, `or [rdi+0x2c], 0x4000` |
| `0xAE147AE1` `sar 4` = `v / −50`, `sar 5` = `v / −100` | **both exact over ±20,000** |

### The control this deserves is not 101

§5a says the magics were checked "with a control against 101 that fails". Both magics reproduce. But
**101 is the wrong control for the claim the section makes** — its headline is *"the divisors are
negative"*, and 101 does not test the sign at all.

> Three controls that do, all failing as they must: **`v / −49`** (the shift one too small),
> **`v / −51`** (one too large), and **`v / +50`** — **the sign, which is the section's actual
> claim**. With `+50`, "the stored delta is a loss, not a magnitude with a sign applied later" is
> established rather than asserted.

Samples over the reachable domain (`v ≥ 50`): `50 → −1`, `99 → −1`, `100 → −2`, `12345 → −246`.

### How this nearly went wrong

My first run reported **both magics as failing** — a harness fault, not an image fact: I applied the
sign correction as "add 1 when the input is negative", where the code adds the **sign bit of the
quotient** (`mov eax, edx` / `shr eax, 0x1f` / `add edx, eax`, reading `edx` *after* the shift).

**The tell was that the control failed at the same time.** A control exists to fail when the claim is
wrong; when it fails *alongside* a claim that should hold, the instrument is the first suspect.
Recorded because every compiler-emitted constant division carries this correction and reading it off
the input is the natural mistake.

`check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency` pass.

**Not claimed:** nothing executed or observed live; `+0x28` — "one-fiftieth of *what*" — remains
unestablished, as §5 says.

> ret` — an **instance field**. `GiResetRenderTargetObj` and `GiResetDefaultRenderTargetObj` carry a
> **per-object** key, and a reconstruction implementing §4.3 literally would give them a fixed layer
> they do not have.

> **"`VideoObj` … composited last, over everything" does not follow from the key.** Four classes carry
> `0x100`, larger than VideoObj's `0x80`. Which draws in front depends on a comparator nobody has
> read — `PROPOSED-xiionline-13-7` records that no consumer walking either list has been located. The
> key values are now all known; the ordering they produce is not. Opened as `-13-14`.

The block's fourth qword, incidentally, is the **next** class's RTTI locator — each vtable's own sits
8 bytes before its listed address, which is how the names were recovered.

## 2026-09-12 — `0016D6A0` is the CFG check thunk, named by the PE header: not four subsystems, 2,480 (OPUS-NOTICE-CFG-THUNK)

A second correction to my own work today, found while auditing the render command list: `0018B4E0`
calls `0016D6A0`, and `functions.tsv` names it **`_guard_check_icall`**. A name in a database is a
claim, so it was checked against the image's own header.

**The PE Load Config directory settles it.** `GuardCFCheckFunctionPointer` is the slot at
`008C31C0`; that slot holds **`0016D6A0`**, whose bytes are `C2 00 00` — `ret 0`.

| | |
|---|---|
| `GuardFlags` | `0x100` — CF **instrumented** |
| `GuardCFFunctionTable` / `Count` | **0 / 0** — an empty guard table |
| direct call sites | **2,868, in 2,480 functions** |
| calls through the slot `008C31C0` | 2 |
| `lea` sites taking its address | **53** |

So the `ret 0` is a no-op **by construction** — the image is instrumented for Control Flow Guard and
ships with no guard table, so the check function returns immediately. It stands in front of indirect
calls across the whole image.

### The database already knew this, in three documents

The retraction is mine alone: `_guard_check_icall` is **already established elsewhere in the
database**, and my "four subsystems / folded 3-byte bodies" reading was the stranded one.

- [`game-application.md`](../00-Engine-Core-Runtime/Application-Root/game-application.md) §: *"`0x0016D6A0`
  is three bytes — `ret 0` — with **2,479 distinct callers (2,867 call sites)**"*;
- [`rtti-vtable-object-model.md`](../00-Engine-Core-Runtime/Object-Model/rtti-vtable-object-model.md)
  §: *"the 42 no-op slots in that table are `0016D6A0`, which the GFZ labels **`_guard_check_icall`**"*;
- [`vtable-method-index.md`](../00-Engine-Core-Runtime/Object-Model/vtable-method-index.md): the same
  address *"in 1,291 classes — `_guard_check_icall`, a `ret` placeholder"*.

What this pass adds is the **header-level proof** — those three take the name from the GFZ's labels,
where `GuardCFCheckFunctionPointer` proves it from the image — and **the split**, which nobody had
stated:

| | sites | functions |
|---|---:|---:|
| by `call` | **2,528** | **2,170** |
| by tail `jmp` | **340** | **319** |
| union | **2,868** | **2,480** |

**Twelve per cent of the population reaches it by a tail jump**, so this is one more count that a
call-only census gets wrong — and `game-application.md`'s figures are the union, which is the right
unit.

Its **2,867 / 2,479 and my 2,868 / 2,480 differ by exactly one, in both units** — one function
contributing one site. I have not run that down; the tail-jmp list is dense with 12-byte-spaced
entries in the `0089xxxx`–`008Bxxxx` thunk region (`008963C0`, `008963CC`, `008963D8`, …), where two
tools can reasonably disagree about where one body ends and the next begins. **Recorded, not
reconciled** — and not adjusted toward either figure.

### What this retracts

Earlier in this sweep I recorded that `0016D6A0` "serves four subsystems" with the cause being
"**the linker folded identical 3-byte bodies**", and in today's status-write pass I wrote that a
branchless `cmov` is "**why a `ret 0` stub exists at all**".

**Both are wrong about the cause, and the count is off by three orders of magnitude** — 2,480
functions, not four subsystems. The `ret 0` exists because it is the CFG check; folding is not
needed to explain it.

What survives is the narrow half, and it is now better founded: the address **is** also materialised
as a do-nothing function pointer — at **53 `lea` sites** across the image — and the status write's
`0030E719 lea rax` is one of them. A branchless two-way call does need a *callable* no-op; the
compiler simply had the CFG thunk to hand rather than emitting one.

**Not claimed:** whether identical user-written empty handlers were *additionally* folded onto this
address is not established either way here; the 53 `lea` sites are consistent with it and do not
prove it. Nothing executed or observed live.

## 2026-09-12 — a check for answers stranded beside obsolete specifications, and its first two corrections (OPUS-TOOL-STRANDED-UNREAD)

**Three documents in one day** were found carrying *"`0046AB10` unread"* against a function the
post-result-events page had read on 2026-09-11 — the status write, its own §2.6, and the HP write.
One is an accident. Three is a **failure mode the database cannot see**, because nothing links the
sentence that admits ignorance to the page that ended it.

`check_stranded_unread.py` looks for exactly that: an address one document calls **unread** that a
*different* document says it **read**.

### What it took to make it useful

The first run reported 130 pairs and most were noise. Three filters, each for a convention this
database actually uses:

- **Append-only history is not a live claim.** `AUDIT-LOG.md`, `COVERAGE.md`, `PROGRAM-STATE.md` and
  `_index/_inbox/` record what was unread *on the day they were written*, and are correct as
  written. Excluded from both sides.
- **Strikethrough is this database's own marker for superseded wording.** `~~…~~` is blanked before
  matching, so a correction already recorded does not read as a live admission of ignorance.
- **A window must not cross a table row.** Key-address tables put rows within a few dozen characters
  of each other, so a plain character window made every address inherit its neighbours' words —
  `0020E600` read as "unread" because the row *above* it said a different function was not read.
  This was most of the first run's noise.

**130 pairs → 74**, and the survivors are worth reading. Falsification-pass sections are also
skipped on the unread side, since they quote the stale wording in the act of correcting it.

**It reports; it does not judge.** "Unread" and "read" can be about different things — a caller
census versus a body, a field versus a function — so a pair is a question, not a defect. Exit status
is always 0, like `check_counts`.

### The first two corrections it found

**`00226BE0` / `00226280`** — the system-stop registry's start and apply steps, **both read whole**
on [the time-stop registry](../00-Engine-Core-Runtime/System-Stop-Registry/the-time-stop-and-system-stop-registry.md)
(§3, §4, and "read whole" in its evidence table). Two pages still called them unread:

- [`field-record-table-navimapdata.md`](../03-World-Area-Field/Field-Record-Table/field-record-table-navimapdata.md)
  — and this one is the failure mode in miniature: **its residue note three lines below had already
  been updated on 2026-09-12** to say the registry's contract *is* documented on that very page. The
  sentence with the word "unread" in it was left behind. A half-propagated correction is exactly
  what nothing else would have caught.
- [`ui-request-router.md`](../16-UI/Request-Router/ui-request-router.md) — "the two large bodies
  unread", in the prose and again in its key-addresses table.

Both corrected, pointing at the page that holds the answer.

**Not claimed:** the remaining 72 pairs are **not** asserted to be stale. They are a queue for
reading, and some will be legitimate — a page can have read a body without having read the caller
census another page wants. Nothing else was changed on the strength of the tool alone.

## 2026-09-12 — my own new check had a filter that always answered "clean" (OPUS-NOTICE-STRANDED-FILTER)

An hour ago I published `check_stranded_unread.py` and wrote that after correcting `00226BE0` /
`00226280` **"the check now returns zero pairs for that address"**. It did. **It returned zero for
every address**, and would have whatever the database said.

```python
if args.addr and a.upper() != args.addr.upper().lstrip("0x"):
```

`lstrip("0x")` strips **every leading `0` and `x`**, not a `0x` prefix — so `"0026DAC0"` became
`"26DAC0"` and never equalled the eight-digit key it was compared against. **The `--addr` filter
matched nothing, so it reported a clean result for anything I asked it.**

That is a **zero-case run presented as a confirmation**, which is precisely what the standard says
cannot pass — and I published it as evidence that a correction had landed.

### Fixed, and re-verified with a control that must be non-zero

`--addr` now strips an optional `0x` prefix and left-pads to eight digits. Re-run:

| query | pairs | meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `--addr 00226280` | **0** | the correction really did close it |
| `--addr 0026DAC0` | **1** | a control — the filter can still find something |
| `--addr 00180620` | **1** | a second control |

**A filter that only ever answers "clean" is indistinguishable from a clean database until you ask it
for something you know is dirty.** The two controls are now the way to check the check.

### And a third noise class, found while fixing it

`0026DAC0`'s hit pointed at `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`'s `FA-3` row, which is marked **ANSWERED** while its
question text still carries the original "unread" wording — as it should: **the row's state column is
the claim, the question text is the record of what was once unknown.** Rows whose state is
`ANSWERED` / `CLOSED` / `RESOLVED` are now dropped before matching.

**130 → 74 → 56 pairs.** The remaining 56 stand as a reading queue.

> The `0026DAC0` pair also shows the tool's own caveat earning its place: the "unread" side asks
> *"what the `−1.0f` at `0026DAC0` means"*, which is a different question from whether the body has
> been read. **It is a pair, and it is not a defect.**

**Not claimed:** the 56 are not asserted stale. Nothing was changed on the strength of this run.

## 2026-09-12 — the stranded check, sharpened by its own false positives — and a fourth stale marker it found (OPUS-TOOL-STRANDED-SHARPEN)

Triaging the check's queue taught it three more things, each from a real hit rather than a guess.

**A phrase belongs to the NEAREST address, not to every address in the row.** A key-address row can
name five functions and say one of them is unread. `002F8E90` and `003588B0` reported as stranded
because the word sat further along the same row, attached to something else. The rule now: take the
nearest occurrence of the phrase and require that **no other address lies between it and this one**.
That alone took 56 pairs to 26.

**Narrative past tense is not an admission.** [`the-steal-roll.md`](../08-Combat-Formula/Steal/the-steal-roll.md)
says `0046AB10` is *"the battle event poster the HP page and the status page **had left** unread"* —
correct prose, reporting that the gap is closed. So is *"read here (previously listed 'not read')"*
on the gambit page. Matched only when it immediately precedes the phrase, so it cannot swallow a live
admission.

**And a tool should not flag its own corrections.** My fix to the HP page's §3 row wrote *"unread"
corrected 2026-09-12"* — which the check then matched. The lesson is for the prose, not the regex:
**a correction note should not restate the stale word.** Reworded to "superseded note corrected".

### The fourth stale marker, found by the check

I corrected the HP page's §3 by hand this morning and **missed §2.5**, which still read
`0046AB10(sourceRecord, 0x10, &zeros)`; **unread beyond**". The check found it. That is the fourth
document-place carrying an obsolete "unread" for this one function, and the second time the same
page carried it twice.

**130 → 74 → 56 → 26 → 24 pairs.** Controls after each change: `00226280` **0** (really closed),
`0046AB10` **0** (now that both places are fixed), and the whole-database count non-zero throughout,
so the filters never silently emptied the result.

**Not claimed:** the surviving 24 are a reading queue, not defects.

|---|---|

So §6's narrower set is right, and it gets there the only way this kind of negative can: **not by
failing to find a caller, but by naming the map and bounding its returns** — *"`00255290` returns

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass 1 on the field runtime pass: the wait slot resolved, and a census that cannot settle its own negative (OPUS-PASS-FIELD-RUNTIME-PASS)

**`audit_coverage` 235 → 236.** Everything on this page rests on one negative — §4's correction that
the inner drive loop is dead because "nothing ever sets the low nibble" — which rests on §11's trap:
the four `mov byte [rsi + 0x14], 1` stores belong to a **wait slot**, not the actor record. §11 proves
that far and stops at *"an element of an array"*.

### The wait slot is a 40-byte record the actor record points at

```asm
0025DFB6  movsx rax, byte ptr [rdi + 0x11]   ; a SIGNED byte index, in the record
0025DFBB  lea   rcx, [rax + rax*4]           ; x 5
0025DFBF  mov   rax, qword ptr [rdi + 0xa8]  ; the array base - a POINTER FIELD of the record
0025DFC6  lea   rsi, [rax + rcx*8]           ; base + index x 40
```

`rsi = *(record + 0xA8) + (int8)(record + 0x11) × 0x28`. **The actor record owns both halves of the
address** — which is exactly why the two `+0x14`s look alike: they are reached from the same record,
one directly and one through a pointer it holds.

### The slot's `+0x14` is an eight-case enum, not a flag byte

`movzx` / `cmp eax, 7` / `ja` / `mov ecx, [r14 + rax*4 + 0x13E3CC]` / `jmp rcx` — a bounded jump table
on `0..7`. So §4's `= 1`, `= 3`, `= 4`, `= 5` are **wait-kind states, not bits**, which is precisely
why they read as low-nibble writes to a displacement census. **The trap is not a coincidence of
offsets; it is an enum whose range happens to be the nibble.** This strengthens §4's conclusion rather
than changing it.

Also exact: the `0x288` = 648 slot block at `02098E10`; the drive loop's own `test cl, 0x40` /
`test cl, 0xf`; all eight writer sites §4 names, found independently; `0025DF00` at 1,228 B.

### Where my own sweep could not help, and said so

My byte-store sweep finds **86** sites at `+0x14` against §4's 80 — a definition difference (I counted
`add`, `xchg`, `setne`), and none of the extra six has an actor record as its base.

in `functions.tsv` that returns **eleven loops, all on `02EBA3F8`** — precisely the eleven § lists,

idiom is a house style"*. Three things rule it out, any one sufficient:

- **`02ADD940` is loaded as a `qword` and used as a base** (`[rdx + rax − 0x14]`), not as a dword

>

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on the resource request queue: a displacement is only an offset when the register holds the base (OPUS-PASS-REQUEST-QUEUE)

**`audit_coverage` 243 → 244.**

**Exact:** twenty stated sizes **20 of 20**; the pool loop is `cmp edx, 0x40` / `jl` with `lea rax,
[rax + 0x80]` — **64 iterations, `0x80` stride**; the counter at `01EED498` set to **1**; the free
head at `022C51D0` loaded with slot 0; the pending head and tail cleared; and the id's **shift of
six** is exactly the 6 bits 64 slots need.

### The pool's end is the pending head

`022C31C0 + 64 × 0x80 = 022C51C0` — **the slot array ends on the byte the pending head begins**, and
the three list pointers then fill through `022C51D7` with the selector/index contiguous at
`022C51D8`. That turns "64 slots of `0x80`" from a loop bound into a layout.

### §2.1's builder fields were instruction displacements, not slot offsets

The builder's cursor starts at `022C31D8` — **slot 0 + `0x18`** — so every displacement in that loop
is `0x18` short of the slot offset. What it actually writes: **`+0x10`** the next slot, **`+0x18`**
the previous, **`+0x20`** a zero word, **`+0x28`** a zero dword, **`+0x58`** the index, **`+0x64`**
−1.

> **The page's own text is the witness.** §2.1 goes on to say `0032EC40(slot)` "sets `+0x64 = −1`",
> and `0032ECC5` is `mov dword ptr [rcx + 0x64], 0xffffffff` with the **slot base** in `rcx` — so one
> paragraph names the same field `+0x4C` and `+0x64`. Independently, `0032E990` links a slot into the
> pending list from its base using only **`+0x10` and `+0x18`**, exactly the two list pointers the
> cursor arithmetic predicts.

This matters for reconstruction: a pool built from the old list would put the index at `+0x40` and
zero `+8`/`+0x10` — **zeroing the next-slot pointer**, the one field a free list cannot lose.

**A decompiler prints the displacement, and the displacement is only an offset when the register
holds the base.** Here the compiler biased the cursor by `0x18` to keep both list pointers in
signed-byte reach, and the bias rides silently into every field name.

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on the party roster and leader change: the stride is the array, and the gap that hid a function (OPUS-PASS-PARTY-LEADER)

**`audit_coverage` 245 → 246.**

**Exact:** the five map bases all appear in `0031B9F0`, all four gaps **`0x12`**; `0x5A86 − 0x5A7E =
8 = 4 × 2`, with each function using **only its own** displacement; **16 of 16** names in §5 match
`functions.tsv`; `003590D0` is two instructions returning `[022C7FE0]`; and `003594C0` is
**confirmed absent** from the function list at **27 bytes**, as § says.

### The stride is the array, so the five maps are contiguous

`0x12` = 18 = **9 slots × 2 bytes** — the distance between bases is exactly one map's size. The five
are **one contiguous 90-byte block of 45 slots**, `+0x5A48`–`+0x5AA1`, with no padding. If the stride
exceeded the content there would be gaps; if it fell short the maps would overlap. It does neither —
which is what turns two independent numbers into a layout.

### Why the census could not see `003594C0`

`003594B0` ends at `003594BD`; two `int3`; the 27-byte function `003594C0`–`003594DA`; five `int3`;
then the next listed entry at `003594E0`. **It sits in a 34-byte gap between listed entries, padded
on both sides** — a complete ordinary function the list simply does not contain.

> `progress.py` reports the same shape in aggregate: the function list covers **92.91 %** of its own
> span, 31,933 regions and 568,793 bytes between listed bodies. **This is one of those regions, and it
> held the only writer of the value § was looking for.**

### The elided instruction is the one that carries "does nothing otherwise"

§'s excerpt runs `003594C9` → `003594CF`, skipping **`003594CC mov r8d, edx`**. `cmovne` overwrites
`r8d` only when the kind is non-zero, so on the zero path the store writes back whatever `r8d` held —
and that `mov` is what puts the *current* kind there. **The omitted instruction is precisely the one
that makes "and does nothing otherwise" true.**

`SpawnEntry_GetDeathLimit` and `SpawnEntry_GetScriptSelection` are the same function twice, differing

| | `00235EF0` | `00236140` |
|---|---|---|
| field read | `movzx eax, word [rcx+0xA]` | `movsx eax, byte [rcx+0x16]` |
| failure return | `or eax, 0xffffffff` → **−1** | `mov eax, 0xfffffffe` → **−2** |

> sentinel is a legal script selection.
>
> §'s conclusion holds *because of the zero-extension*, not because the family agreed a convention. A
> caller testing `== -1` on `GetScriptSelection` never sees its failure; one testing `== -2` cannot
> tell failure from a real selection of −2.

setter with no failure sentinel.

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on authored randomness: the two laws land on different lattices (OPUS-PASS-AUTHORED-RNG)

**`audit_coverage` 248 → 249.** §5's correction turns on one binary32 distinction —
`trunc(v × B − B)` against `trunc((v − 1) × B)` — which is checkable without the binary, because it
is entirely a statement about rounding.

**Both of §'s numbers reproduce**: from `v = 3FB90003` and `B = 10⁹`, the byte law gives
**445,312,896** and the algebraic law **445,312,864**, with the negative bound mirroring exactly.
The three stated sizes are exact, and the six tabulated rows all lie strictly inside their bound.

### They do not merely round differently — they land on different lattices

`P = fl(v·B)` is rounded at the magnitude of `[B, 2B)`, and `B` is a multiple of that ulp, so
**`D = P − B` can only be a multiple of it.** Over 3,000 draws at each of **22 bounds** from `2²⁰` to
`1.6 × 10⁹`, the byte law's outputs share a gcd of exactly `2^(floor(log2 bound) − 23)` at **every
one**, while the algebraic law's gcd is **1** throughout.

| bound | byte-law step | algebraic |
|---:|---:|---:|
| ≤ `2²³` | **1** | 1 |
| `2²⁴` | **2** | 1 |
| 10⁸ | **8** | 1 |
| 10⁹ | **64** | 1 |

> The divergence is **systematic above `bound ≥ 2²⁴`**, not an occasional tie-break. At a bound of a
> billion `f` returns only multiples of 64 — and **445,312,864 is a multiple of 32 but not 64, so it
> is off-lattice and unreachable**; it never appeared in 4,000 draws.
>
> **A reconstruction using the algebraic law would produce values the game can never return.** That is
> the sharper form of §'s own correction.

Below `2²⁴` the lattices coincide, which is why §'s thirteen predicted bounds came back **780 / 780**:
none sat on a boundary, exactly as § says.

`check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency` pass.

**Not claimed:** nothing was executed — this is arithmetic over the same binary32 constants, not the
345 bytes running. `EXP-070`'s isolated execution remains the only evidence that the *bytes* compute
this; this pass confirms the formula derived from them has the properties § attributes to it.

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on the script-to-native calling convention: the spawn vocabulary is 37 verbs, not seven (OPUS-PASS-CALLING-CONVENTION)

**`audit_coverage` 251 → 252.** All **eleven** stated sizes are exact, and so is every claim about
register use, arity (1,0,0,1,1,**2**,1), reverse argument order, `00510160`'s gate and `00510620`'s id
resolution. Three things were wrong.

### ⚠ The spawn vocabulary is 37 verbs, not seven

§1 and §5 told a modder **anything not on this list needs a native hook**. Disassembling **every**
verb handler in `scriptvm-verb-table.tsv` — 2,276 handler bodies over 1,960 rows — and collecting
direct `call`/`jmp` targets owned by `Spawn_Encounter_Lifecycle`: **37 call ids**, 35 handlers,
**35 of the 52** natives that owner holds. **The same instrument recovers all seven documented ids
(7/7) — that is the control**, so the extra **30** are not an artefact. Four are not even `btlAtel*`
(`03B8 bosskillall`, `0478 showenemy`, `0479 hideenemy`, `04DE killgroup`); others already let a
script set spawn distance, level, entry struct, despawn type and attempt limit, and read the death
count, elapsed time and entry point. **A modder following §5 would hook natively for work script
already exposes.** Scope: direct edges only, so **37 is a floor**.

### The return count contradicted the page's own two tables

§2 said "two of the seven return"; §7 said "two tail-jump `VMResult_WriteInt32`". Three do —
`005101F0`, `00510230`, `00510260` all end `jmp 0x26b4e0`; three forward to their native; `00510160`
plain `ret`s. **Three, three and one.** §3 and §9 already said three. The rule itself survives.

### `EF-1` answered — and its pointer was backwards

`0026B4C0` is `VMResult_WriteFloat32` (28 B), immediately *before* the int writer: `movss [slot+0x0C],
xmm1` / `mov byte [slot+0x15], 3`. `EF-1` pointed at `0026B500`, a bitfield setter on an unrelated
record. A census of the whole EXE for the idiom returns **exactly six** functions, including a
**third** writer `002651A0` (26 B) that stores tag `2` and *returns* `slot.+0x0C`. Across all six the
tag takes only `0, 1, 2, 3`, and **`1` is written exactly once and not as a byte**:

```asm
00261B97  mov word ptr [rsi + 0x14], 0x107     ; +0x14 = 7 AND +0x15 = 1, one store
```

A byte-level search for `mov byte […+0x15], 1` finds nothing and would call the value unused.

### The value stack is four parallel arrays, and all four failure modes are silent

`+0x00` depth, `+0x04` tag[64] (**1 = int32, 2 = float32**), `+0x44` byte[64] (pushes store 6),
`+0x84` u32[64] (store 0), **`+0x184` value[64]** — the payload, which the page never located.
**Capacity 63**: both pushes open `cmp eax, 0x3f` / `jge` / `ret`, so a 64th push stores nothing,
does not increment and does not report. And the two pops report on **opposite** conditions — the int
pop is silent on underflow and reports a bad tag, the float pop reports underflow and is silent on a
bad tag. `EF-6`'s "the float pop is the one that reports" is true of underflow only.

`check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency` pass.

**Not claimed:** `EF-2` untouched; `+0x44`/`+0x84` and slot `+0x10`/`+0x16`/`+0x18`/`+0x1C`–`+0x27`

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on script variables: both sevens are real, and they are different fields (OPUS-PASS-SCRIPT-VARIABLES)

**`audit_coverage` 253 → 254.** **The census reproduces exactly — every number.** Re-derived from
the two TSVs without reference to the prose: the six class totals and their script counts (12 of 12),
the classes summing to the descriptor total (**43,466 = 43,466**, no remainder), class 3 genuinely
**0**, and for `global` the **587** distinct offsets, **586** above `+0x200`, range `0x0` and
`0x200`–`0xCF4`, **9,448** declarations, all six width totals, **0** offsets carrying two widths,
**575** scripts on one offset and **110** single-script offsets. The machine side is equally exact,
including both jump-table addresses (`002626A8` scalar, `00262690` array element) and all six width
cases. Three things were wrong, all in the parts that say what to **build**.

### ⚠ `PUSHP` forces the width nibble, not the class

§2.1 said the reference descriptor has "the class forced to 7 (`or r8d, 0x70000000`)". By the page's
own bit table the class is bits 24–26 = `0x07000000`; `0x70000000` is bits 28–30, the **width**. And
the code *preserves* the class rather than forcing it — `and r9d, 0x7000000` / `or r8d, r9d` — then
`or r8d, 0x70000000`. **Width 7 is outside the `0..5` every loader accepts** (`cmp …, 5` / `ja`), so
it cannot be loaded as a value, which is exactly what marks it a reference; the class must survive
because the reference still names one of the six homes. A reimplementation following the old sentence
would write `0x07000000` and the engine would read an **array**.

### ⚠ §4's formula stops one step short for every array element

The resolver returns the element **base** and the flattened **index** separately; the handlers
combine them — `[rcx+rax]`, `[rax+rcx*2]`, `[rax+rcx*4]` in `PUSHV`, and an explicit
`add edx, edx` / `lea edx, [rdx*4]` switch in `PUSHP`. For a scalar the index is 0 and nothing shows;
**for an array element wider than a byte the formula is short by `flatIndex × width`.**

### ⚠ The push tag is bit 27 and is never checked against the width

`PUSHV` picks the *load* from the width nibble and the *tag* from the kind word the resolver sets
from **bit 27 alone**. The fields are independent: width `4` with bit 27 set pushes an integer
**tagged float**, width `5` with it clear pushes a float **tagged int**, the four bytes copied
unreinterpreted either way. The encoding permits it and the engine does not object, so a validator
deriving one field from the other would be inventing a rule.

### The stack contract confirmed from a third site, and the out-record mapped

The resolver **open-codes** the pop for array indices and matches instruction for instruction: tag
array at `+0x04`, payload at `+0x184` stride 4, **tag 1 = int32, tag 2 = float32**, bad tag reports
code `1`, empty stack silently yields index 0. `PUSHV` and `PUSHP` re-check `cmp eax, 0x3f` / `jge`
inline, so a variable pushed at depth 63 is dropped as silently as any other. The 0x30-byte
out-record, which the page mentions and never maps: `+0x00` u8 constant **6**, `+0x04` u16 kind,
`+0x08` u16, `+0x0A` u16 variable index, `+0x0C` u32 original descriptor, `+0x10` u64 base address,
`+0x18` u32 element descriptor, `+0x1C` u32 flattened index. **That `+0x00` answers a loose end**:
the value stack's `+0x44` byte array, which both generic pushes fill with `6`, is written by `PUSHV`
from this field — the `6` is a record value, not a magic constant, and the array records a stack
value's provenance. What its other values are is still unknown.

### Two smaller notes

`0016D6A0`'s body is `C2 00 00`, **`ret 0`**, confirmed from the image, so `DVAR` is inert — but the
page called the callee "the CFG stub", the reading `B-2/a` explicitly warns against. `DVAR` passes
**three** arguments, `(slot.+0x28, poppedInt, &02099D48)` — a data pointer, so a **fourth argument
shape** for the fold beyond the three `B-2/a` catalogues. And §2.3's class-3 base was written
`payload + [payload + 0x40]`, colliding with the *save* payload two rows above; it is `*(slot + 0)`,
the script image — renamed `img`, as §4 already had it.

`check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass.

the `POPV` notification path were not re-derived. Everything static; the corpus figures come from the

The five zeroing stores are qwords; the last, `003847F3 mov qword ptr [rcx + 0x28], rax`, writes

`0x2A` allocation, which would have six bytes of the next variable zeroed.

`00384870 mov qword ptr [rip + 0x2b3a911], rax` caches the resolved target-unit pointer at

it" — true of the context, but this pointer outlives it. **`0031B860` is also called twice with the
same argument**, once for the `+0x55` byte (result cached) and once for the presence test.

### With no source, every has(id) is false rather than unknown

`test r8, r8` / `je` skips the merge **and** the `+0x04` store, so "the source has no statuses" and
"there is no source" are indistinguishable to every slot.

### Three bookkeeping corrections to the field map's columns

The `w / r` column counts distinct **functions**, not sites (`+0x08` is read at 45 sites in 31
functions, `+0x10` at 76 in 34, `+0x29` at 8 in 3); it counts an `rw` as a write at `+0x1B` — which
has **no** pure write, both touches being `and byte ptr [rbx+0x1b], 0x7f` — but not at `+0x08`; and
the `width` column mixed field width with widest access, giving `+0x20` an `8` that was the zeroing
qword when the only read is `movzx ecx, byte ptr [r8 + 0x20]`. `+0x20` corrected to `1`.

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on the encoded-id class registry: the class is the id's top nibble (OPUS-PASS-ID-CLASS-REGISTRY)

**`audit_coverage` 255 → 256.** The jump table at `00323054` was decoded entry by entry and every arm
read to its join. **All 29 descriptors this page lists reproduce exactly**, as does the alias
structure — **29 distinct arm addresses for 32 classes**, `00322EBB` serving 15/30/31 and `00322FCB`
serving 25/32. The shared tail is `lo ≤ id ≤ hi − 1`, so a "bound" is a **count** and the valid set is
`[lo, lo + count)`.

### ⚠ The class *is* the id's top nibble — and the page never says so

§4 calls class 1 "dynamic" and stops. `FUN_00309440` is 30 bytes: `shr eax, 0xc` (the top nibble),
reject above `0xE`, `imul rcx, rax, 0x58`, and **the record's first dword is the class**. Reading the
fifteen records at `01EEBCF8`: nibble `0`→class **5**, `1`→6, …, `E`→class **19**. The arms agree
independently — those classes carry id bases `0x0000`, `0x1000` … `0xE000` in lockstep. **So
`class = (id >> 12) + 5`, an encoded id is `(kind << 12) | index`, and classes 1–4 and 20–32 sit
outside that space indexing from zero.** §3 lists a descriptor per class and leaves every id base
unstated, so a reader would take class 15's ids to start at 0 when they start at `0xA000`.

**The page already knew this in three places without saying it.** §5b names class 14 by
`InventoryBundleClass09_…`, class 15 by `…Class0A_…`, class 18 by `…Class0D_…` — nibbles `9`, `A`,
`D`, exactly `class − 5` — and each kind record's fifth dword is that kind's handler: nibble `9` holds
`002FD530`, `A` holds `002FD640`, `D` holds `002FD780`, **the very three functions §5b names.**

*(Not claimed: the record's second dword looks like a capacity — nibble `0xE` holds `0xFFF`, exactly
class 19's compiled-in span — but that is **one** case, so it is recorded as suggestive only. Nibbles
`5`, `7`, `B` — classes 10, 12, 16 — hold zero there and a null handler, which sits beside §5c's
finding about 12 and 16 without being offered as its explanation.)*

### ⚠ Three more corrections

**Class 19's range is `[0xE000, 0xEFFE]`, not `[0xE000, 0xEFFF]`** — the tail rejects `id > ecx - 1`.
That is `0xFFF` ids, matching the kind record, so class 19 obeys the same rule as the table arms with
the count compiled in.

**Class 22 is a fourth arm without a table**, the twin of class 23 nine bytes before it:
`mov ecx, 4 / xor eax, eax / jmp 0x32302c` → ids `0..3`. §3 said "no global read"; §4 counted three
non-table arms. **It is four** — 1, 19, 22, 23.

**Class 13 is four tables, not one.** Its arm is 105 bytes where the others are 42 because it reads
`02EBF090`, `02EBF088`, `02EBF080` and `02EBF078`, each NULL-guarded, and sums their counts before
the bound check. A census that takes the *first* global a function reads — how §3 was built, and how
my own first pass reproduced it — sees one descriptor and stops.

`check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass.

**Not claimed:** §5b's naming census and §5c's two-referrer argument were not re-derived; what each
descriptor contains is untouched. Everything static.

## 2026-09-13 — retraction: I claimed as new an encoding I had already published and audited (OPUS-RETRACT-NIBBLE-NOVELTY)

The class-registry pass committed hours earlier (`e0ccab6`) carried a section headed **"The class
*is* the id's top nibble — and the page never says so"**, presenting `class = (id >> 12) + 5` as
something the database did not have.

**It had it.** [`the-encoded-id-space-and-the-query-record.md`](../00-Engine-Core-Runtime/the-encoded-id-space-and-the-query-record.md)
§2.1 states `class = nibble + 5` outright, derives `FUN_00309440` instruction by instruction, and
§2.2 gives the whole `0x58`-byte descriptor layout — **and I audited that page myself** (`bf0d33b`,
"falsification pass 1 on the encoded id space"). The claim of novelty was false, and false about my
own work.

**Two factual errors followed from not looking:**

| I wrote | it is |
|---|---|
| "`lea rax, [rip + 0x1be28a2]` → `01EEBCF8`… **the record's first dword** is the class" | the table begins at **`01EEBCC0`**; the class is record **`+0x38`**, and `01EEBCC0 + 0x38 = 01EEBCF8` — which is *why* the function indexes with a bare `nibble × 0x58` |
| "each record's **fifth dword** is that kind's handler" | record **`+0x48`**, and it is the **mutate** handler specifically — the **query** handler is `+0x50` |
| "the **second** dword looks like a capacity … recorded as suggestive" | record **`+0x3C`** is the **id count**, already derived from the rebaser on the sibling page — not a guess needing hedging |

**What survives, and is this pass's own:** all 29 listed descriptors reproduce; 29 distinct arms for
32 classes; the shared tail `lo ≤ id ≤ hi − 1`; **class 19's range is `[0xE000, 0xEFFE]`**;
**class 22 is a fourth non-table arm** (bound 4, ids `0..3`); **class 13 sums four descriptors**
(`02EBF090` + `02EBF088` + `02EBF080` + `02EBF078`); and the fifteen arms carry id bases `0x0000`…
`0xE000` in lockstep — an **independent confirmation** of the sibling's mapping from the validator's
side, which is what the section should have said in the first place.

**Propagated:** the sibling page repeated the same off-by-one (`0xE000`–`0xEFFF`); corrected there
too, with the tail's `lea eax, [rcx - 1]` as the evidence and the record's `+0x3C` count of `0xFFF`
as the cross-check.

**The lesson, recorded because it is the second of its kind this session:** *before calling something
unstated, search the database for it — including one's own recent passes.* `check_links` and
`check_consistency` both pass on a page that claims novelty, because neither can see a claim that is
merely redundant. The first of its kind was `EF-5` on the bridge page, filed as a question whose
answer was already in a TSV; this one is the same failure with my own name on both ends.

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on the type-id partition: the twenty-eighth site tells all thirteen apart (OPUS-PASS-TYPE-ID-BAND)

**`audit_coverage` 256 → 257.** §2's ladder reproduces **instruction for instruction at every address
it quotes**, including the annotation easiest to get wrong — `cmp byte ptr [rbx+5], al` does test
against **zero**, because `al` survives the previous `test eax, eax` / `jne`. `FUN_0050FF20`
reproduces too, with `sub al, 7` / `cmp al, 0x12` giving the nineteen (`7 … 25`) exactly.

### The predicate census, re-run image-wide

`sub <r>, 0x1B` followed within three instructions by `cmp <r>, N`: **27 sites in 24 functions,
every bound `0xC`, every one the `al` form, nothing else** — across CombatAction 6, CombatFormula 5,
ActorEntity 3, Rewards 2, Status 2, CombatAI 1, Script-VM bridge 1, unowned 7, and **all five
functions §3 names are in it**. *§3's own figure of 28 counts a wider net — every constant tested
against a byte loaded from `[reg+4]`. My re-implementation of that criterion found one of them, so
**the instrument is under-powered and the 28 is not challenged**; the 28th site was reached another
way.*

### ⚠ The 28th site is the one place the thirteen are not interchangeable

`BattleSpecialSequence_DeriveActionPresentationCode` (`00309230`) uses `type − 0x1B` **as an index**,
not a bound: `movzx eax, byte [rax+4]` / `sub eax, 0x1b` / `cdqe` / `mov eax, [rsp + rax*4 + 0x20]`
into a **thirteen-entry** table materialised inline from three 16-byte constants (`00D103B0`,
`00D103C0`, `00D103D0`) plus `mov dword [rsp+0x50], 0x4E` — `4+4+4+1 = 13`. The values are
**42, 45, 48 … 78**: thirteen distinct codes forming an exact progression, **`code = 3 × (type −
13)`**. §3's *one predicate, twenty-seven copies* is right about the twenty-seven; **this one
distinguishes every member of the band**, and the stride of 3 says each type owns a run of three
codes, so the presentation space is 39 wide rather than 13.

### ⚠ Two outcomes the tables omit

**A sixth Script-VM class, `−2`** (`0050FF4D mov ebx, 0xfffffffe`), when the record lookup
`00320AB0` returns NULL — before `record[+5]` is read. §2's table began at `+5 = 1 → −1`, so a
reader would map "no record" onto "kind 1".

**The LP rule is the partition *and* a flag gate.** `002F90C0` continues past where §2's excerpt
stops: `(record.+0x64 | record.+0x3C) & 0x80000003` must be zero — bits 0, 1, 31. The span check is
necessary, not sufficient. That field pair is the same merged flag word the evaluation context
builds into its `+0x04`/`+0x08`; whether it is the same record type is **not** established here.

`check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass.

### ⚠ `+0x18`'s zero count was taken at the wrong width

The row declares **u32** and tallies `0 × 424`. At u32 the count is **387**; `424` is the **u16**
count (u8 is 475). This is `EVIDENCE-STANDARD.md`'s own amendment — *a count without its unit cannot
be checked* — landing on a row that states its unit and then counts in another.

The 200 non-`0xFFFF` rows split by high nibble (class = nibble + 5, per the encoded-id space page):

82–145; nibble `4` → class 9, 24 rows, 158–181; nibble `0xC` → class 17, 31 rows within 208–274.
**Each block numbers from its own base**, so "`0x3000 + n`" is true only because the class-8 block
starts at row 0.

### ⚠ The help id changes rule at a single missing row

`+0x00 = 4000 + n + 1` holds **for rows 0–80 and no further**. Row 81 carries `4000` — no help text —
and **from row 82 the rule is `4000 + n`**. One row without a string shifts every id after it by one.
216 rows carry a help id; **81** satisfy the published form. **And those 81 are the same rows as the
class-8 block** — rows 0–80 are one authored block carrying sequential help ids `4001`–`4081` and
sequential menu ids `0x3000`–`0x3050`. Both id schemes are per-block sequences, not per-row
properties.

## 2026-09-13 — retraction: the value-stack layout was published a second time, again as new (OPUS-RETRACT-VALUESTACK-NOVELTY)

The calling-convention pass (`8eecd2e`, this morning) carried a section headed **"The value stack is
four parallel arrays, and both of its ends fail silently"**, and a table of the two pops' opposite
failure modes, presented as findings of that pass.

**Both were already published — by me, on 2026-09-12.**
[`CONTRACT-script-to-native-bridge.md`](../01-Script-VM-Native-Bridge/CONTRACT-script-to-native-bridge.md)
states *"`VmValueStack`, size `0x284`… **Four parallel arrays of 64**, indexed by slot"*, gives
`+0x184 i32/f32[0x40]` as **THE VALUE**, says *"**63 usable slots, not 64** — both pushes write only
when `depth < 0x3F`"*, and records that *"both pushes write literal `0` to `+0x84`"*. The
mirror-image failure modes are the **headline** of `OPUS-PASS-SCRIPT-BRIDGE` that same day:
*"each pop reports one failure, and they report opposite ones."*

### What still stands as that pass's own

| finding | status |
|---|---|
| the spawn vocabulary is **37 verbs, not seven** (2,276 handler bodies censused, with the seven recovered as a control) | **new** |
| the return count is **three / three / one**, not two / five | **new** |
| `EF-1` answered: `0026B4C0` is the float writer, `0026B500` was the wrong pointer, and `1` is written **once in the image** by the fused `mov word ptr [rsi+0x14], 0x107` | **new** |
| the six-function census of the `+0x11` / `+0xA8` idiom, and the third writer `002651A0` | **new** |
| the 40-byte slot field map over all six users | **new** |
| the eleven exact sizes, the register-usage rule, the reverse argument order | confirmations, and published as such |

### Why the gate I built this morning did not catch it

`check_novelty_claims.py` keys on **absence phrasings** — "never says", "no document", "not stated".
That section made **no absence claim at all**; it simply put known facts under a **"New:"** heading.
Matching "new" is not viable — the word is everywhere in this corpus — so **the gate's population
genuinely does not include this shape**, and I am not widening it to chase one case.

**The lesson is procedural, not tooling, and the tool for it already exists:**
`check_already_answered.py --addr 00267E10 --addr 00267F60 --term VmValueStack` would have returned
the contract in one call. It was written for exactly this, its docstring says so, and **I did not run
it — for the second time today.** The first was the nibble retraction eight commits ago, where the
same omission produced the same result.

> Twice in one session, the check that would have caught it was a habit rather than a step. The
> honest conclusion is that **"search before you claim" belongs in the pass procedure, not in a
> checker** — a gate can only see the claims that announce themselves.

One thing does connect forward: the contract's open item *"what the `6` at `+0x44 + slot` is"* is
partly answered by today's script-variables pass — `PUSHV` writes that byte from the resolver's
out-record `+0x00`, so the `6` is a record field rather than a constant in the push helpers. Its
*meaning* remains open, and that finding stands.

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on the display record: the `0x27` bound is on the output, not the index (OPUS-PASS-DISPLAY-RECORD)

**`audit_coverage` 270 → 271.** *(`check_already_answered.py` run first; `0031B9F0` is already held
by `the-five-parallel-slot-maps.md`, which this pass does not repeat.)*

Every stated extent is exact — `00329220` **1,933 B**, `0031FE70` **79 B**, `00320040` **82 B**, and
`0031B9F0` **200 B** — and the record arithmetic reproduces instruction for instruction:
`imul rcx, rax, 0x1c8` / `mov rax, [02EBF190]` / `add rax, 8` / `add rcx, rax`, with `xor ecx, ecx`
for the null record and `xor r9d, r9d` for this wrapper's `full = 0`.

### ⚠ The `0x27` bound is on the resolver's output, not on the member index

§2.1 reads *"a member index `≤ 0x27` becomes … + index × 0x1C8"*. The test sits **two instructions
after the call** and is on `al` — **what the resolver returned**, a mapped slot. The member index is
bounded separately and far more tightly: `0031B9F0` opens `lea ecx, [r8 + 0x17]` / `call 0x322c50` —
`IsValidForClass(**23**, index)` — and **class 23's arm is the literal bound of 9**, so the accepted
indices are **`0`–`8`**, nine, the party configuration's own count.

> **The two chain through a sentinel.** An index of 9 or more returns **`0xFF`**, and `0xFF > 0x27`,
> so the outer test rejects it and the null record results anyway — which is *why* that test looks
> like a bound on the index. They are different numbers on different quantities, and a reconstruction
> admitting indices to `0x27` would index a nine-entry map with forty values. `0x27` = 39 is the
> ceiling on the **slot** a map may name.

`check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass.

**Not claimed:** `00329220`'s 1,933 bytes were not re-read — the field map, the flag word, the twelve
stats fields and the distance threshold are untouched; the five maps belong to their own page.

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on the workbench save/restore: a census on the globals finds the writer and misses the reader (OPUS-PASS-WORKBENCH-SAVE)

**`audit_coverage` 273 → 274.** *(`check_already_answered.py` run first, per today's amendment.)*
**Every cell of §4's table reproduces**: `Save` `0036D930` is **89 B** and `Restore` `0036D8E0`
**66 B**; **9 functions call each**, the two sets are **identical** so neither "saves without
restoring" nor "restores without saving" has a member; **all eighteen site addresses are exact**,
function for function; the **four tail-jumps are precisely `0026F413`, `003AFFAB`, `00431F0A`,
`0046242E`** with the other five `call`; and `0036D91A mov dword ptr [022D8F08], r8d` with `r8d = 0`
is the zeroing that makes a nested save lose the outer frame, on the same count `Restore` loops on.

### A census keyed on the globals finds `Save` and misses `Restore`

§3 quotes `Save`'s `lea r9, [02EC0800]` — a direct rip-relative reference. **`Restore` does not use
that form**: `0036D8EE lea r9, [rip - 0x24d8f5]` materialises **`00120000`, the image base**, and the
two accesses are `[r9 + rax*8 + 0x2da0a00]` and `[r9 + rcx*8 + 0x2da0800]`. So a whole-image sweep
for operands *resolving* to `02EC0800`/`02EC0A00` returns **one function** — the writer — and a
reader doing that census would conclude the save is never read back.

> The database has met this shape before — *a displacement is only an offset when the register holds
> the base*. This is the same trap from the other side: the register holds the **image base**, so the
> displacement is the whole address.

`check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass.

`0030FA00` is **146 B** and `0031B860` **83 B**; the census is **7 instructions in 6 functions**, no
more and no fewer; the six byte-wise sites §2.1 lists are exact **address for address**
(`0030FA0F`, `0030FA79`, `0023B124`, `00325DDF`, `003857C6`, `0038868A`), with `003106EB
mov word ptr [rbx + 0x6b7], bp` the seventh and the only non-byte access.

### Both player-facing claims are single instructions, and both are exact

Movement: `00325DDF cmp byte ptr [rdi + 0x6b7], 0` / `ja` — non-zero leaves immediately. Suppression:
`0023B121 or ebx, 2` builds the value up, then `0023B124 cmp` / **`0023B12D cmova ebx, r14d`**
**replaces** it. **`cmova` is the word "wholesale"** — the distinction §1 draws between *overriding*
and *contributing one more flag* is the difference between that `cmova` and the `or` two instructions
before it, and a reimplementation OR-ing a combo flag into the same accumulator would be wrong in
exactly the way the sentence warns about.

### Nothing to add

The two-byte pair and the word store — what this pass had ready — are already §2.1's opening claim,
with the same instruction offered as its proof. Found by searching before claiming.

`check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass.

**Not claimed:** §3's roll-and-store path, §4's focus fields and §6's reinterpretation were not
re-derived. Everything static.

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on the map_ctrl pack: the census took its layout from the code that enforces it (OPUS-PASS-MAP-PACK)

**`audit_coverage` 277 → 278.** *(`check_already_answered.py` run first, per today's amendment.)*
**The 550 `.mpk` files are not in this working tree** — they live in the VBF — so this pass could not
re-extract the corpus. It checked the two things that make the census trustworthy instead.

**The corpus table matches `census.out.txt` line for line**: 550 of 550 with the output's own
denominator control (`archive index: 550 (published 550)`); `count field: {32: 550}`; `layout ends
exactly at the file size: 550 []` with an empty failure list; `{True: 4568}` with no `False` key;
and fourteen never-present slots.

**An internal check neither artifact makes:** the eighteen per-slot presence counts (`545, 46, 461,
461, 270, 545, 387, 2, 456, 212, 421, 136, 32, 17, 396, 133, 31, 17`) sum to **exactly 4,568**, the
same number as the zero-slot checks — produced by different lines over different loop variables, so
each is a check on the other.

**The census's layout is the loader's own arithmetic.** `0036B980` is **727 B**, both cited ranges
lie inside it, and the size check is `lea eax, [rdx+1]` / `lea rcx, [rcx*4 + 0x3f]` /
`and ecx, 0xffffffc0` — `(count + 1) * 4` rounded up to `0x40` — then per size `je` past zeros,
`add eax, 0x40`, `add ecx, eax`. That is the assumption instruction for instruction, and the
accumulation **is** the "sizes add up to the file" acceptance test. The census did not guess a layout
