## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on the save version stamps: one is checked, the other is only written (OPUS-PASS-SAVE-STAMPS)

**`audit_coverage` 278 → 279.** *(`check_already_answered.py` run first, per today's amendment.)*
Both getters are **six bytes** and nothing but the constant; **each has exactly one caller, the same
one** (`00253A80`), with the control passing at **362** `memcpy` callers. §2's central claim holds:
the one comparison is `00233C4D cmp dword ptr [rax], 0x5071901` / `je`, **an equality test**, with no
ordered branch near it.

### ⚠ The getter is not the only way the stamp reaches memory

Censusing both constants as immediates across every function body finds **four sites**, one of them a
**second writer** of `0x05071901` that never touches the getter: `002370CD mov r8d, 0x7410` /
`call` memset / `002370DF mov dword ptr [rax], 0x5071901`. So §2's *"both are written into the save
header at initialisation"* names one route; **`002370C0` zeroes a `0x7410`-byte block and stamps it
inline**, and a reader tracing the constant through the getter's single caller would never reach it.

### ⚠ The two stamps are not symmetric — only one is ever checked

`0x05071901` has **three** immediates (getter, inline writer, one `cmp`). **`0x20050223` has one** —
its own getter, and nothing else in the executable. The only way to hold that value is to call the
getter, and its **only caller is the initialiser**, so **no comparison anywhere can test against
it.** §2's `V-2` answer is right about `+0x60` and **vacuously** right about `+0x58`: there is no
comparison of it at all. **The `+0x58` stamp is written and never read back** — for a modder a
sharper fact than "it is a magic": editing it cannot make a save fail to load, and editing `+0x60`
can.

`check_links`, `check_counts`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass.

**Not claimed:** which block `00233C10` and `002370C0` belong to, and what `0x237DF0` does on the
mismatch path, were not read; §4's normalise sequence and the open header map are untouched.
Everything static.

## 2026-09-13 — the 294 bare `**ANSWERED**` rows are not a scripted recovery (OPUS-MEASURE-BARE-ANSWERED)

`progress.py` counts a verdict cell that is exactly `**ANSWERED**` as **neither** closed nor open,
because the state was inferred from prose rather than recorded with an answer. That is **291** rows by `progress.py`'s parse and **294** by the looser scan used here —
the single largest lever left on `questions_closed`, and an obvious candidate for a script that lifts
each answer out of the owning document's ticked checklist item.

**Measured before attempting it**, over all 522 documents:

- bare rows with a well-formed id — **294** (looser scan; `progress.py` says **291**)
- a *ticked* item whose **own label** is that id, with ≥40 chars of answer text — **22**
- ticked item but no answer text — **59**
- **no ticked, labelled item anywhere — 211**
- ambiguous, two different answers — **2**

A looser rule — any checklist item merely *mentioning* the id — reports **136**, which is where a
script would have stopped. **Hand-reviewing the 22 that survived the strict rule found about five
unsafe:** `K-12` and `K-13` are different questions sharing one labelled item, so both were offered
the *same* answer; `AY-10` and `F-3` already carry their answer in the **question** cell; `C-11`'s
candidate answers something the row does not ask. **A bulk edit would have been ~23 % wrong**, and
the loose rule far worse.

**Nothing was written to the register.** *(First attempt at the header note used a markdown table; every pipe row in that file is parsed as a register row, so it inflated the denominator by five before I noticed and rewrote it as a list — the metric is measured from the file's shape, so prose has to stay out of table form.)* The measurement is recorded in `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`'s header
instead, so the next person starts from it: **for 211 of the 294 the answer is not written beside a
labelled checklist item at all**, and recovering those is per-row reading by someone who can judge
whether the answer answers the question — not a merge.

> Worth stating plainly because the counter was the temptation. Filling 294 verdicts would have moved
> `questions_closed` by about six points; being wrong on a quarter of them would have put false
> answers in the one index that is supposed to say what is *not* known.

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on the all-ones empty convention: two adjacent pairs, not three, and the sentinel is the width's maximum, not the index space's (OPUS-PASS-ALL-ONES)

**`audit_coverage` 282 → 283.** *(`check_already_answered.py` run first, per today's amendment; 114
documents hit on `sentinel`, so every claim below names its own address.)*

**Everything quoted reproduces.** All six of §2's instructions are at the addresses §2 gives them
with the operands §2 gives them, decoded from the shipped image. The pool base is provable from a
line the page does not quote: `00512CD4  lea r10, [rip + 0x2795515]` → **`02CA81F0`**. And **all four
census rows reproduce exactly** — 169/119, 87/65, 22/18, 107/49 — under a recipe the page does not
state: over every listed function body, a `mov`/`cmp` whose destination is a memory operand **whose
base is not `rip`**. Excluding globals is what makes the numbers come out (it drops 18 byte-set and
9 word-set sites); it is the right choice and an unstated scope.

### ⚠ Two adjacent pairs, not three — and a sixth field named nowhere in the database

The strict test returns exactly **six** (function, displacement) pairs, as §4 says, but not the six
§4 describes: `+0xD`/`+0xE` (`00512CD0`), `+0xB8`/`+0xB9` (`00504F00`), **`+0x695` alone**
(`00306760`), and **`+0x412` (`FUN_004225a0`)**, which no document mentions. `+0x696` is *compared*
against `0xFF` at `00306882` but the store beside it is `0030688B  mov byte ptr [rbx + 0x696], al`
— **the handle moving across from `+0x695`**, not a release. It fails the strict test by exactly the
write-here / check-there asymmetry §4 describes.

### ⚠ The sixth strict field is a countdown, not an index

`FUN_004225a0`'s whole subject is `+0x412`: when it reads `0xFF` the field is re-seeded from a draw
taken modulo `[+0x2DE] - [+0x2DD] + 1` and scaled by a global (`004225B5`–`004225F8`); each call
decrements it; at zero it is written back to `0xFF` and the function returns 1
(`004225FE`–`0042262F`). **One of the six fields carrying this page's strongest evidence is a
timer.** The convention is wider than the title's "index spaces": the general form is that every
value in the field's live range already means something, so *empty* must sit outside it — true of a
countdown (`0` = fires now) for the same reason as an index (`0` = slot zero).

### ⚠ "Maximum of the space" is the maximum of the field width

The pool initialiser settles the size the §2 argument rests on: `00512F10`–`00512F1F` loops
`cmp ecx, 0x20` with `lea rax, [rax + 0x10]`, writing `[rax - 3] = cl`. **The pool is 32 records of
16 bytes, `02CA81F0`–`02CA83EF`, and `+0xC` is each record's own slot number.** So the live index
range is `0`–`31` while the sentinel is `255`: the empty value is the largest the **byte** can hold,
not the largest index. A modder who read §3 literally would write `31`.

### §6's third unknown is untested, not unsearchable — and the instrument's first two answers were discarded

A byte field loaded, **scaled**, and used to *address* something, compared against the candidate
sentinel in the same function, with `00512CD0` `+0xD`/`+0xE` as the positive control: **22**
(function, field) pairs for `0xFF`, **80** for `0`. The first version returned **zero for the
control** (it accepted only field-form compares, where `00512CE7` compares the register, and treated
`00512CEB  movzx eax, al` as a kill) and its numbers were not reported. The second counted bare
`imul` and reported 109; its best candidate — `0035F760` `+0x5D`/`+0x5E`/`+0x5F`, three adjacent
bytes each tested against zero — is `imul r14d ; shr 8`, **fixed-point analog scaling**. 80
unadjudicated candidates is not evidence that `0` is a sentinel; it is evidence that §6's absence
was never searched.

### The widths the census does not reach

Same recipe: **4-byte 569 set / 394 compared**, **8-byte 247 / 14** (non-global, sites). And the
widths differ in kind — **zero** `rip`-relative `cmp byte, 0xFF` and **zero** `rip`-relative
`cmp word, 0xFFFF` against **1,738** `rip`-relative `cmp dword, -1`. **No two-byte field passes the
strict test at all** (0 against 6), so §3's two-byte half rests entirely on its two cited documents
— one of which records a *register*-form check this memory-operand census cannot see.

### Also closed, and routed

§6's "what the `+0x695`/`+0x696` pair holds" was **already answered elsewhere while this page kept
it open**: the battle-unit field map names them PROVEN as `actionPresentationSlot` /
`secondActionPresentationSlot`. `+0xB8`/`+0xB9` is narrowed — `00504F00` is the `.fcp` motion-entry
loader, and that sheet's open item is the same question. Two peer-owned corrections were **routed,
not applied**: `OPUS-CONTRA-SLOT-HANDOFF` (the `0030688B` transcription) and
`OPUS-CONTRA-RELATION-WALK` (`00512F53`–`00512F8A` described as a 32-entry table match — the **32 is
right**, proved from the initialiser that page does not cite, but the instructions are a list walk
from `[r11 + 0xC]` with no bound).

`check_links`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass. `check_counts` adds one advisory of
its own known kind to the 432 it already reports: it reads the "4" out of a §4 cross-reference
beside the six-row strict-test table. Not a defect, and not silenced.

**Not claimed:** six of §3's eight sightings were not re-derived from the image; the two two-byte
ones were re-read in their own documents only. The 80 candidates are unadjudicated. What
`+0xB8`/`+0xB9` and `+0x412` hold is still unread. Everything static — nothing executed, nothing

§4 identifies a thunk "without ambiguity" by *body ≤ 16 bytes and its **first instruction** is a `jmp`

## 2026-09-13 — a tool for the third shape of stranded answer, and the first defect it found (OPUS-STRANDED-UNKNOWNS)

**Built only because the payoff was measured first.** Two passes today hit the same shape: a page
keeping an unknown open that *another* document had already answered —
`the-all-ones-empty-convention.md` §6 on `+0x695`/`+0x696`, which the battle-unit field map names
PROVEN, and `which-roll-is-on-which-generator.md` §10 on `FUN_00319530`, which four register rows
answer. `check_answered_not_established.py` cannot reach either: it looks for a document
contradicting **itself**, in the same block.

`check_stranded_unknowns.py` takes each **un-closed** bullet in a document's *"what is not known"*
section, and reports the addresses it names that another document has already **closed** — an
ANSWERED-class register row whose *question cell* names the address, or a ticked `- [x]` item
elsewhere. Bare co-citation is deliberately not a hit; that is
`check_already_answered.py`'s job at authoring time.

**Measured, run by run:** 259 → **62** (two filters) → **54** (a widened closed-item rule) → **53**
(after fixing the first defect). Each filter came from a real false positive: a bullet naming more
than two addresses is a *list*, not a question about one of them; and a register row must name the
address in its **question** cell, since `FZ-28` merely mentions `002628B0` as a writer. The
closed-item rule had `~~` unanchored and so never matched `- ~~What X computes.~~ Answered`, the
corpus's commonest closed form — thirty already-struck bullets were reported before that was fixed.

### ⚠ The first defect it found: three statements stranded by their own page's correction

`the-record-behind-every-actor.md`:194 asked *"Who calls `00266530`, and therefore when a slot is
recycled. Not traced. `EH-6`."* **`EH-6` was ANSWERED on 2026-09-08**, and its answer says it
*overturned that document's headline*: the pool is one allocation `memset` to zero, so slots are
**never recycled**. §2 of the page carries the correction. **Three statements elsewhere in the same
page did not:**

* the `EH-6` bullet itself, still `- [ ]` and still "Not traced";
* a §7 **modding note** telling readers *"a recycled actor is not a clean actor — everything else in
  those bytes survives from the slot's previous occupant"*, when there is no previous occupant;
* an **evidence row** still reading **PROVEN** for *"It recycles rather than constructs"*.

**All three survived the falsification pass of 2026-09-12.** An append-only correction moves the
section it lands in; it does not move the summary, the advice or the evidence table, and a pass that
reads the corrected section can come away satisfied. All three are now struck and corrected on the
page, with the class recorded there.

**An honest note on the instrument.** That true positive was matched through an *unrelated* register
row, because `EH-6`'s question cell names the function by **name** and this tool keys on addresses.
Recall found the defect; the cited evidence did not explain it. The docstring says so, and says to
read the hit rather than the citation. The residual class is a hot address whose identity is answered
while a question about one of its fields stays open — `01F82D20` accounts for three hits that way,
left in deliberately because the output is a reading list, not a defect list.

`--self-test` carries both of today's shapes as fixtures. `check_links`, `check_questions` pass.

**Not claimed:** the other 53 hits are unadjudicated. The tool keys on addresses only, so every
unknown phrased purely by name is invisible to it — including the very row that answers the defect it
found. Nothing executed, nothing observed live.

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on the 512-byte widget: the unread arm contained the refutation of the read one (OPUS-PASS-512-WIDGET)

**`audit_coverage` 287 → 288.** *(`check_already_answered.py` run **one address at a time and read in
full**, per today's amendment 2026-09-13b — which is how §7's second unknown turned out to be
answered.)*

**Reproduced, instruction for instruction:** sizes **38 / 1,914 / 175**; the registrar's whole body
(`00565DD7 cmp qword [rax+0x168], 0`, `00565DE4 lea rdx,[rip+0x15]` → `00565E00`,
`00565DEB mov ecx, 0x200`, `00565DF0 jmp 0x244F50`); the handler's dispatch and kind-1 store
(`00565E27`, `00565E50`, `00565E57`); and the four instruments — `E8` **0**, `E9` **0**, code
memory-operand **1**, data qword **0**. **§5's correction is confirmed as written**: `00244F50` has
**exactly one** `rip`-relative operand in its 175 bytes, bytes `48 8b 1d d2 9a e4 01` at `00244F7F`
resolving to **`0208EA58`**, and `02093958` does not occur in the body.

### ⚠ The widget is not built once per run — its own handler tears it down

§3 records that only the kind-1 arm was read. Past `kind > 8` the handler tests `0x11F`, then
`sub ecx, 9 / cmp ecx, 9 / ja` and jumps through a **ten-entry table at `0056657C`** covering kinds
**9–18** (`11`, `15`, `17` fall to the default; the table is followed by `int3` padding, so ten is
all of it). **Kind 18 lands at `00566217`** and does `call 0x2922F0`, `002814E0(0x4B8)`, then
`0056622D xor ebx, ebx` / `0056622F mov [0209AC30 → +0x168], rbx` — **it clears the latch.**

So §1's *"nothing will make a second one"* and §6's *"clearing it re-arms `00565DD0`; nothing else
does"* are refuted by the same three instructions, **in the band §3 declared unread**. And message 18
is not exotic: [the widget message protocol](../16-UI/Widget-Object-Model/the-widget-message-protocol.md)
already describes *"a handler that relinks or frees nodes during message 18"* — it is the standard
destroy message. The arms are **ten plus a default, not four**.

**What survives is now measured**: sweeping every listed function for a load of `0209AC30` followed
by a `+0x168` access returns **three instructions in two functions** — the registrar's `cmp`, the
kind-1 `mov`, the kind-18 `mov`. Nothing outside those two touches the field.

### §7's second unknown was answered before this page was written

`0209AC30` is the **UI request router's context object**:
`16-UI/Request-Router/ui-request-router.md` reads its `+0xB8` / `+0xC0` pointer slots and `+0x3F8` /
`+0x400` request words, and records that **message-1 handlers publish self into `+0xB8` / `+0xC0`**
— the same idiom this page calls a latch, at a third slot. **456 functions load the global.** So the
mechanism is an instance of a documented protocol, not a bespoke one.

### A fifth reference form, with a control

*"Raw data-section qword — 0"* is right and incomplete: `00565E00` occurs **three times as a 32-bit
RVA**, twice in `.rdata` and once in `.pdata`. **Control:** `00565DD0`, `00328370` and `00512CD0`,
all frameless, occur **zero** times in that form; `00244F50` once. These are unwind and exception
metadata, so the reachability conclusion is untouched — but on x64 the runtime tables address code
by 32-bit RVA, and a sweep that looks only for 64-bit pointers does not say so.

`check_consistency` and `check_questions` pass. `check_links` reports one unresolved link, in
`spawn-placement-and-retirement.md`, to an evidence README that does not exist yet — **a peer is
editing that file right now** (it and `ASTRA.md` are modified in the working tree and were not
touched here). Left alone; not in this commit.

**Not claimed:** what the widget *is* — `EJ-1` stays open, now with eight unread arms rather than
three. What `002CD510`, `002922F0` or `002814E0(0x4B8)` do. Which sender issues message 18 to this
widget, or when. Whether `+0xB8` / `+0xC0` / `+0x168` are the router context's only self-publication
slots. Nothing executed, nothing observed live.

Every container claim on this page is a claim about a file on disk that nobody had opened. **It holds

```
MD5(file[0 .. 11,995,716))  =  b74187bd5c88f564281dc290ab0ee051
file[-16:]                  =  b74187bd5c88f564281dc290ab0ee051      MATCH
```

**Two negative controls pin the range**, so §3's *"the buffer that gets hashed includes the magic and
the size dword"* is proved rather than inferred: from offset **8** for `n−8` bytes the digest is
`6a33366c09af867f0356d5f18ed8ca0a`; from offset 0 for `n−16` bytes it is
`d9960efaea5114a099740b980566ae26`. Skip the header and it is wrong; stop short and it is wrong.

disassembly — and the two agree.

branch only. The flag is consumed: `0019B0EA movzx esi, al` / `test al, al` / `jne`, and on the
failing path the caller frees the archive's `+0x20` through `001F4120`. §7's second unknown
(*"the check is present; its consequence is assumed, not read"*) is closed, and §4's *"the failure is
at open, not at use"* gains its missing half.

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on the formatted log call: there is no level gate (OPUS-PASS-LOG-GATE)

**`audit_coverage` 289 → 290.** *(`check_already_answered.py` run one address at a time and read in
full.)*

### ⚠ What §5 read as a per-thread verbosity gate is the MSVC magic-static check for the sink

`005CDB0E`–`005CDB2F` — `mov ecx, [02EAED3C]` / `mov rax, gs:[0x58]` / `mov edx, 4` /
`mov rax, [rax+rcx*8]` / `mov ecx, [rdx+rax]` / `cmp [02CB6158], ecx` / `jg 0x5CDB60` — is the
thread-safe-static initialisation check for the singleton at `02CB6150`. **The `jg` does not
return.** `005CDB60` is `_Init_thread_header(&02CB6158)`, `cmp [02CB6158], -1`, `call 005CDA30`,
`mov [02CB6150], rax`, `_Init_thread_footer`, then `jmp 0x5CDB31` — **back onto the emit path**.
`005CDAA0` has **exactly one `ret`**, at `005CDB5F`, after the virtual call. **No message is dropped
and no verbosity is consulted.**

Three pieces of evidence, the first from the file's structure rather than from code:

1. **`02EAED3C` is the PE TLS directory's `AddressOfIndex`** — data directory 9, TLS directory at RVA
   `01BCBED8`, `AddressOfIndex = 0x02EAED3C`. It is the **module's `_tls_index`**, written by the
   loader, so `[slot + 4]` is `_Init_thread_epoch` and not a log level.
2. **The population agrees:** `02EAED3C` is read by **709** functions and **707** call
   `_Init_thread_header`.
3. **`005CD9C0` is the same sequence over the same two globals** and is unmistakably an accessor —
   guard `02CB6158`, `lea rax, [02CB6150]`, return. Both functions are fetching the same singleton.
4. **The database already had it right, one chapter over.** `lazy-statics-and-the-one-time-init-lock.md`
   names `02EAED3C` as **`_tls_index`** and TLS block `+0x04` as **`_Init_thread_epoch`** in its own
   address table, and writes the test as `if (thread_epoch < guard)`.

> **So this is a contradiction, not a discovery.** Two documents described the same two globals — one
> as CRT machinery, the other as a logging threshold and a per-thread level — and nothing caught it.
> `check_consistency.py` compares how an *address* is described and both pages called `02EAED3C`
> "the TLS index"; the conflict was in what `[slot + 4]` **means**, which no checker here compares.

> **Every instruction §5 quotes is decoded correctly** — the `cmp` operand order, the `+4`, the
> `gs:[0x58]`. They were fitted to the wrong idiom, and the reading then explained everything: a
> global threshold, a per-thread level, a sense-of-test warning, a modding note about "two globals and
> a thread-local". **A coherent story is not a control.** The control that breaks it could not be
> taken from the disassembly at all.

**And §8's checklist is the cautionary part.** *"The level is thread-local. Killer: a plain global
read."* The killer was **satisfied** — the read really is thread-local — and the conclusion is still
wrong, because `gs:[0x58]` indexed by `_tls_index` is what every magic static in this image does.
**A killer a wrong reading passes is not a killer**; it has to separate the claim from its nearest
rival, and "is it thread-local?" cannot separate a log level from `_Init_thread_epoch`.

**What survives is stronger for it.** §1's cost claim — `mov eax, 0x4050` / `_alloca_probe` at
`005CDAB2`–`005CDAB7` and `mov r8d, 0x4000` at `005CDAFA` — a 16 KB frame and a full format on
**every** call, with no gate that could ever have skipped them.

### §7's fourth unknown answered, and it corrects the argument reading

Parsing the import directory: `008C2DE0` is
`api-ms-win-crt-stdio-l1-1-0.dll!__stdio_common_vsnprintf_s` and `008C2E10` is
`api-ms-win-crt-stdio-l1-1-0.dll!__stdio_common_vsprintf_s` — **two different symbols**. Since
`vsnprintf_s` is `(options, buffer, sizeOfBuffer, count, format, locale, arglist)`, `005CDAA0`'s
`r9 = -1` is **`count` = `_TRUNCATE`**, not the locale; the locale is the `0` at `[rsp + 0x28]`. §5
reads the `-1` as the locale and omits `count`.

### `005CDA30` is not the sink's constructor

It is **another magic-static accessor** — same shape, guard `02CB6148`, static `02CB6140`. The log
call reaches **two nested lazy singletons**.

### Everything else reproduces

`005CDAA0` **239 B / 136** callers; `0019C5D0` **86 B / 120**; `0016D670` **8 B / 23** and its body is
exactly `lea rax, [rip] ; ret` → `02EBA3D0`; `mov rcx, [rax]` at `005CDB05` and `0019C60C`; the
`0x4050` frame and `0x4000` size; `0019C615 or ecx, -1` / `test eax, eax` / `0019C61A cmovs`; and the
sink's virtual slot 1 with the channel in `edx` and the buffer in `r8`.

The **filename** still says `level-gate` and is kept so every link and index entry resolves; the
title, the `system:` field and the §2 row are corrected in place, with a note saying why.

`check_consistency` and `check_questions` pass.

**Not claimed:** which class the sink is — `005CDA30` and `02CB6140` are the thread to pull. What the
channel id means. What `02EBA3D0` holds. **Whether any caller of `005CDAA0` is itself gated** — that
is where a verbosity control would have to live if one exists; it was not searched for, and its
absence is not claimed. Nothing executed, nothing observed live.

§3 says the magic occurs 0 times *in the image*. Over the **whole 32 MB file**: `.mhe` occurs **zero

(`PS2D` was tried as a second control and discarded: 62,577 occurrences, none in `.text`; a
four-byte literal that is also ordinary data controls nothing.)

`01ECB4D0` has **exactly one** code reference in the image — `002DFAF9` in `FUN_002DF9A0` — and it is
a `lea` whose next instruction **stores the array's address into a global**. Nothing indexes the
array directly. The inertness claim now rests on four legs.

Walking `01ECB4D0` and stopping at the first NULL gives **38** `.mh` names, **no** `in\ANX.mh`, and a

slots, exactly as §3 says. I drafted *"the array holds 38, not 45"* as a correction before asking
the strings who points at them — all 45 are pointed at from **one contiguous run,
`01ECB4D8`–`01ECB7D8`**, 776 bytes, past where my walk had stopped.

> **A terminator you assumed is not a terminator you measured.** Recorded on the page itself,
> because the next reader will walk the same array. This is the third instrument near-miss of the

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on `sead.win.config`: the lifetime question is answered, and `+0x0C` is not unread (OPUS-PASS-SEAD-CONFIG)

**`audit_coverage` 291 → 292.**

**Every figure reproduces**, re-extracted from `FFXII_TZA.vbf` and walked with independent code:
exactly one `.config` at **1,264 B**; header `scnf` / 0 / `0x10` / **10** / pad 0 / fileSize **1,264**;
all ten directory entries carrying `+0x04` 0, `+0x06` `0x10`, `+0x0C` 0, with §2's exact tags, offsets
and counts (`ctgr` `0x0B0`/4, `bus ` `0x150`/1, `mcr ` `0x1A0`/3, `epsp` `0x240`/0, `eps ` `0x250`/11,
`curv` `0x430`/1, `expr` `0x480`/0, `hcam` `0x490`, `evt ` `0x4A0`/0, `ctgl` `0x4B0`/1); the four
categories **`dummy0`, `music`, `se`, `voice`** with `+0x04` **0, 4, 48, 8** and `+0x06` **6, 5, 2, 5**;
**`Master`** with **`1.0f` at `+0x0C`** and its name at **`+0x20`**; `hcam` **16 / 44,100 / 0**;
`ctgl` **`default`**; and `curv`'s **two `1.0f`**.

### ✔ `WC-1`'s lifetime half: the engine copies the whole file

§7 asked whether anything is copied before `00210760` frees the buffer at `002108F1`. **It is.**
`007B0F90` does `mov ecx, [cfg + 0x0C]` (the header's **fileSize**) → `call 007AD550` →
`mov [02EAD3E0], rax` → `mov r8d, [cfg + 0x0C]` → `memcpy` (`00861EBA`) at `007B1005`. `007AD550` is
`[sead]`'s own allocator and says so: it allocates `size + 0x10`, writes **`0x5EAD5EAD`** at `+0x00`,
the tag at `+0x04` and the size at `+0x08`, and returns the pointer past that header.

**`02EAD3E0` has exactly one writer and sixteen readers across fifteen functions.** All nine `curv`
sites are readers, each wrapping the pointer through `007A46E0` (`mov [rcx], rdx ; mov rax, rcx ;
ret`) before the accessor dereferences it. **The late reads are of the copy; no pointer into the
freed buffer survives.**

### ⚠ `+0x0C` is not unread — it is the file's most load-bearing field

§3's field table recorded *"`+0x0C` fileSize — no reader found among the accessors"*. The qualifier is
true and the row still misleads: `+0x0C` is read **twice**, at `007B0FE8` as the **allocation size**
and at `007B0FFE` as the **`memcpy` length**. **Editing it without changing the file's length
truncates or over-reads the engine's only copy of the configuration** — which is exactly what a
modder needs to know, and the table said nothing was reading it.

`check_links`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass.

**Not claimed:** `WC-1`'s first half is untouched — what the element fields *mean*, and what `hcam`'s
16 / 44,100 / flag configure, are still unread. Only `007ADCA0` of the ten accessors was decoded in
full (it matches §3's shape exactly). That `007B0F90` runs before the free was taken from the call
chain, **not** traced instruction by instruction from `00210889`. Archive read, never written;
nothing executed.

be declared TIM2 now rests on every file.

lazily with a relative pointer made absolute from the object at `02AEE868`. **`MOV EBX,1` is a
reservation, not an off-by-one curiosity.**

`TIM2` occurs **once** in the whole file and **zero** times in `.text`, and `00D11470` is referenced by

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on the unnamed `.bin` families: the negative reproduces, and its anchor is load-bearing (OPUS-PASS-UNNAMED-BIN)

**`audit_coverage` 296 → 297.** *(Peer review of work published the same day.)*

**The negative claim reproduces exactly**, re-run from the archive with independent code: **1,439**
`.bin` files folded to **146** families, **20 families / 41 files** with no name in the executable,
and the controls `battle_message.bin`, `npcdic.bin` and `musicctrl.bin` all found.

> **The separator anchor is load-bearing, which is worth stating on a page whose whole result is an
> absence.** The corpus row specifies *"the file name **right after `\` or `/`**"*. Drop the anchor
> and the answer becomes **19 families / 39 files**: `ctrl.bin` false-matches **inside
> `musicctrl.bin`** — one of this page's own controls. **The control and the false positive are the
> same string**, and a substring search would have quietly dropped the four ATEL scripts' parent
> family from the result.

### ⚠ The ten `st2e` families are three different things

§2 calls all ten *"`st2e` table"*. Reading each header as `{magic, count, stride, dataoff}` and
comparing `dataoff + count × stride` with the file size splits them three ways:

* **exact** — `basic_skill` 75,352, `growth_rate` 7,200, `unit_data` 41,612;
* **describes nothing** — `actionchip_data` (count 0), `bukitye_data` (**23 records, stride 0**),
  `mons_act` (**359 records, stride 0**, in front of **11,756** bytes);
* **file much larger than the header accounts for** — `mons_category` 64 of 156, `mons_race` 160 of
  444, `object_data` 560 of 1,708, `target_data` **8,752 of 39,000**.

**Only three of the ten are tables their own header accounts for.** The "bare 32-byte header" reading
is right for both 32-byte files, and `bukitye_data` is not empty *by count* — it is empty because its
**stride is zero**.

### ⚠ §6's run-time-name attack is live, not closed

§6 reasons that the leaf stems occur nowhere. True — and **every directory segment of every unnamed
family is present in the image as a literal**: `ps2data`, `image`, `ff12`, `bin`, `binaryfile`,
`test_battle`, `katano`, `myoshiok`, `worldmap`. **Only the leaves are missing**, so an assembled path
has all its prefixes and the literal search cannot narrow `UB-1` on its own. Not a defect — §1 and §7
both say the assembled route is open — but it measures *how* open.

`check_links`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass.

**Not claimed:** that any of these files is or is not read at run time — `UB-1` untouched, and

families hold. What the surplus bytes in the four over-long `st2e` files are — the arithmetic is
measured, the content is not read. Whether a stride of 0 means anything to a reader: **no reader was
found for any of these**. Archive read, never written; nothing executed.

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on the fade ramp: curve 0 is the LINEAR fade, not silence (OPUS-PASS-FADE-CURVES)

**`audit_coverage` 298 → 299.**

### ⚠ Curve 0 returns `t`, and it is a different exit from out-of-range

The jump table at `007A9F1C` decodes to `007A9F17`, `007A9E76`, `007A9E9D`, `007A9EB9`, `007A9EC5`,
`007A9EE2`. The bound check `cmp edx, 5 / ja` targets **`007A9F14`**, which runs
`xorps xmm0, xmm0` — **but arm 0 is `007A9F17`, one byte past it.** Nothing between the function's
entry and the `jmp rcx` (`sub rsp,0x38`, `movaps xmm3,xmm0`, `cmp`, `ja`, `movsxd`, `lea`, `mov ecx`,
`add rcx,rdx`) writes `xmm0`, so **arm 0 returns the caller's `t` unchanged: curve 0 is the plain
linear fade.**

§3 recorded it as `xorps xmm0, xmm0` → `0`, *"not a shape — it returns silence for the whole ramp"*,
and as the same arm an out-of-range id gets. **Out-of-range really does return 0; curve 0 does not.**
The player-facing statement inverts: a sound on curve 0 fades in a straight line. And *"all five real
curves map 0 → 0 and 1 → 1"* becomes **all six**, the sixth being the linear one.

### The other five reproduce instruction for instruction

`1 − (1 − t²)³`, `1 − (1 − t)²`, `t²`, `2ᵗ − 1`, `2 − 2¹⁻ᵗ` — each decoded from its arm. Only
`01CEBBA8` and `01CEBC08` appear as constants, `00861F6E` is named **`powf`** in the function list,
and `007A9E50` has **63** callers exactly. `007A9E00` reproduces line for line, and `007A9D30` reads
**the same five fields** through a pointer at `+0x40` with `rbx` biased `+0x14`, stride `0x30`,
master at `+0x4C`, and a `count ≤ 0` path that goes straight to `1.0 × master`.

### ⚠ The unread span is 28 bytes, not 24 — and the type store already knew

Readers touch `+0x08`, `+0x0C`, `+0x10`, `+0x14`, `+0x1C`. **`+0x18` is touched by neither
function**, so the unread span is `0x00`–`0x07`, **`0x18`–`0x1B`** and `0x20`–`0x2F` — **28 of 48**.
`_types/fields.tsv` carries `+0x018` as its own `UNRESOLVED` row: **the store was right and the prose
summarising it dropped the middle gap.**

### Propagated to the type store

`fields.tsv`'s `curve` row said *">5 falls to arm 0 and returns 0"* — the same conflation. Corrected
in place to name both exits. **`types_index.py`: 246 types, 1,846 fields, 0 errors.**

### §4's negative holds and gets sharper

No `minss` or `maxss` in any of the three functions, **with the control that the instrument does find
the guard that exists** — `cmp edx, 5 / ja` on the curve id, in the same listing. With curve 0 now
known to be the identity, an `elapsed` past `duration` passes **straight through** as a multiplier
above 1, with no exponent to soften it. `DQ-1` stands.

`check_links`, `check_consistency` pass.

**Not claimed:** which parameter the ramps drive — §5's first bullet stands, no caller traced to a
mixer field. What the 28 unread bytes hold. What `007A9D30` does after the product. **Whether any
shipped data selects curve 0** — the arm is decoded, no authored table was searched. Nothing executed,
no sound heard.

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on the ATEL debug companions: the negative is sound, the substitution is unrolled (OPUS-PASS-ATEL-COMPANIONS)

**`audit_coverage` 299 → 300.**

**The corpus reproduces exactly:** 8 `.sbn`, 8 `.msb`, 8 `.dbg`; **12/12** `ch` copies byte-identical
to their `in` copies; **8/8** `.sbn` block tables valid with the first offset exactly
`4 × (count + 1)`, and the counts **3 / 2 / 2 / 3** falling on the modules §2 names; all twelve sizes
in §5 exact.

**The negative is sound, and its controls are worth writing down.** Route 1's eight literals occur
**0** times each — against **10,380** for `.ebp` + NUL, **2,144** `.bin`, **608** `.seb`, **550**
`.mpk`, **129** `.sab`. And the bare stems `sbn` and `msb` occur **once each** in the whole image,
`dbg` eight times: those are the substitution entries themselves, so **the strings exist only as
substitution material and never as part of a file name** — a sharper statement than "0 occurrences".
Route 2 reproduces to the instruction: `0032E404 cmp ecx, 0xFF` → `0032E438 or eax, 0xFFFFFFFF`,
before any table is touched. The table at `00D10990` reads back as §4 lists it, in order, as fourteen
inline NUL-separated strings.

### ⚠ The substitution is unrolled, not a table walk

§3 cites `0033078D`–`00330A59`. Those are **six** `lea` sites (`bin`, `dbg`, `sbn`, `msb`, `msf`,
`fnt`), and `003306E0` contains **25** `lea` instructions into the block, continuing through
`00330AA4` / `00330AAB` (`cam` **and** `camera` in one step), `00330B49`, `00330BD9` and on. **There
is no loop and no bound** — each extension is named by its own instruction at its own offset, so the
cited range covers the first six of the fourteen. **The conclusion is untouched**: every site still
ends at a `0032E400(0xFF, …)` returning −1.

### Where the fourteen end

The block continues past `vld` with `m%02d`, `.mld`, `CAMDAT`, `CAMCTL`, `SHKDAT`, `SHKCTL`,
`CHRMDL`, `LGTDAT`, `PREFIX` — a format, a dotted name, uppercase tags. The fourteen are a real
group, but **nothing in the data marks the boundary**; it is where the `lea` sites stop naming
extensions, which is a fact about the code and not the table.

`check_consistency` passes. `check_links` reports one unresolved link, in
`spawn-placement-and-retirement.md`, to `spawn-load-success/README.md` — **ASTRA's in-flight work**
(`ASTRA-SPAWN-LOAD-SUCCESS` is the board's one ACTIVE task). Untouched and not in this commit.

**Not claimed:** `SN-1` stands — the inner layouts of all three companions untouched. Whether
`003306E0`'s size queries reach a kind other than `0xFF` on some other path — only the `0xFF` sites
were read, and the function is 3,882 bytes. What `00330E35 cmp esi, 0x10` bounds. Whether the nine
strings after `vld` belong to the same consumer. Archive read, never written; nothing executed.

`+0x10` is a 60 Hz frame counter and `+0x18`/`+0x1A`/`+0x1B` the same clock written out — **8 of 8

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on the widget animation start: the frame counter settled from its writers, and a receiving-side argument against "teardown-ish" (OPUS-PASS-WIDGET-ANIM)

**`audit_coverage` 307 → 308.**

**The function re-read whole and every figure holds.** 148 call sites, **142 `E8` + 6 `E9`** (control:
the `ret 0` stub at 2,868 by the same instruments); `test rdx, rdx` first; `0x3f800000` into `+0xB8`;
the reciprocal guarded by `00229DF0()` and `00229EA0() == 2`; `shl`/`sar 0x1C`; the `js` / `cmp 1,
jle` / `cmp 4, jne` state fan-out; `imul 0x3c` then the `0x10624DD3` divide-by-1000; `bt`/`btr 0xA`,
`shr 0xC`, `and 0x3FF`; `and 0xFFFFFFD2` / `or 0x12` leaving the nibble at 2; and `lea rdx,
[01E0C0E0]` whose first dword is **14**.

### ✖ Corrected: the "mark started" bit is in `+0x40`, not `+0x7C`

`00246B95` is `or dword ptr [rbx + 0x40], 0x200`. §3 wrote `[rbx+0x7C]` — the state word the same arm
reads and rewrites through `edx`, and the word the closing `and`/`or` owns. A reader would look for
bit 9 in the wrong place and see a conflict that is not there.

### ✔ New: the frame reading now rests on the writers

§4 corroborated `0208F570` from a second **reader**. Over all 38,161 bodies it has **149 references —
143 reads in 109 functions and exactly 6 writes**: one **assignment** (`0022819C`, from `[01FD46F4]`)
and five **`add`s**, all in the UI tick family `00250540` / `002506D0` / `00250730` / `002507C0`.
**No decrement, no multiply, no other assignment in the image.** The added step is rate-compensated:
`00250730` adds `2 / [01DFE0B4]` (1 at full rate, **2 at half**), `00250540` adds an `r14d` computed
as **1 or 2**, and three sites add `00184950()` = `[01F3DA18]`.

> A global that only ever advances, by a small step taken once per UI tick, is a frame counter being
> used as one — and because the step **doubles when the tick rate halves**, this function's
> hard-coded `60` is consistent rather than a bug: the counter it spends against is already in 60 Hz
> units. Still a reading, not a live observation; but it rests on six writers now, not two readers.

`00228130` is a widget procedure by the protocol page's own shape test (reads `dword [rdx]` first,
tail-jumps `005C5230`), and its dispatch covers ids 1, 2, 4 and **14**. **The id-14 arm is the one
that re-bases the frame counter** — `00247780`, `00251E80`, `00229510`, `00365980`, `003601C0(3)`,
then `0208F570 = [01FD46F4]`. §4 argued from the **sending** side that 14 is not teardown; this is the
**receiving** side, and a handler that resets the clock and rebuilds is an *enter*. Two independent
ends of the same message, both pointing away from "teardown-ish". **`DL-1` stays open** — routed to
the protocol page's owner as `OPUS-DL1-MESSAGE14-RECEIVER` rather than edited there.

### ✔ New: the message record is used once

`01E0C0E0` has **exactly one** rip-relative reference in the whole image. Not a shared constant — one
record, one reference.

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on gil: the meter reads `cl`, both wrappers add behaviour, and the direct-write question is bounded (OPUS-PASS-GIL)

**`audit_coverage` 309 → 310.**

**Both censuses reproduce set for set.** `GameState_SetGil`: **13 distinct caller functions, exactly
the thirteen §4 names** (`E8` 12 + `E9` 1). `GameState_GetGil`: **19** on the body excluding the
thunk, **3** through the thunk `00309BF0`, **overlap 0, union 22** — the 2026-09-03 correction
reproduces down to which three functions reach it only through the thunk. The setter matches §3
instruction for instruction, including the **zero-delta skip** and the **two separate loads** of the
state pointer. The single `E9` is `Debug_SetGilToMaximum`, ten bytes: `mov ecx, 0x05F5E0FF` then
`jmp 00254EE0`.

### ✔ Settled: `00316A50` reads `cl`, never `ecx`

§3 raised the question and declined it; the first instruction answers it. `cmp cl, 0x1E / jae` then
`movzx esi, cl` and `movzx ebp, cl` — **the upper three bytes of `ecx` are never read**, so
`mov cl, 6` is correct and not a defect. Two further facts: the meter accepts **30 kinds** and indexes
an **8-byte-per-kind table at `00D10460`**, whose kinds 6 and 7 read `04 14` / `04 18` and whose kinds
11 and 17 read `04 10` / `04 1C` — a four-member family stepping by 4.

### ✔ Both wrappers add behaviour, and one changes the statistics

`003004B0` reads gil, adds the delta, **floors at 0 itself** before calling the setter, and branches
on a **second argument** (`test dil, 1`) for the notify. `00300500` floors the same way and **returns
the floored value**. The pre-floor is not redundant with the setter's clamp: because §3's delta is
measured *before* the clamp, a caller that goes further negative meters a larger "spent" figure than
one that floors first. **Which path a mod uses changes what the achievement counters see.**
`003F4AA0` is a **record applier** — `test byte [rcx], 1` guards `SetGil(GetGil() + [rcx+4])`, then it
walks a count at `[rcx+8]`.

### ✔ New: the direct-write question is bounded

§11 says a direct write to `[02092758] + 8` would not appear in a caller census. So the **pointer** was
censused: **10 rip-relative references in 9 functions**, image-wide. One is the binder `00253970`;
of the eight readers **only two write anything** — `00254CC0` adds to `+0x10` and `00254E80` writes
`+0x0C` — and **neither writes `+0x08`**. A direct write would have to arrive through a handed
pointer, which this instrument cannot see and which is now the only remaining way in.

The binder also confirms where the object lives — `002EF640()`, the active save image buffer — which
is **already on record** (the save-payload field map lists `02092758` at payload `-0x200`, and `AB-5`
records the same function binding `020927C0`), and is credited rather than re-announced.

### ○ A lead: 99,999,999 is not gil's alone

`002536D0` reads `+0x0C` and clamps it to **the same `0x05F5E0FF`**. `FU-2` names that field — the
**walked-distance total**, mirrored there by `00254E80` from `00320D50()`. The mirror is on record;
**the shared ceiling is not**, and a reimplementation that clamps only gil would let the other field
pass a limit the engine enforces on both.

`check_links`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass.

**Not claimed:** what `00316A50` does with kinds 6 and 7 — only its argument handling and its table's

## 2026-09-13 — falsification pass on `musicctrl.bin`: every figure reproduces, and the decoding note was one sentence short (OPUS-PASS-MUSICCTRL)

**`audit_coverage` 327 → 328.** Static only; nothing executed and no audio played.

### ✔ Every published figure reproduces

**Two copies, 1,615 B, one SHA-256**; `"MUS0"` and `maxFieldId` **1311**; **all eleven page offsets**; runs per page **12, 28, 39, 29, 30, 33, 35, 18, 29, 27, 11** and **291** in total; **every one of the eleven chains ends exactly at the next page's offset**, the last at end of file; the eleven first-run starts; the last run **start 1311, span 0**, meeting the header's maximum, with **no run's start exceeding it**; and **0 of 1,115** `us` scripts calling any of `0448`–`044F` or `201E`, with the `302B` control finding **exactly six**.

### ➕ The decoding note is missing the widths — supplied from the reader

The corpus row gives *"`start = w & 0x7FF`, `span = w >> 11`, stride `4 + 3 × count`"* and **never says what `w` is or where `count` comes from**. Beside a `>> 11` the natural reading is a dword with `count` as one of its fields; **it is not**, and a walk built that way collapses. `003EAA70` reads three separate bytes: `w = b0 | (b1 << 8)` — **a `u16`** — and **`count` is the byte at run `+2`**, with the advance computed as `lea edx,[r10+2]` / `lea edx,[r10+rdx*2]` = **`3×count + 4`**. So a run is `u16 start:11|span:5`, `u8 count`, then `count × 3` bytes.

**With the widths the walk reproduces to the run; without them it cannot be reproduced at all** — it cost two attempts here. Measured distributions: `count` is **0 in 243 of 291** (max 6) and `span` **0 in 169** (max 5), consistent with a 5-bit span and nothing larger ever appearing.

`check_links`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass.

**Not claimed:** §2.1 onward — the boot loader chain, the rebase callback, the descriptor and the whole BGM-stream half — was **not re-read**; what a run's three-byte entries hold. Nothing executed.

Section 8 claimed the target-record layout rests on producer and consumer *"agreeing on offsets `0x00/0x08/0x10/0x18/0x20/0x28`"*. **The producer writes three of the six** - `+0x00` (the literal `1`), `+0x08` and `+0x10` - and never stores to the other three. ## 2026-09-13 - the HP floor is a clamp, not a shield: a non-zero floor moves the death threshold up (OPUS-HPFLOOR-NOT-INVULNERABILITY)

Specification-propagation debt, closed. Static only; nothing executed.

### The contradiction was inside one document

The contract's section 6 glossed a non-zero `+0x48` floor as *"the shape of a scripted 'cannot be killed'"*. Its own section 12, recording an **executed** isolated-original-code run, said *"the floor is reached, not crossed; damage landing exactly on a non-zero floor is death"*. **Four sections apart, in the same file, for a day.** This is the shape the goal names as an answer stranded beside an obsolete specification, and the executed half was right.

### What the code says

**The lethal test compares against the same floor the clamp uses.** `00300784` reloads `[rsp+0xB0]` - the floor slot filled at `0030056D` - and `0030078B` runs `cmp dword ptr [rsi+0x48], eax` / `jg`. Strictly greater survives. The clamp guarantees `hp >= floor`, so the only bottom value it can produce is `hp == floor`, and that **falls through into the death sequence**. `003007AD` onward runs `0030E360`, the killer-identity write, the kill counter, the time field, `00306F00` and the death event **with no floor-is-zero test anywhere on the path**.

So a floor of 1000 makes a unit run the lethal sequence **at 1000 HP** - *earlier*, in HP terms, than a floor-0 unit. The engine's own verb name already said so: `btlAtelSetHpLowLimit` sets a **low limit**, not a shield.

### New: the two thresholds are different fields

Found while checking the first correction. **Death is tested against the floor; revive is tested against literal zero.** `[rsp+0x54]` is the **pre-clamp** HP, captured at `003005EF` (`mov eax, [rsi+0x48]` / `mov [rsp+0x54], eax`), and `00300752` compares it against `edi`, zeroed at `00300563`. They coincide only when the floor is 0.

**Consequence.** A non-zero-floor unit dies at its floor, step 2 sets KO, and a later heal through this function finds `oldHp == floor > 0`, takes `jg`, and returns **without clearing KO** - this function's revive arm can never fire for it. Whether anything else in the game clears that KO is **not read here and not claimed**; the scope is `00300530` alone.

### Propagated

- **contract section 6** - the gloss removed, the clamp/consequence split stated, with the reimplementation trap named: clamp correctly then test `hp <= 0` and every non-zero-floor unit lives at its floor forever.
- **contract section 9** - the two-threshold table added.
- **contract section 14** - the retired question no longer cites the withdrawn gloss.
- **the implementing page** - the floor sentence corrected; the revive paragraph given the asymmetry; **the executable specification in section 4 given the two transition predicates**, which it did not have at all - it stated the clamp and stopped.
- **the implementing page's modding notes** - *"To make a unit unkillable, raise its floor"* **WITHDRAWN**. It is the worst instance: an instruction a modder would follow that does the opposite of what it says. *"Do not write `+0x48` directly if the value can cross zero"* corrected to *"can reach the floor or zero"*.
- **the battle-unit field map** - *"two shipped areas make a unit unkillable below a threshold is now a fact"* corrected; the `+0x048` row now says the floor is also what the lethal test compares against.

**The two shipped non-zero values stand** - `dst_a01.ebp` 67 and `naf_a02.ebp` 1000, from the byte walk of 1,115 scripts. Only their consequence was misread. What the mechanic is *for* is a semantic reading and is routed to FABLE (`OPUS-REQ-FABLE-HPFLOOR-MEANING`), not asserted here.

`check_links`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass. Nothing executed.


## 2026-09-13 - the spawn-group reset zeroes the masks but clears only flag bit 0 (OPUS-LEDGER-RESET-BIT0)

Specification-propagation debt, closed. Static only; nothing executed.

Two documents said the reset *"empties everything - both masks and the flag"* and *"empties every group completely - members, deaths and the pending flag"*. **The masks are whole-qword zero stores. The flag is not zeroed:** `003070A0`-`003070AB` are four `and byte ptr [...], 0xFE`, which clear **bit 0 only** and leave bits 1-7 untouched.

**The postcondition is `memberMask == 0 && deadMask == 0 && (flags & 1) == 0`, not `flags == 0`.** The contract's own executable specification at §11 already had it right - `ledger[i].flags &= ~1` - so the prose and the test plan were the drift, not the spec.

### The test plan was the live defect

§16 required *"the reset over a fully populated ledger (**all three fields must read zero after it**)"*. That demands the whole flag byte become zero. **A test written to it would have passed**, because nothing else in the image uses bits 1-7 - and it would have been asserting something the code never promised. Rewritten to assert bit 0 clear **and bits 1-7 preserved**, with the discriminating fixture named: pre-fill the byte with `0xFF` and require `0xFE` afterwards.

### Why it happens to hold, measured rather than assumed

Whole-byte census. Every reference into `02EC13C0`-`02EC19C0` is a rip-relative `lea` and there are **exactly six image-wide** (`00306EBC`, `00306F5D`, `00307049`, `00307090`, `003070E0`, `0030712C`) - which **confirms the page's "exactly six functions" from a second direction**, by address rather than by name. Across all six, every access to the flags byte is bit 0: two `or …, 1` (`00306FE0`, `00307133`), one `test al, 1` and one `and al, 0xFE` (`00307053`/`00307057`), and the reset's four `and …, 0xFE`. **No instruction in the image sets, clears or tests any other bit.**

So the byte only ever holds 0 or 1 in the shipped game and the stronger claim is *observationally* true. **That is a fact about the rest of the image, not a guarantee of the reset**, and the two are now recorded separately - which is the whole point of the distinction.

The same loop settles two figures from the code rather than the table: `00307030` walks with `add rdi, 0x18` and `cmp ebx, 0x40` - **stride 24, count 64** - and clears bit 0 as it consumes each pending signal, which is §7's `flags &= ~1` edge.

Five further `lea`s point at `02EC19C0`, one past the end (`64 * 24 = 0x600`). They are the loop bound and an adjacent object, not ledger references, which is why the six stands.

`check_links`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass. Nothing executed; ASTRA's claimed spawn scope (`spawn-placement-and-retirement.md`, `function:00233c10`) was not touched.


## 2026-09-13 - the widget executable specification had drifted from the contract's own header table AND from the reconstruction that passes its differential test (OPUS-WIDGET-SPEC-ALIGN)

Specification-propagation debt, closed. Static only; nothing executed.

§12's reproduction formula was re-derived instruction by instruction from `002465F0`. **Seven drifts**, and the striking part is where the correct version already lived: **§3's header table had every one of them right**, and so did `Reconstruction/Game/UI/widget_construct.c`, the file that passes §13b's differential test. **The knowledge was correct in two places and stale in the one a reimplementer would copy.**

| drift | what it costs |
|---|---|
| `WidgetMessage m = { 1, 0, (uint64_t)locals }` | **the payload is wrong.** `locals` is a `WidgetMessage *`; the constructor copies `initArgs->a` **and** `initArgs->b` into a fresh message whose id is forced to 1 (`00246721`-`00246733`). The old form put the *pointer* in `b` and left `a` zero |
| `& ~0x4000` with no re-set | **the pool bit is lost** - `002466F2` ORs `(pooled & 1) << 14` back in. Built from the old formula, every object is marked heap-owned |
| no `0208F560` gate | the generation bit is set unconditionally instead of **forced to 0** |
| no `+0xAC` / `+0xAD` | two header bytes left at 0 instead of 6 |
| no `+0x7C &= ~0xF` | a fourth field untouched |
| `\| 100` on `+0x44` | the code does a **16-bit store**; equivalent only because the memset ran first, which is a property of the history, not of the expression |
| the `+0xB4` write absent | the ordering fact, below |

### Callback ordering and the lifecycle boundary

The object's life begins at the `memset` (`00246626`) and **every header field is written before the handler is called** (`00246748`) - **except `+0xB4`, which is set after the callback returns** (`0024674A`-`0024675C`). So a construct handler reading its own `+0xB4` during message id 1 sees **`0`**, never `1`, in any frame-rate mode. §3a's 33 handler sites that call `001EDEC0([self+0xB4])` are consistent with this: the two resolved by jump-table decode sit on the **id 2** arm.

**`widget_construct.c` had already found this**, and its comment records something better than the finding - a **withdrawn unproven negative**: an earlier version justified the divergence with *"nothing between them reads `+0xB4`"*, which it then retracted as an unproven negative. That is the standard being applied without being asked for.

**The handler call's guard is dead code.** `0024673B test rbx, rbx / je` cannot fail: `rbx` was `cmove`d to `005C5230` at `00246635` when the argument was null. The formula omits the branch deliberately rather than reproducing one that is never taken.

**Not re-derived:** `Widget_Create`'s own body (`00244F50`) - the `0xC0` default, the `0x120` pool threshold, the 112-slot pool - is carried over unchanged and was not re-read; `001EDDA0` and `00314960` are taken from §3a. No code was changed, so §13b's differential run and the mutation campaign are untouched and were not re-run. `check_links`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass.


## 2026-09-13 - BattleUnit +0x698 and +0xE68: the stats record has TWO homes, and the type store described only one (closing FABLE-CONTRA-OPUS-BU698-E68)

A contradiction FABLE raised against my type rows on 2026-09-12, assigned to OPUS and still `READY`. FABLE's pages already carried the correction; **the structured records did not**, which is the whole point of the item: prose and type store had diverged and the type store is what a reconstruction compiles against.

### The binding is per kind

`BattleUnit_ApplyUnitDefinition` (`0023A570`) takes `kind = definitionId >> 8` (`0023A626` / `0023A62E`) and binds **different objects**:

| | kind 0 (party) | kind 1 (spawn-backed) |
|---|---|---|
| `+0x698` | `*(02EBF190) + 8 + slot*0x1C8` - the BattleSystemState array element | **the SpawnKeep entry + `0x80`** (`0023A787 sub rax, -0x80`), via `[rsp+0x90]` |
| `+0x6A0` | `0` (`0023AAB1`) | the SpawnKeep entry (`0023AC01`) |
| `+0xE68` | **never written**; the reset at `00236AC2` leaves `0` | the `.ard` slot-0 class row |

Both stores land at the same instruction (`0023ABFA`) from a register loaded two different ways, and **there is no other `rbp` or `r15` assignment in the function**.

### What was wrong, and it was wrong in three rows

- **`fields.tsv` `+0x698`** stated the kind-0 path as if universal - *"it is not a spawn record"*. It is, for every enemy.
- **`fields.tsv` `+0xE68`** still read `theSpawnRecordS`, *"the spawn record's +0x80 stats page"*, at **PROVEN** - the exact reading FABLE overturned the day before. Now `ardClassRow`, kind 1 only, at HIGH (the `.ard` slot identification is FABLE's, propagated, not re-derived from the archive here).
- **`types.tsv` `BattleStatsRecord`** said the type is *"slot k inside BattleSystemState, forty of them"* with destruction settled because *"it has no storage of its own to release"*. **The 40-slot array is not the type's extent.**

Four consequences follow, and the third is the one that changes an answer rather than a description: the type **does** have storage outside BattleSystemState; the lifetime splits (save block vs SpawnKeep entry); **the construction answer splits** - the old row said there is *no per-record constructor* because the parent's `002370C0` memset covers everything, but a kind-1 record is initialised by `BattleStats_InitializeDefinitionRecord` at `0023A7A9`, gated on `[entry] & 5 == 0`, **which is a per-record initialiser**; and the `0031B7B1` equality search that finds a unit by comparing against the array **only ever finds kind-0 units**, so any census resting on it under-counts by every enemy.

The `dtor` answer survives in substance - neither home is separately freed - but **its reason was wrong for half the instances.** Confidence lowered PROVEN -> HIGH.

> The row already used the `+0x05` kind byte to discriminate the `+0x10` union - four `f32` for party units, eight `int16` for spawn-backed ones. **It knew there were two kinds of record and not that they live in two places**, which is why the union was right and the ownership was not.

### Re-derived, not propagated

Every cited site was checked against the image, and one confirmation was found that the contradiction did not rest on. **`003879C0` loads both pointers off one unit and treats them as different objects**: `003879DF mov rcx, [rax+0x698]`, `003879EB cmp byte ptr [rcx+5], 1`, then `003879F1 cmp qword ptr [rax+0xe68], 0` with a `je`, then `00387A21`/`00387A28` `mov rax, [rax+0xe68]` / `movzx eax, byte ptr [rax+0x12]` / `shr eax, 7`. Two displacements, two separate null tests - and **the explicit null test on `+0xE68` is exactly the guard a field populated on kind 1 only requires**.

`types_index.py --validate`: 246 types, 1,846 fields, **0 errors**. `check_links`, `check_consistency` pass. Static only; nothing executed. FABLE's own remaining wording is `FABLE-S92-STATSBIND` and is not touched here.


## 2026-09-13 - EC-7: the A/B/C/D disposition surface exists, and its first measurement is the thing the completion plan feared (OPUS-EC7-DISPOSITION-SURFACE)

`COMPLETION-PLAN.md` §3 has defined **A individually explained / B class-explained / C dispositioned** since it was written, and said all of them are *"declared in frontmatter, never inferred"*. **No such key existed and nothing read one.** The formats dimension got the mechanism - `check_assets.py`, whose docstring says it is *"deliberately the same shape as the A/B/C policy"* - and the function dimension, which the policy was written for, never did. That is `EC-7`.

### Built: declaration, census, validator, metric input - and nothing else

`check_dispositions.py`, in `check_assets.py`'s shape and reusing `functions.tsv` and the existing corpus walk. No new framework, no new store.

- **A is MEASURED, never declared** - a `DOCUMENTED` page citing an address strictly *inside* a body (FABLE's rule 2). An entry-only citation is a mention and stays in the frontier.
- **B/C/D are declared** as `function_families:` rows, `name | letter | members file | count | note`, and **refused without a note**: B must answer *could ignorance of this family prevent reproducing FFXII?*, C must name the upstream and the boundary, D must give a reason and a resume condition. **D is never added to any explained total** - it exists so an unsolved operation stays visible.
- **Eight refusal reasons, each a hard zero for its row**: bad letter, no note, unreadable members, **empty members (a zero-case cannot pass)**, count mismatch, a member that is not a function entry, two families claiming one function, and a function both declared and measured as A. **All eight are driven by `--self-test`** (11 cases). A validator nobody tried to break is not a validator.

> **The population had to be fixed before the number meant anything.** My first run counted 38,161 bodies against `progress.py`'s 34,270, because `progress.py` excludes funclets (`Unwind@`, `Catch_All@`). `progress.py` carries a comment about the day that exclusion was applied on one side of a cross-check and not the other - *"a cross-check between two counts is only a check when both count the same population. I built this warning to catch mixed state and its first act was to manufacture some."* I was one commit from repeating it. **34,270 both sides.**

### The first measurement

| measure | count | of 34,270 |
|---|---:|---:|
| `engine_explained` - any citation landing in a body, any document | **10,184** | 29.72% |
| any citation in a body, `DOCUMENTED` page only | 8,620 | 25.2% |
| **interior** citation, any document | 1,936 | 5.6% |
| **A** - interior citation, `DOCUMENTED` page | **1,361** | **3.97%** |
| of the `DOCUMENTED` set, cited **only at the entry address** | **7,259** | |

**The gap is attributed, not asserted.** Of the two filters, the page-status one removes about 1,560 and **the interior one removes about 8,250**. The citation dimension is dominated by *mentions*, which is what §3 said outright would happen: *"citing those 11,836 without explaining them would satisfy the metric and betray the mission."*

**Stated against over-reading, in the tool's own output:** interior citation is a **stricter proxy**, not a true count. A page can explain a six-instruction function perfectly while citing only its entry, and that function scores zero here. **3.97% is not "the database is 4% done"** - it is evidence that the 29.72% is mostly mentions.

### What was deliberately NOT done

- **`engine_explained` is untouched.** It keeps its meaning, its history and its 0.55. `progress.py` **reports** the disposition figure and takes weight from nothing; **OVERALL is unchanged at 52.65%**. Re-weighting is the program-level decision `EC-7` reserves for three identities, and two are recorded and agree - ASTRA's is requested as `OPUS-REQ-ASTRA-DISPOSITION-POSITION`, with the two questions that belong in its lane.
- **No family was declared to make the counter non-zero.** The surface reports 0 accepted and 0 refused and says so in words. FABLE has three enumerations ready (`DF-1` 46, `DF-4` 401, `BK-6` 4) and said it would declare them once the key and format were fixed; they now are. Declaring them is FABLE's evidence work, not my tooling change.
- **The checker does not re-run selectors**, and its docstring says so rather than hiding it. Whether a selector should be a shell command in frontmatter or a named entry the checker dispatches is a tooling and reproducibility question, which is ASTRA's lane.

`EC-7` stays **OPEN** and is narrowed: the mechanism exists, the decision does not.

`--self-test` 11/11; `check_links`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass; `progress.py` runs unchanged in every weighted figure.

## 2026-09-13 - bc7701f re-verified under challenge: the two bindings were not conflated, and the object at entry+0x80 is a stats record by memset size (OPUS-BU698-E68-REVERIFY)

An external review asked whether the `+0x698`/`+0xE68` correction had conflated the two, proposing that the authored/spawn definition `+0x80` binds to `+0xE68` and the BattleSystemState slot to `+0x698`. **Half of that is right and the half that is not is the half being challenged.** Re-derived from the image, not from the earlier note.

### The register trace runs one way only

`r15` is loaded with the `02EBF150` class row at `0023A6F0`-`0023A6FC` - indexed by `word[definitionRow+0]` - and stored to `+0xE68` at `0023A91C`. **It is not reassigned anywhere between those two points.** It is then RELOADED, at `0023AA15`/`0023AA2F` from `[rsp+0x90]` on the kind-1 arms or at `0023AAAA`-`0023AAC1` on the kind-0 arm, and only that reloaded value reaches `+0x698` at `0023ABFA`, after both arms merge at `0023ABCA`.

### The decisive piece is a memset size

`[rsp+0x90]` is set at `0023A795` from `0023A787 sub rax, -0x80` - the SpawnKeep entry + `0x80`. At `0023A7A9` **that same pointer is passed to `BattleStats_InitializeDefinitionRecord` (`0023AC80`), whose first act is `memset(ptr, 0, 0x1C8)`** (`0023ACA4 mov r8d, 0x1c8` / `0023ACBD call 00861EC0`), followed by writes to `+0x50`, `+0x58`, `+0x1C3` and `+0x1C5` - all interior to a `0x1C8` record. The kind-0 arm reaches its object by `imul rcx, r12, 0x1c8`.

> **Both arms carry an object of exactly this type size, and both land at `+0x698`.** `entry+0x80` does not reach `+0xE68` on any path, and `+0xE68` never holds a stats record. The proposed relationship has the two objects the right way round for kind 0 and swapped for kind 1.

### What the commit actually said, and what was still worth fixing

bc7701f did **not** claim one stats object occupies both bindings - its `fields.tsv` text reads *"THIS IS NOT A SECOND HOME FOR +0x698 ... two different objects ... No reader treats them interchangeably."* The substance stands.

**But the challenge found a real presentation defect.** The `types.tsv` row opened with *"TWO HOMES, by unit kind"* immediately above a discussion of `+0xE68`. The phrase names two storage locations for **one type**, both reached through `+0x698` - and sitting where it sat, it invited exactly the misreading raised. Rewritten to *"TWO HOMES OF THIS TYPE, BY UNIT KIND - both of them reached through BattleUnit +0x698, and NEITHER of them is BattleUnit +0xE68"*, with the point restated at the end of the cell and a matching line added to the `+0xE68` field row.

**A reading a careful reviewer can reach from correct text is a defect in the text.** The evidence columns of both rows now carry the register trace and the memset size, so the next challenge is answered by the store rather than by re-running the disassembly.

`types_index.py --validate`: 246 types, 1,846 fields, **0 errors**. Static only; nothing executed.

| **`ABI_UNRESOLVED_DEFAULT`** | **562** | **OPUS** - this is the type/ABI lane, and it is mine |
| `Audio` (frontier-tagged) | 2,021 | FABLE, and see below |

> **Audio is the striking row.** The subsystem has eleven documents and ~2,064 owned functions, and **2,021 of them sit in the frontier**. Eleven documents did not disposition the family they describe - which is precisely the gap `EC-7` exists to make visible, and it is invisible to `engine_explained` because those functions are cited.

### Size matters to the estimate and is printed

The architectural bucket is **7,479** bodies at 64 B or less and **660** over 1 KB. A 12-byte adapter and a 3 KB dispatcher are not the same unit of work, and a plan that counts only functions will mis-estimate either way.

### What this is not

**Nothing here dispositions anything.** The tool has no declaration surface and writes nothing. A function leaves the frontier only when a page declares it with a note that meets the bar and `check_dispositions.py` accepts the row. The buckets are **shape evidence drawn from the checkpoint's own tags and inherit that classifier's errors**, which is why every line of the output says *candidate*.

**And 3.98% is not a completion figure.** It is the strict-A measure over a database whose long tail has never been dispositioned at all, because until today there was nothing to disposition it in.

## 2026-09-13 - the thunk layer: a tag-based census under-counts it by 181, and the first EC-7 family is declared (OPUS-THUNK-FORWARDER-FAMILY)

Static only; nothing executed.

### All four published figures reproduce, and the population they partition is not the thunk layer

Section 2 reproduces exactly: **689** functions carry a `Thunk.*` tag, of which **568** are 5-byte `JMP rel32`, **108** are 6-byte indirect and **12** are 7-byte. **Four figures, four exact matches.**

Counting by **bytes** instead, over the same 34,270 non-funclet bodies: **749 functions have a complete body of exactly five bytes, `E9 rel32`.** The tag knows about 568. **181 byte-identical forwarders carry no `Thunk.*` tag at all - a 32% under-count**, 137 of them filed under `CategoryExitV106`.

> **The document already knew this failure mode and had measured it once.** Section 10's overturn says the 19-byte receiver-binder section was wrong *"because it counted the tagged population rather than the binary"*, and found ONE function. The same instrument error at scale is worth **181**.

### Controls, including one that shaped the definition

**Every one of the 749 targets is a real function entry** - zero dangling, zero self-references; a mis-identified body would land somewhere that is not an entry. **749 forwarders, 749 distinct targets**, one-to-one. **None of the 749 is measured as A.**

> **The five-byte rule earns its tightness.** A looser *"body ends in a jmp"* rule would have swept in **16** bodies of `xor ecx, ecx; jmp` and **12** of `xor edx, edx; jmp`. Those **bind an argument to zero** before tail-calling, so their semantics are NOT their target's - and they are untagged too. Same trap as section 10's receiver-binder, 28 more instances.

**And a miss of my own, in the same class:** my 7-byte filter matched only `FF 25` and found 10 of the 12 the tag reports. The page is right and my pattern was incomplete. Recorded because it is the page's own error made again - a filter that encodes one form of a thing and then reports a count of the thing.

### The first EC-7 family, and what it does not say

The 749 are declared as **B**, with the enumerated population in a members TSV whose header records the selector. `check_dispositions.py` accepts the row. **The bar B must clear:** a forwarder's complete body is one `jmp`, so control transfers with every argument register, the stack frame and the return address untouched, and its observable semantics **are** its target's; a reconstruction calls the target directly and the forwarder need not exist.

> **This row does not disposition the targets.** 713 of the 749 remain in the frontier. Dispositioning a forwarder says nothing about the function it forwards to, and reading 749 as 749 functions explained is exactly the citation-volume error `EC-7` exists to prevent.

### The mechanism held under real parallel use

While this was being written **FABLE declared three families of its own** - return-value adapters (403), owned-buffer reset adapters (46) and stream sentries (4), all **C**. With mine: **4 accepted, 0 refused**, no collision, and neither of us touched the checker. That is the ownership split `TEAM.md` records, working the first time it was used for real.

**A + B + C = 2,567 of 34,270 (7.49%)**, frontier **31,703**. The C-candidate pool falls from 8,311 to 7,549 as FABLE's rows land. `engine_explained` is unchanged and takes no weight from this.

**Not claimed:** the 6- and 7-byte import stubs are **not** declared - an import stub's behaviour is the loader's and the upstream library's, a **C** row needing the upstream named, and somebody should write it. The `Thunk.*` tag is not corrected; it is the checkpoint's, and this pass tests it rather than repairing it.

> **Instrument note, second instance today.** The first draft of this entry was again written through a shell string and again had its backticks command-substituted away. I recorded that exact lesson in the subsystem-index entry an hour earlier **and then repeated it**. The fix is not more care; it is not writing audit prose through a shell at all, which is now what I do. *Knowing a failure mode does not prevent it - removing the surface does.*
