## 2026-09-13 - the import stubs, resolved to their upstreams, and one off-by-one slot that is not one (OPUS-IMPORT-STUB-FAMILY)

Audit pass 2 left these undeclared and said why: *"an import stub's behaviour is the loader's and the upstream library's, a C disposition needing the upstream named, and that is a separate row somebody should write."* Written. Static only; nothing executed.

### The upstream is named per member, not per family

The PE import directory holds **538 slots across 30 DLLs**. Every frontier thunk whose body is `FF 25 rel32` or `48 FF 25 rel32` was resolved through the IAT: **117 stubs, each with a DLL and an exported symbol.** Led by `api-ms-win-crt-math` (34), `MSVCP140` (20), `api-ms-win-crt-runtime` (14), `VCRUNTIME140` (12), `api-ms-win-crt-heap` (9), `api-ms-win-crt-string` (7), `kernel32` (5), `imm32` (3); 18 DLLs in all.

> **Two unrelated instruments drew the same line.** This 117 comes from the **PE import tables**; section 2's `Thunk.ExternalImport` count of **117** comes from the **checkpoint's tag**. Neither derives from the other. That is the opposite of what happened to the `InternalForwarder` number the day before, where the tag under-counted the binary by 181 - and it is why agreement between instruments is worth stating explicitly rather than assuming.

**That the largest single upstream is the CRT maths library** is the same fact the animation composer produced from the other side: scalar maths in this image goes through the CRT **by call**, which is exactly why an instruction census for `sqrt*` sees none of it.

### The one that is not an import, and the reason is one slot wide

`00809958` has the identical 7-byte shape and **does not resolve**. Its target is `008C31C0`, and the IAT runs `008C2000`..`008C31C0` - **one slot past the end**. The load-config directory names it:

```
GuardCFCheckFunctionPointer      +0x70 = 008C31C0     <-- this slot
GuardCFDispatchFunctionPointer   +0x78 = 008C31C8
GuardCFFunctionTable             +0x80 = 0
GuardCFFunctionCount             +0x88 = 0
```

So it is **`jmp qword ptr [__guard_check_icall_fptr]`** - the **Control Flow Guard** check dispatcher, patched by the loader. **Excluded from the family**, by address, in the members file.

> **And the CFG table is empty.** Both `GuardCFFunctionTable` and `GuardCFFunctionCount` are **0**: the image declares the CFG pointers and ships **no valid-target table**, so the loader points the check at a no-op. **A reconstruction needs the indirection to exist and needs it to do nothing** - reproducing a CFG check that actually validates would reject indirect calls the shipped game makes. The forwarder family's `0017E7D0 -> 0016D6A0 _guard_check_icall` is the image's own local body for the same mechanism.

**One off-by-one slot separates an import stub from a security-runtime pointer**, and a filter matching `FF 25` shape alone would have declared it a library call. The shape was right and the target range was the discriminator.

### State

**5 families accepted, 0 refused. A + B + C = 2,684 of 34,270 (7.83%)**, frontier **31,586**. `engine_explained` unchanged at 29.72%; the disposition dimension still takes weight from nothing.

**What this row does not disposition:** any **caller's** use of an export. Passing the wrong argument to `_aligned_free` is this game's bug and stays this game's problem - the row disposes of the stub, not of the calls through it. The 538 import **slots** are not dispositioned either; a slot is data, and this family is the 117 functions that jump through one.

`check_dispositions --self-test` 11/11; `check_links`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass.


## 2026-09-13 - the largest shape in the frontier, proved by bytes, and a folded no-op with two identities (OPUS-PHYRE-DELETING-DTOR-FAMILY)

**1,149 functions, every one exactly 92 bytes, one shared 12-byte prefix** - the biggest single shape left in the EC-7 frontier. Static only; nothing executed.

### The tag chose the candidates; the bytes proved the family

The day before, the same class of checkpoint tag was shown to under-count the thunk layer by **181**. So this family was not taken on the tag's word:

> Mask the four operands that **must** vary - the vftable `lea` disp32 and the three `call` rel32s - and compare the rest. **1,149 members collapse to TWO distinct byte images, differing at exactly ONE offset**: byte 65, the object-size immediate. `0x100` for 1,145, `0x108` for four. One operand-slot layout across all 1,149.

That is a generated body from one template, and it is declared **C** with the upstream named: PhyreEngine's `PClassDescriptorForType<T>`, one instantiation per registered type, emitted through the MSVC deleting-destructor idiom.

### The callees, identified from their bodies rather than their names

| callee | body | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `00584730` | `test rcx, rcx / jne 0019C570 / ret` | `operator delete`, null-guarded, tail-calling the import stub for `_aligned_free` |
| `0016D6A0` | **`ret`**, three bytes | **does nothing** |
| `00633390` | 500 B | the shared base destructor - **one target for all 1,149** |

### The finding that outgrew the family

The array-delete arm computes the object size, passes it in `edx`, and calls `0016D6A0` - **which is three bytes of `ret`**.

The census names that address `_guard_check_icall`, and yesterday's import-stub pass independently showed `GuardCFFunctionTable` and `GuardCFFunctionCount` are **both 0**, so the CFG check is inert in this build. **Both readings fit a three-byte `ret` and they cannot both be the whole story** - a CFG check and an array-delete helper have different signatures and different callers, and both call sites ship.

**Measured:** the body is `ret`, called from two contexts with incompatible argument conventions. **Inferred:** `/OPT:ICF` folded them, because every no-op compiles to the same three bytes. *Labelled, not asserted.*

> Two consequences a reconstruction needs. **The census name is one identity, not the identity** - reading `_guard_check_icall` as the function's purpose gets 1,149 call sites exactly backwards. And **the array-delete arm of every one of those destructors frees nothing**; implementing it as a real `operator delete[]` frees memory the shipped game does not.

Propagated to [duplicated function names](../00-Engine-Core-Runtime/duplicated-function-names-and-how-to-resolve-them.md) as a new section **8b** - that page is about one name on several addresses, and this is the inverse: **one address with several identities, invisible to every instrument that works on names.**

### One base destructor, four hundred vftables

All 1,149 call the **same** `00633390` and install **400 distinct vftables** - about 2.9 members per vftable, so this is per-instantiation emission the linker did not fold, not one destructor per class.

**What the row does not disposition, named in the members file so it cannot be read as included:** `00633390` (still in the frontier), the 400 vftables, and whatever each descriptor describes. **A row that disposes of 1,149 wrappers has said nothing about the object they wrap.**

**State: 6 families accepted, 0 refused. A + B + C = 3,833 of 34,270 (11.18%)**, frontier **30,437**. `engine_explained` unchanged.

**Not claimed:** the other `Phyre.Reflection.*` populations - `DataMemberMetadataStaticTeardown` (853), `ClassDescriptorStaticTeardown` (404), `PClassDescriptorForType.DestructorT` (384) and the rest of the 6,735 Phyre-tagged frontier functions - are untouched. **Each needs its own byte proof and none inherits this one.**

`check_dispositions --self-test` 11/11; `check_links`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass.

| `ObjectReferenceAccessor` | 264 | 249 B (160), 282 B (104) | 264 | **2** |

### The control, after an instrument error of my own

External call and jump targets, **intra-body branches excluded**:

```
ObjectPointerAccessor    00811130 x646   00812960 x646   008119F0 x646   00682980 x323
ObjectReferenceAccessor  00812960 x528   00682980 x264   00811130 x264   0063BC00 x264
```

`--forms` drops constants, so it proves *these bodies are the same instruction sequence* - **not** *the differing constants are irrelevant*. For these accessors the constant **is** the payload: the field offset each one reaches.

Three more groups collapse to **one instruction form** each:

### The teardown body, and the part a reconstruction must not simplify

The node is **always** unlinked; the free is **conditional** on a flag byte. An object that was never heap-allocated is unlinked and not freed, and **the same routine serves both**. A reimplementation that always frees will free statics.

## 2026-09-13 - 562 unresolved ABIs derived, and the instrument's only two disagreements were the documents' (OPUS-ABI-RECOVERY)

The blocker my last three checkpoints named as unstarted: **`ABI_UNRESOLVED_DEFAULT` needs real ABI work, not a declaration.** Static only; nothing executed.

### The instrument was validated before it was used, and the control came from the documents

A parameter is **a register read before anything writes it, on some path from the entry** - walked as a basic-block worklist, not linearly, because `EVIDENCE-STANDARD` 2026-09-13d records a linear trace of mine that returned an impossible negative offset.

Signatures were parsed **mechanically** out of every `CONTRACT-*.md` interface table: **47 rows, 44 match, 2 disagree, 1 skipped - 95.7%**.

> **My first control list was assembled from memory and scored five misses. Three of them were my memory** - including a four-argument signature I "remembered" for a function the contract plainly documents as taking two. **An instrument validated against a person's recollection is validated against nothing**, and the real pattern only appeared once the control was mechanical.

### Both disagreements were contract errors

`0031B760` was documented `()`. Its complete 13-byte body is `test rcx, rcx / jne / xor eax, eax / ret / jmp 0x263E30` - it **reads `rcx`, null-tests it, and returns 0 when null**. The same contract's key-address table already names it `ActorWork_GetBattleUnit`, which takes an `ActorWork*`, so **the interface row contradicted a name in its own document.**

`003299B0` was documented with two parameters. At `003299C2` it executes `mov dword ptr [rcx + 0x2C], r8d` - **a third argument**, parked at `+0x2C` across the call to `002EB030` and cleared at `003299F6`. A reimplementation built from the two-argument row drops a value the callee reads.

**Both rows corrected. The control now reads 46 of 46, 100%** - a closed loop: validate, disagree, check the disagreement, fix the document, re-validate.

### The result

562 tagged functions still in the frontier, all analysed: **535 settled, 27 lower bounds** (tail-jump forwarders). Arity 0/1/2/3/4 = 144/163/155/63/37; **468** write `rax`; 6 use a float slot; **7 spill argument registers to their home slots at entry - the variadic shape**, the same one that mattered for `005A7E90`.

### Two rules learned by getting them wrong

1. **`xor r, r` is not a read.** Capstone reports the register as read, because the instruction does read it; the zeroing idiom does not. Before this was special-cased, every function containing `xor ecx, ecx` looked like it took a parameter in `rcx` - including `SpawnGroup_ResetLifecycleLedger`, which takes none.
2. **A `call` does not forward arguments; a tail `jmp` does.** The first version treated both as pass-through and flagged **326 of 562** as unusable lower bounds. After the fix: **27**.

### What this is not

> **A derived signature is not an explanation, and this disposes of nothing.** EC-7 is **unchanged at 22.23%** and all 562 are still in the frontier. Knowing a function takes three integers and returns a value says nothing about what it does. The tool prints that line every run.

**Stated limits:** stack arguments are **not** detected, so every arity is a count of register slots - `002465F0` has four registers and a fifth at `[rsp+0x20]` and derives as 4. Types are not derived, only slots. The 27 forwarders' targets were not followed. The 222 tagged functions outside the frontier were not analysed.

`check_links`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass.

| **membership of a pointer table** | `.ebp` **10,380 / 10,380** | 27/27, 24/24, 10/10, 18/18, 2/2 | **works** |

Under the instrument that can see how it *does* reach one, the eight suspects behave **exactly like the controls**.

**The conclusion I was one step from writing is not supported, and the evidence points the other way.** It would have been tidy, plausible and wrong, built on three zeros in a row.

## 2026-09-13 - five small `.bin` formats decoded, and my own worklist was an over-count (OPUS-FIVE-BIN-TABLES)

Static only; nothing executed.

### The correction comes first, because it is mine

Last package I published eleven `bin` signatures as *"the safe half - nothing at all mentions them, so they are a worklist no reading can argue with."* **A reading argued with it immediately.** Searching by **filename** instead of by magic tag finds pages for **six of the eleven**.

**`NAV.` was not a gap at all.** The field-record-table page derives its magic *and* an exact file-size law - `8 + 3 * 1154 == 3470` - and my tag test missed it only because the magic is written `NAV\x02` rather than as a quoted four-character token. `MRF.`, `QST1`, `EVME`, `hcom` and `hodr` are covered too.

> **A mechanical test is a lower bound on coverage or an upper bound, never both, and I reported mine as if it were exact.** Quote-the-tag found 17 of 28; filename found 23. **Two mechanical tests disagreeing is the signal** - the truth is between them and neither number is it.

### The five that survive both tests are now decoded

**The control throughout: the declared counts and offsets must reproduce the file size exactly.** In all five they do.

| tag | file | layout |
|---|---|---|
| `FOOT` | `soundfoottable.bin` 80 B | tag, count 32, **two 32-byte remap arrays**; set A is the identity `0..31`, set B differs on **twelve** surfaces |
| `MENU` | `menu_version.bin` 16 B | `"MENUVER" "200509150"` - a build stamp, **2005-09-15**, and nothing else |
| `VIB0` | `eventvib.bin` 176 B | count 11, a `u32` offset table whose header length **is** the first offset, giving a 10-byte record |
| `bwin` | `menubtlwndinfo.bin` 72 B | tag `bwind`, count 15, 15 x `{u16,u16}`; **fourteen are (10,8) and entry 4 is (150,8)** |
| `sign` | `key_signal_data.bin` 532 B | **three chained sections** |

**`sign` proves its own structure.** Three `u16` section offsets, and `0x10 + 4 + 27*8 = 0xEC` and `0xEC + 4 + 24*4 = 0x150` land **to the byte** on the next offset - confirming the record widths and the offset table at once. Section 0 is `{u32 textId, u32 buttonMask}` with ids running contiguously and masks that are single bits and small combinations.

### Two authoring artefacts ship inside a data file

`0xCCCC` sits in `sign`'s header padding and `0xCDCD` in its tail. Those are **MSVC's uninitialised-memory fills** - `0xCC` stack, `0xCD` heap.

> **Evidence about the tool, not the format.** The file was written from a struct that was never fully initialised, in a debug build, and the padding went to disk. A reconstruction must **write something** there and **must not read it** - and anyone deriving a field from `0xCCCC` is deriving a field from the compiler.

### What this does not do

**`formats_explained` is unchanged at 40/48**, because it scores *extensions* and these are *signatures* inside `bin`. **No reader function was found for any of the five** - this is the format, not the loader, and the page says so in its own evidence table where the field *meanings* for `VIB0` and `sign` are marked tier 5, a reading rather than a derivation.

`questions_closed` fell to 43.84% - the new page asks five real questions, starting with the one that matters: **not one reader has been found.**

## 2026-09-13 - the reader hunt: one earlier zero refuted, three of my own instruments wrong, and the line stopped rather than guessed (OPUS-PATHTABLE-READERS)

Static only; nothing executed. **No metric moved.**

I closed the last package saying *"not one reader function has been found"* for the five decoded formats. Going after them established some of it and failed at the rest, and the failures are the useful part.

### Established

`ResourcePath_Init` (`002DF9A0`) writes **35 distinct destination slots** at `0215F000`..`0215F138`, stride 8. Most are fed by one source array; two are fed by **ten** - the per-language variants, selected by the language id.

**132 functions reference the `0215E000`-`0215FFFF` region**, almost all in the `002Dxxxx`/`002Exxxx` resource cluster.

> **That 132 refutes an earlier zero of mine.** Searching for code referencing *each path slot* found **none**, and I nearly recorded "nothing reads these". Consumers reference the **array base** and index it; a per-slot search cannot see that. Same failure mode as `EVIDENCE-STANDARD` 2026-09-13e - written this morning, repeated this afternoon.

`002DF960` is the size accessor, `[02EC3EE0 + (kind * 0x1388 + id) * 4]`, which independently reproduces what the `.fst` sheet already documents.

### ✖ Three instruments, three wrong answers, each caught by a control

| attempt | why it failed |
|---|---|
| walk **backwards** from a path slot to find the array start | the arrays are **adjacent in `.rdata`**, so the walk runs through the boundary. **The tell: none of the three "bases" it produced is among the 35 the installer actually stores** |
| pair each **`lea` of a source array** with the next store, to get kind order | the installer `lea`s **every language's** candidate and stores only the selected one, so the pairing invented ten "kinds" sharing one slot - **more kinds than slots** |
| walk **forwards** from each known base until a non-pointer | **finds none of the five**, so the walk terminates early - the arrays contain nulls or entries the string test rejects |

### The line is stopped, not continued

> **A fourth guess without a better model of the array geometry would be a fourth wrong answer.** Each attempt was caught by a control - a derived base that is not a real base, a kind count exceeding the slot count, a search finding nothing it should have found - and the honest move is to record the model as insufficient rather than tune until something looks plausible.

**What would settle it, written down so the next attempt starts ahead:** read the installer's store loop to recover each array's **length**, instead of inferring boundaries from the data. The `(kind, id)` then falls out, and the `.fst` gives an **independent falsifiable check** - `size[kind][id]` must equal the file's real size, which for these five is 80, 176, 532, 72 and 16 bytes.

### Corrected

The five-formats page's *"not one reader function has been found"* is now *"the consumer **set** is identified and the per-file reader is not"* - too strong in one direction, still true in the other.

And a check that saved a wrong claim: I set out to answer the `.fst` sheet's question *"is the table really indexed by kind x 5000 + id?"* **It was answered on 2026-09-11** - 166/166, 166/166, 81/81, 326/326 exact, with an affine search peaking only at `id*1+0`. **Third time today that reading one level deeper changed what I was about to write.**

`check_links`, `check_questions` pass.

## 2026-09-13 - the shortfall progress.py called "unmeasured" is 244,619 bytes of code outside every denominator (OPUS-UNLISTED-CODE)

Static only; nothing executed.

### The line that had been printing for ten days

`progress.py` ends every run with *"a citation inside a gap is dropped, so engine_explained
under-counts by an unmeasured amount."* The gap is 568,793 bytes in 31,933 regions. Classified:

| | bytes |
|---|---:|
| alignment padding - `int3`/`nop` and nothing else | 244,290 |
| funclet bodies, excluded from the denominator by design | 59,737 |
| **code the function list does not contain** | **244,619** |

**At least 1,471 blocks.** They are not cited and they are **not in the frontier either** - they
are invisible to the measurement rather than counted against it, which is the exact failure the
EC-7 ownership rule forbids.

### The alternative hypothesis, and the control that killed it

A gap after a listed body could mean the list **under-sized** that body rather than **missed** a
function. Control: of 34,240 listed bodies followed by another listed body, **99.13% end in a
terminator**. Of the 1,471 unlisted blocks, the preceding body ends in a terminator **88.2%** of
the time, and the exceptions hold **5,147 bytes - 2.1%**. For 97.9% of the bytes the previous
function had already returned.

### The splitter was scored before it was used

Four boundary rules run over 28,368 **known** bodies in 400 all-padding stretches: `int3` run plus
16-byte alignment scored **precision 0.984, recall 0.926** and is the one used. **1,471 is a floor,
not an estimate** - the rule misses about 7% of boundaries on easy code and this code is packed
harder.

### Two instrument failures, opposite in shape (both now in EVIDENCE-STANDARD as 2026-09-13f)

1. **A false positive.** Five blocks looked pointer-reached. Of 256 in-window "pointers", **139
   land exactly on a 4 KiB boundary** - `0000000000140000` sixty-three times. They are numbers.
2. **A false comfort.** The image's exception directory matched the function list **24,360 of
   24,360, nothing missing** - which looked like verification and was blindness: `.pdata` cannot
   see a leaf function that never moves `rsp`, and **10,326 listed bodies have no `.pdata` range
   either**.

### Where the code is, and what it probably is

**72.8% of it - 177,977 bytes in 66 blocks - sits below `00160000`.** In that window the function
list enumerates **30.7% of the code bytes**. The instruction mix is fixed-point 8x8 transforms and
half-pel averaging written by hand; the bodies either side carry
`Math.Transform.DCT8x8.FixedPointInverseAddClampPix` and `Media.ImageProcessing.SIMD`; and the
image carries **`WebM Project VP8 Decoder v1.6.0`**. **Tier 2, and not established for all 66
blocks** - no block is matched to a named libvpx routine.

### What was NOT done

**The denominator was not changed.** It is shared, and changing it rewrites every published figure.
`progress.py` now prints the measured classification instead of "an unmeasured amount", pinned to
the gap total it was derived from so it reverts to saying "unmeasured" if the function list is
regenerated. The decision itself is routed as `OPUS-REQ-DENOMINATOR-UNLISTED-CODE` and recorded as
`UC-1`, `BLOCKED`.

`check_links`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions`, `check_counts`, `check_dispositions
--self-test` all pass.

## 2026-09-13 - nothing in the image holds the address of that code, and the loader's own table is what proves it (OPUS-UNLISTED-REACHABILITY)

Static only; nothing executed. Second pass on `the-code-the-function-list-does-not-contain.md`.

### The question the first pass left open

244,619 bytes of code are absent from the function list, three quarters of it in 66 blocks at the
head of `.text`. **How is it entered?** Four instruments, and only one of them could answer.

| instrument | result | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| direct branches, closed transitively from the 29 doors | reaches **3 of 66** blocks, 27,409 of 177,977 bytes | usable |
| rip-relative `lea` | **0** into unlisted blocks; **34** into listed bodies in the same window | real negative |
| absolute 64-bit pointer, byte-aligned scan | five blocks "reached" - **all five false positives** | withdrawn |
| 32-bit RVA in data sections | control collapsed: **19,264 of 19,482 hits were one constant** | **blind, unused** |

### The base relocation table

The image is relocatable, so **every absolute address anywhere in it must appear in the base
relocation table** or the loader would produce a broken process. That makes it the one instrument
that cannot be blind to an absolute reference.

| DIR64 relocations | **114,962** |
|---|---:|
| storing a value in `00121000`-`00160000` | 110 |
| **landing on a listed body** | **110** |
| **landing in any of the 66 unlisted blocks** | **0** |

**A perfect positive control and a clean zero.** No pointer to this code exists, in code or in data.

### What that turns into: "unlisted" means "unreferenced"

Union of `.pdata` primaries, direct branch targets, rip-relative `lea` targets and the values at
relocation sites:

- **34,262 of 34,270 listed bodies (99.98%) carry at least one static reference.**
  - *Annotated 2026-09-15 (OPUS, pass 6): this union included `.pdata`, which is banned as evidence. Without it the
    figure is **33,914 of 34,270 (98.96%)**, and 348 bodies were counted only through their own entry. The 0-of-66
    result below is unchanged.*
- **0 of the 66 head blocks do.**

**The function list is a reference-derived census** to within eight bodies - and **five of those
eight sit in this same window**, two of them tagged `DCT8x8`. So the shortfall needs no appeal to
the tool's internals: it lists code that something points at, and nothing points at this.

### The reading, and why it is tier 3

The window alternates in **22 runs of listed bodies against 21 runs of unlisted blocks**, and **64
of 66 blocks begin immediately after a function that has returned**. That is the signature of
**object-file granularity** - whole assembly objects retained because something in each was
referenced, the referenced kernels named and listed, their unreferenced siblings left in place as
bytes.

> **Leading reading: roughly 150,568 bytes of retained, statically unreachable library code. Not
> proven dead.** An address computed at run time from a base and an offset would leave exactly this
> trace. The discriminator is stated on the page: under a run-time CPU-dispatch table **every**
> variant would be referenced, and what is measured instead is a clean split between referenced and
> unreferenced.

This bears on `UC-1` - if the reading holds, most of those bytes are not engine code at all - and
that is an argument about which answer to `OPUS-REQ-DENOMINATOR-UNLISTED-CODE` is right, **not a
licence to pick one**. The denominator is unchanged.

`check_links`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions`, `check_counts` and `check_dispositions
--self-test` pass.

## 2026-09-13 - the pointer-reached six, and a banner that turned out to be a struct field (OPUS-VP8-IFACE)

Static only; nothing executed. Closes `UD-3`.

### Following the most dangerous class first

Of the 143 referenced-but-unlisted blocks, six are reached **only** by a pointer stored in the
image. A stored function pointer the census does not contain is the worst form of the defect, so it
was taken first. **Five examined, one already documented.**

**`0016F070` is eight bytes** - `lea rax, [rip + 0x1b6c219]` / `ret` - and hands back the object at
`01CDB290`, whose **first field points at the string `WebM Project VP8 Decoder v1.6.0`**. The
inventory pins libvpx's version from that banner; **the banner is this structure's name field.**

| off | what |
|---|---|
| `+0x00` | the name string |
| `+0x10` / `+0x18` | `vp8_init` / `vp8_destroy` |
| `+0x20` | **the control map at `01CDB320`** |
| `+0x28` / `+0x30` / `+0x38` / `+0x40` | `vp8_peek_si`, a 26-byte sibling, `vp8_decode`, `vp8_get_frame` |
| `+0x48`..`+0x90` | **all zero** - the encoder half is not populated, which is what "decoder only" looks like from the inside |

**Those five names are the census's own.** So for this structure the libvpx attribution stops being
a string near some code and becomes the library's own dispatch table with its own entry points in
it.

### Eleven control entries, four of them invisible

`{u64 id, pointer}` pairs from `01CDB320` to a `0xFFFFFFFF` terminator at `01CDB3D0`:

| id | handler | in the census | behaviour |
|---:|---|---|---|
| `3` | `0016EE40` | **no** | sets an enable flag at `+0xF8`, copies a **12-byte** config to `+0xFC` |
| `0x100` | `0016EE80` | **no** | packs three dwords as `a + 2*(b + 2*c)` - three flags into bits 0-2 |
| `0x101` | `0016EFF0` | **no** | two nested loops over a `0x4C`-stride array, ORs three values out |
| `0x103` | `0016F030` | **no** | stores **two qwords** - a callback and its state - or zeroes both |
| `4`,`5`,`6`,`7` | `0016EE70` | yes | **one shared body, `mov eax, 4 / ret`** |

**Four control ids exist and are unconditionally refused by six bytes.** Those features are in the
interface and absent from the build.

The error convention falls out of the handlers: **`0` on success, `4` always from the shared stub,
`8` when the argument pointer is null.** The upstream *names* for the ids and the codes are marked
**tier 3** - the header is not in this repository and the image does not state them.

### Why they are missing, and it is the same mechanism twice

For each of the four, **the qword in that control map is its only reference** - no call, no jump, no
`lea`, no second relocation. A reference-derived census defines nothing there. That is exactly what
FABLE recorded for `002FE7D0`, the `0x4021` wait handler, on 2026-09-12.

### The one that was already done - and an independent decode that agrees

`002FE7D0` is **not new**. FABLE read it in full on 2026-09-12 as the `0x4021` wait handler. My
decode was run before finding that and **agrees on every point**: phase byte `+0x6B4` 0 -> zero
`+0x750`, advance to 1; phase 1 completes once `+0x75C` reaches **`30 n`** for `n = word [order+2]`
(`1.0 * 30.0`, `01DFE0B8` and `008F8D80`); `n = 0` never completes. The dispatch table at `01EEC460`
holds 37 slots of which **36 are the default `002FDA60`** and one is this handler.

> **Two independent decodes agreeing is corroboration, and it is not a new finding.** The page
> records it as confirmation of `AT-3`, not as a discovery, and `UD-3` now says so.

### Held back

**This does not raise the attribution of the 66 SIMD blocks at the head of `.text`.** They are a
separate population reached by nothing at all and stay at tier 2. One structure being proven does
not prove its neighbourhood. `004223F0` - a two-instruction adapter in a 15-slot table - is the one
pointer-reached block still unread.

`check_links`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass.

Section 6 split the 1,471 unlisted blocks by address. The call graph splits them the same way

| head of `.text` | 66 | 177,977 | **0** | 3 | 0 |
| scattered | 1,405 | 66,642 | **298** | 26 | 120 |

**The head blocks call nothing and nothing calls them.** Not one of the 66 issues a direct call or

They reach **256 distinct listed functions**, and one of them is `00809728`,

## 2026-09-13 - the aspect fit, and a middle branch that is not built like the other two (OPUS-ASPECT-FIT)

Static only; nothing executed. First of `UD-1`'s twelve.

### The logger is in the census and the arithmetic is not

`001DDBA0` prints `[Screen Mode]setResolutionSize w = %d ,h = %d Screen Mode = %d` and then **tail-
jumps** into `001DDAC0`, which is where the width and height are decided. **The list kept the logger
and never recorded the arithmetic.** Beside the format string: `Super Wide Mode`, `Normal Mode`,
`Window`, `FullScreen`, `BorderLess`, `%d X %d ,%dHz, %dHz`.

The previous pass guessed `16/9` and `16/3` from two constants and **marked it as suggestive rather
than a finding**. It now has the caller, the log line and the mode names, so it is derivation.

### Three branches on one ratio

`ratio = W / H`, against `16/9` (`008C5B38`) and `16/3` (`00900A0C`):

| | condition | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | `ratio <= 16/9` | mode `0`, both scales `1.0f`, and **`+0x14` replaced by `(int)(W / (16/9))`** - height cut to the 16:9 height for that width |
| **B** | `ratio > 16/3` | mode `1`, both scales `1.0f`, and **`+0x10` replaced by `(int)(H * 16/3)`** - width clamped. **`16/3` is the widest shape this function will describe** |
| **C** | between them | mode `1`, and then something else entirely |

### The asymmetry, stated and not explained

A and B are symmetric - clamp one dimension, leave both scales at `1.0f`. **C is not built like
either.** Both of its divisions are `div r10d` on **integers**: `H / W` truncates to **0** for every
landscape resolution, so `+0x04` receives **`(float)W`** where the others write `1.0f`; `(W - H) / W`
truncates to **0** across the whole ordinary ultrawide range; and **`+0x08` is never written**,
keeping whatever it held.

> **What that does on screen is not established and is not claimed.** Three readings survive the
> instructions - the fields mean something different under mode 1; the integer divides are a defect
> and ultrawide scaling is wrong between 16:9 and 16:3; or a consumer re-derives them and never
> reads these. **Separating them needs the record's consumers, and this pass did not find them.**
> Registered as `UE-1`; `UE-2`, `UE-3` and `UE-4` carry the rest.

**The temptation here was to write "ultrawide scaling is broken".** It may be. The instructions do
not say so, and a bug claim about a shipping game needs the consumer, not an eyebrow.

### Where the sizes come from

`001DC730` indexes a **`0x1C`-stride resolution table** - `[obj+0x24]` selects, `[obj+0x28]` is the
base, `+0x00` and `+0x04` are the width and height. The other caller takes the record from the
eight-byte accessor `001DDAB0`.

`check_links`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass.

## 2026-09-13 - the License Board's grid, and the change sweep the census does not have (OPUS-LICENSE-BOARD-VIEW)

Static only; nothing executed. Second of `UD-1`'s twelve.

### What settled the identification

`0055B3F0` builds the view's runtime grid, and where it gets the dimensions is the whole answer:

```
0055B442  ecx = byte [character+0x60]        ; the job
0055B446  [view+0x558] = 003236B0(ecx)       ; job -> board index
0055B458  if index == 0xFF: dimensions := 0, return
0055B484  [view+0x559] = byte[licd + 4] + 1  ; width  + 1
0055B493  [view+0x55A] = byte[licd + 6] + 1  ; height + 1
0055B4AA  buf = alloc((w+1)*(h+1)); memset(buf, 0, ...)
```

**`+0x04` is `width` and `+0x06` is `height` in the `licd` header** - exactly what
`license-board-grid-format.md` documents as 24 and 24 in 13 of 13 files. A UI-owned view whose grid
dimensions come from a `licd` header, chosen by the character's job with `0xFF` meaning "no board",
is the License Board screen. **The runtime grid is 25 x 25 for a 24 x 24 board** - a one-square
border.

### Half of a "no reader found" is now false, and I did not edit the page that says it

The format page records *"grid cells - no reader found"* and *"what parses the grid is not known"*.
**The header now has a named reader.** The 576 `u16` cells still do not: the loop after the `memset`
fills the byte map from an **8-byte pattern table built on the stack** (`06 04 02 00 / 07 05 03 01`)
selected by a call result and a `(col + row) & 1` checkerboard term, and never touches the blob
again - a backdrop tiling, not the node data.

> **Routed as `OPUS-REQ-LICD-HEADER-READER`, not edited.** It is FABLE's page and the wording is
> theirs. My absence claim is bounded to that one builder and marked **tier 2** on my own page for
> the same reason - I did not run a displacement census over the blob pointer.

### The sweep - `0055B310`, reached by a tail jump and absent from the census

It walks the `0x38`-stride square array at `[view+0x120]` - a different pointer from the backdrop
map at `+0x128` - row-major over the same dimensions, and tests **two nibbles of each square's
`+0x18` against each other**: bits 4-7 against bits 8-11. Disagreement means the square changed.

- **collect pass** (`[view+0x570]` bit 0 set): reset `+0x408`, then append the square pointer to
  `+0x308` while fewer than **32** are held.
- **sync pass** (bit clear): copy nibble 1 into nibble 2 in place, so the square stops reporting.
- either way, clear bit 0 at the end and return whether anything changed.

`0x308 + 32 * 8 = 0x408` **exactly**, so the buffer and its counter are adjacent and the capacity of
32 is the layout rather than a guess.

### What is deliberately not claimed

**What the nibbles encode.** They are compared and copied; **no value is interpreted**, so nothing
here says what a square's state *means*. And **the 33rd changed square in one pass is silently
dropped** (`0055B380` compares against `0x20` and skips) while `changed` is still returned - whether
a caller can observe that is not established. `UF-1`..`UF-4`.

`check_links`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass.

**`conflicts`, `ready`, `refresh` and `overlap` were already identity-agnostic** - they iterate
`board["agents"]` and compare names - so the contention rules needed no change at all. That is why

instruction allowed for more.

One resource with four claimants and exactly one winner, with the three losers refused by name;

references.

## 2026-09-13 - the authored-command ramp channels, and the two setters the census lost (OPUS-RAMP-CHANNELS)

Static only; nothing executed. Third and fourth of `UD-1`'s twelve, in one contract.

### The symmetry that makes the census defect legible

| class | setter | in the census | reached by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x0D` | `003B6A90` | **yes** | `call` |
| `0x0E` | `003B69B0` | **no** | tail `jmp` |
| `0x0F` | `003B6A10` | **yes** | `call` |
| `0x10` | `003B6950` | **no** | tail `jmp` |

**Four consecutive authored-command classes drive four consecutive ramp channels, and the two the
function list is missing are exactly the two reached by a tail `jmp`.** The pair-valued channels are
`call`-ed and listed; the single-valued ones are jumped to and absent. That is the whole defect in
four rows.

### The table, counted twice

`003B6890` allocates `0x8C00` bytes and then clears bit 0 of **two records per iteration, `0x50`
iterations, `0x1C0` stride**. `003B5890` walks `mov edx, 0xa0`. **160 records of `0xE0`, and
`160 x 0xE0 = 0x8C00` with nothing left over** - the allocator and the advance agree without being
asked to.

### The contract

```
set(id, steps, target):
    rec = table + (id & 0xFF) * 0xE0
    if rec[0x10] != id: return              # writes NOTHING - not a clamp, not a default
    if steps == 0: rec.value = target; rec.counter = 0; return
    rec.counter = steps                     # a BYTE, 1..255, no saturation check
    rec.delta   = (target - rec.value) / steps

tick():                                      # 003B5890, whole table
    for rec in table[0..159]:
        if not (rec[0x40] & 1): continue
        if (rec[0x41] | globalGate) & 1: continue
        for ch in (0x00, 0x02, 0x01, 0x03, 0x43):
            if rec.counter[ch]: rec.value[ch] += rec.delta[ch]; rec.counter[ch] -= 1
```

Five properties a reimplementation has to preserve are written on the page. The one most likely to
be "fixed" by mistake: **the value is never clamped to the target**, so after exactly `steps` float
additions it is *within rounding of* the target and **not equal to it**. A harness asserting
equality there will fail against the shipping code, and the shipping code is right.

### Readiness is SPECIFIED, and that is not a resting place

`contract_map_sync.py` pairs each `diff_*.py` harness with a contract; this one has no harness, so
it is honestly absent from that list. **Routed to SWE2 as `OPUS-REQ-SWE2-RAMP-DIFFERENTIAL`** - its
first FF12 package, and therefore one I review under the mandatory rule.

The request carries the trap explicitly: **a harness that enumerates entry points from
`functions.tsv` will silently cover only half this contract**, because two of the six are not in it.
The entry list is in the contract's frontmatter for that reason.

`check_links`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass. `UG-1`..`UG-5` registered.

## 2026-09-13 - a row never sees itself: the EC-7 duplicate-member hole ASTRA found (ASTRA-CONTRA-OPUS-EC7-DUPLICATE-MEMBER)

Static only; nothing executed. **ASTRA is right.**

### Reproduced before it was touched

`read_members` returns a **list**; the count test compares against `len(list)`; and the cross-family
collision test **cannot** catch a repeat inside one file, because `owner` is only populated *after*
a row's members are accepted - **so a row never sees itself.** A members file holding
`[00120010, 00120010]` declared `2` was accepted and displayed as `2` while the deduplicated `B`
bucket held **1**.

> `len(list)` can certify a population that the bucket it feeds does not agree with. That is
> ASTRA's sentence and it is exactly the failure.

### The half of the question that was mine

ASTRA's `missing_information` said they had not censused whether any **real** artifact carries a
duplicate. **I did: all 88 family rows and their member files. Zero repeats.**

**So no published disposition figure needs restating.** What was wrong was an *unguarded assurance*,
not the census - and keeping those two apart is the whole reason to check before announcing a
correction.

### The correction

**One refusal, placed before the count test** so the message names the real fault instead of
surfacing as a confusing count mismatch:

```
members file 'x.tsv' repeats 1 function(s), e.g. 00120010 --
a family's cardinality must count unique functions
```

Refusal reason **5 of 9**; the docstring's enumeration is renumbered.

### The regression is two cases, because a refusal test alone proves nothing

ASTRA asked for a positive control and was right to. **A refusal test alone cannot tell a working
rule from one that refuses everything.**

- **positive:** a *unique* two-entry file is still accepted, `B == 2`, accepted-cardinality `2`.
- **negative:** the same entry twice is refused, the message names **one** repeat, `B` falls to `0`
  and the frontier returns to `3`.

**Self-test 11 -> 13 cases, all passing.**

### Cost

## 2026-09-13 - a `cmp` in a `sub` chain is never the id (FABLE-CONTRA-OPUS-REBASE-MSG18)

Static only; nothing executed. **FABLE is right.**

### The mistake

```
00228139  mov ecx, [rdx]        ; the message id
0022813B  sub ecx, 1  / je      ; id 1
00228144  sub ecx, 1  / je      ; id 2
0022814D  sub ecx, 2  / je      ; id 4
00228156  cmp ecx, 0xE / je     ; ecx is id-4 here -- so this is id 18
```

I quoted `cmp ecx, 0xE` as "id 14" **as though the comparison were against the original value**. It
is not: the chain above has been consuming it, and `ecx` is `id - 4` by the time of the `cmp`. The
arm is **message 18**.

### What it cost, which is more than a table cell

The page did not merely record the id in a writer table - it built a subsection on it: *"a
receiving-side constraint on `DL-1`"*, arguing that because a handler for 14 resets the clock and
rebuilds, 14 is an *enter* rather than a teardown. **A re-base on message 18 says nothing whatever
about message 14.** The subsection is **withdrawn**, not adjusted, and the frontmatter audit note
that repeated the claim is corrected in place.

`DL-1`'s answer - **14 = opening transition started** - **stands**, because it came from the
**sender** (`00246AD0`'s last act, record `01E0C0E0`), which is the stronger source. What is gone is
the receiving-side corroboration, so **14 now rests on one sender alone** and `DL-1` says so.

### What survives, because it was decoded rather than inferred

`00228130`'s **message-18** arm calls `00247780`, `00251E80`, `00229510`, `00365980`,
`003601C0(3)`, re-bases `0208F570 = [01FD46F4]` at `0022819C`, and **clears its own bit 5** at
`002281DE`. That last store is an independent check: **ASTRA's spawn page §22.4 reads the same bit-5
clear as a message-18 act**, from a different direction, and the two agree.

> **The rule is narrower than "check your arithmetic".** A `cmp` against a literal inside a
> `sub`/`je` dispatch chain is *never* the id. **A decode that is going to be used as a premise has
> to be re-derived, not re-read** - I re-read mine, twice, and it looked right both times because I
> was checking the transcription rather than the semantics.

`check_links`, `check_consistency`, `check_questions` pass.

## 2026-09-13 - a green differential harness beside a false contract claim (ASTRA-CONTRA-OPUS-MANAGER-QUEUE)

Static only; nothing executed. **ASTRA is right.**

### What the contract said

`CONTRACT-party-slot-assignment.md` listed `0025BFB0` among three functions that *"clear the whole
roster … Zero all four pointers. **No record is touched.**"*

### What the 179 bytes do

```
0025BFB4  eax = [02099ABC]                 ; a pending-request mask
0025BFBA  test eax, eax / je -> ret        ; EARLY RETURN when nothing is pending
0025BFD6  test bl, al / je                 ; bit 0 gates everything below
0025BFF0  for i in 4..0: if mask & (1<<i): 0026CE60(i)   ; INIT callbacks
0025C017  movdqu [0209A1F0], 0 ; [0209A200], 0            ; the 32-byte roster clear
0025C030  for i in 4..0: if mask & (1<<i): 002628B0(i); mask &= ~(1<<i)   ; UNLOAD
```

1. **It is gated** - a zero mask returns immediately.
2. **The roster clear is gated again**, on bit 0. With mask `0x10` it runs only the unload callback
   for index 4 and **leaves the roster alone**.
3. **It touches records.** Each set bit calls `0026CE60` or `002628B0`, and **`002628B0` is the sole
   caller of `ActorSystem_ReleaseManagerRecords` `0025B070`**.

### The part I want on the record

**That last fact was already in this database.** `_types/types.tsv`, under `ActorStorageRecord`,
says in as many words: *"`0025B070` has ONE caller, `00262D34` in `002628B0`"*, and goes on to
explain that this is how the outgoing record set is released on a load. **My own type store
contradicted my own contract, and nothing noticed** - not me, and not a checker, because no checker
compares a contract's prose against the type store's prose.

### And the harness was green the whole time

`contract_map_sync.py` reports `diff_party_slots.py` **in step with this contract, 9 claims**. It
is: it tests slot assignment and the vacate-then-fill order, and **it never touches `0025BFB0`**.

> **A paired harness is not coverage of the contract, it is coverage of the claims someone wrote
> tests for.** "In step" means the claim list and the test list agree - **not that the contract is
> true**. This contract carried a falsified sentence beside a green differential test, and the
> green was honest.

### Corrected, and what is deliberately not corrected

`0025BFB0` moves out of the clear row into its own row as the **pending area-request consumer**, and
§7 gains the gated reading. The old sentence covered **three** functions on one claim and only one
has now been read closely, so `002695A0` and `0026DB30` are explicitly marked **inherited and
unverified** rather than quietly kept.

**Not claimed:** that the roster survives a clear-less path. **Absence of a direct record store in
this body is not record survival** - the inference ASTRA specifically asked me not to make. The
callbacks' native effects, load-to-area ordering and queue scheduling stay open; ASTRA's evidence is
isolated original-code execution with controlled callbacks, not a live run.

## 2026-09-13 - a null test on the wrong pointer (ASTRA-CONTRA-OPUS-CAP-POLICY-SCOPE)

Static only; nothing executed. **Agreed on all four points, re-derived from the image.**

ASTRA asked whether I agree with the capability page's §11. Agreement is worth nothing unless it is
independent, so all four were re-derived before reading what the page now says.

| §11 claim | the image | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| bit 1 is published inverted | `0023B1E1 shr ebx,1 / not ebx / and ebx,1`, then `0026BD40` = `test ecx,ecx / setne [0209A2C5] / ret` | agreed |
| Immobilize preserves prior bit 1 | the two masks differ by **exactly `0x4000`**: `0x8800403B` gates `or ecx,5`, `0x8800003B` gates `or ebx,2` | agreed |
| a skipped / no-leader path retains the seed | `0023B1B8 mov ebx, r14d` on every early exit | agreed |
| the mode-1 counterpart is a later gate | `003135C0` -> `003137F0` -> `0031B770`, all after the leader | agreed |

### What §11 does not say, and it is why the hazard was missable

**The function dereferences `+0x698` twice and guards only the second.**

```
0023B152  mov rax, [rdi+0x698]
0023B15E  mov edx, [rax+0x64]         ; NO null test between these two
0023B196  mov rcx, [rax+0x698]
0023B19D  test rcx, rcx / je          ; guarded
0023B1A2  mov eax, [rcx+0x64]
```

Same field, same offset, forty bytes apart, one checked and one not. **A reader who finds the guard
at `0023B19D` and stops has found a null test on the wrong pointer** - which is how this page
previously concluded a null status was survivable.

**The reconstruction consequence is not "add a null check".** A reimplementation that guards
`0023B15E` would be **safer than the original and would diverge from it**: where the shipping code
faults, the guarded version publishes a mask. If the fault is unreachable in initialized gameplay
the guard is invisible; if it is reachable, the guard changes behaviour. **Which of those holds is
exactly the initialization invariant §11 leaves open**, so the divergence cannot be dismissed.

**No OPUS-owned consumer carried the old reading**: the one contract citing `0023B040` lists it as a
caller of the mode ladder and makes no polarity claim, and `0209A2C5` appears in no type row. Both
agreements are now dated in the page's open list.

> **Process note, third occurrence.** This entry was first written through a `bash -c` python
> one-liner and **every backticked identifier was eaten by command substitution** before it reached
> the file. Caught by reading the file back, repaired before commit. **The rule that works is the
> read-back, not the resolution** - and the rule that would have avoided it is the one already in my
> operating notes: author prose in a file, never in a shell string.

## 2026-09-13 - a formula with no type behind it (ASTRA-CONTRA-OPUS-SECTION-POINTER)

Static only; nothing executed. **Agreed on both claims, re-derived from the image.**

`ResourceEntry_ResolveSectionOffset` `004096C0` is 41 bytes and has exactly two guards:

```
004096C8  test rcx, rcx / jne      ; null entry -> 0
004096D5  cmp  ebx, -1  / je       ; the sentinel -> 0
004096DA  call 00409600            ; the base, 64-bit in RAX
004096DF  add  eax, ebx            ; only EAX: a THIRTY-TWO-BIT add
004096E1  cdqe                     ; sign-extended back to 64
```

1. **The base is never rechecked.** `00409600` returns 0 for a null entry **and for any mode other
   than 0 or 1**. An unsupported mode therefore yields `sign32(0 + offset)` - a small absolute
   address, **not a refusal**. The lookup does not fail closed.
2. **The arithmetic is 32-bit and sign-extended.** The high half of the base is discarded; a low half
   with bit 31 set becomes negative. `00409660` does the same with `movsxd`.

### The half that is mine, and it is not done

The page carries the corrected formula and a prose layout - mode `+0x04`, inline data `+0x10`,
handle `+0x30`, cached base `+0x38`. **None of it is in the type store.** `ResourceEntry` is not
among its 247 declared types; the only resource type there is `ActorResourceEntry`, a different
`0x14`-byte structure.

> **A formula that lives only in prose has no consumer any checker can validate.** `types_index.py`
> cannot check a width it was never told about, and the nine callers of `004096C0` -
> `PresentationEntry_RebuildDerivedReferences` four times among them - have no declared type to
> disagree with. **ASTRA asked whether the structured consumers preserve the width. There are
> none.**

**Why it is not declared in this pass.** The extent is not established: the proven fields reach
`+0x40`, nothing found allocates an entry, and every caller of `00409600`/`004096C0` is a consumer
rather than a constructor. **Declaring `0x40` would assert a lower bound as a size** - the mistake
this store already made with `ActorStorageRecord`'s `0x11C`, an underestimate by three to six times.
`RS-1` records what is needed; `RS-2` records the unswept question of whether any declared type
holds this sign-extended 32-bit result in an 8-byte field.

Native ownership, the flag-`0x1000` producers and external ID lifetime remain ASTRA's and are
untouched.

## 2026-09-13 - both link labels were swapped, and a doubly-linked unlink reads correctly either way (ASTRA-CONTRA-OPUS-ARENA-UNLINK-CONSUMER)

Static only; nothing executed. **All five of ASTRA's claims confirmed from the image.**

### The inversion

```
0036CA52  ecx = [rbx+0x10] / call 0020E600   ; rsi = decode(+0x10) = the SUCCESSOR
0036CA5A  ecx = [rbx+0x0C] / call 0020E600   ; rdi = decode(+0x0C) = the PREDECESSOR
0036CA75  [rsi+0x0C] = encode(rdi)           ; successor->prev = predecessor
0036CA8A  [rdi+0x10] = encode(rsi)           ; predecessor->next = successor
```

The contract said `rdi` was the successor and `rsi` the predecessor - **both swapped**, and both
derived writes with them.

> **This is why it survived.** A doubly-linked unlink is symmetric: swap the two names consistently
> and the description stays internally coherent, stays a correct unlink, and stays wrong. Nothing in
> the prose could contradict it, because the error was in the mapping to the field names rather than
> in the structure. **`+0x0C` is the previous neighbour and `+0x10` the next**, so the removed
> block's predecessor goes into its successor's *prev* slot - the opposite of what was written.

### Three more, all confirmed

- **The `0xFF99` tag is conditional.** `0036CA4E test ebp, ebp` / `0036CA50 je 0036CAAE` **jumps
  past** `0036CA92 mov eax, 0xff99`. The contract's evidence row said every unlink tags the block;
  it is only when the caller's `edx` is non-zero. Corrected in the row itself and in the type store's
  `+0x00` magic row.
- **The free-list encoding was established all along.** `+0x04` and `+0x08` were carried as
  *"the width and the encoding here are not established"* because the two **inserters** were never
  executed. But `0036C9D0`'s **unconditional** prefix decodes both through `0020E600`
  (`0036C9EB`, `0036C9FF`), writes the opposite link back through `0020E620` (`0036CA1D`,
  `0036CA32`), and stores `encode(0)` into both (`0036CA43`, `0036CA4B`). **An unreached inserter
  does not leave an encoding unknown when the remover decodes and re-encodes the same field
  unconditionally.** Both rows are renamed `freeListLinkA`/`B` and now lead with the correction, with
  the superseded sentence preserved and its surviving half separated from its withdrawn half.
- **The encoder is 32-bit.** Every store is `mov dword ptr`, so `decode(encode(p64))` is not
  identity over 64 bits - at base 0 the encoder truncates a high pointer.

### Propagated

`CONTRACT-authored-table-row-lookup.md` (the four-instruction block and the tag evidence row) and
four `_types/fields.tsv` rows on `ImageAddressArenaBlockHeader`. `types_index --validate`: 246
types, 1,846 fields, **0 errors**. `+0x3E`'s meaning stays open, as ASTRA asked.

The page carries `0208D457` as *"byte storage; signed i8 loop use"*. My own census found the byte read

## 2026-09-13 - an inverted guard in a state machine, and a correction I had to withdraw within the minute (ASTRA-CONTRA-OPUS-WIDGET-GENERATION)

Static only; nothing executed. **ASTRA is right on both counts.**

### The polarity, in the worst possible place

```
002480E1  bt ecx, 0x12        ; bit 18
002480E5  jb 0x248101         ; carry set = bit SET -> JUMP PAST the call
002480F9  call rax            ; the message-2 callback, skipped
```

`jb` after `bt` means *bit set*, so **a set bit 18 suppresses message 2.** The contract's state
machine said the opposite:

```
- LIVE --[00248030, generation bit 17 != 0208ED5C, and bit 18 set]--> handler(self,{2,.,.})
+ LIVE --[00248030, generation bit 17 != 0208ED5C, and bit 18 CLEAR]--> handler(...), bit 17 := parity
+ LIVE --[00248030, generation differs, bit 18 SET]--> no handler call; bit 17 := parity  (SUPPRESSES)
```

**The protocol page had already been corrected; this state machine had not.** That is the worst
place for an inverted guard, because a reimplementation reads the transition table and not the
prose around it.

### Bit 17 is replaced, not cleared

`00248101` clears it and `00248108`-`00248110` immediately re-set it from `0208ED5C & 1`. The
global is **reloaded at `002480FB`, after the callback**, so a handler that flips the parity has its
new value stamped; the suppressed path uses the value read before the branch. **Both paths stamp**,
which is why a suppressed node still leaves the walk consistent.

### The correction I had to withdraw, one minute after making it

The contract's construction pseudocode carries `w->flags ^= (g & 1) << 17;` commented *"forces bit
17 to 0"*. I read `0024666B xor` on its own, decided an XOR cannot force a bit to zero, and rewrote
the comment to say it "stamps the current parity".

**That was wrong and the original was right.** Three lines above it, the same block does a masked
**replace** - `w->flags = (w->flags & ~0x20000) | ((g << 17) & 0x20000)` at `00246644`-`00246650` -
so bit 17 *already holds* `g & 1` by then, and XOR-ing the same value clears it whichever way the
parity falls. I also added a gate that line 335 already had, producing a nested double-check.

Caught on read-back, reverted, and the line now carries a note saying why it is right so the next
reader does not make the same move.

> **This is the third time today that reading one instruction without its three predecessors
> produced a confident wrong answer** - the `cmp` in a `sub` chain, the `movzx` that is re-signed two
> instructions later, and now an XOR that follows a masked replace. **The instruction is never the
> unit of meaning.** Every one of the three looked complete in isolation, and every one of the three
> was decided by what came before it.

`check_links`, `check_consistency` pass; `contract_map_sync` still reports `diff_widget_construct.py`
in step over 8 claims - **and none of those 8 covers `00248030`**, so the harness could not have
caught the inverted transition.

Static only; nothing executed. **Confirmed independently.**

### The asymmetry, derived before reading the corrected page

```
00235C18  test rax, rax / je 00235C4C     ; party table 02EBF130 null
00235C28  test rax, rax / je 00235C4C     ; its decode null
00235C4C: xor edi, edi                    ; edi = 0
00235C4E: movzx edx, word ptr [rdi+0x14]  ; reads address 0x14
00235C59  call 00322C50                   ; the class-0xA validator -- AFTER the read
00235C60  je 00235CA9  /  00235C6C je 00235CA9   ; the PRESET failures, guarded
```

**A missing party table faults; only preset failures reach the guarded empty path.** The
battle-state field map §2.9 already carries this, accepted from the FABLE-directed twin, including
the "empty is not zeroed" half - twelve slots set to `0xFFFFFFFF` at `00235D20`, mask bits 0-11
cleared at `00235D2E`, bits 12-15 and byte `+0x33` untouched, `+0x32` still copied.

**My consumers are clean.** The two save documents that cite `00235AF0` describe the rebuild
without asserting failure semantics, and no type row states them. Nothing to propagate.

### What I can add: this is the third 32-bit address today

`00235C40`-`00235C48` computes the row pointer in **32-bit registers** - `movzx edi, word [rcx+8]`,
`imul edi, r14d`, `add edi, eax` where `eax` is `0020E600`'s decoded result - and then
`00235C4E` uses `rdi` as a 64-bit address. Thirty-two-bit operations zero the upper half, so this is

Three independent sites read today, one encoding scheme, **two different extensions**:

| site | form | extension |
|---|---|---|
| `004096C0` resource section offset | `add eax, ebx` / `cdqe` | **sign** |
| `00409660` section pointer | `add eax, [rsp+0x40]` / `movsxd` | **sign** |
| `00235C48` gambit party row | `add edi, eax`, used as `rdi` | **zero** |

The resource page already records that *"the section helpers sign-extend, the child selector
zero-extends"*. **This is a third instance and it is in a different subsystem**, which makes the
split a property of the encoding scheme's consumers rather than of one file's helpers. Registered as

## 2026-09-13 - the conversion is the guard's first instruction (ASTRA-CONTRA-OPUS-OLD-SAVE-CONVERSION)

Static only; nothing executed. **Confirmed independently; nothing of mine to propagate.**

### Both facts, re-derived

```
00233C10  sub  rsp, 0x28
00233C14  call 0x235AF0          <- the compatibility prelude, FIRST
00233C19  mov  rax, [02EBF190]   <- only now is the block pointer read
```

The conversion is not a step the guard reaches; **it is the guard's first instruction**, before any
pointer or stamp is touched.

```
002EF4A0  lea rcx, [rip] -> 021B290C      ; destination, a LITERAL
002EF4A7  mov edx, 0xC0
002EF4AC  lea rax, [rip] -> 02166480      ; source, a LITERAL
          8 x movups per iteration = 0x80 bytes, 0xC0 times = 0x6000
```

**`0xC0 x 0x80 = 0x6000`, not `0x80`** - and the helper takes **no arguments at all**: 103 bytes,
both addresses rip-relative literals, so it cannot be reused for another buffer pair. The
battle-state field map already records the fixed-address half.

### Consumers: clean, and that is the result

- `V-12` in `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` - **already corrected by FABLE**, with the withdrawn prediction
  struck through and the correction leading. Struck-through text is the right shape: the dead
  version stays readable and is visibly dead.
- `CONTRACT-save-image-buffers.md` - **mentions none of** `00233C10`, `00235AF0`, `002EF4A0`,
  "conversion" or "2018". The assumption never reached my contract.
- `derived-call-signatures.tsv` - does not list `002EF4A0`. **Not hand-edited**: it is a generated
  artefact and a hand-added row would break its reproducibility, which is the property that makes
  it worth having.

**Nothing to propagate is the finding, not a shortfall.** ASTRA's routing assumed this claim had
spread into types and contracts; it had not, and saying so beats manufacturing an edit to look
thorough.

### With this, every contradiction filed against OPUS is closed

Eleven this session. **Four had already been corrected in their own page and left standing beneath
the stale claim** - `+0x698`, the capability polarity, the section-pointer formula, the gambit
failure paths - so the fix was structural rather than analytical: lead with the withdrawal, keep the
superseded text marked, separate what survives in it from what does not.

## 2026-09-13 - the two width checks were red for the same reason, and it is this session's pattern with a measurable cost (OPUS-WIDTH-ADJUDICATION)

Static only; nothing executed. With the contradiction queue empty, the next OPUS lane is structured
consistency. Two checkers were reporting one failure each; **both are the same defect and both are
now closed at the row rather than in the tool.**

| check | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `check_census_widths` | **1** row disagreeing with the census | **0** |
| `check_evidence_widths` | **1** row contradicting its own citation | **0** |
| `types_index --validate` | 0 errors | 0 errors |

### Both failures are one pattern: a wide store that tiles two narrow fields

**`BattleUnit +0x1A4`**, declared 4, census `{8: 2, 4: 1}`. The decisive site is the copy:

```
00304BF6  mov dword ptr [rbx+0x120], eax   ; <- source +0x24
00304BFF  mov dword ptr [rbx+0x124], eax   ; <- source +0x28
00304C0F  mov dword ptr [rbx+0x128], eax   ; <- source +0x2C
```

**Three consecutive 4-byte fields, filled individually.** The two qword accesses are *zeroing*
stores - `00304A83 mov qword ptr [rbx+0x124], r14` beside `00304A8E mov dword ptr [rbx+0x120],
r14d`, with `r14` the function's zero register - clearing two adjacent dwords in one instruction.
This corroborates the `+0x1A8` row's own note of a three-dword run, **from a different copy site**.

**`BattleUnit +0x6D8`** is the *source* of that same run and fails the same way: two qword writes
(`00310707`, `00310744`, both `rbp` = 0) spanning `+0x6D8` and `+0x6DC`, against two genuine 4-byte
accesses (`00304A99` write, `00304BFC` read).

> **A wide store that exactly tiles two adjacent declared fields is not width evidence for the
> first of them.** Neither checker can see that, which is why both carry a `WIDTH DELIBERATE`
> mechanism - the exception is stated in the row, listed rather than hidden. **I used it instead of
> changing either tool**: teaching the checker to infer this would move a judgement out of the
> record and into code, which is the opposite of what the mechanism exists for.

### Why `+0x6D8` was red at all, and this is the finding

That row **already carried** `WIDTH CORRECTED 8 -> 4, 2026-09-12`. But the cell still **led** with
*"2 of 2 observed accesses at this displacement are 8-byte; e.g. `00310707 mov qword ptr [rbx +
0x6d8], rbp`"*, and the citation checker reads the cell. **It was the only contradicted row in 629
checked, and it was contradicting a claim its own author had already withdrawn.**

> This is the same defect as four of today's eleven contradictions - **a correction appended beneath
> a stale claim that nobody withdrew** - and here it has a cost that can be counted. **It keeps an
> automated check red.** A check that stays red for a reason everyone has learned to ignore is worse
> than no check, because the next real failure arrives in a column people have stopped reading.

The row now leads with a 4-byte citation, keeps the superseded text **marked and preserved**, and
states the exception.

## 2026-09-13 - `repz ret` is a return, and 162 of my 1,471 blocks are not functions (OPUS-UC5)

Static only; nothing executed. Resolves `UC-5`, and corrects a figure this database has already
published.

### My own terminator set was incomplete

`repz ret` **is a return** - the AMD-preferred encoding, which this binary uses. The page's
terminator set listed `ret`, `jmp`, `int3`, `ud2`, `hlt` and not that. **Three blocks, 802 bytes,
were filed as "the predecessor did not return" when it plainly did.** With it included the control
rises from 99.13% to **99.16%** (33,953 of 34,240) and the open population falls to 170 blocks,
4,345 bytes.

### The adjudication

| predecessor ends with | block start | blocks | bytes | verdict |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| `DECODE-SHORT` | unreferenced | 131 | 3,628 | **truncation tail** |
| `pop` | unreferenced / aligned | 19 | 64 | **truncation tail** - epilogues, ~3 bytes each |
| `mov` / `cmp` / `add` | unreferenced | 12 | 92 | **fall-through continuation** |
| `call` | either | 7 | 548 | **ambiguous** |
| `mov` | **referenced** | 1 | 13 | **a real body** |

**162 blocks - 3,784 bytes - are not separate functions.** The largest group's own example settles
the character of the whole thing: `00121DB0+97` followed by a **one-byte block**. A recorded size
that falls mid-instruction leaves a tail, and the splitter counted the tail as a body.

### The correction to a published figure

> **The floor of 1,471 blocks is too high by about 162; the corrected figure is ~1,309.** The byte
> total moves by **1.5%** (3,784 of 244,619), so the classification in §1 stands and only the count
> changes.

Restated in a new block rather than edited silently into §5, because **1,471 has already been
quoted in commit messages** and a figure that changes without a visible reason is worse than one
that was wrong.

> **The instrument found its own defect in its own residue.** The 173 were set aside as "not
> resolved either way" precisely because they did not fit; going back to them turned up a missing
> terminator that had been quietly inflating the count. **A leftover pile is where an instrument's
> errors accumulate**, which is an argument for working them rather than carrying them.

`UC-5a` keeps the 7 `call` cases - each needs its callee checked for `noreturn` - and the question
of whether any of the 162 tails hides an entry the four-form reference union cannot see.

Static only; nothing executed. **No disposition changed.**

### Why this row and not another

`yebis-ppfx-source-map.md`'s PPFX family is **1,660 functions — 15% of the 11,219 A+B+C total**, the
largest single disposition in the database. Its selector is an **address span**, `006DA880` to
`007911E0` less 104, with direct evidence on **465 entries (28%)**; the other **1,195 ride on
contiguity**. `check_dispositions` accepts it, and correctly — the checker verifies **form**, not
justification. **If I own the mechanism I have to be willing to test its largest customer.**

### Three checks

**The arithmetic is exact.** 1,766 non-funclet census entries lie in the span; 1,660 are declared; 0
declared members fall outside it; 106 span entries are undeclared — which is precisely the 104
already dispositioned (8 A-measured, 96 generated families), one ICF-folded body, and `0071F970`.
**1,766 − 106 = 1,660, to the unit.**

**Nothing in the span is attributed FFXII code.** Of 1,660 members, **zero** carry any `owner` and
**zero** carry an FFXII-subsystem tag.

**The boundary claim holds.** The row says callers are only the `006Cxxxx` integration client,
static initialisers and teardown thunks. All 559 outside callers checked: 426 at `0079xxxx`+, 6 in
the integration client, and 129 elsewhere — 70 static initialisers, 36 thunk/adapters, 15
teardown/destructors, 8 constructor-vtable installs and one already-excluded PPFX body. **All inside
the permitted kinds.**

> **The 129 were my instrument's fault, not the row's.** I bucketed by **address** while the row's
> claim is about **kinds**, and static initialisers and teardown thunks live anywhere in the image.
> The first run looked like a boundary violation and was a category error in the test. Same shape as
> the `movzx`-without-its-successor and the `cmp`-in-a-`sub`-chain: **the check has to be built in
> the claim's own terms, not in whichever terms are easy to compute.**

### What the audit cannot do, said plainly

> It establishes that the span contains **no FFXII engine code** and that the boundary claim
> survives an independent check. It does **not** establish that each of the 1,195 contiguity-only
> members is individually PPFX. **A passing negative control is not positive proof of membership**,
> and no quantity of "nothing wrong found" converts into one.

Limits of the audit itself, recorded on the page: caller kinds came from classifier tags rather than
from each body, and the eight vtable-install callers were sampled. **The row is accepted on this
evidence and stays open to a positive-membership challenge** — the right standing for an
address-span disposition.

The PPFX audit tested one family. The property worth testing is the **class**: does any accepted

**`owner` is a call-graph subsystem attribution, not an authorship claim.** An audio codec
statically linked into the audio subsystem is owned by Audio *and* is third-party code. Bullet's
constraint solver is owned by RNG because it calls the shared generator. Both facts hold at once,
and the C disposition - *not this game's code, upstream named* - is untouched by either.

> **My PPFX audit presented "0 of 1,660 carry an owner" as evidence the span was correctly
> bounded. It is not.** It passes there because the post-effect region is one the classifier never
> attributed to a subsystem - and it would **fail** for a correctly-dispositioned library that
> happens to sit inside a subsystem's call graph, which is exactly what the eight rows above are.
>
> **A test that a correct answer fails and an incorrect answer can pass is not a discriminator.** I
> ran it, it returned zero, and I reported the zero as if it meant something about PPFX. It meant
> something about the address region.

The PPFX note is corrected in place. **What survives there is the arithmetic reconciliation to the
unit and the inbound-caller check by kind** - the two that were built in the row's own terms.

> That makes **five** times today an instrument was weaker than the claim I hung on it, and the

scores low. Measured over all 91 families:

Of the undeclared entries inside library spans, most are **A-measured** - individually explained by

declared by a family and measured as A, so those entries are *supposed* to be outside the row.

## 2026-09-13 - a constant pool 0.18% of the census touches (OPUS-UC3-POOL)

Static only; nothing executed.

UC-3 strengthened, not closed.

The libvpx attribution for the 66 head-of-.text blocks was tier 2 - a version banner and a
neighbourhood of media-transform tags. A shared-provenance test now sits behind it. Hand-written
SIMD reads its constants from a pool, so if the 66 blocks and libvpx's own kernels read the same
pool, that is shared provenance. The 66 blocks read 03000000 (1,020 references) and 01CD0000; the
ten LibVPX-tagged listed bodies in the same window read the same two pages.

The wrong comparison first: I compared the blocks against vp8_init, vp8_destroy, vp8_peek_si,
vp8_decode and vp8_get_frame, and got zero shared pages - which reads as "not libvpx". Those are C
control code and read structures and globals; the blocks are SIMD kernels and read constant
vectors. Two halves of one library that would never share a pool. The comparison that means
something is against libvpx's own kernels, which are listed and tagged, and there the pools match.

The false-positive control: a shared pool proves nothing if everything shares it. Only 63 of
34,270 listed bodies - 0.18% - read into 03000000. Of those, 8 are LibVPX-tagged, 4 sit at
0017xxxx where the named vp8_* bodies live, 51 are unowned bodies inside the head window itself,
and 8 are elsewhere.

Strengthened, not promoted to tier 1. The non-circular core is twelve independently attributed
bodies sharing a pool with the 66 that only 0.18% of the census touches. The circularity is stated
rather than buried: 51 of the 63 readers are themselves unowned bodies in the head window - the
population under question - so counting them as corroboration would be assuming the answer, and
they are excluded from the argument.

Still not established: that any individual block is a named libvpx routine. The pool says the 66
belong to whatever reads 03000000; the banner and the tags say that is libvpx; no block has been
matched to a routine.

That is the sixth time today a test was first built in the wrong terms, and the first time I
caught it by asking what the comparison population should be before believing the answer.

check_links and check_questions pass. Nothing executed. Not completion.

puppet_setcharclipone`). Neither changes family, so the corrected census is identical either way —

**2. §4's correction was predicted, and the prediction was two numbers wrong.** When queuing this

Both are now measured. **A predicted correction is not a measured one**, and a prediction sitting in
