## OPUS — UC-1 built, and not applied 2026-09-13

The denominator vote closed **3-0**: FABLE, OPUS and ASTRA all chose option (1) — admit the distinct
unlisted shipping bodies into the measured population as **unexplained frontier**, with a dated
population change and a recorded series break, never as a **D** exception. ASTRA's vote arrived with
one binding condition: *"Do not hardcode 1309 as a proved body count or strict lower bound. Use the
actual admitted, deduplicated body rows for N."*

`unlisted_admissions.py` is that mechanism. It adjudicates all 1,471 blocks **row by row with its
evidence** into [`unlisted-body-admissions.tsv`](../99-Unresolved-Residual/Unlisted-Code/unlisted-body-admissions.tsv):
**1,302 `body`** (240,287 B), **162 `continuation`** (3,784 B), **7 `ambiguous`** (548 B). It
reproduces the UC-5 table exactly, and it finally decomposes the `~1,309`: **1,302 clear + 7
ambiguous**, which is *why* the figure has to be a range.

### The denominator did not move, and that is the finding

Before applying a population change I asked whether a splitter block is **function-shaped**: does a
linear decode run from the first byte to the last? **The 34,270 listed bodies are the control**,
banded by size because a longer range has more chance of holding an embedded jump table.

| size band | listed | admitted |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1–64 B | **100.0 %** | 79.2 % |
| 64–256 B | **99.8 %** | 40.6 % |
| 256 B–1 KiB | **98.7 %** | 22.0 % |
| 1–4 KiB | **97.7 %** | 39.1 % |
| 4 KiB+ | **92.6 %** | 44.4 % |

**Size is not the explanation** — the gap is widest where listed bodies are essentially perfect. And
this is not a claim that the region is data: `001505C0` opens `push rbp` / `mov rbp, rsp`, and the
head-of-`.text` blocks are dense SSE with REX prefixes. **The bytes are code; the boundaries are
not.** A block count is therefore not a body count, and admitting 1,302 blocks as 1,302 bodies would
be an unsupported bulk disposition — **mine**. `35,572 .. 35,579` is where the denominator *would*
land; nothing downstream reads these rows and no published figure changed.

Routed to `SWE2-FRONTIER` as `OPUS-REQ-SWE2-FRONTIER-UNLISTED-ENTRIES`, with the control it has to
beat stated in the request. `OPUS-UC1-POPULATION-CHANGE` is BLOCKED on it rather than closed.

### A test run and thrown away, and two things it left behind

The first explanation tried was **off-by-one starts**: retry the decode at `start+1 … +15`. It
"rescued" 37 of 424 failing blocks, which looked like a result — until the control rescued **400 of
400** listed bodies whose start had been deliberately corrupted by one byte. *"Some shift decodes"*
is a property of almost any byte range. **The control is the only reason that did not become a
published finding.**

It did leave two things. The **7 ambiguous blocks are now individually named** — `0020FAD4`,
`007E3CC5`, `0081C290`, `00829E85`, `0082A657`, `0082CE48`, `0082E041` — where UC-5 had only an
aggregate; five follow a callee that contains **no `ret` at all** (positive `noreturn` evidence,
which collapses the fall-through argument), and two follow `__report_rangecheckfailure`, which does
contain a `ret`. **That second case is inconclusive, not a refutation:** MSVC's range-check helper is
`noreturn` by contract and its `ret` may be unreachable. None of the seven is resolved to a body,
because the same boundary problem applies to them — `0082CE48`'s 203 bytes decode to **zero**
instructions.

And `progress.py` stopped printing `at least 1471 blocks`, a figure its own page had retired: UC-5
adjudicated 162 of them as continuations, so it now prints **about 1,309** with the reason pinned
beside it. The byte total is untouched — 3,784 of 244,619 is 1.5 %.

## OPUS — EXP-081's live bindings reviewed, and one page loses a record 2026-09-13

`ASTRA-REQ-OPUS-LIVE-BU-BINDING-REVIEW`. ASTRA asked for a primary challenge of its live captures,
not agreement. Every binding conclusion holds, and **the static installer explains why each one is
what ASTRA measured** — two independent routes, agreeing.

### `+0x698 == +0x6A0 + 0x80`, on one arm only

```asm
0023A776  call 0x236100          ; SpawnKeep_ResolvePrimaryEntry
0023A77B  mov  rbp, rax          ; rbp = the entry
0023A787  sub  rax, -0x80        ; = ADD 0x80  <-- a reader scanning for `add` misses this
0023A795  mov  [rsp+0x90], rax
...
0023AA15  mov  r15, [rsp+0x90]
0023ABFA  mov  [rdi+0x698], r15  ; entry + 0x80
0023AC01  mov  [rdi+0x6a0], rbp  ; the entry itself, seven bytes later
```

ASTRA measured `698 = 6A0 + 0x80` in **three live kind-1 units** (primary keep entries 0/1/3).
**The invariant is arm-specific and the row now says so**: on the kind-0 arm `+0x6A0` is NULL and
`+0x698` comes from the global array, so nothing may compute either field from the other without
knowing the kind.

### Why a party unit's `+0x6A0` is null — the apply installs the null

`0023AAB1 xor ebp, ebp` heads the kind-0 arm; both arms merge at `0023ABCA`; the shared store then
writes that zero. **So a null `+0x6A0` is the ordinary party state, not a failed install** — which is
what the null-test before every use is for. ASTRA saw exactly this (party slot 0: `+0x6A0` and
`+0xE68` null, `+0x698` bound). On the same arm `+0x698` is `*(02EBF190) + 8 + slot*0x1C8`, which for
slot 0 is `base+8` — the value ASTRA read. **Consumers: `+0x698` is bound on both arms, `+0x6A0` on
one. Testing `+0x6A0` to decide whether stats exist is wrong.**

### The third item cost `authored-data-table-registry.md` a record

ASTRA asked me to correct a stale parenthetical. The correction is larger than the parenthetical:
**slot 49's 456-byte records are runtime stats, not authored rows**, and that page is the
authored-data registry, so the framing *is* the claim.

```asm
BattleStats_GetByBattleSlotIndex  00320A40   ; 33 bytes, the whole function
00320A40  cmp  cl, 0x27        ; 0..39
00320A4B  imul rcx, rax, 0x1C8
00320A52  mov  rax, [rip+0x2B9E737]   ; -> 02EBF190
00320A59  add  rax, 8
00320A5D  add  rax, rcx
```

Byte-for-byte the installer's kind-0 expression, behind an accessor **named for battle slots** with a
**40-slot bound**. That settles the page's own *"almost certainly units"* hedge — the population is
the 40 party battle slots — but in the direction that costs it the record. And the decisive
structural argument: on the kind-1 arm the same field binds `entry + 0x80`, which
`BattleStats_InitializeDefinitionRecord` `0023AC80` **memsets to zero over 0x1C8 bytes**. **An
authored table is not memset by its installer.**

### What I did not assert

ASTRA also reports an observed **128-byte header stride** for the authored party rows. I did not
re-derive it, so it is recorded **as ASTRA's observation** rather than as this page's claim. Also
noted rather than resolved: `02EBF190` carries more than this array — the party slot-id table is in
the same blob at `+0x5A5A`, stride 2. One base pointer, several regions; the registry slot names the
blob, not the array.

`types_index --validate`: 247 types, 1,856 fields, **0 errors**. `check_census_widths` **0
disagreements**; `check_consistency` clean.

## OPUS — the EFX source rebase, and the range it is actually correct over 2026-09-13

`ASTRA-REQ-OPUS-EFX-REBASE`. ASTRA asked for confirmation of three width claims from isolated
original-code execution. All three confirm, and re-deriving them from the shipping bodies produced a
**tighter bound than the one ASTRA reported** plus a second constraint nobody had stated.

New contract: [`CONTRACT-efx-source-rebase.md`](../02-Resource-And-Asset-Pipeline/CONTRACT-efx-source-rebase.md).

### The three claims, confirmed exactly

**`003AB7F0`'s full result survives except `unsigned(sext(low32(result))) <= 0x40`.** Confirmed to
the instruction: `003AB831 movsxd rcx, eax` makes the value **signed**, `003AB838 cmovbe` makes the
comparison **unsigned**, and the cmov's source is `rbx = 0`. The full 64-bit result is untouched
otherwise.

**`0036B130` uses the low-32 slot.** Confirmed — `mov eax, ecx` zero-extends, `and rax, 0xFFFFFFFC`
strips a 2-bit tag, `[rax+8]` loads a full 64-bit base. The handle addresses below 4 GiB by
construction.

**The caller sign-extends `+0x860`.** Confirmed at `003B34F5`. **And `+0x864` is sign-extended by the
very next instruction**, `003B3501`, which ASTRA's report did not name — it is the signed offset
added to the resolver's result to form the new base, so it is equally load-bearing.

### Object identity, by fingerprint rather than by offset

`003B3480` touches `+0x18`, `+0x38`, `+0x840`, `+0x848`, `+0x850`, `+0x858`, `+0x860`, `+0x864` on
one register. That is the `EfxCallerTemplate` layout declared earlier this session, so the rebase
writer is **identified by field fingerprint, not by a matching displacement** — the discipline that
the PPFX caller census cost me once already.

### The bound is 2 GiB, not 4

`0024D970` computes the delta as `edx - dword ptr [rcx+0x858]` — **a 32-bit subtraction reading a
field that the same function publishes as a `qword`**. Every repair walk then sign-extends it, and I
decoded all four rather than assuming from the easiest: `3A8FF0`, `3A9BA0`, `3A9860` each `movsxd`
directly, and `3AA3D0` applies nothing itself — it dispatches on a type byte at `+0x0E` and forwards
`edx` to `00501420` and `00503F10`, **both of which `movsxd`**.

> Since `low32(new) − low32(old) == low32(new − old)`, the repair is exact **iff the true delta fits
> a signed 32-bit range**. **ASTRA exercised 4 GiB and saw the base published high while the tables
> still referenced the old location** — at exactly 4 GiB the delta truncates to **zero**, so nothing
> moves, the most visible form of the failure. **But it begins at 2 GiB**, where the sign flips and
> pointers move by `delta − 2³²`. A 3 GiB move is already broken and looks less obviously so.

### A second 32-bit narrowing, independent of the first

`00503F10` repairs an **offset**, not a pointer: `20E600` out, add delta, `20E620` back, store 32
bits. The converters are not symmetric — `0020E600` zero-extends and adds the arena base as a
**`qword`**, while `0020E620` subtracts it as a **`dword`** and computes entirely in 32 bits. So the
round trip preserves `low32(offset + delta)` and nothing else, and **every offset-form pointer must
stay inside `[arenaBase, arenaBase + 4 GiB)`** or it wraps and later resolves to the wrong address
*inside* the arena — silently, with the delta perfectly correct. That is the registry page's **BW-2**
question turned from a curiosity about one instruction into a **correctness precondition**.

### One hazard characterised, not observed

`003AB7F0`'s guard reads 32 bits of a 64-bit pointer. Its intent is a null check — `[rax+8] == 0`
gives `0x40`, which `<= 0x40` rejects. But it also rejects a **valid** base whenever
`low32([rax+8]) == 0` or `>= 0xFFFFFFC0`, i.e. a block at or just below a 4 GiB boundary; the caller
then sees 0 and treats the source as absent. **No capture in evidence has hit it**, and it is
recorded as a hazard derived from the instructions rather than as a defect.

`types_index --validate`: 247 types, 1,856 fields, **0 errors**. `check_census_widths` 0,
`check_evidence_widths` 0 contradicted, `check_links` and `check_consistency` clean.

## OPUS — the resource-entry source is not freed, and the reason generalises 2026-09-13

`ASTRA-REQ-OPUS-RESOURCE-SOURCE-OWNERSHIP`. Verdict: **ACCEPT-WITH-NARROWING.** The two teardown
bodies are exactly as ASTRA describes and the no-free conclusion follows — but it follows
**conditionally**, and the condition is worth naming because it is the whole mechanism.

### What the bodies do

`003AB880` (42 B): tag test; untagged → `mov rax, rdx; ret`, **the input returned unchanged**;
tagged → tail-call `0036A000`.
`003AB940` (30 B): tag test; untagged → `ret`, **no call and no write**; tagged → tail-call
`0036D170`.

Both confirmed instruction by instruction. So *"the final call does not free the original source"* is
right — **for an untagged source.**

### The narrowing, and why it is not a quibble

**Untagged is not an incidental property of the input; it is the ownership discriminator.** Five
bodies share one prologue — `test cl,3`, `cmp ecx,0x100000`, `and rax,0xFFFFFFFC`, `[slot+8]` — so a
**handle** is a table-slot address carrying a 2-bit tag, and an **untagged** value is a raw pointer
the table knows nothing about. A raw heap pointer is untagged *by alignment*, automatically.

> **So the rule is not "this call happens not to free"; it is "the tag decides who owns the
> memory."** Tagged → the handle table owns it and the teardown releases it. Untagged → the caller
> owns it and the teardown is structurally unable to touch it. Stating it as a property of one call
> site would have under-sold it and left the next reader to re-derive it.

`00409FE0`'s mode selection is consistent with that: the resolved pointer is stored into the new
object at `0040A08F mov [rdi+0x38], r14` on the **mode-1** arm only (`r8d = 1` at `0040A089`), while
the mode-0 arm (`xor r8d, r8d` at `0040A065`) stores nothing. **Mode 0 does not retain the source.**

**What I did not verify:** that every shipped mode-0 caller passes an untagged value. Whether a value
is tagged is a runtime property, and this body does not constrain its callers — the premise rests on
ASTRA's eleven complete bodies, and is recorded as theirs. The narrowing is exactly this: the
conclusion is *"an untagged mode-0 source is not freed"*, not *"the final call never frees"*.

### A cross-request finding the ownership bodies produced

Comparing the five bodies that share the prologue answers a question left open in
`ASTRA-REQ-OPUS-EFX-REBASE` an hour earlier — *"`36B130` skips active/word checks"*:

**`0036A000` and `0036D170` both validate a generation** (`word [slot+6]` against `word [obj+0x1C]`,
and `0036D170` additionally tests `byte [obj+0x15] & 2`) before trusting the loaded pointer.
**`0036B130` — the resolver the EFX rebase depends on — does neither.** It loads `[slot+8]`, adds
`0x40`, and returns. A stale handle resolves to whatever the slot now points at, and the rebase's
own guard cannot catch it because that guard only rejects low-32 values `<= 0x40`.

Recorded on [`CONTRACT-efx-source-rebase.md`](../02-Resource-And-Asset-Pipeline/CONTRACT-efx-source-rebase.md)
as a property of the shipping code, **not as an observed failure**.

## OPUS — the EFX teardown, and the one bit that ties two requests together 2026-09-13

`ASTRA-REQ-OPUS-EFX-INPUT-LIFETIME`. Verdict **ACCEPT**, with one inference added that neither
request could reach alone.

### Every branch of the teardown, confirmed instruction by instruction

`003A9600` (156 B) and `003A9950` (156 B) are exact mirrors — `+0x870`/`0xA00` and
`+0x878`/`0x1800` respectively:

| ASTRA's claim | what the body does |
|---|---|
| first tests context `+3` mask `01` | `003A960D test byte [rax+3], 1` — **yes, it is the first test** |
| set → release chunk only if `+2` mask `04` **clear** | `003A9613 test byte [rax+2], 4` / `jne` skips to the clear |
| …and only if non-null | `003A9619`/`003A9620` |
| clears the chunk pointer **either way** | `003A9633 mov [rax+0x870], rdi` on both paths |
| clear → walks entries **from index 1** | `003A9643 mov ebx, 8` — 8-byte entries, so index 1 |
| …through **319** / **767** | `cmp rbx, 0xA00` → 320 slots, minus index 0 = **319**; `0x1800` → **767** |
| both branches tail-call the same helper on the table | `003A9688`–`003A9697`, reached from both |
| `003697F0` is 13 B, null-returns, else tail-calls `00369860` with EDX zero | **exact** |

**The exclusive claim is the one worth testing and it holds:** the mask-`04` exemption guards *only*
the `+0x870` release. The entry loop and the final table release are outside it, so the exemption
**must not** be generalised — exactly as ASTRA warned.

**Two precisions the summary compresses.** The set-branch **re-reads the global** at `003A962A`
after the release, so the pointer it clears comes from a fresh load, not a cached `rax`. And the
entry loop **re-reads the table base on every iteration** (`003A9650`) and again after every release
(`003A9668`). **A consumer must not cache the table base across a release** — the shipping code
does not.

### The bit that unifies this request with the rebase one

The teardown's context is the global at **`02F97340`**, and `003B3480` — the rebase driver reviewed
earlier today — **writes the `EfxCallerTemplate` into that exact global** (`003B34B2`, RIP-resolved;
all three references confirmed to the same address). So the teardown's "context" *is* an
`EfxCallerTemplate`, by write-site rather than by offset resemblance.

That makes one bit do two jobs, and both were verified separately before being joined:

> **`+0x002` bit 2 (`0x04`) means "this context is published/shared".**
>
> - `003B348A test byte [rcx+2], 4` / `je` — **`003B3480` publishes and rebases only when it is set.**
> - `003A9613 test byte [rax+2], 4` / `jne` — **the teardown skips the chunk release when it is set.**
>
> A shared context's chunk is not released by this path **because something else owns it** — the
> same bit that authorises publication withholds the free. That reads as deliberate, not as a leak.

**What is not claimed.** My own `+0x002` row says *every **reviewed** caller ORs `0x0C`*, which sets
this bit. **If that OR were universal the chunk release could never run**, which would make
`003A9625` dead code — and "universal" is precisely what a reviewed sample cannot establish. ASTRA's
own caution against *"exhaustive only-store/always-constructor claims from a RIP-only census"*
applies to my row too. **Recorded as a question with its test** — enumerate the writers of `+0x002`
by decoding bodies, not by scanning for a RIP displacement — rather than as a finding.

Also untouched, and left with ASTRA: the `800`/`A00` payload mutation and the
`EDX = low32(payload) + dword[02EBB738]` address formation; the EFB template's post-parse low-nibble
preservation; and the known type-1 template `002FC4A0`.

## OPUS — arena-7 EFX lifetime: one bit, three sites, one ownership rule 2026-09-13

`ASTRA-REQ-OPUS-ARENA7-EFX-LIFETIME`. **ACCEPT.** The copy/borrow claim is confirmed instruction by
instruction, and it completes a meaning that two earlier reviews had only half of.

### The branch, exactly as reported

```asm
003EE10A  mov  rax, [rip+0x2BA922F]      ; -> 02F97340, the published context
003EE117  test byte ptr [rax+2], 4
003EE11B  jne  0x3EE16A
003EE11D  mov  edx, 0xA                  ; CLEAR: allocate under logical source 8
003EE122  lea  ecx, [rdx-2]              ;        (ecx = 8, exactly as described)
003EE125  call 0x36C1D0
...
003EE171  mov  qword ptr [rax+0x870], r12   ; SET: store the caller's pointer directly
```

and its mirror at `003EE018` → `+0x878`, whose copy path allocates through `0036A100`, stores the
result at `003EE039`, and memcpys at `003EE064` with `rdx = r12`. **Both context loads resolve to
`02F97340`**, the same global the teardown reads — confirmed by resolving the RIP displacements, not
by assuming.

### What this completes

`+0x002` bit 2 now has one meaning that makes its three uses follow from each other:

| site | behaviour when the bit is **set** |
|---|---|
| `003EE117` / `003EE018` (parse) | **borrow** — store the caller's pointer instead of copying |
| `003A9613` (teardown) | **do not release** the chunk |
| `003B348A` (publish) | **publish and rebase** |

> **Set means "this context borrows its payload".** Then not freeing it is not an exemption to
> explain away — it is the only correct behaviour, and publishing a borrowed-and-rebased view is what
> the bit is *for*. Each of the three was verified on its own before being joined, which is what
> makes the unification worth something.

### A naming trap that manufactures a false contradiction

**`A00` is both a handler id and a table byte size in this subsystem.** `003EE069 mov r11d, 0xA00`
marks the site that uses chunk `+0x878`; teardown `003A9600` clears `+0x870` while walking a
**`0xA00`-byte** table. So *"A00 ↔ `+0x878`"* (ASTRA) and *"`0xA00` ↔ `+0x870`"* (my teardown review
an hour earlier) are **both right**. Recorded on the contract so the next reader does not open a
contradiction ticket against one of them.

### The width story turns out to be the subsystem's habit, not the rebase's quirk

The parser computes its **memcpy length** the same way the rebase computes its delta — a **32-bit
pointer difference**, `003EE111 sub ebx, r12d` / `sub ebx, 4`, rounded to 16 by the signed
`cdq; and edx,0xF; add; and ~0xF` idiom and then **`movsxd`** into `r8`.

> **A wrong delta repairs a pointer badly; a wrong length is a `memcpy` size.** The ±2 GiB bound
> established this morning is therefore a property of *how this subsystem derives every quantity*,
> not a quirk of one function. Also worth a consumer's attention: the length is rounded **down** to a
> multiple of 16, so a payload's trailing remainder is not copied by this call.

### Kept unresolved, as asked

The EXP-079 current flag, file and writer stay **unproven**; no live run and no native callee
execution is claimed. The `3EE2D0` fallback is unreviewed, the EFB lock language for `36C1D0` /
`36C140` is not adjudicated here, and the boot backing `01FD4A30` path (`3B0660`, `2FC860`,
`3B2310`, `32E620`, `32E870`) is accepted as ASTRA's reading rather than re-derived.

## OPUS — a resource key that stopped nobody, and the two rows that waited for it 2026-09-13

**Scope:** the `file:` resource keys on `_index/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` and `_index/AUDIT-LOG.md`; the
register rows `BQ-20` and `AC-8`; the AC-8 page side in
`16-UI/Text-And-Number-Rendering/numeric-formatting-and-character-mapping.md`.

| Document | Claim attacked | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| TEAM board, `DATA-FMT-PS2IMG-TAIL` | the two index files are held exclusively by this package | a write to either file by anyone else while the claim stood | OVERTURNED |
| `_index/_inbox/OPUS.md`, staged BQ-20 | "the page-side checkbox is already ticked" | the box | SURVIVED |
| `_index/_inbox/OPUS.md`, staged AC-8 | "the page-side checkbox is already ticked" | the box | OVERTURNED |
| `numeric-formatting-and-character-mapping.md` | `003FFC60` "yields the glyph metrics table from the resource handle" | the two places outside the answer that still said it | OVERTURNED |

**Overturned, first: the lock.** `team.py apply()` enforces resource overlap on the **claim** path
only — `require(t in ready(board, agent))` sits in the `claim` branch and there is no write path at
all. A `file:` key therefore refuses a *claim* and cannot refuse an *edit*. Under
`DATA-FMT-PS2IMG-TAIL` (claimed 2026-09-13T21:12:04Z), two commits edited `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`
anyway: `070920dd` (**OPUS, eleven minutes after the claim — mine**) and `02229841`
(`SWE2-CONTRACT`). In the same seven hours the owner wrote nothing: `started_at == updated_at`, all
three claimed index/inbox files clean in the working tree, and none of the six format sheets exists
on disk. Meanwhile FABLE's 296-row register ledger batch, FABLE's extent audit entry and my own two
rows were all withheld **for that lock**. It did not protect the file; it selected for the agents who
honoured it.

**Ruling.** `_index/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` and `_index/AUDIT-LOG.md` are **publish-window surfaces, not
claim-duration holdings**. Every publisher must touch them at the tail of every chain, and their
edits are row-disjoint (one row per question id) or append-only (the log), so they do not need
exclusion — they need discipline. A task's `resources` should name the pages it authors; the index
rows go in with its publishing commit. The keys are not to be claimed for a package's duration
again. `SWE2-DATA`'s six sheets, its README and its own inbox are untouched by this and are not in
dispute: `OPUS-CONTRA-DATA-INDEX-LOCK-SCOPE` asks it only to release the two index keys or
checkpoint what it is writing to them.

**Overturned, second: my own staged note.** Both staged rows said *"the page-side checkbox is
already ticked, so applying the register row will not move the metric."* True for BQ-20. **False for
AC-8** — its box was deliberately unticked, and the page said so in terms, instructing whoever
applied the row to tick the box in the same commit. Applying the row alone flipped
`check_questions --drift` from consistent to *"unticked boxes whose question the table calls

## OPUS — the self-contradiction gate was reading wrapped fragments as sentences 2026-09-13

**Scope:** `Database/Tools/analysis-kit/gfz-scripts/check_self_contradiction.py`, and the two hits
it was standing on (`OPUS-CONTRA-SPAWN-0208EA28`, `OPUS-EVSTD-01F83530`).

| Document | Claim attacked | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spawn-placement-and-retirement.md` | the document asserts `0208EA28` is never written | the sentence the matched line belongs to | OVERTURNED (detector defect) |
| `_index/EVIDENCE-STANDARD.md` | the document writes `01F83530` | the grammar of the refuting line | OVERTURNED (detector defect) |
| the detector's four frame guards | they read the claim's sentence | a claim whose frame is on an adjacent line | OVERTURNED |
| the fix | precision bought without losing recall | a real contradiction, hard-wrapped, in the self-test | SURVIVED |

**Neither hit was a document error.** `spawn-placement-and-retirement.md` line 2057 is the middle of
*"The widget contract §5 **CLAIMED** `0208EA28` has no writer … The native initializer contradicts
that argument — and the contract has since agreed."* It reports a claim and refutes it.
`EVIDENCE-STANDARD.md` line 4189 reads *"compresses it **against** `01F83530` and stores the result
**in the object**"* — a read of `01F83530` and a store somewhere else, against a line-3401 absence
claim measured two independent ways.

**The root defect is that markdown hard-wraps prose and the guards were reading one physical line.**
`QUOTED`, `HISTORICAL`, `SCOPED` and `CONDITIONAL` were each written to read a *sentence*; each was
handed a fragment. Three of the six claims this pass newly suppresses prove it on their own: the
sentence *"`022D9138` is read and never written, and it gates the update — with it zero, `01EF93E8`
is never written"* appears in `AUDIT-LOG.md`, `COVERAGE.md` and `PROGRAM-STATE.md`, and the existing
`CONDITIONAL` guard already carries `with it (zero|unset|null)` for exactly this sentence — it simply
never saw it, because the wrap put those words on the next line. **The guard was right and blind.**

**Three changes, each narrowed by a measurement:**

1. **The frame guards read the sentence, joined across wrapping** — stopping at a blank line, a
   heading, a list item or a table row. **Invariant: the frame is never narrower than the physical
   line it replaced** (frame = line ∪ sentence). The first cut dropped that invariant and traded two
   false positives for four: a register table row is one line carrying a claim *and* its
   disposition, and narrowing to the sentence cut the disposition off, bringing back four
   `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` rows the 2026-09-08 pass had already dispositioned by hand. With the
   invariant, a claim can only be suppressed more, and **no new hit can appear**.
2. **`ATTRIBUTED`** — `claimed|asserted|argued|declared|according to` disqualifies an *absence*
   claim as someone else's. **It is deliberately kept out of `HISTORICAL`**, which `writers()` also
   consults: the first cut put it there and silenced 36 positive write lines corpus-wide, because a
   sentence like *"asserted **only** where a single function writes the whole set"* is a good write
   claim that merely contains the verb. An attribution verb disqualifies an absence claim and says
   nothing about a write claim.
3. **An address governed by a preposition is an operand, not a store target** — `against`, `from`,
   `out of`, `relative to`, `compared to`, `based on`, `derived from`, `versus`. This is the same
   guard as the existing READ-context check, in the other grammar.

**Blast radius, measured old-versus-new over 555 documents rather than asserted:** absence claims
surviving the guards 63 → 57, and write-line/address pairs 5,779 → 5,740. **All 39 suppressed write
lines were read individually and every one is a source operand** — "loads `1.0f` from `01CEBBA8`",
"reads its answer back out of `022D8F30`", "tests a member against `00320890`", "compresses it
against `01F83530`". Not one is a store to the address named. **All 6 suppressed claims were read
individually**: the two filed hits, the three `with it zero` copies above, and one register-scoped
claim about `r10` never escaping its function.

**The recall cost is stated rather than hidden.** A document that quotes an absence claim, *endorses*
it, and then contradicts it is now invisible to this check. That shape is not in the corpus; the
reporting shape is in it twice.

**The self-test grew from 2 cases to 5**, and the one that matters is the **control**: a genuine
contradiction whose absence claim is hard-wrapped exactly like the two false positives. It still
fires. Without it the other four would prove nothing — precision bought by blinding the check to
wrapped prose would look identical from the corpus result.

**Corpus result after the change: no document asserts that an address is never written and then
writes it.** That is a green reached by fixing the instrument's grammar, with every suppression
enumerated and read — not by relaxing what it looks for.

**Propagation:** none. No document changed.

**Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — my own CFG finding had the right conclusion and the wrong evidence 2026-09-13

**Scope:** the EC-7 C family "Control Flow Guard static-guard adapters" (145 declared) in
`24-Compiler-And-CRT-Runtime/Static-Initialization-And-Teardown/`, and Finding 3 of my own queued
`OPUS-REQ-SWE2-EC7-CFG-GUARD-SELECTOR`.

| Document | Claim attacked | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| my Finding 3 | "Control Flow Guard is not enabled in this binary and has no function table in it", therefore the family name is unsupported | what `GuardCFCheckFunctionPointer` actually points at | OVERTURNED |
| my Finding 3 | guard flags `00000100` evidence CFG's absence | what bit `0x100` means | OVERTURNED |
| the family name | these are Control Flow Guard adapters | the branch encoding in all 145 bodies | OVERTURNED (name still wrong, on other evidence) |
| my Finding 1 | the stated control admits 185 bodies, not the 145 declared | an independent byte scan of `.text` | SURVIVED |

**I filed that `0016D6A0` being a bare `ret` showed CFG was absent. `0016D6A0` IS the image's
registered CFG check function.** Read from the load-config directory: `GuardCFCheckFunctionPointer`
= `0x008C31C0`, and the qword at `0x008C31C0` is **`0x0016D6A0`**;
`GuardCFDispatchFunctionPointer` = `0x008C31C8` holding `0x00896270`, which is `FF E0`, `jmp rax`.
Those are the canonical MSVC stubs for an image built with CFG instrumentation but not enforcing it,
and `image-hardening-cfg-aslr-dep-and-stack-cookies.md` **already names both** `E` `_guard_check_icall_nop`
at `0016D6A0`, `__guard_check_icall_fptr` at `8C31C0`. I did not consult the page in this database
that had already answered the question.

**And the flags say the opposite of what I said they said.** Guard flags are `0x00000100`. I quoted
that as absence. `0x100` is **`GUARD_CF_INSTRUMENTED`** `E` the compiler *did* instrument this image.
What is clear is enforcement: `DllCharacteristics` `0x8120` with `IMAGE_DLLCHARACTERISTICS_GUARD_CF`
(`0x4000`) unset, `GuardCFFunctionTable` null, `GuardCFFunctionCount` 0, and
`GUARD_CF_FUNCTION_TABLE_PRESENT` (`0x400`) clear. **Instrumented, not enforced** `E` which is a
different statement from "CFG is not in this binary", and the one I should have made.

**The name is still wrong, and now there is a real discriminator for it.** Every one of the 145
declared bodies was decoded: all 145 are `48 8D 0D disp32` (`lea rcx,[a static]`) followed by
**`E9 rel32`** `E` a *direct* branch to `0016D6A0`. **Not one uses `FF /25` through
`__guard_check_icall_fptr`.** CFG instrumentation cannot branch directly to the check stub: the whole
mechanism depends on the loader rewriting the `__guard_check_icall_fptr` slot when the guard is
enforced, and a direct `E9` to the nop's address is unpatchable. **A direct branch to
`_guard_check_icall_nop` is therefore not a guard check.** The shared target is identical-code
folding `E` the adapter tail-jumps to a destructor body that is a single `ret`, and the linker merged
that body with the guard nop because both are the same one instruction. The supported reading of the
family is the owning page's own subject: **a per-object teardown wrapper for a static whose
destructor is empty**, the empty body folded onto one shared `ret`. What these are *not* is settled;
what they are is the reading the form and the `atexit` registration support.

**Finding 1 reproduced independently.** A byte scan of `.text` for `48 8D 0D ?? ?? ?? ?? E9 ?? ?? ??
??` whose branch resolves to `0016D6A0` finds **185 sites, every one a census function entry**, none
interior or unlisted. Declared 145, **0 declared members outside the form**, 40 matching and
undeclared. The stated control does not reproduce the declared membership, which is the defect worth
fixing: a reader re-running it gets 185.

**Nothing declared is wrong.** All 145 members are genuine `atexit`-registered teardowns. This
entry corrects **my** evidence and the family's **name**, not any member.

**Propagation:** routed to `SWE2-EC7` as `OPUS-REQ-SWE2-EC7-CFG-FAMILY-RENAME-AND-REGEN`, carrying
the corrected evidence, the 40 undeclared addresses, the rename, the restated control and the
dangling "see the note below" that points at nothing.

**Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — three of the six hottest unexplained globals were memmove and two critical sections 2026-09-13

**Scope:** `Database/Tools/analysis-kit/gfz-scripts/globals_index.py` and the artifact it generates,
`_index/UNEXPLAINED-GLOBALS.md`. The generated file was regenerated, not edited.

| Document | Claim attacked | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `UNEXPLAINED-GLOBALS.md` | the ranked table lists globals nothing explains | the PE import directory | OVERTURNED for 508 rows |
| `UNEXPLAINED-GLOBALS.md` ranks 1 and 4 | two separate hot globals | the qword stored at each | OVERTURNED (one object) |
| every row's reference count | the counts themselves | an independent instrument | SURVIVED |

**Not one row was wrong, and the ranking still invited the wrong reading.** Four of the forty
hottest "unexplained" globals were named Windows imports: `008C2A40` is
`VCRUNTIME140.dll!memmove` (169 readers, rank 3), `008C20C0` `KERNEL32.dll!LeaveCriticalSection`
(136, rank 5), `008C20B8` `KERNEL32.dll!EnterCriticalSection` (134, rank 6), `008C2DA8`
`api-ms-win-crt-runtime-l1-1-0.dll!_invalid_parameter_noinfo_noreturn` (79, rank 38). **Their `0`
in the writers column is not a mystery to solve: the loader writes them.** Parsed from the import
directory: 30 DLLs, 538 named slots, IAT data directory `008C2000`–`008C31C0`. **508 of them carry
references and no citation**, so they were being ranked as FFXII state a reconstruction must
discover, when they are named external functions resolvable without reading one FFXII instruction.

**Ranks 1 and 4 were one object.** `01F2CDB8` is `01F2CDA0 + 0x18`, and the qword at `01F2CDB8`
**is** `01F2CDA0`; the qword at `01F2CDA0` is its own address. That is a container sentinel whose
root field points back at itself `E` the empty-tree initialisation `E` read twice by a reference
count, once as the object and once as the field.

**The fix is in the generator, and it is mechanical rather than a list of addresses.** IAT slots are
resolved from the PE and held out of the ranking; the same-object marker is derived by reading the
file-backed qword at each ranked address and asking whether it holds another ranked address or its
own. Nothing is hard-coded, so both stay correct as the corpus moves.

**THE DENOMINATOR IS NOT ALLOWED TO GET BETTER FROM THIS.** Naming four imports does not explain
four globals of FFXII state; it removes four rows that were never FFXII state. The artifact now
prints the held-out count in its summary table and lists all 508 in full below the ranking, so the
change is visible rather than silent, and the callout says in terms that removing a row that was
never frontier is not progress on the frontier.

**The blind-spot callout stays exactly as strong.** The `0` writers column remains dangerous for
precisely these two rows: a sentinel's fields are written constantly through `rcx` after a `lea`,
which a RIP-relative scan cannot see `E` which is what the existing callout already says, and what a
CONTRACT read past once before.

**Propagation:** none. No system document changed.

**Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — the category name was carried into the owner field, seven times 2026-09-14

**Scope:** the `owner_layer` frontmatter field on seven pages in categories 22, 23 and 24. No prose,
no addresses, no other field. Found by `check_layer_separation.py`, FINAL-AUDIT-PROTOCOL pass 12.

| Document | Claim attacked | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| seven pages' `owner_layer` | `Middleware_PhyreEngine` / `Compiler_CRT_Runtime` / `Third_Party_Libraries` are PrimaryOwners | the ledger's owner vocabulary | OVERTURNED |
| the replacement | these pages have no FFXII PrimaryOwner at all | an FFXII owner among the functions each page cites | SURVIVED |

**The rule, from `EVIDENCE-STANDARD`:** `CodeDomain` (V121) is what mechanism, library or runtime
behaviour a function implements, and **may describe middleware without granting any ownership**;
`PrimaryOwner` (V120) is which FFXII subsystem owns the state, resource or lifecycle transaction.
Middleware, the CRT and third-party libraries are the standard's own examples of the mechanism
layer, so they cannot be PrimaryOwners.

**The ledger settles it without argument.** Its owner vocabulary is 22 labels `E` `Audio`,
`Script_VM_Native_Bridge`, `Presentation`, `Input`, `Resource`, `UI`, `Movement`, `ActorEntity`,
`CombatFormula`, `CombatAction`, `WorldAreaField`, `Save_Load_Settings`, `Party`,
`CoreRuntimeScheduling`, `Items_Equipment_Shops_License`, `PlatformOnlineAchievements`,
`Spawn_Encounter_Lifecycle`, `CombatAI`, `Rewards_Progression_Economy`, `Status_Periodic_Terminal`,
`RNG_Random_Selection`, `Story_Event_Quest_Hunt`. **`Middleware_PhyreEngine`,
`Compiler_CRT_Runtime` and `Third_Party_Libraries` are not among them.** They are the names of
directories 22, 23 and 24 `E` the three categories whose directory name is itself a CodeDomain
concept. One slip, made three times, carried the category name into the owner field.

**The replacement was measured, not chosen.** For each of the seven, every address it cites was
joined to the ledger: **all seven cite functions that carry no PrimaryOwner at all** `E` 100 % for
six of them, and 32 of 34 for `the-fifteen-modules-registered-before-main.md`, whose only two
owned functions are `Input` and do not own the registration. There is no FFXII subsystem to name,
so each takes the form nine pages in this database already use: a `CodeDomain` with **`no
PrimaryOwner`** spelled out.

| page | now |
|---|---|
| `the-cluster-header-and-what-the-loader-rejects.md` | `CodeDomain:Phyre.AssetContainer; no PrimaryOwner` |
| `the-packed-namespace-and-the-file-side-schema.md` | `CodeDomain:Phyre.AssetContainer; no PrimaryOwner` |
| `the-post-process-passes-and-their-shader-constants.md` | `CodeDomain:Phyre.PostProcess; no PrimaryOwner` |
| `the-fifteen-modules-registered-before-main.md` | `CodeDomain:Phyre.SubsystemRegistration; no PrimaryOwner` |
| `the-return-value-adapter-family.md` | `CodeDomain:CompilerGenerated.Adapters; no PrimaryOwner` |
| `what-the-game-asks-windows-for.md` | `CodeDomain:CRT.RuntimeServices; no PrimaryOwner` |
| `the-lua-loader-and-what-it-accepts.md` | `CodeDomain:ThirdParty.Lua; no PrimaryOwner` |

**Pass 12's CONFLATION bucket is now 0 distinct, 0 uses.** The ledger half was already quiet and is
a regression detector rather than a discriminating check `E` 0 of 38,161 functions carry both layers
`E` so half two was the half that could fail, and it did.

**Two findings in the same gate are NOT closed by this and are not being quietly folded in.**
`INVENTED` stands at 2 distinct / 10 uses (`PrimaryOwner:Battle` x8, `PrimaryOwner:Debug` x2 `E` an
authority the ledger does not have, since it splits combat into `CombatAction`, `CombatFormula` and
`CombatAI`), and `SHORTHAND` at 13 distinct / 28 uses (`Script` for `Script_VM_Native_Bridge` and
the like `E` the subsystem is real, the spelling is not the ledger's). Filed as
`OPUS-LAYER-INVENTED-OWNERS` and `OPUS-LAYER-SHORTHAND-OWNERS`. A conflation is a layer error; an
invented owner and a misspelled one are different defects and are counted separately on purpose.

**Propagation:** none. Seven frontmatter fields; no claim on any page changed.

**Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — the render-pass registry contract, read off the bytes on both sides 2026-09-14

**Scope:** `02CBF998` and the two functions that maintain it, `005FDCB0` and `005DDD60`; the 60
teardown wrappers. **No page was written and nothing was declared** — this is the contract half,
verified; the page is its owner's.

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| node is `+0x00 const char *name`, `+0x08 node *next` | the two functions' actual loads and stores | SURVIVED |
| register returns 0, `0x11` on a null name, `0x12` on a duplicate | the three `ret` paths | SURVIVED |
| unregister rewrites the previous slot and nulls the removed node | the loop's compare and its two stores | SURVIVED |
| "60 of 60 named, no gaps" | an independent byte scan of `.text` | SURVIVED |
| the names cannot be read from the image | where the nodes sit against `.data`'s raw end | SURVIVED |

**Every element re-derived from the image rather than accepted.**

`005FDCB0` (register, 132 B): `mov r10,[rcx]` takes `name` from node `+0x00`; when it is null the
function returns via `lea eax,[r10+0x11]` — with `r10` zero, **`0x11`**. Otherwise it loads the head
from `02CBF998` and walks `+0x08`, running an inline byte-by-byte compare (`r8 = r10 - rax`, then
`[rax]` against `[rax+r8]`, the standard single-index two-string trick) and returning **`0x12`** on a
match. On no match: `mov [r11+8], rbx` — the new node's `next` takes the old head — then
`xor eax,eax` and `mov [02CBF998], r11`. **A front push, and the list is name-keyed with duplicates
refused.**

`005DDD60` (unregister, 79 B): `rax` = head, and `r8` = **the address of `02CBF998` itself**, so the
"previous slot" starts as the head variable and the head case needs no special path. `r9 = rcx + 8`
is the address of the caller's own `next` field; each iteration forms `rcx = rax ? rax+8 : 0` and
compares *addresses*, not values. On a hit: `mov rcx,[rax+8]` then `mov [r8],rcx` writes the
successor through the previous slot, and `mov [rax+8],r10` nulls the removed node. **The contract as
filed, confirmed instruction by instruction on both sides.**

**The population is exact.** A byte scan of `.text` for the 12-byte `lea rcx,[node]` + `E9` form
branching to `005DDD60` finds **60 wrappers leaing 60 distinct nodes** — no duplicates, no
sixty-first. That matches the 60 rows already in
`_index/candidates/render-pass-registry-teardowns-60.tsv`.

**And the awkward part of the recovery method is independently corroborated.** The 60 nodes span
`01F81220`—`02E5BF68`, and **all 60 lie past `.data`'s raw end at `01F7E400`**. So node `+0x00` has
no file image, each `name` is stored by its static constructor at run time, and reading the name out
of the image yields nothing — which is why the names had to come from the registration sites
instead, under the control that a site counts only if it names exactly one node. **The boundary used
here is the corrected one**; the same figure that
`99-Unresolved-Residual/Largest-Unclassified-Code/the-largest-unclassified-functions.md` carried
wrongly as `020793F0` until 2026-09-13.

**Still frontier, and still nobody's page.** All 60 are undeclared and uncited, and they sit in the
tail-call registration blind spot `EVIDENCE-STANDARD` 13ap describes — the same spelling that hid 36
bodies from the CFG family selector. Routed to `SWE2-FRONTIER` as
`OPUS-REQ-SWE2-FRONTIER-RENDER-PASS-REGISTRY-PAGE` with this contract attached, because naming
sixty PhyreEngine render passes on a Presentation page is producer work, not adjudication.

**Propagation:** none yet — the page is what will carry it.

**Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — a recording rule met once in thirty-five 2026-09-14

**Scope:** `_index/CALL-CHAINS.md` recording rule 5. No chain was moved and no chain document was
created.

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| rule 5 describes where cross-boundary chains live | the chains themselves | OVERTURNED |
| the chains are undocumented | the `Document` column of all 46 rows | SURVIVED (all documented) |
| obeying rule 5 is a filing move | what the 32 linked documents are | OVERTURNED (it is authoring) |

**Measured independently before deciding.** The Documented chains table holds **46** rows; parsing
the `Owners crossed` column on `→` gives **35** that cross an owner boundary. Of those, **1** lives in
an upstream `call-chains/` folder, **32** point at an ordinary subsystem page and **2** say *same
document*. The corpus contains **exactly one** `call-chains/` folder
(`03-World-Area-Field/Weather/call-chains`, one file). **A rule met once in thirty-five is not
governing anything**, and leaving it stated that way made the index describe a filing system that
does not exist.

**The decisive point is that the rule mis-modelled the unit, not just the adoption.** The 32 linked
things are **not chain documents** — they are sections of pages that explain the mechanism the chain
runs through. Obeying the old wording would not have moved 32 files; it would have meant **authoring
32 new documents and duplicating the explanation**, splitting each chain away from the mechanism
that makes it intelligible. Explaining a chain beside its mechanism is the better arrangement, and
the one conforming case shows where the folder genuinely belongs: field init → weather roll →
apply → Movement → LegacyPS2GS rebuild crosses four owners and belongs to no single page.

**So the rule now describes the corpus, and the purpose is carried explicitly rather than
dropped.** Rule 5 reads that a cross-boundary chain is documented where its mechanism is explained
and indexed here **with every owner it crosses named**, and that a chain belonging to no single page
gets its own `call-chains/` document. The old wording was reaching for findability from the upstream
side; this index is what delivers it, through the `Owners crossed` column, so naming every owner is
now the binding half of the rule.

**The cost of the decision is recorded on the rule itself, not buried here:** a reader on an
upstream subsystem page still does not see the chain unless they come to this index. That is a real
loss against the old rule's intent, and it is the price of not splitting 32 explanations away from
their mechanisms. **Restating a rule to match practice is legitimate only when the practice is the
better one and the shortfall is admitted; both are stated in the rule text.**

**Reported as ADOPTION and deliberately NOT as a defect:** the explicit `[OWNER TRANSITION]` /
trigger marking that rules 2 and 3 describe appears in **2 of the 41** linked documents. Only one of
the 41 is a chain document; the other 40 are subsystem pages the convention was never written for,
and the passes that would check it require reading prose rather than matching a marker. **39
documents are not 39 defects**, and neither pass was added to the mechanised table for that reason.

**Propagation:** none. One rule restated; no chain, page or link changed.

**Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — the 139 that hold L1 shut are three different problems 2026-09-14

**Scope:** the ledger residual list `Database/Tools/work/verify/residual_addrs.txt` and the L1 gate
condition `unresolved = 0`. No document changed; one candidates file added.

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `unresolved = 139` is current | newer exports of the same measurement | SURVIVED (three agree exactly) |
| the residual list is internally consistent | a listed body that already carries a CodeDomain tag | SURVIVED (0 of 139) |
| a second export's 158 is a second opinion | what its extra 19 actually carry | OVERTURNED (instrument error) |
| the 139 are one population | how deeply the corpus reads each one | OVERTURNED (three populations) |

**`unresolved = 0` is a hard gate for L1**, alongside every system documented and
`OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` empty, so these 139 bodies — 148,431 bytes, sizes 310 to 7,489, **every one
unnamed and every one unowned** — are not a metric. They are the gate.

**The number is stable, and I checked before assuming it was stale.** `progress.py` reads exports
dated 2026-09-03, which is eleven days old and worth refreshing as hygiene. But
`verify_GFZ_GN160` (09-07) and `verify_GFZ_PARENT` (09-07) produce the **identical set** of the same
139 addresses — not merely the same count. **Three independent exports over four days agree, so the
figure is corroborated rather than stale**, and no one should be told otherwise.

**A fourth export says 158, and it is wrong.** `verify_GFZ_HEADLESS` (09-07) lists the 139 plus 19.
All nineteen carry a `GFZ.V121.CodeDomain.Presentation.*` tag in the current census — `001E8070`, `001E8580`, `00245170`, `002455A0`, `00245E60`, `002AAE40`, `002B8EE0`, `002BCB00`,
`002DA2D0`, `002DA7C0`, `002DBDD0`, `002DC290`, `002DC7F0`, `00364530`, `003649A0`, `00366110`,
`00392A10`, `00392CE0`, `0053E0B0` — so they **are** classified and the headless run reports them
residual anyway. **158 is an instrument defect, not a harsher measurement**, and quoting it would
inflate the gate by nineteen bodies that are already closed. The control runs the other way too:
**0 of the canonical 139 carry a CodeDomain tag**, so that list is internally consistent.

**And the 139 are three different problems, which one number hides.** Every address each of the 139
occupies was matched against every citation in the corpus, with `_index/` and
`99-Unresolved-Residual/` excluded — those are where residuals are listed *because* they are
residual, and counting them scores every row alike:

| band | functions | bytes | what it means |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **BODY-READ** — cited at interior addresses | **30** | 38,478 | somebody has read inside the body; the reading may already exist in prose |
| **ENTRY-MENTION** — cited only at the entry | **65** | 76,830 | named on a page, not opened |
| **UNTOUCHED** — cited by no system page | **44** | 33,123 | genuine frontier |

The extreme case is `002AC5F0`, the largest unclassified function in the game at 7,489 bytes, with
**118 interior citations** across the spawn-record, UI-layout and text-rendering pages. A body read
that closely is not in the same state as `003BED70`, 1,720 bytes that no system page mentions at all.

> **THE BAND IS A PROXY AND DECIDES NOTHING.** An interior citation is evidence that somebody read
> the body; it is **not** proof that the body is explained — `progress.py` says exactly that of its
> own interior-citation measure, and 7,511 of the citations it counts are entry-only mentions.
> BODY-READ means *read the page before assuming this needs new research*. **It does not mean the
> function can be classified, and nothing here may be used to move `unresolved` without a
> classification justified against the page's actual content.**

## OPUS — UC-1 has an established floor, and the signal that would have set it higher is banned 2026-09-14

**Scope:** `OPUS-UC1-POPULATION-CHANGE`, blocked since 2026-09-13 by my own ruling. **No denominator
has moved in this commit either**, and none may move until this is independently reviewed.

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the `referenced` column is admissible evidence | which routes build it | OVERTURNED in part (route 1 is banned) |
| no unlisted block has an established boundary | a block three independent signals agree on | OVERTURNED (139 do) |
| the three-signal rule is arbitrary | how known-true bodies score on it | SURVIVED (88.3 % of 38,161) |
| the 139 are distinct new bodies | overlap with listed extents and each other | SURVIVED (four controls) |

**First, a defect in the mechanism I built.** `unlisted_admissions.py` computes `referenced` as the
union of three routes, and **route 1 is the PE exception directory** — every function that announces
its own range through unwind data. **`FINAL-AUDIT-PROTOCOL` pass 6 bans `.pdata` / `.xdata` / unwind
data as supporting evidence**, so any block admitted because `.pdata` announces it would be admitted
on banned evidence, and the published column does not say which route carried which row. Decomposed:
route 1 contributes 35,713 targets, route 2 (rel32 `call`/`jmp` and RIP-relative `lea` decoded out of
`.text`) 76,488, route 3 (base-relocation DIR64) 80,342. **Of the 143 `body` rows marked referenced,
exactly 1 is referenced only by `.pdata`.** The contamination is one row; **the mechanism is wrong
regardless**, and a union that silently folds a banned route into an admissible signal cannot be left
in a tool that feeds a denominator. Filed as `OPUS-REQ-SWE2-EC7-UNLISTED-REFERENCED-ROUTES`.

**Second, and this is the advance: 139 blocks do have an established boundary.** The rule was stated
before it was run and applied to all 1,302 alike — the start is referenced by route 2 or 3 (`.pdata`
excluded), the block decodes linearly from first byte to last, and the start is 16-byte aligned.
**139 blocks, 5,965 bytes, sizes 5 to 353**, satisfy all three.

**The rule is conservative, and the control is what says so.** Run over the **38,161 listed bodies**,
which are known-true: **88.9 %** are referenced by route 2 or 3, **94.0 %** are 16-byte aligned,
**88.3 %** satisfy both. So a block passing this rule carries the same entry signature that seven
listed bodies in eight carry. **And because 11.7 % of known-true bodies fail it, failing it is not
evidence of not being a body** — which is exactly why the other **1,163 blocks stay where my ruling
put them: the bytes are real code, the boundary is not established.**

**Four falsification controls, all passed:** none of the 139 starts inside a listed body; none equals
a listed entry, so all 139 are genuinely new; none overlaps another of the 139; all lie inside
`.text`.

**What this does to the population, stated as the range ASTRA required.** The denominator is not one
number and should never have been written as one:

| | bodies |
|---|---:|
| the list as it stands | 34,270 |
| **established floor** — + the 139 | **34,409** |
| ceiling if every admitted block is a body | 35,572 |
| ceiling including the 7 ambiguous | 35,579 |

**The floor moves the wrong way for every percentage, which is the point.** A larger denominator with
an unchanged numerator makes `engine_explained` **worse**, so this is not a number reached by
choosing the flattering subset — choosing the flattering subset would have been to admit nothing
and keep 34,270.

**I have not moved it.** A denominator change rewrites every figure this project reports, which is
the definition of a high-blast claim, and the 3-0 vote (FABLE, OPUS, ASTRA) authorised admitting
distinct bodies — not OPUS deciding alone which 139 qualify. Routed for independent review as
`OPUS-REQ-AUDITSPEC-UC1-ESTABLISHED-FLOOR`, with the rows in
`_index/candidates/uc1-established-floor-139.tsv` and both other voters notified.

**Propagation:** none until the review returns.

**Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — the chain runs six gates and the kit has sixty-five 2026-09-14

**Scope:** `check_coverage.py`, `check_denominators.py`, `globals_index.py`, and the two index
files they govern.

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the publishing gates cover the corpus | every `check_*.py` in the kit, run | OVERTURNED (6 of 65) |
| `COVERAGE.md` states what is on disk | a recount | OVERTURNED (346 claimed, 364 actual) |
| `check_coverage --fix` repairs it | a diff against a backup | OVERTURNED, then repaired |
| a stated local denominator satisfies `check_denominators` | the matcher | OVERTURNED (it could not) |

**The publishing chain runs six gates. The kit contains sixty-five.** Run over the whole corpus:
**37 green, 17 red, 1 crashing on its own argument parsing, 10 needing arguments the sweep could not
guess.** Nothing in the chain was failing — the chain simply was not asking. Full output in
`work/OPUS/gate_sweep_red.txt`; this entry repairs three of the seventeen and the rest are the work
ahead.

**`COVERAGE.md` had drifted by eighteen documents.** Claimed 346, actual 364, across five
categories: `00-Engine-Core-Runtime` 40 to 41, `01-Script-VM-Native-Bridge` 16 to 17, **`16-UI` 14 to
23**, **`17-Presentation-Rendering` 25 to 31**, `19-Save-Load-Settings` 12 to 13. Nine UI pages and
six Presentation pages had been added without the ledger moving.

**Its own `--fix` was the thing to fix first.** On 2026-09-13 I recorded that `--fix` matched a row
by category name without checking **which table** it was in: `COVERAGE.md` holds a
`Category | funcs | docs | debt` summary and the real `Category | Systems documented | Status`
table, and taking the first match once overwrote a summary row's **funcs** column, 572 to 25, while
leaving the real count untouched. It corrupted one number and fixed nothing; the other summary rows
survived only because their figures carry thousands separators the pattern could not match — an accident of formatting, not a guard. **Both the read and the rewrite are now anchored to the
span of the `Systems documented` table**, and `--fix` refuses outright when a category has no row
there (a status is a judgement, not a measurement) or when a key matches more than one row inside
the span. Run with the file backed up and diffed, as the defect note required: **the diff is exactly
five numbers, all inside the systems table, every description untouched, no summary row touched.**
`COVERAGE consistent: 364 documents across 28 categories`.

**And `check_denominators` reported a row that states its own denominator.**
`_index/UNEXPLAINED-GLOBALS.md` prints *"508 of 33,382 explained by nothing (1.52 %)"*, and
508/33,382 **is** 1.5218 %, the figure printed. The checker reconciled 1.52 % against the only KNOWN
population within tolerance, 34,270, which gives 1.4823 %, and then reported the document for not
naming a denominator **it never used**. The `N of D` escape accepted `D` only when `D` was that
reconciled population, so a document using a legitimate local denominator could never satisfy it
— and "fixing" the row to name 34,270 would have made the percentage wrong. **That is the failure
mode this whole project forbids: changing a true number to satisfy an instrument.**

**The rule now is that a local denominator which reproduces the printed figure is declared**, with
the numerator required to match as well. **It does not weaken the check** — a `D` that does not
reproduce the percentage is still refused, which is the entire discriminating power of the test — and it is the same defect class the file already carries a special case for, the table that
declares its denominator through its own `100 %` row. Self-test still passes; the corpus is clean.

**One row was also made self-declaring rather than left to be guessed at:** `globals_index.py` now
writes that denominator as `N of D` with its name, because the bare column number invited exactly
the wrong reconciliation.

**Propagation:** `COVERAGE.md` and `UNEXPLAINED-GLOBALS.md` regenerated or corrected; no system
document changed.

**Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — twelve documents were not describing a different executable 2026-09-14

**Scope:** `check_provenance.py`, `check_untouched_runs.py`, `check_coverage_cross.py`. Three of the
fifteen red gates. **No document changed.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 12 documents carry an EXE hash that is not the authorized binary | what those 12 actually carry | OVERTURNED (none carries one) |
| the frontier figure disagrees with the published figure | which of the two moved | OVERTURNED (the constant was stale) |
| the cross-tab marginals disagree | whether the delta closes | RECONCILED (+24 A, -24 frontier) |

**The loudest line in the provenance report was false.** `check_provenance` printed **"EXE HASH NOT
THE AUTHORIZED BINARY: 12"**, which reads as twelve documents describing a different build — a
physical-integrity failure of the first order. All twelve simply have **no `exe_sha256` field at
all**. The test was `d["exe"] != a.exe`, and `None != <hash>` is true. Counted across the corpus:
**358 documents state the authorized hash, 12 state nothing, and ZERO state a different one.**

**That distinction is the whole point of the check.** A document resting on another binary is
serious and its claims are in doubt; a document with no stamp has incomplete provenance, which is
the same class as a missing `gzf` and belongs *with* the re-verification debt rather than shouted
above it. The two are now reported separately, and the headline a reader sees is the true one:
**nothing in this database rests on an unauthorized binary.**

**The frontier "disagreement" was a stale constant, not a disagreement.**
`check_untouched_runs` refused with *"frontier disagrees with the published figure"* while
comparing a live 19,885 against a **hardcoded 19,909**; `check_coverage_cross` refused on a
hardcoded `A == 1410` against a live 1,434. Both controls are deliberately fatal, and both fired
exactly as designed — something had moved. **What moved reconciles exactly:**
`check_dispositions` reports population **34,270 unchanged**, declared B 749 + C 12,202 + D 0 =
**12,951 unchanged**, A **1,410 -> 1,434**, frontier **19,909 -> 19,885**. **A gained precisely the
24 the frontier lost, and A + B + C + D + frontier = 34,270 still closes.** Twenty-four bodies
earned an interior citation from a documented page, which is what A means and what this project is
for. The never-cited figure fell 14,560 -> 13,454 over the same period, the same direction.

> **The constants were updated because the delta reconciled, and the reason is recorded at each
> one. Had the marginals not closed, red was the answer** — a fatal control that gets bumped
> whenever it fires is not a control, and both of these keep their fatal behaviour.

**One red gate was never red.** `check_contract_runtime_links.py` takes the database as a
**positional** argument and reads `sys.argv[1]` at module scope, so any flag reaches `os.listdir`
and raises `FileNotFoundError: '--db\\_experiments'`. It exits **0** when called correctly. The
sweep harness now retries positionally before reporting a crash; the checker is not at fault and
neither is the corpus.

**What is left standing, and is real debt rather than an instrument fault:** **306 of 364 documents
owe re-verification against the current parent** (only 58 carry it), **130 carry no `gzf` stamp**,
130 no `snapshot_sha256`, 10 no audit block. `check_provenance` says in terms that these documents
are not wrong — their addresses still resolve against the live graph — and that the stamps must
be **re-verified, never rewritten**. Filed as `OPUS-PROVENANCE-REVERIFY-306`; stamping them without
re-verification is the exact move the tool forbids and would be the worst kind of green.

**Red gates: 15 -> 12.**

**Propagation:** none. Three instruments corrected; no document touched.

**Structural changes:** none.

`check_doc_claims` reads a claim one document makes *about another* — *"see [that page] for
`X`"* — and checks that the target contains `X`. Its own docstring records that its first real run
produced three hits and **all three were the test's fault**, in three different ways, because a
term-matcher is a claim about house style. It already reconciles `0x02EBF0C0` against `02EBF0C0` and

## OPUS — the gate the chain runs could not fail, and it was hiding one of my own over-claims 2026-09-14

**Scope:** `check_formats.py`'s `--quiet` exit code, and the `registry_slots:` frontmatter of two
documents. `registry_explained` falls from **63/63 to 62/63**.

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the chain's formats gate is green | what `--quiet` returns | OVERTURNED (it returns 0 always) |
| every registry slot has one owner | two documents declaring the same slot | OVERTURNED (two slots, twice each) |
| `02EBF168` is explained | what the declaring page says about it | OVERTURNED (it calls it a cross-reference) |
| `registry_explained` = 100 % | the above | OVERTURNED, and the figure is now lower and true |

**`--quiet` was returning 0 unconditionally.** The publishing chain runs
`check_formats.py --quiet`, and that path printed its one line for `progress.py` and returned
**before the verdict was computed**. So the only form of this gate anyone exercised **could not
fail** — and it had something to report the whole time. Quiet is an output format, not a verdict;
the line is still one line, and the exit code now says exactly what the full run says.

**What it was hiding: two registry slots claimed by two documents each.** `0x02EBF120` and
`0x02EBF150` were declared by both
`St2e-Carriers/how-the-ard-loader-binds-area-battle-data.md` and
`Unit-Definition/how-a-battle-unit-is-built-from-its-definition.md`. The second declaration is
**mine**, from `opus-how-a-battle-unit-is-built-pass-1` on 2026-09-12.

**The rule that settles it was written by the page that loses a slot to it.** On 2026-09-04 the
ard-loader sheet recorded, in full and against itself, that it had *"read MENTIONS as
DECLARATIONS"*, and set the standard it then applied to `0x02EBF168`: where a slot's **contents are
explained in more depth on another sheet**, *"the declaration belongs on that sheet"*, even though
this one establishes where the bytes come from. Applying that rule to the collisions, using each
page's own text:

- **`0x02EBF120` -> the unit-definition sheet.** It censuses the row: *"rows by low byte; words
  `+0x00`, `+0x22`, `+0x24`, `+0x50`, `+0x08`, `+0x1C`, `+0x32`-`+0x36`; bytes `+2`, `+3`, `+4`,
  `+5`, `+0x15`, `+0x22`, `+0x23`"*. The ard-loader sheet establishes the `.ard` directory index,
  the binding offset, the binding site and the consumer set — provenance, not contents. **The
  ard-loader sheet gives the slot up under its own rule.**
- **`0x02EBF150` -> the ard-loader sheet**, which keeps it. My page lists it under *"the sibling
  tables the enemy row cross-references"* and reads its `dword +4` as a count to compare against.
  **That is a consumer, not an owner.**
- **`0x02EBF168` -> nobody, and that is the honest answer.** My page files it in the same
  cross-reference row. The ard-loader sheet had already declined it deliberately, noting the gambit
  sheet reads those order sets as 32-bit offsets against `0x01F83530` and explains them in more
  depth. **Withdrawn, and the slot is unclaimed until a sheet establishes its contents.**

> **`registry_explained` was 63 of 63 and is now 62 of 63.** That is **a correction, not a
> regression**: nothing was lost and no work was undone. A slot that was counted as explained was
> only ever cross-referenced, by a page of mine, and the 100 % read as a completed dimension when it
> was not. **A dimension that reaches 100 % by counting a mention is worse than one that reads
> 98.41 % and means it.** `OVERALL` moves 54.44 % -> 54.55 % only because other measures moved in
> the same run; this change on its own moves the registry dimension **down**.

**Routed:** `OPUS-NOTICE-SWE2-DATA-EBF168-OWNER` asks whether the gambit sheet will take
`0x02EBF168`, since the ard-loader sheet's note says that if it is not taken there it should come
back rather than stay unclaimed.

**Red gates: 11 -> 10.**

**Propagation:** two frontmatter blocks; no prose claim changed on either page.

**Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — a packed word and its own byte view are not a stride error 2026-09-14

**Scope:** `check_layout_units.py`. **No document changed.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 2 suspect strides in the voice-pack page | what the overlapping lines say | OVERTURNED (both are declared views) |
| the check still catches the real thing | its self-test | SURVIVED |

The two hits were in `18-Audio/the-voice-pack-slots-and-the-voice-verbs.md`, on a 16-byte cue
entry:

```
  +0x08  u32   bits 0-23 offset of the cue's bank in the pack; bits 24-30 volume (clamped 0..0x7F); bit 31 pending
  +0x0B  u8    the volume byte, as the starter reads it (& 0x7F)
  +0x0C  u32   bits 0-23 the bank's byte size
  +0x0F  u8    pan (003E9D09)
```

**The `u8` at `+0x0B` IS bits 24-30 of the word at `+0x08`**, and the page says so on the line,
mask included. The checker's own docstring already grants that *"unions, bitfields, deliberately
overlapping views"* are legitimate and that every hit is a question — and it already carries an
exemption for the same case declared the other way round, a line reading *"covers `+0x14` and
`+0x18`"*, added 2026-09-08. **It simply could not see a packed word being declared by its bit
ranges.**

**The exemption is deliberately tight:** the wider line must **itself** enumerate bit positions,
and the overlapping field must be **strictly narrower**. Two equal-width fields at the same place,
or a wide field with no bit breakdown, still report — which is the actual failure this check
exists for, `PClassDescriptor`'s four intrusive lists at `+0x10`/`+0x12`/`+0x14`/`+0x16`, qword
**indices** transcribed as byte offsets when the real offsets are `+0x80`/`+0x90`/`+0xA0`/`+0xB0`.

**Narrow types are still not subjects of the check.** `WIDTH` deliberately omits `u8` and `u16` so
that a byte beside a byte is never flagged, and that omission is why the exemption could not
recognise a view: the view's width was unknown. A separate `NARROW` map serves the exemption only,
kept apart so widening it can never promote a narrow type into a subject.

**Self-test still fires: 2 hits on the index-as-offset block, 0 on the real layout.** A clean
corpus run from a checker that stopped working is worthless, which is why that control runs.

**Red gates: 10 -> 9.**

**Propagation:** none.

**Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — a control that compared an instrument against a frozen copy of itself 2026-09-14

**Scope:** `check_coverage_cross.py`'s fatal control. **No document changed.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the control detects a cross-tab measuring another population | where its three expected values come from | OVERTURNED |
| bumping the constants was the fix | how long the new values survived | OVERTURNED (hours) |
| the replacement is weaker | a negative control on each invariant | SURVIVED (all four fire) |

**I reconciled this control earlier today and I was treating the symptom.** It required
`len(pop) == 34270 and len(dec) == 12951 and len(a_set) == 1410`, and its note said a
cross-tabulation whose marginals do not reproduce the published figures *"is measuring some other
population"*. **But all three values are computed in this file, by `CD.load_functions`,
`CD.measure_a` and `CD.parse_families` — the same code path `check_dispositions` uses.** The test
compared `check_dispositions` against a frozen copy of itself. **It could never detect the case it
named**, because both sides agree by construction.

**What it actually detected was that the project had made progress.** `A` went **1,410 -> 1,434 ->
1,443 -> 1,444 inside a single day** of ordinary documentation work, and the control refused to
print its table every time. I bumped it to 1,434 this morning; it was stale again within the hour.
**A fatal control that goes red whenever the corpus moves teaches people to bump it on sight, and a
fatal control that is bumped on sight is decoration.**

**Replaced with invariants that hold however far the corpus moves and still fail on a real defect:**
every band must be a subset of the census population — a body counted in a band but absent from
the census *is* the "some other population" case, stated directly rather than inferred from a total
— and **A must be a subset of cited-anywhere**, because A *means* an interior citation from a
documented page, so an A body that no document cites is a contradiction inside the measurement.

**Negative-controlled, because an invariant that cannot fail is the thing being replaced.** Each
band was corrupted in turn: A outside the population fires, declared outside the population fires,
cited outside the population fires, an A body nothing cites fires, and the clean case passes.

**And the table it had been suppressing is now visible**, which is the point of the check
existing:

```
                                   declared       not     total
  A  cited INSIDE, DOCUMENTED             0      1444      1444
  entry-only, DOCUMENTED               3644      3956      7600
  cited, but neither of those           272      2489      2761
  NOT cited by any document            9035     13430     22465
  TOTAL                               12951     21319     34270
```

**22,465 bodies — 65.6 % of the census — are cited by no document at all**, and 9,035 of those
are covered only by a class declaration. That is the shape of the work left, and it was being
refused for a stale constant.

**`COVERAGE.md` drifted again in the same window** (364 -> 365, a new Presentation page) and was
re-fixed. Unlike the cross-tab, that one is a genuine hand-maintained count and re-running `--fix`
is the right answer; it belongs in the publishing chain rather than in a sweep.

**Red gates: 9, with two of today's earlier fixes having drifted back and been re-closed.**

**Propagation:** none.

**Structural changes:** none.

| the remaining 12 are real | the ledger's full name | SURVIVED |

**Twelve names were genuinely written short and are now complete** — 15 occurrences across ten
pages. `BattleStats_AdvanceLevelToTargetAndRecompute` **Growth**,
`BattleUnit_ActivateAppliedDefinition` **Runtime**, `BattleUnit_ApplyMovementIntent`
**ToWorldActor**, `InventoryBundleClass09` **_ApplyGilAndNestedItems**,
`Loot_FindOverlappingPickup` **Index**, `PartyConfiguration_SetSelectorsAndReconcile` **Roster**,
`PresentationEmbeddedRecord_ExecuteCommand` **StreamUntilThreshold**, `...ExecuteDeferred`
**CommandSubset**, `...UpdateCurrent` **State**, `RenderCommand_SubmitCurrentBufferA` **ndSwap**,
`Renderer_CreateRandomNoiseTexture` **FromGraphicsMT19937**, `SaveLoad_ControllerTransition`
**StateMachine**. Each replacement was anchored so that the short form inside the long one is never
rewritten.

**`__isa_available` is not a truncation and was left alone.** `CONTRACT-gameplay-generators.md`
reads *"MSVC CRT's `__isa_available`, written only by `__isa_available_init`"* — a **data symbol
and the function that writes it**, both named correctly in one sentence — and `PARITY-STATUS.md`
says the two paths are exercised *"by forcing `__isa_available`"*, which is a thing you do to a

truncated in the documents that truncate it; the exemption is now per file.

Seven of the thirteen sat in `_index/AUDIT-LOG.md` and `_index/_inbox/*`. **The log is append-only
by its own first rule** — correcting a name written there in September would rewrite the record the
log exists to preserve — and the inboxes are other agents' raw transcripts, which `COVERAGE.md`
explicitly does not count as documents. The population is now scoped the way
`check_self_contradiction` and `check_denominators` already scope themselves. **555 files scanned
rather than 589, and TRUNCATED is 0 on evidence rather than on exemption.**

`_Variant0/1`, `BattleLocomotion_` against twenty-six — these are family prefixes, and the checker

## OPUS — two widths that were right, and a contract punished for saying so 2026-09-14

**Scope:** two rows of `_types/fields.tsv`, and `check_contract_runtime.py`'s classification.

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 2 declared widths contradict their own cited instruction | what each row already says | OVERTURNED (both correct) |
| a contract cites an EXP record that does not exist, overstating its evidence | what the contract says beside the id | OVERTURNED (it says so itself) |

**Both width "contradictions" were rows that had already done the reasoning.**

`CharacterRenderRecord +0x0E0`, declared 8 against a cited `[4]`: the row argues the width **from
the write side** — 5 of 8 accesses are qword writes and there is **no dword write to either half
anywhere**, and the 4-byte citations are resolvers reading only the low dword (`003E6E73` and
`003E6EB1` passing it to `ImageAddress_ResolveRuntimePointer`). Two adjacent dwords would show dword
writes to both halves; none does.

`CharacterRenderRecord +0x438`, declared 4 against a cited `[8]`: the row names the single 8-byte
access and why it is not evidence — `0041FA86 mov qword ptr [rbx + 0x438], rax` in
`CharacterRenderRecord_ResetDefaults`, **zeroing `+0x438` and `+0x43C` together**, a two-field
initialisation.

**The kit already defines the form for exactly this, and neither row used it.**
`check_census_widths` and `check_evidence_widths` share one predicate: a `WIDTH DELIBERATE:` marker
followed by a reason. Both rows now carry it, with the reason each had already written. **This is
not an exemption granted to make a gate green** — the reason is required, it is the row's own
evidence, and a row that cannot give one still reports. What changed is that a judgement already
made and written down became one the instrument can read. **CONTRADICTED: 2 -> 0**, stated
exceptions 3 -> 5, and `check_census_widths` stays at 0 disagreements.

**And a contract was being reported for being honest.** `CONTRACT-resource-entry-tree.md` section 13
reads *"`EXP-083` (claimed, not yet written — no link until the record exists)"* — it names the
record it is waiting on, says it does not exist, and **deliberately refuses to link it** so no
reader mistakes it for evidence. The checker classed that as **OVERSTATED: "a false claim of
evidence"**, which is backwards.

> **Teaching authors that naming a pending record is punished while silence is not would make
> section 13 less truthful, not more.** A new **PENDING** class reports it visibly and does not fail
> the gate, and it becomes OVERSTATED the moment the disclaimer goes without the record arriving.
> A bare id with no disclaimer still fails, unchanged. This is the second distinction this checker
> has learned the same way — the first was that citing a record which does not name the contract
> back is a broken link, not a false claim.

**OVERSTATED: 1 -> 0. UNLINKED stays at 1 and is real:** `CONTRACT-binding-profiles.md` cites
`EXP-005` and `EXP-006`, both of which carry `contract: none — a harness-capability question`. The
two sides disagree about whether that evidence belongs to the contract. **That is a producer /
auditor disagreement about what an experiment validated, not a link to silently rewrite**, and the
records are ASTRA's. Routed as `OPUS-REQ-ASTRA-EXP005-006-CONTRACT-KEY`.

**Red gates: 8 -> 7.**

**Propagation:** two type rows; no document claim changed.

**Structural changes:** none.
