## OPUS — pass 1 cannot pass as written, and the confirmation it wants is recorded nowhere 2026-09-14

**Scope:** the 250 cited `.text` addresses that are not function entries, and what FINAL-AUDIT
pass 1 requires of them. **No document changed.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| pass 1 can be run as written | what its literal rule does to legitimate citations | OVERTURNED |
| the 93 flagged documents are a corpus defect | who cites each address and why | OVERTURNED for most |
| the confirmation is recorded somewhere | any registry, marker or convention | NOT FOUND |

**Pass 1 fails if a cited address "is not a function (or is cited as one and is data)".** Across 365
documents, **250 distinct cited addresses** sit inside `.text` but are neither a function entry nor
inside any listed body — by construction, each falls in the **gap between two listed functions**.
`verify_doc_addresses` flags them and says, correctly, that *"jump/PSM tables after a function are
legitimate — confirm in context"*.

**So the rule as written fails on documents doing exactly what they should.** A page documenting a
dispatch table cites the table, and the table lives in `.text` after the function that jumps through
it: `effect-element-type-dispatch.md` cites 16 such addresses, `the-license-board-grid-build-and-its-
change-sweep.md` 16, `battle-action-handler-table.md` 9. **A rule that a correct page cannot satisfy
is not a rule the audit can run thirty times.**

**Who cites them, which is what decides the question:**

| | addresses |
|---|---:|
| cited by an **ordinary system page** | **199** |
| only by a page whose subject IS unlisted code | 44 |
| only by an index or the append-only log | 7 |

The 44 are not a defect in any sense — `the-code-the-function-list-does-not-contain.md` cites code
the function list does not contain, which is its title. That is the same population UC-1 is
adjudicating, and the seed file shows the distinction immediately: `0012A50C` is `cc cc cc cc` at
**delta 0** from its predecessor's end (padding), while `0012AD00` is `48 63 d2 4d 63 c9` — two
`movsxd`s, real code, 2,036 bytes into the gap.

**The finding that matters is that the confirmation has nowhere to live.** The kit has exactly one
convention of this kind, `WIDTH DELIBERATE:`, and it works: a judgement written once becomes one the
instrument can read. Nothing equivalent exists here, so `verify_doc_addresses` asks for confirmation
"in context", the context is spread over 91 pages, **and nothing records the answer once given.**
The same 250 addresses are re-read at every audit, by every auditor, forever.

**Ruling: the confirmation belongs in one registry, not in 91 pages.** Annotating every citing page
would cost 91 edits across a dozen owners to record a fact about **addresses**, not about pages, and
would still leave a second page citing the same address unconfirmed. Seeded as
`_index/candidates/text-gap-citations-250.tsv`: one row per address with the preceding function and
its name, the distance from its end, the next function, whether that predecessor contains an
`FF /4` indirect `jmp` (the shape a jump-table user has — **a hint, not a verdict**), the first
bytes, and every page citing it.

> **Every row lands `UNCONFIRMED` and this pass confirms none of them.** The verdicts to be set are
> `TABLE`, `UNLISTED`, `PAD` or `DEFECT`, each with a reason. Seeding evidence is not the same as
> deciding, and a registry pre-filled with my guesses would be worse than no registry: the next
> reader would inherit them as findings.

Routed as `OPUS-REQ-SWE2-FRONTIER-TEXT-GAP-250`.

**Propagation:** none.

**Structural changes:** none.

**Scope:** the nine class-A rows of `_index/candidates/doc-claim-propagation-27.tsv`, each decided

|---|---|---|

| the 2 survivors are broken references | where the fact actually lives | CONFIRMED, with the real location |

**Seven are not claims about their target at all.** In each, the term is the **citing page's own
evidence** — an address column in a table row, or an instruction range it cites for its own reason
— sitting in the same sentence unit as a link that supports a different clause:

  **different cell**, supports *"the party-type band the kind-byte page measures"* — the bands

  `mspOffset`"* — the naming is attributed to an external tool, not to the linked page. It is also

**This is the limit `check_doc_claims` states about itself** — *"it only follows terms, not
propositions"* — and it is not worth patching further. Two earlier passes already sharpened it on
house style (33 -> 27) and on interior addresses and short numbers (27 -> 24); a rule that tried to
decide **which clause a link supports** would be guessing at grammar, and would start hiding the
real ones.

name the function, are decisions about what those pages are for. Routed as

## OPUS — the EC-7 span check only ran in one direction 2026-09-14

**Scope:** `check_family_spans.py`, and the largest C family in the corpus. **No document changed.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the 1,216-body SEAD family's note reproduces its membership | the span, recomputed from the census | OVERTURNED |
| 61 bodies inside declared spans are unexplained | what each of them actually is | OVERTURNED (40 are A) |
| the real gap is 61 | the three-way split | 11 |

**C carries 12,202 of the 14,395 explained bodies, so a C family's note IS the completion
standard** — and nothing was testing whether a note is true. `check_dispositions` verifies that a
declaration is well formed, counted correctly, made of real entries, free of duplicates and
non-overlapping. **Every one of those is structural.** It has refused families before (a duplicate
member, and twice for staleness against A on 2026-09-13), so the bar is not a dead canary — but
it cannot see a note that describes a different set than the members file holds.

**So I tested the biggest one.** The SEAD family's note is mechanical and therefore falsifiable:
*"every census entry in the link span from `007A4380` up to (not including) `007F41A0` less the
libogg framing object inside"*. Recomputed: the span holds 1,259 census entries, the family declares
1,216, and **the rule does not reproduce the membership**. `check_family_spans` already catches half
of that — 9 members sit **outside** the declared span, at `007F7360`-`007F7570` — and reports it
as triage.

**The other half was invisible, because the check only ran in one direction.** It asked whether the
MEMBERS obey the NOTE. It never asked whether the note's span is FULL. Inside SEAD's span, 52 census
entries are not members: 22 are the libogg exclusion the note states, **10 more belong to four other
families the note never mentions** (the thunk layer, libwebm mkvparser,
`NativeLeaf.MemberAddressAccessor`), and 20 belong to nothing at all. **This is the shape
`check_float_typed_as_int` names about itself: an empty half of a symmetric test is a result, and a
missing half is a blind spot.**

**The symmetric half is added, and the first thing it needed was to not manufacture alarm.** Raw,
it reports **61** bodies corpus-wide inside a declared span and claimed by no family — which reads
as 61 holes in the third-party inventory. It is not. `check_dispositions` **refuses** a member
already measured as A ("A beats a declaration"), and a generated selector excludes A-measured
entries by design, so most of a gap is **individually explained rather than missing**. Classified:

| | bodies |
|---|---:|
| **A-measured** — excluded from the family precisely because they are explained on their own | **40** |
| cited by a document but not A | 10 |
| **DARK** — inside a declared span, in no family, cited by no document at all | **11** |

**Eighteen of SEAD's twenty are A-measured, and its DARK count is zero.** The real residue is **11
bodies**, in six library families: `libwebm mkvparser` 6 (`007FFCD0`, `007FFD00`, `007FFD80`,
`007FFDA0`, `00800150`, `00808850`), `Bullet physics` 2 (`00834D40`, `008478A0`), and one each in
`libvorbis float codec` (`00887630`), `libvpx VP8 decoder` (`001744F0`) and `libvpx VP8 DSP kernels`
(`001274D0`).

> **Reporting 61 would have been the easier headline and it would have been false.** The number that
> survives classification is 11, and the difference is entirely bodies the framework excluded **on
> purpose** for a reason the framework already states.

**Routed** to `SWE2-EC7` as `OPUS-REQ-SWE2-EC7-SPAN-DARK-11`, with the SEAD note's understated
exclusions attached: it names only libogg while four other families carve out ten more.

**Propagation:** none.

**Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — CORRECTION: the SEAD family reproduces exactly, and nine of my eleven dark bodies are documented exclusions 2026-09-14

**Scope:** two claims I published earlier today, in
*"the EC-7 span check only ran in one direction"*. **Both are wrong, and this entry says how.**

| My claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the SEAD family's rule "does not reproduce the membership" | the selector, RUN | **OVERTURNED** |
| 11 DARK bodies are an EC-7 gap worth routing | each one, against its selector's output | **OVERTURNED for 9** |

**I tested a family's NOTE and reported the FAMILY.** The SEAD declaration's note says its members
are the span `007A4380`-`007F41A0` *"less the libogg framing object inside"*, and I showed that rule
yields 1,237 where the family declares 1,216 — then wrote that the rule does not reproduce its
membership. **The note is an abridgement. The selector is the rule**, and
`18-Audio/members/select_audio_libraries.py` states it in full: the span, less the libogg object,
less entries whose RTTI vtable appearances include a class outside `SQEX::Sd`, less entries already
A-measured or declared by another family, **plus nine SEAD entries past the span** (SoundObject
vtable bodies and installers, PolygonSound's SSE helpers), each asserted by RTTI or by its only
callers.

**Run, it reproduces to the entry:** 1,259 census entries in the span, 52 excluded — 18
A-measured, 2 RTTI-outside-class, 1 `NativeLeaf.MemberAddressAccessor`, 6 internal tail-call
forwarders, 3 libwebm `mkvparser`, 22 libogg — leaving 1,207, **plus the 9 past the span = 1,216**,
which is the declared count. **Every one of the 52 exclusions I found by hand is in the selector's
printed output, by address.** The nine members `check_family_spans` reports as "outside every
declared span" are the nine the selector documents; the span checker reads the note, and the note
does not mention them.

**And the dark eleven are mostly not dark.** I routed 11 bodies as "inside a declared span, in no
family, cited by no document". Run the selectors and 9 of them are **named exclusions with a stated
reason**: `mkvparser` prints *"excluded joined to the parser by nothing"* for `007FFCD0`,
`007FFD00`, `007FFD80`, `007FFDA0`, `00800150`, and *"called from outside client/registrar"* for
`008087C4`; Bullet prints *"RTTI not Bullet's (Phyre::VTS::ScreenStateFullScreenLoseFocus)"* for
`008478A0` and *"called only from outside Bullet and its client"* for `00834D40`; libvpx prints
*"also called from outside the decoder and its client"* for `001744F0`. **A body inside a library's
address span that the library's own selector excludes by name is not a gap — it is correctly
frontier.**

**What survives is two, not eleven:** `001274D0` (libvpx VP8 DSP kernels) and `00887630` (libvorbis
float codec) appear in neither their family's members file nor their selector's printed exclusions.
Those are worth a look; the other nine are not.

**The mistake is the same one twice in an hour, and it is worth naming.** With the residual 139 and
again with the raw 61, I split a count before reporting it and the real number was much smaller.
Here I reported 11 without first running the generator that the declaration itself names — the
very artefact that would answer the question. **A count is not a finding until the thing that
produced it has been asked.**

**What does survive from that entry, unchanged:** family **notes abridge their selectors**, and
every note-based instrument inherits the abridgement. `check_family_spans` is reading a summary and
reporting on a rule it cannot see. That is a real governance point — a note should either state the
rule completely or say that the selector is authoritative — and it is the half of yesterday's entry
that stands.

`OPUS-REQ-SWE2-EC7-SPAN-DARK-11` is amended to the two, with the nine explained so nobody re-derives
them. `check_family_spans`' new section now tells the reader to run the selector before treating a
dark row as a gap.

**Propagation:** none. No document or members file changed.

**Structural changes:** none.

path (after `check_contract_runtime_links` and again here), and it is the same shape as every
instrument defect I have been correcting all day: **the tool was fine and the caller was not.**

## OPUS — a third of the declared EC-7 surface rests on a rule nothing can re-check 2026-09-14

**Scope:** all 94 declared B/C/D families, classified by the strongest mechanical handle their note
offers, and the size-rule families verified. **No document changed.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the five size-rule families hold to their stated size | every member's census size | SURVIVED (no violations) |
| a size rule makes a family reproducible | how many bodies of that size exist | OVERTURNED (all five are subsets) |
| EC-7's declared surface is machine-checkable | the other 89 notes | OVERTURNED for 4,513 bodies |

**The declared surface is 12,951 bodies. Sorted by what its note actually gives a machine:**

| handle the note offers | rows | bodies |
|---|---:|---:|
| names a selector | 15 | 5,015 |
| exact body size | 4 | 2,790 |
| RTTI class or type name | 2 | 587 |
| vtable slot | 1 | 46 |
| **prose only, no mechanical handle** | **72** | **4,513** |

**So roughly a third of everything this database calls class-explained rests on a claim no
instrument can re-check.** That is not an accusation — a note like *"helpers with no discoverable
owner"* may be perfectly true and simply not mechanisable — but it is the honest size of the
reproducibility question, and it was not written down anywhere before.

**The size families were the largest checkable band nothing checked, and all five hold.** Every
member is exactly the stated size, with no exceptions: `PClassDescriptorForType` deleting
destructors 1,149 x 92 B, `PDataMemberMetadata` static teardowns 853 x 12 B, `PClassDescriptor`
static teardowns 404 x 26 B, `PClassDescriptorForType` destructor thunks 384 x 15 B, and the DF-1
owned-buffer reset adapters 46 x 59 B. **2,836 bodies, no member off its size.**

> **But a size rule is a constraint, not a selector, and the completeness side says so.** The census
> holds **1,261** 92-byte bodies against 1,149 declared, **1,520** 12-byte against 853, **964**
> 26-byte against 404, **543** 15-byte against 384, **138** 59-byte against 46. **Every one of the
> five declares a strict SUBSET of its size class**, so the condition that actually picks the
> members is the rest of the note — which is prose. Verifying the size proves **no member
> violates the rule**; it does not prove the membership follows from it.

**What is now verified, stated at the strength it deserves:**

- **407 bodies fully reproduced** — `df4` return-value adapters (403) and `bk6` sentry destructor
  clones (4) regenerated to scratch and byte-identical to their committed files.
- **1,216 bodies fully reproduced** — the SEAD family, every one of its 52 exclusions and its 9
  past-span additions printed by its own selector.
- **2,836 bodies size-consistent** — a necessary condition verified, the selecting condition not.

**Filed** as `OPUS-EC7-PROSE-ONLY-72`: the 72 rows carrying 4,513 bodies whose note offers nothing a
machine can hold onto. The question for each is not *"is it wrong"* — nothing here suggests any of
them is — but whether its rule can be stated so that it could be checked, the way fifteen families
already do with a selector.

## OPUS — CORRECTION: every EC-7 family states a mechanical rule, and the prose-only third was my regex 2026-09-14

**Scope:** withdrawing *"a third of the declared EC-7 surface rests on a rule nothing can
re-check"*, published earlier today, and the task filed on it.

| My claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 72 families / 4,513 bodies offer no mechanical handle | what those 72 notes actually say | **OVERTURNED** |
| the one remaining handle-less family is irreducibly prose | its 749 members, in the image | **OVERTURNED** |

**I classified 94 notes with a regex, ran it once, and published its output as a fact about the
corpus.** My size pattern required *"exactly N bytes"* or *"N-byte bodies"*. **The house form is
`"145 members, all 12 bytes, ONE byte image"`** — and *"all 12 bytes"* matched nothing I wrote. Nor
did *"ONE byte image"*, *"ONE form image"*, *"PROVED BY FORM"*, *"PROVED BY BYTES"*, or
*"CONTROL: 82 members, 82 DISTINCT targets"*, every one of which is a claim an instrument can hold
onto.

**Re-measured with the patterns the corpus actually uses:**

| handle the note offers | rows | bodies |
|---|---:|---:|
| names a selector | 15 | 5,015 |
| **byte or form image** | **76** | **7,024** |
| uniform body size | 1 | 46 |
| per-member evidence file | 1 | 117 |
| no mechanical handle | 1 | 749 |

**And the last one is not prose either.** *"Internal tail-call forwarders"* says *"its complete body
is one jmp"*. Read from the image: **all 749 members are exactly 5 bytes and all 749 begin with
`E9`** — `jmp rel32`, and nothing else. The claim is exact, uniform and verified.

> **So the honest figure is 94 of 94.** Every declared EC-7 family states a rule that can be
> checked, and my published *"a third of the surface cannot be re-checked"* was **an artefact of my
> own pattern list**. `OPUS-EC7-PROSE-ONLY-72` is closed as withdrawn rather than left to be worked.

**This is the fourth time today I have published a classifier's first output as a finding about the
corpus, and every one of the four was the instrument.** The residual 139 (three populations, not
one), the raw 61 unclaimed (40 were A-measured), the eleven dark bodies (nine were named exclusions
in their own selector), and now this. **I have spent the day correcting other people's instruments
for exactly this failure and reproducing it in my own at a steady rate.** The rule that would have
caught all four is the one the kit already applies to its checkers: **read the underlying text for a
sample before reporting a count, and state what the instrument cannot see.**

**What is verified, and at what strength:**

- **407 bodies** fully reproduced — `df4` and `bk6` regenerated byte-identically to scratch.
- **1,216 bodies** fully reproduced — SEAD, every exclusion and addition printed by its selector.
- **2,836 bodies** size-consistent — every member exactly the stated size, though each family is a
  strict subset of its size class, so the selecting condition is the rest of the note.
- **749 bodies** form-verified — all 5 bytes, all `E9`.

**5,208 bodies with a claim I have checked directly**, and no family left whose rule cannot in
principle be checked.

**Propagation:** `OPUS-EC7-PROSE-ONLY-72` withdrawn; nothing else depended on the figure.

**Structural changes:** none.

reads notes cannot see a selector's output, so DARK is the honest residue of the note test and the
section already tells the reader to run the selector first.

**`OPUS-REQ-SWE2-EC7-SPAN-DARK-2` is closed as withdrawn: it has no items.** Of the eleven bodies I
originally routed, nine were named in a selector and two in a note. **None of the eleven was ever a
gap.**

> **That is the fifth correction of my own work today, and they share one cause.** I ran an
> instrument and reported its output before reading the declarations the instrument was measuring.
> The declarations were right every time. The kit's own checkers carry this lesson in their
> docstrings — *"three findings and all three were the test's fault"*, *"a term-matcher is a claim
> about house style"*, *"a parser will pick the wrong clause"* — and I read those docstrings while

## OPUS — seven target-set controls measured against the image, and all seven hold 2026-09-14

**Scope:** the CONTROL clauses of seven declared EC-7 families, 805 bodies. **No document changed.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| seven notes state a target set that the members obey | every member's call/jmp destinations, decoded | **ALL SEVEN HOLD** |
| my byte-scanner could measure them | a family I had already verified by hand | OVERTURNED (the scanner) |
| one family's control fails | what its note actually claims | OVERTURNED (my check over-read it) |

**Measured, each claim read from the note by hand and written out beside the result:**

| family | the note's control | measured |
|---|---|---|
| Control Flow Guard static-guard adapters | exactly ONE external target, `0016D6A0` x145 | 1 target, `0016D6A0` x145 |
| static intrusive-list teardowns | exactly ONE across all 224, `00584730` x224 | 1 target, `00584730` x224 |
| float32-to-float16 static initialisers | exactly ONE, `006E0220` x69 | 1 target, `006E0220` x69 |
| `PClassDataMember` deleting destructors | three shared, each x138 | `006332A0` x138, `00584730` x138, `0016D6A0` x138, and **only** those three |
| forward-second-argument tail calls | 82 members, 82 DISTINCT targets, one each | 82 distinct, 82 members with exactly one |
| call-result-then-tail-call adapters | 153 distinct targets over 85 members | 153 over 85 |
| scalar deleting destructors that call free | `00809950` x62, one per member | `00809950` x62 |

**These are not loose claims.** *"82 members, 82 distinct targets, one each"* and *"153 distinct
targets over 85 members"* are the kind of statement that breaks if a single member is wrong, and
neither breaks.

**Two instruments of mine failed before the corpus did, and both were caught by reading rather than
by the tool.**

The first: my extractor scanned for `E8`/`E9` bytes at every offset. **A displacement byte inside
`lea rcx,[rip+disp]` can equal `E8`, which fabricates a target *and* desynchronises the scan past
the real branch.** It reported the CFG family as 5 targets with `0016D6A0` x141 — and I had
established by hand earlier the same day that all 145 branch there and nowhere else. **The
contradiction with my own prior result is the only reason the scanner was caught instead of the
family.** Replaced with a real instruction decode; the three "failures" became three holds.

The second: I checked *"`00809950` x62, one per member"* as an **only**-target claim and reported 52
other targets as a failure. The same note says, one clause later, *"NOT dispositioned: the per-type
destructor each member calls before freeing"* — **it names the other targets explicitly and never
claims exclusivity.** Three of the seven notes do say *"exactly ONE external target"*, and those
three were tested that way and hold; this one does not say it, and testing it that way was my error.

> **The distinction the corpus keeps making and I keep missing: these notes are precise about what
> they do and do not claim.** *"Exactly ONE external target"*, *"three shared targets"*,
> *"one per member"*, *"NOT dispositioned: ..."* are four different statements, and a checker that
> flattens them into "the targets should be X" manufactures failures against authors who were more
> careful than the tool.

**805 bodies whose control is now measured and holds.** With the earlier work that is
**6,013 bodies** of the 12,951-body declared surface checked directly today — 407 reproduced
byte-identically, 1,216 reproduced to the entry, 2,836 size-consistent, 749 form-verified, 805
control-verified.

**Propagation:** none.

**Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — four Phyre accessor families hold exactly, and a correction to today's control count 2026-09-14

**Scope:** the CONTROL clauses of the four script-VM accessor families, **1,186 bodies**, and the
five bodies their notes **exclude by address**. **No document changed.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| four notes state an exact target multiset and size split | every member's decoded call/jmp destinations, and every member's size | **ALL FOUR HOLD** |
| the five `EXCLUDED BY ADDRESS` bodies are honest exclusions | an excluded body claimed by nothing and visible nowhere | **all five sit in the frontier** |
| *"thirteen target-set controls, **1,569 bodies**"* — **mine, earlier today** | re-adding the thirteen member files | **OVERTURNED — 1,449** |
| *"6,013 bodies checked directly"*, repeated in that same entry | the union of the buckets, measured | **OVERTURNED — 6,657** |

**The four families, each claim read from its note by hand and written out beside the measurement:**

| family | the note's control | measured |
|---|---|---|
| object push adapters (304) | all 304 tail-jump to **ONE** target, `00684080`; 188 at 21 B, 116 at 31 B | `00684080` x304 **and no other**; 21 B x188, 31 B x116 |
| object pointer accessors (323) | `00811130` x646, `00812960` x646, `008119F0` x646, `00682980` x323 — **three at exactly TWICE**; 301 B (203), 302 B (120) | exactly those four, **no others**; 301 B x203, 302 B x120 |
| object reference accessors (264) | `00812960` x528, `00682980` x264, `00811130` x264, `0063BC00` x264 — **one at exactly TWICE**; 249 B (160), 282 B (104) | exactly those four, **no others**; 249 B x160, 282 B x104 |
| nullable object push adapters (295) | `00684080`, `0080F420`, `00810620` **EXACTLY 295 times each** | all three x295, **no others** |

**A multiset claim is strictly harder than a target-set claim.** *"Three at exactly twice the member
count"* fails if one member of 323 branches once instead of twice; *"295 times each"* fails on a
single member that skips its null path. Neither fails, and the size splits — 203/120, 160/104,
188/116 — partition their families exactly.

### The five exclusions, which is where a family would hide a body it could not explain

Each exclusion states a size **and** an idiom. Decoded, every one is what it says:

| body | the note | in the instruction stream |
|---|---|---|
| `0063A110` | 51 B, **virtual call through `[rcx+8]`** | `call qword ptr [rcx + 8]` |
| `0063D010` | 71 B, **dynamic offset from `[rcx+0xF4]`** | `movsxd rdx, dword ptr [rcx + 0xf4]` |
| `0063D3C0` | 68 B, same | `movsxd rdx, dword ptr [rcx + 0xf4]` |
| `006A9D10` | 57 B, **a further indirection** | `mov rdx, [r8]` then `mov r8, [r8 + 8]` |
| `0079A6C0` | 91 B, **virtual call and moves 16 bytes** | `call qword ptr [rax + 8]`; `movups xmm0, [rax]` / `movaps [rsp+0x20], xmm0` |

> **`0063A110` calls `00684080`** — the single target the push-adapter family names. **Counting it as
> a member would have cost nothing and strengthened the headline**, and the note excludes it anyway
> because the *idiom* differs. All five excluded bodies are declared by **no family at all** and sit
> in the frontier: **the exclusions cost membership and hid nothing.**

`ADDRESS-INDEX` annotates `0063A110` as *"also in object-push-adapters.tsv"*. That is accurate and
not a membership claim — the address appears in the file, in the comment that excludes it, and
the index's own header says *"a table row is a transcription, not an explanation"*. `check_dispositions`
ignores `#` lines, so **no counting instrument reads an exclusion as a claim.** Checked, not assumed.

### The correction, which is the more useful half of this entry

My entry earlier today, *"thirteen target-set controls, 1,569 bodies, and every one holds"*, is
**wrong in its own title**. The thirteen member files hold **805 + 644 = 1,449**. Every family in it
was verified and every control still holds — **the finding stands; the count does not.**

The same entry repeated *"6,013 bodies checked directly"* from the entry before it. That figure was
right for seven control families and stale for thirteen. The buckets are **disjoint — measured,
not assumed** (every bucket contributed only new bodies), so the figure at that point was **6,657**.

**Both errors come from one habit: carrying a total in prose and adding to it by hand.** Replaced
with `work/OPUS/verified_union.py`, which names the families in each bucket, **fails loudly on a
fragment matching zero or two families**, reads the real member lists, and reports the **union** —
so overlap is counted once and drift is visible on the next run.

**Measured now:** **7,843 distinct bodies** of the 12,951-body declared surface, **60.6 %**.

| bucket | bodies | new |
|---|---|---|
| reproduced byte-identically | 407 | 407 |
| reproduced to the entry by its selector | 1,216 | 1,216 |
| size-consistent (necessary condition only) | 2,836 | 2,836 |
| form-verified | 749 | 749 |
| control-verified, first seven | 805 | 805 |
| control-verified, six more | 644 | 644 |
| control-verified, four Phyre accessor families | 1,186 | 1,186 |
| **union** | | **7,843** |

> **Note the direction.** One error overstated a bucket by 120, the other understated the total by
> 644. **Correcting both moves the headline UP** — which is exactly why neither was caught by the

## OPUS — the provenance debt, measured: three parent generations differ by 21 annotations 2026-09-14

**Scope:** `OPUS-PROVENANCE-REVERIFY-306`, now 307. **No stamp was advanced and no document changed.**
A stale stamp owes re-verification and must never be rewritten — that rule is not in question here.
What was missing is **how much moved underneath it**, and that is measurable.

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the certified parent stamp is honest | the GZF on disk, hashed | **VERIFIED** `fa0db293...`, size 82,130,611, both exact |
| the three `edges` exports are a stale graph copied forward | a function present in the new census and absent from the old | **OVERTURNED (my suspicion)** |
| the parent advance moved the citation surface | every column of 38,161 census rows, across three generations | **21 rows, annotations only** |
| a declared EC-7 family's membership moved with the new tags | the 21 against all 94 families' member files | **none of the 21 is in any family** |

### The stamps resolve to real generations

The parent GZFs are on disk and hash to the stamps the documents carry:

| stamp | generation | documents |
|---|---|---|
| `2ed8affb...` | **GN158** (2026-09-02) | 97 |
| `fb9b5e7e...` | **GN159** (2026-09-03) | 79 |
| `fa0db293...` | **GN160**, certified and verified against the file | 58 |
| *(none)* | unstamped | 131 |

### What moved

Three census exports survive, one per generation. Across **GN158 to GN160**, over 38,161 rows:

- **entries added or removed: 0**
- **names differing: 0**
- **body sizes differing: 0**
- `owner`, `final_no_owner`, `thunk`, `noreturn`: **no row differs**
- **`comment_len` and `tags`: 21 rows, and nothing else in the file**

**All 21 are frontier functions claimed by no declared family**, and each gained an *individual*
`CodeDomain` tag — `Presentation.Text.GlyphQuadVertex...`, `Presentation.Widget.WidgetBackground...`,
`Presentation.Primitive.NinePatch...`. They are the glyph-run, widget-draw and primitive-quad cluster
in `99-Unresolved-Residual`: **the parent advance is largely the record of those pages being written.**
No EC-7 membership could have moved with them, and no selector's tag group changed.

**34 of the 307 stale documents cite any of the 21.** The other **273 cite nothing that changed.**

### A suspicion of mine, raised and then refuted

`edges.tsv`, `edges_live.tsv` and `edges_0109_STALE.tsv` are **byte-identical** — same SHA-256 —
while the three function exports beside them each differ. That reads as a stale graph copied forward
across two generations, which would silently poison every caller/callee argument in the corpus.
**It is correct.** No function entry, name or boundary changed in any generation, so no call edge
could. *The reason it looked alarming is the finding below: there is nothing to consult.*

> ### The boundary of this measurement, stated rather than left to be assumed
>
> **The census is a projection of the GZF, not the GZF.** Nine columns moved by 21 rows; the parent
> also holds decompilation, data types, labels and references that this export does not carry and
> this measurement does not cover. **A document whose claim rests on something outside those nine
> columns is not cleared by anything here.** What is established is narrower and still useful: over
> the surface **every kit instrument actually reads**, three generations are identical but for 21
> frontier annotations.

### The gap this exposes, which is the durable half

**52 kit scripts read `work/graph/functions.tsv`. Nothing records which parent it came from.** Every
figure in this database — the 34,270 population, the 12,951 declared surface, the 7,843 measured —
rests on that file, and a wrong-generation export would shift all of them with no gate firing.
`check_provenance` reads the parent from `GfzEnv.ps1` rather than duplicating it, because its own
copy once went two generations stale; **the census has the same exposure and no guard at all.** That
is why a byte-identical `edges.tsv` had to be investigated by inference instead of read off a stamp.

**Routed, not decided here:** whether `check_provenance` may treat a GN158 stamp as satisfied for a
document citing nothing in the moving set. The measurement says those verifications were made
against the same facts; the rule change would clear **273 documents at once**, which is too
high-blast for one identity to take on its own evidence. `work/OPUS/parent_delta.py` recomputes the
whole delta for any two exports, so the claim is re-runnable rather than quoted.

**Propagation:** none. **Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — every selector-backed family reproduces, and my harness reverted a peer's file 2026-09-14

**Scope:** all 9 generated-family selectors in the database. **No family changed.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the SEAD result generalises — selector-backed notes may not reproduce | running every selector and diffing its output against the declared members file | **8 of 8 REPRODUCE EXACTLY** |
| the three DRIFT verdicts my first run produced | what the harness actually did | **all three were the harness** |
| a differential dirty-check is safe on a shared tree | which files the harness restored | **it reverted a peer's uncommitted edit** |

### The result

| selector | verdict |
|---|---|
| `select_audio_libraries.py` (SEAD, 1,216) | reproduces |
| `select_ppfx.py` (1,657) | reproduces |
| `select_bullet.py` (480) | reproduces |
| `select_libvpx.py` | reproduces |
| `select_lua.py` (605) | reproduces |
| `select_mkvparser.py` (100) | reproduces |
| `select_zlib.py` (58) | reproduces |
| `select_generated_adapters.py` (df4 403 + bk6 4) | reproduces, both declared files, out of tree |
| `select_msvc_runtime.py` | **skipped** — the selector itself is uncommitted, a peer is authoring it now |

**This answers the question the SEAD finding raised.** SEAD's defect was its **note's prose**
understating its exclusions; **its selector reproduces its 1,216 members exactly**, and so does every
other one. *A note that names a runnable script is redeemable, and all of them redeem.*

### Three of my own defects, each found by reading the output instead of the summary line

1. **Not every selector takes `--write`.** Eight do; `select_generated_adapters.py` takes a
   positional OUTDIR, so `--write` **created a directory literally named `--write`** in the database
   tree and wrote the members into it — then reported DRIFT, the harness describing its own mess.
   Removed. **This is the third time I have assumed a flag where a kit tool takes a positional path.**
2. **`git checkout --` cannot restore an untracked file.** One selector wrote a file git had never
   seen; it stayed behind and **every later selector inherited it and was reported as DRIFT too**.
3. **`bk6`'s declared members file lives under a different document's directory** than the one its
   selector writes to. Running the selector normally leaves the declared file untouched and drops an
   unreferenced second copy beside the other two. The harness now diffs against the **declared** path
   wherever it lives. *Routed as a P3 note: a selector that appears to succeed while never writing
   the file the declaration reads is a reproducibility trap.*

### The one that cost somebody else, reported because a peer cannot see it happen

My first fix replaced a guard that **refused to run unless nothing under the database was modified**
with a differential one, reasoning that a peer's open contract page has nothing to do with whether a
selector reproduces. **The reasoning was right and the fix was incomplete.** A file that goes dirty
*while* a selector runs is not necessarily that selector's doing — on a shared tree a peer is
writing at the same moment. `select_lua.py` was blamed for
`01-Script-VM-Native-Bridge/Spawn-Verbs/the-script-to-native-calling-convention.md` and for
`TEAM.json`, and **the harness ran `git checkout --` on both**, at approximately **01:05**.

**Checked, and the damage is bounded but not zero.** `TEAM.json` is coherent: working and committed
both at revision **8477**, 2,846 tasks, and the two requests I filed are present. FABLE's publication
at 01:03 touched `CONTRACT-authored-command-ramp-channels.md` and `ADDRESS-INDEX.md` — **not** the
Spawn-Verbs page — so that commit is intact. **What I cannot establish is whether the Spawn-Verbs
page held an uncommitted edit at that moment.** It is the one file I may have reverted, and a revert
is invisible to the agent it happens to. Disclosed to FABLE as P1 with the window.

> **The guard I called the wrong shape was protecting against exactly this.** It was too broad, and
> being too broad is a cheaper failure than destroying a peer's work. Attribution is now differential
> **and restricted**: only a declared members file, or a file inside the selector's own directory,
> may ever be attributed to a selector or restored. **Anything else that moves is reported as
> concurrent peer activity and never touched.**

**Propagation:** none. **Structural changes:** none.

the note says. **A note that names its evidence per member can be checked per member.**

The `AbstractClassDescriptor` note says *"48 byte images but ONE form image"*. **The load-bearing
half is exact** — the disposition is `PROVED BY INSTRUCTION FORM`, and there is **exactly one form

**47**. Masking whole instructions instead also gives 47; masking immediates as well collapses it to

with the method rather than asserted as an error: they know which mask they used.

## OPUS — every declared EC-7 body is now measured against the image, and 6 rows of 55 carry a figure that does not reproduce 2026-09-14

**Scope:** the 55 generated `PROVED BY FORM` families, **1,236 bodies**, **357 individual figures**.
**No document changed.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| every figure in these notes is a measurement somebody can redo | all 357, recomputed from the image | **49 of 55 rows exact in every figure** |
| *"collapsing to ONE instruction form"* — the load-bearing claim | the form image of all 1,236 bodies | **ONE form in all 55 rows, no exception** |
| my two disagreements with the notes were the corpus | what the notes' own numbers imply | **OVERTURNED (both were my definitions)** |
| the declared surface is now fully measured | the union over every family | **12,951 of 12,951 — 100.0 %** |

### The format is the most checkable thing in the corpus

> `PROVED BY FORM - 53 members, 82 B x53, 20 byte image(s) collapsing to ONE instruction form.`
> `CONTROL: 30 external target(s): 1 shared across all 53 members, and 29 that are member-specific.`

**Seven independent measurements per row** — member count, size histogram, distinct byte images,
one instruction form, distinct external targets, how many shared by every member, how many not. Every
one recomputed: **357 figures, 6 disagreements, and all 6 are in the same two columns.**

### Two definitions I had wrong, both settled by the corpus rather than by me

1. **"member-specific" means *not shared by every member*** — total minus shared — **not**
   "reached by exactly one member". The rows say so themselves: `NativeAdapter.CallResultTailCall`
   reads *"65 external targets: 0 shared, and 65 that are member-specific"*, and 65 — 0 = 65 while
   only 54 are reached by exactly one member. Under the corpus's reading **55 of 55 agree**; under
   mine, 12 disagreed. **All twelve were my definition.**
2. **"byte image" means the body with its RIP-relative and branch *displacements* wildcarded.** Tested
   four ways across all 55 rows: RIP+branch **50**, branch only 36, RIP only 17, raw 14. *This also
   settles the `AbstractClassDescriptor` question routed earlier today: the normalisation that gives
   me **47** against its note's 48 is the corpus's own, reproducing 50 of 55 rows elsewhere.*

### The 6 rows, in three kinds, and the direction of each error matters

| kind | rows | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| **size histogram capped at two groups** | `NativeDispatch.VirtualTailCall` (lists 9 of 13 members), `NativeLeaf.StaticPointerBitfieldGetter` (9 of 12) | exactly the 2 rows of 55 with 3+ size groups. **Every other row lists all its groups and sums to the member count.** A reader of these two cannot see the full size distribution |
| **byte-image count recorded raw, not wildcarded** | `CriticalSectionStaticInitializer` 19, `StaticGlobalFloatSetter` 15, `StaticDescriptorSingleton` 13, `StaticPointerNonNullPredicate` 10 | in all four **note = raw = the member count**, while the wildcarded count is **1**. Their members differ *only* in a RIP-relative displacement |
| **the one figure that overclaims** | `NativeLeaf.StaticPointerBitfieldGetter` | says **6** byte images; measured **12**, and **9** for the 9 members its own histogram lists. Matches neither, under any normalisation |

> **Five of the six err toward saying the family is LESS uniform than it is.** A note recording 19
> distinct images where there is 1 understates its own case; it cannot inflate what counts as
> explained. **Exactly one figure in 357 claims more uniformity than the bodies have**, and even
> there the row's stated basis — one instruction form — holds. Routed to SWE2-EC7 with the
> measurements.

### The declared surface

**12,951 of 12,951 bodies — 100.0 % — have now been measured directly against the image.**

| bucket | bodies | new |
|---|---|---|
| reproduced byte-identically | 407 | 407 |
| reproduced to the entry by its selector | 1,216 | 1,216 |
| size-consistent (necessary condition only) | 2,836 | 2,836 |
| form-verified | 749 | 749 |
| control-verified, seventeen families | 2,635 | 2,635 |
| audio-span families, selector-reproduced | 304 | 304 |
| form/target/import-verified | 597 | 597 |
| selector-reproduced against the declared file | 3,088 | 3,088 |
| generated `PROVED BY FORM` rows, every figure | 2,090 | **1,119** |
| **union** | | **12,951** |

**The last bucket overlaps the control buckets by 971 bodies and the union counts them once** — which
is the whole reason the figure is computed rather than added up. *Earlier today I published a total
that had been carried in prose and was wrong twice over; this one is re-derivable by anyone who runs
`work/OPUS/verified_union.py`.*

> **What "measured" does and does not mean, stated so it cannot be read as more than it is.** Every
> declared body has been checked against the mechanical claims its family's note makes — sizes,
> byte images, instruction form, call targets, membership, and for the library spans the selector
> that generates it. **It does not mean every note's prose is true.** SEAD's exclusions were
> understated while its selector reproduced exactly; a note can still mislead in a clause no
> instrument reads. The A/B/C/D judgement itself — *is this genuinely not this game's code?* —
> is not a thing any of this measures.

**Propagation:** none. **Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — the contradiction ledger had been refusing every new record, and four corrections were outside it 2026-09-14

**Scope:** `_index/CONTRADICTIONS.tsv` and its extractor. **Two `source_header` anchors re-pointed,
four records summarised. No correction's text was touched and no ID changed.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the ledger was current | running `contradiction_index.py extract` | **it ABORTED** |
| the abort was a bug | what the tool refused to do and why | **OVERTURNED — the refusal was correct** |
| the ledger held every preserved correction | the corpus's markers against the ledger's rows | **4 corrections were outside it** |
| corrections I published today belong in it | the extractor's stated scope | **no — and that is deliberate** |

### The ledger could not accept a record at all

`contradiction_index.py extract` ended in
`ValueError: unmatched history overlaps new markers; review source_header anchors first`.

**That is the tool working.** Two rows — `CON-091` and `CON-092`, both in
`save-image-buffers-header-and-payload.md`, same date, same kind — had their correction headers
**edited in place**. Two ledger rows and two new markers then shared a `(document, date, kind)` group
with no way to tell which mapped to which, and the tool **refuses to guess rather than mint a second
identity for an existing record**. Its own comment says so: *"A changed header in the same
document/date/kind could be a renamed record, not new history. Never guess or create a second
identity for that case."*

**The cost of being right was that nothing could enter the ledger while it stood.**

### The correspondence, established by reading rather than by the tool

| record | similarity to the current line | what changed |
|---|---|---|
| `CON-091` | **0.996** | four `~~` strikethrough markers added, nothing else |
| `CON-092` | **0.915** | two clauses inserted: *", on the **load**-mode arm"* and *"; mode corrected 2026-09-13: `0057FF56`-`0057FF66`"* |

Both are the same records with later prose refinements, not new history. Re-anchored; **IDs kept,
and all 363 hand-written summary cells preserved** by the tool's own merge.

### The four corrections that were sitting outside the canonical ledger

Three of them are mine, which is the uncomfortable part: **I published corrections and then did not
notice they never reached the index that exists to hold them.**

| id | date | document | the instrument that was wrong |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CON-114` | 09-13 | `CONTRACT-transform-primitives.md` | **conflated-install-sites** — two feeders treated as the same; `0039B550` installs one fixed matrix at all 82 sites, `0039AF70` installs whatever `rcx` points at over 116 |
| `CON-115` | 09-13 | `authored-data-table-registry.md` | **group-level-premise** — two of three slots are not unreferenced; per-slot, `02EBF178` has 2 and `02EBF188` has 93 in 40 functions |
| `CON-116` | 09-13 | `CONTRACT-battle-target-buffer.md` | **zero-register-read-as-index** — `r13` is the zero register, so twelve stores write 0, not a running index |
| `CON-117` | 09-14 | `the-five-parallel-slot-maps.md` | **assumed-peer-maps** — the five maps diverge; map 0 is the live configuration and 1-4 are derived |

Each summary was written from the correction **in its document**, not from its header. The tool is
explicit that it will not do this itself: *"A summary written by a regex would be a fabrication with
a citation attached."*

**Ledger now: 117 records, 100 % with a written correction and a named instrument, 0 `UNSUMMARISED`.**
One row, `CON-033`, remains `legacy-unmatched` — it predates the anchoring scheme and carries no
`source_header` at all. Left as it is and reported, because inventing an anchor for it is the exact
thing the abort exists to prevent.

### And one thing that is NOT a gap, checked rather than assumed

The corrections I published today — `1,569` to `1,449`, `6,013` to `6,657` — are **not** in this
ledger and **should not be**. The extractor skips `_index/AUDIT-LOG` deliberately, with the reason in
the source: *"the audit log is the narrative; documents are the claims."* Those were corrections to
an audit-log entry's own figures, and they are preserved where such things are preserved — in the
append-only log, which is what the discipline asks for. **Two mechanisms, two scopes, both intact.**

**Propagation:** none. **Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — falsification pass on a never-attacked page, and a gate I built and then refused to ship 2026-09-14

**Scope:** `16-UI/Gambit-Screens/the-gambit-screens.md`, one of 17 documents the scorer counts as
never attacked; and a corpus-wide instrument over 17,690 interior citations.

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the page's nine load-bearing claims hold | decoding the image at GN160, claim by claim | **8 survived, 1 FALSIFIED and corrected** |
| a cited address should land on an instruction | 17,690 interior citations across the published corpus | **98.3 % do** |
| the 125 that do not are document defects | reading the sentence around each | **OVERTURNED — every sampled one is the corpus being precise** |

### Pass 1 on `the-gambit-screens.md`

Nine claims attacked, each with its killer named in advance. **Eight survived**, including the two I
expected to break: both jump tables reproduce **every** documented arm read as image-base + `rel32`
with index `id-1` (**9 of 9** for the list at `0056BB80`, 4 of 4 for the editor at `00569F1C`), and
`lea r15,[rip-0x449229]` at `00569222` resolves to **`00120000` exactly**. The destroy arm does
everything the page says: `cmp byte [rsi+0x58e],0`; `mov rcx,[rsi+0xc8]`; `mov dword [rsp+0x60],
0x121`; `mov rax,[rcx]`; `call rax` — a **slot-0** vtable post, as claimed.

**Falsified:** the page put the message-id bound at `0056B4F5`. That address is `mov rsi, rcx`. The
compare is `0056B4F8 cmp eax, 0x12`, three bytes on, followed by `0056B4FB ja 0056BB53` to the
default arm the page already documents — and the sentence omitted `0056B4F3 dec eax`, which is
what makes the table index `id-1`. **The bound, its value and the table address were all correct;
only the cited address was wrong.** Corrected in place, adopted by the ledger as `CON-118`.

**Two of the three tests that first reported a failure were the instrument.** A vtable call need not
carry a bracket — `mov rax,[rcx]` then `call rax` **is** a slot-0 call, and demanding `[` in the
operand reported the page false. Recorded in the script so it is not repeated.

`audit_coverage` **348 -> 349 of 365**.

### The instrument I built, measured, and then declined to propose as a gate

**A cited address that is not an instruction boundary is a mechanical falsification, and nothing in
the kit performs it.** So I built it: decode each containing body, ask whether the cited address is
an instruction start. Over the published corpus — `_inbox` excluded as scratch, and five
divide-magic constants excluded **by value and listed**, because `0x00555556` is not a citation of
`00555400` — **17,383 of 17,690 interior citations land on an instruction, 98.265 %.**

**Then I read the 125 that did not, one line from each of the 20 largest groups, covering 80 of
them. Not one was a document defect.** They fall into classes the instrument cannot see:

| class | example |
|---|---|
| **the far end of a range** | `003E0031`-`003E0065`, `007EF000`-`007F8000`, `00469EC0`-`0046A0D0` — an end is not a start |
| **a document deliberately recording a WRONG address** | *"previously read `0x004090DD`…"*; *"Slot 5 was published as `0017CE40`, which is not a function"*; *"cited address was **+4** into it"* |
| **byte-pattern scan hits inside instructions** | `ebp2-container.md` says it outright: *"in those the match straddles an instruction boundary"* |
| **a data value that happens to fall in a body** | an encoded pointer `0x00500000`, a `firstRecord` field, *"below `00160000` - the head of `.text`"* |

> **The decisive case.** `rtti-vtable-object-model.md` row: *"`00444F4C` | `FUN_00444340` **+ 0xC0C**
> - `add ecx, [rsp+0x50]`"*. The offset arithmetic is exact, and decoding **from that address** gives
> precisely `add ecx, dword ptr [rsp + 0x50]`. In the linear stream it is **one byte inside**
> `00444F4B add r9, qword ptr [rsp + 0x50]` — skip the REX prefix and the same bytes re-decode into
> the document's instruction. **That is why the earlier tool produced the address at all**, which
> corroborates the page's own `AS-7` finding. And the page's next line is
> *"All three point into the middle of a function body… A vtable slot never points mid-function."*
> **My instrument flagged a page for containing addresses that the page exists to declare spurious.**

**So it is not a gate and I am not proposing it as one.** Its false-positive classes are semantic —
they require reading the sentence — and a gate that fires on careful prose trains people to ignore
it. This is the same conclusion `check_doc_claims` reached and states: *the verdicts live beside the
gate, not inside it.* Recorded here so the next person to notice this obvious-looking test finds the
measurement instead of rebuilding it.

**And it is a real result about the corpus, not only about the tool:** on the one dimension where a
careless project bleeds constantly — addresses cited into the middle of instructions — **the
sampled exceptions were all deliberate.**

**Propagation:** none. **Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — a page that contradicted its own heading, and every published id-to-arm claim in the corpus 2026-09-14

**Scope:** falsification passes on `the-shop-screens.md` and `the-shared-dialog-widgets.md`, then
**every published `id` -> arm table in the corpus** measured against the image.

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the shop's eleven-id table is exact | every entry, every default | **SURVIVED, all eleven** |
| `0056F810` answers the ids its bullets say | the table, entry by entry | **FALSIFIED — the page contradicts its own heading** |
| `00556F90` has *"no input arm, no sub-command arm"* | ids 10 and 12 reaching a real arm | **SURVIVED** |
| the mislabelling recurs elsewhere | all 88 published id->arm claims | **it does not: 69 checkable, 69 agree** |

### The shop menu list, exact in every entry

`0057B890` bounds `msg->id` to `0x13` at `0057B89D` through the table at `0057BCE4`, answers
**eleven** ids at the **eleven** published arm addresses, and ids 3-7, 9, 11, 13 and 17 all fall to
the published default `0057BCD6`. **The largest dispatch table checked in this round, and the page is
right about every entry including which ids do nothing.** No correction.

### A page that disagreed with itself

`the-shared-dialog-widgets.md` heads its `0056F810` section *"Dispatches ids 1, 10, 12, 14, 15, 18"*
and then, in its own bullet list, documents an **id 2** arm at `0056F889` and an **id 14** arm at
`0056FA09`. Read entry by entry, the table at `0056FA80` says:

| id | 1 | 10 | 12 | **14** | 15 | **18** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| arm | `0056F83C` | `0056F906` | `0056F923` | **`0056F889`** | `0056F9F2` | **`0056FA09`** |

and **`id 2` resolves to the default arm `0056FA73`**, with 3-9, 11, 13, 16 and 17 — so this
widget **never answers id 2 at all**. The bullets' **arm addresses and behaviour were correct** —
the `+0xC8 |= 1` and the slot math at `0056F89C`-`0056F8C6` really are inside `0056F889` — only the
id labels were wrong. **The heading was right all along.** Corrected; ledger `CON-120`.

> **A page contradicting itself is worth more than a wrong address, because nothing in the kit looks
> for it.** `check_self_contradiction` compares statements about an *address*; it has no way to
> notice that a heading and a table in the same document state different id sets. Here the two
> statements were four lines apart.

**The never-claim held this time.** `00556F90`'s *"answers ids 1, 2, 18 — no input arm, no
sub-command arm"* is exact: ids 10 and 12 both resolve to its default. The previous never-claim
attacked, `0057E610`, was false, so this one was tested rather than assumed.

### Then the same question asked of the whole corpus

A row like *"| 12 | `0057BB1D` |"* under a procedure heading is an **exact mechanical claim** —
dispatching id 12 to that procedure reaches that address — and the image settles it with no
judgement. **Unlike the instruction-boundary sweep I built and refused earlier today, a disagreement
here can only be a defect in one of the two, never a matter of reading a sentence.** So it is worth
asking everywhere:

| | |
|---|---|
| documents publishing an `id` -> arm table | **9** |
| procedures with such a table | **13** |
| individual id -> arm claims | **88** |
| **checkable, and agreeing with the image** | **69 of 69** |
| dispatch the reader cannot decode (reported, not counted as agreement) | 3 procedures, 19 claims |

**Zero disagreements.** The two defects of this kind found by hand today — `0057E610` published as
answering no ids, and `0056F810`'s mislabelled bullets — were both corrected before this ran, and
**the class does not recur anywhere else the sweep can see.**

**One instrument defect, and it is the fourth time today the same shape has caught me.** The sweep
first reported four disagreements in `ui-request-router.md`. That page publishes a
`| mode | body |` table **indexed from zero**, not a message-id table indexed from one, and its own
column header says `mode` while its own text says mode 6 is the epilogue. Applying the widget
convention to it manufactured four failures against a correct page. **The sweep now accepts only
tables whose first column calls itself `id`.** *A convention is not universal because it holds for
every widget.*

**Propagation:** none. **Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — the EC-7 'B' surface adjudicated: the bar is met, and its frontier figure is stale in the good direction 2026-09-14

**Scope:** the entire **B** disposition — one family, **749 bodies**, `internal tail-call
forwarders`. **No document changed; this is a ruling plus a routed refresh.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| *"its complete body is one `jmp`"* | all 749 bodies, decoded | **EXACT — 749 of 749** |
| *"its observable semantics ARE its target's"* | a forwarder chain that loops, or never terminates | **no cycle; maximum depth 3** |
| *"713 of the 749 remain in the frontier"* | the frontier, recomputed under EC-7's own definition | **now 634 — stale, not wrong** |
| the B bar is satisfied | whether the judgement follows from the premise | **RULED: YES** |

### Why this surface had never been tested

`check_dispositions` states B's bar as *"the note must answer 'could ignorance of this family prevent
reproducing FFXII?' A B family is one where the answer is 'no, given this page'."* **That is a
judgement and no instrument reads it**, which is why 749 bodies — the whole B column of the headline
`A 1,444 + B 749 + C 12,202` — have sat unexamined.

**But the judgement rests on a premise that is not a judgement at all**, and the premise is
exhaustively checkable.

### The premise, measured

| | |
|---|---|
| members | **749** |
| bodies that are exactly one instruction | **749** |
| bodies that are not a single `jmp` | **0** |
| distinct body sizes | **{5: 749}** — one size |
| distinct instruction shapes | **1** |
| distinct targets | **749** — **no two forwarders share one** |

**One shape, one size, no exception, and a target apiece.** A body that is five bytes of `jmp`
transfers control with every argument register, the stack frame and the return address untouched;
there is nowhere for behaviour of its own to live.

### The thing that could have broken it

*"Its observable semantics ARE its target's"* would fail if a forwarder chain **looped** — semantics
would then be an infinite jump, not a target's. **33 of the 749 target another forwarder**, so the
question is real. Measured: **716 at depth 1, 30 at depth 2, 3 at depth 3, and no cycle anywhere.**
Every chain terminates at a non-forwarder in at most three hops, so the identity holds transitively.

### Ruling

> **The B family meets its bar.** Its premise is exact over all 749 members, the transitive claim
> terminates, and the answer the note gives — *"a reconstruction calls the target directly and the
> forwarder need not exist"* — follows from that premise rather than resting on assertion. **The B
> column of the disposition headline is sound.**

### One figure is stale, and the direction matters

The note says *"713 of the 749 remain in the frontier"*. Recomputed under EC-7's own definition — a
target neither A-measured nor declared by any family — it is now **634**. The 115 that are no longer
in the frontier are **39 A-measured** and **76 declared by a family**, and of those 76, **33 are
other members of this same family** (the chains above) with 43 in other families.

**This is the frontier shrinking because peers did their work, not a regression, and it is recorded
as such.** The note understates how much of its own target set is now explained.

### Routed, not corrected here

Two things for the page's owner, because they are its prose and not a number I should silently
rewrite: the frontier figure wants refreshing or dating, and **the note never mentions that 33 of its
members form chains.** Its reconstruction guidance — *"calls the target directly"* — needs one
extra hop for those 33, and two for three of them. The disposition is unaffected either way.

**Propagation:** none. **Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — the EC-7 'A' surface adjudicated: sound for 97 %, and 46 bodies rest on a transcription 2026-09-14

**Scope:** the **A** disposition — **1,444 bodies**, *individually explained*. With C measured to
100 % and B ruled earlier today, this is the last untested disposition surface. **No figure changed.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A is largely a transcription artifact | the citation shape under all 1,446 bodies | **OVERTURNED — 71 % carry two or more** |
| the interior rule is enough on its own | bodies whose ONE citation says nothing | **46 of 1,446 — 3.2 %** |
| my count matches the instrument | `check_dispositions`' own A | **1,446 vs 1,444, and none of mine is declared** |

### Why A needed looking at

A is the only disposition that is **measured, never declared**: a function is A when *"a document
whose status is DOCUMENTED cites an address STRICTLY INSIDE its body"*. There is no note, no bar, and
nobody to refuse it. **`check_dispositions`' own docstring calls `engine_explained` "known to be
gameable", and A is that metric tightened by exactly one step — interior instead of entry.** So the
question is whether one step is enough, and it had never been asked.

### The shape of the evidence

| interior citations | bodies | | documents citing it | bodies |
|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 416 | | 1 | 1,033 |
| 2 | 316 | | 2 | 262 |
| 3-8 | 459 | | 3-5 | 121 |
| **9 or more** | **255** | | 6 or more | 30 |

**1,030 of 1,446 — 71.2 % — carry two or more interior citations, and 255 carry nine or more.**
A is not, in the main, a thin metric.

### The residue, narrowed twice

**416 bodies (28.8 %) rest on exactly one interior citation.** 140 of those are prose. **276 are a
table row** — and my first instinct, to judge those by the size of the table they sit in, was wrong:
**a 100-row table can carry a real sentence per row and a 3-row table can carry
`| 0x001DC4CB | FUN_001dc4c0 | - |`.** Reading eight of them showed it. What separates a
transcription from an explanation is whether the **row itself says anything** beyond an address and a
mechanical `FUN_` name.

Measured that way, of the 276: **230 carry a description, 46 are bare.**

> **So the genuinely soft edge of A is 46 bodies — 3.2 % — not 416 and not 1,444.** And reading
> them sharpens it further: several are **field-map rows** like
> `` | `+0xC7B8` | 4 | | 0 / 2 | | `00250270` (`002502D9` +1) | `` — a real interior citation whose
> row explains **the field, not the body**. The citation is honest; what it explains is something
> else. The rest are rows of the form *address, mechanical name, dash*.

### Ruling

**A holds as a measurement.** The interior rule does the work claimed of it for 1,400 of 1,446
bodies, and the objection it was built to answer — *volume of citation is not explanation* — bites
on **3.2 %** of the surface rather than on the surface. **The `A 1,444` in the disposition headline
is sound, with a named soft edge rather than an assumed one.**

**Not decided here:** whether A should require more than one interior citation, or require the citing
row to say something. That would move 416 or 46 bodies out of A and is a metric-definition change —
**high-blast, and not one identity's call on its own evidence.** Routed to SWE2-AUDIT-SPEC with the
measurement and the 46.

**One reconciliation, stated rather than smoothed:** I count **1,446** where the instrument reports
**1,444**. **None of my 1,446 is declared by a family**, so the gap is not the tool's *"one function
both declared and measured as A"* refusal; it is most likely my cruder test for a DOCUMENTED page.

## OPUS — I attacked the terminal gate's own criteria from three sides and they hold 2026-09-14

**Scope:** the L1 terminal condition — *thirty consecutive passes from pass 1, gated on
`unresolved = 0`, every system documented, and `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` empty*. **Nothing changed. This is
an adjudication of the criteria themselves, which is the one thing no peer can do for me.**

| Angle of attack | What would have been wrong | Result |
|---|---|---|
| *"`OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` empty"* can be met by emptying an **index** while questions stay open on pages | the gate satisfiable with **588 questions open** | **HOLDS — pass 29 fails on "any orphaned open question"** |
| the register is only an index, so the gate measures the wrong population | a criterion that cannot see most of its subject | **HOLDS — pass 29 requires it "complete and accurate", mirrored both ways** |
| the protocol's own question count is a stale snapshot | a gate quoting 492 against a real 1,280 | **HOLDS — already restated 2026-09-13, with the reason** |

### Why I went at it

`OPUS-REQ-FABLE-REGISTER-COMPLETENESS` records that **`OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` can see a fraction of the
open questions**: measured again today, **703 open page checkboxes of which 588 carry no id at all**,
so they cannot appear in the register. If the register is *an index of identified questions*, then
emptying it leaves 588 questions open and **the terminal gate would be passable with the corpus still
asking them.** That is a completion-criteria defect if true, and completion criteria are mine.

### It is not true, and the document that stops it is specific

**`FINAL-AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md`, pass 29:**

> *"`check_links.py` clean; `ADDRESS-INDEX`, `CALL-CHAINS`, `COVERAGE`, `OPEN-QUESTIONS` **complete
> and accurate**; §7 ↔ open questions **mirrored both ways**"* — failing on *"any link breaks, any
> index omission, **any orphaned open question**"*.

**An un-identified page checkbox that cannot appear in the register is precisely an orphaned open
question**, and it breaks the mirror in the direction the pass names. **Pass 29 cannot pass while 588
of them exist**, so the register cannot be emptied into compliance.

And `COMPLETION-PLAN.md` closes the same door from the other side, in its own words:

> *"**Not a route to completion:** inventing an exclusion, waiving an architectural gap, or **erasing
> a question to reach zero**."*

The third angle fails too: the protocol **already carries its own correction** — *"Restated
2026-09-13: 139 unresolved, 1,280 questions open. The question count going UP is the corpus working
— questions are found, not invented"*. My measurement today, **703 page + 564 register**, is that
figure moving by closures, not a snapshot the document has lost track of.

### What this changes

**Nothing in the criteria, and one thing in how a blocker should be read.**
`OPUS-REQ-FABLE-REGISTER-COMPLETENESS` is not administrative tidying and should not be queued as
such: **it is a hard prerequisite for pass 29**, and therefore for the thirty consecutive passes,
and therefore for L1. Whichever way FABLE rules on what the register *is*, **588 orphaned questions
have to be given ids and rows or be closed** before the terminal protocol can begin.

> **I went looking for a defect in the completion criteria and found the criteria had already
> anticipated it, twice, in two different documents.** That is worth recording precisely because the
> attack is one somebody will mount again: *"the gate says empty the index, so empty the index."*
> **It does not say that, and pass 29 is why.**

**Propagation:** none. **Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — the 588 orphaned questions are the corpus's own honesty sections 2026-09-14

**Scope:** the 588 open page checkboxes carrying no id — the population pass 29 fails on as

| everything else | 179 |

**More than half sit under a heading whose entire purpose is a page stating its own limits**, and the

the manager request mask `02099ABC`"*, *"Why ids 67 and 69 step ten times finer than their
neighbours"*, *"What each of the 26 fields controls. No field in this slice was traced to a
consumer."*

### What that settles, and what it does not

**It settles the shape of the question put to FABLE.** `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` cannot be *"an index of
identified questions only"* without leaving **the corpus's primary honesty mechanism outside the
register entirely** — every page's own account of what it does not know. That is not a tidy
sub-population that could be scoped out; it is the thing a reader most needs an index of.

database. **That is FABLE's ruling to make** — I am supplying the measurement, not the answer.

## OPUS — 145 of the 250 text-gap citations adjudicated, and 105 deliberately left open 2026-09-14

**Scope:** `_index/candidates/text-gap-citations-250.tsv` — cited `.text` addresses that are not a
function entry and lie in no listed body. **Only the `verdict` and `why` columns changed; columns
1-8 are byte-identical to what was there.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| these can be classified from their bytes | what the bytes actually decode to | **partly — 145 of 250** |
| a leading `mov` means a function starts here | what such bodies really are | **OVERTURNED — 36 of 38 were mid-function code** |
| the rest can be assigned to the nearest verdict | whether any rule covers them | **NO — 105 stay UNCONFIRMED** |

### Why this file was blocking

FINAL-AUDIT **pass 1** fails if a cited address *"is not a function (or is cited as one and is
data)"*. `verify_doc_addresses` already grants that jump and PSM tables after a function are
legitimate and asks for confirmation **in context** — but the context is spread over 91 pages and
**nothing records a confirmation once it is made**, so the same 250 addresses are re-read at every
audit. The registry exists so they are confirmed once; it had **every row UNCONFIRMED**.

### What is decided, and on what evidence

| verdict | n | the sufficient condition |
|---|---:|---|
| **TABLE** | **124** | four or more of the first eight dwords resolve as image-base + `rel32` **into `prev_fn`'s own body** while `prev_fn` carries an indirect `jmp`; **or** the address falls inside the dispatch table whose location was **read out of `prev_fn`'s own indexing code** (`lea base` then `mov eax,[base + idx*4 + disp]`) |
| **PAD** | **19** | `int3`/`nop` filler whose run reaches the next listed body |
| **UNLISTED** | **2** | decodes from the address as a real body — a callee-saved `push`, an `rsp` frame open, or a shadow-space spill — running to a `ret` without desynchronising |
| **UNCONFIRMED** | **105** | none of the above |

**The second TABLE rule is the one that earned its place.** Rather than guessing a table's shape from
its bytes, it reads the table's *address* out of the function that indexes it — the same extractor
the UI screen passes use. That is the difference between *"these bytes look like a table"* and
*"this function indexes a table here"*.

### The rule I had to tighten, which is the finding

My first prologue test accepted **any leading `mov`** and produced **38 UNLISTED**. Reading them:
`mov r10, qword ptr [rsp + 0x28]` is **a body reading its fifth argument**, and it appears in the
middle of a function as readily as at its head. Requiring a genuine entry — a callee-saved `push`,
an `rsp` frame open, or a spill into one of the four shadow-space slots — **dropped 38 to 2, and 36
of those 38 would have been published as newly-found function bodies.**

> **The 105 are not a bucket.** Every rule above is a *sufficient* condition, so anything meeting none
> of them stays UNCONFIRMED for a person to read. **A verdict with no evidence is worth less than no
> verdict** — which is exactly why this file was seeded rather than filled when it was created.

**What the 105 are, so the next reader starts ahead:** **52** sit after a `prev_fn` that *does* carry
an indirect `jmp` whose table this reader could not locate — a second table form, not an absence of
one. The rest decode as **data misread as code**: 23 begin with `00`, which disassembles as
`add byte ptr [rax], al`, the classic signature of a data region read as instructions.

**One defect of mine, caught and reverted before it mattered.** The first write appended a 251st row
whose `verdict` column literally read *"verdict"* — **the column header in this file is itself a `#`
line**, and my writer emitted it as a bare TSV row as well. Restored from backup, the writer
corrected, and the re-write verified column-by-column against the original: **columns 1-8 identical,
250 rows.**

**Propagation:** none. **Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — the two-level dense switch, read whole, and two gaps that refused it 2026-09-14

**Scope:** the 17 registry rows whose `prev_fn` carried an indirect `jmp` my reader could not follow.
**Columns 1-8 verified byte-identical; 250 rows.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| those 17 lacked a locatable table | the dispatching code itself | **they use a TWO-LEVEL switch** |
| a dword dispatch table is `bound+1` entries long | where the byte table starts | **OVERTURNED** |
| the new rule should cover all 17 | which rows it actually reaches | **2 of 17 — the rest are not tables at all** |

### The form, and the sizing error inside it

```
cmp   eax, 0x35                                 ; bound
ja    default
lea   rdx, [rip - 0x1de704]                     ; rdx = image base
movzx eax, byte  ptr [rdx + rax   + 0x1de790]   ; BYTE index table
mov   ecx, dword ptr [rdx + rax*4 + 0x1de77c]   ; DWORD target table
add   rcx, rdx
jmp   rcx
```

**Two tables, not one** — and the dword table is **not** `bound+1` entries long. It holds one entry
per **distinct target**; the byte table maps each of the `bound+1` indices onto one of them. Here the
dword table begins at `002FE77C` and the byte table only **20 bytes later** at `002FE790`, so sizing
the dword table as `4 × (0x35+1)` = 216 bytes **runs it straight through the byte table and past the
end of both**. Bounding it by where the byte table starts is what makes the region right.

`00441970`'s two citations land inside its region exactly: dword table `00441A90`, byte table
`00441A98`, bound `0x90`.

### The two that refused the rule, reported rather than forced

**`002FE660`** — nine citations, all sitting **past** its switch tables in the gap between them and
the next body. The rule does not reach them and **I have not invented one that would.**

**`00133B40`** — seven citations spread from `00133BBF` to `00140001`. That function is **127 bytes**
and the gap to the next listed body is **over 80 KB**. So `prev_fn` there is not a function whose
tables these could be; it is merely **the nearest listed predecessor of a large unlisted region**,
the libvpx SIMD kernels. **Those seven belong with the 71 already held for the UC-1 ruling**, and
saying so is more useful than a verdict.

> **`prev_fn` is a proximity label, not a relationship.** In a corpus where the function list is
> known to be short by ~1,300 bodies, "the nearest preceding listed function" can be 80 KB away and
> unrelated. **A rule keyed on `prev_fn` is only as good as the assumption that the gap is small**,
> and this registry contains gaps where it is not.

**TABLE 147 · PAD 19 · UNLISTED 4 · UNCONFIRMED 80** — 170 of 250 decided.

**Propagation:** none. **Structural changes:** none.
