## OPUS — the A soft edge is 4 bodies, and all four are a page proving a negative 2026-09-14

**Scope:** the 46 A bodies I named this morning as the soft edge of the A surface. **The ruling that
A holds is unchanged; the residue under it is now 0.28 %, and it is qualitatively different from what
I assumed.** One registry added.

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the soft edge is 46 bodies — **mine** | whether anything else explains them | **NARROWED to 4** |
| a bare interior row means nothing explains the body | entry citations from DOCUMENTED pages | **42 of 46 have one** |
| the 4 are careless rows | what the page is actually doing | **OVERTURNED — it is careful negative evidence** |

### From 46 to 4

*"Its only interior citation is bare"* is **not** the same as *"nothing explains this body"*. A page
can discuss a function throughout, cite it at its **entry** every time, and touch its interior once
in a table. `check_dispositions` rightly refuses an entry citation for A — *"an entry-only citation
is a mention and stays in the frontier"* — but for judging how soft the edge is, what matters is
whether **any** documented page has something to say.

| of the 46 | |
|---:|---|
| **42** | are **also cited at their entry** by a DOCUMENTED page |
| 23 | are mentioned by more than one document |
| 2 | carry an **authored** name rather than `FUN_`/`LAB_` |
| **4** | have **none** of that |

**The soft edge of the A surface is 4 bodies of 1,446 — 0.28 % — not 46 and not 416.**

### And the four are one table on one page

`weather-terrain-element-scaling.md` lists **"every site that loads a `0.6f` constant"** — eight
sites — in order to support a **negative**:

> *"**Not one is in CombatFormula, and not one is the weather scaler.** The `0.6` values in this
> binary belong to movement, presentation and middleware."*

The `Owner` column reads `-` for those four **precisely because they are not owned by the domain the
page is about**. `001DC4C0`, `001ED240`, `003D8DA0` and `00336AE0` are cited **as the result of a
search**, and the page's sentence about them is that **they are not what it is about**.

> **The A rule counted four functions as individually explained because a page proved they were
> irrelevant.** That is the gameability A was tightened to avoid, in its sharpest possible form —
> and it is not sloppiness. **The page is doing exactly what this database asks of it: locating every
> site, naming the ones that fail the hypothesis, and correcting its own earlier wording** (*"nobody
> wrote 0.6 anywhere"* was too strong, and the page says so two lines above).

**This sharpens the question already with SWE2-AUDIT-SPEC.**
`OPUS-REQ-SWE2-AUDIT-SPEC-A-CITATION-BAR` asks whether A should require the citing row to *say
something*. **Here the row does say something, and what it says is the opposite of an explanation.**
A word-count bar would pass these four; only reading the sentence catches them. That is worth having
in front of the auditor before the rule is decided.

**Recorded, not just published:** `_index/candidates/a-surface-bare-citations.tsv` carries all 46
with the entry-citation, document-count and name columns, so the 4 are inspectable and the 42 are
not re-derived. **That is the second registry written today for a verdict I had previously left in
prose.**

**Propagation:** none. **Structural changes:** one registry added under `_index/candidates/`.

## OPUS — a gate refused to run all afternoon because a constant I set this morning went stale 2026-09-14

**Scope:** `check_untouched_runs.py`. **Red gates 10 -> 9.** One kit change.

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the gate's refusal meant the corpus disagreed with itself | the two instruments it cites | **OVERTURNED — they agree exactly** |
| the frozen figure was a control | what it can and cannot distinguish | **it cannot tell movement from breakage** |

### What it was doing

`check_untouched_runs` computes the frontier independently — population minus A minus declared —
and then held `frontier == 19885`, refusing with exit 2 otherwise. **I set that constant this
morning**, reconciling it from 19,909 and writing beside it: *"the constants are updated BECAUSE the
delta reconciles; had the marginals not closed, red was the answer."*

**By the afternoon it was stale.** Peers documented addresses all day, A grew **1,434 -> 1,449**, and
the frontier fell to **19,870**. So the gate spent the day refusing to run — while every figure it
cites agreed:

| | |
|---|---|
| this file's independently derived frontier | **19,870** |
| `check_dispositions`' frontier | **19,870** |
| this file's never-cited | **13,366** |
| `check_coverage_cross`' never-cited | **13,366** |

**Nothing was wrong except the number I had frozen.**

### The fix, and the precedent for it

**A frozen figure cannot tell *"the corpus moved"* from *"the corpus broke"***, and in a project whose
entire purpose is moving that figure it will be wrong more often than right. The control now compares
**two live measurements**: this file derives the frontier its own way and refuses if
`check_dispositions` disagrees. **The real cross-check — two independent derivations landing on one
number — is kept; only the frozen expectation is gone.**

> **`check_provenance` already learned this exact lesson and records it in its own source:** its
> duplicated parent hash *"was found naming GN158 while the sealed parent was GN160 — two
> generations stale, in the tool whose entire job is detecting stale stamps"*, so it now **reads** the
> parent rather than copying it. **I wrote a duplicated constant into a different gate on the same
> day I was quoting that comment back at other people.**

### What the gate says now that it runs

**13,366 never-mentioned bodies, 2,680,304 bytes, in 3,589 unbroken runs** — 88.5 % of them sit in a
run of 2 or more, 45.6 % in a run of 8 or more. The longest runs are named as *"where to look, not
what to declare"*: `0016AF20`-`0016D540` (302 bodies), `005850F0`-`00597200` (220), `008BDF30`-`008C1470`
(143). **That is frontier-attack guidance that has been unavailable for as long as the constant was
wrong.**

**Propagation:** none. **Structural changes:** one kit control replaced with a live comparison.

## OPUS — the answered-but-called-unknown rows, both halves in one file, and a backspace in a regex 2026-09-14

**Scope:** `check_answered_not_established`'s 16 rows — the only red gate with **no open task
against it**. One registry added; no document changed.

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the 16 need a person each | what the register actually answers for each id | **6 resolve without one** |
| a page saying "not established" contradicts an ANSWERED id | whether both halves are about the same fact | **2 are about different facts** |
| my classifier found no different-subject rows | one I had already read by hand | **OVERTURNED — its regex matched nothing** |

### Why the gate could not be adjudicated as it stood

`check_answered_not_established` says of itself: *"Each is a QUESTION, not a defect: check whether
the sentence is stale or whether the ledger closed the id too early."* **Both halves of that check
are impossible from its output**, because it prints the page's sentence and **not the register's
answer**. Adjudicating one row meant going to find the register entry first, sixteen times.

`_index/candidates/answered-but-called-unknown.tsv` puts both halves on one line.

| verdict | n | |
|---|---:|---|
| **ANNOTATED** | 4 | the page **already carries the answer inline**, in the sentence right after the one the gate matched — *"(answered since — `EX-1`, 2026-09-11 …)"*. The gate is matching the clause the annotation exists to correct, and the page is behaving exactly as it should |
| **DIFFERENT-SUBJECT** | 2 | the page's sentence and the register's answer name **disjoint addresses** |
| **UNADJUDICATED** | 10 | genuinely needs a person: stale prose, or an id closed too early |

**The DIFFERENT-SUBJECT case is a third thing, and calling it either of the other two would be
wrong.** `Z-11`: the page says *"What `02064ACC` feeds is not established here"*; the register's
`Z-11` answers **the scheduler state block at `01DFE0B4`-`01DFE0BC`**, a time-base triple. Both are
true. **The id is answered and the clause the gate matched is about something else entirely** — the
gate found an id near an unrelated *"not established"*.

### The instrument defect, caught the same way as this morning's

My classifier reported **zero** different-subject rows — **against a row I had already read by hand
and knew was disjoint.** The cause: writing the pattern through a shell heredoc turned `` into a
literal **backspace byte**, so `HEX` was `(0[0-9A-Fa-f]{7})` and **matched nothing at all**.
A regex that matches nothing returns a clean, confident **0**.

> **That is the second time today an instrument of mine reported a confident negative and was caught
> only because it contradicted something I had already established by reading.** The first was the
> `E8`-scanner that fabricated a CFG target; this one silently matched nothing. **Both would have
> published as findings.**
>
> It is also the third time this session that a shell heredoc has mangled a backslash into something
> else — **a failure mode I have a standing note about and reached for anyway.**

**Six of sixteen resolved, ten left for a person with the register's answer already beside each
one.** That is the difference between a gate that costs twenty minutes a row and one that costs a
minute.

**Propagation:** none. **Structural changes:** one registry added under `_index/candidates/`.

| `OPEN-QUESTIONS` | ten | answered↔prose mirror **clean**; 588 orphans still block the other direction |
| **`CALL-CHAINS`** | **one file mentions it, and only to read it** | **never measured until now** |

### The index nobody was testing

`check_novelty_claims.py` names `CALL-CHAINS.md` in a list of index files it reads. **Nothing tested
it for anything** — yet pass 29 must certify it complete and accurate before the thirty consecutive
audits can begin.

`check_call_chains.py` now measures what can be measured: **46 rows in the *Documented chains* table,
43 document links resolve, 3 defer to the previous row, ZERO broken or absent**, and **zero documents
in a `call-chains/` directory missing from the index.** Exit 0.

### Two things it refuses to test, stated rather than implied

**The header's *"documented in both directions"* claim.** The obvious test — does the named document
mention the owner on the other side? — **fails**, because owner labels are CodeDomain names like
`WorldAreaField` or `InputGameplay/UI` and **no page writes them as one token**. A page entirely
about WorldAreaField never contains the string. **My first version reported 13 of 35 crossings as
one-sided on exactly that basis, and all 13 were the test.** Testing it properly needs a label →
owner mapping the corpus does not publish, so it is reported **UNTESTED**.

**Completeness against the engine.** *"Every cross-subsystem transition"* cannot be derived from the
corpus — **nothing enumerates the true set, because that is what the database is being written to
discover.** A proxy is reported instead: documents in a `call-chains/` directory the index omits,
**the one population where a missing row is unambiguous.** There are none.

### A parser defect of mine, first

The file holds **six other three-column tables** — accessor hubs, the foe-class sightings, the
`0x80000003` predicate — and matching every `| a | b | c |` row swept them all in and reported **31
of them as having a broken link**. They have no Document column at all. **Read the section, not the
shape.**

### And `ADDRESS-INDEX` verified exactly

Regenerated and diffed against the committed file: **all 63 differing lines are attributable to one
peer's untracked `msvc-runtime-tail.tsv`** — 28 new table-only addresses, 33 annotation changes, 2
count lines. **The committed index is accurate for the committed tree**, and the difference is a
colleague mid-package, not drift.

> **Three of pass 29's four indexes were already covered and the fourth had no instrument at all.**
> That is the shape of final-audit readiness worth knowing before the thirty passes start, rather
> than discovering it at pass 29 with twenty-eight behind it.

**Propagation:** none. **Structural changes:** one kit checker added.

## OPUS — every tool the final-audit protocol names can be run, and three do not take the obvious arguments 2026-09-14

**Scope:** the 12 distinct tools `FINAL-AUDIT-PROTOCOL` names across 15 of its 30 pass rows. **No
document changed.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the named tools can be run | invoking each one | **12 of 12 run** |
| they take the obvious `--db` | each tool's own `--help` | **three do not** |
| pass 12's chain is runnable here | its prerequisite artifact | **present, and the chain is clean** |
| my first run's three failures were the tools | reading their interfaces | **OVERTURNED — all three were mine** |

### Why ask

The protocol's own cautions say: *"A crash is not a false clean, and it is the good failure. A
checker that dies loudly during a thirty-pass run costs a re-run; one that returns green because it
never reached the rows costs the audit."* **The streak resets on any failure**, so a named tool that
cannot be invoked is not a pass-N problem — it is an **N-1-passes-wasted** problem. **Nothing had
ever checked that the tools the protocol names can be run at all.**

### The invocation recipe, which is the deliverable

**Three do not take `--db`, and discovering that at pass 22 wastes twenty-one passes.**

| passes | tool | how it must actually be called |
|---|---|---|
| 1, 17 | `verify_doc_addresses.py` | `--db <db> --all` — **`--db` alone is refused** |
| 2, 4, 17, 22 | `audit_crossrefs.py` | `--docs <db> --functions work/graph/functions.tsv --edges work/graph/edges.tsv` |
| 12 | `check_layer_separation.py` | `--db <db> --fas2 <tsv>`, **and the tsv must be produced first** by `fas2_export.py <certified snapshot> --tsv <file>` |

**Pass 12 is the one with a prerequisite *artifact*, not just an argument.** It needs the certified
FAS2 snapshot `b57264ba…` — **present in four locations**, including
`work/verify_GFZ_GN160/snapshot.fas2`. The full chain was run end to end and is clean:

> 38,161 functions · owner 9,409 · domains 28,028 · **unresolved 139** · **overlap 0**
> documents half: 156 declaring a PrimaryOwner, **22 distinct labels matching the ledger exactly**,
> **CONFLATION 0 · INVENTED 0 · SHORTHAND 0**

**A cross-check worth recording:** the FAS2 export reports **unresolved = 139**, the same 139 the
ledger and `progress.py` carry. **Two independent readings of the parent agree.**

### And my own first run was wrong

It reported **three tools as "not runnable"** — and all three were **my invocation**, not the tool.
That is the **fourth time this session** I have assumed an interface instead of reading it, after
`--write` on a positional-OUTDIR selector, `--db` on two kit tools, and the `| a | b | c |` table
shape. **The protocol's own caution applies to the person checking the tools as much as to the
tools:** *run each against a known-positive before believing a zero.*

**What is still not mechanised:** 15 of 30 pass rows have no tool named, and the protocol already
says passes 3 and 5 are ones **no tool can help with** — pass 5, fresh-import reproducibility, being
*"the only pass that re-validates the parent every other pass is measured against"*.

**Propagation:** none. **Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — the protocol's tool table names 12 of 66 checkers, and a correction to what I said the kit cannot do 2026-09-14

**Scope:** `FINAL-AUDIT-PROTOCOL`'s pass→tool table against the kit as it actually stands. **No
document changed; one correction to an entry of mine from earlier today.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| *"nothing in the kit looks for a page disagreeing with itself"* — **mine** | reading the kit | **OVERTURNED — `check_doc_self.py` does** |
| 15 of 30 pass rows are unmechanised | what the other 54 checkers actually do | **several are instrumented and unrecorded** |

### The correction first

Publishing the shared-dialogs finding this morning I wrote that **nothing in the kit compares two
statements within one page**, and that `check_self_contradiction` works at address level only.
**`check_doc_self.py` exists and does exactly that**, for two shapes its own docstring names:

- **EMPTY-SECTION** — *"A document says 'section 13 is empty' while section 13 has content"*, after a
  stale sentence *"outlived the thing it described, and was believed over the thing itself"*.
- **FRONTMATTER** — frontmatter readiness against body readiness, after one document carried
  `readiness: RUNTIME VALIDATED` in its metadata while its body asserted `CONTRACT READY`.

**The accurate statement is narrower and more useful than the one I published:** the kit has an
intra-document contradiction checker covering **two** shapes, and *a heading and a table stating
different id sets* is a **third** it does not cover. **The category exists; my case was a gap in it,
not a gap in the corpus's imagination.**

### The table names 12 tools; the kit holds 66

The protocol's mechanisation table maps 15 pass rows to **12 distinct tools**. The kit contains
**66 checkers**, and reading their own docstrings shows pass rows the table calls unmechanised that
have instruments nobody recorded:

| pass | the table | instruments that exist, in their own words |
|---|---|---|
| **9** Killer observation | *(none)* | `check_absence_claims` *"test every 'nothing references this' claim against four instruments"*; `check_caller_claims` *"re-derive every 'only caller' / 'N callers' claim, four ways"*; `check_novelty_claims` |
| **14/15** Constants, struct offsets | *(none)* | `check_evidence_widths` *"each declared width against the instruction the row itself cites"*; `check_cited_site_widths` *"decode the address a row cites and compare the operand width"*; `check_layout_units` *"decompiler ARRAY INDICES transcribed as BYTE OFFSETS"*; `check_strided_fields` |
| **16/27** Enum-namespace, naming | *(none)* | `check_names` *"verify every function name the database quotes against the ledger"*; `check_named_not_cited` |
| **11** Ownership inheritance | *(none)* | `check_global_claims` *"writer claims about globals against BOTH reference instruments"*; `check_contract_globals` |
| **23** "Do not confuse with" | *(none)* | `check_uncompared_pairs` *"two functions that touch the same thing and have never been compared"*; `check_instance_aliases` *"two types describing the same memory"* |
| **19/20/21** Chains | *(none)* | `check_call_chains` (added today) |
| **28** Contradiction sweep | `check_doc_claims` **partial** | also `check_consistency` *"facts the database asserts about the same address in more than one place"*, `check_self_contradiction`, `check_doc_self` |

> **The protocol is not wrong; it is out of date, and it says so about itself elsewhere** — it carries
> dated addenda for passes 6, 7, 12 and 24 as each gained an instrument. **The table simply stopped
> being updated while the kit kept growing**, and a reader planning the thirty passes from it would
> conclude that far more is unmechanised than actually is.

**What this does not claim:** that those instruments *satisfy* their passes. Most are partial, and
the passes they touch ask for more than they check — pass 23 wants every stated distinction attacked,
not just uncompared pairs surfaced. **Naming them is a starting inventory, not a coverage claim**,
and the difference matters: this is exactly the *"volume is not explanation"* mistake in a different
costume.

**Propagation:** none. **Structural changes:** none.

## OPUS — pass 5 already has its evidence: ten independent imports, and within each generation all four artifacts are byte-identical 2026-09-14

**Scope:** FINAL-AUDIT **pass 5** — *"fresh-import, reproduce ledger + snapshot + embedded EXE +
residual; fails if any of the four differs"*, which the protocol calls one of the two passes **no
tool can help with** and *"the only pass that re-validates the parent every other pass is measured
against"*. **No document changed.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| pass 5 has no evidence short of a fresh import | what is already on disk | **OVERTURNED — ten runs are** |
| the four artifacts reproduce | hashing all four across all ten | **byte-identical within every generation** |
| the embedded EXE reproduces | all ten runs | **one hash, ten times** |

### The evidence was already there and had never been compared

`Tools/work/` holds **ten `verify*` directories**, and each contains **exactly the four artifacts
pass 5 names**: `coverage.tsv`, `snapshot.fas2`, `embedded_exe.bin`, `residual_addrs.txt`. **They are
prior fresh-import runs, and nothing had ever hashed them against each other.**

| generation | runs | `coverage.tsv` | `snapshot.fas2` | `residual_addrs.txt` |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| **GN158** | **6** | `4f1f68e6e27e` | `46f02e26104e` | `c5d4b7f7fb1f` |
| **GN159** | 1 | `27e4f8453039` | `a9cead877759` | `3188016e8634` |
| **GN160**, certified | **3** | `20911fb2e5ae` | `b57264ba7323` | `b5008f9d42c7` |

**Within each generation, every one of the four is byte-identical across every run.** Six independent
imports of GN158 produced the same ledger, the same snapshot and the same residual; three of the
certified GN160 did likewise.

> **And `embedded_exe.bin` is a single hash across all ten runs — `73461d089620…`, the shipping-EXE
> authority `CLAUDE.md` declares.** One of pass 5's four artifacts reproduces across **every import,
> every generation**.

### A three-way cross-check nobody had drawn

The snapshot hashes in document frontmatter partition the corpus **97 / 79 / 59**. The parent GZF
hashes partition it **97 / 79 / 58** — the measurement I published this morning — **plus the one
document I stamped today.** `GfzEnv.ps1`'s `$GfzParentSnapshot` names `b57264ba…` as certified, which
is the 59-document group.

## OPUS — pass 8 gets an instrument, and building it showed why most of pass 8 cannot have one 2026-09-14

**Scope:** FINAL-AUDIT **pass 8**, tier inflation. **One kit checker added (67th); no document
changed.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| tier 11 alone is inflation by the standard's own words | what the twelve such rows actually claim | **OVERTURNED — they are claims ABOUT the call graph** |
| tier 10 without a runtime marker is inflation | what those rows say about themselves | **OVERTURNED — two are annotated as corrected TO tier 10** |
| pass 8 can be mechanised | the eleven tier definitions | **two are rules; nine are readings** |

### What could be built

`check_tier_presence` states its own boundary: *"pass 7 asks whether a tier is cited, not whether it
is **earned** — that is pass 8."* Pass 8 had no instrument. Two of the eleven tiers are written as
**rules** rather than descriptions, so those are checkable:

> tier **11** — *"Call graph / neighbourhood — supporting context only, **never a primary claim**"*
> tier **10** — *"Runtime evidence — LiveLab, DynamoRIO traces, Cheat Engine"*

**2,488 claim rows carry a tier. 12 cite tier 11 alone; 9 cite tier 10 in a document with no runtime
marker.** A short list instead of 2,488 rows.

### Then reading them changed the verdict, and that is the finding

**Every one of the twelve tier-11 rows makes a claim whose subject IS the call graph** —
*"639 references to the array base"*, *"One caller"*, *"`007AD450`'s 98 callers are all
Audio-owned"*, *"Only 1 of the 585 has callers in 3+ owner categories"*. **For a claim about the call
graph, the call graph is not a weak substitute for better evidence; it is the right evidence and the
only evidence.** One row even reads `tier 11 (corroboration)` — the page marking itself as
supporting rather than primary.

So *"never a primary claim"* almost certainly means **never primary for a claim about behaviour or
ownership**, not for a claim about the graph itself. **Which of the twelve is which is exactly the
reading pass 8 exists to perform.**

**The tier-10 proxy leaks too.** At least two of its nine rows are annotated *"(corrected 2026-09-13
from 3: this is runtime evidence, not a qualified symbol)"* — the document asserting runtime
evidence in words my marker list does not contain.

> **So the checker reports both lists as CANDIDATES and exits 0.** A checker that goes red on
> candidates teaches people to ignore it. **The value is handing a human 21 rows instead of 2,488,
> not pretending the judgement was made.**

**Tiers 1-9 are not judged and cannot be**: whether a body earns tier 1, or a string is really tied
to it for tier 2, or an RTTI marker is independently verified for tier 4 — that is the reading, and
no test replaces it.

**This is the third instrument today whose first version would have published findings that reading
dissolved** — after the address-boundary sweep and the CALL-CHAINS crossing test. **The pattern is
stable enough to state: an instrument built from a rule in a document will find rows the document's
authors already thought about.** Run it, then read what it found, and expect the corpus to have been
there first.

**Propagation:** none. **Structural changes:** one kit checker added.

## OPUS — pass 13 run properly on one document, and a correction to what I claimed I had been doing 2026-09-14

**Scope:** FINAL-AUDIT **pass 13** — *"re-derive each mechanism from the body **without reading the
document**, then compare; fails if the independent reading differs."* **No document changed.**

| Claim | Killer looked for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| my nine falsification passes were pass 13 — **mine, last checkpoint** | what pass 13 actually requires | **OVERTURNED — they read the page first** |
| pass 13 is unrunnable without a tool | running it | **run, on one document** |
| the independent reading differs | every claim the page makes | **it does not** |

### The correction

My last checkpoint said pass 13 is *"what I have in fact been running all day without naming it"*.
**It is not.** Every one of today's nine falsification passes began by **reading the note or the page
and writing its claims out**, then measuring — the discipline I adopted deliberately after publishing
an instrument's output before reading the declarations it was measuring.

**Pass 13 requires the opposite order.** Its whole content is the word *without*: derive from the
body first, uncontaminated, and only then compare. **Reading first is a different pass** — closer to
pass 9's killer observation — and claiming pass-13 credit for it would be exactly the tier inflation
pass 8 exists to catch.

### So it was run, properly

Target: `18-Audio/the-five-slot-array-the-console-reads.md`, chosen for size and because I had not
read it. **Only its cited addresses were extracted** — `0020A760`, `01DFE40C`, `01F832B0` — and the
prose deliberately not read. The derivation, written before opening the page:

> `0020A760(slot)` stores `slot` into `01DFE40C`, bounds it `cmp ecx,4 / ja` — **five slots, 0-4**.
> It resets a global pointer pair `01F832C8`/`01F832D0` (`cursor = base`), indexes **two arrays of
> 32-byte records** at `01F832F0` and `01F83390` by `slot*32` resetting each `{base, cursor}` at
> `+0/+8`, and zeroes `dword [01F832B0 + slot*4]` — so **`01F832B0` is a 5-dword per-slot array**.
> Every path exits writing **`01DFE40C = 0xFFFFFFFF`**, so the selector is transient.

**The page, read afterwards, agrees on every claim it makes:**

| the derivation | the page |
|---|---|
| five slots from `cmp ecx,4 / ja` | *"the classifier manages **five** named bank slots"* |
| always exits `-1`, so the selector is transient | *"`01DFE40C` is **−1 at rest**… reset on **every** exit path, including the early ones"* |
| `01F832B0` is a 5-dword array indexed by slot | *"a dword array indexed by a small integer"* |

**The derivation went further than the page, and the page says so itself:** *"What this document does
not claim: what a slot's dword holds, what `0020A760` does with a non-zero entry."* The two 32-byte
cursor-record arrays and the global pointer pair are outside its scope by declaration, not by
oversight.

**And the page has one thing the derivation could not reach**: the console's row renderer at
`001CD262` indexing the same array, which is its entire point — *"one of them is safe only because
of a property the other establishes"*. **From one body there is no path to the pair.**

> **Pass 13's value showed up as the thing it did NOT find.** The page's own falsification pass asked
> *"Is `01DFE40C` really the index?"* and answered from the **console's** side. This derivation
> answered it from the **classifier's** side, without knowing the console existed. **Two independent
> derivations of the same fact, arrived at from opposite directions.**

**What it cost:** one function decoded, one comparison, on a 4 KB page with 3 addresses. **That is
the number the protocol needs** — pass 13 over 409 documents is not a checker run, it is a reading
campaign, and its unit cost is now measured rather than guessed.

**One thing worth noting about the target:** its `verified_against` is **GN159**, a generation behind
the certified parent. The derivation used the **current** census and the same EXE — whose hash is
identical across all ten import runs — so the agreement holds across the generation gap.

**Propagation:** none. **Structural changes:** none.

## 2026-09-17 — OPUS-REQ-STRUCT-ACTOR-RESOURCE-ENTRY-UNDECLARED-FIELDS (SWE2-STRUCT)

Three fields declared on `ActorResourceEntry`, closing its gap list to the single `+0x13`
tail byte - and the REQ's own premise got sharpened by reading the descriptor both ways.

The release path (`003DC0D0`) and the insert (`003DB7A0`) read/write the same three fields,
and the descriptor-build side (`00268850`, ScriptVM_SubmitActorRuntimeRequest) names what
they carry:

- `+0x03` `requesterWaitSlot` (u8) - desc +3 <- `byte[r15+0x11]`, the requester's
  currentWaitSlot (`002689A4`/`002689A9`); the release copies it to the re-request's
  descriptor +2 (`003DC0EA`/`003DC0F3`).
- `+0x08` `requesterManagerIndex` (u32) - desc +0xC <- `dword[r13+0x28]`, the requester's
  OWN manager index, written unconditionally (`002689D9`/`002689DF`). The release feeds it
  to resolver `003587C0` as argument 1 (`003DC0DD`) and re-files it at descriptor +0xC
  (`003DC104`) - so `(+0x08, +0x06)` resolves the REQUESTING actor, and `003DC0D0` is the
  request telling that actor to drop the entry.

## 2026-09-17 — OPUS-REQ-STRUCT-AUTHOREDTABLE-REFERENCE-CONSUMERS (SWE2-STRUCT)
CONSUMER CENSUS RUN, AND THE ANSWER IS SPARSE. Built a slot-load taint scan
(Database/Tools/work/SWE2-STRUCT/authored_header_consumers.py): a register is tainted when
`mov rX, qword [rip->slot]` resolves into the 40-slot band 02EBEF70..02EBF3FC; taint carries
through mov/lea copies, is subregister-normalised (movzx ecx clears rcx), drops volatile regs
at calls (recorded as arg-pass events, then propagated into each callee) and is cleared at
unconditional jumps - the last two fixes caught a false hit where a loop-tail reload leaked
across a backward jmp. Control passed (the known +0x0C consumer at 003281DD reproduces), and
the slot-qualification rule (same function reads u16 +0x08 and dword +0x0C) reproduces the
document's 40-slot roster within two.
RESULTS, distinguishing the three identical-rebase refs the registrar cannot:
- +0x10: ZERO consumers anywhere - no censused read or write off a header, and no callee
  reads it off a header argument. A ref nothing consumes; stays UNRESOLVED by construction.
- +0x18: ONE reader - 00238234 on the equipment header 02EBF0F8, `add eax, dword [rcx+0x18]`
  accumulating the ref into a running offset decoded by 0020E620. Per-table role.
- +0x1C: ONE reader - 0x32A25A on the grouped tutorial table 02EBF020, resolved by 0020E600
  to a counted index array ([rax]-1 bound check). Per-table role.
Excluded: hits on band slots 02EBEF70/80/88 that lack the header shape (qword stores at
+0x10, `inc word [+0x18]` - a refcounted list node of some other type). The lesson the REQ
asked for: the four rebases are uniform but the FIELDS ARE PER-TABLE - same offset means a
different thing per blob, and +0x10 may simply be unused by every table the image ships.
Gates: types_index --validate 0 errors; field counts unchanged.

## 2026-09-18 — OPUS-NOTE-SWE2-EC7-ABSTRACTDESC-48-BYTE-IMAGES (SWE2-EC7)

the difference is the instrument:

  instructions, and the literal `E8` immediate byte of `mov r9d, 0xE8`
  (member offset 58 in every AbstractClassDescriptor constructor) is a false

  mask merges them — exactly +1 overcount.

  settled by the six-rows package.

## 2026-09-18 - OPUS - storage class and embedding containment: the ownership half of the type store (OPUS-STORAGE-CLASS-AND-EMBEDDING-CONTAINMENT, OPUS-ACTOR-RECORD-POOL-OWNERSHIP-AND-FOUR-MANAGER-FIELDS)

**Scope:** the `allocation_site`/`ctor`/`dtor` columns of all 78 game-side types and every `route`
alternative in the store, measured against the shipping image. No field semantics on BattleUnit or
CharacterRenderRecord: both access censuses were dirty under a peer's hand all day.

**What the 33-UNRESOLVED figure was.** The external audit counted leading tokens in a column written
as if every type has a heap allocation site. Measured here the figure was 35, and most of those types
*cannot* have one: their storage is a static object in the image, a sub-object of a named parent, or a
buffer the caller supplies. One cell, `SecondaryContext`, was not about allocation at all - it held an
unresolved *element count* note, which is why a leading-token census scored it. Every game-side row now
opens with one of IMAGE / INTERIOR / CALLER / HEAP / POOL / RESOURCE / MIXED / UNRESOLVED, documented in
`_types/README.md`: **IMAGE 21, INTERIOR 34, HEAP 7, CALLER 5, MIXED 3, POOL 2, RESOURCE 2, UNRESOLVED
4** - and each of the four UNRESOLVED names its specific unread path instead of carrying a bare token.

**`POOL` exists because of `BattleUnit`.** Its allocation site named `00234480`, which is a linear scan
of `*(0208E688)` in `0xF50` steps for the first slot whose bit 0 is clear - an *acquire*. The block is
allocated at `00236924` through the tagged allocator `00384510` with the tag `BtlWork`, published to
`0208E688` at `0023693C` and zeroed at `00236943`; `SpawnRecord`'s is the `btlKeepCharWork1` bank in the
same function, and a second bank of the same shape follows it, matching the two `SpawnKeepImage` regions
`SavePayload` declares. Four more rows named a *constructor* as an allocation, and the rule that finds
them is mechanical: a row whose `dtor` says the type has no storage of its own cannot have one.

**`ActorStorageRecord`'s allocation, and why `(array element)` was wrong.**
`ActorStorage_AllocateAndInitializeRecords` (`002679F0`) carves ONE block through the indirect call on
`ActorManagerSlot +0x88` at `00267A79`; the single caller `0026CE60` stores it into `ActorManagerSlot
+0x08` at `0026CEB8` with the slot at `02098E10 + managerIndex*0x288`. The records are **not equally
sized** - each is `align16(ActorSequenceDescriptor[group].recordSize)` and those eight sizes run `0x2D0`
to `0x6E0` - so record *i* is found through the pointer table at `block+8`, which is what
`ActorManager_GetRecordByOrdinal` (`00358940`) does. An index-times-stride reader is wrong for every
layout but one. Four `ActorManagerSlot` fields declared UNKNOWN as unobserved spans are closed from the
same function: `+0x88` the pool allocator, `+0x1D0` `uint16 recordCountByKind[4]`, `+0x1D8` `uint16
recordBaseByKind[4]` written as a prefix sum, `+0x1F0` the block's second region. The array model
*subsumes* two rows a peer had already proven - the former `pairedWord1D6`/`pairedWord1DE` are elements
3 of the two arrays, and the sum they were read in is `base[3] + count[3]`.

**New instrument.** `check_storage_class.py` parses the route grammar, resolves every anchor to its PE
section, containment-checks every `EMBED` against its parent's declared size, cross-checks each
`EMBED`/`CHAIN` against the parent's field map, and reports the ownership-column contradictions above.
Four `--self-test` controls; a silent control refuses the run. It also earned a route verb: `RELOFF`,
`parent + *(int32*)(parent+off)`, which two rows needed and neither could say - one was written as a
`CHAIN`, which means `*(parent+off)` and is a different ABI.

**One hard failure is left standing and was not made to pass.** `PresentationEntryReferenceNode`'s
`EMBED` runs `0xC00` bytes past its parent's declared `0x30`, because that `0x30` is the container's
*header* while its own instance column puts a 64-node table inline after it. Routed to SWE2-STRUCT as a
contradiction; the other 17 `EMBED` routes all fit, with no sibling overlaps.

**A page correction and an instrument blind spot.** `battleunit-slot-pool-and-actor-class.md` said the
three allocator tag arguments point at zero-filled `.rdata` and that the `btlKeepCharWork` strings live
at `007F46B8`/`007F46D0`. Read out of the image the tags *are* the strings, and the two addresses
offered instead are inside `.text` - each is the canonical address less `0x00120000`, a second
subtraction of the image base. The page contradicted itself: its own allocation table calls the tags
real. `verify_doc_addresses` returned **ok** on the page at HEAD, counting one of the two as a function
entry and the other as interior to a body, and printed *0 documents to confirm* - it checks that an

**Also repaired:** `knowledge_db.py` could not be imported at HEAD - `fa68c18e4` left `ROOT = KP.ROOT`
sixty lines above the `import kit_paths as KP` it needs, so a step of the publication chain raised

## 2026-09-18 - OPUS - parity's 395 of 716 is partly a scope measurement, and here is the floor (OPUS-REQ-SWE2-CONTRACT-PARITY-395-OF-716-IS-A-SCOPE-MEASUREMENT)

**Scope:** every `CONTRACT_MAP` in `Reconstruction/Tests/Differential`, 45 harnesses and 764 mapped
section-15 rows. No harness and no contract edited; `parity_status.py` untouched and dirty under a
peer's hand throughout.

**The finding.** `parity_status` reports 395 of 716 testable claims exercised, and the gap reads as a
backlog of test cases. **At least 114 of the 369 non-EXERCISED rows - 31 % - are scope, not work**:
their own reason carries a literal marker its author wrote to say the claim is about code the pilot
does not contain or does not reach. `not driven` 71, `never runs here` 14, `out of scope` 8, `not
among this suite's entries` 6, `past the driven part` 5, and five smaller families. The other 255 are
UNCLASSIFIED and are claimed to be neither: **this is a floor, not an estimate.**

`storage_read` is the extreme and the clearest. Fifty-five rows, five exercised - and those five are
exactly the five claims about the two bodies the harness reconstructs, the read and the restore. Its
contract describes a save/load subsystem: a message pump, a queue, a controller dispatcher, a
thirteen-kind dispatcher, path builders, client shims. Forty-one of its fifty unexercised rows carry a
scope marker. `field_gate` says the same thing in its own words: *the first 120 bytes of 1,297 are
executed and the rest is not.*

**Why this matters to the readiness gate.** Read as a backlog the number says 321 test cases are owed.
Read as a scope measurement it says a much smaller set of cases is owed and the rest is an integration
programme - a pilot growing into a subsystem harness - with a different cost and a different owner.
**Only 1 of 45 declarations covers INTEGRATION today, which is what the second reading predicts.**

**The instrument's own controls caught it being wrong twice.** `parity_claim_scope.py --self-test`
runs a corpus negative control - *no marker may fire on any row a harness declares EXERCISED* - and
it failed on four rows, of which two were matching the NOUNS "the allocator" and "the initialiser"
rather than any scope statement. Both markers are gone, a positive guard refuses any reason that also
asserts something IS compared, hooked or driven, and the control is now silent at 0.

**Not fixed, and deliberately.** `parity_status.py` is SWE2-CONTRACT's, and deciding what its number
MEANS is not a change to make unilaterally - the same reasoning that kept me out of
`check_contract_globals` on the 27-bucket. Routed as a request.

## 2026-09-18 - OPUS - the image-backed state block's twelve slot tables, and why UNKNOWN rows are the wrong unit

**Scope:** `ImageBackedStateBlock`, the achievement/state block interior to the save image. Field
semantics only; no page rewritten, no census regenerated.

**3,862 of its 6,063 unexplained bytes closed.** `unobservedSpan386C` was 3,916 bytes of "no
censused access". `SaveRuntime_InitializeImageBackedPointerDescriptor` (`00253240`) is called twelve
times by the init path, once per slot `0..0xB`; each arm of its twelve-way jump table sets a base
`block + 0x38CC + delta` and an element count, and fills that many `u16` with `0xFFFF`. **The bases
chain exactly in slot order, all twelve** - `38CC/0x40`, `394C/0xC8`, `3ADC/0x8C`, `3BF4/0x30`,
`3C54/0x20`, `3C94/0x28`, `3CE4/0x100`, `3EE4/0` (empty), `3EE4/0x18`, `3F14/0x51`, `3FB6/0x200`,
`43B6/0x200` - each base being the previous plus its own byte length, the last ending at `+0x47B6`,
two bytes before the dword array. *Twelve exact boundaries is not a coincidence, and it is also what
shows the jump table maps slot k to arm k rather than permuting them.*

`unobservedSpan47BC`, 44 bytes, is elements 1..11 of a twelve-element `uint32` array whose element 0
was already declared as `dword47B8`. **Two independent sites, one writing and one reading, both
scaled by the same slot index:** `00253240` zeroes `dword [r14 + 0x47B8]` with `r14 = block +
slot*4`, and the row's own census evidence had `002502D9 cmp dword ptr [rdx + r10*4 + 0x47B8], eax`.
The former width was right for one access instruction and wrong for the field.

**What the ids denote is NOT established and the rows say so.** The layout, the counts and the
`0xFFFF` empty marker are proven; the meaning is not, and the per-slot descriptor table in `.data`
at `02092760` (stride 8, count word at `+2`, encoded reference at `+4`) is where that will come from.

**A false absence corrected on four more spans.** `+0x0000`, `+0x0032`, `+0x0094` and `+0x3246` each
said "no censused access". All four lie inside regions the initialiser writes, and the row now names
the memset: the whole block at `00253AA7`, then `+0x30` for `0x1F4` at `00253B42`, `+0x3244` for
`0x80` at `00253B56`, `+0x224` for `0x3020` at `00253B84`. **Confidence stays UNKNOWN**: being zeroed
is provenance, not meaning.

**And an ordering fact worth having.** The masks on `+0x3244` and `+0x3245` at `00253B1C`/`00253B23`
run BEFORE the memset that zeroes `+0x3244..+0x32C4`, so whatever they preserve is cleared again on
this path, with `002DDE60` the only callee in between and therefore the only thing that can read it.

### UNKNOWN rows are the wrong unit, and the two orders disagree

Shipped `unknown_bytes.py`. 267 UNKNOWN game-side rows, but **29,961 of 569,818 declared bytes - 5.3
%**. An undeclared span is one row whether it is 3 bytes or 3,916, so a row count makes a type with
many small holes look worse than a type that is one enormous hole. Measured by bytes:

| type | UNKNOWN rows | UNKNOWN bytes | share of the type |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `BootSingleton01F7F598` | 2 | 3,519 | **99.3 %** |
| `LegacyPs2GsSourceTextureRecord` | 3 | 86 | **89.6 %** |
| `PersistentFlagPayload` | 9 | 4,477 | **82.4 %** |
| `CharacterRenderSystemTail` | 4 | 214 | **70.4 %** |
| `SaveImageHeader` | 5 | 350 | **68.4 %** |
| `CharacterRenderObject` | 6 | 958 | **58.4 %** |
| `BattleUnit` | 31 | 1,357 | 34.6 % |
| `CharacterRenderRecord` | **42** | 253 | 13.6 % |
| `ActorStorageRecord` | 11 | 37 | **2.1 %** |

> **`CharacterRenderRecord` has the most UNKNOWN rows in the store and is 86 % explained by bytes;
> `ActorStorageRecord` has eleven and is 98 % explained.** The two records a row count nominates as
> the worst are among the better-closed in the store, and `BootSingleton01F7F598` - two rows - is
> essentially undocumented. Both numbers are printed together so neither can be quoted alone.

## 2026-09-18 - OPUS - the boot singleton's 3,514-byte tail mapped from its constructor (99.3 % -> 16.6 %)

**Scope:** `BootSingleton01F7F598`, the 0xDD8 lazy singleton at `01F7F598` that the boot table calls
"pumped three times per tick, the only one that is". It had **two** UNKNOWN rows and was the worst
explained type in the store by bytes.

**Its constructor maps most of it.** `00184F20` (335 B, called at `00189061` on the block
`00189034` allocates) builds three runs of sub-objects and then writes fourteen scalars. **The three
runs tile exactly, which is what makes them safe to declare:**

- `00808FE4(obj+0x20, 0x338, 2, 00184CE0)` - `eh_vector_constructor_iterator` by name in the
  function graph - then a **third element of the same type built alone** at `obj+0x690` through the
  same `00184CE0`. `0x20 + 3*0x338 = 0x9C8`, exactly where the next run's first constructor call
  points.
- `0062DD10(obj+0x9C8)` and `0062DD10(obj+0xA50)`. The element size is the **difference between the
  two bases**, `0x88`, not a size operand - and `0xA50 + 0x88 = 0xAD8`, exactly the constructor's
  next scalar write.
- `00808FE4(obj+0xC38, 0x20, 4, 00184CB0)` - four `0x20` elements.

**34 rows now tile `+0x1E..+0xDD8` exactly**, asserted by the patcher before it wrote anything.
Fourteen remain UNKNOWN, 589 bytes, all of them holes between constructor writes.

**Confidence follows this type's own existing convention**, not a new one: a scalar the constructor
zeroes with no reader is `PROBABLE`, a constructor argument stored verbatim is `HIGH`, and a
sub-object run whose element size and count come from the instruction is `PROVEN`. **What the
sub-objects ARE is not established and every row says so** - only their size, their count and their
constructor. Two of the scalars are worth naming anyway: `+0xD10` is the only non-zero *byte*
constant the constructor writes, so it is a default rather than cleared state, and `+0xD14` is
`0x40A00000`, which is `5.0f`.

**Unaligned on purpose.** `+0xDB8` is a byte and `+0xDB9` a word; `+0xDBC` is an unaligned qword. The
field boundaries are the instructions' and not a natural alignment, and the rows say so.

`BootSingleton01F7F598`: **99.3 % of its bytes unexplained to 16.6 %.** Game-side unexplained bytes
across the store **27,156 -> 24,226**, and 33,823 at the start of the day - **9,597 closed, 28.4 %**.

> **UNKNOWN ROWS WENT UP, 266 to 278, and that is the metric working rather than failing.** One
> 3,514-byte span became 34 rows of which fourteen are small holes. `unknown_bytes.py` prints rows
> and bytes together precisely so that this is visible instead of looking like a regression.

## 2026-09-18 - OPUS - the +0x32C4 bitmap is five bytes, not 0x80, and the conflict dissolves

**Scope:** the layout half of the routed contradiction `OPUS-CONTRA-SWE2-STRUCT-32C4-BITMAP-EXTENT-IS-NOT-ESTABLISHED`.
Routed is not resolved; SWE2-STRUCT owns the ruling on their rows, bounding the index is mine.

**Neither accessor bounds its `u16` index**, so the extent has to come from the callers - and every
one of the **nineteen** call sites in the image hands a compile-time constant. `0023F8B0` and
`002405F0` each run a switch whose arms load `0x1E`-`0x23` into a shared `movzx ecx, ax`. `002CDAE0`
has sixteen arms: thirteen `mov ecx, imm`, and three `lea ecx, [rax + imm]` **under a `test eax, eax`
/ `jne` guard that makes `rax` zero on the path reaching the call** - constants established by the
branch rather than by an immediate. The one writer, `002E23E0`, tail-jumps with the index from the
translator `002E13C0`, whose ten jump-table arms and out-of-range default were read from the image.

**Union: `0x00`-`0x06`, `0x08`-`0x16`, `0x1D`-`0x23`** - nothing hands `0x07` or `0x17`-`0x1C`.
Highest index `0x23`, highest byte **4**: the accessors reach **`+0x32C4..+0x32C8`, five bytes**.

**The conflict dissolves rather than needing a choice.** `imageByte32CC` would have been bitmap byte
8 and `imageByte330C` byte 72 - both outside the five. *Those two rows stand; the extent was the
wrong claim.*

**A third instance of one wrong default.** The page that propagated this row has had `0x80` struck
**twice already**, on both group persistent banks (corrected to `0x200` on 2026-09-11). The nearest
`0x80` in the code is the memset at `00253B56`, whose base is `+0x3244` and which therefore ends
exactly where this bitmap begins.

> **NOTHING WAS CONSUMED.** `+0x32C9`..`+0x3344` is not folded into the bitmap and not renamed, and
> the row now says the upper bound is **not established** rather than trading one unsupported figure
> for another. *Five bytes reached is a floor on the object, not a proof of its end.*

**The instrument refuses.** `Tools/work/OPUS/bitmap_bound.py` prints no bound while any call site
fails to resolve to a constant - which it did three times while being built: once because the writer
reaches the accessor through a call a backward walk cannot see, once because small immediates print
in decimal and a `0x`-only pattern skipped seven sites silently, and once because the switch arms all
jump to one shared tail so a backward walk finds only the last of them.

Corrected in `_types/fields.tsv` and in `the-save-payload-field-map.md` in both places the `0x80`
appeared; the measurement is handed to SWE2-STRUCT in their inbox for the ruling on their rows.

## 2026-09-18 - OPUS - eight per-id arrays declared where the store had one byte and a gap each

**Scope:** `ImageBackedStateBlock +0x32C4` through `+0x3844`. The store had **byte 0 of each array
named** - `imageByteNNNN`, "byte inside the image-backed region" - **and the rest of the array beside
it as an unexplained span.** Eight times over.

Laid out, the bases are `+0x32C4`, `+0x32CC`, `+0x330C`, `+0x334C`, `+0x336C`, `+0x33F4`, `+0x3404`,
`+0x3604`, and `firedBitmap` at `+0x3844` - and **the delta between consecutive bases is each
array's size.** Two of them prove that independently, from an explicit bound in their own accessor:

| base | accessor | bound | that implies | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `+0x334C` | `00315620` | `cmp ecx, 0x100` then `byte[id >> 3]` bit-tested | 256 ids = **32 B** | `0x20` **EXACT** |
| `+0x3404` | `00315420` | `cmp ecx, 0x200` then `byte[base + id]` | 512 ids = **512 B** | `0x200` **EXACT** |

**A third is bounded the same way and does NOT fill its delta - so it is declared short.** `+0x336C`
is a nibble array: `00315470` bounds ids at `0x100` and packs two per byte (`shr rcx, 1`, then
`shr al, 4` on odd ids), giving **128** bytes where the delta is **136**. *The eight bytes between
are not part of it and stay UNKNOWN.* Rounding that array up to its delta is exactly the move this
project forbids, and the arithmetic was there to catch it.

**`+0x3404` also gives a semantic, not just an extent:** the byte is stored **one-based** - the
accessor returns it minus one and treats a stored zero as absent by returning `-1`.

evidence naming the accessor and stating that it carries no `cmp` bound.

**And the `+0x32C4` bitmap now has a two-sided bound.** The callers reach five bytes (measured
earlier today); `+0x32CC` being the next array's base caps it at **eight**. The withdrawn `0x80` was

## 2026-09-18 - OPUS - an instrument for "byte 0 named, the rest a gap", and the block head it closed

**The pattern had been found three times by hand in one day**, so it is now a check.
`check_array_heads.py`: a census records an access at displacement D and the store declares ONE
field there, sized from the instruction - correctly, because a width comes from the instruction and
never from the next offset. But when the instruction is **indexed**, that field is element ZERO of
an array and the rest lands beside it as an unexplained span.

> **The check was wrong first, and the corpus said so.** Its first run returned thirteen candidates
> and **nine were spurious**: it matched any indexed instruction quoted anywhere in a row's evidence,
> including ones whose index runs over the PARENT's array of records and whose displacement is a
> parent-relative offset or an unrelated global. The discriminator is that **the instruction's
> displacement must equal the field's own offset**. Eight candidates survived it.

**And the first two it flagged closed the block head.** `FUN_00252610(kind, index, count)` clears
entries of `*(020927C0)`, selecting one of three arrays on `kind` and **clamping the index with a
`cmov`** - which is the bound:

| kind | access | clamp | extent |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | `word [r9 + idx*2 + 0x30]` | `min(edx, 0x1F)` | 32 entries, **64 B** |
| 7 | `byte [rax + r9 + 0x70]` | `min(edx, 0x1F)` | 32 entries, **32 B** |
| 8 | `dword [r9 + idx*4 + 0x90]` | `min(edx, 0x64)` | **101** entries, **404 B** |

**Four boundaries, all exact:** `+0x30 + 64` is `+0x70`, the byte array's own displacement;
`+0x70 + 32` is `+0x90`, the dword array's displacement; `+0x90 + 404` is `+0x224`, where
`achievementCounterEntryTable` begins; and `+0x224 - +0x30` is `0x1F4`, exactly the length the
initialiser re-zeroes at `00253B42`.

The middle array is the interesting one: **`+0x70` has no census row at all** and the detector could
not see it. It is declared because two boundaries pin it on both sides - and `101` entries rather
than a round hundred is the kind of detail a tidied layout would have lost.

**The first of the buyable parity claims, and the headroom analysis predicted the outcome exactly.**

> before any write and the one after only buffer-0 writes still agree, which is what a correct

## 2026-09-18 - OPUS - nothing re-reads a CONTRACT_MAP reason, so now something does

**The failure mode, found twice today.** `parity_status.py` re-reads each contract and checks the
CLAIM strings against it, so a reworded claim shows as drift. **Nothing re-reads the REASONS.** A
reason is written once, when a row is graded, and never revisited as the script around it grows - so
a row can say *"the suite does not drive X"* long after someone added the cases that drive X.
`frame_gate`'s did, for an unknown length of time, and a reader trusting the parity table would have
believed it.

**`check_stale_reasons.py`** cross-reads a non-EXERCISED reason that asserts the suite does NOT
reach something against the harness's own source, minus its `CONTRACT_MAP` so a reason cannot
corroborate itself. A hex constant named in such a reason that also appears in the file is a
candidate, because the only reason for a harness to mention an address is to drive it.

**The regression control is the reason to believe it.** Run against the pre-fix `diff_frame_gate.py`
out of `75f2c38ca~1`, it fires **exactly once**, on the row that was in fact wrong.

At HEAD: **10 of 105** negative-phrased reasons flagged. **The two most suspicious were read by hand
and are benign** - `verb_dispatch`'s `002621D0` and `status_write`'s `00387730` appear only in a
docstring, another row's reason and a `print`, never in a driving context, so both reasons are
accurate. *That noise is the price of a check that would have caught the one that was not.*

> **It reports candidates, never a verdict**, and says so in its own output. A constant can appear
> in a comment or an unrelated case and the check cannot tell the difference. What it replaces is
> nobody ever looking.

## 2026-09-18 - OPUS - the window record's destructor is a MESSAGE, and the last three unresolved sizes are not gaps

### The destructor, closed through the family rather than around it

`MessageWindowRecord` is a widget, and the store already says a widget's `+0x00` is *"the message
handler; NEVER null"* - which is exactly what `002A2C00` installs when it hands `002A6190` to the
allocator. **So the release is not a virtual call into an unknown vtable; it is a MESSAGE to this
record's own handler, and the record has an arm for it:**

    00244F00(record)
      00244F0A  or dword [rcx+0x40], 0x40          the release-pending bit
      00244F2D  lea rdx, [00915058]                whose first dword is 0x0F - the message id
      00244F34  call rax                           the record's own proc, 002A6190
                  -> arm for id 15 at 002A6904: 002A8410(record), then if +0x3E8 bit 20 is set,
                     release the COMPANION widget at the global 0209C610 through 00244DD0
      00244F39  call 00245020                      the free

`00915058`'s `0x0F` is inside the handler's own bound (`id - 1 <= 0x14`), so it lands on a **real
arm** and not the default. Read from the jump table at `002A698C`: ids run 1 to 21 and **this record
answers nine of them** - 1, 2, 3, 4, 10, 12, 15, 18, 21 - the other twelve falling to `002A6971`.
*That message set is what makes `002A6190` this record's identity rather than a shared dispatcher.*

**Not established, and named rather than assumed:** nothing on this path clears the record's own
registry slot. `002A79E0` nulls all eight wholesale, but that is a reset of the registry, not the
release of one window.

Game-side `ctor` UNRESOLVED is now **1**, `dtor` UNRESOLVED **3**.

The external audit counted four game-side types with no size as a gap. One of them,

`00467D20` releases the previous bank at `00467DC6` through `003EC8A0`, builds the element count and

`LegacyPs2GsSourceTextureRecord`'s declared size.** `003EC8D0` allocates it, `00467DEB` stores it to
the container's `+0x08` - the `[[owner+0x150]+8]` this type's instance column names - and `00467DF9`
zeroes `count * 0x60`. *A release paired with an allocate is a rebuild, not a leak.*

**And the count's two homes are explained:** `002F7380` reads `[owner+0x150]` at `002F73A9` and
copies its first dword to `owner+0x224` at `002F73B7`. Same number, copied - which is why the row

## 2026-09-18 (OPUS) - RenderModelInstance's destructor, and 33 paragraphs written from a misaligned decode

**The last open lifetime cell is closed, and the answer is that there is no destructor.** The row
had narrowed the question to "two .data descriptors, 02CA74A0 and 02CA7540, that 00477EE0 passes to
0051F9F0 - those two are where an element policy would live, and they have NOT been read". They are
not descriptors. They are the container's two INDEX TABLES, static `.data` arrays handed in as
arguments 5 and 6, and 0051F9F0's own loops give their extents: 5 entries of 0x20 at 02CA74A0 (0xA0
bytes, ending exactly where the second table begins) and 160 entries of 0x10 at 02CA7540 (0xA00).

An element's end of life is a slot release, `0051FCF0`, which **calls nothing**: it decrements the
bank's live count, unlinks the slot from a doubly linked list and writes -1 back. The container is
never destroyed - it is embedded at +0xF0 of a static `.data` root at `022C6F30`. And the function
the graph calls `RenderModelInstanceContainer_TeardownAllEntries` (`00478030`) is **not a teardown**:
its callback `00504940` *resolves* ids into pointers through `004096C0`, which this store already
names `ResourceEntry_ResolveSectionOffset`. It is a relocation fix-up, because the slot and bank
entries hold base-relative offsets rather than pointers.

Also established, where the cell said the backing allocation was not: **one** heap block, 0x17C00
bytes at `0051FAFE`, sized from the container's own geometry (5 banks << 5 = 160 slots x 0x260).

**Declared:** `RenderModelInstanceContainer` (0x70), `ChunkedSlotBankEntry` (0x20),
`ChunkedSlotEntry` (0x10), 37 fields - of which **11 are explicit UNKNOWN**, including the two spans
`types_index --validate` reported as gaps. They are declared open rather than absorbed: a 0x70 size
derived from the neighbour's start is not a licence to call the tail padding.

### The contradiction this package walked into

`CONTRACT-render-record-pool-lifecycle.md` describes `0051F9F0` as "the descriptor writer's arm
cluster ... per-arm float writes ... Interior anchor `0051F9F2` (the `movups` arm head)". The body
contains **zero SSE instructions in 380 bytes**, and `0051F9F2` is not an instruction at all - the
entry instruction spans `0051F9F0`-`0051F9F4`.

That is a mechanical signal, so it became a check. `check_interior_anchors.py` decodes each named
body from its graph entry and reports anchors that are not instruction starts: **176 checked, 143 on
a boundary, 33 MID-INSTRUCTION across 17 documents in 12 subsystems.** Eight were read by hand and
all eight describe instructions the bodies do not contain - including `00409600`
`ResourceEntry_GetResolvedBasePointer`, a **named** function other contracts already build on.

x86-64 is not self-synchronising: start two bytes late and the decoder emits a fluent, plausible,
entirely fictional instruction stream. That is the hardest kind of error to catch downstream, because
nothing about the prose looks wrong. The census, with an addendum recording that four of the 33 paragraphs state of their own subject
that "the window opens mid-instruction", is at
`_index/candidates/interior-anchor-census-2026-09-18.txt` (the `Tools/work` copy the board task
cites is git-ignored). Filed as `OPUS-CONTRA-EC7-INTERIOR-ANCHORS-ARE-MID-INSTRUCTION`
(board revision 20589), and it generalises `SWE2-CONTRACT-REQ-EC7-PHYRE-LEA-QUOTE`, which had caught
one instance of the same pass.

**A boundary anchor is not a certificate.** `001823B0`'s anchor is a real `test rax,rax` and its
paragraph still describes a mod-4 sequence absent from that 46-byte body. 33 is a floor.

**Store:** 265 types / 2,729 fields / 0 gaps / 0 errors. Game-side `size`/`allocation_site`/`ctor`/
`dtor` UNRESOLVED: 3 (all stating UNRESOLVED is correct) / 0 / 0 / **0**.

## 2026-09-18 (OPUS) - the seven children get field maps, from their MEMBER functions

A sub-object reached only through its parent's pointer slot **has no callers of its own in any call
graph**: the call site passes `parent + 0xNNN`, and nothing records that the argument was this
object. That is why the parent's slot census saw seven holes - its users hand the address away and
stop touching it. The members are found the only way they can be, by taking each site where the
address is FORMED and reading forward to the call it feeds.

**42 fields across seven types that had none.** `arg_extent_scan --via-slot --at` finds the member
call sites, then unions what each member touches off its own `rcx`.

### Depth 0, and why that is not timidity

At `--depth 1` the union for `+0x7FB0` picked up `+0x00`, `+0x18` and `+0x40` from `00245040` - a
**widget release**, a generic helper that happened to receive something else in `rcx`. Three fields
of an object that does not have them, about to be written into the store. Only what a member touches
off its own first argument is declared.

### The two censuses agree where they overlap

For `_57E0` the parent-side scan had already produced +0xC4, +0xD0, +0x1A0, +0x2490, +0x2498,
+0x249C and +0x24A2; the member-side scan reaches **the same seven from six entirely different
functions**. Neither knew about the other. That agreement is the reason to believe either.

### What the shapes are

- `_00A0` opens with **four floats written together**, then nothing until +0x52A0 - except two
  addresses taken, at +0x20 and +0x4020, *exactly 0x4000 apart*. Recorded as a question, not a
  buffer.
- `_7EA0` is the dense one: 15 fields in 0x78 bytes, four qwords cleared in a row, a float
  accumulated with `addss`, a counter four members decrement.
- `_8FA0` is 0x1130 bytes whose members touch **three qwords, 18 reads, not one write**, all in the
  last 0x30. **"It is secretly an array" was tested and is false**: the new indexed-access report
  finds none in any of the five members.

### A blind spot both scanners had

They discarded indexed accesses silently, so an object that is mostly an array read as an object
that is mostly empty. Across 4,001 functions **103 index off their first argument**, so the blind
spot was real - just not this type's. Indexed bases are now reported separately, with the caveat
that `scale` is a LOWER bound on the stride because MSVC folds multiplies into the index.

**Store:** 272 types / 2,869 fields / 0 gaps / 0 errors; storage-class hard failures 0.

## 2026-09-18 (OPUS) - a widget inside the frame singleton, and a cap in my own scanner

**A correction to a row written earlier today comes first.** `MessageWindowRecord`'s destructor cell
describes `00244F00` as one unconditional path - set bit 6, send message 15, free. The bytes have a
branch and a null check it does not mention:

```
00244F14  and eax, 0x21          bits 0 and 5 of +0x40
00244F19  jne 0x244F25
00244F20  jmp 00244DD0           BOTH SET -> leaves entirely. No message, no free.
00244F28  test rax, rax          THE PROC IS NULL-CHECKED
```

A record with bits 0 and 5 set never receives message 15 and never reaches the free. And the proc
the Widget row calls *"the message handler; NEVER null"* is null-checked by the function that calls
it. What the cell says about the message-15 path is right; **the claim that it was the only path was
not.**

### Widget `+0x40` bit 5 = do not free me

`00245020` ends `test byte ptr [rdi+0x40], 0x20`. Clear tail-jumps to `002482E0`; **set** calls
`002473F0(obj, 0)`, clears bit 1 and **sets bit 10** instead of releasing anything. That is what lets
a widget be *embedded* in another object rather than pooled or heap-allocated - the independent
companion to the bit 14 the flags row already records for the 112-slot pool.

### `ManagerSub0209BE80_57E0` is a widget

`0028F0C0` reads the singleton, forms `+0x57E0`, asks `00273A20` whether its first qword is non-null,
checks bit 0 of the singleton's `+0x58A4` is clear, and hands `+0x57E0` to **`00244F00`** - the widget
release itself. So a 0x26C0-byte sub-object of the per-frame gate's singleton is a member of the UI
widget family, and bit 5 is what stops its release freeing the singleton's interior.

### And a constant in my own scanner was hiding all of it

`singleton_field_scan` kept the first **six** sites per offset. Harmless as a display limit -
except `arg_extent_scan --via-slot` builds a sub-object's MEMBER SET out of exactly those sites, so
an object with more than six address-taking sites **silently lost members**.

| child | sites | floor | ceiling | bracket |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `+0x57E0` | 6 -> **10** | 0x24AA -> **0x26AF** | 0x26C0 | **0x11** |
| `+0x8FA0` | 6 -> **24** | 0x1088 -> **0x10FC** | 0x1130 | 0x34 |
| `+0x5380` | 6 -> 8 | 0x438 | 0x460 | 0x28 |

**The previous package asked "who writes `_8FA0`'s three pointers?" and recorded that the writer was
not among the members. The writer was among the members** - `002BDCE0`, reached from `0028E220` -
**and my cap had removed it.** It was the seventh site. Cap raised to 64 with the reason written
into the constant.

27 fields added, `Widget +0x40` extended. **Store:** 275 types / 2,899 fields / 0 gaps / 0 errors.

## 2026-09-18 (OPUS) - a singleton reached through an accessor was invisible to the scanner

`singleton_field_scan` followed only functions that load a slot **themselves**. That is not how most
singletons are reached. `01F7F598` is loaded directly by **three** functions and returned by
`00189120` - whose entire body is `mov rax, [rip->01F7F598]; ret` - and that accessor has **117
callers**. Everything those callers do to the object was invisible.

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| functions reaching the slot | 3 | **120** |
| distinct offsets | 2 | **29** |

`0209BE80`, the object the scanner was written against, happens to have **no** accessor - 136
functions load it directly. **That is the only reason the first version worked at all**, and it is
why the gap survived a self-test, a corpus run and three packages built on the tool.

### The result is mostly corroboration, which is what makes the exceptions worth acting on

**Twenty-six of the twenty-nine offsets land inside fields this store already declares** - an
independent byte-level census agreeing with forty-four hand-built rows that knew nothing about it.

Three do not, and each lands in a span whose own text says nothing accesses it:

- **`+0xC30`** - `mov dword ptr [rax+0xc30], 3` at `00184926`; 3 reads, 1 write.
- **`+0xC34`** - `cmp byte ptr [rax+0xc34], r15b` at `001E2CB3`; 2 reads.
- **`+0xCC0`** - `movss xmm0, dword ptr [rax+0xcc0]` at `001E33C6`. **A float immediately below
  `+0xCC4`**, which this store declares as `cameraOverrideFov`, the first of the answered UQ-12
  triple `+0xCC4/+0xCC8/+0xCCC`. A fourth float adjacent to three named ones makes the triple look
  like the tail of a **quad** - and the row says exactly that and renames nothing, because
  `001E33C6` reads it alone and no site read here treats the four as a unit.

### And a check that had passed all day

The store's evidence for the UQ-12 triple says *"r14 = [01F7F598]"*, but `0018797A mov r14, rcx`
makes r14 the **first argument** of `00187950`, and that function never loads the slot. Tracing it:
its single caller `0017D090` calls `00189120` and passes the result. **The store's claim is correct**
- reached through the accessor, exactly the path the scanner could not see. The forty-four rows are
attached to the right type.

**Store:** 275 types / 2,903 fields / 0 gaps / 0 errors.

### The sweep: every pointer-slot singleton in the store, censused against its own rows

`singleton_field_scan --against <Type>` diffs the byte-level census against the hand-built field
map. Where they agree each is evidence for the other; where the image uses an offset that lands in a
row whose own name says nothing was seen there, one of them is wrong.

| slot | type | loaders | offsets | accessor | result |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| `01F7F598` | BootSingleton01F7F598 | 3 -> **120** | 2 -> **29** | `00189120` | **3 gaps, fixed** |
| `020927C0` | ImageBackedStateBlock | 51 | 14 | `002536A0` | **4 gaps, fixed** |
| `01F82D20` | GameSettingConfig | 61 | 33 | - | 33/33 clean |
| `02EBF190` | BattleSystemState | 170 | 38 | - | 38/38 clean |
| `02ADD100` | FieldRecordTable | 7 | 1 | - | 1/1 clean |
| `01F81300` | PostProcessParamContext | 3 | 11 | - | 11/11 clean |
| `01F7F5F0` | PostProcessParamContext | 3 | **0** | - | see below |
| `0209BE80` | ManagerSingleton0209BE80 | 136 | 56 | - | this session's work |

**Both types with an accessor had gaps. None of the five without one did.** The blind spot was
exactly where the missing fields were, which is about as clean a correlation as this kind of sweep
produces.

`01F7F5F0`'s zero is a real negative, not a failure: all six references are `mov reg, [slot]` paired
with `mov [slot], reg` in the same function. **The slot is saved and restored, never dereferenced**,
so there is nothing to census. The context's actual users go through `01F81300`.

### `ImageBackedStateBlock`'s head

Forty bytes declared as one unobserved span, and the image uses four offsets in it that **tile the
span exactly**: a dword at `+0x00` (5 reads, 7 writes), a word at `+0x06`, and **two 16-byte vectors
at `+0x08` and `+0x18`** ending precisely at `0x28`, where the next declared field begins. Nothing
was stretched to make that land - `0x08 + 0x10 = 0x18` and `0x18 + 0x10 = 0x28` are the
instructions' own arithmetic. `+0x04` is left as a two-byte hole rather than folded into a
neighbour, and what the vectors HOLD is not claimed: `movups` gives width, not type.

## 2026-09-18 (OPUS) - the save payload's bulk copies, and an absence that is finally bounded

`SavePayload`'s 12,018 unexplained bytes were the largest open region in the store. They are still
unexplained - but the question has changed from *"nobody has looked"* to **"no code names these
bytes"**, which is a different kind of statement and a reason to stop expecting another read to
produce a field map.

### The three bulk copies

Three functions move large payload regions with an unrolled `movups` loop whose counter is **blocks
of 0x80** (`sub rdx, 1 / jne` at `002EF82D`). Count x 0x80 gives an exact extent, and all three land
on boundaries this store already declares - which is the check on the reading, not a convenience.

| copier | source | destination | count | bytes | lands on |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| `002EF7C0` | `+0xE040` | `021C8B80` | 4 | 0x200 | **exactly `groupPersistentBankA`'s 512** |
| `002EF740` | `+0xE240` | `021C8D80` | 0x400 | 0x20000 | `spawnKeepImageA` is 0x20010 - **0x10 short** |
| `002EF4A0` | `+0x2000` | `+0x4E48C` | 0xC0 | 0x6000 | `mirrorBattle` -> `imageBackedStateBlockRegion`; dest is **exactly** `battleSystemStateRegion` |

The `spawnKeepImageA` shortfall is recorded as a fact, **not as a correction**: `0xE240 + 0x20010 =
0x2E250` is exactly where `groupPersistentBankB` begins, so the declared size is right and the final
sixteen bytes simply are not in *this* copy. The two external destinations are 0x200 apart, so the
pair lands contiguously, and each is referenced by exactly one function in the image - its own
copier.

### The absence, bounded two ways

- An **accessor-aware census of the buffer** (`02164280`, handed out by `002EF640` as `lea rax; ret`)
  reaches 52 offsets across 28 functions, and **every one is inside the first 0x200** - the header.
  Nothing reached through the buffer's own accessor touches the payload at all.
- A **byte-granular** absolute-address scan of each span, control returning 298 references:
  **0 of 6121** in `+0xC818`, **0 of 3061** in `+0x5589C`, and 1 of 2761 in `+0x1538` - that one
  being the span's own *exclusive end*.

Across the whole 0x56490-byte payload there are **nine** absolute references, all inside
`002EF3C0`-`002EF7CC`.

**This is not "unused".** The bytes still travel with the payload, and an access through a base
computed some other way is invisible to both scans by construction. What is established is that no
code *names* them.

### The tool

`singleton_field_scan --static` was added for this: an object whose ADDRESS is a constant, reached
by `lea` and by `lea rax; ret` accessors, rather than a pointer slot reached by `mov`. The save
buffer is that shape, and so is a large part of the store's `STATIC`-routed population.

**Store:** 275 types / 2,907 fields / 0 gaps / 0 errors.

### A route that had half of itself hidden from its own gate

`PartyReadMachineRecord` declares two static instances. Its route joined them with a **comma**:

```
STATIC 0x02EBF3D0, STATIC 0x02EBF3F0
```

`check_storage_class` splits on `" | "`. So the whole string parsed as **one** alternative, the
leading verb and address parsed fine, and everything after the comma - a second real instance at
`02EBF3F0`, with two references in `0037C730`, the verb-scheduled driver this row's own instance
column already names - **was never anchor-checked**. Nothing failed. The type simply had half a
route, and had done for as long as the row existed.

It surfaced only because the parsed-alternative count was **one short of the type count**: 92
against 93. Separator corrected; the count is now 93 of 93.

A guard was added rather than a convention, because the failure is silent by construction: any
comma immediately followed by a route verb is now reported. It stays quiet on the pipe form and on
`ActorStorageRecord`'s `DYNAMIC` route, whose commas are inside a subscript expression and are
legitimate.

## 2026-09-18 (OPUS) - CORRECTION to the entry above, published hours earlier in `374b8386f`

That entry said, of the save payload's three unexplained spans:

> An accessor-aware census of the buffer reaches 52 offsets across 28 functions, and **every one is
> inside the first 0x200** - the header. Nothing reached through the buffer's own accessor touches
> the payload at all.

**The second sentence is false, and the first was measured with a broken scanner.**

`--static` was meant to match `lea reg, [rip -> obj]`, because for a static object the ADDRESS is
what code forms. The line choosing the mnemonic **never landed** - a heredoc ate the backslash
continuations and the patch reported success - so static mode went on matching `mov`, which for a
static object loads its *first eight bytes* rather than its address. Everything the census found
came through the one path that did work: the `lea rax; ret` accessor. Functions forming the
buffer's address directly were invisible.

Corrected: **32 functions, and 17 of the 52 offsets are inside the payload.**

### The conclusion survives - as a stronger result, not the same one

Every one of those 17 lands in a field the store already names: `persistentFlagPayloadRegion`,
`mirrorBattle`, `imageBackedStateBlockRegion`, `imageChecksumCrc32`, `groupPersistentBankA`/`B`,
`spawnKeepImageA`/`B`, `payloadSlot4E460`, `payloadDword4E464`, `battleSystemStateRegion`.
**Not one lands in an unexplained span.**

The old sentence asserted a vacuous absence - the scan reached nothing, so of course it reached
nothing *there*. The corrected scan reaches deep into the payload and still reaches nothing there,
which is evidence instead of an artefact. And one boundary is now corroborated exactly: the highest
offset touched below `+0x1538` is **`+0x1535`**, the last bytes of `persistentFlagPayloadRegion`.

The byte-granular absolute-address scans quoted alongside it are unaffected - they never used this
tool.

### Why this one is worth the space

**A silently failed patch is worse than a failed one**, and the second time today my own heredoc
mangled a backslash continuation the result was a published false claim rather than a syntax error.
Static mode now has its own control - `02EB3870` is reached by `lea` from three functions and by no
accessor, so it reads **zero under the broken form and three under the correct one**, and the
self-test fails loudly if the mnemonic ever reverts.

**Store:** 275 types / 2,907 fields / 0 gaps / 0 errors.

### The STATIC sweep, and a third addressing pattern the scanner did not know

A static object is reached three ways, and the scanner knew one and a half of them:

1. `lea reg, [rip -> obj]` - the base formed into a register. (Fixed above; never worked before.)
2. `lea rax, [obj]; ret` - an accessor. (Worked.)
3. **Each field addressed by its own RIP-relative operand**, with no base register anywhere.

**The third is the only pattern some types use.** `BattleFormulaScratch` has 45 declared rows and
**zero** functions that form its base - all 43 of its dword-aligned addresses are referenced
individually, the first by 47 functions on its own. Reported as untouched, which is the most
misleading answer a census can give. `--span` now enables that detection.

| type | loaders | offsets | against the store |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `BattleFormulaScratch` | **157** | 44 | **44/44 corroborated**, 0 gaps |
| `Mt19937State` | 3 | array | stride-4 indexing plus the cursor at `+0x9C0` written *absolutely* at `02EB4230` - both declared rows confirmed |
| `SharedGameplayLcgState` | 9 | 1 | 1/1 |
| `PartyReadMachineRecord` | 1 | 1 | 1/1; separator fixed so both instances are now gated |
| `RenderModelInstanceContainer` | 0 | 0 | expected - it is embedded, reached as parent+0xF0, never absolutely |

**Zero gaps in the STATIC population.** `Mt19937State` is the neatest confirmation: `0x9C4` is
`624*4 + 4`, the scan finds `[base + index*4]` for the vector and an absolute write to
`02EB4230 = base + 0x9C0` for the draw cursor, and the store's two rows say exactly that.
