## 2026-09-19 - SWE2-STRUCT - CRR +0x0340 is a staged model transform: the copy destination names the source

OPUS's 793335806 withdrew the +0x0340 vec4/matrix typing on the correct general principle - the
shared 0x40 block-copier 00202C70 says nothing about the bytes it moves - but the citation list
stops one hop short. Tracing the call site: 00427E78 `lea rdx,[rbx+0x340]` / `mov rcx,rbx` /
`call 004209F0`, which sets the +0x284 bit-0x200 dirty flag, advances rcx to +0x180, and tail-
jumps through 0046D100 into 00202C70. The copier moves [rdx]->[rcx], so +0x340 lands on
`modelTransform` - the proven 4x4 row-major affine slot - as the staged transform committed when
the record is dirty. The destination establishes the source's shape: the same evidence class OPUS
kept for the +0x1C0/+0x050 siblings (identity-reset), one hop deeper. The array docs independently
describe "the +0x340 pending-record swap". Row re-declared `stagedModelTransform float[4][4]`
TYPE RESOLVED / PROVEN with the full chain cited.

positives plus 17 new `readDword*/readQword*` BootSingleton rows (OPUS). Audited: all 17 are

## 2026-09-19 - SWE2-STRUCT - U-7 refined: _57E0's span is thirteen 0x2A0 claim-slot records, not forty-two 0xD0 ones

OPUS narrowed `ManagerSub0209BE80_57E0 +0x278` (8,728 B, the store's second-largest unknown span)
to "probably 42 more of the 0xD0 records the store already has twice" and rightly refused to
declare it without an indexing site, then answered U-7 negatively: all three imul-by-0xD0 sites
belong to another type, and the +0xD0/+0x1A0 pair are standalone slots (003F9F40 null-tests each
by hand, no loop). Both rulings are correct - and the span is resolved anyway, because the
question's premise had the wrong stride. The witness was the span's only accessor: 003FA39E,
the `lea rbx,[rsi+0x270]` behind `subAddr0270`, opens a slot-claim loop - 003FA3A5 tests
`byte [rbx+0x272],1` per record and while set walks `rbx += 0x2A0`, `edi < 0xD`; on the first
free record it calls 00275550(rcx=rbx, edx=0x2A0) - a rep stosd memset of exactly the record
size - then seeds +0x272 = slot+1 and fills +0x00/+0x10 (two 16B 00202C90 copies) and
+0x260/+0x264(-0.25f)/+0x268/+0x26C. Three independent agreements (stride 0x2A0, memset 0x2A0,
bound 13) and 0x270 + 13*0x2A0 = 0x2490 lands to the byte on ptr7C70. Declared:
`ManagerSub0209BE80_57E0ArrayRecord` (0x2A0, 10 rows incl. slotFlag272 PROVEN - bit0 occupied,
written slot+1) and `claimSlotRecords = [13]` at +0x270, absorbing subAddr0270; 8,736 unknown
bytes retired. The +0xD0 pair is untouched - a different shape (count word at rel +0xC2 vs the
array's flag at +0x272). U-7 refined in place; OPEN-QUESTIONS updated. 276/2960/2957/3/0/0.

## 2026-09-19 — SWE2-AUDIT-SPEC shadow-audit: FABLE VFX permission handshake (ACCEPT)

Sweep queue empty; shadow-audited the newest substantive landing pair:
FABLE `55b246327` (the per-container gate) + `adf714fbd` (the
character-side renewer). Claims verified bit-exact against the
shipping image:

- `003B33A0` (46 B, renewer) — `ecx & 0x3F` index, x0x38 stride into
  02EBD480, `cmp [entry], ecx` handle gate, and the set idiom
  `((flag<<2) ^ old) & 4 ^ old | 2` = raise bit 1, set bit 2 from flag.
  Exact.
- `0024D770` (431 B, gate) — head verified: `+0x364` nonzero -> out;
  `+0x36A` bit 0 raised; kind dispatch kinds 2-9 via table 0024D920
  (rel32-resolved, exact). Kind-2 arm: two byte-table bit-1 tests
  (02F8F23C/02F8F27C) via words +4/+6, exact.
- Kind-3 handshake verified: entry = table[low6(dword+4)]; container
  flag bit 3 up -> bit 1 not required (and bit 2 of the entry is
  cleared if bit 1 was down — a cleanup detail the commit text does
  not state); bit3 down -> entry bit 1 required; edx!=0 clears entry
  bit 1 (the consume); entry bit 2 copied to container flag bit 0 via
  `(flag>>2)&1`; `+0x39B` nonzero required to draw.
- `004210D0` (72 B) — "flag bit 4 up on the record and every
  ancestor" verified: `test byte [rcx+0x284], 0x10` per node, chain
  walked by word[+6] x 0x740 into 022C6F28, -1 ends -> ret 1, any
  miss -> ret 0. One unmentioned detail: `cmove rcx,0` when an
  ancestor's +0x284 dword is 0 (dead-record guard; semantics worth a
  footnote, not a contradiction).

Verdict: ACCEPT — the two-sided contract claim ("an effect hung on a
character is shown exactly while the character and everything it is
attached to is flagged shown") reproduces from the bytes.

## 2026-09-19 — SWE2-AUDIT-SPEC shadow-audit: OPUS RenderResourceEntryBuffer (e66f260d7) — ACCEPT WITH ONE REFUTED DETAIL

`0051EF90` (desc, src, count) — verified end to end:
- capacity `[+0x10]` and used `[+0x18]` loaded, `used + count <= capacity`
  (`cmp r9d, ecx; jbe`) skips the grow — exact.
- growth: granularity `[+0x14]`; `lea eax,[rsi-1]; add eax,r9d; div r9d`
  = ceil(count/granularity); `imul r9d, eax` rounds count up to a
  granularity multiple; `lea edx,[rcx+r9]` = oldCap + delta; reserve
  `0051EEB0` called. `0051EEB0` confirmed edx is the target element
  count (`esi` straight into the `003AB8B0` alloc call; `cmovb` against
  old capacity as the copy bound). Exact.
- append: buffer ptr `[+0x08]` through `003AB7F0`, offset by `[+0x18]`,
  copy `00861EBA`, `used += count` at 0051F002. Exact.
- constructor `0051EE12`: `mov qword [rcx+0x14], 0x800` — the qword
  store writes granularity=0x800 AND zeroes used in one instruction.
  The "not a 64-bit field" reading is correct and well-evidenced.

REFUTED (narrow): "ZERO GRANULARITY ... it grows by a single unit
rather than dividing by zero." The zero path at 0051EFC5 is
`lea eax,[r9+1]` with r9 = granularity = 0 -> quotient = 1, then
`imul r9d, eax` -> delta = 0 * 1 = **0**. The reserve is called with
edx = oldCap + 0 — the buffer does NOT grow. The special case exists
to skip `div r9d` (div-by-zero); its arithmetic result is a zero
delta, not +1. Reimplementation consequence is the opposite of the
prose: grow-by-one would diverge, grow-by-zero (with the append then
writing `count` elements past `used`) is what the bytes do.
Everything else in the commit — the two-derivation 0x1C extent, the
+0x00 "role unread" restraint, the privacy hedge — verified or
appropriately hedged.

## 2026-09-19 — SWE2-AUDIT-SPEC shadow-audit: FABLE navmesh page (fad7a2fb1) — PARTIAL: one claim REFUTED, one correction ACCEPTED

`00383670` size correction ACCEPTED — `ret` at 0038373B, extent
exactly 204 B as the commit says (prior map's 1,223 B was wrong).

`00382D10` "point-in-triangle test by three cross-product signs" —
REFUTED as a behavioral claim, with the structure confirmed:

- Structure verified: 3-iteration loop over the static edge-pair
  table at 00D112B0 ({0,1},{1,2},{2,0}); `0020E600` returns the
  vertex array base (02AEDFB0->+0xC); vertices are 8-byte XZ pairs;
  triangle vertex indices are u16s read from [r14 + idx*2]; per edge
  it builds edge vector and point-to-vertex vector and computes the
  2D cross `pz*ex - px*ez` at 0051E28..E31. All consistent with a
  point-in-triangle shape.
- BUT the sign-rejection can never fire. The accumulator xmm9 is
  zeroed at entry (xorps xmm10; movaps xmm9, xmm10) and its only
  in-loop write is `movaps xmm9, xmm0` on the cross==0 path — so
  xmm9 is identically 0 forever. The nonzero-cross path computes
  `product = cross * xmm9` = 0 and tests `comiss xmm10, xmm0` →
  `ja` requires 0 > product; product is 0 or NaN, so `ja` never
  fires. `ucomiss xmm9, xmm10` at 00382E10 is also dead (its flags
  are clobbered before any jcc).
- Consequence: the function RETURNS 1 UNCONDITIONALLY — every point
  is "inside" every triangle. A reimplementation that performs a
  real three-sign test would diverge from the shipped binary on
  exactly the points the test was meant to reject. Whether callers
  compensate (e.g., the grid lookup at 00383F10 doing the real work)
  is outside this function's body, but the commit's description
  overstates shipped behavior: the three crosses are computed, the
  three signs are never effectively compared.

- `00420FB0` verified: `test al,8` per node then `and eax,0x30;
  cmp 0x30` — bits 3 AND 4 AND 5 required on the record AND every
  ancestor (word[+6] x 0x740 walk into 022C6F28, cmove dead-record
  guard). Exact.

  setter; mirrors into `or/and [rax], 4` on the looked-up resource
  entry; calls one of two routines. Exact.
- Call-site census independently re-run (raw E8/E9 byte scan, RVA
  corrected): exactly three sites — 00429DAB, 00429DEC (inside
  00429D40) and 0042DE73 (inside 0042DE50). Matches "three call
  sites, all in the propagation and its descendant callback".
- THE NEGATIVE re-swept: all 108 +0x304 accesses re-listed. Every
  register-valued OR computes its value through `and reg,
  <single-bit>` or a bounded `lea flag*2` / `shl` — provenance per
  site: 0x100, 0x400, 0x800, 0x10, 0x20, 8, 2, (edx&3)<<0xC,
  <<0x11, <<0x1B, 2*bool. NONE can produce bit 2. Constant ORs on
  the record family: bits {0,3,5,6,7,8,10..17+,27} — none is 0x4.
  Whole-word stores carrying bit 2 (e.g. mov 0x56 at 007FC535)
  exist only on unrelated structs.
- +0x290 write sweep re-run: every render-record-family OR
  immediate is in {8,0x10,0x40,0x800,0x2000,0x4000,0x8000,0x10000,
  0x20000,0x400000,0x200000,0x800000,0x2000000,0x4000000,
  0x8000000,0x10000000,0x20000000,0x40000000,1,2,0x400,0x200} —
  no 0x20 anywhere. Bit 5 of the dirty word is never raised.
- `0041F754` calls CRT memset (00861EC0) at record creation —
  consistent with the zero-init claim.

Verdict: ACCEPT — the double dead-end holds as stated: +0x290 bit 5
never raised (propagation never runs) AND +0x304 bit 2 never set
(the flag operand would be 0 regardless). `00420FB0` returns 0 for
every record; the handshake's second flag and the container bit it
feeds are constant 0. The claim's own bound ("a writer through a
shifted base would escape them") is honestly stated — my sweep has
the same bound.

## 2026-09-19 — SWE2-AUDIT-SPEC shadow-audit: FABLE bone-history freeze correction (589c9771d) — ACCEPT

The core mechanism verified literally at 0051C450..0051C45C:
- `movzx eax, byte [rbx+5]` — the entry's +5 byte IS read.
- `or al, byte [02CA8402]` — OR'd with the global flag byte.
- `test al,1; jne 0x51CB73` — bit 0 set skips the whole entry.

So the byte the time-stop set-3 writes is exactly the byte this
per-frame update gates on — the "no reader" finding was wrong for
the reason the correction states (the earlier scan followed only
the base-referencing functions; this update walks the list head
02CA8408 and never touches the base). Set 3 does freeze the
auxiliary bone histories. The re-sample chain (00422170 ->
003711D0) and the list-head walk shape were not re-derived; the
audited region covers the gate the correction rests on.

Verdict: ACCEPT — a correct self-correction on the same
scoped-scan failure pattern as the FCP section-3 fix.

## 2026-09-19 — SWE2-AUDIT-SPEC shadow-audit: FABLE pose-sequencer page (ed33032cc), defect claim — ACCEPT

`00477610` verified — the variant setter is broken in the shipped
code exactly as claimed:
- `movzx ecx, dl; shl rcx, 6` — indexes the 0x40-stride phase
  table by the SECOND argument's low byte.
- `cmp dword [rcx+4], edx; cmovne rcx, rax` — the entry's handle
  must equal the second arg.
- `mov dword [rcx+0xC], eax` where eax = edx-1 — stores arg2-1.

Under the sibling convention (arg1 = handle, arg2 = variant —
`00477670` uses `movzx r9d, cl` + `cmp [r9+4], ecx`; the aux pool
accessor `0051CDC0` uses `movzx edx, cl` + `cmp [rax], ecx`), a
real call indexes by a small variant value and demands the entry's
handle equal that value — it can never match, so the store never
fires. The claim "two arguments crossed ... can never store" is
verified. (Under the alternative signature reading the store would
write handle-1 as the variant — wrong either way.)

The format claims (eight event offsets, six-byte records, 0x40
phase entries at 02CA6CA0) are consistent with the verified
accessor shapes; the corpus figures and the eyelid inference were
not re-derived.

Verdict: ACCEPT — the shipped-bug claim is instruction-exact.

## SWE2-DATA-? mpk slot 9 `ACTL` container decode (2026-09-20)

**MP-2 narrowed — `ACTL` decoded end-to-end.** A two-level
id-indexed record list: 16 B header `{magic, ver=1,
stride=0x16, idBound, resv, idxOff=0x10, auxOff}` + index
`{u16 bucketCount; {u16 bound, u16 byteOff}[]}` + contiguous
`0x16`-stride records per bucket + trailing aux table.
`003E8230` lookup decoded in full (id/100 bucket via
0x51EB851F magic; `id>=idBound`, `bucket>=bucketCount`,
`slot>=bound` miss). 270/270 shipped blocks parse with zero

## SWE2-DATA-0920-e tag-30 runtime expansion decode

002F6AB0's post-index tail (002F6F2A-002F727E) expands tag-30's
0x30 records into a 0x70-stride runtime array at ctx+0x1C0
(003EC8D0(6, count*0x70)). Field consumers decoded:

- dword[rec+0x0C] = 32-bit flag word: b13 colour arm, b14
  bucket (inc dword[ctx + b14*8 + 0x1F4] -> counters +0x1F4/
  +0x1FC), b30 tag-24 link.
- b30 -> u16[rec+0x14] indexes tag-24's 0xE0 table (ctx+0x1D0;
  count +0x220, sources +0x198), writes -1 at entry+0xC0 ->
  deferred alloc of dword[ctx+0x22C] bytes; +0x22C written by
  tag-33's callee 002F6740.
- b13 -> dword[rec+0x18] = packed RGBA (00466140) * xmm6 ->
  runtime +0x40 vec4 (default 1.0x4).
- colour==0 + ctx+0x40 matrix -> u16[rec+0x02] indexes tag-0's
  0x40 rows (ctx+0x188), +0x30 position vec4 transformed by
  00231A90 -> runtime +0x40. So +0x02 = tag-0 row index.
- Cross-link pass: r13d = dword[02EBB6E0] (slot bound) x each
  record -> 00466CB0(slotIdx, tag0idx=rec+0x02, seq=rec+0x08,
  mask=qword[rec+0x20]); walks the 0x50-stride table at
  02EBB6F0 BUILT BY tag-23's callee 00466E70 (count =
  dword[chunk+0x10], bound 02EBB6E0, cursor 02EBB6E4=-1, chunk
  stash 02EBB6F8) -- the same family ACTL's +0x02 indexes.
  rec+0x20 = per-slot bitmask (bit u16[sub+0x2A]). runtime+0x58
  = -1 sentinel -> first match fills, second match zeroes
  (uniqueness), leftover -1 -> 0 in pass 002F71A1.
- Tail: counts dword[ctx+0x1F4]/dword[ctx+0x20C] -> u16 arrays
  +0x1E0/+0x1F8 + bitmaps +0x1E8/+0x200; +0x20C writer is
  outside 002F6AB0 (residue).

So tag-23 supplies the slot objects the tag-30 records bind
to, and ACTL's +0x02 is the same slot index space -- the
ACTL<->YM00 coupling.

## SWE2-DATA-0920-f tag-30 per-bank consumer 002F7380

002F7380 (called on the ctx from 0026E290 when flag 0209A708
fires - a bank-change refresh) re-reads the tag-30 source
records:

- u16[rec+0x04] indexes the 0x60-stride entry table off the
  tag-26 buffer (qword[qword[ctx+0x150]+8], count dword[buf]
  -> ctx+0x224 built by 00467D20); guard <=0x3FFF; 0xFFFF is
  an authored sentinel - 10,346 records corpus-wide.
- dword[rec+0x0C] & (1 << (dword[0209A6E8]+0x17)): the flag
  dword's bits 24-31 (byte at +0x0F) = per-bank presence
  mask. Census +0x0E values decode: 0x8000->{14},
  0x8700->{7,8,9,14}, 0x9700->{7,8,9,11,14}.
- u8[rec+0x1D] = variant byte, deduped vs previous record.

Per bank-member record it bumps u16[entry+0xE] refcounts
(following word[entry+0xC] chains), keeps refcount>1 entries
under budget 00467AA0 (=0x1007FF - 3*(G1*G2) - 02CA6008 -
02CA6004, &0xFFFFF800) with cost 00466190 (byte[+5] clamp7,
word[+6], word[+8]) and type filter 00466220 (byte[entry] in
{0x14,0x1C}); survivors (ctx+0x228) get a count*0x28 zeroed
table at ctx+0x218 - the active-bank working set. Tag-30 =
authored instances; tag-26 = per-bank variant entries;

(msg kinds 1/2/0x11): create reads `msg+8` (kind) only; `msg+0x10` unread in
all branches; context built from `0051EDC0` variant + `0020E600` SP1 cursor +

**Nested index (DATA, corpus-wide).** Tags 22 and 26 carry the same index
shape as YM00's own chunk index: `{u32 count; (count+1)×{u24 off16 | u8 tag}}`,
offsets in 16-byte units from chunk base. Tag 26: interior tags all `0xFF`,
459/459 packs, 20,809 records, sentinel lands exactly at EOF. Tag 22: interior
tags all `0x00`, 461/461 packs, sentinel offset×16 = chunk size exactly.
Zero parse failures (920 census rows).

**Tag 26 — named TIM2 bank (DATA + STATIC).** Each record:
`{char[0x28] name (BGnpc_n1039, shops_*, grm010, sav010/020, dst010, lus010,
hne010, ozm010, ztc010, byu010, ene010, pla010…); u32 picCount; u32 0; TIM2}` —
`+0x28` mirrors the TIM2's own `u16[+6]` picture count exactly, all 20,809
records. Loader arm `002F6ED1` shares the tag-14 alloc/copy tail at `002F6EB9`
(tag 14 never authored → `ctx+0x150` is always tag-26's) and sets `+0x230=1`.
Copy callback `00467D20` is a two-pass builder: pass 1 sums every TIM2's
`u16[+6]` via `00536080` into `dword[buf]` (= Σ pictures = `ctx+0x224`, NOT the
record count); pass 2 allocs `Σ×0x60` at `qword[buf+8]` and expands each
picture. `00536080` reads the TIM2 header as the list header:
`byte[+0x05]` → first-picture offset `+0x10`/`+0x80` (0 corpus-wide),
`u16[+0x06]` count, u32-length-prefixed pictures (144 B–349 KB). Per-picture
0x60 entry: `byte[pic+0x13]−1` (imageType 4/5 only) → class `+0x00` via
stride-4 table `00D12520`; `word[+0x14]`/`word[+0x16]` → `+0x06`/`+0x08`
(width/height), width → `003A1FE0` → `byte[+0x02]` + two bit-scans →
`+0x03`/`+0x04`; `byte[+0x11]` → `+0x05`; `word[+0x0C]`-relative link →
`0020E620`-index `+0x14`; `j` → `word[+0x0C]`; `+0x20..+0x5F` = 16 encoded-null
dwords; gate `byte[+0x12] ≠ 0x10` (always 3 → taken) → `dword[+8]`-base link →
`+0x18`, flag `0x10` → `byte[+0x01]`, `word[+0x0E]` → `word[+0x0A]`. This is
the `0x60`-stride table `002F7380` (per-bank reselection) reads — the authored
texture bank tag-30 instances index via `+0x04`.

**Tag 22 — f32-block container (DATA).** Same nested index, interior tags 0;
records are float blocks (geometry-class). Stored verbatim at `ctx+0x180` by
arm `002F6D91`. Consumer unresolved — explicitly named residue.

## SWE2-DATA — prefetch selector contradiction adjudicated (2026-09-21-c)

**Filings.** `FABLE-CONTRA-PREFETCH-SELECTOR-IS-ZERO-NOT-FIVE` (P2) +
`FABLE-AMEND-PREFETCH-SELECTOR-NARROWS-THE-CORRECTION` (P2) against
`Prefetch-And-Json-Data/how-the-prefetch-manifests-are-read.md` §3 + §7.

**Verdict: FILINGS UPHELD, one figure corrected in turn.** Verified from the
shipped image (capstone, raw bytes):

- `0x001DA74C xor r8d,r8d` → `call 0x597970` at `0x001DA758`, and
  `0x001D9B6A xor r8d,r8d` → `call` at `0x001D9B75`: both pass selector **0**,
  not 5 — and both are the opens of the **manifest files** (paths built by
  `0x001DAB30` immediately prior), not token requests. The page's claim that
  each surviving token is handed `(..., token, 5)` at those two sites was
  wrong on both axes.
- The per-token request is the loop `0x001DA810`–`0x001DA83F` in
  `FUN_001DA610`: `mov r8b, 5` → `call 0x597970` → `0x0059BD40` (frees
  `[rcx+0x30]`, releases `[+0x40]` handle) → `0x00598100` (stream destructor,
  vtable `0x00D26C60`) → next list node. Construct-teardown-destroy, never
  read — FABLE's "resolve-and-mark" holds.
- **Independent 20-site census** (raw `E8` scan of `.text` for `0x00597970` ×18
  + `0x00597930` ×2, selector read from the `r8` setup at each site):
  0 ×5 (`0x001D8DC2`, `0x001D9B75`, `0x001DA758`, `0x001DAA05`, `0x00677076`),
  1 ×11 literal + 2 flag-derived (`setne r8b` at `0x001D6F4D`; `movzx r8d,r9b`
  with `r9b=1` at `0x006CCB53`), 5 ×1 (`0x001DA81B`), and **`lea r8d, [r14+3]`
  at `0x001DAFD8` — selector is `r14b` (∈{0,1}, the function's own flag) + 3,
  i.e. 3 or 4, NOT 24** as the filing's census figure stated. r14's upper
  bits are caller state (r14b-only writes in the function); the authored
  intent is flag+3.

**Page changes.** §3 paragraph rewritten (manifest opens vs token loop, both
selector values, resolve-and-mark, eventList numeric records); §4
`0x00597970` row role; §7 open question restated around the real selector
distribution + `0x0059EE90` route byte. Markers: `CORRECTED 2026-09-21
(SWE2-DATA)` at both sites.

## SWE2-DATA — MP-2 `YM00` tag-22 consumer + record semantics (2026-09-21-d)

**Work.** Found and decoded the `ctx+0x180` (tag-22 chunk) consumer:
`002F4520`, the method callback installed at `ctx+0x130` by `002F6AB0`.
`002F4765` is the only pointer-load of `[ctx+0x180]` in `.text` (stores:
`002F6D91` arm, `002F6B9D` init-zeroing; `xmmword [rbp+0x180]` hits in
`002F5xxx` are stack-local matrix copies, not the ctx).

**Selection.** `002F4520` walks a u16 candidate-id list
(`qword[ctx + sel·8]`, counts at `+0x10`, `sel` = arg), range-checks ids
against bound globals, resolves tag-30 source `ctx+0x178 + id·0x30` and the
`0x70` runtime entry `ctx+0x1C0 + id·0x70`, then — flag-gated on
`dword[rec+0x0C]` — resolves tag-22:
`movsx eax, word[rdx]; inc eax; mov eax, [rbx+rax*4]; and 0xFFFFFF;
add rax,3; shl rax,4; add rax,rbx` →
`rec = chunk + (index[v+1] & 0xFFFFFF)·0x10 + 0x30` where `v` = tag-30
`+0x00`. **Census correction:** `+0x00` is not a sequential ordinal — it is a
deduplicated tag-22 index, `< n22` in all 764,018 tag-30 records (only 9
packs sequential; `n22 < n30` in 447 packs; 5,714 zero-length index-entry
aliases corpus-wide).

**Record semantics.** All 348,239 records share the header
`{vec4 AABBmin(w=1.0); vec4 AABBmax(w=1.0); vec4(128,128,128,128)}`
(348,210/348,210 readable verified). `002F4520` reads exactly two fields:
`+0x30` u32 axis mode — 0 = static, skips the phase apply (338,279 / 97.2%);
1 = lane 2 only (704); 2 = lanes 1+3 (7,594); 3 = all three (1,633) — and
`+0x34` u32 period
(∈{2,3,4,6,8} iff mode≠0, else 0). The phase = a scaled timer float
(`qword[[rsp+0x78]+0xA8]` × `xmm9`), `trunc` clamped into `[0, period)` and
subtracted → the **fractional remainder** injected into the vec3 lanes by
the axis mask and applied via `00180720` — a tail-jump to `001E5540`, which
stores lane 1 → runtime `+0x1FC`, lane 2 → `+0x200`, then walks the entry's
`[+0x18..+0x20)` linked list calling `0060EC30(node, frameIndex)`. The
separate earlier apply `00180730` (the `001A9930`-singleton → `001A9B70`
family) uses
a mode `edi ∈ {0..4}` derived from the `+0x30`-nonzero test plus flag bits
7/15/16-17 + variant byte `+0x17`; `edi ∈ {1,4}` first runs `00202D70`
(matrix op). So tag-22 = a per-instance **oscillation/mover spec**
deduplicated across tag-30 instances; the AABB header and `+0x38` tail are
authored but unconsumed by the sole reader (residue).

**Files.** `the-map-ctrl-pack.md` §2.2 (tag-30 `+0x00` row corrected, new
consumer paragraph, arm row, residue), `gen_ym00_tag2226_census.py` +
regenerated `ym00-tag2226-census.tsv` (per-record header check + per-pack
mode histogram; 920 rows, 0 failures), `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` MP-2 row.

**Addendum (same session).** The four method slots `002F6AB0` installs at
`ctx+0x128`–`+0x140` are the runtime-array consumers — slot stores verified
in the ctor (`lea rax,[rip-…]` targets): `+0x128` `002F5450` = destructor
(`003EC8A0` ×8 over `+0x150`/`+0x1C0`/`+0x1C8`/`+0x1D0`/`+0x1D8`/`+0x1E0`/
`+0x210`/`+0x218`/`+0x220`); `+0x130` `002F4520` = the update pass;
`+0x138` `002F5550` = the presentation pass (tag-30 records + `0x70` array,
tag-24 `0xE0` entries, `+0x22C` → `00861EC0`, `0026E5F0` fold, matrix ops);
`+0x140` `002F5540` = `return [ctx+0x160]`. So `ctx+0x1C0`/`+0x218` readers
are the callback family — that residue item is closed. `ctx+0x20C`'s writer
is still open: zero `[+0x20C]` refs in the `002F`/`0026E`/`0037` families —
it arrives through generic indirect dispatch (92 `call [reg+0x128..0x140]`
sites `.text`-wide).

## SWE2-DATA — MP-2 `YM00` tag-0 matrix + tag-33 fade chain (2026-09-21-f)

Commit: pending — `the-map-ctrl-pack.md`, `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`.

`ctx+0x188` xref scan over `.text` found three non-loader readers, all
inside the presentation pass `002F5550` and its callee `002F67C0`:

- **Tag 0 = a 4x4 row-major transform-matrix table** —
  `{u32 count; 12B pad; count x 0x40}`; rows 0-2 basis (w=0), row 3
  translation (w=1.0) — all 390,136 rows verified, `0x10+count*0x40`
  == chunk size in every pack. `002F5550` stores the row pointer
  (`word[tag30+0x02]*0x40 + ctx+0x188`) into the output record and
  composes it via `00202D70` -> `00217150` (a full 4x4 multiply — all
  16 floats read). Closes the "three vec3 roles" residue.
- **`002F5550` per-record gates**: `+0x20` u64 slot mask vs per-pass
  masks; flag dword bit 28 inverted-enable; `word[+0x0A]` would
  discriminate `{1..4}` but is 0 in all 764,018 records (dead-authored
  branch); `word[+0x14]` -> tag-24 `0xE0` entry whose `+0xBC`/`+0xC8`
  floats are cull thresholds and `+0xC0` is a byte-bitmap pointer
  (expansion's `-1` = unset sentinel) — b30 writes
  `byte[bitmap+sel]` in {1,2}, 2 skips the record.
- **`002F67C0` = distance-gated fade**: u16 selector list (low 12 bits
  = tag-33 index) -> tag-33 authored `0x10` records at `ctx+0x1A0`:
  `word[+0x02]` = tag-0 row (position), `s16 +0x08/+0x0A/+0x0C`
  x 1/4096 (`00908E30`) = fixed-point bound extents; horizontal
  distance `sqrt(dx^2+dz^2)` (`00861F14` thunk) + dy check vs the
  row's `+0x30` translation; edge-writes the state dword at runtime
  `+0x04` and integrates `f32[+0x08]` — runtime record is
  `{u32 enable; i32 state; f32 accum}`, a hysteresis fade timer.
- Chain: tag-30 (+0x02, b30) -> tag-29 `word[+0x02]` -> tag-33 ->
  tag-0 matrix — instance -> fade-group -> node transform.

Residue unchanged: `ctx+0x20C` writer, tag-30 `+0x16`/`+0x28`/`+0x2C`.

## SWE2-DATA — MP-2 `ACTL` member-object charge timer + `02EBF420` base fix (2026-09-21-j)

Commit: pending — `the-map-ctrl-pack.md`, `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`.

Disassembled the full member-op family behind `+0x08`. All eight
resolvers `lea` the group table at **`02EBF420`** — mechanically
resolved; the doc's earlier `02E2F420` has zero `.text` references and
is corrected. Table = **5 groups x 0x50** (`0037A450` walks
`02EBF420`..`02EBF5B0`; `0037B230` initializer rejects idx > 4 and
zeroes `+0x00..0x3F`, sets `f32[+0x40/44/48]=1.0`, `byte[+0x4C]=0`).

Member objects are `0x70`-stride off `qword[group+0x00]` (walk bound =
`word[objArray+0xA]`). Field decode:

- `obj+0x12` kind: `== 2` gates `0037A450`, `0037A270`, `0037A500`,
  `0037B030`.
- `obj+0x13` b0 = suspend (`0037B0F0` set / `0037B190` clear; skips
  charge, pending-test, snapshot, traversal).
- `obj+0x13` b1 = charging enabled (`0037A130` clear / `0037A1D0` set).
- `obj+0x13` b2 = re-arm on overflow (`0037A310` clear / `0037A3B0`
  set): overflow -> acc=0, else clamp at limit.
- `obj+0x28` f32 limit; `obj+0x2C` f32 accumulator charged **+1.0**/tick
  by `0037A450`; `0037A500` stores `+0x28`->`+0x2C` (mark spent);
  `0037A270` zeroes acc; `0037B030` returns `+0x28 > +0x2C` (pending).

So `003E8C50` activate = `{b0=1,b1=0,b2=0}` suspended, `003E8690` =
`{b0=0,b1=1,b2=0}` charging, and the query mask's `0x08` bit = "member
still charging". Residue: the upstream consumer of a completed charge,
the `+0x28` limit writer, non-2 kinds.

Addendum to 2026-09-21-j: `w0` bit3's reader also closed — `003E8020`'s
tail folds `w0 & 0xC` (bits 2-3) with bit1 into the re-activation
predicate `ecx = (w0&0xC)!=0 ? !bit1 : bit1`; bit1 is the
`003E85B0`/`003E8690` alternator (`r14w = 0xFFFD`). The
`003E8890`/`003E8860` verb pair (`00357100`/`00357490` tails) drives
bit3 = the override half of that field.

## SWE2-DATA — MP-2 `SP1` `01F83530` re-attributed to the universal decode base (2026-09-21-m)

Commit: pending — `the-map-ctrl-pack.md`, `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`, `SWE2-DATA.md`.

Scope: the SP1 weather-fallback's `+0x04`/`+0x20` read and the named
residue "what writes the cursor at `01F83530`".

- `00363B40` fallback re-traced: `rbx = movsxd(eax) + qword[022CBAF0]`
  where `eax = 0020E600(dword[SP1+0x04])` — i.e. `SP1 + low32(listBase +
  qword[01F83530])`. With the decode base zero the expression is
  `SP1 + 0x20`, the `{u32 count; i32 idx[]}` index-list region. The
  variant selector is `ebp = 00265920() - 1`, applied after the walk to
  the deduplicated gather array at `022CBB58` (count `022CBB70`).
- `01F83530` is the engine-wide `0020E600`/`0020E620` offset-decode base
  (~815/~279 callers — the neighbours pass §4c hub), **not** a sound
  cursor as the earlier paragraph claimed. Its writer question is
  already CD-2/UQ-83 territory: BSS-zero, no rip-relative store, no
  `lea`, no stored pointer. Independently re-verified and extended this
  pass: no absolute-addressing form, no rip-relative store overlapping
  the qword, and no intra-function `lea`-base + displacement access
  reaches it — the address is never materialised in-image.
- Residue wording corrected accordingly; the writer half stays open only
  as CD-2's external-write edge, which is outside SP1's scope.

Residue: tag-30 `+0x16`/`+0x28`/`+0x2C`, SP1 listener interiors +
`+0x1C` + prefix list, ACTL `+0x28` limit writer + charge-consumer
upstream + non-2 `obj+0x12` kinds.

## SWE2-DATA — MP-2 `ACTL` member objects are authored `LGT2` records (2026-09-21-n)

**Claim.** The `02EBF420` five-group × `0x50` table is the **`LGT2` runtime**, and
the `0x70`-stride "member objects" the ACTL `+0x08` targets drive are **authored
`LGT2` records inside the slot-17 block** — the `+0x28` "charge-limit writer"
question closes as authored data.

- `0037AA90(block, group)` gates on `dword[block]==0x3254474C` (`'LGT2'`),
  resets the group via `0037B230`, and stores the block itself at `group+0x00`.
  Callers: the slot-17 binder (`02ADD090`, group 0, alongside `003DE920`) and
  `0032F1B0(idx)`, which installs `qword[022C6E20 + idx*8]` into groups 1–4.
  `0037AA50(idx)` clears the group's pointers; `0037ACA0`/`0037ACD0` are the
  group-0 gates called from `003DE920`.
- Members are inline: `member[i] = block + i*0x70`, `i < u16[block+0x0A]` —
  member[0]'s first 0x10 bytes carry the file header (`'LGT2'`, `u16
  subChainOff @+0x04`, `u16 memberCount @+0x0A`). `subChainOff ==
  0x10 + count*0x70` in all 212 packs; a `{u16 size, u16 tag}` sub-record
  chain (8-way jump table `0x37AC7C`) fills `group+0x08`/`+0x10`/`+0x18`/
  `+0x20`/`+0x28`/`+0x30`/`+0x38`: tag0→+0x08, tag1→+0x10, tag2→+0x18 (+
  element-byte clear + `0037A9B0`), tag3→+0x20 (objIndex table), tag4 skipped,
  tag5→+0x38 (`0020E620` offset fixup pass), tag6→+0x28 (memberId→objIndex
  search table), tag7→+0x30. Corpus tags: {3:212, 5:212, 6:211, 0:198,
  2:123, 7:20}; tags 1/4 never appear.
- `+0x28`/`+0x2C` are **authored unions**: on kind-2 members (`+0x12`==2, 50 of
  5,860 members) `+0x28` is a real f32 limit (100.0×32, 10.0×16, 240.0, 30.0)
  and `+0x2C` the authored-0 accumulator; on kind 0/1 both carry packed
  non-float payloads (`0x00FF00FF`, `0x00460050`, …) that `0037A450` never
  reads because it gates on kind==2 first. Member `+0x12` kinds are authored
  {0: 5,157, 1: 653, 2: 50} — kinds 0/1 are simply non-chargeable classes.
- Post-install fixups: `member[i]+0x31` remapped through `01EF94E4` when <6;
  group-0 members get `member+0x37 |= 0x20`.

## 2026-09-21 SWE2-DATA — MP-2: SP1 listener grid, variant selector, `+0x1C` dead-data closure

- `SP1+0x08` resolves to **one 0x220 listener-grid record** in all 456 packs:
  `{f32 cellW; f32 cellH; f32 minX; f32 minZ; u32 16; u32 16; u16 grid[256]}`.
- `00362E50` is the evaluator: bounds-checks the listener (x,z) against
  `origin + count*cellSize`, divides and clamps to cell indices, and returns
  `SP1 + u16[+0x20 + 2*(idxX + idxZ*countZ)]` (0 when outside/empty). Cell
  offsets name **bit15-terminated u16 emitter-index lists** inside the `+0x20`
  region — the same list encoding `003631B0` walks (`&0x7FFF` entries index
  `word[emitIndex+2+i*2]` record offsets). So `+0x20` mixes two list kinds:
  the `{u32 count; i32 idx[]}` weather-variant lists at its head, and one
  per-cell emitter list.
- Corpus: 0 bad cell offsets, 0 out-of-range entries across 456 packs;
  116,736 cells total, 39,080 empty (33.5%); nonempty lists 1-17 entries
  (1-dominant, 57,378).
- The per-frame driver (`0x362ACE` body): mark every indexed emitter
  (flag bit6) → `00362E50` listener eval → `003631B0` over the cell's list,
  then over the arena-head default list (`{0x8000}` = emitter 0 alone) →
  `002DF410(1, 0xB4, idx)` dispatches the winning voice into `022CBA80` →
  flag bit3 cleared on all.
- `00265920` closes: it is the already-named
  `WorldField_GetCurrentWeatherSlot1To3WithDebugOverride` —
  `0017D490()` = `dword[settings singleton 01F81428 +0xAAC]`
  (debugWeatherSlotOverride) wins when positive, else
  `byte[002EF2B0()+0x1060]` = save-image `currentWeatherSlot` +1
  (weather-slot-state-model.md). It indexes both the emitter `+0x0C`
  volume-percent triple and the `+0x20` weather-variant lists.
- Emitter `+0x1C` is **dead authored data**: zero `+0x1C` accesses anywhere
  in the consumer family (0x362A..0x3642, `00361810`, `00361DE0`,
  `00362230`, `003623C0`, `00363F30`, `00363FD0`, `003638B0`); the
  1.0-dominant 0.03-0.9 scalar shape fits a retired pitch/rate multiplier.

Evidence class: **NATIVE/STATIC** (evaluator + driver bodies read whole) +
corpus census over all 456 SP1-bearing packs (`gen_sp1_census.py` /
`members/sp1-census.tsv`).

## 2026-09-21 SWE2-DATA — MP-2: LGT2 member `+0x12` kind semantics + `003CC5F0` curve evaluator

- `0037A5B0(member+0x10, group)` is the channel evaluator, gated on
  `member+0x13` bit1, dispatching on `member+0x12`:
  - **kind 0** (5,157/5,860 members): no arm — `+0x30`/`+0x34`/`+0x38` stay at
    their authored f32 values. Static light.
  - **kind 1** (653): s16 lerp — `out[k] = s16[+0x14+2k] +
    t*(s16[+0x28+2k] - s16[+0x14+2k])`, scaled 1/128 (`0x08C5B34`), stored
    `+0x30`/`+0x34`/`+0x38`. `t = 00466BF0()` = active `02EBB6E0` tag-23
    slot's `f32[obj+0xA8] * 0.01` — the same slot family ACTL `+0x02` ids
    index. Kind-1 lights fade on the tag-23 timeline.
  - **kind 2** (50): `+0x14`/`+0x16`/`+0x18` are three consecutive i16
    indices (i,i+1,i+2 — all 50 records, groups spaced 4 apart) into the
    tag-5 u32 offset table (`group+0x38`); each offset `0020E600`-decodes to
    a `003CC5F0` piecewise-cubic curve evaluated at `f32[member+0x2C]` (the
    charge accumulator), clamped [-1,1] -> `+0x30`/`+0x34`/`+0x38`.
- `003CC5F0(curve, t, &out)` decoded: `{u32 @0; u32 keyFlag@4; f32 tFirst@8;
  f32 vFirst@0xC; f32 tEnd@0x10; f32 vEnd@0x14; keys @+0x38 stride 0x24 =
  {f32 span@+0; ...; f32 c3@+0x28; f32 c2@+0x2C; f32 c1@+0x30; f32 c0@+0x34}}`.
  t<tFirst -> vFirst; t>tEnd -> vEnd; else t/tEnd walks key spans and
  evaluates c0 + f*c1 + f^2*c2 + f^3*c3 in the hit key.
- Census: all 50 kind-2 members carry consecutive index triples; all 150
  indices in tag-5 table bounds; tag-5 bodies are mod-4 (u32 offsets) in all
  212 packs; all 123 tag-2 records have count=0 (20-byte bodies) — the
  `0037AF4D` kind-gated entry walk is dead on shipped data.
- Correction: the kind byte read at `0x37AF23` belongs to tag-2 table
  entries (`{u32 pad; u32 count; {u16,u8,u8,u16,u16}[]}` at `group+0x18`),
  not member `+0x12` — member-kind reads are the `0037A5B0` dispatch plus
  the `==2` charge gates.
- `+0x30`/`+0x34`/`+0x38` = the output channel triple; `member+0x30`
  pointers are gathered into `02EBF5C0` by the `0037AExx` collection pass.

Evidence class: **NATIVE/STATIC** (`0037A5B0`, `003CC5F0`, `00466BF0`,
`0037AF4D` bodies read whole) + corpus census (212/212 LGT2 blocks, 5,860
members, 123 tag-2 bodies, all 50 kind-2 index triples).

## 2026-09-22 SWE2-DATA — UQ-76 closed: type-6 items are blanked text slots (embedded-MRP census artifact)

- Extended the typed-list type-id census to the embedded half of the
  corpus: new `members/gen_listtype_census_embedded.py` +
  `listtype-census-embedded.tsv` walk all **228 `MRP` units inside the
  ten locale `packfiles/mrppack_ys.bin` archives** (fixed 32-slot offset
  table, `0xFFFFFFFF` unused slots; 23 units in the nine normal packs,
  21 in `in_sdver`). Every unit validated: `MRP\0` magic, outer-table
  bounds, `sum(count)` item walk landing on the unit's own `+0x08`
  items-blob end within a zero pad. **Zero malformed units, zero walk
  misses.**
- Embedded histogram {1: 2396, 2: 17088, 4: 1997, 5: 3001, 6: 46,
  7: 258, 8: 537} over 6,207 records / 25,323 items; combined with the
  116 standalone files {1: 2661, 2: 20181, 4: 2017, 5: 4484, 6: 46,
  7: 278, 8: 879} over 7,665 records / 30,546 items — matching the
  atlas-name census's 30,546-item total exactly.
- **Type 6 read:** all 46 occurrences are 0x18-byte items in the type-5
  text shape — `{s16 x,y; u16 w,h; u32 colour 0x80808080; u8 0x64
  opacity; 3 zero pad; u32 stringId = 0xFFFFFFFF}` — i.e. a text item
  authored with no string (`+0x14 = -1`, the type-5 no-string
  sentinel). Type 6 is the compiler's disabled-text placeholder; type 3
  is never emitted anywhere; type 9 likewise ships zero items. That
  closes UQ-76's "why two empty ids": 6 is authored (a blanked text
  slot), 3 is not.
- MP-2 slot-15 residue reduced to nothing slot-15-specific.

Evidence class: authored-data corpus census, reproducible
(`gen_listtype_census_embedded.py`), cross-checked against the
`002432B0` decoder body's count-plus-length walk.

Commit: pending — `a-typed-list-measured-once-and-built-in-one-allocation.md`,
`members/{gen_listtype_census_embedded.py, listtype-census-embedded.tsv}`,
`the-map-ctrl-pack.md`, `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`, `SWE2-DATA.md`.


- ACTL mask-bit `0x08` upstream CLOSED (2026-09-22, same package line):
  there is no stored bit — `003E8350` composes the mask live.
  `003E82F0(id)` resolves the record (`003E8230`), computes
  `aux = actl + word[+0x0E]`, fetches the variant via `00265920`, then
  `003E8350(rec, aux, variant)` returns `{1: w0 bit4 was-active;
  2: +0x02 slot-live via 004735E0; 4: +0x0E flag-slot 0026FDB0==2;
  8: +0x08 member charge pending; 0x10: +0x10 obj 00362E30 bit0}`.
  The `0x08` arm: `+0x08` bit14 -> `003E8190` list-any over the aux
  row's member ids (callback `003E82A0` = two-instruction
  `0037B030(0, id)` trampoline, early-exit on first nonzero); bit14
  clear -> `0037B030(0, id)` direct. `0037B030` itself runs the
  tag-6 -> tag-3 two-hop (memberId -> outIdx -> memberArrayIdx) and
  returns `member+0x28 > member+0x2C` on kind-2 unsuspended members;
  a tag-6 miss defaults to `tag3[0]`. The effective "setter" is the
  already-documented `0037A450` +1.0/tick accumulator vs the authored
  `+0x28` limit. Evidence: NATIVE/STATIC bodies of `003E82F0`,
  `003E8350`, `003E82A0`, `003E8190`, `0037B030`, `00362E30`,
  `004735E0`, `0026FDB0` read whole.

## 2026-09-22 SWE2-DATA — handbook index family: hctg/hchk/hdat decoded end-to-end

New page `hchk-hctg-hdat-handbook-indexes.md` closes the three
sibling formats that wrap the `himg` page bundles. Corpus: all 54
`hchk` + 101 `hdat` + 54 `hctg` files across 9 locales parse clean;
`hchk.count == hctg.u16[+0x0E] == Σ hdat.count` per family with
zero violations; `hdat +0x08` is the base-ordinal running total
(zero violations across all 101 files). Native bindings:

- **Resource-id enumeration closed.** `hctg +0x14` = the family's
  `hdat` file count (native: `005773D2` stores `word[+0x14]+2` as the
  first `himg` delta); deltas run `.bin`=0, `hchk`=1, `hdat`=2..,
  `himg` after. The himg page's `+0x14` unbound note is resolved.
- **`hctg`** = `{tag, aux region, 12-byte {textId; group; index}
  record table at word[+0x0A], count at +0x0E}` plus a monster-only
  `{u16 count; u16 relOff[]}` tail indexing 8-byte aux records.
- **`hchk` non-monster record** = an 8-byte four-slot conjunctive
  gate (`00575E80`): save nibble `+0x336C` == val, save bit `+0x334C`
  set, `0032A8A0` gate on `+0x14F4`, and `i16 global_flag[0] >= w6`
  (the scenario-flag word 0 at `02098E58` — story progress). Story
  thresholds are monotonic across all locales. **`hchk` monster
  record** = `u16[8]`: `v[0..6]` per-slot operands, `v[7]` mode bits
  selecting kill-count (`00315420`, save `+0x3404`) vs scenario-flag
  thresholds via `00576E30`/`00576860`.
- **Sync pass `00577550`** (from panel message arms `0056F79B`,
  `0056FB5C`, `00571FC1`, `005750AF`) persists predicate results into
  the save `+0x32CC` bit array (`00315910`, categories via
  `00D23750`) and monster slot flags into `+0x3604` bytes
  (`00315AD0` bank 6); `00576920` reads them back for tab counts and
  the new-entry badge. This binds save-block family A = the unlock
  flags (FG-1 narrowed).

Residual: `hctg` `+0x08`/`+0x0C`/`+0x10`/`+0x12`/`+0x16` field names,
the aux-region interior, `hchk +0x0A`/`+0x03`, and `hdat` record
interiors past the `12+4k` envelope are listed as open items on the
new page. Files: `hchk-hctg-hdat-handbook-indexes.md` (new),
`himg-handbook-image-bundles.md`, `the-handbook-screen.md`,
`OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` (FG-1), `SWE2-DATA.md`.

## 2026-09-22 SWE2-DATA — hctg aux region: conditional-caption table decoded

Follow-on to the handbook-index package. `00576A50` is the aux-table
resolver: `hctg +0x18` = `u32 textId[word[+0x12]]` (message-table ids
0x11495–0x116E5, `0xFFFFFFFF` = none) followed by a `{u16 count;
u16 relOff[]}` blob index — only monster ships blobs (32 = the
conditionally-revealed captions). Blob = `{u8 lo4|nCond<<4; u8 nNav;
u16 condId[nCond]; u16 navimapId[nNav]}`: each condId probed via
`00309EC0` (encoded-id set), each navimapId vs the current map
(`003779F0`/`003148F0`, visited via `00255120`/`00255060(..,0x20)`).
Any pass → `002F9920(idTable[i])`; all fail → `002F9860(0x3EC)` =
the locked placeholder caption. Both helpers are reciprocal-hash
text-id lookups (28 buckets). hctg `+0x12` = captionN bound;
`+0x0C` = aux-region offset (chapter/ramp map, partially read).
Doc + handbook-screen section updated; residue list narrowed.

## 2026-09-22 SWE2-DATA — hctg monster tail reader found: 005760A0 detail resolver

The detail-panel descriptor resolver `005760A0(out, recIdx)` (companion
`00576030` fills the family half from bound object `root+0x108`:
`byte[obj+0xD2]` = the family ordinal, `hctg +0x08>>4`, `+0x12`,
`+0x0E`, `+0x10`). Key decodes:

- **The monster hctg tail IS read** — `0x57625F` computes
  `hctg + word[+0x0A] + word[+0x0E]·12` = the `{u16 count; u16 relOff[]}`
  tail, bounds-checks recIdx, dereferences relOff[recIdx], reads byte 0
  (= v0) as the count of hchk slots to materialize via
  `00576860(root, fam, recIdx, slot)` into `out+0x18+slot`. So tail `v0`
  = the monster record's active predicate/display slot count — which is
  why it equals the hdat `strCount` byte 384/384 (the strOff list renders
  those slots). `v1`/`v2`/`v3` are NOT read by this path.
- Name resolution split: families 0–4 `002F9920(textId)` (reciprocal-hash
  text table); monster `002B58B0(003214B0(textId), 0)` — monster textId is
  a `bank:index` packed word into the battle-text banks `02EBF170`
  (`003214B0`'s sole caller is this function — matches the bank-table
  page's note).
- Esper subtitle path: `textId ∈ [0x4210,0x421C]` — exactly 13 monster
  records/locale (the Espers) — indexes a 13-dword `.rdata 00D23790`
  table; `entry + 0x106` → `0035D330` encoded-id row → `row+0x18` name →
  `002B58B0` → `out+0x08`.
- `out+0x14` = `byte[rec+0xA]` — a monster-only flag that is 1 exactly on
  the 172 records whose tail `v3 ∈ {0,1}` (corpus-exact, locale-invariant)
  = the "shows kill count" category marker; `out+0x16` = live kill counter
  `00315420(recIdx)` (save `+0x3404`, −1→0), monster only.
- `hchk +0x0A` shown locale-invariant: 18 for the four lore families, 0
  tutorial/monster — a per-family constant, not an hdat count; consumer
  still unbound.

Doc `hchk-hctg-hdat-handbook-indexes.md` (record +0x0A flag, tail reader,
detail-resolver table) + `the-handbook-screen.md` updated.

## 2026-09-22 SWE2-DATA — hdat strBlob reader 00577A40: embedded op-programs, dead-on-ship

`00577A40(root, slot)` resolves the bound `hdat` resource
(`root+0x110` object; `word[obj+0xCE]` = selected record's global
ordinal, window-checked `[base@+8, base+count@+0xA)`), walks
`recOff[]` at `+0x12`, bounds `slot < strCount`, lands on
`stringsOff + strOff[slot]`. It interprets each entry as
`{u8 tag=4; u8 0; u8 nOps; u8 0; {op,target,arg,pad}[nOps]}` and
executes ops as save-bank writes: `op0` `00315CD0(t, clamp(a,0,15))`,
`op1` `00315A20(t, a==1)`, `op2` `00315CD0(t, min(nib[t]+a,15))`,
`op3` `00315CD0(t, max(nib[t]-a,0))` — the same `+0x336C`/`+0x334C`
banks `hchk` predicates read. Corpus: all 12,168 shipped entries carry
`nOps=0` (header `04 00 00 00`, then section-002-encoded NUL text) —
the executor is dead-on-ship machinery; the per-record `strOff[]`
list is therefore the entry's program/text table, not display strings.
No direct callers (indirect panel dispatch). Doc's hdat section,
buffer graph (`+0x110` = bound hdat), and residue updated.

## 2026-09-22 SWE2-DATA — hctg page-map decode: +0x0C/+0x10/+0x16 all bound natively

`00575DD0(root, kind, pageIdx)` = the page→image request: bounds
`pageIdx < hctg.word[+0x10]` (pageCount), reads
`word[hctg + word[+0x0C] + pageIdx·2]` — so `+0x0C` = file offset of a
`u16[pageCount]` page→resource-slot map (non-decreasing, 0..+0x16−1,
`0xFFFF` checked but never ships; single 0 pad u16 in non-monster
files) — into the shared `{u8 kind; u16 sel; u16 idx}` descriptor →
`00575A50` widget dispatcher → loader `00575C30`, which computes
`resource id = word[00D23740 + kind·2] + word[widget+0xCA] + sel` —
`sel` = resource-delta slot; for the himg path `+0xCA` =
`hctg.word[+0x14]+2` (first himg delta). `00575DD0` then calls
`00575B80` on `root+0x118` — bound-object roles now complete:
`+0x108` hctg / `+0x110` hdat / `+0x118` himg. Corpus: map max =
`+0x16`−1 on all 54 files → `+0x16` = resource-slot count (monster
192 ↔ 192 two-page himg files; story 17 slots vs 26 files — manifest
slot≠file ordinal, open). Also `00575D10` (content request) reads
`word[rec+6]` = record +0x04's high u16 — so the record's group field
is `{u16 lo → detail desc +0x10; u16 hi → request sel}`.
`00575A50` = the widget dispatcher: kind check vs `obj+0xD2`, dedup
`desc.sel` vs `obj+0xCC`, queue ring at `+0xD6`/`+0xD3`.

## 2026-09-22 SWE2-DATA — hctg record +0x04 fully bound: {u16 group; u16 hdatFile}

Follow-on to the page-map decode: `word[rec+6]` (the +0x04 u32's high
half) = the numbered `hdat` file index — the `00575D10` request's `sel`
(resource-delta slot past the widget's `+0xCA`). Corpus-exact: the
per-value histogram equals each family's per-file record counts
(knowledge {0:88,1:12}, monster {0:71,1:74,2:98,3:141}; all-zero in the
single-hdat families). Low half `word[rec+4]` = a small display-group
key (0..7) copied to the detail descriptor `out+0x10`. The 12-byte
record is now `{u32 textId; u16 group; u16 hdatFile; u16 index;
u8 flag; u8 pad}` — only `textId` space and `+0x0B` pad remain.

## 2026-09-22 SWE2-DATA — hdat arg byte characterized; 00577970 bridge bound

`hdat` record `+0x01` (`arg`): corrected the earlier "0 for type-2/3/7"
note — multi-string records carry nonzero arg. Corpus-wide it is a
locale-invariant cumulative u8 serial: family-partitioned contiguous
blocks in a global index space (story 14–35, person 57–74, knowledge
123–153, world 242–255 wrapping to 0–8 mod 256, tutorial/monster all
zero). A `byte[reg+1]` sweep of the whole handbook family
(`00575000–00578000`) plus inspection of `00577A40`/`00575D10`/
`00577970`/`005760A0` finds no reader — authored-order serial,
semantics unbound, possibly dead-authored.
Also bound `00577970(root, kind, recIdx)`: the record→page-image bridge
— reads `word[rec+0x08]` and calls `00575DD0(root, kind, rec.index)`,
so selecting a detail record loads its page. Recorded that hctg records
are not unique-keyed (story ships four identical 0x113D6/index-10 rows).

## 2026-09-22 SWE2-DATA — hctg sectioning system closed: group = section index

`00576740(out, sectionIdx)` decoded: resolves the section's conditional
caption via `00576A50`, then scans the record table for `word[rec+4] ==
sectionIdx`, writing first-member index (`out+0x0A`), member count
(`out+0x0C`) and unlocked-member count (`out+0x0E`, via `00576CA0`) —
the "n/total" progress line on each section header. `005766E0(recIdx)`
is the plain `word[rec+4]` accessor. Corpus-exact: `rec.group` takes
exactly 0..captionN−1 in all 54 hctg files — **group IS the section
index into the +0x18 conditional-caption table**, so `+0x12` is the
section count and the aux region is the section-header table. Monster's
32 = its bestiary sections; the conditional gates hide spoiler section
titles (placeholder 0x3EC) until encountered.

Follow-up on the sectioning decode: `00576CA0(famOrd, recIdx)` — the
predicate `00576740` runs per member — ignores `recIdx` entirely; it
returns the family-tab availability flag (`byte[00D23750+fam]` →
save-byte `003154B0`; fam 6 → `0037F060(menuquest.dat, 1)`, gated by
root `+0x100` bit1; else 1). So the section header's `out+0x0E` is a
tab-active toggle, not per-record unlock progress. Also binds
`root+0xF8` (menuquest.dat) to its consumer.

## 2026-09-22 SWE2-DATA — hdat line builder 00576300: per-slot hchk gating bound

`00576300(out)` is the main record-content path: resolves the selected
record (global ordinal `obj+0xCE` window-checked against
`base@+8`/`count@+0xA`), copies the record's 8-byte sentinel tail to
`out+0x48…+0x4E` (so the constant `00 80 00 80 FF FF FF + chapter`
tail IS consumed — unset markers resolved downstream), then loops
`slot = 0..strCount` calling `00576E30(familyOrd, globalIdx, slot)` —
the per-slot hchk predicate — and materializes only gated-in slots
into the `out+0x08` pointer array (`out+0x03` = gated-in count).
`strOff[slot]` ↔ hchk slot vector is 1:1; each display line is
independently gated (monster name/lore/title revealed as kill
thresholds pass). Also decoded the blob-entry header: `word[entry]` is
a self-relative text offset (always 4 → text at `+4`; `0xFFFF` = empty
→ default string `01CEB638`); `byte[entry+2]` = nOps for `00577A40`'s
executor — ops and text share `+4` (nOps=0 ⇒ literal text on all
12,168 shipped entries).

## 2026-09-22 SWE2-DATA — loader-bound bin residue: fontpack names, subtype 0x75, behindcamera evaluator chain

`loader-bound-bin-families.md` — all three tracked open items resolved:

- **`fontpack_*` interior tables named** (§2). `fontpack_fs`: dir0 = the
  glyph-metrics container `{s16 faceCount=12; s16 pitchField}` + chained
  elements `{u32 nextOff; u32 glyphCount; u32 glyphBytes; u32 auxHdr;
  GlyphRecord[glyphCount]; auxTable}` — `00366080` absolutizes element i to
  `+0x10+i*8` (the documented glyph-table band) and its trailing table to
  `+0x90+i*8`; `+0x244` = `(pitchField + pitchField&1)*2`. dir1 = a small
  texture payload — `00365990` hands it to `00474600`/`003A22A0` (GPU command
  packet) with `+0x244` as pitch, gated on ready bit `0x40000000`. dir2/4/5/6
  = `.btm` pixel buffers pre-bound for faces `0xB`/`0xD`/`0xE`/`0xF` — the
  same `+0x110` band `00365810(slotIdx)` fills for dynamic `font_stf_*`
  loads (array slot = `slotIdx-1`, face = `slotIdx+0xA`, registered via
  `0017FC00`). dir3 = alias of dir2 (already proven). `fontpack_it`
  corrected: dir0 → `02AEE810` = `fontVariant[0]` TIM2 glyph sheet
  (`0039BF50` relocates TIM2 interiors; `0039BB60` lazy-fills slots 1..7);
  dir1 → `02AEE850`/`858`/`860` secondary TIM2+pixels+palette; dir2 →
  `02AEE870` = the text decoder's 28×5-byte special-character table
  (`0039BA00(code)` = `blob+1+(code&0x1FF)*5`, callers `003FFAD8`/`003FFB51`/
  `003FFBF6` read `sbyte[+0]`); dir3/4 → `02AEE878`/`880` dense u16 LUTs
  **bound but never read** (image-wide negative); dir5 → `02AEE888` =
  `{u32 count; Rec8[n]}` icon table via `0039BB20` → `002A5330` (kind byte
  `+7` selects a `0035D330` request cell); dir6/7 = sentinel-armed
  alternates (`dir[6]` skips `-1`, needs `00254A10()==0`; `dir[7]` would
  overwrite `02AEE880`) — never fire on shipped data.
- **Subtype `0x75` disposition** — tolerated-absent, not dead: the
  `002C8EE0` loop requests `0x74+edi` unconditionally for both slots; the
  `{status, alloc}` pair lands in `0209E648` and the font-table copy-out
  (`002CECF4`+) writes it verbatim into the consumer at `+0xD0` beside
  slot 0's `+0xC0`. A shipped file would bind with no code change.
- **`behindcamera` evaluator chain isolated** (§3/§6). `00259820` =
  camera-mode dispatcher (0x110-stride descriptors at `02097300`, mode mask
  `02098DEC` bit-scanned); its `desc+0xF0 == 2` arm `00259990` selects the
  `0x860` context and calls `003D9930(obj)` / `003D9950(obj, desc+0x20,
  ctx+0x640)` on the polyline object `ctx+0x10`. `003D9950` copies vec4
  state and **accumulates `obj+0x74 += obj+0x64`** — the record scalar is a
  per-frame phase increment, not a distance. `003D9930` stashes it at
  `+0x3CC` and tail-calls `0032AEC0(obj+0x2B0)`, the shared mover/spline
  engine. Residual narrowed to axis semantics only (the actual polyline
  walk sits inside `0032AEC0`/`003CC130`).

The `+0x90` per-face trailing tables in `fontpack_fs` dir0 are
kerning-shaped but have no indexed reader image-wide — recorded as a
written-but-unread cache, not named.

  not a phase accumulator. `003D9950` stages key B = `ctx+0x640` target
  vec4 into `obj+0x70` — `+0x74` is overwritten by the copy *before* the

  arm `003D9930` routes the same scalar to `obj+0x3CC` = `mover+0x11C`
  (mover base `obj+0x2B0`), which `0032B1C0` adds into `target.y` on latch;
  the field's constructor default (`0032B790`) is `0x3FA66666` = **1.3** —
  record 0's scalar.

  `00259C40` runs it on a second polyline-mover object at `ctx−0x638`
  (`020976E8`/`02097F48`); it writes seven `{x,y}` pairs from `.rdata`

  (`x = −0.7,0,0.3,1.4,4.5,5.0,7.6`; `y = 2.8,4.4,4.8,5.7,7.3,7.5,8.8`),
  then mover-inits and calls `003D9C40`. The authored table replaces a

## SWE2-DATA (2026-09-21) - ATEL debug-companion inner layouts (SN-1 narrowing)

**Claim.** The SN-1 residual on

(`ch/bin` copies; `in/bin` byte-identical).

**Result.** Container layouts of all three companions decoded and verified on the
full 12-file corpus; SN-1 stays PARTIAL on payload semantics only.

- `.sbn` - second block-header word resolved: it is the **file-absolute offset of
  the block's text region** (`0x84C`/`0x1484`/`0x1510`/`0x1730` for the four
  module sources; FABLE's open 2,124 and 23,356 are exactly the two `ctrl.sbn`
  text starts). `u16[lineCount]` = text-relative line-start offsets. Remaining:
  a second `u16` array between line table and text (21-188 entries per block,
  mostly text-region offsets, a few out-of-range) whose run rule is undecoded.
- `.dbg` - mapped end-to-end: five `(offset,size)` header slots (three used),
  a 17-entry `dirA` of packed `{u32 count; u32[count]}` tables tiling
  contiguously (`dirA[t+1] = dirA[t] + 4 + 4*count`, all four files), a front
  `{u16 srcTextOff; u16 flags}` stream at `+0x6C..dirA[1]` whose first field is a
  byte offset into the module's `.sbn` block-0 text (flags in
  {0,1,0x1000,0x2000,0x3000,0x4000,0x5800}). Non-empty tables: T1 (1,389-1,436
  byte offsets into the scope-stream region, non-4-aligned targets), T3
  (203-211 heap positions in the local-identifier range), T4 (exactly 131 into
  `global_flag[]`), T8 (exactly 103 into `battle_global_flag[]`, empty in
  btlctrl). S0 = `{count; offs[4*count]; 0}` over 7/13/23/7 scopes, each scope a
  quartet {src-pos stream; name index; counted table; counted table with -1
  marker}. S2 = 0-terminated offset array (65 entries x3, 301 for mapctrl). Tail
  = class-ordered NUL-separated string heap; T3/T4/T8 entries land mid-string in
  97%+ of cases - heap-position indices, anchoring rule undecoded.
- `.msb` - `u32[msgCount]` directory (`msgCount = dir[0]&0xFFFF / 4`; 42/47/48/57)
  of `(flag<<16)|offset` entries, strictly ascending. Payloads open
  `0F 24 81 81`, end `00`. Interior is a tag-and-atom byte stream: `0F
  <subtype> 81 <val>` fields (24/2F/37 observed; 37 optional, appears in both
  flag classes), tags < 0x80, atoms >= 0x80; `10 C8 xx` argument-index counter,
  `88 xx xx xx` 4-byte atom (likely identifier reference). The flag bit has no
  static correlate across the 194 messages; tag grammar undecoded.

**Corrections to the page.** FABLE's "three (offset,size) pairs" is five slots
(two empty); the `.dbg` "body from +0x30" is the 17-entry `dirA` ending at +0x6C;
the S0 scope count is not fixed at 7 (7/13/23/7); `.msb` flag counts confirmed
(35/22/36/29 flag-1 of 42/48/47/57).

and the two payload grammars are marked undecoded rather than guessed.

## SWE2-DATA (2026-09-21, addendum) - .sbn line table fully decoded (SN-1)

**Correction to the earlier SN-1 entry.** The reported "second `u16` array
between line table and text" does not exist - it was the tail of the line table
read from a misdrawn boundary. The whole `u16` span is a **paged line map, 32
lines per page**: every full page is `{u16 lineOff[32]; u16 chunkEnd; u16 0}`
where `chunkEnd` is the file-absolute last byte of that page's text chunk; the
final page is a bare `u16 lineOff[32]` with unused slots zeroed. The table
therefore spans `(pages-1)*34 + 32` u16s exactly - 1052 for `ctrl.src`, 100 for
`systemctrl.ath` (79 lines, 3 pages), 2684 for `btlctrl.src`, 2616 for
`evctrl.src`, 2956 for `mapctrl.src`, 610 for `mapctrl_mj.src` - verified on all
9 blocks across the four files. The text is stored as one chunk per page tiling
contiguously `[textOff .. blockEnd)`; `lineOff[j]` locates line j's slot within
its page's chunk (a slot may begin inside a NUL run where blank lines widen the
gap). `.sbn` is now fully decoded; SN-1's residual is the `.dbg`/`.msb` payload
grammars only.

## SWE2-DATA (2026-09-21, addendum 2) - .dbg scope-stream records + heap anchoring (SN-1)

**Deepening, not correction.** The per-scope q0 stream is 4-byte records
`{u16 pos; u8 0; u8 flag}` with flag in {0,1}: `pos` is monotonic
non-decreasing per scope over a small range (ctrl scope3: 0x90..0x2D5) -
consistent with a line-number or PC coordinate; `flag=1` marks the first
record of each variable-length item (equal-`pos` records form a run; items
are flag1 + flag0 groups within it, e.g. run lengths split 3,1,3). Quartet
roles refined: q0 = position stream, q1 = counted u32 table of heap
positions (scope names), q2 = counted u32 of small ascending values in the
scope's own q0 range, q3 = counted u32 list headed 0xFFFFFFFF. The string
heap is suffix-compressed - `global_flag[25]` is a suffix of
`event_global_flag[25]` at +6, `flag[25]` at +13 - so mid-string positions
can name suffixes; T3/T4/T8/q1 entries nonetheless land at irregular
mid-string depth (~15-22B stride through names), anchoring rule still
unresolved. T1 is a byte-granular, ~95%-ascending index over the
scope-table region whose in-order entries map to non-decreasing `pos` -
a position-ordered field index; exact referent unresolved. Front-stream
`srcTextOff` is byte offsets into `.sbn` block-0 text but only 94/1693 land
on line starts - finer than per-line granularity.

## SWE2-DATA (2026-09-21, addendum 3) - .msb token grammar pinned (SN-1)

**Deepening, not correction.** The `.msb` payload is a NUL-terminated
text stream in the module's custom charset (JP glyph table; bytes
`>= 0x80` are single-byte codes, not the US `0x20..0x53` Latin
mapping). Verified token rules across all 194 messages:

- `0F <cmd> <args>` escapes are variable-length by `cmd`: `cmd <
  0x40` takes 2 arg bytes (both `>= 0x80` in every occurrence),
  `cmd >= 0x40` takes 1 arg byte. Zero violations corpus-wide.
  Observed cmds - 2-arg {24, 25, 27, 28, 29, 2D, 2E, 2F, 37, 3C,
  3E}; 1-arg {40, 42, 45, 48, 49, 4A, 4B, 50, 51}.
- Every payload opens `0F 24 81 81` (194/194), then 0-3 further
  escapes; the most common prologue is `0F 24 81 81` +
  optional `0F 37 81 CB` + `0F 2F 81 80`.
- `12 <b>` (b `>= 0x80`) is the dominant 2-byte body token
  (10,730/10,742 args `>= 0x80`; ~36% of evctrl's payload bytes) -
  the regular text carrier.
- `0E <b>` (b `>= 0x80`) is a 1-arg tag; `02 0E <arg>` recurs as a
  line-header construct.
- `02` = line break, `04` = space (charset doc); `10 C8 xx` recurs
  as an argument-index counter (xx ascending across item lists);
  `ctrl` menu items take the shape `88 <label atoms> 10 C8 <idx>
  34 35`.

Still unresolved and so marked: the directory flag bit's semantics
(no static correlate), per-`cmd` escape semantics, the JP glyph
table, and the remaining low-tag (`01`, `10`, `11`, ...) arities -
their arg runs interleave so sliding-window counts are unreliable.

---

## SWE2-DATA (2026-09-21, addendum 4) - .msb flag correlate found (SN-1)

**Correction to addendum 3's "no static correlate".** The directory
flag does correlate with payload content: the two-byte sequence
`10 C8` - the argument-index counter - appears **only inside
`flag=1` messages**; every `flag=0` message in all four modules
carries zero occurrences. The implication is one-directional:
`flag=1` messages without `10 C8` exist (min item count is 0 in
that class too), so the flag marks a message *class* -
menu/selectable-bearing - rather than literally gating the
counter. Supporting shape: `btlctrl` and `mapctrl` each run a long
contiguous `flag=0` tail (19 and 21 entries), consistent with a
second, non-menu bank appended to the directory. What the flag
still does not gate: the `0F 37` escape, message length, or the
`0F`-cmd set.

## SWE2-DATA (2026-09-21, addendum 5) - .dbg heap positions are span references (SN-1)

**Deepening, not correction.** T3/T4/T8 and the per-scope q1 name
tables hold u32 byte positions into the string heap. Resolved
further: an entry lands *anywhere inside a name's NUL-bounded
span* - start, interior, or the terminator byte itself
(terminator hits 32/183/12/168 of the per-file totals; up to 41%
in evctrl) - and exact-duplicate entries occur (12 per file). The
referent is therefore the enclosing name span, not the pointed
byte: any position in [name_start .. terminator] identifies the
name. The suffixes observed earlier (`lag[209]`, `ag[210]`,
`flag[211]`, `inepos`, `trac3offset`, `]`...) are not declared
identifiers - the bare `flag[`/`ag[`/`lag[` forms do not occur in
the `.sbn` texts - so the position's depth inside the span is
writer-internal (plausibly an intern/search probe landing point)
and stays open. This kills the "suffix-named identifier" reading
while keeping the span-membership rule exact.

**Front-stream flag classes partition by coordinate space.** In
the `{u16 srcTextOff; u16 flags}` stream: `flag=0` spans the whole
block-0 text; `flag=1` occurs only in btlctrl/mapctrl - exactly
the two 3-block modules carrying `mapctrl_mj.src` - consistent
with a second-source mark; `flag=0x2000` (32 entries) and
`flag=0x5800` (7) carry byte-identical position lists in all four
files, so they mark shared content - read as positions relative
to the flag-name heap region they resolve to the same suffixes
everywhere (a stride-2 walk inside `global_flag[186]`/`[187]`).
`flag=0x3000` (~419, `0..0xCEE`, near-identical counts) is
confined to the shared includes/declarations band, and in stream
order it is a parallel u16 counter over the flag-0 marks:
`pos = 2×(flag-0 ordinal − 62)` for the first run, restarting
at 0 for a second run - per-run word indices, not positions.
Per-class coordinate bases remain unproven.


  **2026-09-21 addendum 6 - SWE2-DATA (SN-1): the `.dbg` scope-stream
  `pos` field is the 0-based source line number.** Direct content
  verification on `ctrl` scope2: `flag=1` marks land on statement
  lines - `0x49`=`main`, `0x4D`=`{`, `0x4E`=`if( debug_padd() )`,
  `0x50`=`snapend();`, `0x59`=`trl push_button_actor{`. Corpus-wide:
  per-scope `pos` ranges tile the block-0 text sequentially -
  `evctrl` scopes cover `0x21..0x4C`, `0x198..0x4BF`, `0x4C5..0x505`,
  `0x50C..0x522`, `0x527..0x540`, `0x546..0x57E`, ... and `mapctrl`
  `0x21..0x4C`, `0x4..0x6E5`, `0x6EF..0x727`, `0x73B..0x82F`,
  `0x85D..0xA2C`, `0xA34..0xA86` - i.e. each scope is one top-level
  entity's contiguous line region in source order (`ctrl` has a few
  overlapping ranges, consistent with nested scopes). Items are
  fixed-arity: a `flag=1` record plus (usually) two `flag=0` records
  all sharing the item's `pos` - dominant sizes {1,3} (`ctrl`:
  63/70, 1087/1134, 186/239 triples); size-1 items fall on
  structural lines (`main`, lone `{`, `trl <actor>{`), size-3 on
  statement lines - a slot-footprint arity whose referent is open.
  The earlier "line/PC coordinate" hedge is resolved: it is the
  line number, not a PC.

  **2026-09-21 addendum 9 - SWE2-DATA (SN-1): the `.dbg` front stream
  is the module's name-index directory `{u32 nameHeapPos; u32 index}`
  pairs; addendum 7's flag model, a8c4f705d's scope-sectioning, and
  99711fc65's "u32 tagged-value stream" framing are all retracted/
  superseded.** The stream's true end is the first `dirA` table
  (`btlctrl` ~0x9CB0); earlier passes read past it into the packed u32
  tables, producing phantom classes `0x0002`/`0x0100`/`0x0101`/`0x0102`
  and `0xFFFF` "scope sentinels" (the count matching scopeCount was
  q3's `0xFFFFFFFF` list headers - coincidence). On the correct range
  it is strict `u32` pairs (5000 `btlctrl`, 5020 `mapctrl`, 846
  `ctrl`, 1004 `evctrl`): element 0 = byte position into the string
  heap from `global_flag[0]` (98.6% land inside NUL-bounded names,
  mid-name per the heap-position convention); element 1 = a 12-bit
  symbol index 0..4095 (the heap's `global_debug_flag[0..4095]` block
  is exactly 4096 entries) or a tagged index `tag|value` (`0x3000`+2
  counter, `0x2000`/`0x5800`/`0x1000`/`0x4000` shared classes). Pairs
  run in heap order: positions ascend at name-length strides (the
  "stride-24 lattice" was `global_debug_flag[NNNN]`'s exact 24-byte
  names) while the index counts +1 through the whole table. For
  `btlctrl` index N <-> `global_debug_flag[N+34]`: slots 0..4061 =
  debug flags 34..4095, slots 4062..4095 = the module's own names
  (`resumebattle`...`frameinfo`). A sparser head section (pairs
  0..~902, index space 0..0xCED) precedes the full pass; ctrl/evctrl
  have only that section (~378/510 indices). So: `symbolIndex ->
  heapPos` directory over a 4096-slot table whose bulk is the shared
  debug-flag table. Still open: which symbol kind each slot binds.

  mechanisms re-verified against the shipped image byte-exact (three gate

## 2026-09-26 — SWE2-DATA-CLOBBER-RECOVERY-0926 (integrity repair)

- **Root cause, confirmed against the tool:** `publish_paths.sh` stages each
  named path's worktree bytes. The `0cd44bd1e` publish built AUDIT-LOG and
  PROGRAM-STATE as `HEAD + my blocks` splices (the standard flow for peer-mixed
  files) but the post-publish step that restores the worktree copy was skipped
  for these two paths — it ran for OPEN-QUESTIONS in the same batch. ~600 lines
  of uncommitted SWE2-CONTRACT entries dated 2026-09-22 to 09-25 were discarded
  from the worktree; none had ever been committed (`git log -S` confirms).
- **Recovery source:** a pre-splice worktree snapshot from 2026-09-26 ~07:40
  local survives at `Database/Tools/work/SWE2-DATA/tmp/AUDIT_worktree.md`
  (`PS_worktree.md` for PROGRAM-STATE). The 34 sections below are byte-verbatim
  from it; authorship and wording are unchanged. The only other lost range
  (snapshot ~59339-59391: GLYPH-PAGESTACK/ALIGNRES/DELIVERY) is not re-landed
  here because SWE2-CONTRACT already re-landed those entries in expanded form
  above; the same applies to the five one-line index bullets inside the GJ-8
  block, which are kept verbatim as originally written.
- **Window caveat:** the snapshot predates the clobber by ~20 minutes. Anything
  appended to the worktree files in 07:40-08:01 is outside it and
  unrecoverable by this path; no such entries are known.
- **Own entries verified intact:** `KE1-CLOSE-0927` and `SEADCFG-G3-0927` are
  committed at HEAD. The PROGRAM-STATE loss (9 entries) is re-landed there in
  the same commit.
- **Rule going forward:** after a splice publish, restore the pre-splice
  worktree bytes before releasing `@publication`; the file must diff against
  the new HEAD by exactly the still-uncommitted peer content.

## 2026-09-23 — SWE2CONTRACT-STATUS-GE23-0923 (SWE2-CONTRACT)

- **What:** `the-thirty-two-statuses.md` `+0x0A` amendment — OPEN-QUESTIONS `GE-3` (what `[rsi+0x0A]`
  reads when the registry slot is missing) and `GE-2` (whether the 32-bit row-pointer build can
  truncate).
- **Finding (GE-3):** `rsi` is not "whatever it already held" — it is `0031C5D0`'s null constant,
  cleared at `0031C5EC` (`xor esi, esi`) in the prologue; the only `mov rsi, rax` sites
  (`0031C6FF`, `0031C808`) sit on other arms' success paths that exit through the epilogue, and the
  class-1 arm's re-dispatch (`0031C632`–`0031C639`) never writes it, so every arm entry sees
  `rsi = 0` and every `cmp qword [rip+d], rsi` is a null test. On the `0031E259`/`0031E266` fail
  paths `0031E288` reads `word [0x0A]` — the null page, a guaranteed fault, not a graceful
  fallback; the arm has no missing-slot path at all. Reachability is the install window only:
  `02EBF118` is written by `003847B0`, a 3-instruction shim (`lea rcx, [02EBF118]` at `003847B3`,
  `jmp 003845F0`) resolving the master record's `+0x40` — the same installer mechanism as the
  class-13 slots. Once run, `desc+0x0C` is a shipped nonzero offset and `0020E600` cannot return 0,
  so both branches are dead in normal play; a pre-install class-26 query faults rather than
  mis-resolves.
- **Finding (GE-2):** `rsi = u32(low32(rowbase) + stride×idx)` — the carry out of `add esi, eax`
  is dropped, so truncation needs `low32(rowbase) + 40×idx ≥ 2³²`; with shipped stride 40 and 32
  rows that is a resolved base in the top ~1.2 KiB under 4 GiB, or above it. Sibling build
  `0031C7B5` identical on its own descriptor. Whether the arena ever lands there is the `J-C` live
  read of `01F83530` — same residual as the registry rebase; the design assumes sub-4 GiB backing
  (arena self-links are 32-bit, FABLE's `CD-2`/`J-C` finding), so the truncation window is a
  configuration the arena cannot address either. Nothing shipped observes it; no defect claimed.
- **Edits:** resolution bullet appended to the `+0x0A` amendment; both ledger rows flipped to
  ANSWERED.
- **Gates:** doc-addresses clean (64 cited, 0 unconfirmed); check_questions consistent
  (GE-2/GE-3 now ANSWERED); consistency 1 pre-existing peer disagreement (`006B9120`); links

## SWE2CONTRACT-SOUND-SR6-0923 — sound-request SR-6 + §15a resolution (2026-09-23)

- **Question (`SR-6`, OPEN-QUESTIONS):** whether a slot above 63 ever reaches a resolver — the
  table is 64 entries and `003A1240`'s `movzx r8d, cx` (`003A1245`) does not bound the index.
- **Answer:** no shipped path can mint such a handle — the bound is a data-flow invariant, not a
  code check. Enumerated every route:
  - All handles derive from `003A0C90` (find-or-allocate). Match path returns the walked node's
    tag pair `(entry[+0xA]<<16)|entry[+8]` (`003A0D0A`–`003A0D19`); the init writes
    `entry[i].+8 = i` for all 66 nodes (`003A1443`), so the low word is a real walked slot.
    Miss path pops the free list (sentinel node 65 at `02AEF3D8`) via unlink `003A1750`, which
    splices only list-internal links and poisons the popped node to `-1`.
  - Bank globals `02AEF3FC`/`400`/`404` writers: `003A12E4`/`003A1344`/`003A13A4` (each stores
    `003A1650`'s `edi` return, re-validated against `entry[di]`'s tag at `003A1694`–`003A16CC`)
    plus `-1` clears `003A14BE`/`003A153D`/`003A15BC`. No other writers.
  - `003A1240`'s sole caller is `002E9FB2` (in `002E9D90`, actor-side sound lookup), reading a
    stored handle from the sound set's `+0x30+group*4` array — written only by `002E61E9`
    (`003A1650` result) or `002E61C2` (`-1`). No stored pointer to `003A1240` image-wide.
- **Bonus resolution — §15a QUALIFIED row:** the 64/66/72 discrepancy reconciles exactly. Init
  loop `003A1434`–`003A14A6` writes 66 nodes (`cmp edx,0x42`): 64 pool slots + sentinel head
  nodes 64 (`02AEF3C0` used) and 65 (`02AEF3D8` free); the bitmap `02AEF3F0` is 9 zeroed bytes =
  72 bits padding 64 slots. "Exactly 64 entries" now PROVEN on the init body's own evidence.
- **Residual (honest):** a corrupted stored handle would still index OOB unchecked — the
  resolvers' trust is real. Read-only compare bounds the harm; no writer produces the input.
- **Edits:** `CONTRACT-sound-request.md` §14.6 struck with the full route census, §15a addendum
  appended (OPUS's text preserved, resolution as a dated blockquote), §15 row upgraded to
  PROVEN; `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` SR-6 flipped.

class code — sole reader `007EE01D` special-cases `==1` (`se001` → `frpan=0`, non-positional

## SWE2-DATA — 2026-09-28 — SeSep payload decoded: {u32,u8} live record + dead program stream

`spp-map-sound-list.md` + OQ SQ-1 (package `SWE2-DATA-SESEP-FIELDS`). Corrects one loose phrase in
the band-split entry: `00222DC0` copies the payload as a **5-byte pair** — dword0 → record `+0x40`
and `+0x45`, flag byte → `+0x44` and `+0x49` (not three copies of the byte). The `SeSep` payload is
`{u32 dword0, u8 flags, program stream}` — two stacked `{u32,u8}` records in exactly the `.seb`
node's `{u32@0,u8@4}+{u32@5,u8@9}` double-record shape. **The stream (payload `+5` …, 72–1,064 B
per chunk) is dead-authored on PC**: `002DF070` is the only `SeSe`-magic walker; it hands
`(id, payload)` down `001DBE60` → `00210C40` → `0021A040` → `00222DC0`, which reads `pl[0..4]`
only; the pointer is never stored and no code re-walks or re-finds chunks. The playable program
ships in the `.sab`'s `snd `/`seq `/`trk `/`mtrl` chunks. **`dword0` is live, unlike the `.seb`
twin:** the record's `+0x40`..`+0x4c` block is cloned into the request-entry shape and `00213140`
pushes it to a child object through the shared SEAD param-push slot `vft[+0x100]`
(`edx`=dword0, `00213179`–`00213199`); the leaf's field-level use is engine-side and stays open.
Authored `dword0` shape over all 6,523 chunks: `b0` ∈ 1–16 `|0x80` (`0x82`/`0x83`/`0x84` dominate
1k and 50k; `0x04` dominates 10k at 1,486/3,398), `b1` = `0xE0` dominant (varies when `w0hi`=2),
`w0hi` ∈ {1,2} — the same record template as the `.seb` u32. Residual: flag-bit names, `dword0`
leaf semantics (engine lane), env99 computed-kind-1 producer.
Gates: ledger consistent (0 cell mismatches), links clean (6 pre-existing peer breaks),
doc-addresses 146 cited/0 to confirm, consistency PASS. Published `1eb1b3e9a`; the OQ SQ-1
row edit is written in the worktree but withheld - the file carried two in-flight peer rows
(OPUS B-2/b + B-2/c) whose referenced candidate package is still untracked; it rides the
next ledger publish.

## SWE2-DATA BQ-9 TSV marking decision + application - 2026-09-27

Request FABLE-REQ-DATA-VERB-TABLE-ARITY-STATUS-BQ9: whether
scriptvm-verb-table.tsv should carry BQ-9's 90-row answer and how to mark the
24 two-valued rows.

**Decision:** yes - all 90 rows now carry the measured answer.

- 33 no-callback rows (the `*sync` family + 5 others): `arity=0`,
  `net_or_sums=0`, `pops_int`/`pops_float` left EMPTY. Empty is the measured
  answer - there are no pop sites at all, since the executor hands the value
  stack only to begin/result callbacks and none exists. Keeping them empty
  also preserves FABLE's A1 census signature (33 empty-pops rows).
- 33 exact rows (22 single-need + 11 hand-read loops): `arity=net_or_sums=n`,
  status CONFIRMED (45 total incl. sync rows) when the catalog count agrees,
  DERIVED (21) when the catalog declares the verb unknown. Zero CONFLICTs.
- 24 two-valued rows: NEW status `CONDITIONAL` - distinct from GUARDED
  (early-out where only one branch reads). These diverge mid-handler through
  class-3 predicate 00263D00 skipping one pop: `net_or_sums = lo|hi`
  (GUARDED's `0|1` convention), `guard = 00263D00` names the selecting
  predicate, `arity` = the catalog value where it matches a measured path
  (15 rows incl. aturny=2, the smaller) else the larger. 12 turn verbs
  (00357DE0) are 2|3; 12 look-at (00357D10/00357C40) are 3|4.
- `pops_*` columns left as observed per-type counts (floors where partial):
  param_types is the authored signature, not the stack split (verified - no
  correlation on CONFIRMED rows). `arity` is the total.

Changes: `Verb-Dispatch/members/bq9_arity_update.py` (idempotent member
generator), the TSV, the doc's trust table (CONDITIONAL row added,
LOWER-BOUND/UNPROVEN retired to 0, counts rebalanced - total still 1,960),
