## 2026-09-28 — SWE2-DATA — progress-report checkpoint-10 repair (FRONTIER-REQ-SWE2-DATA-PROGRESS-REPAIR-CKPT10)

Package: `_index/progress/{progress_report.py,test_progress_report.py,
progress.config.json,*}`, `PROGRESS.md`, `gfz-scripts/swe2_watchdog.py`.

Repairs (each asserted by an executed test):

- **Terminal evidence is receipted, not filename-counted.** `final_audits`
  now reads the PROGRAM-STATE declared counter plus AUDIT-LOG complete-run
  headings; `AUDIT-PASS*` files are reported as round artefacts and never
  summed (AUDIT-PASS13-ROUND1/ROUND2 are two rounds of one pass, not 2/30).
- **LIVE counts only where ruled.** A LIVE cell satisfies iff its own text
  cites the governing criterion ruling (`Criterion: … ruling <date>`); bare
  LIVE is reported as LIVE-UNRULED and never folds into MET.
- **Reviewers resolve from assignment/receipt fields only** (`reviewer` /
  `recipient` / `reviewed_by`), never `requester`; absent identity = UNKNOWN.
- **Dispositions separated:** accepted answers, withdrawn (never learned),
  contradiction dispositions, untracked transfers, new debt (READY), reopened.
- **Fingerprint covers everything consumed:** parser version, generator sha,
  config sha, every input sha, the document-tree consumed surface (path +
  frontmatter head), `check_questions.py`/`transfer_audit.py` shas, and the
  board revision/epoch.
- **Coherent generation:** inputs are captured before AND after the build; a
  mid-build move aborts with nothing published. Missing required input ->
  INCOMPLETE: snapshot.json names it, last-good outputs retained.
- **Staged publish:** all five outputs staged to temp, committed with the
  fingerprint-bearing snapshot.json LAST (a mid-commit failure leaves a
  detectably mixed set, never a silent one); snapshot.json records each text
  output's content sha256 so a hand-edit or foreign write fails `check()`.
- **History is success-only:** one history.jsonl row per published
  fingerprint, appended after the committed set verifies; failed candidates
  and duplicate triggers record nothing.
- **`.dirty` is debt:** it forces regeneration regardless of fingerprint and
  is consumed only after a successful run (generator auto/generate and the
  watchdog both enforce rc==0 before unlinking).
- **Parity** is read from PARITY-STATUS.md; absent/unparseable = UNMEASURED.
- **auto() regenerates** when the published set is incoherent even if the
  fingerprint is unchanged (deleted/tampered output members).

Tests: `test_progress_report.py` — 26 checks, all green (live-tree T1-T8 +
fixture T9-T26 covering config edit, same-count edit, doc add/delete,
missing source, mid-build move, mid-commit failure, deleted/tampered
outputs, dirty-mark contract, duplicate triggers, transferred-obligation
visibility, parity UNMEASURED, watchdog tick/skip/failure receipts, dated
snapshots, history behaviour). A real `maybe_progress_report` invocation on
the live tree logged the `progress_report` event receipt (rc 0, UNCHANGED
skip).
## 2026-09-28 — SWE2-FRONTIER — transient same-revision board divergence disposition (ASTRA-NOTICE-FRONTIER-TRANSIENT-DIVERGENCE-35478)

Incident: at 2026-09-27T23:38Z the journal records two writers committing the
same revision twice — SWE2-FRONTIER (foreign session, op `3915b8325c`, board
`7eff63eb…`) at :29 and SWE2-EC7 (op `6224f04310`, board `795ec660…`) at :35
for rev 35478, then the same pair at :47/:52 for rev 35479. EC7's postimages
won; ASTRA's same-revision guard correctly rejected the earlier image, a
supported recheck passed, and nothing was lost — the overwritten ops (add and
claim on `SWE2-FRONTIER-PUB-BATCHK-EXT27E`) were retried and landed; the
extension-27e payload is commit `0b2f92e5c`.

Defect (evidence-backed): exclusion depended on lock-file existence. EC7's
wake log documents manual reaps during live contention — a wedged record
(pid 59356), the file rotating to a live peer (pid 66076) between observation
and action, then a dead record (pid 27988) reaped by hand. Any unlink of a
live holder's file admits a second writer, and the displaced holder's own
`finally: unlink` then deletes the NEXT generation's file — the collision
self-amplifies, matching two same-revision pairs 24 s apart. Whether
`team.py`'s own reap path also misjudged a live record is unprovable — no
lock-file contents were captured — but its latent form is now closed too: a
record carrying `"started": true` made `int(recorded)==1`, failing the
recycle compare and reaping a live holder.

Fix: `team.py` exclusion is now the named kernel mutex
`Local\XIIOnlineTEAMBoardLock` (Windows) — no file to delete, released by the
OS if the holder dies mid-write (WAIT_ABANDONED still grants ownership; a
torn write stays detectable via the journal's intent/commit records).
TEAM.lock is still created and honoured inside the mutex (a peer running an
older team.py respects only the file) and doubles as the diagnostic holder
record. `_holder_is_live` no longer treats `recorded is True` as comparable;
the file-lock remains the non-Windows fallback. TEAM.md updated: manual
TEAM.lock reaps are forbidden — removing a live writer's file still admits a
second holder while unrefreshed peers remain; a wedged holder is resolved by
proving the recorded PID stopped and re-running `team.py`, which reaps dead
records itself. The board still writes only through the journaled
transaction.

Preserved: the journal and ASTRA's receipt
(`Database/Tools/work/ASTRA/authored-grid-shape/transient-board-guard-receipt.json`)
are untouched; no board restoration, replay, waiver, or duplicate wake was
performed. Residual sub-cause (which unlink removed which lock generation)
is unresolved-by-design — the needed receipt (per-acquisition lock-record
capture during contention) is moot now that exclusion no longer rides on the
file.

## 2026-09-28 — SWE2-CONTRACT — workbench Save/Restore contract: two preconditions qualified

Three routed requests on `CONTRACT-transform-workbench-save-restore.md`, all verified against the
image before edit:

- **`ASTRA-RETURN-CONTRACT-SAVE-POINTER-RECORD-ALIAS`** (P1) — accepted. Re-verified Save's order:
  `0036D969` stores the pointer into record slot `02EC0A00+i*8` *before* `0036D974`/`0036D977` loads
  the target's 16 bytes. Added **Precondition 3**: no target's span may overlap a pointer-record slot
  written before its own load — the snapshot is a *load-time* capture, so `target == 02EC0A00+i*8`
  records the pointer's own bytes in positions 0–7, and Restore writes them back silently.
- **`ASTRA-RETURN-CONTRACT-SAVE-COUNT-BITS`** (P2) — accepted. `test ecx,ecx`/`je` (`0036D948`)
  skips only exact zero; `mov r10d,ecx` zero-extends; `sub r10,1`/`jne` loops `ecx` times for any
  nonzero u32. §12's signed `i < count` sketch qualified as valid-domain-only — a high-bit count is
  not a no-op and is not a promised fault.
- **`FABLE-REQ-CONTRACT-WORKBENCH-COUNTER-OVERLAP`** (P2) — already satisfied: Precondition 2 (OPUS)

## 2026-09-28 — SWE2-DATA — UQ-218 @FMC payload grammar decoded

Claim `SWE2-DATA-UQ218-MOTION-RESIDUE`, pass 3. The `@FMC` payload is a
command-stream format, proven executor-side:

- `0041CD30` (init): `u32 +0x0C` = event record count; records walk from
  `+0x30` advancing `word[+4]` (byte length). Scans for the `0xFFFF`-keyed
  sub-record into state `+0x90`.
- `0041E000` (`PresentationEmbeddedRecord_ExecuteCommandStreamUntilThreshold`):
  per record `{u8 kind, u8 0, u8 0, u8 subCount, u16 byteLen}`, sub-records
  `{u16 key, u16 {cmdCount:6, byteLen:10}}`, commands
  `{u16 {opcode:7, byteLen:9}}` + operands dispatched through the 76-entry
  x 0x10 table `01EFFAF0` (`{fn, gate byte}`; named
  `PresentationAuthoredCommand_ClassNN_*`, unused slots = `_guard_check_icall`).
- Corpus-total verification: 32,151 @FMC entries (.cm + .ca), 112,439
  records (one kind-1 per entry), 439,220 sub-records, 1,714,500 commands,
  zero structural violations; 33/76 opcodes used.
- Op 0x00 = duration command (word[+2] sign bit = held; else frame count
  -> state +0x16/+0x18 + phase +0x1C); op 0x2C = selector/match (word[+2]
  vs state+0x326 & 0xFFF, s8 pair list, writes cursor +0x32A).
- Census `fef_motion_entry_census.py` gained the grammar walk — 16/16.
- The earlier `+0x44`/`+0x48`/`+0x4E` word-pattern and `{u16,u16,f32}` tail
  readings were the first record's commands (len-8 op-0x10 triples); the
  residue item narrows to per-opcode operand semantics and the sub-record
  key domain.
